REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle frame until the weight is off the rear springs with 
the wheels still touching the floor.

Remove the nuts and washers from the spring U-bolts and drive the 
U-bolts out of the spring seat cap. Remove the auxiliary spring and spacer.

Support the spring and remove the front shackle pins. The upper pin is 
held in place by a cotter pin and the lower pin by lock bolts.

Remove the rear rebound pin, which is held in place by a cotter pin, 
and remove the spring.

 Installation 

Position the spring in the rear bracket, and install the rebound pin 
and cotter pin.

Position the spring in the front bracket. Install the upper rebound pin 
and secure with a cotter pin.

Using a C-clamp or jack, force the front eye of the spring up into the 
bracket until the eye is aligned with the holes in the bracket. Install the 
lower shackle pin through the front bracket and spring eye. Align the pin 
groove with locking bolt holes in the bracket and install the locking bolts, 
nuts and washers. Tighten to 68-95 Nm (50-70 lb-ft).

Position the spring seat and wedge (if so equipped) between the axle 
and spring. Install the auxiliary spring and spacer (if so equipped). Place 
the U-bolt pad on top of the spring at the tie bolt and put the spring U-bolt 
over the spring assembly and axle.

Install the spring cap on the spring U-bolts and install the nuts and 
washers on the U-bolts.

Lower the vehicle to the floor and tighten the spring U-bolts to 489-650 Nm
 (360-480 lb-ft).

Section 04-02B: Wheel Bearings and Seals, Rear

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wheel Bearings and Seals, Rear

Unitized wheel bearing seals are standard on all rear axles. The 
unitized wheel seal combines the function of a wear sleeve and seal in one 
self-contained unit with the seal and sleeve surfaces inside. The unitized 
design provides maximum protection for the sealing surface during installation 
and operation. The tools required for unitized seal installation are only 
available from C.R. Industries. Refer to Special Service 
Tools/Equipment at the end of this section for service tool availability.

A two-piece seal is available as a regular production option. The seal 
consists of a lip-type oil seal and a wiper sleeve. The seal is installed in 
the wheel hub and the wiper sleeve is installed on the axle tube housing. When 
the hub is installed, a seal is formed between the wear sleeve and seal lip. 
The tools required for Stemco seal installation are only available from the 
Stemco warehouse. Refer to Special Service Tools/Equipment at the end of this 
section for the service tool availability. 

New wheel seals must be installed whenever the hub is removed. A 
damaged or worn seal can permit bearing lubricant to reach the brake linings, 
resulting in ineffective brake operation and necessitating premature 
replacement of linings.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel Hubs

 Removal 

Raise the rear wheels off the floor and place safety stands under the 
rear axle housing so the axle is parallel with the floor. Back off the rear 
brake adjustment. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 06 for procedure. 

Remove the axle shaft stud nuts and lockwashers. 

If tapered dowels are installed in the axle shaft flange, place a drift 
in the center of the flange and strike it sharply to loosen the dowels.

[FIGURE: E73621A.gif]

Remove axle shaft. 

Remove lock nut, lockwasher and adjusting nut.

[FIGURE: E7473C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

4254

Lock Nut

2

1124

Lockwasher (21K, 23K, 40K, 46K Rear Axles)

3

4254

Adjusting Nut (21K, 23K, 40K, 46K Rear Axles)

4

4255

Adjusting Nut (17.5K, 19K, 34K Rear Axles)

5

1124

Washer (15K, 17.5K, 19K, 34K Rear Axles)

Using Rotunda Heavy-Duty Wheel Dolly 014-00030 or equivalent, raise the 
wheel so that all wheel weight is removed from the wheel bearings.

[FIGURE: E69531A.gif]

Remove the outer bearing cone. Pull the wheel straight out and away 
from the axle.

 CAUTION: Do not use a chisel to cut through the wear sleeve. Damage to the 
spindle can occur. 

If the old seal is a two-piece design, remove the old wear sleeve by 
striking the ring surface several times with a ball peen hammer.

[FIGURE: E43491A.gif]

Thoroughly clean the spindle of the axle housing.

With a piece of hard wood that will just clear the outer bearing cup, 
or a brass drift, carefully drive the inner bearing cone and inner seal out of 
the wheel hub. 

Clean all the old grease or axle lubricant out of the wheel hub. 

Inspect the bearing races and rollers for pitting, galling and erratic 
wear patterns. Inspect the rollers for end wear.

[FIGURE: E67831A.gif]

If the bearing cups are to be replaced, refer to Bearing Cup 
Replacement (Aluminum Hubs) in the Removal and Installation portion of this 
section. 

 Installation 

If bearing cups are removed, install new bearing cups using the 
appropriate bearing cup replacer. Refer to Bearing Cup Replacement (Aluminum 
Hubs) in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Check for proper seating of the new bearing cups by trying to insert a 
0.038-mm (0.0015-inch) feeler gauge between the bottom of the cup and the 
wheel hub seat. You should not be able to insert the feeler gauge. 

Dip the inner and outer bearing cones in differential oil or pack with 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B. 

Place the inner bearing cone and roller assembly in the wheel hub. 
Install a new wheel hub seal. 

Apply a light film of lithium-base grease such as Premium Long-Life 
Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to 
the axle spindle. Position a seal protector tool over the axle spindle 
threads. 

With the hub centered on the axle spindle, carefully slide hub assembly 
straight onto the axle housing spindle (to avoid seal damage). Then remove the 
seal protector from the axle spindle. 

Fill the wheel cavity with rear axle lubricant before installing the 
outer bearing. 

[FIGURE: E44261A.gif]

Install the outer wheel bearing and start the bearing adjuster nut. 
Remove the wheel jack. 

Adjust the wheel bearings. Refer to Adjustments in this section.

Install the axle shaft, a new gasket, lockwashers and axle shaft 
retaining nuts. Tighten the nuts to specifications listed at the end of this 
section.

Adjust the brakes. 

Check the rear axle lube level and add oil, if required. 

Remove the safety stands and lower the vehicle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bearing Cup Replacement (Aluminum Hubs)

 WARNING: DO NOT USE OXYACETYLENE OR SIMILAR EQUIPMENT TO HEAT THE HUB. THIS CAN 
CAUSE OVERHEATING IN LOCALIZED AREAS WHICH WILL RESULT IN LOSS OF STRENGTH 
THAT CAN CAUSE FAILURE OF THE HUB ASSEMBLY AND ULTIMATELY LOSS OF VEHICLE 
CONTROL. 

Remove the wheel bearings.

Thoroughly clean and degrease the hub with a nonflammable solvent. 

Heat the hub evenly throughout in an oven to 79°-96°
C (175°-205°F). 

 WARNING: REPLACE DAMAGED HUBS. USING A DAMAGED HUB ON A VEHICLE CAN RESULT IN 
HUB FAILURE AND ULTIMATELY IN LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL. 

 CAUTION: Take care to avoid damage to the bearing cup bore and shoulder. 

 NOTE: Variations in tolerances of materials and oven temperatures can allow 
bearing to drop in and out easily. 

Remove the hub from the oven and quickly press out the bearing cup.

Heat the hub evenly as in Step 3. 

 CAUTION: Take care to avoid damage to the bearing cup and shoulder. 

Remove the hub from the oven and quickly press in the new bearing cup. 
Be sure the cup is properly aligned and fully seated.

[FIGURE: E1739E.gif]

Check for proper seating of the new bearing cups by trying to insert a 
0.038-mm (0.0015-inch) feeler gauge between the bottom of the cup and the 
wheel hub seat. You should not be able to insert the feeler gauge. 

Install the wheel bearings.

Section 04-02B: Wheel Bearings and Seals, Rear

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hub Seal, Rear, Unitized 

 Removal 

With a piece of hard wood that will just clear the outer bearing cup, 
or a brass drift, carefully drive the inner bearing cone and inner seal out of 
the wheel hub. 

Remove and discard the old oil seal. If a wear sleeve is in place on 
the spindle, carefully remove the wear sleeve and discard. Unitized seals will 
leak if installed over a wear sleeve. Thoroughly clean all grease and dirt 
from the spindle, spindle threads, seal bore and wheel cavity. 

Remove all burrs from the shoulder of the spindle and seal bore in the 
hub with emery cloth. Remove any nicks or scratches from the seal bore or 
spindle with emery cloth. 

Scratches in the hub seal bore might be too deep to be dressed out by 
light polishing with an emery cloth. In this case, apply a thin layer of 
non-hardening sealer such as Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or -BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4G92-A or ESE-M4G195-A to the 
colored outside diameter of the new seal prior to installation. 

 Installation 

Dip the inner and outer bearing cones in differential oil or pack with 
grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B before installation. 

Position the inner bearing cone in the bearing cup. 

Seat smaller outside diameter of seal in the recess of the tool 
adapter. Use green tool with the green seal. Use red tool with the red seal. 

Insert centering plug of tool in bore of inner bearing cone. The plug 
prevents cocking of the seal in the bore. 

Use a 1.8-2.3 kg (4-5 lb) hammer and hold the tool firmly to avoid 
bouncing and unseating the seal from the tool. Hold the tool handle firmly and 
strike until the sound of the impact changes to a ringing as the seal bottoms 
out. After seal is bottomed in the bore, check for freedom of movement by 
manually moving interior rubber component of seal backward and forward. A 
slight movement indicates damage-free installation. 

[FIGURE: E43501A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 4436
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 04-02B: Wheel Bearings and Seals, Rear

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hub Seal, Rear, Two-Piece 

 Removal 

Remove and discard the old oil seal. 

 CAUTION: Do not use a chisel to cut through the wear sleeve. Damage to the 
spindle can occur. 

Remove the old wear sleeve by striking the ring surface several times 
with a ball peen hammer.

 Installation 

Thoroughly clean the axle spindle with a wire brush. Remove all burrs 
with an emery cloth. 

If the spindle shoulder is scored or pitted, apply a thin coat of 
non-hardening sealant such as Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or -BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4G92-A or ESE-M4G195-A.

Install the wiper sleeve on the axle housing. For a list of the 
appropriate tools, refer to the Special Service 
Tools/Equipment portion of this section. Do not use heat on the wiper sleeve to facilitate installation.

[FIGURE: E1928F.gif]

After bottoming, rotate the tool while applying several light hammer 
blows to make sure the seal ring is flush and square with the face of the 
shoulder. The sleeves are designed with flanges to eliminate the possibility 
of installing them backwards. 

Remove all burrs and protrusions from the oil seal area of the wheel 
hub. 

Dip the inner and outer bearing cones in differential oil or pack with 
grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent lubricant 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B before installation. 

Position the inner bearing cone in the bearing cup. 

Pack grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B between the spring and seal lip to 
prevent the spring from dislocating when the seal is installed.

Position the oil seal in the hub bore and drive it squarely into 
position using the correct tool. The seal must be evenly bottomed.

ADJUSTMENTS

Wheel Bearings, 17.5K, 19K and 34K Rear Axles 

Tighten the adjusting nut to 237 Nm (175 lb-ft) while 
rotating the wheel to seat the bearings. 

Back off the adjusting nut one quarter turn. 

Install the lockwasher. Advance the adjusting nut if necessary to align 
the dowel pin in the nut with the hole in the lockwasher. 

Install the lock nut and tighten to 237 Nm (175 
lb-ft). The wheel assembly must rotate freely with an end play of 0.000-0.125 
mm (0.000-0.005 inch). Do not preload the bearings.

[FIGURE: E73631A.gif]

================================================================================

Section 04-02B: Wheel Bearings and Seals, Rear

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Wheel Bearings, 21K, 23K, 40K and 46K Rear Axles 

Tighten the adjusting nut to 237 Nm (175 lb-ft) while 
rotating the wheel to seat the bearings. 

Back off (loosen) the adjusting nut one quarter turn. Install the 
tabbed lockwasher so that the prebent arms fit over either the point or flat 
of the inner nut. If necessary, advance the adjusting nut to align the prebent 
tabs with the flat on the adjusting nut. 

Install the lock nut and tighten to 237 Nm (175 
lb-ft). The wheel assembly must rotate freely with an end play of 0.000-0.125 
mm (0.000-0.005 inch). Do not preload the bearings. Bend a minimum of two of 
the tabs on the lockwasher outboard over the flats of the lock nut.

Section 04-02C: Suspension, Rear, Hendrickson U2-, RS- and RT2-Series Tandem Axle

1997 LT, LTS, LNT-8000-9000 and LTL, LTLS-9000 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension

Hendrickson tandem suspensions U2-340, UE2-340, RT2-400, RTA2-380, 
RTE2-400, RTEA2-380, RS-400, RT2-460 and RS-460 are available on LT, LTS, 
LNT-8000-9000 and LTL, LTLS-9000. 

The prefix letters U2, RT2 and RS indicate the type of suspension. The 
prefix letter A indicates that the suspension is equipped with aluminum 
equalizing beams. The prefix letter E stands for extended leaf springs, which 
provide a two-stage spring action, offering a superior ride whether empty or 
loaded. The prefix number 2 indicates the latest, most updated, lightweight 
version of these suspensions.

The suffix numerals 340, 380, 400 or 460 indicate the rated capacity at 
ground. Suspensions are available in capacities of 34,000 pounds (340), 38,000 
pounds (380), 40,000 pounds (400) and 46,000 pounds (460). 

 U2- and RT2-Series Suspensions 

The U2 and RT2 steel leaf suspensions have conventional stacked leaf 
springs. Equalizing beams and the below-axle load design absorb strain, twist 
and road shock.

================================================================================
PAGE 4442
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 04-02C: Suspension, Rear, Hendrickson U2-, RS- and RT2-Series Tandem Axle

1997 LT, LTS, LNT-8000-9000 and LTL, LTLS-9000 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Leaf Springs, Extended

The extended leaf suspension consists of conventional stacked leaf 
springs with the top two leaves extended to the rear. A two-stage spring 
action on the tandem suspension is created when the top two spring leaves come 
into contact with a second, inner hanger. When the vehicle is empty, the 
spring weight is carried by the rearmost hanger and most of the spring 
deflection is through the top two leaves. As the load increases, the inner 
hanger comes in contact with the spring. At contact, the effective spring 
length is reduced, increasing the spring rate. 

U2-Series suspensions attach the leaf spring to the equalizing beam 
with U-bolts. RT2-Series suspensions attach the leaf spring to the equalizing 
beam with bolts and a spring top pad.

Saddle

 RS-Series Suspensions 

The RS rubber load cushion suspension system uses four cored rubber 
cushions, which replace the steel leaf springs of the conventional suspension, 
and is particularly effective with varying loads. Aluminum saddles, walking 
beams and rubber cushions offer a weight advantage over spring suspensions. 
Equalizing beam design distributes the load equally between the axles.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring, U2 and RT2 Suspensions 

 Removal 

Raise the rear of the vehicle and position blocks under the frame 
behind the rear axle. 

Remove the wheels and the hub and drum from the forward rear axle. 

Position a jack under the front end of the equalizing beam. 

Remove the caps from the lower side of the saddle. 

Remove the spring pin lock bolts from the spring front hanger.

Remove the lube fitting and spring eye pin. 

Remove rebound bolt at the rear hanger. 

Lower the spring and saddle and remove the spring from the equalizing 
beam.

U2 and UE2 suspensions only — remove the U-bolt nuts 
and remove the saddle and U-bolts from the spring. 

RT2, RTA2, RTE2 and RTEA2 suspensions only — remove the 
spring top pad retaining bolts and nuts. Loosen the setscrews and remove the 
saddle and spring top pad from the spring. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Lubricate the threads of all bolts with SAE-20 oil. The axle must be in 
the operating position before the saddle caps are tightened. 

U2 and UE2 suspensions only: position the saddle to the spring and 
install the U-bolts and nuts. Tighten the U-bolt nuts to 321-408 Nm
 (237-302 lb-ft). Hit the U-bolts on the top of the U2 
firmly with a hammer and retighten the U-bolt nuts. 

RT2, RTA2, RTE2 and RTEA2 suspensions only: 

Position the saddle on the leaf spring assembly and install the top pad 
on the leaf spring. 

Install the four top pad bolts and nuts. Alternately and evenly tighten 
the nuts until snug to hold the assembly in place (top view in the following 
illustration). 

Install the setscrew in the saddle and tighten to 136-203 Nm
 (100-150 lb-ft) before final tightening of the top pad 
bolts (side view in the following illustration). 

Tighten the lock nut on the setscrew until the lockwasher is locked 
(side view in the following illustration). 

Tighten the nuts on the bolts retaining the top pad to the saddle. 
Tighten the nuts alternately and evenly in the sequence shown in top view of 
the following illustration. Tighten the nuts to 373-406 Nm 
(275-300 lb-ft). 

If removed, install the saddle cap stud in the saddle and tighten to 
75-88 Nm (55-65 lb-ft) (side view in the following 
illustration).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Saddle and Cushions, RS Suspension Only 

 Removal 

Raise the rear of the vehicle and position safety stands under the rear 
end of the frame. 

Remove the axle shafts from both rear axles. 

Back off the brake adjustment at both wheels. 

Remove the wheel and drum assemblies from both axles with a wheel dolly. 

Position jacks under the equalizing beam to support the beam and remove 
the saddle caps. 

Lower the equalizing beam and remove the nuts and washers from hanger 
pins. 

Lower the saddle on the beam and remove the saddle and cushions from 
the vehicle. 

Remove the retaining nuts and the saddle hanger pin bushing retainer.

Place the saddle in an arbor press and remove the saddle hanger pin 
bushings. 

Clean the saddle bushing bores with solvent and remove any burrs. 

 Installation 

Lubricate the bushings and saddle pin bore with Motorcraft Premium 
Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B. Install the bushings in the saddle. 

Install the saddle hanger pin bushing retainer and tighten the nuts to 
136-169 Nm (100-125 lb-ft). 

Install the saddle and cushions on the hanger assemblies and install 
the washers (curved downward) and nuts. Tighten the nuts to 238-305 Nm
 (175-225 lb-ft). 

Raise the beam to seat the saddle over the beam and install the wheel 
and drum assemblies. 

Adjust the brakes and install both axle shafts. 

Lower the vehicle. Make sure the saddle is seated on the equalizing 
beam bushing and install the saddle caps.

With the weight of the vehicle on the wheels and the axles in the 
normal operating position, tighten the nuts to 306-372 Nm 
(225-275 lb-ft).

 Removal

pin. Place safety stands under the frame and support the weight of the axles 
with a floor jack.

Remove the spring lock bolts from the spring front hanger. 

Remove the lubrication fitting from the spring eye pin and remove the 
spring eye pin from the spring and spring hanger. 

 Installation 

Align the spring eye with the hanger and install the pin.

Install the spring pin lock bolts and retaining nuts and tighten the 
nuts to 102-142 Nm (75-105 lb-ft).

Install the spring hanger pin lubrication fitting and lubricate the pin 
with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

Remove the floor jack safety stands. Lower the vehicle.

Section 04-02C: Suspension, Rear, Hendrickson U2-, RS- and RT2-Series Tandem Axle

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Equalizing Beam 

 Removal 

Block the front wheels and both tandem axles to prevent the vehicle 
from moving. 

Exhaust the air from the air brake system. Mark and disconnect all air 
lines to the rear axles. Plug all lines to prevent the entry of dirt. Unlock 
all mechanically set safety brakes on the tandem axles. Refer to Section 06-08E or Section 06-08F . 

 CAUTION: The axle is free to pivot on the beam ends. Use necessary blocking to 
prevent damage to the interaxle driveshaft, power divider and differential 
carriers. 

Remove the U-bolts and nuts and disconnect the driveshaft from the 
forward/rear tandem axle. 

Remove the bolts retaining the torque rods to the axle bracket ends and 
disconnect the torque rods.

Remove the nuts and washers from the saddle studs and remove the saddle 
caps. If a stud is removed along with a nut during saddle cap removal, remove 
the nut from the stud. Clean the stud threads and install the stud in the 
saddle with an appropriate stud installation tool. 

Raise the rear of the vehicle with an overhead hoist or A-frame and 
roll the tandem axles and equalizing beams out as an assembly. Support the 
frame with safety stands of an appropriate capacity. 

Apply penetrating oil to the threads of the bolts and nuts that connect 
the bar pin bushing to the axle bracket.

 WARNING: ALWAYS PLACE AN APPROPRIATE SUPPORT UNDER THE END OF THE EQUALIZING 
BEAM ASSEMBLY. THE BEAM CAN DROP UPON REMOVAL OF THE BAR PIN BUSHING RETAINING 
BOLTS. 

Remove the bolts and nuts retaining the bar pin bushing to the axle 
brackets.

[FIGURE: F8904B.gif]

Item

 WARNING: DO NOT REUSE THE FASTENER. AFTER ALL FASTENERS ARE REMOVED, DISCARD 
THEM. 

Remove the bar pin end connection on the opposite end of the equalizing 
beam.

With both ends of the equalizing beam disconnected from the axle 
brackets, pull the beam off the crosstube.

Inspect the mounting surfaces of the axle brackets for gouges, cracks 
or excessive wear. Any cracks detected near the top of the axle bracket legs 
require replacement of the axle bracket. If any one of these conditions 
exists, contact the axle manufacturer for instructions.

The dimension between the inside surfaces of the axle bracket must be 
57-58 mm (2.263-2.313 inches).

[FIGURE: F8905B.gif]

 Installation 

Coat the connection holes in the axle bracket legs with an appropriate 
anti-seize compound. 

On equalizing beams with rubber center bushings, insert the crosstube 
into the center bushing inner sleeve of both equalizing beam rubber center 
bushings. On equalizing beams with bronze center bushings, apply Motorcraft 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B to the bushing and inner sleeve. 

Coat the inner and outer surfaces of the rubber end bushings with an 
appropriate anti-seize compound. 

Install the equalizing beams onto the crosstube. Position the two beams 
and crosstube under the drive axle assembly. 

 WARNING: WHEN USING THE SHIM-STYLE BAR PIN BUSHING, A SHIM MUST BE INSTALLED AT 
EACH BOLT LOCATION. THE SAME PART NUMBER SHIM IN THE SAME ORIENTATION MUST BE 
USED AT BOTH BOLT LOCATIONS ON ANY ONE BUSHING ASSEMBLY. DO NOT INSTALL OR 
STACK MORE THAN ONE SHIM AT EACH BOLT LOCATION. USE GENUINE HENDRICKSON SHIMS. 
DO NOT USE STANDARD WASHERS. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THIS WARNING CAN RESULT IN THE 
FRACTURE OF EITHER THE BRACKET OR BAR PIN, WHICH COULD RESULT IN THE LOSS OF 
VEHICLE CONTROL AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

 CAUTION: Once the retaining nuts are removed, they must be replaced. The nuts 
incorporate a self-locking feature that is damaged upon removal. 

Raise the beam end into the axle bracket and support it with a jack. If 
the axle pinion angle causes difficulty in assembly, disconnect the upper 
torque rod and rotate the axle so the bar pin slips into the bracket. Minor 
alignment adjustments to the inner metal of the bushing can be made with OTC 
tooling or an open end wrench.

Disconnect the longitudinal torque rods and assemble the bolts, washers 
and lock nuts. Do not tighten the nuts at this time.

With the equalizing beams attached to the axles, roll them under the 
center of the saddle, making sure the center bushing of each equalizing beam 
is lined up with the center of the saddle legs. Lower the frame and center 
saddles on the equalizing beam center bushings. Install the saddle caps, 
washers and new nuts. Do not tighten the nuts at this time.

Connect the torque rods to the axle brackets and frame brackets. 
Install lock nuts and tighten to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft).

Tighten the equalizing beam end nuts to 611-813 Nm 
(450-600 lb-ft).

With the vehicle weight on the center bushings, evenly tighten the 
saddle cap lock nuts to 170-196 Nm (125-145 lb-ft) for 
U2-Series and 306-372 Nm (225-275 lb-ft) for RT2-Series. 
Maintain an even gap between the saddle cap and saddle during tightening to 
avoid distortion of saddle caps.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Beam End Bushing, Equalizing 

 Removal 

Remove the equalizing beam.

Remove the confinement washer from one end of the bushing for pushing 
tool clearance. If required, use a chisel where the washer has been staked to 
the inner casting of the bushing.

[FIGURE: F8907A.gif]

Cut the protruding rubber on the same end of the beam end as shown. 
This permits the pushing tool to contact the outer metal of the bushing.

[FIGURE: F3529B.gif]

 WARNING: WHEN REMOVING AND INSTALLING BUSHINGS IN AN EQUALIZING BEAM, FOLLOW THE 
PROCEDURES DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION. DO NOT USE A TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHING 
OUTER METAL PRESSED IN THE BEAM. WELDING, TORCHING OR ATTACHING MATERIAL TO 
THE EQUALIZING BEAM MUST NEVER BE PERFORMED. ALL EQUALIZING BEAMS (ALUMINUM 
AND STEEL) ARE HEAT TREATED FOR STRENGTH AND SERVICE LIFE. THE USE OF HEAT CAN 
ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF THE BEAMS. AFTER REMOVING THE EQUALIZING BEAM 
BUSHINGS, THOROUGHLY INSPECT THE BEAM BORES. IF THE BEAM BRACKETS ARE DAMAGED, 
REPLACE WITH A NEW EQUALIZING BEAM. 

 NOTE: If OTC tooling is to be used, follow the instructions provided with the 
OTC tooling.

If OTC tooling is not used, fabricate a piece of steel tubing 102 mm (4 
inches) long and 108 mm (4-1/4 inches) OD with 12.7-mm (1/2-inch) wall 
thickness to press out the bushing. The press should have a capacity to remove 
the bushing of at least 72,570 kg (80 tons).

[FIGURE: F3531C.gif]

 Installation 

Inspect the bushing bores for nicks and burrs. Remove any nicks or 
burrs with emery cloth. 

Coat the bushing bore with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C 
or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

Clean the outer sleeve of the bushing with emery cloth to remove the 
phosphate coating that acts as a rust preventative. 

 NOTE: If OTC tooling is to be used to install the bushings, follow the 
instructions provided with the OTC tooling.

A shop-made installation tool can be fabricated using a steel tube 127 
mm (5 inches) long, 127 mm (5 inches) OD and 12.7-mm (1/2-inch) wall 
thickness. The installation tool must be split in half, then bolted or clamped 
together to compress the rubber to allow contact with the bushing outer metal.

side of the bushing.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Center, Bronze, Beam Installed

 Removal 

Block the front wheels to prevent the vehicle from moving. 

Remove the nuts retaining the saddle caps to the saddle. Remove the 
saddle caps. 

Raise the rear of the frame until the saddle cap studs clear the 
equalizing beam assembly. 

If required, remove and replace the lube fitting in the equalizing beam 
assembly. 

Remove the thrust washers and center sleeves from the equalizing beams. 
Remove the crosstube from the beam center bushing bore. 

Remove the bushings using Bushing Remover Tool Set 1745 and adapters as 
shown in the illustration under Bushing, Center, Bronze, Beam Removed. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Do not install a bronze center bushing in an aluminum equalizing beam.

Position the bronze center bushing and seals in the bore so the 
lubricant groove lies along the vertical centerline of the equalizing beam. 

Press the bronze bushing and seals into the bore.

Coat the bushing inside diameter and the center sleeve with Motorcraft 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent lubricant meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

 NOTE: When installing thrust washers on the center sleeves, install washers 
until the gap is less than one washer. 

Install two thrust washers (total four) on the inboard side of each 
bronze bushing. Install the crosstube and center sleeves. Install two thrust 
washers (total four) on the outboard side of each bronze bushing. 

Install the lube fitting in the equalizing beam. 

Lower the frame until the saddle is in position over the equalizing 
beam and crosstube assembly. 

 NOTE: The weight of the vehicle must be on the suspension (axle in operating 
position) when the saddle cap retaining nuts are tightened.

Install the saddle caps. Install the washers and nuts on the studs. 
Lower the vehicle and tighten the nuts to 306-372 Nm (225-275 
lb-ft). 

Pressure lubricate both center bushings with Motorcraft Premium 
Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Center, Rubber, Beam Removed 

 Removal 

Remove the equalizing beam. 

Inspect the area surrounding the bushing outer metal for signs of 
mushrooming. Remove all signs of mushrooming with a chisel or disc sander.

 WARNING: WHEN REMOVING AND INSTALLING BUSHINGS IN AN EQUALIZING BEAM, FOLLOW THE 
PROCEDURES DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION. DO NOT USE A TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHING 
OUTER METAL PRESSED IN THE BEAM. WELDING, TORCHING OR ATTACHING MATERIAL TO 
THE EQUALIZING BEAM MUST NEVER BE PERFORMED. ALL EQUALIZING BEAMS (ALUMINUM 
AND STEEL) ARE HEAT TREATED FOR STRENGTH AND SERVICE LIFE. THE USE OF HEAT CAN 
ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF A BEAM. AFTER REMOVING THE EQUALIZING BEAM 
BUSHINGS, THOROUGHLY INSPECT THE BEAM BORE. IF TORCH UNDERCUTTING IS FOUND, 
REPLACE WITH A NEW EQUALIZING BEAM. 

 CAUTION: When pressing the bushing out, make sure the equalizing beam is 
securely supported at the center bore area on the press bed to avoid bending 
the equalizing beam. 

Remove the rubber bushing with OTC tool set Y-849 for Series 340 
suspensions and tool set Y-849 and adapter Y-861 for Series 380, 400 and 460 
suspensions. If the tool set is not available, press the bushing out in a 
press of at least 45,359 kg (50 tons) capacity. On Series 340 suspensions, 
press the bushing out with a piece of tubing with an 88-mm (3-1/2-inch) 
outside diameter and a 178-mm (7-inch) length. On Series 380, 400 and 460 
suspensions, press the bushing out with a piece of tubing with a 117-mm 
(4-5/8-inch) outside diameter and a 178-mm (7-inch) length.

 Installation 

Inspect the bushing bore for nicks and burrs. Remove any nicks and 
burrs with emery cloth. 

Clean the outer steel sleeve of the rubber bushing with emery cloth to 
remove the phosphate coating that acts as a rust preventative. 

Apply a coating of Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B around the bushing outer 
sleeve. 

Position the bushing in the bore and install using a press of at least 
45,359 kg (50 tons) capacity. Press the bushing in with OTC tool 302031 
(Series 340 suspension) or 302026 (Series 380, 400 and 460 suspensions). If 
tool is not available, press the bushing in place with a piece of tubing with 
an outside diameter of 88 mm (3-1/2 inches) and a length of 178 mm (7 inches) 
for Series 340 suspension or an outside diameter of 117 mm (4-5/8 inches) and 
a length of 178 mm (7 inches) for Series 380, 400 and 460 suspensions. 

Install the equalizing beam.

 CAUTION: Do not use a torch to remove the welded plug; the equalizing beam can 
be damaged. 

Remove the plug welded in the center bushing bore that retains the

(2-inch) diameter saw on Series 340 suspensions or a 64-mm (2-1/2-inch) 
diameter hole saw on Series 380, 400 and 460 suspensions. Remove the welded 
plug from the right and left equalizing beams.

Remove the crosstube.

bushing outer metal is excessively worn, and the edge is "mushroomed" over the 
inner face of the equalizing beam hub, remove the mushroomed surface with a 
chisel or disc sander.

THE EQUALIZING BEAM MUST NEVER BE PERFORMED. ALL EQUALIZING BEAMS (ALUMINUM 
AND STEEL) ARE HEAT TREATED FOR STRENGTH AND SERVICE LIFE. THE USE OF HEAT CAN 
ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF A BEAM. AFTER REMOVING THE EQUALIZING BEAM 
BUSHINGS, THOROUGHLY INSPECT THE BEAM BORES. IF THE BEAM BORES ARE DAMAGED, 
REPLACE WITH A NEW EQUALIZING BEAM.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Torque Rod, Straddle (Longitudinal) Mount 

 Removal 

Position a jack under the differential carrier housing to prevent the 
axle from tipping. 

Remove the two retaining nuts and the two retaining bolts that retain 
the torque rod to the axle, and rotate arm clear of housing. 

Remove the two nuts that retain the torque rod and bracket to the frame 
crossmember, and remove torque rod and bracket from vehicle. 

Inspect the torque rod and bushings for damage and bushing wear. If 
metal-to-metal contact exists between torque arm housing and torque rod pin, 
if rubber seems excessively worn, or if looseness is encountered between pin 
and bushing, replace torque rod assembly. If unusually damaged (cracks in weld 
or parent metal or rod bent so that ends are not parallel with each other), 
replace the torque rod assembly. 

 Installation 

If original axle angle settings are to be retained, install torque rod 
and bracket to frame crossmember with original shims in place and tighten nuts 
to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). Go to Step 5. 

If new axle angle settings are to be employed, install torque rod and 
bracket assembly to frame crossmember on top of original spacers. Assemble 
nuts loosely onto bracket retaining bolts. Assemble torque rod to axle and 
tighten to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft).

Set new angles by adding or subtracting spacers to original spacer pack 
under the torque arm frame bracket. (Remove the jack under the axle housing 
during this procedure, if necessary). When the desired axle angle is attained, 
reset the jack under the housing (if removed).

Assemble spacers properly under torque rod bracket and tighten nuts to 
204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 

Install the torque rod to axle by rotating the torque arm into position 
and installing nuts, bolts and washers. (Place a washer under the bolt head 
and nut.) Tighten nuts to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 

Remove the jack from under the differential carrier housing.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Torque Rod, Taper (Transverse) Mount 

 Removal 

Remove the lock nut retaining the torque rod stud to the axle bracket. 

Position a jack under the differential carrier housing to prevent the 
axle from tipping. 

Push the torque rod stud from the axle bracket with 2-Jaw Puller 
D80L-1002-L or equivalent. Rap the bracket to free the tapered torque rod 
stud. 

Remove two nuts retaining the torque rod bracket to the frame, and 
remove the torque rod and bracket from the vehicle. 

 Installation 

Position the torque arm and the torque rod bracket on the frame, and 
install the retaining nuts. Tighten the nuts to 299-406 Nm 
(220-300 lb-ft).

Position the torque rod to the axle bracket and install the retaining 
nut. Tighten the nut to 238-305 Nm (175-225 lb-ft). Rap the 
bracket after tightening and retighten. 

Remove the jack from under the differential carrier housing. 

 Torque Rod, Taper Mount Installation

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension

The Hendrickson E4-360 and E4-400 tandem suspension is a lightweight, 
shackled equalizing beam-type, four-spring suspension. It has four 
conventional multi-leaf springs operating in conjunction with four torque rods.

 Hendrickson Tandem Suspension

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring 

 Removal 

Chock axle wheels. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE ANY FASTENERS. DO NOT USE A 
CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHINGS FROM THE EQUALIZING BEAM ASSEMBLY. THE 
USE OF HEAT ON SUSPENSION COMPONENTS WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF 
THESE PARTS. A COMPONENT DAMAGED IN THIS MANNER CAN CAUSE THE LOSS OF VEHICLE 
CONTROL AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

Straighten keeper tabs on bolt retainer plate and loosen both upper and 
lower shackle bolts. 

Remove rebound bolt, rebound roller, lock nut, washers, and spacer from 
end spring hanger. 

Raise rear of frame far enough to remove load from spring. 

Remove U-bolt lock nuts and washers. 

Remove U-bolts, bottom cap, and top pad. 

Remove both shackle bolts (raise frame, if necessary, for bolts to 
clear tires). Discard shackle bolt retainer plate. Do not reuse.

Remove spring assembly. 

 Installation 

Position shackle on eye of new or serviced spring assembly as shown in 
the following illustration. Hook must go through opening provided in shackle. 
Threaded bosses must be positioned toward vehicle frame.

[FIGURE: F37081D.gif]

Assemble one shackle bolt with new retainer plate through upper shackle 
hole and spring eye.

Position spring on spring seat with spring center bolt piloting into 
counter-sunk hole in spring seat while aligning lower shackle legs over 
equalizing beam end bushing. 

Assemble other shackle bolt through retainer plate and lower shackle 
hole and equalizing beam end bushing. Hand-tighten shackle bolt. 

Assemble top pad, U-bolts, bottom cap, washers and lock nuts. 

Lower frame so that end spring hanger engages spring. 

Tighten U-bolt lock nuts to specified torque, rap top of U-bolts, and 
retighten to 489-650 Nm (360-480 lb-ft).

Assemble shackle bolts and tighten to 406-542 Nm 
(300-400 lb-ft). Bend both keeper tabs at each bolt. 

Assemble rebound bolt, rebound roller, spacer, washers, and lock nut in 
end spring hanger. Tighten lock nut to 102-142 Nm (75-105 
lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Beam End Bushing, Equalizing

 Removal 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE ANY FASTENERS. DO NOT USE A 
CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHINGS FROM THE EQUALIZING BEAM ASSEMBLY. THE 
USE OF HEAT ON SUSPENSION COMPONENTS WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF 
THESE PARTS. A COMPONENT DAMAGED IN THIS MANNER CAN CAUSE LOSS OF VEHICLE 
CONTROL AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

Chock wheels or rear drive axle, and support rear of frame. 

[FIGURE: F3709C.gif]

Remove torque rod bar pin lock nuts, bolts, washers and any shims from 
the center spring hanger. Note the number of shims at each location. These 
must be reinstalled in the same manner to avoid affecting alignment. 

 WARNING: DO NOT REUSE SHACKLE BOLT RETAINER PLATES. 

Straighten all keeper tabs on shackle bolt retainer plates and remove 
all shackle bolts. Discard shackle bolt retainer plates. 

Reinstall upper shackle bolts through spring eyes with new shackle bolt 
retainer plates. Do not tighten. 

Remove center spring hanger-to-equalizing beam lock nut, washers and 
bolt. 

Lower frame so that equalizing beam ends drop clear of shackles. 

Slide equalizing beam forward and down, out of center spring hanger. 
Note that there are thrust washers between the beam and the hanger (one on 
each side of each beam). 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE HEAT OR A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHING OUTER METALS 
THAT ARE PRESSED IN THE BEAM. THE USE OF HEAT WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE 
STRENGTH OF THE BEAM. 

 CAUTION: Make sure the beam is securely supported at the bore area on the press 
bed for safety and to avoid bending the equalizing beam. 

Press out old bushings. Use a vertical shop press with a capacity of at 
least 15 tons. For end bushing removal, use a 102-mm (4-inch) long piece of 
2-1/4-inch outside diameter x 6-mm (1/4-inch) wall steel tubing. For center 
bushing removal, use a 127-mm (5-inch) long piece of 66.7-mm (2-5/8-inch) 
outside diameter x 6-mm (1/4-inch) wall steel tubing.

Clean bores of equalizing beam with emery cloth to remove any nicks or 
metal buildup from bushing removal. 

Clean outer metal of new bushings with emery cloth to remove phosphate 
coating which acts as a rust preventative. Apply a thin coat of grease on the 
outer metal of bushings. 

 CAUTION: Make sure the beam is securely supported at the bore area on the press 
bed for safety and to avoid bending the equalizing beam. 

Press in new bushings. For end bushing installation, use a 76-mm 
(3-inch) piece of 2-1/2-inch outside diameter x 1/4-inch wall steel tubing. 
For center bushing installation, use a 76-mm (3-inch) long piece of 2-3/4-inch 
outside diameter x 1/4-inch long steel tubing. Center all bushings in beam. 
The pushing tool must contact only the outer metal of the bushings.

Remove any remaining grease from ends of rubber bushings. End faces of 
rubber bushings must be clean and dry before assembling beam with shackles and 
center spring hanger. 

 Installation 

Position equalizing beam with thrust washers in center spring hanger. 
The inside diameter of the thrust washers must be on the outside diameter of 
the beam center bushing inner metal. There must be one thrust washer on each 
side of each beam.

Assemble bolt, washers and lock nut. With equalizing beam parallel to 
frame as viewed from the side of the vehicle, tighten lock nut to 543-671 Nm
 (400-495 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: F3710D.gif]

Raise frame until equalizing beam ends align with lower shackle bolt

during disassembly. Tighten lock nuts to 204-277 Nm (150-205 
lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Torque Rod 

 Removal 

Chock wheels of drive axles. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE ANY FASTENERS. THE USE OF HEAT ON 
SUSPENSION COMPONENTS WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF THESE PARTS. A 
COMPONENT DAMAGED IN THIS MANNER CAN CAUSE THE LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL AND 
POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

Remove bar pin lock nuts and washers at axle end of torque rod.

Loosen rebound bolt in spring hanger from which torque rod is being 
removed. 

Remove bar pin lock nuts, bolts, washers and any alignment shims at 
spring hanger ends of torque rods. Note the number of shims at each location. 
These must be installed in the same manner to avoid affecting alignment. 

Remove torque rod.

 Installation 

 NOTE: The torque rod can be installed in one way only. Be sure to read the 
instructions on the rod before installation. 

Position axle end of new torque rod on axle cap studs and assemble 
washers and bar pin lock nuts. Hand-tighten lock nuts. 

 NOTE: For the center spring hanger, the equalizing beam center bolt must be 
tightened before the rear torque rod is installed. 

Position forward bar pin end of new torque rod at forward face of 
spring hanger legs and assemble bolts, washers, bar pin lock nuts and any 
alignment shims that were removed.

Tighten the lock nuts to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 

Tighten rebound bolt lock nut to 102-142 Nm (75-105 
lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Torque Rod

 Removal 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE HEAT OR A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHINGS FROM THE 
TORQUE ROD. THE USE OF HEAT WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF THE TORQUE 
ROD. 

Use a press with a minimum capacity of 90,718 kg (10 tons). 

 CAUTION: Make sure the torque rod is securely supported on the press bed. 

Support the torque rod on a piece of 6-mm (1/4-inch) wall steel tubing 
that is 127 mm (5 inches) long with an inside diameter of 50.8 mm (2 inches).

Push directly on the bar pin to remove bushing from the torque rod. 

 Installation 

Clean and inspect the inside diameter of the ends of the torque rod. 
Use an emery cloth to remove any nicks and small scratches from the bore. 

 CAUTION: Do not use a petroleum or soap base lubricant. 

Lubricate the inside diameter of the torque rod and the new bushing 
with a vegetable base oil such as cooking oil or lard. 

 CAUTION: Make sure the torque rod is securely supported on the press bed. 

Support the torque rod on the piece of steel tubing used during 
removal. Make sure the bore of the torque rod is centered in the tube.

Put the bushing in the bore of the torque rod so that the mounting flat 
of the bar pin is positioned as shown in the following illustrations.

 Front Torque Rod Bushing Installation 

[FIGURE: F6434A.gif]

 Rear Torque Rod Bushing Installation 

[FIGURE: F6435A.gif]

Press the bushing into the torque rod so that the bushing extends 4.763 
mm (3/16 inch) on the opposite side of the torque rod. 

Turn the torque rod over and press on the bar pin so that the bushing 
is centered in the torque rod bore.

Install the spring(s).

ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment 

 Tandem Suspension 

The following procedure should be performed after all service has been 
completed and all suspension fasteners have been tightened to specified torque 
values. 

Place tractor on a level floor area. Move it back and forth several 
times slowly and without using brakes to free and center all suspension 
joints. In this condition, equalizing beams must be essentially level. 

Chock front wheels and make sure tractor brakes are released. 

Using C-clamps, securely clamp a nine-foot piece of straight bar stock 
or angle iron across frame as shown in the following illustration. Select a 
location as far forward of the forward drive axle as possible so that vehicle 
components will not interfere. On some vehicles, lower frame flange might be 
preferred. Otherwise use upper frame flange. 

Accurately square straightedge to frame using a carpenter's square. 

Begin alignment by checking rear drive axle first. Use a trammel bar or 
its equivalent to measure from straightedge to centerline of rear drive axle 
on both sides of vehicle as shown in the following illustration, Ll and Lr. If 
both sides measure within 5 mm (3/16 inch) of each other, alignment of rear 
drive axle is acceptable.

[FIGURE: F37051A.gif]

If Ll and Lr differ by more than 5 mm (3/16 inch), adjust rear drive 
axle by loosening up torque rod bar pin lock nuts on center spring hanger, and 
add drop-in shims as shown in the following illustration. The torque rod bar 
pin must always be mounted adjacent to forward face of spring hanger legs. No 
more than four shims may be used (1/4-inch maximum total thickness). Snug 
torque rod bar pin lock nuts, but do not tighten to specification.

[FIGURE: F3706F.gif]

Item

With rear drive axle properly aligned, front drive axle alignment can 
be checked by measuring forward from rear drive axle center using a trammel 
bar. Adjust pointers on trammel bar to pilot into center-drilled holes in axle 
shafts. If the forward drive axle spacing measurements (Sl and Sr in the 
illustration in Step 5 above) differ by more than 3 mm (1/8 inch), make 
adjustments at forward spring hangers in a similar manner. Snug torque rod bar 
pin lock nuts.

[FIGURE: F3707B.gif]

Following alignment of both axles, move vehicle back and forth several 
times prior to removing straightedge from frame, and recheck alignment to 
confirm adjustments. Tighten torque rod bar pin lock nuts to 204-277 Nm
 (150-205 lb-ft).

MAINTENANCE

U-Bolts 

Retighten to specified torque after first 1,609 km (1,000 miles) of 
service on a new vehicle or a vehicle with a serviced spring assembly, and 
then each 160,934 km (100,000 miles) of service thereafter.

SPECIFICATIONS

 NOTE: All threads must be clean before assembly to obtain the correct 
relationship of torque and fastener tension. To obtain maximum service life 
from the suspension system, check mounting bolts and nuts periodically and 
tighten to specified torque.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension

The Hendrickson HAS-400 Series tandem air suspensions are made up of 
four air springs. The air springs are supported on main support beams, which 
are fastened to the axle and to the frame. A torque rod from the frame bracket 
to the bottom axle cap provides stability. Additional stability is provided by 
a transverse torque rod from the frame to the axle housing. The shock 
absorbers help to control bump and rebound during vehicle operation.

 HAS-Series Tandem Air Suspension

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Control System

Air from the air supply system is used to inflate each of the air 
springs.

The suspension air control system uses air supplied from the secondary 
air brake supply system. The air suspension supply line is connected to the 
auxiliary no. 1 port in the dash-mounted air manifold.

[FIGURE: F6445A.gif]

[FIGURE: F6446C.gif]

The correct vehicle ride height is maintained through use of an 
adjustable frame-mounted height leveling valve. The valve senses changes in 
the ride height due to varying loads and either adds or exhausts air from the 
air springs until the correct ride height is reached.

If a loss of air occurs forward (upstream) of the protection valve, air 
pressure within the air spring system will be partially maintained until 
repairs can be made. However, if a loss of air occurs rearward (downstream) of 
the protection valve, the air in the brake system will be protected but the 
air pressure in the air springs will be lost.

 HAS-Series Air System 

[FIGURE: F6676B.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Dump Valve System

 CAUTION: This control must not be operated during normal vehicle operation. 
Damage to the system and/or vehicle can occur. 

This system permits deflation of the rear suspension air springs during 
trailer coupling and uncoupling operations. On LT, LTS, LTL-9000 vehicles, the 
control valve is located on a pedestal to the right of the driver seat. On 
LNT-9000 vehicles the control is located on a bracket at the rear of the cab 
between the driver and passenger seats.

Valve operation requires that the valve be manually pushed and held to 
deflate the air springs. When manual pressure is released, the air springs 
will automatically inflate to the normal operating pressure.

When the control is pushed and held, the signal line is pressurized, 
closing the supply port on the relay valve and allowing the air from the air 
springs to exhaust. When the control valve is released, the signal line 
pressure is removed from the signal line port, allowing the air springs to 
inflate to normal ride height.

[FIGURE: F6447B.gif]

Signal

The dump control valve air supply is obtained from one of two secondary 
air sources, depending on vehicle seat equipment. On vehicles without air 
seats, the dump valve supply line is connected to the auxiliary no. 1 port of 
the dash-mounted air manifold. On vehicles with air seats, the dump valve 
supply line is connected to the air seat supply line at the bulkhead fitting 
below the cab floor.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Control Valve

The TW-4 control valve is a normally closed valve that operates 
whenever the button is pressed. Pressing the button closes the exhaust passage 
allowing supply air to flow through the delivery port and signal line to the 
relay valve. Releasing the button shuts off the supply air and opens the 
delivery port exhausting the signal line to atmosphere.

[FIGURE: F6441C.gif]

PAGE 4472
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

1997 LT, LTS, LNT, LTL, LTLS-9000 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Relay Valve

The relay valve is a pilot-operated, inverting, two-way valve. Without 
air pressure on the control, the valve delivers supply air to the delivery 
port and then to the air springs. When air pressure is applied to the control 
port, the supply port is opened to the exhaust port deflating the air springs.

 Removal 

 WARNING: EXERCISE EXTREME CARE WHEN HANDLING OR PERFORMING MAINTENANCE IN THE 
AREA OF THE MAIN SUPPORT BEAM. DO NOT CONNECT ARC WELDING GROUND LINE TO THE 
MAIN SUPPORT BEAM. DO NOT STRIKE AN ARC WITH THE ELECTRODE ON THE MAIN SUPPORT 
BEAM. DO NOT USE HEAT NEAR THE MAIN SUPPORT BEAM. DO NOT NICK OR GOUGE THE 
MAIN SUPPORT BEAM. A MAIN SUPPORT BEAM THAT HAS BEEN SUBJECTED TO ANY OF THESE 
CONDITIONS CAN FAIL, CAUSING LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL 
INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

Place blocks under the wheels to prevent the vehicle from moving.

Support the axle with safety stands.

[FIGURE: F9370A.gif]

Exhaust all the air from the air supply system.

 WARNING: DO NOT USE A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE ANY FASTENERS. THE USE OF HEAT ON 
SUSPENSION COMPONENTS WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF THESE PARTS. A 
COMPONENT DAMAGED IN THIS MANNER CAN CAUSE LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL AND 
POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Torque Arm Assemblies

 Removal 

Remove the lock nuts, washers and bolts retaining the transverse torque 
rod to the frame. Remove the reinforcement plate.

Remove the lock nuts, washers and nuts retaining the transverse torque 
rod to the axle housing.

Remove the transverse torque rod, mounting bracket and spacer.

If worn or damaged, replace the bushing in the transverse torque rod. 

 Installation 

If removed, install the bushings in the torque rod with bushing 
installation tool.

Position the transverse torque rod on the axle housing bracket. Install 
the retaining bolts and lockwashers. Tighten the nuts to 204-277 Nm
 (150-205 lb-ft).

Position the bracket and spacer on the frame. Position the transverse 
torque rod on the bracket.

The vehicle is built with a shim pack of three 2.794-mm (0.11-inch) 
thick spacers that are used to adjust axle lateral tracking offset. Install 
spacers as required to adjust tracking.

Install the reinforcement, bolts, washers and lock nuts retaining the 
torque rod and bracket to the frame. Tighten the nuts to 299-406 Nm
 (220-300 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Torque Rod

 Removal 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE HEAT OR A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHINGS FROM THE 
TORQUE ROD. THE USE OF HEAT WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF THE TORQUE 
ROD. 

Use a press with a minimum capacity of 90,718 kg (10 tons).

 CAUTION: Make sure the torque rod is securely supported on the press bed. 

Support the torque rod on a piece of 6-mm (1/4-inch) wall steel tubing 
that is 127 mm (5.0 inches) long with an inside diameter of 50.8 mm (2.0 
inches).

Push directly on the bushing bar pin.

 Installation 

Clean and inspect the bushing bores. Use emery cloth to remove any 
nicks and small scratches from the bore.

 CAUTION: Do not use a petroleum or soap base lubricant. 

Lubricate the bushing bores and the new bushing with a vegetable base 
oil such as cooking oil or lard. 

 CAUTION: Make sure the torque rod is securely supported on the press bed. 

Support the torque rod on the piece of steel tubing used during 
removal. Make sure the torque rod bore is centered in the tube.

Position the bushing in the torque rod bore so the bar pin mounting 
flats are positioned 10 degrees counterclockwise to the rod shank.

Press the bushing into the torque rod so the bushing extends 4.763 mm 
(3/16 inch) on the opposite side of the torque rod.

Turn the torque rod over and press on the bar pin so the bushing is 
centered in the torque rod bore.

[FIGURE: F65461A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Pad, Rear Spring Hanger Bracket

 Removal 

 NOTE: The vehicle must be empty of all load. Service empty vehicle, one axle, 
both sides at a time.

Chock all rear wheels.

Support the frame with suitable frame stands.

Support the axles with suitable jack stands.

Exhaust all air from the air springs.

Remove the rebound bolt lock nuts, washers, bolts, spacers and rollers 
from rear spring hanger. The torque rods can remain in place.

Apply an upward force on the crosschannel or air spring mounting 
brackets with a jack or pry bar. This will cause the tips of the main support 
members to drop away from the rear spring hanger cam surface.

Remove the slipper attaching fasteners, retainer plates and slipper pads.

[FIGURE: F8410C.gif]

 Installation 

Place new slipper pad on rear spring hanger.

Place the retainer plate over the slipper pad and tighten the retaining 
screws to 23-33 Nm (17-24 lb-ft).

Release the jack or pry bar on the crosschannel or air spring mounting 
brackets, allowing the main support member to come up to the new slipper pads.

Assemble the rebound roller, spacer, bolt, washer and lock nut. Tighten 
the lock nut to 68-95 Nm (50-70 lb-ft) torque.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Height Leveling Valve

 Removal 

Exhaust all air from the air supply system.

Disconnect and mark both of air lines to the leveling valve.

Remove the lock nut attaching the arm to the leveling valve. Remove the 
arm.

Remove the lock nuts, washers and bolts attaching the leveling valve to 
the frame. Remove the leveling valve.

Remove the brass air fittings from the leveling valve.

 Installation 

Install the brass air fitting on the leveling valve.

Position the leveling valve on the frame. Install the lock nuts, 
washers and bolts. Tighten to 10-13 Nm (7-10 lb-ft).

Connect the air lines to the correct ports on the leveling valve.

Position the arm on the leveling valve. Install the lock nut and 
tighten to 12-16 Nm (9-12 lb-ft).

Apply air system air pressure and check the valve for leaks.

Adjust the height leveling valve.

ADJUSTMENTS

Height Leveling Valve

Operate the vehicle to make sure the air suspension system is charged.

Measure the distance between the bottom of frame and the bottom edge of 
the main support beam at the axle housing centerline. The distance must be 108 
mm (4.25 inches). This distance is critical and must be maintained. All other 
distances can vary due to variations in the shape of the main support beam.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension

The Neway ARD-244-6 air suspension system uses air drawn from the 
vehicle air system to pressurize the air spring assemblies through height 
control valves. The valves regulate the air pressure according to the loads 
being carried and maintain a constant vehicle ride height at all times. 

In the event of an air leak or air spring failure, air can be shut off 
to either side by disconnecting the air leveling valve linkage at the axle 
bracket. 

Neway ARD air suspension has four independently mounted rolling lobe 
air springs for exact load equalization. The trailing arm beam is curved to 
provide clearance for spring brakes. The transverse beam maintains trailing 
arm beam alignment and aids in roll control through rubber-mounted end 
connections. Four heavy-duty shock absorbers control axle rebound and damp 
oscillations. Single-pin design rubber bushings are used for all pivot joints. 
The six-inch axle articulation minimizes diagonal weight transfer between 
axles. Automatic leveling valves provide constant vehicle height.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Control System

Air from the air supply system is used to inflate each of the air 
springs. 

The suspension air control system uses air supplied from the secondary 
air brake supply system. The air suspension supply line is connected to the 
auxiliary no. 1 port on the dash-mounted air manifold. 

[FIGURE: F6439B.gif]

The correct vehicle height is maintained through use of two adjustable 
frame-mounted height leveling valves. The valve senses changes in the ride 
height due to varying loads and either adds or exhausts air from the air 
springs until the correct ride height is reached. 

If a loss of air occurs forward (upstream) of the protection valve, air 
pressure within the air spring system will be partially maintained until 
service can be performed. However, if a loss of air occurs rearward 
(downstream) of the protection valve, the air in the brake system will be 
protected but the air pressure in the air springs will be lost. 

 Air Control System

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Dump Valve System Optional 

 CAUTION: This control must not be operated during normal vehicle operation. 
Damage to the system and vehicle can occur. 

This system permits deflation of the rear suspension air springs during 
trailer coupling and uncoupling operations. On LT, LTS, LTL-9000 vehicles, the 
control valve is located on a pedestal to the right of the operator's seat. On 
LNT-9000 vehicles, the control is located on a bracket at the rear of the cab 
between the operator and passenger seats. 

Valve operation requires that the valve be manually pushed and held to 
deflate the air springs. When manual pressure is released, the air springs 
will automatically inflate to normal operating pressure.

When the control button is pushed and held, the signal line is 
pressurized, closing the supply port on the relay valve, which allows the air 
from the air springs to exhaust. When the control valve is released, the 
signal line pressure is removed from the signal line port of the relay valve 
allowing the air springs to inflate to normal ride height. 

[FIGURE: F6443C.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Control Valve 

The TW-4 control valve is a normally closed valve that operates 
whenever the button is pressed. Pressing the button closes the exhaust 
passage, allowing supply air to flow through the delivery port and signal line 
to the relay valve. Releasing the button shuts off the supply air and opens 
the delivery port, exhausting the signal line to atmosphere. 

[FIGURE: F6441B.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 4489
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 04-02F: Suspension, Rear, Neway Air

1997 LT, LNT, LTS, LTL-9000 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Relay Valve 

The relay valve is a pilot-operated, inverting, two-way valve. Without 
air pressure on the control port, the valve delivers supply air to the 
delivery port and then to the air springs. When air pressure is applied to the 
control port, the supply port is opened to the exhaust port, deflating the air 
springs. 

[FIGURE: F6442A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring, Air

 Removal 

Raise rear of vehicle approximately 25.4 mm (1 inch). Support vehicle 
frame and axle with adequate jack or stands. 

Disconnect lever arm links at transverse bar and rotate air leveling 
valve lever arms downward to exhaust all air from suspension system. 

Remove nuts securing spring assembly to transverse bar bracket. 

Disconnect air supply line at spring assembly. 

Remove nuts securing spring assembly to upper bracket assembly. 

Remove spring assembly noting the position of the spring assembly with 
respect to the upper bracket assembly. 

 Installation 

Before installing new air spring assembly, make sure piston is in 
correct relationship to upper bracket assembly.

Position spring assembly between upper bracket assembly and transverse 
bar mounting bracket. Secure with nuts at upper bracket and tighten to 35-45 Nm
 (26-33 lb-ft). Install lower mounting bolts and tighten to 
35-45 Nm (26-33 lb-ft). 

Connect air line. 

Lower vehicle. 

Connect lever arm links at transverse bar. 

Build air pressure in system to above 449 kPa (65 psi) and check for 
air leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Beam Assembly 

 Removal 

Raise rear of vehicle approximately 25.4 mm (1 inch) and support 
vehicle frame and axle with adequate jacks and stands.

Disconnect and rotate air leveling valve lever arms downward to exhaust 
all air from suspension system. 

While supporting beam assembly, remove nuts and bolts securing beam 
assembly at transverse bar, frame bracket and beam axle bracket. Remove beam 
assembly. Use puller to remove beam assembly from transverse bar, if 
necessary. 

Measure and record bar pin bushing pinion angles for assembly reference.

Press out bushing from beam assembly. Clean bore in beam assembly of 
any rubber, dirt, etc. 

 Installation 

Before installing new rubber bushings in beam assembly, coat with a 
rubber lubricant meeting Ford specification ESA-M1B6-A. 

 NOTE: Bar pin bushing must be installed with bushing pinion set at angle 
measured before removal.

Press bushings into bore past center, turn beam over and center 
bushings in bore. 

Inspect beam hanger bracket assembly bushings for wear. If excessive 
wear is evident, replace bushings. 

If beam hanger bracket assembly bushings are being replaced, coat outer 
surface of new bushings with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. Install bushings in beam 
hanger bracket using soft hammer to lightly seat bushings. 

Inspect frame bracket beam mounting holes for excessive wear or 
elongation. Replace beam bracket if required. 

Inspect transverse bar rubber bushings for excessive wear. If required, 
remove old rubber bushings and clean bore of any old rubber, dirt, etc. Rubber 
bushings are part of the transverse bar adapter assembly. 

 CAUTION: Do not use any lubricant when installing the bushings. 

Install new rubber bushings in transverse bar, if required.

Position beam assembly to vehicle frame and secure at transverse bar 
with large retainer washer first and then smaller flatwasher and nut. 

Coat forward adapter assembly bolt and beam hanger bracket assembly 
bolt with thin layer of Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. Install bolts through bracket and beam 
assembly and secure with nuts. 

Tighten forward and rear bar pin assemblies to 450-600 Nm
 (332-442 lb-ft). Tighten beam hanger bracket assembly to 
299-406 Nm (220-300 lb-ft). 

Lower vehicle and position on level ground. Refill air system and 
adjust air leveling valve assembly.

================================================================================

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushings, Transverse Beam 

 Removal 

Raise rear of vehicle approximately 25.4 mm (1 inch) off spring 
assemblies. Support vehicle and axle with adequate jacks or stands.

Disconnect and rotate air leveling valve lever arms downward to exhaust 
system.

Remove shock absorber lower mounting bolts. 

Remove nuts retaining spring assemblies to transverse bar mounting 
brackets. 

Remove nuts and washers retaining transverse bar to beam assemblies. 

Remove transverse bar from beam assembly stud. 

Remove bushings from transverse bar sleeves. 

Clean bushing sleeves of old rubber, dirt, etc. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not use any lubricant when installing bushings. 

Install bushings.

Push transverse bar onto beam assembly stud and secure with new 
retainer washers, flatwasher and nut. Tighten nut to 814-949 Nm
 (600-700 lb-ft). 

Position spring assembly onto transverse bar bracket and install 
mounting bolts. Tighten bolts to 43-55 Nm (31-42 lb-ft). 

Install shock absorber lower mounting bolts. Tighten to 110-150 Nm
 (82-110 lb-ft). 

Lower vehicle. 

Lower vehicle and position on level ground. Refill air system and 
adjust air leveling valve assembly.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Torque Rod Assemblies 

 Removal 

Before disconnecting torque rod assembly, check the pinion angle with a 
protractor. Record the pinion angle(s) for future reference. 

Support differential in present position so that alignment will not 
change with removal of torque rod assembly. 

Remove retaining nuts and bolts, noting number and location of 
reinforcements and/or spacers. 

Remove torque rod assembly. 

 Installation 

Position rod torque arm assembly and recheck pinion angle to make 
certain differential has not moved. If differential has moved, return to 
original position. 

Install same number and size reinforcements or spacers and secure 
torque rod assemblies with nuts and bolts. Tighten torque arm assembly bolts 
and nuts to following specifications:

longitudinal (both ends): 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft)

transverse (frame end): 299-406 Nm (220-300 lb-ft)

transverse (axle end): 238-305 Nm (175-225 lb-ft)

Remove support from differential. Check that pinion angle is the same 
as previously noted.

Exhaust (Down)

Check all suspension fasteners including the equalizer beam pivot, axle 
and transverse beam connections for tightness. Tighten to specifications

Check for air leakage. Cycle the air suspension dump valve once with

 CAUTION: Jack stands or gauge blocks must be of sufficient strength to support 
vehicle. 

Either gauge blocks or jack stands can be used to obtain the ride 
height setting shown in the following illustration for the rear rear axle. 
Gauge blocks must be made to allow for contour of axle in rear view on short 
leg side. Shim jack stands to achieve proper ride height, if necessary. 

[FIGURE: F6558D.gif]

 NOTE: The height control valves can be used as an improvised jack, but first 
the linkage must be disconnected at the lower bracket. Then push control arms 
to UP position to raise vehicle and remove jack stands. Push control arms to 
DOWN position, completely exhausting system, then reconnect lower linkage. 

Disconnect valve linkages at lower brackets, push valve control arms to 
UP position, and raise vehicle. Then position gauge blocks or jack stands (one 
each side) at proper ride height between the vehicle frame and rear rear axle. 
With gauge blocks or jack stands in position, push control arms to DOWN 
position, lowering vehicle and deflating all air from air springs and vehicle 
system. Recheck for proper ride height. Shim jack stands to achieve proper 
ride height, if necessary, at this time. 

Move valve control arms to a 45-degree DOWN position for duration of 
10-15 seconds. Return the control arms slowly to the center position and 
insert wood locating pins into the adjusting block and bracket on the height 
control valves. Repeat this procedure on opposite valve. Loosen the 1/4-inch 
adjusting blocks. This will allow the control arms to oscillate approximately ±
 25.4 mm (1 inch). Reconnect the linkage to the lower 
brackets. 

 CAUTION: Do not overtighten adjusting lock nuts. 

Tighten the 1/4-inch adjusting lock nuts at the adjusting blocks to 3-5 Nm
 (27-44 lb-in). Complete this operation on both valves.

Remove the wood locating pins inserted in Step 6 and raise the vehicle 
to remove the blocks or jack stands. 

The suspension system will return to and maintain the proper ride 
height.

Section 04-04: Wheels and Tires

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Tires 

Tube and tubeless-type tires are available on all L-Series vehicles. 
Tubeless-type tires are available in either bias or radial ply. Tube-type 
tires are available in bias ply. Tubeless-type tires are mounted on 15-degree 
drop-center rims and wheels. Tube-type tires are mounted on two-piece flatbase 
rims or wheels and three-piece flatbase rims or wheels.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wheels 

Cast spoke wheels consist of a cast spider and brake drum, and a 
separate demountable rim. Clamps and hold-down nuts on the 3/4-inch studs 
secure the rim firmly to the wheel. On dual rear assemblies, a ring-shaped 
spacer holds the inner and outer rims apart. Optional rear cast spoke wheels 
have five spokes on 13,000, 15,000, 17,500 and 34,000-pound axles and six 
spokes on 21,000, 23,000, 40,000 and 46,000-pound rear axles. 

[FIGURE: F8385A.gif]

The front cast spoke wheels are of the six-spoke design. 

[FIGURE: F8386A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not mix 10-hole ISO hub mount disc wheels with 10-hole BSN stud 
mount disc wheels. 

Heavy-duty 10-hole BSN stud mount disc wheels have a 285.75-mm 
(11.25-inch) bolt circle diameter. 

[FIGURE: F8387A.gif]

Medium-duty 8-hole ISO disc wheels have a 275-mm (10.8-inch) bolt 
circle diameter with 20 mm x 1.5 wheel mounting bolts. 

[FIGURE: F8919A.gif]

[FIGURE: F2606D.gif]

Heavy-duty 10-hole ISO disc wheels have a 285.75-mm (11.25-inch) bolt 
circle diameter with 22 mm x 1.5 wheel mounting bolts. 

[FIGURE: F8388A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wheels and Rims 

 Drop-Center Rims 

The one-piece full-drop-center rim has a 15-degree tapered bead seat 
and is used for tubeless tires on demountable rims with cast spoke wheels and 
on disc wheels.

 Demountable Rims with Cast Spoke Wheels 

[FIGURE: F8379A.gif]

 Disc Wheels 

[FIGURE: F8384A.gif]

The wide base drop-center rim has a 15-degree bead seat. It is used 
with disc wheels or demountable rims for flotation bias and radial tubeless 
tires. 

[FIGURE: F8383A.gif]

 Two-Piece Convertible Rims 

The two-piece flat rim base is common with FL or CR type three-piece 
(Code D) rim. It has a split side ring and is used for disc wheels or 
demountable rims on cast spoke wheels. It is also used with 20-inch tube-type 
tires. 

[FIGURE: F8380A.gif]

 Three-Piece Rims 

The three-piece flat rim base is common with FL or CR type flat-base 
(Code C) two-piece rim. It has continuous side ring and split lock ring and is 
used for disc wheels or demountable rims on cast spoke wheels. Optional with 
20-inch tube-type tires. 

[FIGURE: F8381A.gif]

The flat-base three-piece 5-degree rim has a wide seat with split lock 
ring and is used for disc wheels or demountable rims for cast spoke wheels and 
is used with 20-inch tube-type tires only. 

[FIGURE: F8382A.gif]
