ADJUSTMENTS

Driveshaft Angles, Tandem Axles, Check and Adjustment

This procedure must be performed for all tandem axle suspensions in 
which both axle pinion angles are set by longitudinal torque rod lengths and 
adjusted by varying the number of shims under the torque rod mounting brackets 
at the frame crossmember. 

Before measurements are made, make sure the vehicle is in cab-chassis 
condition and tires are inflated to normal pressure ± 69 
kPa (10 psi). 

Before any angles are measured, the vehicle must be standing on a level 
surface (labeled Horizontal in the illustration).

With the forward torque arm installed, measure the forward axle pinion 
angle vs. the horizontal to the nearest 5 minutes, using a vernier 
inclinometer or electronic level gauge. The measuring instrument should be 
calibrated to provide repeated readings within ± 5 minutes 
of 0 degrees when placed on the level surface. 

Measure the slope of the engine and transmission vs. the horizontal 
(labeled Angle 1 in the figure) with the same inclinometer resting against a 
machined surface known to be parallel to the crankshaft (the manufacturing 
pads on some transmission cases are a suitable surface). Subtract this angle 
from the forward axle pinion angle measured in Step 3 to obtain the difference 
angle (labeled Angle 4 in the figure). 

Compare the calculated difference angle to the range shown for the 
suspension in the chart Tandem Axle Angle Settings. If the measurement is 
within the specified range, the forward pinion angle is correct (omit Step 6). 

Add or remove shims from the forward torque rod bracket to bring the 
measured forward axle pinion angle within the range specified for the 
suspension in the chart. Each thick shim (Part No. E4HT-4N002-CA or 
equivalent, 0.12-in. thick) will subtract approximately 22 minutes from the 
forward axle pinion angle (reverse for Neway air suspensions). Each thin shim 
(Part No. E4HT-4N002-BA or equivalent, 0.06-in. thick) will subtract 
approximately 11 minutes from the forward pinion angle. Repeat Step 3 
following any change in the number of shims under the forward torque rod 
bracket. 

With the rear torque arm installed, measure the rear axle pinion angle 
vs. the horizontal (labeled Angle 6 in the figure) to the nearest 5 minutes, 
using the same gauge as for the forward axle. 

Compare the measured rear pinion angle to the range shown for the 
suspension in the chart. If the measurement is within the specified range, the 
rear pinion angle is correct (omit Step 9). 

Add or remove shims from the rear torque rod bracket to bring the 
measured rear axle pinion angle within the range specified for the suspension 
in the chart. Each thick (0.12-in.) shim will add approximately 22 minutes to 
the rear axle pinion angle. Each thin shim (0.06 in.) will add approximately 
11 minutes to the rear pinion angle. Repeat Steps 7-9 following any change in 
the number of shims under the rear torque rod bracket.

ADJUSTMENTS

Driveshaft Angles, Single Rear Axles, Check and Adjustment 

Check and record the angle of the engine and transmission. This reading 
can be taken at the rear of the transmission on the output yoke or flange. 
Record this reading. 

EXAMPLE: 1 degree (down from horizontal) 

Check the angle of the driveshaft. Record this reading. 

EXAMPLE: 4 degrees 30 min. (down from horizontal) 

Check the axle yoke angle. Record this reading. 

EXAMPLE: 2 degrees (down from horizontal) 

Subtract the angle measured in Step 1 of this procedure from the angle 
measured in Step 2 of this procedure.

Example:

4° 30 min.

(driveshaft angle down from horizontal)

-1°

(engine and transmission down from horizontal)

= 3° 30 min.

(transmission output shaft U-joint operating angle down from horizontal)

Use the angle measured in Step 3, and subtract it from the angle 
measured in Step 2.

Example:

4° 30 min.

(driveshaft angle down from horizontal)

-2°

(axle yoke angle down from horizontal)

= 2° 30 min.

(axle yoke U-joint operating angle down from horizontal)

Now, subtract the answer found in Step 4 from the answer found in Step 5.

Example:

3° 30 min.

(transmission output shaft U-joint operating angle down from horizontal)

-2° 30 min.

(axle yoke U-joint operating angle down from horizontal)

= 1°

(U-joint operating angle difference)

ADJUSTMENTS

Driveshaft Runout and Balance 

 Driveshaft and Yoke Runout Check 

 NOTE: With transmission in neutral, turn the rear wheel/drum to rotate the 
coupling shaft and driveshaft when checking runouts. 

Check coupling shaft for proper phasing. Refer to Adjustments, U-Joint 
Phasing in this section. Check all U-joint to yoke installations for 
improperly seated U-joint bearing caps. 

Check the runouts at the front and rear of the coupling shaft and the 
front, center and rear of the driveshaft. The runout check at the rear of the 
driveshaft should be made on the tube as close to the universal joint as 
possible.

[FIGURE: E5362D.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Runout Area "D"

2

4840

Center Bearing Assy

3

Mark the points of the greatest runouts on the coupling shaft and 
driveshaft. 

If the runout is 0.889 mm (0.035 inch) or more on the coupling shaft or 
at the front or center of the driveshaft, replace the shaft. 

If the runout at the rear of the driveshaft is less than 0.889 mm 
(0.035 inch) and the front and center runouts are also less than 0.889 mm 
(0.035 inch), proceed to driveshaft balance. 

 NOTE: The runout at the rear of the driveshaft can be caused by either the 
driveshaft or the rear axle yoke. 

If the runout at the rear is more than 0.889 mm (0.035 inch) and the 
front and center runouts are less than 0.889 mm (0.035 inch), mark the point 
of greatest runout on the shaft.

To determine the cause of the runout at the rear of the driveshaft, 
mark the U-joint and yoke, remove and rotate the driveshaft 180 degrees to the 
rear axle yoke and check and mark the greatest runout at the rear of the 
driveshaft. If the runout is less than 0.889 mm (0.035 inch), evaluate on the 
hoist. Road test if the vibration is not present. Proceed to Driveshaft 
Balancing if vibration is present. If runout is more than 0.889 mm (0.035 
inch), proceed to Step 5. 

Compare the first and second marks at the rear of the driveshaft to 
determine the cause of the runout. If the marks are within approximately 25.4 
mm (1 inch), replace the driveshaft. If the marks are approximately on 
opposite sides of the shaft, replace the yoke.

[FIGURE: E2722D.gif]

Item

After replacing either the driveshaft or rear axle yoke, recheck 
runouts. If the excessive runout is still evident after replacement of the 
rear axle yoke, it will be necessary to replace the ring gear and pinion and 
repeat the above checks until runout is within specifications. 

Evaluate on hoist. If the vibration is still present, proceed to 
Driveshaft Balancing procedure. 

 Driveshaft Balancing 

Vibration or shudder that is noticeable either on fast acceleration, 
when coasting, or when using the engine for braking may be caused by the rear 
axle housing being loose on the rear springs, improper tire balance, improper 
driveline installation, or driveline imbalance. 

If detailed parts of the driveshaft are replaced and shaft vibration is 
encountered after installation, disconnect the shaft at the slip-spline. 
Rotate the slip-spline 180 degrees. Reconnect the shaft to the slip-spline. If 
the vibration persists, disconnect the shaft at the rear axle yoke. Rotate the 
rear axle yoke 180 degrees and reconnect the shaft to the yoke. 

If rotating the driveshaft 180 degrees does not eliminate vibration, 
the driveshaft may be balanced, using the following procedure. Two people are 
required to perform this operation: one in the vehicle, and one under the 
vehicle making adjustments.

Raise the vehicle on a twin-post hoist so that both the front and rear 
axles are safety supported with all wheels free to rotate.

With the transmission in gear, increase the vehicle speed to the 
maximum vibration level. Note and record the speedometer speed of this 
vibration period as a baseline speed.

Check the attachment of all U-joint bearing caps of the driveshaft or 
coupling shaft to the transmission yoke, front or rear axle pinion yokes and 
all transfer unit drive yokes for improper installation or damaged U-joint 
bearing cap locating lugs. All yokes with worn, shaved, or damaged locating 
lugs must be replaced.

Check the driveshaft and coupling shaft for correct phasing. Refer to U-joint Phasing 
 under Adjustments in this section.

 WARNING: DO NOT WEAR LOOSE CLOTHING THAT COULD GET CAUGHT ON THE ROTATING SHAFT. 

With the transmission (and transfer unit) in gear, run the vehicle with 
the driveshaft and coupling shaft rotating at a speedometer speed of 65-80 
km/h (40-50 mph), carefully bring a crayon, piece of chalk, or colored pencil 
up until it just barely contacts the rear end, center and front end of the 
driveshaft. The chalk marks will indicate the heavy side of the driveshaft. 
Use caution when checking the driveshaft near the balance weights to prevent 
injury to the hands.

[FIGURE: E1685D.gif]

Install two screw-type hose clamps on the driveshaft so that their 
heads are located 180 degrees from the chalk mark, starting at the pinion yoke 
end of the driveshaft. Tighten the clamps and cut off the excess band from the 
clamps.

[FIGURE: E16861B.gif]

Run the vehicle up to the baseline speed. If vibration is still 
evidenced, rotate the clamps approximately 45 degrees away from each other and 
test for correction of vibration.

If necessary, continue to rotate the clamps apart in smaller increments 
until the vibration is eliminated or begins to be reduced.

If the vibration is not completely eliminated, repeat the foregoing 
procedure and balance the front end of the driveshaft, checking for 
elimination or reduction in the vibration level.

[FIGURE: E16871B.gif]

To completely eliminate the driveline vibration, it may be necessary to 
balance the coupling shaft, following the same procedure as for the 
driveshaft. To prevent overheating, do not run the vehicle on the hoist for an 
extended period.

Remove the vehicle from the hoist and road test.

 Alternate Procedure 

Road Test — Evaluate and record road speed at which 
vibration occurs. 

Raise vehicle on a twin-post hoist or jack stands and re-evaluate by 
starting the engine, engaging the transmission and accelerating to the 
indicated speeds at which the vibration was most severe during the road test. 

Disconnect the driveshaft from the axle yoke. Rotate the driveshaft 180 
degrees from its original position and reinstall. Repeat evaluation per Step 2 
above. In some cases, rotating the driveshaft 180 degrees may decrease the 
vibration to an acceptable level. However, if the vibration level is 
increased, install the driveshaft in its original position and proceed to Step 
4. 

A vehicle is more sensitive to excessive imbalance and runout at the 
rearward end of the driveshaft; therefore, locate the heavy side of the 
driveshaft by the use of the strobe light, such as Rotunda Electronic Strobe 
Balancer 006-01399 or equivalent and transducer, as follows: 

Remove rear wheels and tires, reinstall all the wheel lug nuts in 
reverse, flat side of the nuts toward the drum or disc to avoid lug nut 
imbalance and to prevent the drum or disc from dislodging.

Scribe an axial chalk line (at any radial location) approximately 101 
mm (4 inches) long at the rear of the driveshaft.

Locate the transducer so it is contacting the bottom side of the 
differential carrier and secure it in place.

Run the engine and driveline at the worst vibration speed noted and 
visually note the position of the chalk line by use of the strobe light. This 
provides a starting point for the initial location of the hose clamps. 

Stop the engine and rotate the driveshaft so that the chalk line is in 
the same location as it was noted under the strobe light.

[FIGURE: E27231B.gif]

[FIGURE: E27241B.gif]

Install two screw-type (stainless steel) hose clamps on the driveshaft. 
Position the clamp heads 180 degrees from the transducer and tighten the 
clamps. 

 CAUTION: Do not run the engine with the transmission engaged on the hoist for 
extended periods due to the danger of overheating the engine and transmission. 

Run the engine and driveline through the speed range. If no vibration 
is felt, remove the lug nuts, install the wheels and tires and reinstall the 
lug nuts in the correct position and proceed to Step 9. However, if any 
vibration still exists, the combined weight of the two hose clamp heads may be 
in excess. To reduce this excess weight, rotate the clamp heads away from each 
other approximately 15 degrees (one each way from the original position). Run 
the engine and driveline and note if the vibration has been reduced.

[FIGURE: E55901A.gif]

Continue to rotate the clamp heads apart in smaller angular increments 
until the feel of balance is best. At this point, install the wheels and tires 
as described in Step 7 and road test the vehicle to determine the actual 
degree of improvement. If satisfactory improvement has been obtained, proceed 
to Step 9. If no improvement has been obtained, the clamps must be removed and 
diagnosis should be redirected to other areas, such as wheels, tires, 
driveline angle, and yoke runout. 

When the vehicle has been corrected to a satisfactory level, as 
determined by a road test evaluation, tighten the clamps securely. Clean 
thoroughly with lacquer thinner, and spray the clamps with a commercially 
available black paint for a finished appearance.

ADJUSTMENTS

Ring Gear Backlash Adjustment

 Specifications 

 NOTE: Measure the outer diameter of ring gear for approximate pitch diameter. 

Ring gears that have a pitch diameter of less than 431.8 mm (17 inches).

Range of backlash setting — .20-.46 mm (.008-.018 inch). 

Backlash setting for new gearsets — .30 mm (.012 inch). 

Ring gears that have a pitch diameter of 431.8 mm (17 inches) or 
greater. 

Range of backlash setting — .25-.51 mm (.010-.020 inch). 

Backlash setting for new gearsets — .38 mm (.015 inch).

[FIGURE: E78321A.gif]

If the old gearset is installed, adjust the backlash to the setting 
that was measured before the carrier was disassembled. 

If a new gearset is installed, adjust the backlash to the correct 
specification for new gearsets. 

During the check of tooth contact patterns, the backlash can be 
adjusted within specification limits, if needed, to change the location of the 
pattern. 

Attach Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent on the 
mounting flange of the carrier.

[FIGURE: E5348D.gif]

Adjust the dial indicator so that the plunger or pointer is against the 
tooth surface. 

Adjust the dial of the indicator to zero (0). 

Hold the drive pinion in position. 

 NOTE: Backlash is increased by moving the ring gear away from the drive 
pinion. Backlash is decreased by moving the ring gear toward the drive pinion. 
When you adjust backlash, move the ring gear only. Do not move the drive 
pinion. 

Read the dial indicator, while rotating the differential and ring gear 
a small amount in both directions, against teeth of the drive pinion. If the 
backlash reading is within specification, continue by checking tooth contact 
patterns. If the backlash reading is not within specifications, adjust 
backlash as needed. Continue by following Steps 6 and 7.

[FIGURE: E78331A.gif]

Loosen one bearing adjusting ring one notch, then tighten the opposite 
ring the same amount.

[FIGURE: E78341A.gif]

Repeat Steps 2 to 6 until the backlash is within specifications.

Check tooth contact patterns of the gearset. Refer to Tooth Contact 
Patterns Check of Gearset under Diagnosis and Testing in this section.

Install cotter keys, pins or lock plates that hold the two bearing 
adjusting rings in position. Use the following procedures.

Cotter keys — Install cotter keys between lugs of the 
adjusting ring and through the boss of the bearing cap. Bend the two ends of 
the cotter key around the boss.

Pins — Install pin through boss of the bearing cap 
until the pin is between lugs of the adjusting ring. Use a drift and hammer to 
install the pin.

Lock plates — Install lock plate on bearing cap so that 
the tab is between lugs of the adjusting ring. Install the two capscrews that 
hold the lock plate to the bearing cap. Tighten the capscrews to correct 
torque value as listed under the Specifications portion of Section 05-02A .

[FIGURE: E7835B.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 4543

ADJUSTMENTS

Preload Adjustment on Differential Side Bearings

 Specifications 

Preload of differential side bearings: 1.7-3.9 Nm 
(15-35 lb-in)

Expansion between bearing caps: 0.080-0.220 mm (0.003-0.010 in.)

There are two methods for checking and adjusting the preload on the 
differential side bearings:

Dial indicator method 

Micrometer method 

 Dial Indicator Method 

 CAUTION: When turning the adjusting rings, always use a tool that engages two or 
more opposite notches in the ring. A suitable "T" bar wrench can be used for 
this purpose. If the tool does not correctly fit into the notches, damage to 
the lugs will occur. 

Attach Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent on the 
mounting flange of the carrier.

Adjust the dial indicator so that the plunger or the pointer is against 
the back surface of the ring gear.

[FIGURE: E7827B.gif]

[FIGURE: E78281A.gif]

Loosen the bearing ring that is opposite the ring gear so that a small 
amount of end play shows on the dial indicator. Move the differential and the 
ring gear to the left and right with pry bars while you read the dial 
indicator. Use one of the following methods.

Use two pry bars that fit between the bearing adjusting rings and the 
ends of the differential case. The pry bars must not touch the differential 
bearings.

[FIGURE: E78291A.gif]

Use two pry bars between the differential case or the ring gear and the 
carrier at locations other than those described in Step a. The pry bars must 
not touch the differential bearings.

[FIGURE: E78301A.gif]

Tighten the same bearing adjusting ring so that no end play shows on 
the dial indicator. Move the differential to the left and right as needed. 
Repeat Step 3a or 3b.

Tighten each bearing adjusting ring one notch from the zero end play 
measured in Step 4. The side bearings of the differential now have a preload 
of 1.7-3.9 Nm (15-35 lb-in).

[FIGURE: E79731A.gif]

Continue by checking runout of the ring gear.

 Micrometer Method 

 CAUTION: When turning the adjusting rings, always use a tool that engages two or 
more opposite notches in the ring. A suitable "T" bar wrench can be used for 
this purpose. If the tool does not correctly fit into the notches, damage to 
the lugs will occur. 

A second method of checking preload is to measure the expansion between 
the bearing caps after you tighten the adjusting rings. Use the following 
procedure:

Turn both adjusting rings hand-tight against the differential bearings.

Measure the distances X and Y between opposite surfaces of the bearing 
caps. Use a large micrometer of the correct size. Make a note of the 
measurement.

[FIGURE: E78311A.gif]

[FIGURE: E53471A.gif]

Tighten each adjusting ring one notch.

[FIGURE: E79731A.gif]

Measure the distances X and Y again. Compare the dimensions with the 
distances X and Y measured in Step 2. The difference between the two 
dimensions is the amount the bearing caps have expanded.

Example: Distances X and Y before tightening adjusting rings = 389.00 
mm (15.315 inches).

Distances X and Y after tightening adjusting rings = 389.23 mm (15.324 
inches).

15.324 inches - 15.315 inches = 0.009-inch difference

389.23 mm - 389.00 mm = 0.23 mm difference

Continue by checking runout of the ring gear if the dimension is at or 
within specifications. If the dimension is less than specifications, repeat 
Steps 3 and 4 as needed.

ADJUSTMENTS

Differential Gears Rotating Resistance Check

 NOTE: Make a tool for checking the rotating resistance of the differential 
gears. The tool can be made from an axle shaft that matches the spline size of 
the differential side gear. 

 Specification 

67.8 Nm (50 lb-ft) torque maximum applied to one side 
gear.

[FIGURE: E78211A.gif]

Install soft metal covers over vise jaws to protect the ring gear. 

Put the differential and ring gear assembly in the vise. 

Install the tool into the differential until the splines of the tool 
and one side gear only are engaged.

[FIGURE: E78221A.gif]

Attach a torque wrench to the nut of the tool and rotate the 
differential gears. As the differential gears rotate, read the value indicated 
on the torque wrench.

[FIGURE: E51531A.gif]

If the torque value exceeds the specification, disassemble the 
differential gears from the case halves. 

Check the case halves, spider, differential pinions, gears and thrust 
washers for the problem that causes the torque value to exceed the 
specification. Repair or replace parts. 

Assemble the parts and repeat Steps 1 through 6 after the parts are 
repaired or replaced.

ADJUSTMENTS

Ring Gear Runout

 Specification 

 .20 mm (.008 inch)

Attach Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent on the 
mounting flange of the carrier. 

Adjust the dial indicator so that the plunger or pointer is against the 
back surface of the ring gear. 

Adjust the dial of the indicator to zero (0). 

Rotate the differential and ring gear while you read the dial 
indicator. The runout of the ring gear must not exceed .20 mm (.008 inch). 

If runout of the ring gear exceeds specifications, remove the 
differential and ring gear assembly from the carrier. 

Check the differential parts including the carrier for the problem that 
causes the runout of gear to exceed specifications. Repair or replace parts. 

After the parts are repaired or replaced, install the differential and 
ring gear into the carrier. 

Repeat preload adjustment of differential bearings.

[FIGURE: E5346D.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

Tight Fit Yoke Installation

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not install tight fit yokes on shafts using a hammer or mallet. A 
hammer or mallet will damage the yoke. 

 CAUTION: Do not use the assembly yoke nut for installation purposes. Use the nut 
that is supplied with the three-piece pilot tool. 

 NOTE: The installation tool can be purchased from Kent-Moore Tool Division, 
29784 Little Mack, Roseville, Mich. 48066, or can be made from drawings 
available from the Technical Communications Dept., Rockwell International, 
2135 W. Maple, Troy, Mich. 48084.

Apply axle lubricant on the yoke seal.

Check all surfaces of the yoke hub for damage. If necessary, polish the 
yoke hub with an india stone, emery cloth or crocus cloth.

Install the pilot shaft on the input shaft of the assembly.

[FIGURE: E37301B.gif]

Slide the yoke over the installation shaft. Align the yoke splines with 
the input shaft splines.

Put the collar on the pilot shaft and slide it against the yoke.

Install the nut on the pilot shaft and against the collar. Tighten the 
nut against collar until the yoke is completely in position on the shaft. 
Sometimes a torque of 271 Nm (200 lb-ft) on the nut is 
required to install the yoke correctly.

Remove all parts of the pilot tool from the shaft (pilot shaft, collar 
and nut).

Install the washer (if required) and yoke nut on the shaft. Tighten the 
nut to the specified torque.

ADJUSTMENTS

Pinion Bearings Preload Adjustment

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spring Scale

T74P-3504-Y

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T57T-4851-B

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T78P-4851-A

 Specifications 

New pinion bearings .56-5.08 Nm (5-45 lb-in) torque. 

Used pinion bearings in good condition 1.13-3.39 Nm 
(10-30 lb-in) torque. 

 Press Method 

 NOTE: If a press is not available, or the press does not have a pressure 
gauge, use the yoke or flange method to adjust preload. 

Put the drive pinion and retainer assembly in a press, gear head 
(teeth) toward the bottom. 

Install a sleeve of the correct size against the inner race of the 
outer bearing. 

Apply and hold the correct amount of pressure to the pinion bearings. 
Refer to the Pinion Bearing Preload Specifications chart. As pressure is 
applied rotate the bearing retainer several times so that bearings make normal 
contact. 

While pressure is held against the assembly, wind a cord around the 
bearing retainer several times. 

Attach a Spring Scale T74P-3504-Y to the end of the cord. 

 NOTE: Do not read starting torque. Read only the torque value after the 
retainer starts to rotate. Starting torque will give a false reading. 

Pull the cord with scale on a horizontal line. As the bearing retainer 
rotates, read the value indicated on scale. Make a note of reading.

[FIGURE: E5341C.gif]

Measure the diameter of bearing retainer where the cord was wound. 
Measure in inches or centimeters. 

Divide the dimension in half to get the radius. Make a note of radius 
dimension. 

Use the following procedure to calculate the bearing preload (torque).

Pounds pulled x radius (inches) = lb-in preload x .113 = Nm
 preload OR kilograms pulled x radius (centimeters) = kg-cm 
preload x .098 = Nm preload 

Examples: 

Reading from spring scale = 3.4 kg (7.5 lb) 

Diameter of bearing retainer = 16.8 cm (6.62 in) 

Radius of bearing retainer = 8.4 cm (3.31 in) 

7.5 lb x 3.31 in = 24.8 lb-in preload x .113 = 2.8 Nm 
preload OR 

3.4 kg x 8.4 cm = 28.6 kg-cm preload x .098 = 2.8 Nm 
preload 

If the preload (torque) of pinion bearings is not within 
specifications, do the following procedure. Then repeat Steps 1 through 9. 

To increase preload, install a thinner bearing spacer. To decrease 
preload, install a thicker bearing spacer. 

Check the bearing preload with the drive pinion and retainer assembly 
installed in the carrier. Follow the procedures to adjust preload of pinion 
bearings, yoke or flange method.

[FIGURE: DE0367A.gif]

 Yoke or Flange Method 

 CAUTION: Do not install tight fit yokes or flanges on shafts using a hammer or 
mallet. A hammer or mallet will damage the yoke or flange. 

 NOTE: If the fit between the yoke or flange splines and drive pinion splines 
is tight, use a press or three-piece pilot tool to install the yoke or flange. 
Refer to Tight Fit Yoke Installation in Adjustments in this section.

Install the input yoke or flange, nut and washer on the drive pinion. 
The yoke or flange MUST be against the outer bearing. If a press is not 
available, use a suitable three-piece pilot tool for installation as described 
in Tight Fit Yoke Installation in Adjustments in this section.

[FIGURE: E77991A.gif]

Temporarily install the drive pinion and retainer assembly in the 
carrier. Do not install shims under the bearing retainer. 

Install the bearing retainer to carrier capscrews. Washers are not 
required at this time. Tighten the capscrews hand-tight.

[FIGURE: E65931B.gif]

Fasten a yoke or flange bar such as Companion Flange Holding Tool 
T57T-4851-B or T78P-4851-A to the input yoke or flange. The bar will hold the 
drive pinion in position when the nut is tightened. 

Tighten the pinion nut to specifications. Refer to Section 05-02A , 
 Section 05-02B or Section 05-02C .

[FIGURE: E6635E.gif]

Remove the yoke or flange bar. 

Attach a torque wrench on the drive pinion nut. Rotate the drive pinion 
and read the value indicated on torque wrench.

 NOTE: The preload (torque) of pinion bearings can be increased or decreased 
by tightening or loosening the pinion nut within specifications. 

If the preload (torque) of pinion bearings is not within 
specifications, remove the pinion and retainer assembly from carrier. Do the 
following procedure, then repeat Steps 1 through 7. To increase preload, 
install a thinner bearing spacer. To decrease preload, install a thicker 
bearing spacer.

[FIGURE: E78001A.gif]

After adjusting preload of pinion bearings, remove the drive pinion and 
bearing retainer from carrier as described in the appropriate axle section in 
Group 05.

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT STEEL PARTS OR TOOLS WITH A STEEL 
HAMMER. PARTS OR TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

 NOTE: If a press is not available, use a mallet and a suitable sleeve or 
driver to install the seal.

Install a new seal into cover as follows if the carrier has a cover and 
seal assembly over the bearing retainer.

Apply Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B to the seal lips and cavities between lips.

Apply a sealing compound on the outer diameter of seal.

Put the cover in a press, large diameter toward the ram or up.

Support the cover under the small diameter opening with metal or wood 
blocks.

Press the seal into cover until seal is flat against the bottom of 
bore. Use a sleeve or seal driver of the correct size that fits against the 
metal retainer of seal.

[FIGURE: E78011A.gif]

[FIGURE: E78021A.gif]

Install a new triple-lip seal as follows if the pinion seal mounts 
directly into the bearing cage.

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT STEEL PARTS OR TOOLS WITH A STEEL 
HAMMER. PARTS OR TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

 NOTE: If a press is not available, use a mallet and a suitable sleeve or 
driver to install the seal.

Apply Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B to the seal lips and cavities between lips.

Apply axle lubricant to seal bore in bearing retainer.

Put the drive pinion and retainer assembly in a press, seal bore toward 
the ram or up.

[FIGURE: E7803B.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

Shim Pack Thickness Adjustment for Pinion Bearing Retainer

Use this procedure if a new drive pinion and ring gearset is installed, 
or if the depth of the drive pinion has to be adjusted. 

[FIGURE: DE0366A.gif]

Measure the thickness of the old shim pack that was removed from under 
the pinion bearing retainer with a micrometer. Record the measurement for 
later use.

[FIGURE: E78091B.gif]

Look at the pinion cone (PC) variation number on the old drive pinion 
that is being replaced. See Description and Operation, Gearset Information in 
this section, for examples and locations of the number. Record the number for 
later use.

The pinion cone number can be either 1,000ths of an inch or 100ths of a 
millimeter. See the following examples. 

PC+3, PC-3, +3 or -3 equal .003 inch. 

PC+.03, PC-.03 mm, +.03 mm or -.03 equal 
.03 mm. 

To change inches to millimeters, multiply inches by 25.40. 

To change millimeters to inches, multiply millimeters by 0.039.

[FIGURE: E78101A.gif]

 NOTE: The value calculated in Step 3 or 4 is the thickness of the standard 
shim pack, without a variation. 

Subtract the number from the old shim pack thickness that was measured 
in Step 2 if the old pinion cone number is a plus (+). 

If the old pinion cone number is a minus (-), add the number to the old 
shim pack thickness that was measured in Step 2.

Look at the pinion cone (PC) variation number on the new drive pinion 
that will be installed. Record the number for later use. 

 NOTE: The value calculated in Step 6 or 7 is the thickness of the new shim 
pack that will be installed. 

If the new pinion cone number is a plus (+), add the 
number to the standard shim pack thickness that was calculated in Step 3 or 4. 

If the new pinion cone number is a minus (-), subtract the number from 
the standard shim pack thickness that was calculated in Step 3 or 4.

[FIGURE: CE78111B.gif]

Install the drive pinion, bearing retainer and new shim pack into the 
carrier.

ADJUSTMENTS

Slip-Yoke Spline

Vehicle noise and vibration can be caused by a seized driveshaft 
slip-yoke spline resulting in the rubber isolator being pulled out of the 
driveshaft center bearing bracket. 

The service resolution to minimize driveshaft slip yoke spline 
contamination and ultimate seizure is as follows: 

Disconnect the driveshaft from the rear axle yoke and remove it from 
the truck. 

Clean the male splines of the coupling shaft using care not to damage 
the plastic coating. Fine abrasive cloth may be required to dress and polish 
the male spline. Remove all hardened grease deposits, dirt or rust. Inspect 
for worn or galled splines. The plastic coating on the stub spline must not be 
removed. Replace coupling shaft if necessary. 

Clean and inspect the female splines of the driveshaft slip-yoke, 
removing any hardened grease deposits, dirt or rust. Inspect splines for worn 
or galled conditions; replace driveshaft slip-yoke if necessary. 

Apply a coating of High-Temperature 4 x 4 Front Axle and Wheel Bearing 
Grease E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C198-A to 
the entire splined stub end of the coupling shaft prior to the assembling of 
the driveshaft to the coupling shaft. 

Using a clean, long-handle (stencil-type) brush, apply High-Temperature 
4 x 4 Front Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M1C198-A spread evenly on all the female splines of the 
slip-yoke. The spline joint must slide freely by hand. 

Assemble the driveshaft to the coupling shaft with the yokes phased 
properly. Attach driveshaft to rear axle yoke. 

Using a hand-type grease gun, lubricate the driveshaft slip-yoke 
through the zerk fitting with High-Temperature 4 x 4 Front Axle and Wheel 
Bearing Grease E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C198-A.

LUBRICATION

Axle Lubrication, Rear

The ability of any rear axle to deliver quiet, trouble-free operation 
over a period of years is largely dependent upon the use of good quality gear 
lubricants. To make sure gears and bearings will last as long as possible, use 
only specified hypoid gear lubricants.

For more information on recommended fluid changes, types of fluids and 
capacities, refer to Specifications .

PAGE 4551
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 05-00: Axle and Driveshaft, Service

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

LUBRICATION

Draining and Filling

Remove the drainplug from bottom of axle housing and drain lubricant 
from the assembly.

Fill the axle with the specified lubricant according to the following 
procedure. 

Make sure the vehicle is parked on a level surface. When the angle of 
the drive pinion changes, the lubricant capacity of the axle will change. 

Install drainplug. Tighten to 47 Nm (35 lb-ft).

Remove the fill plug from the side of the bowl cover of the axle 
housing. 

[FIGURE: E79111B.gif]

Put the specified axle lubricant in through the fill plug hole. Fill 
the axle with lubricant until the lubricant level is to the bottom of the fill 
plug hole. See the Lubricant Specifications and Capacities under 
Specifications in this section for the specified axle lubricant. 

Install the fill plug and tighten to a minimum torque of 47 Nm
 (35 lb-ft). When correctly installed, one complete thread 
of the fill plug is visible. 

Drive the vehicle in an unloaded condition for 1.6-3.2 km (1-2 miles) 
at speeds not more than 40 km/h (25 mph). Operating the vehicle makes sure 
that the lubricant flows through the complete axle assembly.

LUBRICATION

U-Joints 

Apply High-Temperature 4x4 Front Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease 
E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C198-A through the 
zerk fitting until fresh lubricant purges at each of the four seals. This 
flushes abrasive contaminants from each bearing and assures all four bearings 
are filled properly. 

Move the driveshaft from side to side while applying gun pressure if 
any seal fails to purge. This allows greater clearance on the thrust end of 
the bearing that is not purging.

[FIGURE: E67771A.gif]

 CAUTION: After lubricating, make sure that the bearing caps are firmly in place, 
and that the restraining bolts are tightened per specifications. 

If seal still will not purge, release seal tension by removing the 
bearing straps or loosening the bearing cap bolts and backing off the bearing 
cap assembly approximately 1.6 mm (1/16 inch). 

[FIGURE: E67781A.gif]

================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 05-00: Axle and Driveshaft, Service

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

LUBRICATION

Slip-Yoke 

Apply High-Temperature 4x4 Front Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease 
E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C198-A through the 
zerk fitting until the lubricant appears at the pressure relief hole in the 
welch plug at the slip-yoke end of the spline.

[FIGURE: E6779C.gif]

After the lubricant appears at the pressure relief hole, cover the hole 
with finger and continue to apply grease gun pressure until grease appears at 
the slip-yoke seal.

[FIGURE: E6780D.gif]

Section 05-01: Driveshaft

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Driveshaft

The driveshaft or coupling shaft is composed of the universal joints 
(U-joints), connecting shafts and the attaching yokes.

All the vehicle U-joints and sliding splines are equipped with 
lubrication fittings. They should be lubricated periodically with 
High-Temperature 4x4 Front Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease E8TZ-19590-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C198-A.

The vehicles are equipped with center support bearings that are 
prelubricated and sealed for the life of the bearing. 

 NOTE: All driveline shafts are balanced. If a vehicle is to be undercoated, 
cover all shafts to prevent getting undercoating material on the shafts.

Vehicles have the following types of driveshafts: 

Driveshaft — The shaft that accommodates the change in 
length (slip) in the driveline system. The driveshaft is the shaft that is the 
input to the rear axle. 

Coupling shaft — All shafts that connect the 
transmission to the rear axle, except the driveshaft. Coupling shafts are 
attached to a support plate via a shaft support bearing. 

Interaxle shaft — The shaft that connects the forward 
axle of a tandem drive unit to the rear axle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Driveshaft, Rear 

 Removal 

Disconnect driveshaft from yoke at rear axle. 

If working on a vehicle with a coupling shaft spline, slide driveshaft 
off coupling shaft splines. Otherwise, disconnect driveshaft from yoke at rear 
of transmission. Unscrew grease seal on slip-yoke spline and separate 
driveshaft from slip-yoke spline.

Working from center support nearest to rear of vehicle, remove two 
retaining bolts and support bearing. To remove center support bearing, remove 
nut that retains the yoke (behind the bearing) and remove the yoke.

Remove forward joint from mating yoke. 

Repeat Steps 3 and 4 until last shaft has been removed. 

Thoroughly clean old grease and dirt from driveshaft splines, and then 
check splines for wear, warpage and cracks. If shaft is worn, warped or 
cracked, replace it. 

Using a suitable cleaning fluid, clean all dirt from slip-yoke, 
slip-yoke splines, and shaft splines. Carefully inspect the slip-yoke splines 
for wear or evidence of twisting. Check clearance between the slip-yoke 
splines and shaft splines. 

Wash all parts except the sealed ball bearing and rubber cushion in 
suitable cleaning fluid. Do not immerse the sealed bearing in cleaning fluid. 
Wipe bearing and cushion clean with a cloth dampened with cleaning fluid. 

Check bearing for wear or rough action by rotating inner race while 
holding outer race. If wear or roughness is evident, replace bearing. Grease 
retainers and slingers are serviced only as part of the bearing assembly.

Examine rubber cushion for evidence of hardening, cracking or 
deterioration. Replace cushion if damaged in any way. 

 Installation 

Connect front joint of driveshaft or coupling shaft to yoke on 
transmission. Tighten nuts or bolts to specification listed at the end of this 
section. 

Install center bearing and yoke, if removed (if so equipped). Secure 
center bearing to frame crossmember or bracket with center support, bolts and 
nuts (if so equipped). Tighten nuts to specification listed at the end of this 
section. Make sure that center bearing is not twisted in support plate. 

If working on a vehicle with more than one coupling shaft, connect rear 
shaft to forward shaft. Install remaining center support. 

Connect slip-yoke spline to driveshaft and hand-tighten grease seal 
firmly on slip-yoke spline. Use zerk fitting in slip-yoke spline to lube 
spline with High-Temperature 4x4 Front Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease 
E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C198-A.

Connect rear U-joint to rear axle yoke. Tighten nuts or bolts to 
specification listed at the end of this section. Be sure all driveshaft and 
coupling shaft yokes are properly in phase.

================================================================================
PAGE 4560
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 05-01: Driveshaft

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Universal Joint, Plate-Type

 Removal 

Bend the tangs of the lock plates away from the bolts.

Remove the bolts and lock plates that attach the bearing caps to the 
U-joint flange. Discard lock plates. Remove the plate-type bearing caps and 
needle bearings from the flange and spider. Use Spicer U-Joint Tool 
D79T-4635-A or equivalent.

If the bearing and cap are integral, tap bearing cap lightly clockwise 
and, with a screwdriver, pry under first one end of the bearing cap and then 
the other until the bearing cap comes out of yoke. Turn joint over and remove 
the opposite bearing cap in the same manner. If bearing cap and bearing are 
separate, bearing cap will come off with a light tap. 

Remove bearings by first tapping with a soft round drift on the exposed 
face of one bearing until the opposite bearing cap comes out. Turn joint over 
and tap the exposed end of journal cross pin until the opposite bearing cap is 
free. 

Remove grease seal and retainer from cap. Remove the needle bearings 
from bearing cap bore. 

Remove spider. All burrs on bearing cap or yoke must be removed before 
replacing the spider in yoke. 

Wash all parts in cleaning fluid. Make sure the lubricant passages in 
the journal cross are clean. Check needle bearings and journals for evidence 
of wear or damage from excessive heat. 

Soak the needle bearings in a commercial cleaning fluid to soften 
particles of hardened grease. Then, wash these parts in cleaning fluid using 
stiff brush if necessary to remove all old lubricant. Check each bearing for 
missing rollers. Replace the U-joint if any of the rollers are missing.

After needle bearing assemblies are thoroughly clean, apply clean 
lubricant to the rollers. Rotate them on the trunnion of journal to check 
wear. Before reassembly, fill the journal passages with High-Temperature 4x4 
Front Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C198-A and fill bearings approximately one-third full of 
the same lubricant. 

[FIGURE: E6784B.gif]

 Installation 

Position needle bearings in the bearing caps and install grease seal 
retainer and seal on cap. 

Position spider in the yoke and install bearing caps through yoke and 
onto spider. Press or tap with a soft drift. 

Position lock plates to bearing caps and secure them with the bolts. 
Tighten bolts to specification listed at end of this section. Bend the tangs 
of the locks up against the bolt heads, if so equipped. Bolts with serrations 
under the head do not use lock plates.

 NOTE: When lubricating U-joints, apply lubricant through zerk fitting until 
fresh grease purges at each of the four seals. When lubricating slip-yoke, 
apply lubricant through zerk fitting until it purges at the vent hole in the 
welch plug. Place finger over hole in welch plug and apply lubricant until it 
purges at the seal at rear of slip-yoke. 

Lubricate U-joints through zerk fitting with High-Temperature 4x4 Front 
Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C198-A.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Universal Joint, Bolt-Type

 Removal 

Remove the four bolts that retain the two bearing straps in the yoke. 
Remove straps from yoke.

Remove cross from yoke. 

 NOTE: Repeat above steps on opposite end of driveshaft assembly. 

Remove second bearing from yoke lug.

Remove grease seals from caps and remove needle bearings. 

[FIGURE: E67851A.gif]

Wash all parts in cleaning fluid. Make sure lubricant passages in 
journal cross are clean. Check the needle bearings and journals for evidence 
of wear or damage from excessive heat. 

Soak needle bearings in a commercial cleaning fluid to soften particles 
of hardened grease. Wash these parts in cleaning fluid using a stiff brush, if 
necessary, to remove all old lubricant. Check each bearing for missing 
rollers. If a roller is found to be missing, replace entire U-joint. 

After needle bearing assemblies are thoroughly clean, apply clean 
lubricant to rollers. Rotate them on trunnion of the journal to check wear.

Before assembly, fill journal passages with High-Temperature 4x4 Front 
Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C198-A. Fill bearing caps approximately one-third full 
with same lubricant.

[FIGURE: E67931A.gif]

[FIGURE: E67941A.gif]

 Installation 

Insert needle bearings in cap bore. Install grease seal. 

Put small amount of recommended grease into each outside diameter of 
bearing race assemblies, if not already done. Refer to Step 8 of Removal 
procedure. 

When assembling journal cross to slip-yoke and/or weld-yoke, position 
zerk so that it is to inside of yoke lugs and in same orientation as slip-yoke 
zerk. 

Place journal cross in yoke opening so that yoke nubs retain bearing 
caps. 

Place bearing straps over caps and install two bolts through each strap 
into yoke. 

Tighten bolts to specification listed at the end of this section.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Standard Single Reduction Carriers 

The single reduction carriers are front-mounted into the axle housing. 
These carriers have a hypoid drive pinion and ring gearset and bevel gears in 
the differential assembly. 

A straight roller bearing (spigot or pilot) is mounted on the head of 
the drive pinion. All other bearings in the carrier are tapered roller 
bearings. 

When the carrier operates, there is normal differential action between 
the wheels all the time.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Axle Speed Sensor, Anti-Lock Brake System

Speed sensors are multi-point, variable reluctance devices that provide 
individual wheel speed data at a 100 pulse per wheel revolution, resulting in 
high-quality output signals.

The sensor is used in the anti-lock brake system (ABS) to monitor and 
report individual wheel speeds to the ABS electronic controller.

There are two sensor assemblies in each differential carrier. The speed 
sensors are mounted in each differential bearing adjusting ring.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Axle Speed Sensor

 WARNING: HYDROGEN AND OXYGEN GASES ARE PRODUCED DURING NORMAL BATTERY OPERATION. 
THIS GAS MIXTURE CAN EXPLODE IF FLAMES, SPARKS OR LIGHTED TOBACCO ARE BROUGHT 
NEAR THE BATTERY. WHEN CHARGING OR USING A BATTERY IN AN ENCLOSED SPACE, 
ALWAYS PROVIDE VENTILATION AND SHIELD YOUR EYES. 

 WARNING: KEEP BATTERIES OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. BATTERIES CONTAIN SULFURIC 
ACID. AVOID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES OR CLOTHING. ALSO, SHIELD YOUR EYES WHEN 
WORKING NEAR THE BATTERY TO PROTECT AGAINST POSSIBLE SPLASHING OF THE ACID 
SOLUTION. IN CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH THE SKIN, EYES OR CLOTHING, FLUSH 
IMMEDIATELY WITH WATER FOR A MINIMUM OF FIFTEEN MINUTES. IF ACID IS SWALLOWED, 
DRINK LARGE QUANTITIES OF MILK OR WATER, FOLLOWED BY MILK OF MAGNESIA, A 
BEATEN EGG, OR VEGETABLE OIL. CALL A PHYSICIAN IMMEDIATELY. 

 Removal 

Disconnect the ground cable from the battery.

 CAUTION: Do not disconnect the sensor plug from the receptacle by pulling the 
wiring harness. Damage to the plug will occur and cause an open circuit. 
Always disconnect the sensor by pulling the plug housing. 

Disconnect the left-hand and right-hand sensor plugs from the 
receptacles. Grasp the plug, press the lock tab on the top of the plug housing 
and pull the plug from the receptacle.

[FIGURE: E9272A.gif]

Remove the rear axle differential carrier. Refer to Differential 
Carrier in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

With snap ring pliers, remove the snap ring that holds the speed sensor 
in the adjusting ring of the differential bearing.

[FIGURE: E9275A.gif]

 CAUTION: When you pry out the speed sensor from the bearing adjusting ring, 
always position the screwdrivers under the two metal tabs. Do not pry out the 
sensor from the plastic coil housing; damage to the coil will occur. 

Pry the speed sensor loose, but do not completely remove it from the 
bearing adjusting ring. Use two screwdrivers to pry the sensor at the two 
opposite tabs.

[FIGURE: E9476B.gif]

Both sensor receptacles are mounted through bores in the flange of the 
carrier. Using two screwdrivers, pry the snap ring out of the groove in both 
the left-hand and right-hand sensor receptacles.

[FIGURE: E9477A.gif]

Remove the receptacle from the differential carrier flange by pushing 
the receptacle from the outside surface of the flange toward the inside 
surface of the carrier. If the receptacle cannot be removed using this 
procedure, position a small block of wood against the receptacle and tap the 
block with a leather or plastic mallet until the receptacle is removed from 
the carrier flange.

[FIGURE: E9273A.gif]

 CAUTION: When removing the speed sensor assembly from the bearing adjusting 
ring, do not drop the assembly; damage to the components can occur. 

Completely remove the speed sensor assembly by pulling it out from the 
bearing adjusting ring.

[FIGURE: E9274A.gif]

Remove the wave washer from inside the bore of the bearing adjusting 
ring.

[FIGURE: E9478A.gif]

 NOTE: Removal of the drive tubes from the differential case halves is not a 
requirement to remove the speed sensors. Remove the drive tubes from the case 
halves only if required due to damaged parts.

Remove and disassemble the differential and ring gear assembly. Refer 
to Differential and Ring Gear, Disassembly in the Disassembly and Assembly 
portion of this section.

[FIGURE: E9479A.gif]

Using a screwdriver, remove the snap ring that holds the drive tube in 
position inside the differential case half.

[FIGURE: E9480A.gif]

Lift out the backup washer that is behind the snap ring, inside the 
differential case half.

[FIGURE: E9481A.gif]

Pull the drive tube out from the bearing side of the differential case 
half.

[FIGURE: E9482B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

—

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not use cleaning solvents to clean the speed sensor assembly. Damage 
to components can occur. Clean the speed sensor assembly only with a clean dry 
rag or paper towel. 

 NOTE: If the drive tube was not removed, omit Steps 1 and 2.

Install the drive tube into the differential case half from the bearing 
side.

While holding the drive tube in position, place the backup washer over 
the drive tube and against the inside of the differential case half. Install 
the snap ring into the groove in the drive tube, using a screwdriver if 
necessary.

[FIGURE: E9481A.gif]

[FIGURE: E9480A.gif]

Assemble differential and ring gear assembly. Refer to Differential and 
Ring Gear, Assembly in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section.

Install differential and ring gear assembly. Refer to Differential and 
Ring Gear, Assembly , Installation in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of 
this section.

Before installing the speed sensor assembly and components into the 
bearing adjusting ring, check the position of the roll pin that locks the 
adjusting ring in place. The speed sensor cannot be correctly installed if the 
roll pin extends beyond the snap ring groove in the lugs of the adjusting 
ring. Adjust the position of the roll pin if necessary by using a drift and 
hammer.

[FIGURE: E9483A.gif]

Check the outside of the speed sensor receptacle. There must be an 
O-ring positioned in the first groove. Install an O-ring if necessary.

[FIGURE: E9484A.gif]

Install the speed sensor by pushing the receptacle through the large 
hole in the carrier flange. Push from the inside of the flange toward the 
outside surface.

Apply and hold pressure against the back of the receptacle and install 
the snap ring into the first full groove that appears past the outside surface 
of the carrier flange. Using needle nose pliers, install the snap ring. 
Temporarily rest the sensor on the inside flange of the carrier.

[FIGURE: E9485A.gif]

Install the wave washer inside the bore of the bearing adjusting ring.

[FIGURE: E9486A.gif]

Apply axle lubricant to the outer surface of the drive tube and on the 
drive seal of the speed sensor.

[FIGURE: E9487A.gif]

Install the speed sensors in the bearing adjusting rings. The wire 
outlet area of the coil of each sensor must face out and align with the 
correct slot in the bearing adjusting ring.

[FIGURE: E9488A.gif]

[FIGURE: E9489A.gif]

Place the speed sensor over the bearing adjusting ring with the wire 
outlet area of the coil in correct position as shown. Turn the rotor in the 
sensor until the tabs align with the slots in the drive tube.

[FIGURE: E9490B.gif]

 CAUTION: The speed sensor must be installed carefully and evenly into the bore 
of the bearing adjusting ring or damage to the sensor can occur. 

Press the speed sensor evenly into the bore of the bearing adjusting 
ring manually, while carefully sliding the drive seal over the drive tube. 
Make sure the wire outlet area of the coil freely enters the selected slot in 
the bearing adjusting ring. Use even pressure around the sensor, near the 
outer diameter, until the sensor is seated against the wave washer.

If the drive seal slips off the rotor of the speed sensor, remove the 
speed sensor from the bearing adjusting ring. Place the drive seal in position 
on the rotor and repeat Steps 10 and 11.

Press the speed sensor down into the bearing adjusting ring so that the 
top of the sensor is past the snap ring grooves in the lugs. Hold the sensor 
in this position.

Place the snap ring over the speed sensor with the opening aligned with 
the wire outlet area of the coil housing. Start by placing one end of the snap 
ring in the groove close to the wire outlet area of the coil. Apply even 
pressure around the sensor and install the snap ring into the grooves in the 
lugs of the adjusting ring. Use snap ring pliers or a screwdriver, if 
necessary, to install the snap ring.

[FIGURE: E9491B.gif]

The sensor should be positioned firmly and evenly against the snap 
ring. If it is not, apply hand pressure to the sensor, depressing it against 
the wave washer until sensor alignment is obtained.

After the sensor is installed, make sure the outlet wires of the sensor 
are as close to the carrier leg as possible to make sure the wires are not 
pinched when the carrier is installed in the axle housing.

Install differential carrier into axle housing. Refer to Differential 
Carrier in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Refer to Section 06-09 for diagnostic and service procedures for the 
anti-lock brake system.

Section 05-02A: Axle, Rockwell Single-Speed

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Differential Carrier 

 Removal 

 WARNING: DO NOT WORK UNDER THE VEHICLE IF IT IS SUPPORTED BY JACKS OR LIFTING 
TOOLS ONLY. JACKS AND LIFTING TOOLS CAN SLIP AND CAUSE INJURY. 

 NOTE: If the rear rear axle of the tandem axle is being serviced and if it is 
equipped with a driver-controlled main differential lock, refer to Main 
Differential Lock in Section 05-02C before performing any service procedures. 

Raise the vehicle.

[FIGURE: E77601A.gif]

Put jack stands under each spring seat of the axle to hold vehicle in 
the raised position. 

Remove the plug from bottom of axle housing and drain lubricant from 
the assembly. 

Disconnect the driveline universal joint from the pinion input yoke or 
flange on the carrier.

[FIGURE: E77611A.gif]

Remove the capscrews and washers or stud nuts and washers from the 
flanges of both axle shafts.

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT THE ROUND DRIVING LUGS ON THE HEAD 
OF AXLE SHAFTS. LUGS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

Loosen the tapered dowels in the flanges of both axle shafts as 
follows. (Some Rockwell axles are not equipped with tapered dowels.) 

Hold a 1-1/2-inch diameter brass drift against the center of the axle 
shaft, inside the circular driving lugs. (A 1-1/2-inch diameter brass hammer 
can be used as a drift.) 

 CAUTION: Do not use a chisel or wedge to loosen the axle shafts and dowels. The 
chisel or wedge can damage the hub, axle shafts and, if used, oil seals. 
Hit the end of the drift with a large hammer (five to six pounds), and 
the axle shaft and tapered dowels will loosen.

[FIGURE: E51311A.gif]

Remove the tapered dowels and both axle shafts from the axle assembly.

Place a Rotunda Heavy Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or 
equivalent under the differential carrier to support the assembly.

[FIGURE: E77621A.gif]

Remove all but the top two differential carrier-to-housing capscrews or 
stud nuts and washers. 

Loosen the top two differential carrier-to-housing fasteners and leave 
attached to the assembly. The fasteners will hold the differential carrier in 
the housing. 

Loosen the differential carrier in the axle housing. Use a leather 
mallet to hit the mounting flange of carrier at several points.

 NOTE: Some differential carrier models have threaded puller screw holes in 
the mounting flange. Puller screws can be used to loosen and pull the 
differential carrier from the axle housing. If puller screws are used, clean 
the threaded holes before the puller screws are installed. 

Remove the top two fasteners after the differential carrier is loosened. 

 CAUTION: When using a pry bar, be careful not to damage the carrier or housing 
flange. Damage to these surfaces will cause oil leaks. 

Remove the carrier from the axle housing carefully, using the hydraulic 
roller jack.

Lift the differential carrier by the input yoke or flange and put the 
assembly in a suitable repair stand. Use a lifting tool for this procedure. Do 
not lift by hand.

[FIGURE: E7083D.gif]

 Installation 

 WARNING: BE CAREFUL WHEN USING CLEANING SOLVENTS. FOLLOW THE SOLVENT 
MANUFACTURER'S INSTRUCTIONS FOR SAFE USE TO PREVENT INJURY. 

Clean the inside of rear axle housing and the mounting surface where 
the differential carrier fastens. Use a cleaning solvent and rags to remove 
dirt. Blow dry the cleaned areas with air. Refer to Section 05-00 for cleaning 
and inspection procedures. 

Inspect the axle housing for damage. Service or replace the axle 
housing. Refer to Section 05-00 for cleaning and inspection procedures. 

Check for loose studs in the mounting surface of the housing where the 
differential carrier fastens. Remove and clean the studs that are loose. (Some 
Rockwell axles are equipped with capscrews and some are equipped with stud 
nuts.) 

Apply liquid adhesive to the threaded holes and install the studs into 
the rear axle housing. Refer to Section 05-00 . 

Apply silicone gasket material to the mounting surface of the rear axle 
housing where the carrier fastens. Refer to Section 05-00 .

[FIGURE: E77631A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not install the carriers using a hammer or mallet. A hammer or 
mallet will damage the mounting flange of carrier and cause oil leaks. 

Install the differential carrier into the rear axle housing, using 
Rotunda Heavy Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or equivalent. 

Install nuts and washers or capscrews and washers in the four corner 
locations around the differential carrier and rear axle housing. Tighten the 
fasteners hand-tight at this time.

[FIGURE: E77641A.gif]

Push the differential carrier into position. Tighten the four fasteners 
two or three turns each in a pattern opposite each other. 

Repeat Step 8 until the four fasteners are tightened to the correct 
torque value. Refer to the Specifications portion of this section. 

Install the other fasteners and washers that hold the carrier in the 
rear axle housing and tighten to the correct torque value. Refer to the Specifications 
 portion of this section. 

Connect the driveline universal joint to the pinion input yoke or 
flange on the carrier. 

Install the gaskets and axle shafts into the rear axle housing and 
carrier. The gasket and flange of the axle shafts must fit flat against the 
wheel hub. 

Install the capscrews and washers that hold the axle shaft to the wheel 
hub. Tighten capscrews to the correct torque value as listed under Torque 
Specifications at the end of this section. 

[FIGURE: E7765B.gif]

Install the tapered dowels at each stud, if equipped, and into the 
flange of the axle shaft. Use a punch or drift and hammer if needed.

Install the nuts and washers on the studs. Tighten nuts to the correct 
torque value. Refer to the Specifications portion of this section. 

Fill rear axle with specified lubricant. Refer to Section 05-00 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Yokes, Tight Fit

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not install tight fit yokes on shafts using a hammer or mallet. A 
hammer or mallet will damage the yoke. 

 CAUTION: Do not use the assembly yoke nut for installation purposes. Use the nut 
that is supplied with the three-piece pilot tool. 

 NOTE: The installation tool can be purchased from Kent-Moore Tool Division, 
29784 Little Mack, Roseville, Mich. 48066, or can be made from drawings 
available from the Technical Communications Dept., Rockwell International, 
2135 W. Maple, Troy, Mich. 48084.

Apply axle lubricant on the yoke seal.

Check all surfaces of the yoke hub for damage. If necessary, polish the 
yoke hub with an india stone, emery cloth or crocus cloth.

Install the pilot shaft on the input shaft of the assembly.

[FIGURE: E37301B.gif]

Slide the yoke over the installation shaft. Align the yoke splines with 
the input shaft splines.

Put the collar on the pilot shaft and slide it against the yoke.

Install the nut on the pilot shaft and against the collar. Tighten the 
nut against collar until the yoke is completely in position on the shaft. 
Sometimes a torque value of 271 Nm (200 lb-ft) on the nut is 
required to install the yoke correctly.

Remove all parts of the pilot tool from the shaft (pilot shaft, collar 
and nut).

Install the washer (if required) and yoke nut on the shaft. Tighten the 
nut to the specified torque. Refer to the Specifications portion of this 
section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Differential and Ring Gear, Disassembly

 Removal 

Before starting work on the differential carrier, inspect the hypoid 
gearset for damage. If the inspection shows no damage, the same gearset can be 
used again. Measure the backlash of the gearset using a Dial Indicator with 
Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent, and make a note of the dimension. Adjust 
the backlash to the same dimension after the gearset is installed into the 
differential carrier. For more information on ring gear backlash, refer to 
 Section 05-00 . 

[FIGURE: E5348D.gif]

Loosen the jam nut on the thrust screw. 

Remove the thrust screw and jam nut from the differential carrier. 
(Some Rockwell axles are not equipped with thrust screws.) Some Rockwell 
carrier models have a thrust block. The thrust block will fall away from the 
ring gear inside the carrier when you remove the thrust screw. 

[FIGURE: E77681A.gif]

Rotate the differential carrier in the repair stand until the ring gear 
is at the top of the assembly. 

Mark one rear axle differential carrier leg and bearing cap for the 
purpose of correctly matching the parts when you assemble the carrier. A 
center punch and hammer can be used to mark the parts.

[FIGURE: E77691A.gif]

Remove the cotter keys, pins or lock plates that hold the two bearing 
adjusting rings in position. Use a small drift and hammer to remove pins. Each 
lock plate is held in position by two capscrews.

[FIGURE: E77701A.gif]

Remove the capscrews and washers that hold the two bearing caps on the 
differential carrier. Each cap is held in position by two capscrews and washers.

[FIGURE: E65591B.gif]

Remove the bearing caps and bearing adjusting rings from the 
differential carrier.

[FIGURE: E7771B.gif]

Using Endless Lifting Sling D87L-1000-A or equivalent, lift the main 
differential and ring gear assembly from the differential carrier. Put the 
assembly on a workbench. 

Remove the thrust block, if so equipped, from inside the differential 
carrier.

[FIGURE: E7772B.gif]

 Disassembly 

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT STEEL PARTS WITH A STEEL HAMMER. 
PARTS OR TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

Mark each case half with a center punch and hammer, if the matching 
marks on the case halves of the differential assembly are not visible. The 
purpose of the marks is to match the plain half and flange half correctly when 
you assemble the carrier.

[FIGURE: E77731A.gif]

Remove the lockwire capscrews and washers or bolts, nuts and washers 
that hold the case halves together.

Separate the case halves. If necessary, use a brass, plastic or leather 
mallet to loosen the parts. 

Remove the differential spider (cross), four pinion gears, two side 
gears and six thrust washers from inside the case halves.

In some assemblies, the hub length of one side gear is longer than the 
other. Note in which case half the respective hub length side gears are to be 
reassembled later. 

[FIGURE: E7774D.gif]

Remove the bolts, nuts and washers that hold the gear to the flange 
case half if the ring gear needs to be replaced. 

Remove the rivets as follows if rivets hold the ring gear to the flange 
case half. 

 CAUTION: Do not remove the rivets or rivet heads with a chisel and hammer. The 
chisel can damage the flange case half. 
Centerpunch each rivet head in the center, on the ring gear side of the 
assembly. 

Drill each rivet head on the ring gear side of the assembly to a depth 
equal to the thickness of one rivet head. Use a drill bit that is 1/32 inch 
smaller than the body diameter of the rivets.

[FIGURE: E77751A.gif]

Press the rivets through holes in the ring gear and flange case half. 
Press from the drilled rivet head.

Separate the case half and ring gear using a press. Support the 
assembly under the ring gear with metal or wood blocks and press the case half 
through the gear.

[FIGURE: E7776C.gif]

Remove the bearing cones from the case halves, if the differential 
bearings need to be replaced. Use a bearing puller or press.

[FIGURE: E77771A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Drive Pinion, Bearing Retainer and Shim Pack Carrier, Removal

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T57T-4851-B

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T78P-4851-A

Fasten a yoke or flange bar such as Companion Flange Holding Tool 
T57T-4851-B or T78P-4851-A to the input yoke or flange. The bar will hold the 
drive pinion in position when the nut is removed. 

Remove the nut and washer, if so equipped, from the drive pinion. 

Remove the yoke or flange bar.

[FIGURE: E77781A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use a hammer or mallet to loosen and remove the yoke or flange. 
A hammer or mallet can damage the parts and cause runout or alignment 
problems. 

Remove the yoke or flange from the drive pinion. If the yoke or flange 
is tight on the pinion, use Gear and Pulley Puller D80L-522-A or equivalent 
for removal.

[FIGURE: E7779B.gif]

Remove the capscrews and washers that hold the rear axle pinion bearing 
retainer in the carrier.

[FIGURE: E7780B.gif]

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT STEEL PARTS WITH A STEEL HAMMER. 
PARTS OR TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

Remove the cover and seal assembly and gasket from the rear axle pinion 
bearing retainer. If the cover is tight on the bearing cage, use a brass drift 
and hammer for removal. 

 NOTE: If the carrier does not have a cover and seal assembly, the pinion seal 
will be mounted in the outer bore of the rear axle pinion bearing retainer. 
Remove the seal after the drive pinion is removed from the rear axle pinion 
bearing retainer. 

Remove the seal from the cover if the pinion seal is damaged. Use a 
press and sleeve or seal driver. If a press is not available, use a 
screwdriver or small pry bar for removal. Discard the pinion seal.

[FIGURE: E7781B.gif]

Remove the drive pinion, bearing retainer and shims from the carrier. 
If the bearing retainer is tight in the carrier, use the following procedures 
to loosen the retainer.

[FIGURE: E7782C.gif]

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT STEEL PARTS WITH A STEEL HAMMER. 
PARTS OR TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

 CAUTION: Do not use a pry bar to remove the bearing retainer from the carrier. A 
pry bar can damage the bearing retainer, shims and carrier. 
Hit the bearing retainer at several points around the flange area with 
a leather, plastic or rubber mallet. 

Some bearing retainers have threaded puller screw holes in the mounting 
flange. Puller screws can be used to loosen and pull a tightly fitted retainer 
from the carrier. If puller screws are used, clean the threaded holes before 
the puller screws are installed.

[FIGURE: DE0356A.gif]

Keep the shims together for use later when the carrier is assembled, if 
the shims are in good condition. 

Measure the total thickness of the pack if the shims are to be 
discarded because of damage. Make a note of the dimension. The dimension will 
be needed to calculate the depth of the drive pinion in the carrier when the 
gearset is installed.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Drive Pinion and Bearing Retainer 

 Disassembly 

Put the drive pinion and bearing retainer in a press. The pinion shaft 
must be toward the top of the assembly.

[FIGURE: DE0370A.gif]

Item

Bearing Spacer

Support the bearing retainer under the flange area with metal or wood 
blocks. 

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT STEEL PARTS WITH A STEEL HAMMER. 
PARTS OR TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

Press the drive pinion through the bearing retainer. The inner bearing 
cone and bearing spacer or spacers will remain on the pinion shaft. 

[FIGURE: E7784F.gif]

Item

Part Number

1
