Rear Axle Differential Pinion Pilot Bearing

Use a leather, plastic or rubber mallet to drive the pinion through the 
bearing retainer, if a press is not available.

 CAUTION: Be careful when using a screwdriver or pry bar to remove the seal. Do 
not damage the wall of bore. Damage to the bore can cause oil leaks. 

Remove the seal if it is mounted directly in the outer bore of the 
bearing retainer. Use a screwdriver or small pry bar for removal. After the 
seal is removed, lift the outer bearing cone from the retainer.

[FIGURE: DE0357A.gif]

Remove the inner and outer bearing cups from the inside of retainer if 
the pinion bearings need to be replaced. Use a press and sleeve, bearing 
puller or a small drift and hammer. The type of tool used depends on the 
design of the bearing retainer. When a press is used, support the bearing 
retainer under the flange area with metal or wood blocks.

[FIGURE: E77861A.gif]

Remove the inner bearing cone from the drive pinion with a press or 
Bearing Pulling Attachment D79L-4621-A or equivalent if the pinion bearing 
needs to be replaced. The puller must fit under the inner race of the cone to 
remove the cone correctly.

[FIGURE: E6583E.gif]

Put the drive pinion in a vise if the pilot bearing needs to be 
replaced. Install a soft metal cover over each vise jaw to protect the drive 
pinion. 

 NOTE: Some pilot bearings are fastened to the drive pinion with a special 
peening tool. For information about the peen tool write Rockwell International 
Communications Department, 2135 West Maple Road, Troy, Michigan 48084. A peen 
tool, part number J-26883, is available from Kent-Moore, Heavy-Duty Division, 
29784 Little Mack, Roseville, Michigan 48066-2298.

Remove the snap ring, if so equipped, from the end of drive pinion with 
snap ring pliers that expand.

[FIGURE: E7787D.gif]

Remove the pilot bearing from the drive pinion with a suitable bearing 
puller.

[FIGURE: E65841A.gif]

If the pilot bearing is a two-piece assembly, remove the inner race 
from the pinion with a bearing pulling attachment. Remove the outer 
race/roller assembly from carrier with a drift or a press. 

[FIGURE: E77891A.gif]

 Assembly 

Put the bearing cage in Rotunda Hydraulic Press 014-00021 or equivalent.

[FIGURE: E7790C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

4614

Rear Axle Pinion Bearing Retainer

2

—

Press (Part of 014-00021)

3

—

Sleeve (Part of 014-00021)

4

4616

Differential Bearing Cup

5

—

Supports (Part of 014-00021)

Support the bearing retainer with metal or wood blocks. 

 NOTE: Use the same procedure for both bearing cups. 

Press the bearing cup into the bore of bearing cage until cup is flat 
against bottom of bore. Use a sleeve of the correct size to install bearing cup.

Put the drive pinion in a press, gear head (teeth) toward the bottom. 

Press the inner bearing cone on the shaft of the drive pinion until the 
cone is flat against the gear head. Use a sleeve of the correct size against 
the bearing inner race.

[FIGURE: E65871B.gif]

 NOTE: Some pilot bearings are fastened to the drive pinion with a snap ring, 
some are fastened with a peening tool, and some are a two-piece bearing 
assembly with the inner race pressed on the nose of the pinion and the outer 
race pressed into its bore in the carrier. 

Refer to the following steps if pilot bearing being serviced is 
one-piece design. 

Put the drive pinion in a press, gear head (teeth) toward the top. 

Press the pilot bearing on the end of drive pinion until the bearing is 
flat against the gear head. Use a sleeve of the correct size against the 
bearing inner race.

[FIGURE: E65881B.gif]

 NOTE: If no snap ring or snap ring groove is present, refer to Step 7. For 
two-piece pilot bearing assemblies, refer to Step 8.

Install the snap ring, if so equipped, into groove in end of drive 
pinion with snap ring pliers.

[FIGURE: E7791B.gif]

 NOTE: Some pilot bearings are fastened to the drive pinion with a special 
peening tool. For information about the peen tool write Rockwell International 
Communications Department, 2135 West Maple Road, Troy, Michigan 48084. A peen 
tool, part number J-26883, is available from Kent-Moore, Heavy-Duty Division, 
29784 Little Mack, Roseville, Michigan 48066-2298.

If pilot bearing is held in place by peening the end of the drive 
pinion, refer to the following procedure. 

[FIGURE: E77921A.gif]

Apply 3,000 kg (6,614 pounds) pressure on a 10-mm (0.375-inch) ball. 

Peen the end of drive pinion at a minimum of five points. 

When a peen tool and press are used, calculate the pressure required on 
the tool as follows. 

3,000 kg (6.614 pounds) x amount of balls in tool = kilograms or pounds 

Example: 6,614 pounds x 3 balls = 19,842 pounds 

[FIGURE: E77931A.gif]

Put the drive pinion and the tube of the peen tool in a press, pilot 
bearing toward the top. 

Calculate the amount of pressure that will be required on the peen 
tool. See specification and example calculation. 

 CAUTION: Do not align new points with grooves in end of drive pinion or in old 
points. If the new peen points are put in the wrong areas, the pilot bearing 
will not be held correctly on the pinion. 
Put the punch of the peen tool over the end of the pinion and pilot 
bearing. Apply the required amount of pressure on the punch.

 NOTE: If a three-ball peen tool is used, rotate the tool 180 degrees. 

Rotate the punch as many times as required for a minimum of five 
points. Repeat Step f for each point.

[FIGURE: E7794B.gif]

Use the following procedure to install two-piece pilot bearing 
assemblies: 

With a press or a soft mallet and sleeve, install the inner race of the 
pilot bearing onto the nose of the pinion. Use a sleeve of the correct size 
and press the bearing race until it is squarely against its shoulder on the 
nose of the pinion. 

 NOTE: Some Rockwell carriers will have a loose fit on the outside diameter of 
the pilot bearing in the carrier casting. 

With a press or a soft mallet and sleeve, install the outer race and 
roller assembly into its bore in the carrier. Use a sleeve that is the same 
size as the outer race and press the bearing until it is squarely against the 
shoulder in the bottom of its bore.

Apply axle lubricant on bearing cups in the retainer and bearing cones. 

Install the drive pinion into the bearing retainer.

[FIGURE: E7795B.gif]

 NOTE: The spacer or spacers control the preload adjustment of the drive 
pinion bearings. 

Install the bearing spacer or spacers on pinion shaft against the inner 
bearing cone.

 NOTE: DO NOT install pinion seal in bearing retainer. Continue with adjusting 
preload of pinion bearings. 

Install the outer bearing cone on pinion shaft against the spacer. 
Assembly will require the use of a press and a sleeve against the inner race, 
supporting the pinion on the pilot end (on the pinion itself, not the pilot 
bearing).

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Drive Pinion, Bearing Retainer and Shim Pack Carrier, Installation

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T57T-4851-B

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T78P-4851-A

 NOTE: If a new drive pinion and ring gearset is installed, or if the depth of 
the drive pinion has to be adjusted, calculate the thickness of the shim pack. 
Refer to Section 05-00 .

Install the correct shim pack between the bearing retainer and carrier. 

 NOTE: Use a minimum of three shims in a pack. If the pack is made from 
different thickness shims, install the thinnest shims on both sides of the 
pack for maximum sealing. 

Align the oil slots in the shims with oil slots in the bearing retainer 
and carrier. The use of guide studs will help align the shims.

[FIGURE: E65921A.gif]

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT STEEL PARTS WITH A STEEL HAMMER. 
PARTS OR TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

Install the drive pinion and bearing retainer into the carrier. If 
necessary, use a rubber, plastic or leather mallet to hit the assembly into 
position.

[FIGURE: DE0358A.gif]

Install the cover and seal assembly and gasket over the bearing 
retainer, if so equipped. 

Align the oil slots in the cover and gasket with oil slots in the 
bearing retainer.

[FIGURE: DE0359A.gif]

Install the bearing retainer-to-carrier capscrews and washers. Tighten 
capscrews to correct torque specification. Refer to the Specifications 
 portion of this section.

[FIGURE: E65941A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not install tight fit yokes or flanges on shafts using a hammer or 
mallet. A hammer or mallet will damage the yoke or flange. 

 NOTE: If the fit between the yoke or flange splines and drive pinion splines 
is tight, use the three-piece pilot tool for installation. Refer to Yokes, 
Tight Fit in the Removal and Installation portion of this section for 
procedure. 

Install the input yoke or flange, nut and washer (if used) on the drive 
pinion. The yoke or flange must be against the outer bearing.

Using a flange or yoke bar such as Companion Flange Holding Tool 
T57T-4851-B or T78P-4851-A, tighten the pinion nut to the correct torque 
specification listed under Specifications at the end of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Differential and Ring Gear, Assembly 

 Assembly 

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE CLOTHING AND GLOVES THAT WILL PROTECT YOU FROM INJURY WHEN 
YOU TOUCH THE HOT RING GEAR. 

 CAUTION: Do not press a cold ring gear on the flange case half. A cold ring gear 
will damage the case half because of the tight fit. Metal particles between 
the parts will cause gear runout that exceeds the Rockwell specification of 
0.2 mm (0.008 inch). 

Expand the ring gear by heating the gear in a tank of water to a 
temperature of 71°C to 82°C (160°
F to 180°F) for 10 to 15 minutes.

Lift the ring gear from the tank of water using a lifting tool. 

Install the ring gear on the case half flange immediately after the 
gear is heated. If the ring gear does not fit easily on the case half flange, 
heat the gear again. Repeat Step 1. 

Align fastener holes of the ring gear and case half flange. Rotate the 
ring gear as needed. 

Install the bolts, nuts and washers that hold the ring gear to the case 
half flange, if so equipped. Install the bolts from the gear side of the 
assembly. The bolt heads must be against the ring gear.

[FIGURE: E7812B.gif]

Tighten the bolts and nuts to the correct torque value. Refer to the Specifications 
 portion of this section. 

 CAUTION: Do not heat rivets before installation. Use only cold rivets to fasten 
the ring gear correctly on the differential case half flange. 

Install the rivets used to hold the ring gear to the differential case 
half flange, using the following procedure:

Install the correct size rivets in pairs opposite each other from the 
differential case half side of the assembly. The rivet heads must be against 
the flange case half.

[FIGURE: E7813B.gif]

 CAUTION: The pressure on rivets must be held for approximately one minute so 
that the rivet body will fill the hole. 
Press the rivets into position from the ring gear side of the assembly. 
Use a riveter machine and apply the correct amount of pressure. See chart for 
rivet pressures.

 RING GEAR RIVET PRESSURES

Check for gaps between the back surface of the ring gear and the 
differential case half flange after the rivets are installed. Use a 0.08-mm 
(0.003-inch) feeler gauge and check at four points around the assembly. 

If the gauge fits more than one-half the distance between the outer 
diameter of the flange and the pilot diameter of the gear, remove the ring 
gear. If the gap is less than 0.08 mm (0.003 inch), continue by following Step 
8.

[FIGURE: E78151A.gif]

Check the case half flange and ring gear for the problem that causes 
the gap. Service or replace parts. 

After the parts are serviced or replaced, assemble the ring gear on the 
case half flange. 

Install the bearing cones on both of the case halves. Use a press and 
sleeve of the correct size.

[FIGURE: E7816C.gif]

Apply axle lubricant on the inside surfaces of both case halves, spider 
(cross), thrust washers, side gears and differential pinions. 

Put the differential case half flange on a bench, ring gear teeth up. 

 CAUTION: The side gears in some carrier models have hubs of different lengths. 
Install the correct length side gear into the differential case half flange. 

Install one thrust washer and side gear into the case half flange.

[FIGURE: E7817C.gif]

Install the spider (cross), differential pinions and thrust washers 
into the case half flange.

[FIGURE: E51501A.gif]

Install the second side gear and thrust washer over spider and 
differential pinions.

[FIGURE: E7818B.gif]

Put the plain half of the differential case over the flange half and 
gears. Rotate the plain half as needed to align the match marks.

[FIGURE: E7819B.gif]

Install Dri-Loc® fasteners into the case halves. 

If used, install four capscrews and washers or bolts, nuts and washers 
into the case halves. The distance between the fasteners must be equal. 
Tighten the fasteners to the correct torque value in a pattern opposite each 
other. Refer to the illustration for the correct tightening sequence. 

Install the other fasteners into the case halves. Tighten the fasteners 
to the correct torque value. Refer to the Specifications portion of this 
section for the correct torque specifications. 

[FIGURE: E78201A.gif]

Check the rotating resistance of the differential gears. Refer to 
 Section 05-00 . 

 Installation 

Clean and dry the bearing cups and bores of the carrier legs and 
bearing caps. 

Apply axle lubricant on the inner diameter of the bearing cups and on 
both bearing cones that are assembled on the case halves. 

Apply Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSK-M2G349-A1 in the bearing bores of the carrier legs and 
bearing caps. Apply a single continuous bead of adhesive 360° 
around the smooth, ground surfaces only. Do not put adhesive on threaded areas.

[FIGURE: E78231A.gif]

Install the bearing cups over the bearing cones that are assembled on 
the case halves.

Lift the differential and ring gear assembly using Endless Lifting 
Sling D87L-1000-A or equivalent, and install into the carrier. The bearing 
cups must be flat against the bores between the carrier legs. 

[FIGURE: E7824C.gif]

Install both of the bearing adjusting rings into position between the 
carrier legs. Turn each adjusting ring hand-tight against the bearing cup.

[FIGURE: E7825B.gif]

Install the bearing caps over the bearings and adjusting rings in the 
correct location as marked before removal. 

[FIGURE: E78261A.gif]

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT STEEL PARTS WITH A STEEL HAMMER. 
PARTS OR TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

 CAUTION: If bearing caps are not installed in correct locations, the bores and 
threads in caps will not match the carrier and damage to parts can occur. Do 
not force the bearing caps into position. 

 CAUTION: Do not force the bearing caps into position. 

Hit each bearing cap into position with a light leather, plastic or 
rubber mallet. The caps must fit easily against the bearings, adjusting rings 
and carrier. 

Check the alignment of match marks between caps and carrier if bearing 
caps do not correctly fit into position. Remove the caps and repeat Steps 6 
through 8. 

Install the capscrews and washers that hold bearing caps to the 
carrier. Tighten the capscrews by hand four to six turns, then tighten the 
capscrews to the correct torque value. Refer to the Specifications portion of 
this section.

If so equipped, do not install the cotter keys, pins or lock plates 
that hold the bearing adjusting rings in position. Continue by adjusting the 
preload of differential bearings, adjust backlash of the hypoid gear and check 
tooth contact patterns.

ADJUSTMENTS

Thrust Screw 

 NOTE: Some Rockwell axles are not equipped with a thrust screw. 

 Specification 

Clearance between thrust screw or block and ring gear: 0.65 to 1.14 mm 
(0.025 to 0.045 inch). Loosen the thrust screw one-half turn, 180 degrees. 

If the carrier does not have a thrust block, start at Step 4. 

Rotate the carrier in the repair stand until the back surface of ring 
gear is up.

[FIGURE: E78361A.gif]

Put the thrust block on the back surface of the ring gear. The thrust 
block must be in the center between the outer diameter of gear and 
differential case. 

Rotate the ring gear until the thrust block and hole for drive gear 
thrust screw in carrier are aligned. 

Install the jam nut in the middle of the drive gear thrust screw.

[FIGURE: E5350B.gif]

Install the drive gear thrust screw into the carrier until the screw 
stops against the ring gear or thrust block. 

Loosen the drive gear thrust screw one-half turn, 180 degrees.

[FIGURE: E7837B.gif]

Tighten the jam nut to the correct torque value. Refer to the 
Specifications portion of this section.

If the rear rear axle of the tandem axle is being serviced and if it is 
equipped with a driver-controlled main differential lock, refer to Section 05-02C before performing any service procedures.

SPECIFICATIONS

SPECIFICATIONS

Drive Pinion Bearings Preload

 Specification: New bearings — 0.56 to 5.08 Nm
 (5 to 45 lb-in) torque. Used bearings in good condition —
 1.13 to 3.39 Nm (10-30 lb-in) torque.

 Adjustment: Preload is controlled by the thickness of the 
spacer between bearings. To increase preload, install a thinner spacer. To 
decrease preload, install a thicker spacer.

Drive Pinion Depth in Carrier

 Specification: Install the correct amount of shims between 
the bearing retainer and carrier. To calculate, use old shim pack thickness 
and new and old pinion cone numbers.

 Adjustment: Change the thickness of the shim pack to get a 
good gear tooth contact pattern.

Hypoid Gearset — Tooth Contact Patterns (Hand Rolled)

 Specification: Conventional gearset — 
toward the toe of the gear tooth and in the center between the top and bottom 
of the tooth. Generoid gearset — between the center and toe of 
the tooth and in the center between the top and bottom of the tooth.

 Adjustment: Tooth contact patterns are controlled by the 
thickness of the shim pack between the pinion bearing retainer and carrier and 
by ring gear backlash. To move the contact pattern lower, decrease the 
thickness of the shim pack under the pinion bearing retainer. To move the 
contact pattern higher, increase the thickness of the shim pack under the 
pinion bearing retainer. To move the contact pattern toward the toe of the 
tooth, decrease backlash of the ring gear. To move the contact pattern toward 
the heel of the tooth, increase backlash of the ring gear.

Main Differential Bearings Preload

 Specification: 1.7 to 3.9 Nm (15 to 35 
lb-in) torque or expansion between bearing cap. RS-XX-140 and RS-XX-145 
carrier models — 0.08 to 0.22 mm (0.003 to 0.009 inch). All 
other carrier models — 0.15 to 0.33 mm (0.006 to 0.013 inch).

 Adjustment: Preload is controlled by tightening both 
adjusting rings after zero end play is reached.

Main Differential Gears Rotating Resistance

 Specification: 68 Nm (50 lb-ft) maximum 
torque applied to one side gear.

Ring Gear Backlash

Ring gears that have a pitch diameter of less than 431.8 mm (17 inches) —
 range 0.20 to 0.46 mm (0.008 to 0.018 inch); 0.30 mm (0.012 
inch) for a new gearset. Ring gears that have a pitch diameter of 431.8 mm (17 
inches) or greater — range 0.25 to 0.51 mm (0.010 to 0.020 
inch); 0.38 mm (0.015 inch) for a new gearset.

 Adjustment: Backlash is controlled by the position of the 
ring gear. Change backlash within specifications to get a good tooth contact 
pattern. To increase backlash, move the ring gear away from the drive pinion. 
To decrease backlash, move the ring gear toward the drive pinion.

Ring Gear Runout

 Specification: 0.20 mm (0.008 inch) maximum.

Sensor Switch — Installation (Carriers with 
Differential Lock Only)

 Specification: Shift the differential to the locked 
position. Tighten the sensor switch into the carrier until the test light 
comes on. Tighten the sensor switch one additional turn.

Spigot Bearing — Peening on the Drive Pinion

 Specification: Apply 3,000 kg (6,614 lb) pressure on a 
10-mm (0.375-inch) ball. Peen the end of the drive pinion at a minimum of five 
points.

Thrust Screw or Thrust Block — Clearance

 Specification: 0.65 to 1.14 mm (0.025 to 0.045 inch) or 
loosen the thrust screw 1/2 turn after tightening the thrust screw, 
hand-tight, against the ring gear.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Rockwell Two-Speed Axle

The Rockwell two-speed rear axle has a first reduction differential 
ring gear and pinion set and a second reduction planetary gearset.

The differential pinion is supported by two differential pinion 
bearings mounted on the pinion shaft in front of the gear head. A rear axle 
drive pinion pilot bearing supports the pinion in the rear axle differential 
carrier.

The main differential and the planetary gearset are mounted in the 
differential case halves that are contained in the planetary support case. The 
planetary support case is mounted in the rear axle differential carrier on two 
tapered differential bearings.

An electric shift unit is mounted on the carrier and is actuated by a 
switch in the cab of the vehicle. The driver can actuate the switch to shift 
the drive unit into high or low gear range.

[FIGURE: E8158B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

4045

Shift Fork

2

4229

Planetary Pinion Gear

3

—

Ring Gear (Part of 4209)

4

—

Pinion (Part of 4209)

5

4127

Support Case

6

4141

Differential Carrier Assy

7

—

Planetary Sun Gear (Part of 4237)

In low gear range, the sun gear is shifted to engage with the clutch 
plate. The four planetary pinions are then free to rotate and become the 
second reduction gearset. The hypoid gearset ratio is now multiplied by the 
planetary gearset ratio. This gives the drive unit a higher numerical ratio 
for increased pulling power, but decreases the top speed.

[FIGURE: E66231A.gif]

In high gear range, the sun gear is engaged with the support case and 
the planetary pinions are locked in place. When the planetary pinions are 
locked, there is no second reduction and the power is sent directly from the 
hypoid gearset to the main differential. This hypoid single-reduction drive 
gives a lower numerical ratio for higher road speeds, but less pulling power.

[FIGURE: E66241A.gif]

PAGE 4588
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 05-02B: Axle, Rockwell Two-Speed

1997 F700, F800 and B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Shift Control, Electric 

A slider block type, electric shift control is used in conjunction with 
the two-speed axles. 

The electric shift control system is composed of the control switch, 
the speedometer adapter, the electric shift unit, the relay, and the wiring 
harness. 

The control switch, mounted on the gearshift lever has two positions: 
up for high range and down for low range.

[FIGURE: E17931C.gif]

For vehicles with automatic transmission, the two-speed rear axle 
switch is located to the left of the steering column on the instrument panel. 
Push the top of the rocker switch for high range and push the bottom of the 
rocker switch for low range. When the switch is in either of these positions, 
the switch contacts complete the circuit between the battery and the motor in 
the axle shift unit.

A circuit breaker protects the system against a short circuit. Should a 
short circuit occur, the circuit breaker will open and will de-energize the 
entire system until the condition has been corrected.

[FIGURE: E64911A.gif]

Relays are used in the circuit to connect the shift motor to battery 
power on vehicles with automatic transmission only. The rear axle shift 
control switch connects the relay coil to battery power. The contacts in the 
relay complete the circuit to the motor.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Axle, Rockwell Two-Speed

Axle shafts, wheel hubs, wheel hub bearings, wheel hub grease seals, 
the electric shift unit and the differential drive pinion oil seal can be 
replaced without removing the differential carrier assembly from the axle 
housing or the rear axle assembly from the vehicle. 

The axle shafts, wheel hub, bearings, and grease seal may be replaced, 
lubricated or adjusted. Refer to Section 04-02B . 

For axle alignment, refer to Section 05-00 . 

The electric shift unit can be replaced or overhauled. Refer to Shift 
Unit, Electric, Slider Block-Type , in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of 
this section. 

 Inspection and Verification 

Visually inspect the wiring harness for broken or frayed wires. 
Service, if necessary. Check harness connectors for corrosion and contact. 
Clean, if necessary. Verify that the connectors are properly mated (wiring 
into connector matches designated color out of connector). 

 Component Tests 

 Shift Unit Testing, Electric, Slider Block-Type 

Disconnect harness connector from unit by prying up locking tab with a 
small screwdriver and pulling on connector portion of harness. 

Remove four hex-head screws retaining cover to motor housing and remove 
cover. 

Disconnect three fast-on terminals from cover.

[FIGURE: E6495C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Cover (Part of 4062)

2

—

Negative Lead

3

—

If motor movement is not observed in both cases, proceed to Step 7.

Attach a jumper wire between positive terminal of a 12-volt power supply and

If motor moves in both cases but did not move in Step 5, check 
connections at cover harness port or check cover for damage.

Remove motor fast-on terminal lead wire from circuit board.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Differential Carrier

 NOTE: All parts for models RS-15-210, RS-17-220, RS-19-220, RS-21-230 and 
RS-23-240, except the shift unit to carrier studs and carrier to housing 
capscrews, are manufactured in metric dimensions. When the carriers are 
serviced, it is important to use the correct size tools.

 Removal 

 NOTE: Before starting any service or maintenance work on the carrier assembly 
make sure the drive unit is shifted into the LOW range position. This will 
eliminate interference between the sun gear and the carrier mounting ring of 
the axle housing to allow carrier removal. 

To ensure a complete shift and positive gear engagement, drive the 
vehicle a short distance while shifting the drive unit into the low range 
position. 

Remove plug from bottom of axle housing and drain lubricant. 

Disconnect the driveline universal joint from the pinion input yoke or 
flange on the differential carrier. 

Remove the stud nuts and washers from the flanges of both axle shafts. 

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT THE ROUND DRIVING LUGS ON THE HEAD 
OF AXLE SHAFTS. LUGS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

 CAUTION: Do not hit the circular driving lugs on the shaft head. This may cause 
the lugs to shatter and splinter. Do not use chisels or wedges to loosen the 
shaft or dowels. This will damage the hub, shaft and oil seal. 

Loosen the tapered dowels in the flanges of both axle shafts. 

To loosen the dowels, hold a 38 mm (1-1/2-inch) diameter brass drift 
against the center of the axle shaft head, inside the circular driving lugs. 
Strike the drift with a 2.7 kg (5-6 lb.) hammer or sledge. A 38 mm 
(1-1/2-inch) diameter brass hammer can be used as a drift.

[FIGURE: E64971B.gif]

Remove the tapered dowels and axle shafts from the axle assembly. 

Disconnect the electric lines from the shift unit. 

Remove all but the top two differential carrier-to-housing capscrews 
and washers. 

Loosen the top two differential carrier-to-housing fasteners but leave 
them attached to the assembly. The fasteners will hold the differential 
carrier in the housing. 

 NOTE: If it is necessary to use puller bolts, there are two threaded holes in 
the carrier flange. Use the differential carrier-to-housing bolts. 

Loosen the differential carrier in the axle housing. Use a soft mallet 
to hit the mounting flange of the carrier in several places.

Place Rotunda Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or 
equivalent under the differential carrier to support the assembly.

[FIGURE: E64981B.gif]

 CAUTION: Take care not to damage the differential carrier or housing flange as 
damage to these surfaces will cause oil leaks. 

Remove the top two differential carrier-to-housing fasteners and 
carefully remove the differential carrier from the housing with the roller 
jack. Use a pry bar with a round end to help remove the differential carrier 
from the housing.

Place differential carrier in suitable stand.

[FIGURE: E64991A.gif]

 Installation 

 WARNING: BE CAREFUL WHEN USING CLEANING SOLVENTS. FOLLOW THE SOLVENT 
MANUFACTURER'S INSTRUCTIONS FOR SAFE USE TO PREVENT INJURY. 

Clean the inside of axle housing and the mounting surface where the 
carrier fastens. Use a cleaning solvent and clean rags to remove dirt. Blow 
dry the cleaned areas with air. Refer to Section 05-00 for cleaning 
procedures. 

Inspect the axle housing for damage. Refer to Section 05-00 for 
inspection procedures. 

Apply silicone gasket material to the mounting surface of the housing 
where the carrier fastens. Refer to Section 05-00 .

[FIGURE: E77631A.gif]

Make sure that the differential carrier is shifted into the low speed 
gear range. This will permit clearance between the sun gear and the 
differential carrier mounting ring on the housing. 

 CAUTION: Do not install the differential carrier using a hammer or mallet. A 
hammer or mallet can damage the mounting flange of the differential carrier 
and cause oil leaks. 

Install the differential carrier into the axle housing, using Rotunda 
Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or equivalent. 

 NOTE: Apply four or five drops of Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G349-A1 on the capscrew threads. 
Refer to Section 05-00 . 

Install capscrews and washers in the four corner locations around the 
carrier and axle housing. Tighten the capscrews hand-tight at this time.

[FIGURE: E77641A.gif]

Push the carrier into position. Tighten the four capscrews two or three 
turns each in a pattern opposite each other. 

Repeat Step 7 until the four fasteners are tightened to the specified 
torque specification. Refer to the Specifications portion of this section.

Install the remaining capscrews that hold the carrier in the axle 
housing. Tighten the fasteners to the correct torque specification. Refer to 
the Specifications portion of this section. 

Connect the driveline universal joint to the pinion input yoke or 
flange on the carrier. 

Install the gaskets and axle shafts into the axle housing. The gasket 
and flange of the axle shaft must fit flat against the wheel hub. 

Install the tapered dowels over each stud and into the flange of the 
axle shaft, if used. Use a punch or drift and hammer, if necessary. 

Install Grade 8 nuts and lockwashers on the studs. Tighten the stud 
nuts to the correct torque specification. Refer to the Specifications portion 
of this section. 

Connect the electric lines to the shift unit. 

 NOTE: For additional lubrication information, refer to Axle Lubricant 
Capacities in the Specifications portion of this section. 

Fill the rear axle with the specified lubricant according to the 
following procedure.

Make sure the vehicle is parked on a level surface. When the angle of 
the drive pinion changes, the lubricant capacity of the rear axle assembly 
will change. 

Remove the fill plug from the axle housing. 

Fill the rear axle with lubricant until the lubricant level is to the 
bottom of the filler plug hole. See the Lubricant Specifications and 
Capacities in Section 05-00 for the specified axle lubricant. 

Install the fill plug and tighten to a minimum torque of 47 Nm
 (35 lb-ft). When correctly installed, one complete thread 
of the fill plug is visible. 

Drive the vehicle in an unloaded condition for 1.6-3.2 km (1-2 miles) 
at speeds not more than 40 km/h (25 mph). Operating the vehicle make sure that 
the lubricant flows through the complete rear axle assembly.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Differential Carrier 

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: There may be a small amount of spring tension in the shift unit during 
removal. 

Remove shift unit-to-carrier stud nuts and washers. Lift shift unit 
from differential carrier and set aside.

[FIGURE: E65521B.gif]

Remove shift fork seal diaphragm and retaining spring from shift unit 
tower by pulling it off top of fork.

[FIGURE: E65531B.gif]

 NOTE: The pin will bottom against a shoulder if driven the opposite way. 

Remove shift fork and plugs. Use a thin brass drift to tap out pin and 
two plugs from side of differential carrier.

[FIGURE: E65551C.gif]

Slide the shift fork away from the planetary sun gear/collar end to 
remove both the fork and planetary sun gear from the carrier. Pull the 
planetary sun gear/collar through the clutch collar. If necessary, index the 
planetary sun gear teeth to fit them through the clutch plate.

[FIGURE: E65561B.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not strike directly on the plate as damage will occur. Do not use 
chisels or wedges that may cause damage. 

Remove stud nuts, washers and dowels (or capscrews only in some models) 
that hold the clutch plate to the differential carrier to disassemble the 
clutch plate from the differential carrier. To remove the dowels, use a brass 
drift against the clutch plate. Hit the drift hard with a hammer to loosen the 
dowels. Do not remove the studs unless required.

[FIGURE: E65571B.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 4594
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 05-02B: Axle, Rockwell Two-Speed

1997 F700, F800 and B800 Workshop Manual

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Planetary Gears, Differential and Ring Gear, Disassembly

 NOTE: Before measuring backlash, completely remove oil from ring gear and 
pinion teeth. Refer to Section 05-00 for recommended solvents. Then, dry parts 
according to drying procedure. 

Measure and make note of the hypoid gear backlash. Refer to Section 05-00 .

Remove cotter pin from right adjusting ring. 

[FIGURE: E65581B.gif]

Mark one carrier leg and the matching bearing cap so that the parts can 
be correctly aligned at assembly. A center punch and hammer can be used to 
mark the parts.

Loosen and remove bearing cap capscrews and washers.

[FIGURE: E65591B.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not strike these hardened steel pieces directly with a steel hammer 
as damage to parts or personal injury from chips or splinters can result. 

Remove the bearing cap and adjusting rings. If necessary, hit the caps 
with a soft mallet to loosen them.

[FIGURE: E81341A.gif]

 NOTE: The differential bearing cups and cones will be removed with the 
differential. The cups will be loose and the cones will be on the support case 
halves. Do not remove the bearing cones unless required. 

Lift the planetary, differential and ring gear assembly from the 
carrier. Place the assembly on a workbench.

[FIGURE: E65611B.gif]

Remove capscrews holding support cases and drive gear together.

[FIGURE: E65621A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not strike these hardened steel pieces directly with a steel hammer 
as damage to parts or personal injury from chips or splinters can result. 

Separate the right (planetary half) support case from the ring gear. If 
necessary, use a brass hammer to tap the support case from the gear.

[FIGURE: E65631A.gif]

Lift the planetary/differential case assembly and thrust washer from 
the gear and left (plain half) support case assembly.

[FIGURE: E6564C.gif]

 WARNING: DO NOT HIT THESE HARDENED STEEL PARTS DIRECTLY WITH A STEEL HAMMER. 
PARTS OR TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

Separate the left support case from the ring gear, if necessary.

Remove the differential bearing cones from the support case halves, if 
necessary. Use a press or bearing puller on the left (plain half) support case.

[FIGURE: E65651B.gif]

Use a punch through the holes from inside the case to remove the 
bearing cone from the right (planetary half) support case. Tap on the bearing 
cone inner race, alternately through each hole until the cone is removed.

[FIGURE: E66261A.gif]

Mark both halves for correct alignment at assembly if the alignment 
marks on the differential case halves are not clear.

[FIGURE: E65671B.gif]

Remove the differential case capscrews and washers and separate the 
case halves.

[FIGURE: E6569C.gif]

Remove the thrust washer and side gear.

[FIGURE: E65701B.gif]

Remove the spider cross, the four differential pinions and the thrust 
washers for the pinions as an assembly. Do not lose the thrust washers from 
the assembly.

[FIGURE: E6571C.gif]

Lift the side gear and thrust washers from the differential case.

[FIGURE: E65721B.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not hit the lock pin with heavy hammer blows. Heavy blows can damage 
the differential case bore and the burrs can cut or damage the nylon lining on 
the planetary shaft. 

Disassemble the planetary components from the differential case half. 
Use a thin drift and hammer to tap the pinion shaft lock pins into the 
planetary shaft. The lock pin is shorter than the pinion shaft so that the 
shaft can be removed when the lock pin is released.

[FIGURE: E81611A.gif]

Mark each shaft and its bore for identification at assembly before the 
pinion shafts are removed. Each shaft must be assembled into the same bore 
from which it was removed. 

 CAUTION: Do not hit the shafts with a steel hammer. Be careful not to scratch or 
damage the nylon lining on the pinion shafts. 

Tap the planetary pinion shafts from the case half. Use a soft mallet 
or a brass drift and hammer.

Remove the planetary pinion gear and the inner and outer thrust washers 
when each shaft is removed.

[FIGURE: E6574D.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 4595
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 05-02B: Axle, Rockwell Two-Speed

1997 F700, F800 and B800 Workshop Manual

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Hypoid Pinion and Cage Assembly 

 Disassembly 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T57T-4851-B

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T78P-4851-A

Hold flange or yoke with suitable tool, such as Companion Flange 
Holding Tool T57T-4851-B or T78P-4851-A and remove pinion shaft nut and washer.

[FIGURE: E65751A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use a hammer to loosen the yoke or flange. A hammer can damage 
the parts and cause alignment concerns. 

Remove the yoke or flange with Gear and Pulley Puller D80L-522-A or 
equivalent.

[FIGURE: E65761B.gif]

 NOTE: Inspect the seal for damage. If the seal lips are worn, the outside 
diameter surface of the seal is damaged, or if the mounting surface of the 
flange is not flat, replace the seal at time of assembly. 

Remove the pinion oil seal. Pry at several points around the 
circumference between the flange of the seal and the bearing cage. Remove the 
seal straight out from the cage. Be careful that you do not damage the 
mounting surface of the bearing cage.

[FIGURE: E65771B.gif]

Remove the pinion bearing cage to carrier capscrews and washers. 

[FIGURE: E65781B.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use a pry bar, wedges or chisels between the bearing cage and 
the carrier. These tools can damage the bearing cage, shims and carrier. 

Remove the bearing cage and pinion assembly.

Keep the shims together for use when the carrier is reassembled if they 
are in good condition. 

Measure the total thickness of the pack if the shims are to be 
discarded. This dimension will be needed to calculate the depth of the drive 
pinion when the gearset is installed.

Put the pinion and cage assembly in a press with the spigot bearing at 
the bottom. 

 WARNING: DO NOT HIT STEEL PARTS WITH A STEEL HAMMER. PARTS OR TOOLS CAN BREAK 
AND CAUSE INJURY. 

Support the bearing cage under its flange with metal or wood blocks and 
press the pinion through the cage. If a press is not available, use a soft 
mallet to drive the pinion through the bearing cage.

[FIGURE: E65801B.gif]

Remove the outer bearing cone from the bearing cage. 

Inspect all of the pinion bearings (cups and cones) to determine if 
replacement is necessary. Refer to Section 05-00 . 

Remove the inner and outer bearing cups from inside the cage if the 
bearings need to be replaced. 

Use Gear and Pulley Puller D80L-522-A or equivalent to remove the outer 
bearing cup.

[FIGURE: E65811A.gif]

Use a bearing driver to remove the inner bearing cup.

[FIGURE: E65821B.gif]

Remove bearing adjusting spacer from pinion shaft. 

Remove inner bearing cone from pinion shaft with a press and Bearing 
Pulling Attachment D79L-4621-A or equivalent.

[FIGURE: E6583E.gif]

Remove the pinion spigot bearing snap ring. 

Remove the spigot bearing with a press or bearing puller.

[FIGURE: E65841A.gif]

 Assembly 

Lubricate the inside surfaces of the bearing cage and all the 
components to be installed in the cage with axle lubricant. 

Install both the inner and outer bearing cups into the cage, if 
removed. Install the cups into their bores in the bearing cage until the cups 
are flat against the bottoms of the bores. Use sleeves of the correct size to 
install the cups.

[FIGURE: E65861A.gif]

Press the inner bearing cone onto the pinion shaft until the cone is 
flat against the gear head. Use a sleeve of the correct size against the inner 
race of the bearing.

[FIGURE: E65871B.gif]

 NOTE: The pinion spigot bearing can be of two different designs. 

Install the spigot bearing.

[FIGURE: E8162B.gif]

On the RS-15-210, RS-17-220 and RS-19-220 axles (spigot bearing with 
retaining ring): 

Install the bearing on the journal of the pinion so that the retaining 
ring of the bearing is on the same side as the snap ring groove on the 
journal. Press the bearing on to the pinion until the bearing is flat against 
the head of the pinion. Use a sleeve of the correct size against the bearing 
inner race. 

Install the snap ring into the groove on the journal of the pinion with 
snap ring pliers. 

[FIGURE: E65881B.gif]

On the RS-21-230, RS-23-240 axles (spigot bearing with abutment ring): 

Set the bearing on a sleeve that fits against its inner race. 

Put the abutment ring, with its inner diameter radius up, on top of the 
bearing. Carefully align the sleeve, inner race and abutment ring. 

Press the pinion through the abutment ring and into the spigot bearing 
until the abutment ring is flat against the head of the pinion. 

Install the snap ring into the groove on the journal of the pinion with 
snap ring pliers. 

[FIGURE: E81631A.gif]

Install the pinion and inner bearing assembly into the bearing cage. 

Install the bearing adjusting spacer or spacers over the pinion shaft 
against the inner bearing cone.

[FIGURE: E81641A.gif]

Press the outer bearing cone over the pinion shaft until it is flat 
against the adjusting spacer. Use a sleeve that presses against the inner race 
only. 

Check the preload of the pinion bearing. Refer to Section 05-00 . 

 CAUTION: Make sure that the seal lips are clean and free from dirt and particles 
that will cause a leak between the shaft and the seal. 

 NOTE: The old triple-lip oil seal can be installed back into the bearing cage 
if the seal is not worn or damaged. 

Install a new triple-lip oil seal into the bearing cage.

Apply the same lubricant used in the axle housing to the outer surface 
of the seal and the seal bore in the bearing cage.

[FIGURE: E81431A.gif]

On reused seals, apply Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to the seal lips. 

Install the seal into the bearing cage until the flange of the seal is 
flat against the top of the bearing cage. Use a sleeve or seal driver that 
fits against the metal flange of the seal. 

After the seal is installed, check the gap with a feeler gauge at 
several points between the flange of the seal and the bearing cage. The gap 
must be within 0.38-0.76 mm (0.015-0.030 inch). The difference between the 
largest and smallest measurements must not be more than 0.25 mm (0.010 inch).

[FIGURE: E65911B.gif]

 NOTE: If a new pinion and ring gear is to be installed, or the depth of the 
pinion must be adjusted, calculate the required thickness of the shim pack. 
Refer to Section 05-00 .

Install the yoke or flange onto the pinion shaft and against the outer 
bearing cone. Use a press or a three-piece pilot tool set. Refer to Section 05-00 . Install the pinion nut on to the pinion shaft, finger-tight only.

Install two guide studs temporarily in the carrier to help align the 
shim pack and bearing cage during assembly. Install the correct shim pack 
between the bearing cage and carrier. Make sure that the shims do not restrict 
the oil passage holes in the bearing cage. Use a minimum of three shims with 
the thickest in the center of the pack.

[FIGURE: E65921A.gif]

Install the pinion and cage assembly into the carrier.

[FIGURE: E65931B.gif]

Remove the two guide studs. Apply Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G349-A1 to the bearing cage to 
carrier capscrew holes. Refer to Section 05-00 . Install the capscrews and 
tighten them to the specified torque value. Refer to the Specifications 
portion of this section. 

Tighten the pinion nut to the minimum torque. Refer to the Specifications 
 portion of this section. Use a yoke or flange bar such as 
Companion Flange Holding Tool T57T-4851-B or T78P-4851-A to tighten the nut. 

Check the pinion bearing preload. If necessary, increase the torque on 
the pinion nut to the maximum torque listed in the Specifications portion of 
this section to get the pinion bearing preload specified in Section 05-00 .

[FIGURE: E6635E.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Planetary Gears, Differential and Ring Gear, Assembly

Lubricate the inside surfaces of both differential case halves and all 
of the components to be installed in the case with axle lubricant. 

 NOTE: Make sure that the bent tabs on the thrust washers are pointing away 
from the planetary pinions. If the old planetary pinion shafts are being 
installed, make sure that they are installed into their correct bores, as 
marked at disassembly. Each pin must be assembled into the same bore from 
which it was removed. 

Assemble the four planetary pinions and the eight thrust washers.

[FIGURE: E65951A.gif]

Assemble the four planetary pinion shafts and lock pins. Align the lock 
pin hole in the shafts with the hole in the differential case. Use a small 
hammer to tap the pins into position, flat to the surface of the differential 
case. Do not cut or damage the nylon coating on the pinion shafts.

[FIGURE: E65961A.gif]

Assemble the differential into the planetary case half. First put the 
thrust washer and the side gear with the short hub into position in the case 
half.

[FIGURE: E65721B.gif]

Assemble the four pinions and thrust washers on the spider cross. While 
you hold the parts together, put them in position over the side gear in the 
case half.

[FIGURE: E6571C.gif]

Install the second side gear with the long hub and thrust washer over 
the spider and pinions. 

Put the plain case half in position with the match marks aligned with 
those on the planetary case half. 

Install four of the differential case capscrews at equally spaced 
points. Tighten the capscrews to the specified torque. Refer to the Specifications 
 portion of this section. 

Check the rolling resistance of the differential gears. Refer to 
 Section 05-00 .

 NOTE: Remove the four capscrews installed in Step 8 and apply four or five 
drops of Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSK-M2G349-A1 to the threaded capscrew holes.

Install and tighten the capscrews to the specified torque. Refer to the Specifications 
 portion of this section. 

Install the remaining differential case capscrews when rolling 
resistance meets specifications. Apply four or five drops of Stud and Bearing 
Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G349-A1 to 
the threaded capscrew holes. Refer to Section 05-00 . Install the capscrews and 
tighten to specified torque value. Refer to the Specifications portion of this 
section.

Install the bearing cones if removed, on both support case halves with 
a press and sleeve that fits against the inner races only. On the right case 
use a support sleeve to prevent cracking the case (casting) with press pressure.

[FIGURE: E66271A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not press the support case half into a cold ring gear. A cold ring 
gear will damage the case half because of the tight fit. 

Expand the ring gear by heating it in a tank of water at a temperature 
of approximately 90°C (190°F) for 10 to 15 
minutes. Wear gloves to protect hands from the hot ring gear.

 WARNING: DO NOT HIT THE SUPPORT CASE DIRECTLY WITH A STEEL HAMMER. PARTS OR 
TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

Install the right-hand support case half into the ring gear. Use two 
equally spaced bolts for alignment and tap the support case into position with 
a soft mallet.

Put the differential case assembly and its thrust washer into the 
support case. Permit the ring gear to cool.

[FIGURE: E66011A.gif]

Heat the flange half of the support case in the tank of hot water and 
assemble the case half to the ring gear. 

Install the ring gear to case capscrews. Apply four to five drops of 
Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
WSK-M2G349-A1 to the threaded capscrew holes. Refer to Section 05-00 . Install 
the capscrews and tighten them to the specified torque value. Refer to the Specifications 
 portion of this section.

[FIGURE: E66021A.gif]

 Differential and Ring Gear Assembly 

 Installation 

Clean and dry the bearing cups and bores of the carrier legs and 
bearing caps. 

Apply axle lubricant to the inner diameter of the bearing cups and to 
both of the bearing cones that are assembled on the support case. 

Apply Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSK-M2G349-A1 to the bearing bores of the carrier legs and 
bearing caps. Refer to Section 05-00 . 

Install the bearing cups over the bearing cones on the support case. 

Install the differential and ring gear assembly into the carrier. The 
bearing cups must be flat against the bore in the carrier legs.

[FIGURE: E66051B.gif]

Install the left bearing adjusting ring (with holes) into position on 
its carrier leg. Install the right adjusting ring (with lugs) on its carrier 
leg. Turn each adjusting ring tight against the bearing cup.

[FIGURE: E81651A.gif]

Install the bearing caps over the bearing cups and adjusting rings. 
Make sure that the matching marks are aligned.

[FIGURE: E81341A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not force the caps into position, the carrier housing and carrier 
legs can be damaged. 

Tap each bearing cap into position with a soft mallet. The caps must 
fit easily against the adjusting rings and the carrier. Do not force the 
bearing caps into position. If the bearing caps do not fit correctly over the 
adjusting rings and carrier, the adjusting rings may be cross threaded. Remove 
the caps and repeat Steps 6 and 7.

Install the bearing cap to carrier capscrews and washers. Tighten the 
capscrews to the specified torque. Refer to the Specifications portion of this 
section. 

Adjust the differential bearing preload. Refer to Section 05-00 .

Check the hypoid gear backlash. Refer to Section 05-00 .

Check the hypoid gear tooth patterns. Refer to Section 05-00 .

On the RS-23-240 axle only, install and adjust the hypoid gear thrust 
screw. 

Install the thrust screw into the carrier until the screw touches the 
back of the ring gear. 

To get the correct clearance adjustment of 0.635-1.143 mm (0.025-0.045 
inch), loosen the thrust screw one half turn (180 degrees). 

Apply sealing compound to the outer threads of the thrust screw. 

Hold the thrust screw in position and tighten the lock nut against the 
carrier to 203-258 Nm (150-190 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: E81661A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Shift Fork Assembly and Diaphragm

 Assembly 

Install the studs into the carrier and bearing cap if the studs for the 
clutch plate were removed. Tighten each stud so that the length between the 
top of the stud and its boss on the carrier and cap is 26.2-27.2 mm (1.03-1.07 
inch). 

Put the clutch plate in position so that the lock pin hole in the 
clutch plate is aligned with one of the adjusting ring holes. 

Install the clutch plate, dowels, washers and stud nuts or capscrews. 
Apply four or five drops of Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G349-A1 on the fastener threads. Refer to 
 Section 05-00 . Tighten the fasteners to the specified torque value. Refer to 
the Specifications portion of this section. 

Tap the lock pin through the clutch plate hole and into the adjusting 
ring hole to lock the adjusting ring.

Clean and inspect the shift fork for damage (bending, scoring or rough 
edges). Replace the shift fork if necessary. 

Install the cotter pin lock for the right adjusting ring. 

Hold the shift fork in position in the shift tower and put the 
planetary sun gear (gear end first) into the carrier. While the planetary sun 
gear is being installed, rotate the fork until it can engage the outer groove 
in the collar end of planetary sun gear. 

Rotate the planetary sun gear collar as required to engage with the 
teeth of the support case and the planetary pinion gears.

[FIGURE: E65561B.gif]

 NOTE: One of the pivot pin bores in the shift tower has a smaller inside 
diameter shoulder than the other bore. 

Install the shift fork pivot pin.

Apply sealing compound Loctite® No. 515 to the 
external surface of one of the pivot pin plugs. From the inside of the tower, 
install the plug into the bore so that it is tight against the shoulder of the 
smaller bore. 

Align the hole in the shift fork with the holes in the shift tower and 
install the shift fork pivot pin through the larger bore in the tower until it 
is tight against the plug.

surface of the second plug and install the plug tight against the pivot pin.

 CAUTION: Do not force the diaphragm into position. Damage will occur.

Shift Unit, Electric, Slider Block-Type 

 Disassembly 

Remove four hex-head screws retaining cover to motor housing. 

Remove cover. It may be necessary to pry cover off carefully with tip 
of a thin-bladed screwdriver to break sealant bond. 

Remove circuit board lock nut securing circuit board to motor housing. 

Pull circuit board out to gain access to black motor wire. Remove 
circuit board washer. 

Remove motor wire fast-on terminal from circuit board. 

Remove three hex-head screws retaining motor to motor housing.

Separate motor from housing. It may be necessary to carefully pry motor 
away from housing with tip of a thin-bladed screwdriver to break gasket 
sealing bond. Guide motor fast-on terminal through hole in motor housing. 

Remove four hex-head screws retaining base housing to motor housing. 

Separate base housing from motor housing. It may be necessary to pry 
housings apart with tip of a thin-bladed screwdriver to break sealant bond. 

Remove slider block. 

Remove gear lock nut with a deep well socket while holding opposite end 
of shaft with pliers. 

Pull shaft and gear from motor housing. 

 NOTE: The cam pins are removed from the gear side of the motor housing. It is 
not necessary to disturb the switch spring. 

Remove cam pins from holes in motor housing.

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Use only Rheolube® 362 or equivalent for lubrication 
purposes. The use of any other type of lubricant may cause shift unit 
operational concerns under certain low temperature conditions. 

Clean all parts, with exception of motor and circuit board, in a 
suitable shop solvent prior to assembly. Dry with clean, lint-free shop towels 
or compressed air prior to lubrication or assembly. Make sure all traces of 
gasket material and sealant are removed from mating surfaces. 

Lubricate cam pins with light film of Rheolube® 362 
or equivalent. Install pins in respective bores in motor housing. 

Lubricate both sides of gear washer with Rheolube® 
362 or equivalent. 

Lubricate gear by wiping a light film of Rheolube® 
362 or equivalent on side of gear facing gear washer. Liberally apply Rheolube®
 362 or equivalent to edge of gear to completely fill space 
between gear teeth. 

Lubricate portion of gear shaft that slips into gear with Rheolube®
 362 or equivalent. Position gear on shaft. Install gear 
and shaft in motor housing. 

Install gear lock nut onto end of gear shaft. Hold gear end of shaft 
with locking pliers. Tighten lock nut to 8-9 Nm (71-80 lb-in). 

Rotate gear in a counterclockwise direction to make sure no binding is 
present. 

Lubricate length of gear shaft with light film of Rheolube®
 362 or equivalent. Fill entire slot area of slider block 
that engages shaft with a liberal amount of Rheolube® 362 or 
equivalent. 

Fill cavity next to gear (adjacent to hole for motor shaft in housing) 
with a liberal amount of Rheolube® 362 or equivalent. 

Turn gear so pin beneath gear is 90 degrees from centerline of slider 
block shaft. 

Install slider block in motor housing by nesting shaft in recessed 
pockets of housing. It may be necessary to move slider block slightly in one 
direction or the other to engage gear pin. 

Apply a continuous bead of Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or 
D6AZ-19562-BA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESB-M4G92-A or 
ESE-M4G195-A around outer edges of base housing. 

Align dowel of base housing with dowel hole in motor housing. Press 
housings together. 

Install four hex-head screws retaining base housing to motor housing 
loosely. Make sure housings are mating properly by wiggling slider block from 
side to side. Tighten screws to 11-13 Nm (8-10 lb-ft). 

Apply a continuous bead of Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or 
D6AZ-19562-BA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESB-M4G92-A or 
ESE-M4G195-A around motor shaft and lead wire. 

Guide motor wire fast-on terminal through hole in motor housing along 
with motor shaft. The motor flange must be bottomed against motor housing 
mating surface. 

Install three hex-head screws retaining motor to motor housing. Tighten 
to 5-6 Nm (44-53 lb-in). 

Install circuit board washer on gear shaft end on top of gear shaft 
lock nut. 

Connect motor lead fast-on terminal to male terminal on circuit board. 

Install circuit board over gear shaft and install circuit board lock 
nut. Tighten lock nut to 1.6-1.8 Nm (14-16 lb-in). 

Apply a continuous bead of Black Non-Acid Cure Silicone Rubber Sealant 
E7TZ-19562-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESL-M4G273-A around 
outside outer edge of motor housing (around tapped holes for cover screws).

Connect wires to fast-on terminals on back of cover. Connect black wire 
to terminal closest to edge of cover. Connect green wire to center terminal. 
Connect red wire to remaining terminal. 

Carefully push wires back in housing. Do not smear gasket compound. 

Carefully align holes in new gasket and cover with tapped holes in 
motor housing and press cover to housing. Install four hex-head screws. 
Tighten to 5-6 Nm (44-53 lb-in).

SPECIFICATIONS

SPECIFICATIONS

Drive Pinion Bearings Preload

 Specification: New bearings — 0.56 to 5.08 Nm
 (5-45 lb-in) torque. Used bearings in good condition —
 1.13-3.39 Nm (10-30 lb-in) torque.

 Adjustment: Preload is controlled by the thickness of the 
spacer between bearings. To increase preload install a thinner spacer. To 
decrease preload install a thicker spacer.

Drive Pinion — Depth in Carrier (Thickness of Shim Pack)

 Specification: Install the correct amount of shims between 
the bearing cage and carrier. To calculate, use old shim pack thickness and 
new and old pinion cone numbers.

 Adjustment: Change the thickness of the shim pack to get a 
good gear tooth contact pattern.

Hypoid Gearset — Tooth Contact Patterns (Hand Rolled)

 Specification: Between the center and toe of the tooth and 
in the center between the top and bottom of the tooth. 

 Adjustment: Tooth contact patterns are controlled by the 
thickness of the shim pack between the pinion bearing cage and carrier and by 
ring gear backlash. To move the contact pattern lower, decrease the thickness 
of the shim under the pinion bearing cage. To move the contact pattern higher, 
increase the thickness of the shim pack under the pinion bearing cage. To move 
the contact pattern toward the toe of the tooth, decrease backlash of the ring 
gear. To move the contact pattern toward the heel of the tooth, increase 
backlash of the ring gear.

Main Differential Bearings Preload

 Specification: 1.7-3.9 Nm (15-35 lb-in) 
torque or expansion between bearing caps — 0.15-0.33 mm 
(0.006-0.013 inch).

 Adjustment: Preload is controlled by tightening both 
adjusting rings after zero end play is reached.

Main Differential Gears Rolling Resistance

 Specification: 68 Nm (50 lb-ft) torque 
applied to one side gear.

Ring Gear Backlash

 Specification: 0.20-0.46 mm (0.008-0.018 inch), 0.30 mm 
(0.012 inch) for a new gearset.

 Adjustment: Backlash is controlled by the position of the 
ring gear. Change backlash within specifications to get a good tooth contact 
pattern. To increase backlash, move the ring gear away from the drive pinion. 
To decrease backlash, move the ring gear toward the drive pinion.

Ring Gear Runout

 Specification: 0.20 mm (0.008 inch) maximum.

Thrust Screw Clearance (RS-23-240 Axles Only)

 Specification: 0.65-1.14 mm (0.025-0.045 inch) or loosen 
the thrust screw 1/2 turn after tightening the thrust screw, hand-tight, 
against the ring gear.

1997 L-Series Tandem Vehicles Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Drive Unit

The 145-Series and 160-Series forward axle drive units of these tandem 
axles have a single-reduction, through-drive carrier. The drive gearing 
consists of a two-helical gear train and a hypoid ring gear and pinion. Bevel 
gears are used in the main differential and the inter-axle differential.

[FIGURE: E78691A.gif]

The inter-axle differential is located behind the helical drive gear on 
the input shaft. The forward side gear of the inter-axle differential is part 
of the upper helical gear hub and the through-shaft is splined to the rear 
side gear of the inter-axle differential.

[FIGURE: E7870C.gif]

The 160-Series axle is different from the 145-Series axle in the

The 160-Series axle has a wider helical driven gear. 

There are two notches on the inter-axle differential case of the 
160-Series axle. The notches permit the differential case to clear the helical 
driven gear when the input shaft assembly is removed from the carrier.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Pressurized Lubrication System 

The forward axle can be equipped with an optional pressurized 
lubrication system. This filtered system has an oil pump that is driven by the 
input shaft and circulates lubricant to the journals in the forward and rear 
input shaft bearings and through the inter-axle differential.

================================================================================
PAGE 4610
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 05-02C: Axle, Rockwell Tandem, Forward Carriers

1997 L-Series Tandem Vehicles Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Driver-Controlled Main Differential Lock 

Both the forward and rear axles can be equipped with an optional 
driver-controlled main differential lock. This differential lock is operated 
by an air-actuated shift unit that is mounted on the carrier. When the 
differential lock is activated, the shift collar is moved along the splines of 
the axle shaft toward the differential case. When the splines on the collar 
are engaged with the splines on the differential case, the axle shaft and the 
differential assembly are locked together. 

When the carrier operates in the locked position, there is no 
differential action between the wheels of the axle. When the carrier is 
operated in the unlocked position, there is normal differential action between 
the wheels at all times.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Differential Carrier

 NOTE: For axles without an oil pump, omit Steps 2, 3 and 4.

 Removal 

Remove the oil drain plug from bottom of axle housing and drain 
lubricant from the assembly. 

Remove the oil filter shield from the input bearing cage. 

 CAUTION: There can be approximately 0.47 liter (one pint) of lubricant remaining 
in the filter. Be careful that the oil does not spill when removing the 
filter. 

Use a filter strap wrench to remove the oil filter. Replace it with a 
new filter at assembly.

[FIGURE: E78741A.gif]

Remove the oil filter adapter, if necessary. 

For axles so equipped, shift differential lock into locked (engaged) 
position. Refer to Driver-Controlled Differential Lock Engagement
Procedures in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Remove the stud nuts or capscrews and the washers from the flanges of 
both axle shafts.

[FIGURE: E7875C.gif]

Washer

Loosen the tapered dowels in the flanges of both axle shafts, if used, 
as follows:

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT THE ROUND DRIVING LUGS ON THE 
FLANGES OF AXLE SHAFTS. LUGS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

 NOTE: A 1-1/2-inch diameter brass hammer can be used for a drift. 

Hold a 1-1/2-inch diameter brass drift against the center of the axle 
shaft, inside the round driving lugs.

Hit the end of the drift with a large hammer (five to six pounds) and 
the axle shaft and tapered dowels will loosen.

[FIGURE: E51311A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use a chisel or wedge to loosen the axle shafts and dowels. The 
chisel or wedge can damage the hub, axle shafts and if used, the oil seals. 

Remove the tapered dowels, if used. Remove both axle shafts from the 
axle assembly.

Disconnect the forward and rear driveshafts. 

Disconnect the air lines at the inter-axle differential and main 
differential lock shift unit. 

 CAUTION: Do not use a hammer to loosen or remove the output yoke or flange. A 
hammer can damage the parts and cause difficulty with alignment. 

Remove the output shaft nut, washer and output yoke. Use a suitable 
yoke puller to remove the output yoke from the shaft.

[FIGURE: E79021A.gif]

Position a hydraulic roller jack under the differential carrier to 
support the assembly. 

Remove the bearing cage capscrews and washers. Pull the bearing cage, 
bearings and shaft assembly from the axle housing. If necessary, loosen the 
cage from the housing with a soft mallet. Be careful that the oil seal is not 
damaged.

[FIGURE: E79031A.gif]

Remove all but the top two carrier-to-housing capscrews or stud nuts 
and washers.

[FIGURE: E79041A.gif]

Loosen, but do not remove, the top two carrier-to-housing fasteners. 
The fasteners will hold the carrier in the housing. 

Loosen the differential carrier in the axle housing. Use a leather 
mallet to hit the mounting flange of carrier at several points. 

Remove the top two capscrews or stud nuts and washers that hold the 
assembly in the axle housing. 

 CAUTION: When using a pry bar, be careful not to damage the carrier or housing 
flange. Damage to these surfaces will cause oil leaks. 

Remove the carrier from the axle housing using the hydraulic roller 
jack. Use a pry bar that has a round end to help remove the carrier from the 
housing.

Release air pressure, if used to shift the differential into the locked 
(engaged) position, on axles equipped with main differential lock. Disconnect 
the air hose from the shift unit. 

Lift the differential carrier by the input yoke or flange and put the 
assembly in a suitable repair stand. Use Endless Lifting Sling D87L-1000-A or 
equivalent. Do not lift by hand.

[FIGURE: E79051A.gif]

 Installation 

 WARNING: BE CAREFUL WHEN USING CLEANING SOLVENTS. FOLLOW THE SOLVENT 
MANUFACTURER'S INSTRUCTIONS FOR SAFE USE TO PREVENT INJURY. 

Clean the inside of the axle housing and the mounting surface where the 
carrier fastens. Use a cleaning solvent and clean rags to remove dirt. Blow 
dry the cleaned areas with air. 

Inspect the axle housing for damage. Repair or replace the axle housing. 

Check for loose studs, if used, in the mounting surface of the housing 
where the carrier fastens. Remove and clean the studs that are loose. 

Apply liquid adhesive to the threaded holes. Install the studs in the 
axle housing. Tighten the studs to 203-312 Nm (150-230 lb-ft). 

 CAUTION: On axles that use a main differential lock, the lock must be shifted 
into and held in the locked (engaged) position. The locked position gives 
enough clearance between the shift collar and the axle housing to permit the 
installation of the carrier. 

 NOTE: When the differential carrier is to be installed into the axle housing, 
the shift collar must be held in the engaged position. This can be done by 
keeping the air pressure applied to the shift cylinder, or by using the manual 
engaging bolt. Failure to keep the differential in the locked (engaged) 
position will make it impossible to install the carrier assembly into the axle 
housing. After the differential carrier is installed into the axle housing, 
shift the differential into the unlocked (disengaged) position to permit the 
installation of the left-hand axle shaft. 

Use the following procedure if an auxiliary air supply is available. 

 NOTE: A similar tool can be made from a damaged left-hand axle shaft by 
cutting off approximately 610 mm (24 inches) from the spline end. 

Before the differential carrier is installed into the housing, install 
the left-hand axle shaft through the shift collar and into the side gear. (The 
axle shaft is being used as a spline alignment tool.)

 WARNING: DO NOT USE YOUR HANDS TO HOLD THE COLLAR IN POSITION. INJURY CAN RESULT 
WHEN AIR PRESSURE IS APPLIED TO THE ACTUATOR. 
Align the splines of the shift collar and differential case half by 
rotating the axle shaft tool or drive pinion.

Connect an auxiliary air supply to the actuator assembly. 

Apply and hold pressure to the actuator assembly. The air pressure will 
move the shift collar to engage the differential case half and lock the 
assembly. 

Rotate the axle shaft tool or the drive pinion one complete rotation to 
the right or left if the shift collar has not moved the full distance on the 
splines of the differential case half. 

 NOTE: Continue to hold the main differential in the locked (engaged) position 
with air pressure until the differential carrier is completely installed in 
the axle housing. 

Remove the axle shaft tool from the carrier.

Use the following procedure if an auxiliary air supply is not available. 

Align the splines of the shift collar and the differential case half. 
This can be done by hand or by installing the left-hand axle shaft through the 
shift collar and into the side gear. Refer to Steps 5a and 5b of this 
procedure. 

Install the manual engaging capscrew into the threaded hole in the 
center of the cylinder cover.

 NOTE: When the manual engaging capscrew is removed from the service position

Remove the plug and gasket from their position. Remove the manual

Clean the plug, gasket, cylinder cover, and threaded hole in the center 
of the cylinder cover. 

Install the plug and gasket into their operating position in the

Tighten the plug to 20-34 Nm (15-25 lb-ft). Tighten 
the manual engaging capscrew to 20-34 Nm (15-25 lb-ft). 

Install the gaskets

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Driver-Controlled Differential Lock Engagement Procedures 

 NOTE: The Rockwell carrier models with driver-controlled differential lock 
equipment are manufactured in metric dimensions and sizes. When these carriers 
are serviced, it is important to use the correct metric size tools on the 
fasteners. Refer to the metric torque chart at the back of this manual. 

 NOTE: If the axle shafts were removed for towing with the differential in the 
unlocked (disengaged) position, install the right-hand axle shaft into the 
housing before continuing. 

Before the differential carrier can be removed or installed, the 
differential lock must be shifted into and held in the locked (engaged) 
position. The locked position gives enough clearance between the shift collar 
and the axle housing to permit the removal or installation of the carrier.

To shift into the locked position, use either the following air 
pressure method or the manual engaging method below. 

 Air Pressure Method 

Remove the drain plug from the bottom of the housing and drain the 
lubricant. 

 WARNING: DO NOT START THE VEHICLE ENGINE AND ENGAGE THE TRANSMISSION WITH ONE 
WHEEL RAISED FROM THE FLOOR. WHEN THE DIFFERENTIAL IS IN LOCKED (ENGAGED) 
POSITION, POWER WILL GO TO THE WHEEL ON THE FLOOR AND CAUSE THE VEHICLE TO 
MOVE. 

Raise the right-hand wheel of the drive axle off the floor with a hoist 
or jack.

 WARNING: DO NOT WORK UNDER A VEHICLE SUPPORTED ONLY BY JACKS. JACKS CAN SLIP OR 
TIP OVER AND CAUSE INJURY. 

Put a jack stand under the right-hand spring seat to hold the vehicle 
in the raised position.

Disconnect the driveline from the pinion input yoke. 

Disconnect the vehicle air line from the differential lock actuator 
assembly. 

 NOTE: If an auxiliary air supply is not available, refer to Manual Engaging 
Method of locking the differential. 

Connect an auxiliary air supply to the differential lock actuator 
assembly.

Apply and hold air pressure to the actuator assembly. The air pressure 
will move the shift collar to engage with the splines on the differential case 
half and lock the assembly. 

Make sure that the shift collar has moved the full distance on the 
splines of the differential case half. Rotate the drive pinion or the 
right-hand wheel until the right-hand wheel makes one complete rotation 
(forward or backward). 

Continue to hold the main differential in the locked position with air 
pressure until the carrier assembly is completely removed from the axle 
housing. 

 Manual Engaging Method 

If an auxiliary air supply is not available or if the differential 
carrier is to be stored for later use, use this manual engaging method.

[FIGURE: E7913D.gif]

Follow Steps 1 through 5 of the Air Pressure Method. 

Remove the plug and gasket from the hole in the center of the cylinder

Remove the manual engaging capscrew from the top storage hole in the

 NOTE: The storage hole for the plug and gasket is the opposite end of the

 CAUTION: There will be a small amount of spring resistance felt when you turn in

capscrew threads will be damaged. 

Turn the manual engaging capscrew to the right until the head is 
approximately 6.35 mm (0.25 inch) from the cylinder cover. Do not turn the 
capscrew beyond its normal stop. The capscrew is now in the service position 
and the main differential lock is completely engaged.

A high resistance on the capscrew indicates that the splines of the 
shift collar and the differential case half are not aligned or engaged. To 
align the splines use the following procedure:

Rotate the drive pinion or left-hand wheel to align the splines of the 
shift collar and case half while turning in the manual engaging capscrew. 

When the normal amount of spring resistance is again felt on the 
capscrew, the splines are aligned. Continue to turn in the manual engaging 
capscrew until the head is approximately 6.35 mm (0.25 inch) from the cylinder 
cover.

Differential Shift Assembly, Removal 

Remove the differential lock sliding shift collar by tapping out the 
two retainer roll pins until they are level with the inner face of the shift

[FIGURE: E79141A.gif]

Remove the differential lock shift unit, if required. 

Remove the sensor switch and lock nut.

[FIGURE: E80851A.gif]

Remove the shift shaft from the shift fork. 

 NOTE: Some models use Silastic® seal instead of the

 NOTE: A roll pin is installed in the shift shaft and is used as a stop for
