REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Main Differential Case and Ring Gear Assembly

 Removal 

Move the carrier so that the ring gear is toward you. 

Use a punch and a hammer to mark the position of the bearing caps on 
the legs of the differential carrier. 

[FIGURE: E79511A.gif]

Use a hammer and a drift to remove the adjusting ring lock pins on the 
bearing caps.

 CAUTION: Do not hit the adjusting ring with a hammer. Do not use a hammer and a 
drift to loosen the adjusting rings. These methods damage the adjusting rings. 

Use a T bar wrench or equivalent tool to loosen the adjusting rings. Do 
not remove the adjusting rings.

[FIGURE: E79521A.gif]

Remove the capscrews and the washers that fasten the bearing caps to 
the legs of the differential carrier.

 NOTE: Each bearing cap must be installed on the carrier leg from which it was 
removed. The cap is matched to the carrier leg. Do not mix bearing caps on 
carrier legs.

Remove the bearing caps, the adjusting rings and the bearing cups from 
the differential carrier.

[FIGURE: E7771B.gif]

Use Endless Lifting Sling D87L-1000-A or equivalent to remove the main 
differential case and ring gear assembly from the differential carrier.

[FIGURE: E7772B.gif]

 NOTE: If either the bearing cup or the cone needs to be replaced, both parts 
must be replaced in a set from the same manufacturer. 

 NOTE: The bearing cones are not interchangeable.

Use a suitable bearing puller to remove the cones if the bearing cones 
on the main differential case need to be replaced.

[FIGURE: E79531A.gif]

 Installation 

 Install a new cone and cup in a set from the same manufacturer if the 
bearing cones on the main differential case were removed. Use a press and a 
sleeve to install the cones on the case. Press on the inner race of the bearing.

[FIGURE: E79711B.gif]

Clean and dry the bearing cups and bores of the carrier legs and 
bearing caps. 

Lubricate the bearing cups and cones with the lubricant used in the 
axle housing. 

Apply Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSK-M2G349-A1 in the bearing bores of the carrier legs and 
bearing caps. Refer to Section 05-00 . 

Install the cups over the bearing cones. 

Using Endless Lifting Sling D87L-1000-A or equivalent, lift the main 
differential case and ring gear assembly and install in the carrier. The 
bearing cups must be flat against the bores between the carrier legs.

[FIGURE: E7824C.gif]

Install both of the bearing adjusting rings into position between the 
carrier legs. Turn each adjusting ring hand-tight against the bearing cup.

[FIGURE: E7825B.gif]

Install the bearing caps over the bearings and adjusting rings in the 
correct location as marked before removal. 

[FIGURE: E79721A.gif]

 WARNING: WEAR EYE PROTECTION. DO NOT HIT STEEL PARTS WITH A STEEL HAMMER. PARTS 
OR TOOLS CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY. 

 CAUTION: The bearing caps must be correctly installed or the adjusting rings 
will be damaged by cross-threading. Forcing the caps into position damages the 
caps and the carrier housing. 

Hit each bearing cap into position with light leather, plastic or 
rubber mallet. The caps must fit easily against the bearings, adjusting rings 
and carrier. Do not force the bearing caps into position.

 NOTE: The lock pins for the adjusting rings are installed after the tooth 
contact pattern is checked. 

Install the capscrews and washers that hold the bearing caps to the 
carrier. Tighten the capscrews by hand four to six turns. Then, tighten the 
capscrews to 650-810 Nm (480-600 lb-ft) on 160-Series or to 
434-542 Nm (320-400 lb-ft) on 145-Series.

Adjust preload on the differential side gear bearings. Refer to Section 05-00 . 

Check the ring gear runout. Refer to Section 05-00 . 

Adjust the ring gear backlash. Refer to Section 05-00 .

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or

[FIGURE: E79191A.gif]

[FIGURE: E7920C.gif]

Install the flatwasher (when used) or apply Silastic®

 (7-12 lb-ft).

Slide the shift collar into the fork and engage the shift collar 
splines with the splines of the differential case. Use the manual engaging 
capscrew to move the shift collar splines into the differential case splines. 
Refer to Manual Engaging Method under Driver-Controlled Differential Lock 
Engagement Procedures in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Hold the shift collar in the locked (engaged) position and tap in the 
two roll pins in the shift fork ends until they are level with the outer yoke 
faces. 

[FIGURE: E7924B.gif]

While the shift collar is still in the locked position, put the sensor 
switch (with the lock nut loosely attached) into its hole. 

Connect a battery/bulb tester to the sensor switch and rotate the 
switch into its hole until contact with the shift fork causes the light to go 
on. Turn the switch one additional revolution and tighten the jam nut to 34-47 Nm
 (25-35 lb-ft).

 NOTE: For carriers without the differential lock (less air shift), assemble 
the sensor switch plug and cover plate as follows: 

Install the washer and plug into the hole for the sensor switch. 
Tighten the plug to 61-75 Nm (45-55 lb-ft).

the carrier. Refer to Section 05-00 . 

Install the four washers and capscrews. Tighten the capscrews to 9-16 Nm
 (7-12 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: E79341B.gif]

the yoke or flange to the input shaft.

[FIGURE: E79351A.gif]

Remove the capscrews and the washers that fasten the input bearing cage

[FIGURE: E79361A.gif]

Move the carrier so that the input shaft is in a vertical position with

Remove the input shaft, the oil pump (if used) and the inter-axle

145-Series Carriers or 160-Series Carriers for the appropriate procedure.

 145-Series Carriers 

Lift the input shaft assembly from the differential carrier. If 
necessary, tap on the bearing cage with a brass or plastic mallet to separate 
the cage from the carrier.

Place the input shaft assembly on a bench. 

[FIGURE: E79371A.gif]

 160-Series Carriers 

 CAUTION: On 160-Series carriers, this procedure MUST be followed. There are two 
notches on the case of the inter-axle differential. One of the notches on the 
case must be aligned with the helical driven gear. If the notch is not aligned 
over the gear, the gear will prevent the removal of the input shaft assembly 
and cause damage to the assembly. 
Lift the input shaft assembly until the bearing cage is separated 
from the carrier. If necessary, tap on the bearing cage with a brass or 
plastic mallet to separate the cage from the carrier.

Lift the input shaft assembly slowly. 

Place the input shaft assembly on a bench.

[FIGURE: E80861A.gif]

 Rotating Inter-Axle Differential Case to Remove Input Shaft Assembly 

 NOTE: There are two notches on the side of the inter-axle differential case. 
When one of the notches is aligned with the helical driven gear, the case can 
be removed. 

If the input shaft assembly comes out of the carrier easily, remove 
the assembly. 

If the input shaft assembly cannot be removed easily, the case of the 
inter-axle differential must be rotated. Rotate the input shaft until one of 
the notches on the case is aligned over the helical driven gear. Remove the 
input shaft assembly from the carrier.

[FIGURE: E80871A.gif]

Remove the shims from between the bearing cage and the differential 
carrier.

Remove the rear side gear and the bearing cone from the carrier. Remove 
the collar. 

[FIGURE: E79381A.gif]

 NOTE: If either the bearing cup or cone on the rear side gear needs

equivalent to remove the cone from the rear side gear, if necessary.

[FIGURE: E7939B.gif]

Use a brass drift and a hammer to remove the rear side gear bearing cup 
from the carrier, if necessary.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Main Differential Case and Ring Gear Assembly, Assembly

 WARNING: DO NOT USE AN OPEN FLAME SUCH AS A TORCH FOR THIS PROCEDURE. 

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE CLOTHING AND GLOVES THAT WILL PROTECT YOU FROM INJURY WHEN 
YOU TOUCH THE HOT RING GEAR. 

 CAUTION: Do not press a cold ring gear on the flanged half of the differential 
case. A cold ring gear will damage the case because of the tight fit. Metal 
particles between the parts will cause gear runout that exceeds Rockwell 
specification of 0.2 mm (0.008 inch). 

Expand the ring gear by heating the gear in a tank of water to a 
temperature of 71°-82°C (160°
 -180°F) for 10 to 15 minutes.

Use a lifting tool to safely lift the ring gear from the tank of water. 

Immediately install the ring gear on the flanged half of the 
differential case. If the ring gear does not fit easily on the flange, heat 
the gear again in a tank of hot water. Rotate the ring gear to align the 
fastener holes in the case with the holes in the gear. 

Install the bolts, washers and nuts that fasten the ring gear to the 
flange as follows:

Install the bolts from the gear side of the assembly. The heads of the 
bolts must be against the ring gear. 

Install the washers on the bolts from the flange side of the assembly. 

Install the nuts and tighten to 265-355 Nm (196-262 
lb-ft) on 160-Series or to 217-285 Nm (160-210 lb-ft) on 
145-Series.

 (75-95 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: E7959B.gif]

 Assembly and Installation 

 NOTE: The depth of the drive pinion in the carrier is controlled by the 
thickness of the shim pack between the pinion inner bearing cup and the 
carrier. Adjust the depth of the drive pinion by changing the thickness of the 
shim pack. Increase the thickness of the shim pack to increase the depth of 
the drive pinion. Decrease the thickness of the shim pack to decrease the 
depth of the drive pinion. 

[FIGURE: E7960D.gif]

Shims

The preload of the bearings on the drive pinion is controlled by: 

A gear spacer between the outer bearing on the drive pinion and the 
helical driven gear. 

A cone spacer between the inner bearing on the drive pinion and the 
helical driven gear. 

Adjust the preload by changing the size of the gear spacer between the 
outer bearing on the drive pinion and the helical driven gear. Use a thicker 
gear spacer to decrease the preload. Use a thinner gear spacer to increase the 
preload. 

If the depth of the drive pinion is changed, the thickness of the gear 
spacer must also be changed the same amount. When the depth of the drive 
pinion is increased, the location of the bearings on the drive pinion must be 
increased the same amount. When the depth of the drive pinion is decreased, 
the location of the bearings on the drive pinion must be decreased the same 
amount. For example, if a 0.0762-mm (0.003-inch) shim is added to the shim 
pack to increase the depth of the drive pinion, then a 0.0762-mm (0.003-inch) 
larger spacer must be installed to keep the preload of the drive pinion 
bearings. If a 0.0762-mm (0.003-inch) shim is removed from the shim pack to 
decrease the depth of the drive pinion, then a 0.0762-mm (0.003-inch) smaller 
spacer must be installed to keep the preload of the drive pinion bearings.

 NOTE: The helical driven gear, the cone spacer and the gear spacer are 
installed when the bearing preload on the drive pinion is checked and 
adjusted. 

Determine the correct thickness of the shim pack between the pinion 
inner bearing cup and the carrier if a new ring gear and drive pinion are 
being installed. Refer to Section 05-00 for shim pack adjustment procedure 
before temporarily assembling and installing the drive pinion assembly 
according to this procedure. Install the drive pinion assembly temporarily 
according to this procedure if the original ring gear and drive pinion are 
being installed. 

Use a press and a sleeve to install the inner bearing cone on the drive 
pinion, if removed. Place the sleeve on the inner race of the bearing. Apply 
pressure until the bottom of the cone touches the shoulder on the pinion.

[FIGURE: E79611A.gif]

Apply the lubricant that is used in the axle housing to the bearing 
cups and cones. 

Install the shim pack and the inner bearing cup of the drive pinion 
according to the following procedure, if removed. 

 NOTE: If a new ring gear and drive pinion are being installed, a shim pack 
size must be determined and a new shim pack installed. Refer to Section 05-00 
for shim pack adjustment procedure.

Position the carrier on a press so that the legs of the carrier are 
toward the top of the press.

Install the correct amount of shims in the bore for the inner bearing 
cup of the drive pinion. 

Place the cup in the bore.

[FIGURE: E79621A.gif]

Position supports under the differential carrier so that the carrier is 
level. 

Place a sleeve or a bearing driver tool on the cup and press the cup 
into the bore until the bottom of the cup touches the shims. If a press is not 
available, use a sleeve, a brass drift or a bearing driver tool and a hammer 
to install the cup.

[FIGURE: E79631A.gif]

Install the outer bearing cup for the drive pinion according to the 
following procedure, if removed. 

Position the carrier in a press so that the legs of the carrier are 
toward the bottom of the press. Position supports under the carrier so that 
the carrier is level. 

Place the outer bearing cup for the drive pinion in the bore of the 
carrier. 

Use a sleeve or a bearing driver tool and a press to install the cup. 
Press the cup into the carrier until the bottom of the cup touches the bottom 
of the bore. If a press is not available, use a sleeve, a brass drift or a 
bearing driver tool and a hammer to install the cup.

[FIGURE: E79641A.gif]

Install the drive pinion in the carrier according to the following 
procedure.

Position the drive pinion in the carrier so that the pinion is through 
the inner and the outer bearing cups. 

Position the carrier in a press so that the legs of the carrier are 
toward the bottom of the press. Position supports under the carrier so that 
the carrier is level. Place a support under head of the drive pinion so that 
the inner bearing cone on the pinion shaft touches the inner bearing cup in 
the carrier. 

Place the outer bearing cone on the pinion shaft. 

Use a press and a sleeve to install the bearing cone on the pinion. 
Apply 1815 kg (4000 lb.) of pressure to make sure that the bearing cone is 
correctly installed. 

[FIGURE: E79651A.gif]

Install the washer and the nut on the shaft of the drive pinion. Place 
a wood block between the teeth of the pinion and the inner wall of the carrier 
to prevent the pinion from turning. Tighten the nut to 1627-2034 Nm
 (1200-1500 lb-ft).

carrier. The boss on the fork must be toward the adjusting bolt of the 
carrier. 

Position the shift shaft in the carrier so that the smaller part of the 
shaft goes through the fork and the spring. 

Install the O-ring on the piston, if removed. Apply the lubricant used 
in the axle housing to the O-ring. 

Install the piston into the shift cylinder. 

Apply silicone gasket material on the mounting surface of the cover of 
the shift cylinder. 

Install the shift cylinder over the shift shaft. Install the 
socket-head capscrews that fasten the cover to the carrier. Tighten the 
capscrews to 9-16 Nm (7-12 lb-ft).

 NOTE: The adjusting screw is set to the specified distance after the input 
shaft assembly is installed in the carrier. 

Install the adjusting screw and jam nut for the shift shaft in the 
carrier.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Input Bearing End Play

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T57T-4851-B

Specification: End play of the input shaft: 0.050-0.200 mm (0.002-0.008 inch). 

[FIGURE: E80021A.gif]

Place a wood block between the ring gear and the differential case to 
keep the ring gear from rotating.

Install capscrews, but not the washers, that fasten the input bearing 
cage to the carrier. Rotate the input shaft in each direction to make sure the 
bearings are correctly installed while tightening the capscrews by hand. Do 
not tighten the capscrews to the specified torque.

Use a feeler gauge to measure the gap between the input bearing cage 
and the differential carrier. Check the gap at four equally spaced places on 
the cage.

[FIGURE: E80031A.gif]

Add up the four measurements and determine the average gap between the 
cage and the carrier. Add 0.13 mm (0.005 inch) to the average gap measurement 
to determine the size of the shim pack between the cage and the carrier. 

Use at least three shims to build a shim pack. Place the thickest 
shim(s) in the middle of the shim pack. 

Remove the capscrews that fasten the input bearing cage to the carrier. 

Install the shim pack according to the following procedure. 

Connect a lifting device to the input yoke. Lift the input shaft 
assembly until there is a distance of 6-12 mm (0.250-0.500 inch) between the 
cage and carrier mounting surface. 

Install the shim pack under the bearing cage. Make sure the 
installation pattern of the shim pack matches the installation pattern of the 
cage.

[FIGURE: E80041A.gif]

Position the shield for the oil filter on the bearing cage. 

Install the capscrews and the washers that fasten the cage to the 
carrier. Make sure the capscrews are aligned with the holes in the shim pack. 
Tighten the capscrews so the threads engage in the holes of the carrier. 

Lower the input shaft assembly so the cage and the shim pack are 
installed against the carrier. Remove the lifting device from the yoke or 
flange. 

Tighten the capscrews to 102-129 Nm (75-95 lb-ft) 
while rotating the input shaft in each direction to make sure the bearings are 
correctly installed. 

Remove the block of wood between the ring gear and the differential 
carrier. 

Using a holding tool such as Companion Flange Holding Tool T57T-4851-B 
to hold the input yoke or flange in a stationary position, tighten the nut to 
813-1085 Nm (600-800 lb-ft). 

Check the input shaft end play as follows:

Rotate the input shaft in each direction and push the yoke or flange 
toward the bearing cage. This makes sure that the input shaft assembly is at 
the bottom of its travel. 

Use Dial Indicator/Magnetic Base D78P-4201-B or equivalent or a C-clamp 
base to check the end play of the input bearing. Make sure the pointer of the 
dial indicator is against the top of the input shaft. Set the dial indicator 
to zero (0).

[FIGURE: E8005B.gif]

Use a pry bar and a support to push the yoke or the flange away from 
the carrier. Read the dial indicator. The reading must be 0.050-0.200 mm 
(0.002-0.008 inch). 

Add or remove shims from the shim pack if the end play of the input 
bearing is not within 0.050-0.200 mm (0.002-0.008 inch). Repeat Steps 5-9 of 
this procedure.

ADJUSTMENTS

Bearing Preload Adjustment on Drive Pinion 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spring Scale

T74P-3504-Y

If the depth of the drive pinion was changed, then the amount of the 
change must be added or subtracted to size of the spacer between the outer 
bearing cup and the helical driven gear. 

Specifications: 

New pinion bearings: 0.56-5.08 Nm (5-45 lb-in) 
rotational torque 

Used pinion bearings: 1.13-3.39 Nm (10-30 lb-in) 
rotational torque

After the correct gear tooth contact pattern is obtained and the 
correct thickness of the shim pack behind the pinion inner bearing cup is 
installed, the bearing preload on the drive pinion is adjusted. 

The preload on the inner and outer bearings of the drive pinion is 
controlled by a spacer between the helical driven gear and the outer bearing. 
Preload is adjusted by replacing the spacer between the helical driven gear 
and the outer bearing. The spacer between the helical driven gear and the 
outer bearing is available in different sizes. The spacer between the inner 
bearing and the helical driven gear is available in only one size. 

Check and record the backlash of the ring gear. 

Remove the main differential case and ring gear assembly from the 
differential carrier. 

Remove the nut and the washer from the drive pinion. 

Position the carrier in a press so that the threaded end of the pinion 
is toward the top of the press. Position supports under the flange of the 
carrier so that the carrier is level. Place a wood block under the head of the 
pinion.

[FIGURE: E9958A.gif]

If the depth of the drive pinion was changed, the thickness of the 
spacer that controls the preload of the pinion bearings must be changed the 
same amount. If shims were added to increase the depth of the drive pinion, 
then the total amount of added shims must be added to size of the spacer. If 
shims were removed to decrease the depth of the drive pinion, then the same 
amount of removed shims must be removed from the size of the spacer. 

EXAMPLE: 

Determined size of spacer for bearing preload: 12.926 mm (0.509 inch). 

Amount of shims added to increase depth of pinion: 0.076 mm (0.003 inch). 

Final size of spacer for bearing preload: 12.902 mm (0.512 inch). 

Determined size of spacer for bearing preload: 12.926 mm (0.509 inch). 

Amount of shims removed to decrease depth of pinion: 0.076 mm (0.003 
inch). 

Final size of spacer for bearing preload: 12.850 mm (0.506 inch).

 CAUTION: Do not apply pressure after the helical driven gear touches the spacer

pinion bore in the carrier. Press the gear on the drive pinion until the gear 
touches the spacer. Do not remove the wood block at this time. 

Install the correct size of spacer on the shaft on the pinion in front 
of the helical driven gear.

 NOTE: Make sure the wood block is still under the head of the drive pinion. 
The inner bearing cone on the pinion must touch the cup in the carrier. 

Use the following procedure to install the outer bearing cone on the 
shaft of the drive pinion. 

Place the outer bearing cone on the shaft of the drive pinion. 

Place a sleeve on the inner race of the outer bearing cone. 

Use a press to apply 1815 kg (4000 lb) of pressure on the bearing cone 
to install the cone on the shaft of the drive pinion. Move the carrier in both 
directions (so that the carrier pivots on the drive pinion) while the cone is 
being installed to make sure that the bearing cone is correctly installed. 

Release pressure on the bearing cone. Remove the wood block from under 
the head of the drive pinion. 

Remove the carrier from the press and place the carrier in a suitable 
repair stand. 

Install the washer and the nut on the drive pinion. Prevent the drive 
pinion assembly from rotating by using a fixture to hold the teeth of the 
helical driven gear or put wood blocks between the head of the pinion and the 
carrier wall. Tighten the nut to 1627-2034 Nm (1200-1500 
lb-ft). Remove the holding fixture or the wood blocks. 

Use a Nm (lb-in) torque wrench or a spring scale to 
check the preload of the bearings on the drive pinion. If a spring scale is 
used, refer to Step 27.

[FIGURE: E79841A.gif]

Place a Nm (lb-in) torque wrench and the correct 
socket on the nut of the drive pinion.

The end play of the output bearing is controlled by the size of the

available in increments of 0.076 mm (0.003 inch). Install the correct snap 
ring to get an end play of 0.025-0.102 mm (0.001-0.004 inch).

 (450-600 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: E8009B.gif]

be 0.025-0.102 mm (0.001-0.004 inch).

Drive Pinion Bearings Preload

 Specification: New bearings — 0.56-5.08 Nm
 (5-45 lb-in) torque. Used bearings in good condition —
 1.13-3.39 Nm (10-30 lb-in) torque.

 Adjustment: Preload is controlled by the thickness of the 
spacer between bearing cones. To increase preload install a thinner spacer. To 
decrease preload install a thicker spacer.

Drive Pinion — Depth in Carrier

 Specification: Install the correct amount of shims between 
the inner bearing cup of the drive pinion and the carrier. To calculate, use 
the old shim pack thickness and the new and old pinion cone numbers.

 Adjustment: Change the thickness of the shim pack to get a 
good gear tooth contact pattern.

Hypoid Gear Set — Tooth Contact Patterns (Hand Rolled)

 Specification: Toward the toe of the gear tooth and in the 
center between the top and bottom of the tooth.

 Adjustment: Tooth contact patterns are controlled by the 
thickness of the shim pack between the inner bearing cup of the drive pinion 
and the carrier, and by ring gear backlash. To move the contact pattern lower, 
increase the thickness of the shim pack between inner bearing cup of the drive 
pinion and the carrier. To move the contact pattern higher, decrease the 
thickness of the shim pack between the inner bearing cup and the drive pinion 
and the carrier. To move the contact pattern toward the toe of the tooth 
decrease backlash of the ring gear. To move the contact pattern toward the 
heel of the tooth increase backlash of the ring gear.

Main Differential Bearings Preload

 Specification: 1.7-3.9 Nm (15-35 lb-in) 
torque or expansion between bearing caps: 0.08-0.22 mm (0.003-0.009 inch).

 Adjustment: Preload is controlled by tightening both 
adjusting rings after zero end play is reached.

Main Differential Gears Rolling (Rotating) Resistance

 Specification: 68 Nm (50 lb-ft) torque 
applied to one side gear.

Output Bearing End Play and Preload

 Specification: 0.025-0.102 mm (0.001-0.004 inch) bearing 
end play.

 Adjustment: End play is controlled by the size of the snap 
ring in the output bearing cage. Increase end play by installing a thinner 
snap ring. Decrease end play by installing a thicker snap ring.

 NOTE: If the end play on the output bearing measures zero (0), a thinner snap 
ring is required.

Ring Gear Backlash

 Specification: 0.20-0.46 mm (0.008-0.018 inch); 0.30 mm 
(0.012 inch) for a new gearset.

 Adjustment: Backlash is controlled by the position of the 
ring gear. Change backlash within specifications to get a good tooth contact 
pattern. To increase backlash, move the ring gear away from the drive pinion. 
To decrease backlash, move the ring gear toward the drive pinion.

Ring Gear Runout

 Specification: 0.20 mm (0.008 inch) maximum.

Sensor Switch (Carriers with Differential Lock Only)

 Adjustment: Shift the differential to the locked position. 
Connect a test light to the sensor switch. Tighten the sensor switch into the 
carrier until the test light illuminates. Tighten the sensor switch one half 
to one additional turns. Tighten the jam nut to 34-47 Nm 
(25-35 lb-ft).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Hydraulic 

 CAUTION: The hydraulic brake system consists of two separate fluid systems, the 
service brake master cylinder system and the Hydro-Max booster/parking brake 
system, that use two distinctly different, incompatible hydraulic fluids. DO 
NOT MIX THESE FLUIDS. 

The split hydraulic service brake system provides two separate 
hydraulic subsystems, one of which actuates the front disc brakes (secondary 
subsystem) and the other which actuates the rear drum brakes (primary 
subsystem). Brake power assist is provided by a Hydro-Max hydraulic booster.

The service brake system consists of the following components:

Hydro-Max booster and brake master cylinder

electric motor pump

front disc brakes

rear drum brakes

warning lamps/buzzer

Hydro-Max monitor

electric motor pump relay

engine-driven brake pump with remote reservoir

The parking brake system consists of the following components:

parking brake control valve 

parking brake unitized valve 

spring chambers

warning lamps/buzzer

 Brake Master Cylinder/Hydro-Max Booster Service Brake System 

The service brake master cylinder system operates the front disc brakes 
and rear drum brakes and requires a glycol-based hydraulic fluid such as Ford 
High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A. Always use new clean fluid dispensed 
from a clean, tightly sealed container. Do not reuse brake fluid from a 
vehicle. The service brake system is filled through the plastic reservoir of 
the brake master cylinder which is labeled FILL ONLY WITH DOT 3 TYPE BRAKE 
FLUID.

Use of a petroleum-based hydraulic fluid (power steering or automatic 
transmission fluid) in the brake master cylinder will cause swelling of the 
rubber components in the system. If the service brake system becomes 
contaminated by improper usage of petroleum-based hydraulic fluid, the rubber 
seals must be replaced in the brake master cylinder, front wheel disc brake 
calipers and rear wheel brake cylinders.

 Hydro-Max Booster/Parking Brake System 

The Hydro-Max power service brake system is composed of a brake master 
cylinder, a reserve system electric motor pump, a hydraulic-powered booster, 
an electric relay and electric monitor and a warning system. It supplies a 
hydraulic assist in service brake application.

The Hydro-Max booster and spring-set rear wheel parking brake system 
(spring chambers) require either power steering fluid or automatic 
transmission fluid such as Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX 
or MERCON® equivalent. The Hydro-Max/parking brake system is 
filled through the metal remote-mounted reservoir of the engine-driven brake 
pump. This reservoir is labeled FILL ONLY WITH THE RECOMMENDED POWER STEERING 
FLUID. For a more detailed description of the brake pump, refer to Section 06-07A .

Use of a glycol-based hydraulic brake fluid in the Hydro-Max 
booster/parking brake system will cause swelling of the rubber components in 
the system. If the brake booster and the parking brake system have become 
contaminated by use of glycol-based hydraulic fluid, the rubber seals must be 
replaced in the parking brake control valve, parking brake unitized valve, 
Hydro-Max Booster, engine-driven brake pump and electric motor pump.

Section 06-00: Brake System, Hydraulic, Service

1997 LN-7000 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake Master Cylinder, Dual

The dual hydraulic system brake master cylinder contains two separate 
pressure chambers, primary and secondary, for actuation of the two separate 
service brake subsystems. Each pressure chamber has a piston/actuator 
subassembly containing a preloaded spring and a return spring. In the released 
position, actuators of both the primary and secondary pistons are in contact 
with their respective compensating valve stems which project into the cylinder 
bore. This maintains the valves in an open position, which allows hydraulic 
fluid in the reservoir to replenish any fluid displaced from the cylinder 
bore. 

As the brake pedal is depressed, the initial forward travel of the 
primary piston moves the primary actuator away from its compensating valve 
counterpart, permitting the valve to seat. Closure of this valve shuts off the 
passage between the primary pressure chamber and the reservoir section serving 
the primary chamber. 

Further movement of the primary piston creates a pressure in the 
primary pressure chamber, causing the secondary piston and actuator to move. 
As the secondary piston and actuator move, the secondary compensating valve 
closes, shutting off the passage between the secondary pressure chamber and 
the reservoir section serving the secondary chamber. Additional movement of 
the primary piston causes both chambers to build pressure. 

When the load on the primary piston is removed, fluid pressure in each 
chamber, combined with return spring force, causes the primary and secondary 
pistons to return to their initial released positions. Each actuator opens its 
respective compensating valve, reopening the passage between the individual 
reservoir sections and its associated pressure chamber. 

Should the rate of release be great enough to cause a partial vacuum in 
a chamber or should additional fluid be required because of the brake 
adjustment or lining wear, the compensating valve will open to allow 
replenishment of fluid in the cylinder bore. 

Any excess fluid remaining at the end of the stroke due to "pumping" or 
volume change due to temperature fluctuation is released as the compensating 
valve ports open.

Brakes, Front Disc 

The front disc brakes are the dual-piston, rail-slider type. Two

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brakes, Rear Drum 

The rear hydraulic drum brake consists of two brake shoe and lining 
assemblies, an adjuster cylinder assembly and a park cylinder assembly. The 
adjuster assembly acts as a conventional wheel cylinder and adjusts the brake 
shoes to maintain a lining-to-brake drum clearance within a specified range. 
The park cylinder assembly acts as a conventional wheel cylinder and also 
expands and retracts the brake shoes to set and release the drum brakes as a 
parking brake.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Parking

 NOTE: Do not disassemble the parking brake control valve. It is serviced as 
an assembly. 

The parking brake control valve is actuated by a push-pull knob. 
Pushing the knob in releases the parking brake, and pulling the knob out 
applies the parking brake.

The parking brake unitized valve controls the pressurizing and 
exhausting of fluid during the apply and release mode to the spring chambers. 
It also sets and maintains operating pressure and serves the function of a 
diverter valve, a relay valve, a pressure check valve and a pressure relief 
valve. 

The spring chambers produce the mechanical force to actuate the park 
cylinder in the rear drum brake. For a more detailed description of the wheel 
cylinders, refer to Section 06-02B .

For a more detailed description of the parking brake system and spring 
chambers, refer to Section 06-05B .

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Hydraulic Brake System

 Inspection and Verification 

Occasional brake squeal can be caused by environmental conditions such 
as cold, heat, rain, snow, salt and mud. This occasional squeal is not a 
functional problem and does not indicate any loss in brake effectiveness.

 NOTE: After any major brake system or component overhaul, the system should 
be purged of old fluid.

Always make the following preliminary checks before testing the brake 
system.

Check the service brake system fluid level in the brake master cylinder 
reservoir. If the fluid level is not to the level of the bottom of the rings 
on the brake master cylinder reservoir, add Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake 
Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A.

Check the parking brake system fluid level in the remote brake pump 
reservoir with the engine off and the parking brake applied. The fluid level 
must show between the ADD and FULL markings on the dipstick. If the fluid is 
below the ADD mark, add Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or 
MERCON® equivalent.

 Road Test 

Perform a road test to compare actual vehicle braking performance with 
the performance standards expected by the driver. The ability of the test 
driver to make valid comparisons and detect performance deficiencies will 
depend on experience. 

The driver should have a thorough knowledge of brake system operation 
and accepted general performance guidelines in order to make good comparisons 
and detect performance concerns.

An experienced brake technician will always establish a route that will 
be used for all brake diagnosis road tests. The road selected will be 
reasonably smooth and level. Gravel or bumpy roads are not suitable because 
the surface does not allow the tires to grip the road equally. Crowned roads 
should be avoided because of the large amount of weight shifted to the low set 
of wheels on this type of road. Once the route is established and consistently 
used, the road surface variable can be eliminated from the test results. 

Before a road test, get a complete description of the customer concerns 
or suspected condition. From the description, the technician's experience will 
allow the technician to match possible causes with symptoms. Certain 
components will be tagged as possible suspects while others will be eliminated 
by the evidence. More importantly, the customer's description can reveal 
unsafe conditions which should be checked or corrected before the road test. 
The description will also help form the basic approach to the road test by 
narrowing the concern to specific components, vehicle speed or conditions. 

Begin the road test with a general brake performance check. Keeping the 
description in mind, test the brakes at different vehicle speeds using both 
light and heavy brake pedal pressure. To determine if the problem is in the 
front or rear braking system, first use the service brake pedal, then use the 
parking brake. If the condition occurs when the service brake pedal is 
depressed, it could be in the front or rear. If the condition does not occur 
when the parking brake is applied, this is an indication that the problem is 
in the front brakes.

Avoid locking the brakes and sliding the tires. Locked brakes and 
sliding tires do not indicate brake efficiency. A heavily braked and turning 
wheel will stop the vehicle in less distance than locked brakes. If the 
condition becomes evident during this check, make sure it fits the description 
given before the road test. If the condition is not evident, attempt to 
duplicate the condition using the information from the description. 

If a concern exists, use the symptom chart in this section in order to 
isolate it to a specific subsystem and condition description. From this 
description, a list of possible sources can be used to further narrow the 
cause to a specific component or condition.

 Dual Brake Warning Lamp System Tests 

Key to run or key to accessory. If the light on the red brake warning 
indicator lamp remains on, there may be a shorted or broken brake pressure 
differential switch, grounded switch wires or a pressure differential valve 
which is not centered properly. Apply and release the brake pedal. If light 
does not go out, check for fluid leaks. Refer to Hydraulic Leak 
Test in the Service Procedures portion of this section. Check for a grounded switch 
connector or wire and service or replace the wire assembly. If the wire is in 
good condition, replace the brake master cylinder.

Key to start. If the red brake warning indicator lamp does not light, 
check the lamp and wiring and replace or repair wiring, if necessary.

When both brake systems are functioning normally, the equal pressure in 
the pressure differential valve will keep the valve centered during brake 
pedal application. The brake warning indicator lamp will only come on with the 
key in start.

If the brake warning indicator lamp does not light when pressure is not 
equal in both brake systems, the warning lamp may be burned out, the brake 
pressure differential switch may be inoperative or the switch-to-lamp wiring 
may have an open circuit. Check the bulb and replace it, if required. Check 
the switch-to-lamp wires for an open circuit and service or replace them, if 
required. If the warning lamp still does not light, replace the brake master 
cylinder.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Hydraulic Leak Test

 Service Brakes 

 NOTE: The wet appearance of the outer cover of rubber brake hoses is called 
sweating and is normal with neoprene rayon braid hose. It is not evidence of a 
brake fluid leak and will not result in a loss of pressure in the system.

With the brakes applied, visually inspect all hydraulic lines, 
connections, and hoses for evidence of leaks. Replace leaking parts as 
necessary.

If the leak has not been found, check the disc brake piston seals or 
rear drum brake wheel cylinders for evidence of leaks. Replace or rebuild 
caliper piston or wheel cylinders as required.

If the leak has not been found, disconnect the hydraulic tubes from the 
brake master cylinder and plug the output ports using the appropriate size 
flared tube type plugs. Push the brake pedal down as hard as possible. If the 
brake pedal slowly moves downward, the brake master cylinder is leaking 
internally and should be rebuilt or replaced.

 Parking Brakes 

With the engine off, wipe all brake system components to aid in leak 
detection.

With the engine running at 1000-1500 rpm, release, and then apply the 
parking brakes.

Shut off the engine and check for leaks.

Determine the exact source of leakage.

Traces of fluid at the booster or park brake circuit components are 
considered normal and should not be a cause for component replacement. Traces 
of fluid on the bottom of the booster between the booster and brake master 
cylinder, below the parking brake unitized valve at the mounting bracket or on 
the bottom of the spring chambers between the wheel cylinder and end cap are 
considered normal. A very small amount of fluid at any of these areas will be 
spread by air currents, either the fan in the engine compartment or airflow 
over the parking brake chambers.

To determine the presence of a fluid leak other than normal amounts, 
wipe the suspect area dry and use the following procedure.

For traces at the Hydro-Max booster/brake master cylinder junction, 
with the engine running, apply the service brake and hold for at least a 
minute. If a drop of fluid forms at the junction, the Hydro-Max booster end 
cap seal should be replaced.

For traces at the bottom of the spring chambers, with the engine 
running, release the parking brake. If a drop of fluid appears at the end cap 
to wheel cylinder joint in one minute, replace the spring chamber.

For traces at the parking brake unitized valve, with the engine 
running, apply and release the parking brake at ten-second intervals for one 
minute. If a drop of fluid appears at the back of the parking brake unitized 
valve, replace the parking brake unitized valve. If a drop appears at a 
fitting, service or replace the fitting as required.

 Fitting and Tube Seat Leak Inspection 

Since most fluid leaks occur at the fittings and connections, these 
areas should be checked before any other part is replaced.

Pressure connection at brake pump — tighten tube 
fitting to 39 Nm (29 lb-ft). If leak persists, disconnect 
tube fitting and check O-ring on tube for cuts or distortion. Replace O-ring 
if necessary.

Return line hose clamping — tighten or reposition 
adjustable hose clamps to eliminate leakage.

Thread damage — if leakage is due to damaged threads 
(cross-threaded), replace the connector or the hose fitting end or replace the 
hose assembly where required.

O-ring fittings — tighten the fitting. If the leak 
persists, remove the fitting and inspect the O-ring for cuts or damage. 
Service or replace the fitting as required.

Tube seat fittings — tighten the tube nut to 
specifications. If the leak persists, disconnect the tube and inspect the tube 
seat for debris, burrs or other damage. Service or replace as required.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Brake System Pressure Test

The brake pump flow and pressure tests will confirm or rule out the 
brake pump as the cause of brake system problems.

Prior to performing the pump flow and pressure test, perform the Hydraulic Leak Test 
 in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

If all preliminary items are to specification or have been corrected, 
and the loss of assist still exists, use the following procedure to test the 
brake pump flow and pressure to determine whether the trouble is in the brake 
pump, the Hydro-Max booster, the parking brake unitized valve, the plumbing or 
the pressure relief valve.

 Preparation for Hydraulic Pressure/Flow Tests 

The power steering analyzer is to be used when the brake system is 
suspected of erratic operation or insufficient power assist, and the brake 
pump does not exhibit sustained failure or internal damage that can 
contaminate the fluid in the system. Use Rotunda Analyzer 014-00230 or 
equivalent which consists of a pressure gauge, flow meter, shutoff valve, 
thermometer, hose and adapter attachments.

Possible contamination of the system fluid can cause permanent damage 
to gauges and instruments incorporated in the analyzer. If there is a 
possibility of burned fluid or metal particles in the fluid, the brake system 
should be purged before connecting the power steering analyzer.

To connect the analyzer into the brake system, disconnect the pressure 
line from the connector at the gear, brake pump or lines, as indicated in the 
hookup diagrams.

Thread M-16 Metric Adapter D85T-33610-A or equivalent to the connector 
and insert in gauge pressure line.

Connect the analyzer to the adapters and tighten both connections to 
proper torque. Be sure the analyzer line at the shutoff valve end is connected 
to the brake pump of the vehicle brake system as indicated in hookup diagram.

Fully open the shutoff valve, start engine and purge the air from the 
brake system by applying the brakes several times. Shut off engine and check 
connections for leaks.

Check for proper fluid level at reservoir and add or remove fluid as 
required. Recheck for air in the system by restarting engine; partially close 
the shutoff valve and view the pressure gauge. If the gauge needle vibration 
is excessive, too much air remains in the system. Repeat Step 4 to purge any 
remaining air from the system.

Install thermometer provided with analyzer in the reservoir and connect 
tachometer to the engine.

 Brake System Test Procedure 

Check brake system back pressure as follows.

Fully open the analyzer shutoff valve.

Start engine and run at 2,000 rpm.

When fluid temperature reaches 55°C (130°
F), record flow and pressure.

If flow is below 11.7 lpm (3.1 gpm), check to see if correct brake pump 
is installed for the vehicle being tested. If correct brake pump is installed, 
continue testing to find problem.

If pressure exceeds 172 kPa (25 psi), check lines for kinks or 
obstructions. If none are found and pressure remains high, continue testing to 
find problem.

Check brake pump for minimum efficiency flow.

Decrease engine speed to 800 ± 50 rpm.

Slowly close the shutoff valve to build pressure to 8400 kPa (1200 psi).

Record flow with temperature at 55°C (130°
F) or above.

If flow is below 5 lpm (1.3 gpm), check if correct brake pump is 
installed for vehicle and equipment being tested.

Brake pump may require service or replacement, especially if flow in 
Step 1 was also below value indicated.

 CAUTION: Do not hold the valve closed for more than five seconds. Failure to 
follow this caution will result in damage to brake pump. 

Check brake pump for pressure relief valve operation as follows.

Run engine at 800 ± 50 rpm.

Completely close and partially open the shutoff valve three times.

Read pressure when valve is fully closed.

If pressure is below 8480 kPa (1230 psi), clean or replace pressure 
relief valve.

If pressure reading exceeds 9307 kPa (1350 psi), clean or replace 
pressure relief valve.

If flow/pressure checks are within specifications, the brake pump is 
operating normally and other areas should be investigated.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Brake Tubing

For rear axle brake tube replacement, use Connector Block C8TZ-2074-B 
with fabricated tube assemblies to right and left brake. If a section of the 
brake tube is damaged, replace the entire section with tubing of the same 
type, size, shape and length. Be careful not to kink or crack the tubing when 
bending to form fit the axle.

For service brake system, use only SAE J527 brazed double wall steel 
tubing or equivalent tubing coated with zinc primer meeting Ford 
specifications ESA-M2P118-A and ESA-M6J138-A or equivalent. Double flare the 
tube ends according to SAE J533 specifications (double flare 45-degree). For 
parking brake system, use only SAE J526 welded single wall low carbon steel 
tubing or equivalent. Double flare the tube ends according to SAE 
specification J533 (double flare 37-degree).

Flare tubing as described below should provide good leakproof 
connections. Always clean the inside of a new brake tube with clean isopropyl 
alcohol.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Flaring a Line

 Split-Die Type 

Cut off and straighten the required length of line. A tubing cutter 
tool will simplify making a clean and square cut.

Square off the ends of the line with a file and chamfer the end of the 
line to be flared.

Select the split die for the line to be used and insert the die into 
the tapered hole in the body.

Push the tube through the die until the line is even with the face of 
the die. Lock the line in this position by tightening the wing nut securely.

[FIGURE: H46841A.gif]

The punches are marked Op. 1 and Op. 2. Slide the first operation punch 
into the hole in the center of the body and tighten the screw securely to form 
the single flare.

Release the screw and replace the first operation punch with the second 
punch and tighten the screw to form the double flare.

Release the screw, wing nut, punch and dies.

Remove the line and inspect the flare for cracks or poor flare form. If 
the flare is not correct, cut it off and repeat the process.

The finished flare must be square with the line, free of cracks and 
have a smooth mating surface to make sure connection is leakproof.

 Flaring-Bar Type 

Cut off and straighten the required length of line (a tubing cutter 
tool will simplify making a clean and square cut).

Square off the ends of the line with a file and chamfer the end of the 
line to be flared.

Insert the line through its appropriate rubbed hole in the bar assembly 
until the end of the line sticks out about as far as the thickness of the 
adapter above the bar, or even with the bar, depending on the tool used.

[FIGURE: H46851A.gif]

Fit the adapter onto the line and slide the bar into the yoke. Lock the 
bar in position with the line beneath the yoke screw.

Form the single flare by tightening the yoke screw securely.

Release the screw and remove the adapter.

Form the double flare by tightening the yoke screw again, with second 
adapter fitted, depending on the tool use.

Release the screw bar and flared line. Inspect the flare for cracks or 
poor flare form, and repeat the process if the flare is not correct.

Repeat Steps 3 through 6 at the opposite wheel cylinder.

Brake Hose

 Service Brake System 

If flexible brake hose shows signs of softening, cracking or other 
damage, replace with hose of the same type, size, shape and length. Use only 
SAE J1401, low expansion brake hose or equivalent.

When installing a new brake hose, position the hose to avoid contact 
with other vehicle parts.

 Parking Brake System 

Replace a flexible brake hose if it shows signs of softening, cracking 
or other damage with hose of the same type, size, shape and length.

Use the following hoses:

1/2- and 3/8-inch inside diameter parking brake hose — 
SAE 100R3 hose or equivalent.

5/8-inch inside diameter parking brake jounce hose — 
SAE 100R5 wire braid hose or equivalent.

5/8- and 3/4-inch inside diameter parking brake hose — 
SAE 100R6 hose or equivalent.

When installing a new brake hose, position the hose to avoid contact 
with other vehicle parts.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Service Precautions 

 WARNING: DO NOT INHALE DUST FROM BRAKES, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. 
INHALATION OF DUST FROM THESE COMPONENTS COULD BE INJURIOUS TO YOUR HEALTH AND 
COULD CAUSE CANCER OR ASBESTOSIS. COMPRESSED AIR OR BRUSHES MUST NOT BE USED 
TO CLEAN BRAKES, BRAKE DRUMS, CLUTCHES AND ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. USE A VACUUM 
CLEANER SUCH AS ROTUNDA BRAKE/CLUTCH/SERVICE VACUUM 164-R3600 OR EQUIVALENT 
EQUIPPED FOR THIS PURPOSE TO CAREFULLY REMOVE ANY DUST. ADHERENT DUST SHOULD 
BE REMOVED WITH A DAMP RAG. ANY DUST SHOULD BE CONTAINED IN A SEALED AND 
LABELED BAG FOR DISPOSAL. WEAR AN APPROVED HIGH EFFICIENCY CARTRIDGE OR AIR 
LINE RESPIRATOR AND USE EXTRA CAUTION TO AVOID BREATHING THIS DUST. USE 
NON-ASBESTOS REPLACEMENT PARTS WHENEVER POSSIBLE. 

 CAUTION: When cleaning brake parts, use only Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake 
Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A, isopropyl alcohol or clear, methylated spirits. Do not use 
mineral base cleaning solvents such as gasoline, kerosene, carbon 
tetrachloride, acetone or paint thinner to clean brake parts or the rubber 
parts will be damaged.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Hydraulic System 

 Brake Master Cylinder 

Refer to Section 06-06 for disassembly and assembly procedures.

 NOTE: When a brake master cylinder repair kit is used, follow the 
instructions in the kit and install all of the parts provided.

Clean all brake master cylinder parts in clean isopropyl alcohol or the 
Rotunda Brake Washer 065-00016 or equivalent, and inspect the parts for wear 
or damage. Replace as required.

Make sure all ports and vents in the brake master cylinder are open and 
free of foreign matter.

Inspect the cylinder walls for scores or rust. Remove scores and rust 
or obtain a smooth wall surface by honing the cylinder walls, but not more 
than 0.076 mm (0.003 inch) of material. Remove any burrs or loose metal from 
the honing operation and clean the cylinder with clean isopropyl alcohol.

 Brake Booster, Hydro-Max 

Use clean automatic transmission fluid, Motorcraft MERCON®
 ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent for 
cleaning and lubricating parts and seals.

Inspect the power piston input and output shaft surfaces for scratches 
or nicks. Also, check that the large piston seal surface is smooth and 
continuous without excessive wear. If any wear or damage is found, replace the 
power piston assembly. Confirm that the check ball is in place and is clean 
and free to move. Confirm that the reaction piston bore and poppet valve seat 
surface inside the piston are clean and undamaged.

Inspect housing for grooves, scratches or nicks in the input bore area. 
If any are found, replace the housing. Minor wear, as indicated by a shiny 
appearance on the large bore surface area, is normal.

Inspect the input plug for wear in the actuator pin hole. Replace the 
plug if wear is evident.

ADJUSTMENTS

Hydraulic Brake Fluid Color

Hydraulic brake fluid color must conform with the requirements of 
Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 116. Under this standard, brake fluids 
are visually different from other automotive fluids such as transmission, 
power steering and engine.

The color of the fluid in a normal brake system in service can vary 
from its original color for many reasons. Sometimes a brake master cylinder 
may show significantly different shades of fluid color between the two 
reservoirs. Color may appear to vary between cast steel and die cast aluminum 
reservoirs. Some of the reasons for the apparent difference in color in a 
system are listed below.

Fluid discoloration can occur due to heat and aging.

Difference in fluid color of a two-compartment reservoir can be due to 
the different operating temperatures or different rates of normal oxidation 
between the two reservoir compartments.

Fluid discoloration can exist when different brands/shades of brake 
fluid are used in topping off during normal service.

Fluid discoloration can occur through dissolution of color dye used on 
brake master cylinder internal springs in manufacturer's assembly procedure.

 NOTE: Brake fluid contaminated with a hydrocarbon/mineral based fluid (power 
steering or transmission fluid) can be detected by an obvious swelling of the 
brake master cylinder cap gasket. If the swollen brake master cylinder gasket 
condition is present, all brake system rubber parts must be replaced. All 
brake tubes and hoses must be thoroughly flushed with Ford High Performance 
DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M6C25-A before the vehicle goes back into service.

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake Fluid Level Check

 Service Brake System 

 WARNING: THE HYDRO-MAX BOOSTER/PARKING BRAKE SYSTEM USES AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION 
FLUID IN THE RESERVOIR OF THE ENGINE-DRIVEN BRAKE PUMP. THE SERVICE BRAKE 
SYSTEM USES BRAKE FLUID. THESE FLUIDS ARE INCOMPATIBLE. DO NOT MIX. FAILURE TO 
OBSERVE ALL PRECAUTIONS PREVENTING CONTAMINATION OF EITHER SYSTEM WILL RESULT 
IN DETERIORATION OF RUBBER PARTS, LEADING TO REDUCED BRAKE PERFORMANCE AND 
EVENTUAL FAILURE. 

 NOTE: Brake fluid color may change from the original color due to normal 
vehicle operation. Such color changes will not affect the operation of the 
brake system.

Remove the filler caps from the brake master cylinder.

Fill to the level of the bottom of the rings as indicated on the brake 
master cylinder reservoir. Use Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid 
C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A. Do not use DOT 5 or any other nonrecommended fluid.

Replace the brake master cylinder filler caps.

 Parking Brake System 

 NOTE: To minimize parking brake system release and actuation during 
continuous cold weather operation — constant operation during 
-18°C (0°F) — fill the 
parking brake system with Esso UNIVIS-N-22 hydraulic oil or equivalent. DO NOT 
MIX WITH OTHER FLUIDS.

Check the fluid level in the brake pump reservoir with the parking 
brakes applied. If required, fill the brake pump reservoir to the specified 
level with Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON®
 equivalent.

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake Rotor, Disc

 Runout 

Rotor runout is the side-to-side movement or wobble of the rotor as it 
rotates. Excessive runout can cause vibration, brake pedal pumping or brake 
chatter. Use the following procedure to check rotor runout.

Tighten the spindle nut to eliminate all end play from the bearings. Be 
sure the hub and rotor can be turned.

Attach Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent to some 
part of the vehicle suspension so the stylus of the indicator touches the 
surface of the rotor approximately one inch from the outer edge of the rotor.

[FIGURE: H2581E.gif]

Set the dial indicator to zero. Slowly turn the rotor one complete turn 
and note the high and low readings on the dial. The total between the high and 
low reading must not exceed 0.38 mm (0.015 inch) total at the center of the 
braking surface.

 CAUTION: Be sure to adjust the spindle nut to specifications after the runout 
check. Refer to Section 04-01 . 

Refinish or replace the rotor as required.

 Parallelism 

Parallelism refers to the variations in the thickness of the rotor. If 
the two rubbing surfaces of the rotor are not parallel, the rotor may cause 
excessive brake pedal travel, a pulsating brake pedal or noise.

Two methods can be used to check if the two faces of a rotor are 
parallel. A micrometer can be used to measure the rotor thickness at 12 points 
approximately 30 degrees apart and 25 mm (1 inch) from the outer edge of the 
rotor.

The other method is to mount the rotor on a precision lathe designed 
for machining disc brake rotors. Attach two dial indicators, one on each side 
of the rotor, so that the stylus of each indicator contacts the rubbing 
surface approximately 25 mm (1 inch) from the outer edge of the rotor.

Zero both indicators and rotate the rotor while watching both dials. If 
the total readings of both indicators exceed the specified limit for 
parallelism, the rotor must be refinished or replaced.

 Refinishing 

Use a disc brake lathe to refinish the disc brake rotors.

Do not attempt to refinish if rotor thickness falls below the minimum 
rework thickness. When refinishing, remove an equal amount of material from 
both surfaces. Replace the rotor if thickness falls below the minimum 
thickness shown on the rotor.

[FIGURE: H47461E.gif]

The finished braking surfaces of the rotor must be flat and parallel 
within 0.050 mm (0.002 inch). Lateral runout must not exceed 0.38 mm (0.015 
inch). The total indicator reading is taken on the inboard surface of the 
rotor at a 183-mm (7.24-inch) radius. The surface finish of the braking 
surfaces must be 39 to 118 micro-inches.

 Service Limits 

 CAUTION: Never refinish a rotor to the minimum wear or discard thickness. 

Measure the thickness of the rotor to determine if it is within the 
specifications listed at the end of this section. Disc brake rotors have a 
minimum thickness dimension (minimum wear thickness or discard thickness). 
THIS IS NOT THE REFINISHING DIMENSION.

Brake Drum

 Refinishing

0.254 mm (0.010 inch) maximum.

For safety, the following rebore and wear limits are recommended:

Brake drums should be machined or replaced in axle pairs to get the 
same braking on both sides of the vehicle.

If the brake drum diameter is less than 0.762 mm (0.030 inch) oversize 
after refinishing, install standard linings on the brake assemblies.

Minor scores on a brake drum can be removed with fine emery cloth, 
provided the emery is thoroughly cleaned off the brake drum after the operation.

A badly scored, rough or out-of-round brake drum should be ground or 
turned on a brake drum lathe. Turn brake drums only when necessary and remove 
only as much material as necessary. Do not remove any more material from the 
brake drum than is necessary to provide a smooth surface for the brake shoe 
contact. Brake drum maximum braking surface diameter is shown on each brake 
drum. Brake drums which exceed the maximum braking surface diameter shown on 
the brake drum, either through wear or refinishing, must be replaced. The 
replacement brake drum should be of the same type, size and shape. It is not 
necessary to turn a replacement brake drum on installation. The brake drum 
pilot will accurately locate the braking surface.

After refinishing the brake surface, runout must not exceed 0.25 mm 
(0.010 inch) total indicator reading, measured from the bearing cups.

Fade resistance and strength of brake drums rebored in excess of the 
above limits are reduced to a point approaching a safety hazard. All brake 
drums exceeding the total rebore and wear limits should be replaced.

Oversize brake drums will result in rough or chattering brakes and a 
pulsating ride. They produce fast fade.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Drum

A brake drum's function is to provide a friction surface for the brake 
lining and to absorb and dissipate the heat generated by the braking action.

Two types of brake drums are available: the full cast and the Centrifuse®
 type. The full cast brake drum is machined from a single 
iron casting and is a uniform material throughout. The full cast brake drums 
feature a mill balance or machine-to-balance process. In this process, the 
brake drums are cast with a thicker band around the perimeter near the open 
face of the brake drum. This band is approximately 51 mm (2 inches) wide and 
13 mm (0.5 inch) thick. This band can be precisely machined to bring the brake 
drum into balance. This process will greatly reduce "hot spots" caused by 
balance weights welded to the brake drum. 

The Centrifuse® type brake drum is made of an outer 
steel shell with an iron alloy fused to the inside by centrifugal force. This 
design takes advantage of the strength and relative lightness of steel and the 
heat dissipation and wear characteristics of iron. The Centrifuse®
 type brake drum is not available for cast spoke wheel 
applications. 

 Brake Drum, Centrifuse® 

[FIGURE: H10263A.gif]

 Brake Drum, Full Cast, Spider Wheel 

[FIGURE: H10264A.gif]

 Brake Drum, Full Cast, Disc Wheel 

[FIGURE: H10265A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake, Service

 Air Brakes 

The cam-type brake is an air-operated, two-shoe brake. 

As the brake pedal is applied, air pressure is routed to the brake air 
chamber. The brake air chamber has an internal diaphragm that will push 
against the brake air chamber push rod with a force proportional to the air 
pressure being applied to the brake air chamber. The brake air chamber push 
rod then pushes on the slack adjuster arm, which causes rotation of the brake 
camshaft. Rollers riding on the brake cam lobes are forced apart with rotation 
of the brake camshaft. The brake shoes riding on the rollers are then forced 
apart and into contact with the brake drum.

When the brake pedal is released, return springs in the brake air 
chamber and brake shoe assembly pull the components back to the at-rest 
position.

For more air service brake information, refer to Section 06-08D .

 Hydraulic Brakes 

The rear hydraulic drum brake consists of two brake shoe and lining 
assemblies, a wheel cylinder/adjuster assembly and a wheel cylinder/parking 
brake expander assembly. The wheel cylinder/adjuster assembly acts as a 
conventional wheel cylinder and adjusts the shoes to maintain a 
lining-to-brake drum clearance within a specified range. The wheel 
cylinder/parking brake expander assembly acts as a conventional wheel cylinder 
and also expands and retracts the shoes to set and release the drum brakes as 
a parking brake.

For more hydraulic service brake information, refer to Section 06-02B .

PAGE 4665
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 06-02A: Brake Drum

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake, Parking

 Air Brakes 

The parking brake system is composed of a parking brake control valve, 
double check valve, quick release valves and spring brake air chambers. The 
spring brake air chambers use a powerful spring to mechanically apply the 
service brakes. Brake system air pressure in the spring brake air chambers 
keeps the spring brakes from being applied. Therefore, the spring brakes will 
be applied whenever brake system air pressure falls below a preset level, 
whether intentionally or unintentionally.

 Spring Brake Applied, Air Brakes 

[FIGURE: H10291A.gif]

 Hydraulic Brakes 

On vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes, the parking brake system is 
composed of a parking brake control valve, a parking brake unitized valve, an 
engine-driven brake pump and remote reservoir, and two parking chambers that 
are spring-operated. The parking brake is applied by the parking chamber 
spring acting through the brake wedge and is released by the engine-driven 
brake pump which provides hydraulic pressure through the parking brake 
unitized valve to release the parking brakes.

 Parking Brake Chamber, Hydraulic 

[FIGURE: H40901A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake Shoe Automatic Adjustment

 Air Brakes 

Brake shoe automatic adjustment design uses both brake air chamber push 
rod travel and shoe-to-brake drum force to maintain proper brake adjustment. 
Upon brake application, the brake air chamber push rod rotates the slack 
adjuster until the adjusting link engages a one-way cone clutch on the 
wormshaft within the slack adjuster. At this point, if the brake shoes are not 
in contact with the brake drum, the cone clutch will remain engaged with the 
wormshaft and the link will rotate the wormshaft. This wormshaft rotation 
adjusts the brake shoes by reducing shoe-to-brake drum clearance. Adjustment 
continues until the brake linings are forced against the brake drum. The 
shoe-to-brake drum force creates a resistance torque that exceeds the slip 
torque of the cone clutch and allows the clutch to slip on the wormshaft for 
the remainder of the slack adjuster travel. During the return stroke the 
one-way cone clutch allows the link to return without wormshaft movement. The 
adjustment cycle will repeat until shoe-to-brake drum contact force occurs 
simultaneously with the link-to-clutch engagement.

 Automatic Slack Adjuster

 Hydraulic Brakes 

Automatic adjustment of brake shoes as the lining material wears has a 
number of important advantages.

The lining-to-brake drum clearance is maintained at an optimum.

Response time of the brake is kept to a minimum.

Hydraulic brake fluid movement is kept to a minimum.

Excessive taper wear of the lining along the shoe is avoided and lining 
life maximized.

Vehicle downtime for adjustment is eliminated.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake Drum Mounting Inboard, Outboard

All brake drums on cast spoke wheels are mounted inboard of the hub and 
bearing assembly; on disc wheel hubs, the brake drums are outboard-mounted.

The outboard-mounted brake drum is mounted on the outboard face of the 
hub and fits over the wheel mounting studs. The wheel is mounted on the face 
of the drum, providing access to brakes without disturbing bearings or seals. 

Make sure the brake drum pilot diameter does not interfere with the 
mating hub pilot diameter.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheels, Cast Spoke

 WARNING: DO NOT INHALE DUST FROM BRAKES, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. 
INHALATION OF DUST CAN BE INJURIOUS TO YOUR HEALTH AND COULD CAUSE CANCER OR 
ASBESTOSIS. COMPRESSED AIR OR BRUSHES MUST NOT BE USED TO CLEAN BRAKES, BRAKE 
DRUMS, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. USE A VACUUM CLEANER SUCH AS ROTUNDA 
BRAKE/CLUTCH/SERVICE VACUUM 164-R3600 OR EQUIVALENT EQUIPPED FOR THIS PURPOSE 
TO REMOVE ANY DUST. ADHERENT DUST SHOULD BE REMOVED WITH A DAMP RAG. ANY DUST 
SHOULD BE CONTAINED IN A SEALED AND LABELED BAG FOR DISPOSAL. WEAR AN APPROVED 
HIGH-EFFICIENCY CARTRIDGE OR AIR LINE RESPIRATOR AND USE EXTRA CAUTION TO 
AVOID BREATHING THIS DUST. USE NON-ASBESTOS REPLACEMENT PARTS WHENEVER POSSIBLE. 

 Removal 

Remove the tire and demountable rim. Refer to Section 04-04 .

For a rear wheel, remove the axle shaft. Refer to Section 05-02A , 
 Section 05-02B or Section 05-02C as necessary. For a front wheel, remove the 
hub cap and gasket.

As necessary, remove the cotter pin, lock nut, washer and adjusting nut 
from the spindle (front) or axle (rear). Discard the cotter pin.

Pull the cast spoke wheel, bearing and brake drum assembly off the 
spindle (front) or axle (rear).

Remove the nuts, washers and brake drum bolts attaching the brake drum 
to the cast spoke wheel.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Replace the brake drum with the same size and type. Failure to do so 
will affect vehicle performance. 

Inspect the brake drum and service or replace as necessary. Use a 
degreaser to remove the protective coating on a new brake drum.

Service the hub, seals and bearings as necessary. Refer to Section 04-01 for front wheels or Section 04-02B for rear wheels. 

Position the brake drum on the cast spoke wheel and install the brake 
drum bolts, washers and nuts. Tighten the brake drum nuts to 272-338 Nm
 (200-250 lb-ft).

Position the cast spoke wheel on the front spindle or rear axle. 

Install the adjusting nut, washer, lock nut and a new cotter pin as 
necessary. 

Adjust the bearings. Refer to Section 04-01 for front wheels or Section 04-02B for rear wheels. 

For front wheels, install the gasket and hub cap. For rear wheels, 
install the axle shafts. Refer to Section 05-02A , Section 05-02B or Section 05-02C . 

Observing tightening sequence and torque specifications, install the 
tire and demountable rim. Refer to Section 04-04 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheels, Disc — Outboard-Mounted Drums

 Removal 

 WARNING: AFTERMARKET WHEEL ASSEMBLIES MAY NOT BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE VEHICLE. 
USE OF INCOMPATIBLE WHEEL ASSEMBLIES MAY RESULT IN EQUIPMENT FAILURE AND 
POSSIBLE INJURY. USE ONLY APPROVED WHEEL ASSEMBLIES. 

 WARNING: DO NOT PAINT DISC WHEEL MOUNTING SURFACE OR WHEEL STUDS. EXCESS PAINT 
CAN ADVERSELY AFFECT DISC WHEEL MOUNTING SYSTEM. 

 WARNING: USE ONLY FLANGED NUTS, INTEGRAL TWO-PIECE SWIVELING WHEEL NUTS ON 
VEHICLES EQUIPPED WITH DUAL REAR WHEELS. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO USE BALL SEAT 
ONE-PIECE WHEEL NUTS ON THESE VEHICLES. IF USED, BALL SEAT ONE-PIECE WHEEL 
NUTS CAN COME LOOSE DURING VEHICLE OPERATION. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO USE PAST MODEL 
WHEELS THAT HAVE BALL SEATS ON THIS VEHICLE. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO USE PRESENT 
DESIGN WHEELS AND WHEEL NUTS ON PAST MODEL WHEEL HUBS. ATTEMPTED USE OF 
INTERMIXED WHEELS CAN LEAD TO DAMAGE TO THE WHEEL MOUNTING SYSTEM AND COULD 
RESULT IN WHEELS COMING LOOSE. 

Remove the tire and wheel assembly. Refer to Section 04-04 .

[FIGURE: H33351B.gif]

Remove the brake drum from the hub.

 CAUTION: Replace brake drums with brake drums of the same type. Failure to do so 
will affect vehicle track and performance. Replace cast brake drums only with 
cast brake drums. Replace Centrifuse® brake drums only with 
Centrifuse® brake drums. 

Check the brake drum for damage or wear and service or replace as 
necessary. If a new brake drum is installed, be sure to remove the protective 
coating with degreaser.

Check wheel seals for leakage. If the hub is removed from the axle, 
install new wheel seals. Refer to Section 04-01 for front wheel seals or 
 Section 04-02B for rear wheel seals.

 Installation 

 WARNING: MAKE SURE THE BRAKE DRUM SLIDES OVER THE PILOT LOCATORS WITH REASONABLE 
EFFORT AND THAT BRAKE DRUM FLANGE IS FULLY SUPPORTED BY THE MATING HUB FLANGE. 

Install the brake drum on the hub.

Observing tightening sequence and torque specifications, install the 
tire and disc wheel assembly on the hub. Refer to Section 04-04 .

Refer to Wheel Nut Torque Requirement in the Removal and Installation 
portion of this section for proper torque specifications.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel Hub Bolt 

 Cast Spoke Wheel 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE OXYACETYLENE OR SIMILAR EQUIPMENT TO HEAT THE HUB. THIS MAY 
CAUSE OVERHEATING IN LOCALIZED AREAS, WHICH WILL RESULT IN LOSS OF STRENGTH 
THAT MAY CAUSE FAILURE OF THE HUB ASSEMBLY AND, ULTIMATELY, LOSS OF VEHICLE 
CONTROL. 

 WARNING: WHEN ONE BROKEN STUD IS REPLACED, THE STUD ON EACH SIDE OF IT MUST BE 
REPLACED. IF MORE THAN ONE STUD IS BROKEN, ALL STUDS MUST BE REPLACED. 

 Removal 

Remove the tire and demountable rim. Refer to Section 04-04 .

If enough of the rim stud is exposed, use a stud remover and back out 
the stud.

 Installation 

 WARNING: WHEEL MOUNTING HARDWARE SPECIFICATIONS ARE CRITICAL. ALWAYS CHECK AND 
OBSERVE MANUFACTURER'S RECOMMENDATIONS FOR DIMENSIONS AND QUALITY. FAILURE TO 
USE CORRECT PARTS CAN CAUSE COMPONENT FAILURE LEADING TO SERIOUS INJURY OR 
DEATH. 

Install a new rim stud and tighten to 136-257 Nm 
(100-190 lb-ft).

Install the tire and demountable rim. Refer to Section 04-04 .

 Disc Wheel 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE OXYACETYLENE OR SIMILAR EQUIPMENT TO HEAT THE HUB. THIS MAY 
CAUSE OVERHEATING IN LOCALIZED AREAS, WHICH WILL RESULT IN LOSS OF STRENGTH 
THAT MAY CAUSE FAILURE OF THE HUB ASSEMBLY AND, ULTIMATELY, LOSS OF VEHICLE 
CONTROL. 

 WARNING: WHEN ONE BROKEN STUD IS REPLACED, THE STUD ON EACH SIDE OF IT MUST BE 
REPLACED. IF MORE THAN ONE STUD IS BROKEN, ALL STUDS MUST BE REPLACED. 

 Removal 

Remove the tire and wheel. Refer to Section 04-04 .

Remove the hub and brake drum assembly from the front or rear axle. 
Refer to Section 04-01 for front wheels or Section 04-02B for rear wheels.

Separate the hub and brake drum assembly.

Position the hub on a suitable press with the inner bearing cup facing 
down.

Support the hub flange evenly, and adjacent to the mounting stud being 
removed.

Using a steady, uninterrupted movement, press the damaged mounting stud 
out of the hub.

 Installation 

 WARNING: WHEEL MOUNTING HARDWARE SPECIFICATIONS ARE CRITICAL. ALWAYS CHECK AND 
OBSERVE MANUFACTURER'S RECOMMENDATIONS FOR DIMENSIONS AND QUALITY. FAILURE TO 
USE CORRECT PARTS CAN CAUSE COMPONENT FAILURE LEADING TO SERIOUS INJURY OR 
DEATH. 

 CAUTION: Left-hand threaded studs (except metric) are used on the left-hand side 
of the vehicle. Metric fasteners are right-hand threaded only. 

Position the hub on the press with the inner bearing cup facing up.

Support the hub evenly and adjacent to the mounting stud hole.

Insert the new mounting stud in the hub.

 CAUTION: Make sure the flat edges on the mounting stud are in line with the 
groove or shoulder on the hub. Make sure the mounting stud is fully seated and 
that the shoulder does not become embedded in the hub. If the mounting stud is 
embedded into the hub, the hub must be replaced. 

With a steady, uninterrupted movement, press the new mounting stud all 
the way into the hub.

Remove the hub from the press.

Reassemble the hub and brake drum assembly.

Observing tightening sequence and torque specifications, install the 
wheel and tire. Refer to Section 04-04 .
