SERVICE PROCEDURES

Brake Drum Refinishing

 NOTE: All production brake drum tolerances are as follows: 

15-inch diameter ±0.254 mm (0.010 inch) maximum.

16.5-inch diameter ±0.254 mm (0.010 inch) maximum.

For safety, the following rebore and wear limitations are recommended:

 REBORE AND WEAR LIMITS

Brake Drum Original Inside Diameter Size

Rebore Limits

Permissible Additional Wear

Total Rebore and Wear Limits

Over 14 Inches Standard

2.032 mm

 (0.080 Inch)

1.016 mm

 (0.040 Inch)

3.048 mm

 (0.120 Inch)

Brake drums should be machined or replaced in axle pairs to get the 
same braking on both sides of the vehicle.

Minor scores on a brake drum can be removed with fine emery cloth, 
provided the emery is thoroughly cleaned off the brake drum after the operation.

A badly scored, rough, or out-of-round brake drum should be ground or 
turned on a drum lathe. Turn brake drums only when necessary and remove only 
as much material as necessary. Do not remove any more material from the brake 
drum than is necessary to provide a smooth surface for brake shoe contact. 
Brake drum maximum braking surface diameter is shown on each brake drum. Brake 
drums which exceed the maximum braking surface diameter shown on the brake 
drum, caused either by wear or refinishing, must be replaced. The replacement 
brake drum should be of the same type, size and shape. It is not necessary to 
turn a replacement brake drum on installation. The brake drum pilot will 
accurately locate the braking surface.

[FIGURE: H4152B.gif]

After refinishing the brake surface, runout must not exceed 0.25 mm 
(0.010 inch) total indicator reading, measured from the bearing cups.

Fade resistance and strength of brake drums rebored in excess of the 
above limits are reduced to a point approaching a safety hazard. All brake 
drums exceeding the maximum brake (drum) face diameter should be replaced.

Oversize brake drums will result in rough or chattering brakes and a 
pulsating ride. They produce fast fade.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cleaning

 WARNING: DO NOT INHALE THE DUST FROM BRAKES, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. 
INHALATION OF DUST FROM THESE COMPONENTS COULD BE INJURIOUS TO YOUR HEALTH AND 
COULD CAUSE CANCER OR ASBESTOSIS. COMPRESSED AIR OR BRUSHES MUST NOT BE USED 
TO CLEAN BRAKES, BRAKE DRUMS, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. USE A VACUUM 
CLEANER SUCH AS ROTUNDA BRAKE/CLUTCH/SERVICE VACUUM 164-R3600 OR EQUIVALENT 
EQUIPPED FOR THIS PURPOSE TO REMOVE ANY DUST. ADHERENT DUST SHOULD BE REMOVED 
WITH A DAMP RAG. ANY DUST SHOULD BE CONTAINED IN A SEALED AND LABELED BAG FOR 
DISPOSAL. WEAR AN APPROVED HIGH EFFICIENCY CARTRIDGE OR AIR LINE RESPIRATOR 
AND USE EXTRA CAUTION TO AVOID BREATHING THIS DUST. USE NON-ASBESTOS 
REPLACEMENT PARTS WHENEVER POSSIBLE. 

Removal of dust and dirt from brake assemblies should be done with 
Rotunda Brake/Clutch/Service Vacuum 165-R3600 or equivalent, or Rotunda Brake 
Washer 065-00018 or equivalent. Brake assembly dust and dirt should not be 
removed by blowing off with an air gun or by vacuuming with a standard 
industrial vacuum.

ADJUSTMENTS

Hub/Spider and Drum Balancing

If conventional wheel balancing methods do not correct cab pitch or 
steering wheel vibration that occurs between 68-90 km/h (42-56 mph), the hub 
and brake drum or cast spoke wheel and brake drum assembly must be balanced 
separately from the wheel and tire assembly. Use the following procedure to 
statically balance the assembly. (The hub and brake drum assembly is used as 
an example.)

Mark all tires and hub assemblies as to their respective positions on 
the vehicle.

Remove the hub and brake drum. Refer to Wheels, Cast Spoke , or Wheels, Disc — Outboard-Mounted 
Drums 
, in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Clean all loose dirt and rust from the hub and brake drum assembly.

Drain all excess oil from the inside of the hub cavity.

Mount the assembly on a suitable brake drum balancing mandrel. Use 
Rotunda Truck Arbor Set 104-00034 and Truck Hub/Hubless Adapter Set 104-00014 
or equivalent to center the assembly (leave the wheel bearings installed in 
the hub). Tighten the large nut.

Place the mandrel and the hub and brake drum assembly onto two safety 
stands. Install a support bearing (C3AZ-7025-C or equivalent) on each end of 
the mandrel.

 Brake Drum Balancing Setup, Typical 

[FIGURE: H10342A.gif]

Rotate the mandrel and the assembly to make sure it turns freely on the 
support bearings.If required, apply light lubricating oil to the two support 
bearings to reduce friction.

Rotate the assembly several times and allow it to come to a stop. If 
the assembly remains stationary at all positions, it does not require 
balancing. If the assembly does not remain stationary at all positions, the 
assembly requires balancing. The heaviest part will normally rest at the 
bottom. Refer to Steps 9-11 for balancing procedures.

Mark the top of the brake drum, which will be the lightest part. Rotate 
the assembly a few times to verify that the mark always appears at the top of 
the brake drum.

Tape small pieces of flat, mild steel on the light area of the brake 
drum. Experiment with different weights until hub and brake drum will not 
rotate when stopped at any position. When adding weights, remember to allow 
for clearance between the brake drum and wheel during installation.

 CAUTION: Under no condition should any welding method be used other than arc 
welding. To prevent brake drum distortion, do not use a current setting of 
more than 100 amps. 

 NOTE: Do not add balance weights to the 8-hole brake drums on 8 bolt hubs for 
rear axles.

After determining the proper weight to balance the hub and brake drum 
assembly, tack weld the weight to the brake drum. Use a 3-mm (1/8-inch) 
welding rod, either silver-nickel or chrome-nickel.

Install the hub and brake drum, and the tire and wheel assembly.

Rebalance the wheel and tire assembly using an appropriate electronic 
balancer.

Road test the vehicle for several miles to verify that vibration or cab 
pitch has been reduced to an acceptable level.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Drum, Rear Hydraulic 

The rear hydraulic drum brake system consists of two brake shoe and 
lining assemblies, an adjuster cylinder and a park cylinder. The adjuster 
cylinder acts as a conventional wheel cylinder with auto-adjusters that 
maintain a lining-to-drum clearance within a specified range. The park 
cylinder acts as a conventional wheel cylinder and also acts to expand and 
release the shoes for parking.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake, Service

On brake pedal application, hydraulic fluid pressure in the adjuster 
cylinder forces the pistons outward, moving the shoes toward the drum. At the 
same time in the park cylinder, hydraulic fluid pressure forces the expander 
piston and the hand brake piston outward. The expander piston directly moves 
the shoes toward the drum, while the hand brake piston pushes against the 
abutment tappet outer roller piston, which moves the shoes toward the drum.

[FIGURE: H4049E.gif]

Adjuster Cylinder Assy

When the shoes contact the drum, the pistons will be forced around in 
whichever direction the drum is moving. Regardless of forward or reverse 
rotation, the brake will always be a two leading shoe brake. In the forward 
direction, the torque load is taken by one automatic adjuster assembly 
bottoming in its bore, and by the abutment piston resting against the park 
cylinder body. In the reverse direction, the torque is taken by the other 
wheel cylinder piston bottoming and the expander piston head resting against 
the park cylinder assembly body.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake, Parking 

The parking brakes are applied when the parking brake knob in the cab 
is pulled out or the parking brake lever is pushed up (cowl). This action 
releases the hydraulic pressure in the spring chamber which holds the parking 
brake in the released position. As the pressure is released, a spring in the 
parking brake chamber forces a wedge and roller assembly into the park 
cylinder and forces the pistons to move outward. The pistons force the shoes 
into contact with the drums.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake Shoe Automatic Adjustment

Automatic adjustment of shoes as the lining material wears has a number 
of important advantages:

The lining-to-drum clearance is maintained at an optimum.

Response time of the brake is kept to a minimum.

Hydraulic brake fluid movement is kept to a minimum.

Excessive taper wear of the lining along the shoe is avoided and lining 
life maximized.

Vehicle downtime for adjustment is eliminated.

[FIGURE: H9455A.gif]

Piston (Part of 2C200)

In the A2LS (Automatic Two Leading Shoe) brake, automatic adjustment is 
carried out only by the adjuster cylinder. The adjuster cylinder contains two 
adjuster units. Each unit individually adjusts the appropriate shoe, and the 
clearance between shoe and drum is governed by the backlash built into each 
adjuster mechanism.

The following illustrates brake application when no adjustment is 
required. Travel takes place only between the drive ring and the adjuster screw.

 Service Brake Application 

[FIGURE: H9544A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Drive Ring Seated

9

—

Drive Ring (Part of 2C198)

As the lining wear and the piston travel lengthens, the predetermined 
clearance range between lining and drum is exceeded and adjustment is 
required. Each wheel cylinder piston has an adjuster mechanism screwed into it 
and the rotation of this mechanism adjusts the brake according to the rate of 
lining wear. The adjuster shaft has a fast helix thread to which a drive ring 
is mounted. The adjustment rate varies, and each brake application takes up 
only a percentage of the excess shoe-to-drum clearance. Avoid overadjustment 
when the drums get hot and expand.

[FIGURE: H9545A.gif]

The drive ring is retained in the cylinder housing by the load spring. 
When the brake is applied, hydraulic pressure causes the piston to move 
outward and the adjuster shaft is lifted off the seat in the cylinder body. 
The adjuster shaft passes through the drive ring. No relative rotation occurs 
between the adjuster shaft and piston.

Adjustment is required when movement exceeds the axial clearance. After 
the brake application has been completed, the shoe return springs cause the 
shoe to push the piston and adjuster shaft back so the adjuster shaft passes 
through the axial clearance in the drive ring thread. When the ends of the 
helix and drive ring meet, the drive ring is pushed into its seat with the 
resultant friction restricting it from further rotation.

Further retraction causes the helix to rotate through the drive ring. 
This rotation of the adjuster shaft, relative to the piston, unscrews the 
adjuster shaft from the piston, increasing the overall length and reducing the 
shoe-to-drum clearance. The reliability of the mechanism is enhanced by 
immersion in brake fluid, which prevents corrosion and gives predictable 
friction levels between the components.

[FIGURE: H9546A.gif]

Brake Drum

 WARNING: DO NOT INHALE THE DUST FROM BRAKES, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS.

INSTALLING A COMPLETE BRAKE ASSEMBLY ON ONLY ONE SIDE OF THE VEHICLE. (ALWAYS 
REPLACE BRAKE LININGS IN AXLE SETS.)

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle and install safety stands. Remove the wheel and tire 
assembly.

Release parking brake and cage parking brake chamber spring by turning 
out the center bolt. Refer to Section 06-05B .

Remove the adjuster plugs from the slots in the backing plate marked 
ADJ. Remove the adjuster sight hole plugs.

Insert Rear Brake Adjustment Tool D90T-2588-AR or equivalent into the 
adjustment slot until the blade engages the slots in the adjustment wheel 
assembly. Turn the wheel in a clockwise direction (when viewed looking down 
the piston) until the shoe and lining clears the drum. Remove the drum.

 CAUTION: Use of a drum puller or a torch is not recommended. Drum distortion may 
result. 

If the drum is rusted to the axle shaft, use coarse sandpaper to remove 
the rust buildup. Remove the drum.

Check the brake drum surface. If the surface is worn or if the drum is 
suspected of having excessive runout, the drum should be machined. After 
machining, check maximum drum diameter. Drum must be replaced if diameter is 
outside maximum limit. Maximum drum diameter is stamped on the outside of the 
drum.

 Installation 

Clean the exterior of the drum with a wire brush and wipe the inside of 
the drum with a rag moistened with isopropyl alcohol or water. Install the 
drum or spider/drum assembly. Refer to Section 06-02A .

Manually adjust the wheel cylinders/adjusters through the backing plate 
adjusting holes until the shoe-to-drum clearance is less than 0.51-0.76 mm 
(0.020-0.030 inch). Apply the brake pedal to centralize the shoes and release 
the brake pedal.

 NOTE: Be sure the feeler gauges are on the lining surfaces and not in the gap 
between the lining blocks. The feeler gauges should reach the center of the 
block.

Check the shoe-to-drum clearance by using a feeler gauge placed through 
the lining inspection holes in the backing plate. If the reading is not 
0.51-0.76 mm (0.020-0.030 inch), manually adjust the wheel cylinder/adjuster 
by turning the manual override wheel in a counterclockwise direction (as 
viewed while looking down the piston) until the specified dimensions are 
obtained.

Install the wheel and tire. Install the lug nuts and tighten to the 
following specifications.

CLEANER SUCH AS ROTUNDA BRAKE/CLUTCH/SERVICE VACUUM 164-R3600 OR EQUIVALENT 
EQUIPPED FOR THIS PURPOSE TO REMOVE ANY DUST. ADHERENT DUST SHOULD BE REMOVED 
WITH A DAMP RAG. ANY DUST SHOULD BE CONTAINED IN A SEALED AND LABELED BAG FOR 
DISPOSAL. WEAR AN APPROVED HIGH-EFFICIENCY CARTRIDGE OR AIR LINE RESPIRATOR 
AND USE EXTRA CAUTION TO AVOID BREATHING THIS DUST. USE NON-ASBESTOS 
REPLACEMENT PARTS WHENEVER POSSIBLE. 

 Removal 

After the drums are removed, two procedures are available to fully 
retract the wheel cylinders. They are as follows:

 NOTE: To avoid locking the auto-adjust mechanism in the fully retracted 
position, wind out each wheel cylinder piston one complete turn after fully 
retracting the pistons.

Before removing the shoe and lining assemblies, a load must be applied 
to the wheel cylinder pistons to fully retract the cylinders.

Insert brake adjustment tool into the adjustment holes marked ADJ in 
the backing plate. Engage the tool in a slot in the adjuster manual override 
wheel. Use the backing plate as a fulcrum to turn the manual override wheel in 
a clockwise direction (as viewed while looking down the piston) until the 
piston is fully retracted.

 NOTE: Do not use power tools. Periodically check the position of the piston 
under load. After the piston has stopped moving in, screw the piston out 
(counterclockwise) one turn under load. Reinstall manual override wheel 
assemblies.

After removing the shoe and lining assemblies, remove the manual 
override from the pistons. Insert a screwdriver in the slot between the 
assembly and piston to aid in disassembly. Insert a 51-mm (2-inch) piece of 
19-mm (3/4-inch) inside diameter heater hose into a 24-mm (15/16-inch) 
12-point socket. Using a ratchet or speed brace driver, push the piston in 
hard while turning clockwise.

Clockwise to Retract

 CAUTION: Do not let the tips of the shoe webs rest on the wheel cylinder dust 
boots. 

With the return springs still installed, support the bottom shoe. 
Remove the shoe and lining assemblies by first lifting the top shoe one end at 
a time out of the wheel cylinders' tappet head slots, starting with the wheel 
cylinder/adjuster end, then the wheel cylinder/parking brake expander end.

Lift the top shoe using an adjustable wrench (305-mm [
12-inch] minimum) and a durable load plate. To avoid damaging the lining, the 
load plate should be a minimum of 102 mm (4 inches) x 25.4 mm (1 inch) x 3.2 
mm (1/8 inch).

With the top shoe lifted, rotate the protective shield of the top 
manual override wheel assembly approximately 45 degrees toward the drum to 
protect the dust boot during shoe removal.

[FIGURE: H9707B.gif]

Rotate the lifted shoe using the park cylinder assembly as the pivot 
point away from the backing plate and set it down outside the slot on the 
manual override wheel assembly. Set it far enough outside the slot so the shoe 
will slide down the protective shield.

Set the adjustable wrench and load plate aside, grasping both outer 
ends of the top shoe by hand.

Slide the top shoe out of the park cylinder slot. Lower the top shoe so 
the bottom shoe drops free of the adjuster and park cylinder assemblies.

When the hub remains attached to the axle, lift the adjuster cylinder 
assembly end of the top shoe using an adjustable wrench (305-mm [
12-inch] minimum) and a durable load plate. To avoid 
damaging the lining, the load plate should be a minimum of 102 mm (4 inches) x 
25.4 mm (1 inch) x 3.2 mm (1/8 inch). Set the shoe web outboard of the shoe 
slot as much as possible and onto the protective shield.

Using the spring removal tool, unhook adjuster cylinder return spring 
from the bottom shoe.

Lower the bottom shoe away from the park cylinder using the adjustable 
wrench and load plate. Position the bottom shoe so that the shoe web is 
outboard of the park cylinder's dust boot, then set the shoe end on the end of 
the park cylinder.

Remove the bottom shoe by disconnecting the park cylinder return 
spring. Remove the top shoe.

Remove and discard the return springs.

Inspect both the adjuster cylinder and the park cylinder for leaks. If 
leaking, replace or rebuild as necessary. Refer to Self-Adjuster and to Wheel Cylinder/Parking Brake Expander 
 in Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section.

 CAUTION: When cleaning brake parts, use only Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake 
Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 brake fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A, isopropyl alcohol or clear mentholated spirits. Do not use 
mineral base cleaning solvents such as gasoline, kerosene, carbon 
tetrachloride, acetone or paint thinner to clean brake parts or the rubber 
parts will be damaged. 

If leakage is not evident, install the dust boot and manual override 
wheel assembly on the wheel cylinder. Temporarily place an elastic band (such 
as a vacuum cleaner beater bar drive belt) around the cylinders to keep the 
pistons in place. Use a wire brush to remove any corrosion from the backing 
plate, taking care not to damage the wheel cylinder and boots.

 Installation 

Remove the elastic band from the wheel cylinders.

 NOTE: All return springs are installed behind the shoe web.

Discard and replace the shoe return springs removed from the vehicle to 
make sure auto adjuster operates properly. Use the correct color of new shoe 
return springs as indicated in the diagram, or per the instructions in the 
shoe return spring service kit.

Install the springs on the shoes in the position shown by arranging the 
top and bottom shoes and springs together on the floor as if already installed 
on the vehicle. Keep the shoes spread apart to keep tension on the springs so 
they are securely hooked into each shoe web.

 CAUTION: Do not let the tips of the shoe webs rest on the wheel cylinder dust 
boots. 

 NOTE: The replacement brake shoes must be installed correctly to the brake. 
Correct shoe installation is shown in the following illustration.

Pick the top shoe up with the bottom shoe suspending from the return 
springs. Fit the lower shoe into the lower wheel cylinders' tappet head slots, 
then walk the top shoe one end at a time onto the upper wheel cylinders' 
tappet head slots, starting with the park cylinder assembly end and finishing 
with the adjuster cylinder assembly.

[FIGURE: H9457A.gif]

Clean the exterior of the drum with a wire brush and wipe the inside of 
the drum with a rag moistened with isopropyl alcohol or water. Install the 
drum or spider/drum assembly. Refer to Section 06-02A .

Manually adjust the adjuster cylinder assemblies through the backing 
plate adjusting holes until the shoe-to-drum clearance is less than 0.51-0.76 
mm (0.020-0.030 inch). Apply the brake pedal to centralize the shoes and 
release the brake pedal.

 NOTE: Be sure the feeler gauges are on the lining surfaces and not in the gap 
between the lining blocks. The feeler gauges should reach the center of the 
block.

Check the shoe-to-drum clearance by using a feeler gauge placed through 
the lining inspection holes in the backing plate. If the reading is not 
0.51-0.76 mm (0.020-0.030 inch), manually adjust the adjuster cylinder 
assemblies by turning the manual override wheel in a counterclockwise 
direction (as viewed while looking down the piston) until the specified 
dimensions are obtained.

Install the wheel and tire. Install the lug nuts and tighten to the 
following specifications.

Insert the plugs in the inspection holes, adjuster sight holes and 
adjustment slots in the backing plate.

Uncage parking brake chambers by turning in the center bolts. Refer to 
 Section 06-05B .

Release the parking brakes and check that the right and left rear 
wheels can be rotated by hand freely and without drag.

Apply the parking brake and check that the right and left rear wheels 
cannot be rotated by hand.

Remove the safety stands and lower the vehicle to the floor.

 NOTE: The service brake system uses Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid 
C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A 
and is filled at the Hydro-Max master cylinder. The parking brake system uses 
Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® 
equivalent and is filled at the engine-driven brake pump reservoir. Do not mix 
fluids.

Check the brake fluid in the master cylinder. If required, add Ford 
High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A.

Check service and parking brakes for proper operation. Bleed both 
systems as required. Refer to Section 06-06 .

Road test the vehicle for proper operation of service and parking brake 
systems.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel Cylinder 

 CAUTION: During brake service, the parking brake chamber springs must be caged. 
Refer to Section 06-05B . 

 Removal 

 NOTE: Under no circumstances is brake fluid to be reused after being removed 
from the brake system.

Attach a tube to the bleeder screw on the park cylinder assembly. Place 
the other end of the tube in a container. Unscrew the bleeder screw one-half 
turn. Pump the brake pedal to remove all brake fluid from the rear brake 
system. Discard the brake fluid.

Remove the brake shoe and lining. Refer to Brake Shoes and 
Lining in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Disconnect the hydraulic brake line from the fitting on the adjuster 
cylinder assembly.

Remove the screw retaining the bridge pipe clip to the backing plate 
and remove the clip. Disconnect the bridge pipe from the wheel cylinders and 
remove the bridge pipe.

Remove the three 9/16-18 bolts, nuts and washers retaining the adjuster 
cylinder assembly and backing plate to the axle flange.

Use an Allen wrench to remove the bolts in the rear of the backing 
plate which retain the adjuster cylinder assembly to the backing plate. Remove 
the adjuster cylinder assembly and gasket from the backing plate. Discard 
gasket.

Remove any rust or corrosion from the backing plate with a wire brush.

 Installation 

Install a new gasket on the adjuster cylinder assembly. Position the 
assembly on the backing plate.

Install the three 9/16-18 bolts, nuts and washers retaining the 
adjuster cylinder assembly and backing plate to the axle flange. Tighten the 
bolts to 184-216 Nm (135-160 lb-ft).

Connect the bridge pipe to the wheel cylinders and tighten to 17-23 Nm
 (13-17 lb-ft). Install the bridge tube retainer and 
tighten the bolt to 6-9 Nm (53-80 lb-in).

Connect the hydraulic brake line to the adjuster cylinder assembly and 
tighten to 14-23 Nm (10-17 lb-ft).

Install the shoe and lining and drum assemblies and adjust the 
lining-to-drum clearance. Refer to Brake Shoes and Lining in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section. Tighten the bleeder screw to 17-23 Nm
 (13-17 lb-ft).

Adjust lining-to-drum clearance to 0.51-0.76 mm (0.020-0.030 inch). 
Refer to Brake Shoes and Lining in the Removal and Installation portion of 
this section.

Uncage parking brake chamber springs. Refer to Section 06-05B .

 NOTE: The service brake system uses Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid 
C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A 
and is filled at the Hydro-Max master cylinder. The parking brake system uses 
Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® 
equivalent and is filled at the engine-driven brake pump reservoir. DO NOT MIX 
FLUIDS.

Fill the Hydro-Max master cylinder reservoir with clean Ford High 
Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A. Bleed the brake system. Refer to Section 06-06 .

Release the parking brake and check that left and right wheels can be 
rotated by hand freely and without drag.

Apply the parking brake and check that the left and right wheels cannot 
be rotated by hand.

Remove the safety stands and lower the vehicle to the floor.

Check service and parking brake for proper operation. Bleed both 
systems as required. Refer to Section 06-06 .

Road test the vehicle for proper operation of service and parking brake 
systems.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Parking Brake Expander

 Removal 

 WARNING: DURING BRAKE SERVICE, THE PARKING BRAKE CHAMBER SPRING MUST BE CAGED. 
REFER TO SECTION 06-05B. 

 CAUTION: UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES IS BRAKE FLUID TO BE REUSED AFTER BEING REMOVED 
FROM THE SYSTEM. 

Attach a tube to the bleeder screw on the park cylinder assembly. Place 
the other end of the tube in a container. Unscrew the bleeder screw one-half 
turn. Pump the brake pedal to remove all brake fluid from the rear brake 
system. Discard the brake fluid. 

Remove the wheels, tires, drums and the shoe and lining. Refer to Brake 
Shoes and Lining in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Remove the parking brake chamber from the park cylinder assembly. Refer 
to Section 06-05B .

Remove the screw retaining the bridge pipe clip to the backing plate 
and remove the clip. Disconnect the bridge pipe from the cylinder and remove 
the bridge pipe.

Remove the three 9/16-18 bolts, nuts and washers retaining the park 
cylinder assembly and backing plate to the axle flange.

Use an Allen wrench to remove the bolts in the rear of the backing 
plate which retain the park cylinder assembly to the backing plate. Remove the 
park cylinder assembly and gasket from the backing plate.

Remove any rust or corrosion from the backing plate with a wire brush.

 Installation 

Install a new gasket on the park cylinder assembly. Position the 
assembly on the backing plate.

Install the three 9/16-18 bolts, nuts and washers retaining park 
cylinder assembly and backing plate to the axle flange. Tighten the bolts to 
184-216 Nm (135-160 lb-ft).

Connect the bridge pipe to the wheel cylinders and tighten to 17-23 Nm
 (13-17 lb-ft). Install the bridge pipe clip and tighten 
the screw to 6-9 Nm (53-80 lb-in).

Install the shoe and lining and brake drum assemblies. Tighten the 
bleeder screw to 17-23 Nm (12-17 lb-ft).

Fill the Hydro-Max master cylinder reservoir with clean Ford High 
Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A. Bleed the service brakes. Refer to Section 06-06 .

Push the parking brake wedge shaft in approximately 12.7 mm (1/2 inch) 
and center it in the park cylinder housing.

Install the parking brake chamber. Refer to Section 06-05B . Be careful 
to keep wedge shaft centered.

Adjust lining-to-drum clearance to 0.51-0.76 mm (0.020-0.030 inch). 
Refer to Brake Shoes and Lining in the Removal and Installation portion of 
this section.

Uncage parking brake chamber springs. Refer to Section 06-05B .

 NOTE: The service brake system uses Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid 
C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A 
and is filled at the Hydro-Max master cylinder. The parking brake system uses 
Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® 
equivalent and is filled at the engine-driven brake pump reservoir. Do not mix 
fluids.

Bleed the parking brakes. Refer to Section 06-05B . Check the 
engine-driven brake pump reservoir and, if required, check fluid level with 
the park brake applied and fill to the specified level with Motorcraft MERCON®
 ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent.

Release the parking brake and check that left and right wheels can be 
rotated by hand freely and without drag.

Apply the parking brake and check that the left and right wheels cannot 
be rotated by hand.

Remove the safety stands and lower the vehicle to the ground.

Check service and parking brake for proper operation. Bleed both 
systems as required. Refer to Section 06-06 .

Road test the vehicle for proper operation of service and parking brake 
systems.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Self Adjuster 

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: Use only clean Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or 
equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A to clean the 
parts. The same brake fluid is also required for lubrication purposes upon 
assembly.

Make sure cylinder, workbench, tools and hands are clean before 
proceeding with disassembly. Place a clean sheet of paper on the bench.

Remove the manual override wheel assembly. Slip the dust boot off the 
housing.

 NOTE: USE CARE WHEN APPLYING AIR PRESSURE TO REMOVE THE PISTON.

Remove pistons and adjuster assemblies from housing being careful not 
to cock them and scratch the housing bore. Air pressure may be used to assist 
removal. 

 NOTE: DO NOT REMOVE DRIVE RING FROM ADJUSTER SHAFT.

Remove adjuster shaft from piston. Keep adjuster shafts and pistons 
together as sets. 

Remove the seal from the piston. Use care not to score the seal groove. 
Discard the seal.

 WARNING: DO NOT USE GENERAL PARTS CLEANING EQUIPMENT. WEAR SAFETY GLASSES WHEN 
CLEANING PARTS. 

Wash all parts with clean Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid 
C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A. Place cleaned parts on a clean sheet of paper.

To clean adjuster shaft hole in piston, half-fill threaded hole with 
new brake fluid. Cover hole and shake piston vigorously. Rapidly turn piston 
upside down and drain brake fluid. Do not use cleaning brush.

Clean adjuster shaft assembly by immersing it in new brake fluid. Blow 
off threads, ports, drive ring and spring. Do not use cleaning brush.

Coat piston and adjuster shaft threads with new brake fluid.

Assemble piston and adjuster shaft. Adjuster shaft must turn freely and 
smoothly without roughness or drag.

 NOTE: Cylinder bore diameter must not be larger than 44.5 mm (1.753 inches). 
If larger than specified, replace the cylinder housing.

 NOTE: Some discoloration of the bore surface near the mouths of the cylinder 
housing or around the diameter of the piston may be apparent. This is a 
natural result of brake actuation over a period of operation.

Inspect the cylinder housing bore for evidence of glazing, scoring, 
corrosion or ridges. If glazing, scoring, corrosion or ridges are present, 
either hone or replace the cylinder housing.

Use the following procedure when honing:

Hone the cylinder bore using a 220 spring-loaded wheel cylinder stone 
that gives a smooth finish.

Clean the cylinder with isopropyl alcohol to remove all honing residue.

Install a new seal kit using the following assembly instructions.

 Assembly 

Install a new seal in the groove on the piston so that the seal lip 
faces away from the shoe web slot as shown.

[FIGURE: H5089A.gif]

 NOTE: It is essential that the adjuster shaft rotates freely in the piston to 
allow for the initial self-adjuster movement to take place. If the shaft binds 
or does not rotate freely in the piston, replace the piston and adjuster shaft.

Turn the adjuster shaft until it bottoms in the piston and then unscrew 
the shaft one full turn.

[FIGURE: H40601A.gif]

Install the spring locator and load spring in the adjuster shaft.

Lubricate the piston with clean Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid 
C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A. Install the piston assembly in the housing cylinder bore.

Install the dust boot onto the wheel cylinder.

 NOTE: Make sure the piston head ears are properly located in the 
corresponding flats in the piston.

 NOTE: Do not turn the manual override wheel assembly.

Install the manual override wheel assembly.

 Assembly 

 CAUTION: Care must be taken when assembling the park cylinder assembly. Both 
Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 
fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A and a synthetic-based grease 
(BATCO 5-86-B grease or equivalent or Castrol G148 or equivalent) are used 
within the housing because they are compatible with each other. The 
lubrication points are shown in the following figure. THE USE OF ANY 
MINERAL-BASED GREASE WILL CAUSE CONTAMINATION OF THE SEALS AND MAY RESULT IN 
BRAKE FAILURE. Use only the specified lubricants. 

 NOTE: The BATCO 5-86-B or Castrol G148 or equivalent silicone grease will 
occasionally migrate through the brake system. When this occurs, it may form a 
clear gel-like substance that floats on top of the brake fluid in the master 
cylinder. This condition is normal and in no way affects the operation of the 
brake system.

sleeve into position.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cleaning

 WARNING: DO NOT INHALE DUST FROM BRAKES, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. 
INHALATION OF DUST CAN BE HAZARDOUS TO YOUR HEALTH AND COULD CAUSE CANCER OR 
ASBESTOSIS. COMPRESSED AIR OR BRUSHES MUST NOT BE USED TO CLEAN BRAKES, BRAKE 
DRUMS, CLUTCHES AND ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. USE ROTUNDA BRAKE/CLUTCH/SERVICE 
VACUUM 164-R3600 OR EQUIVALENT EQUIPPED FOR THIS PURPOSE TO CAREFULLY REMOVE 
ANY DUST. ADHERENT DUST SHOULD BE REMOVED WITH A DAMP RAG. ANY DUST SHOULD BE 
CONTAINED IN A SEALED AND LABELED BAG FOR DISPOSAL. WEAR AN APPROVED 
HIGH-EFFICIENCY CARTRIDGE OR AIR LINE RESPIRATOR AND USE EXTRA CAUTION TO 
AVOID BREATHING THIS DUST. ALWAYS USE NON-ASBESTOS REPLACEMENT PARTS WHENEVER 
POSSIBLE. 

Use Rotunda Brake/Clutch/Service Vacuum 164-R3600 or equivalent to 
remove all dust from backing plates and interior of brake drums.

================================================================================
PAGE 4696
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 06-02B: Brake, Hydraulic Drum

1997 LN-7000 Equipped with Hydraulic Drum Brakes Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Inspection

 Wheel Cylinders 

Wheel cylinders should not be disassembled unless they are leaking. 
Carefully pull lower edges of wheel cylinder boots away from cylinders to see 
if the interior of the cylinder is wet with brake fluid. Excessive fluid at 
this point indicates leakage past piston cups and a need for wheel cylinder 
overhaul.

 NOTE: A slight amount of fluid is nearly always present and acts as a 
lubricant for the piston. It is not necessary to remove the brake cylinder 
from the backing plate to disassemble, inspect, hone and overhaul the 
cylinder. Removal is necessary only if the cylinder is damaged or scored 
beyond service.

 Brake Drums 

Minor scores on a brake drum can be removed with sandpaper. Do not 
refinish brake drums to remove score marks. A drum surface that is highly 
polished can cause the brake to lock up. This polished condition should be 
removed either with sandpaper or by refinishing the drum. A brake drum that is 
out of round sufficiently enough to cause vehicle vibration or noise when 
braking should be refinished. Remove only enough stock to true-up the brake 
drum. Brake drum maximum inside diameter is shown on each brake drum. If the 
maximum inside diameter shown on the brake drum is exceeded either through 
wear or refinishing, the brake drum must be replaced.

Check the inside diameter of the brake drum with Brake Adjustment Gauge 
D81L-1103-A or equivalent or Rotunda Brake Drum Micrometer 104-00046 or 
equivalent.

 After a brake drum is refinished, wipe the refinished surface with a 
cloth soaked in clean denatured alcohol. If one brake drum is refinished, the 
opposite brake drum on the same axle should also be refinished to the same 
diameter.

 Brake Lining 

Brake linings that are worn to within 0.8 mm (1/32 inch) of a rivet 
head or 1.5 mm (1/16 inch) of the shoe on bonded linings or have been 
contaminated with brake fluid, grease or oil must be replaced. Failure to 
replace worn linings will result in a scored drum. When it is necessary to 
replace linings, they must also be replaced on the wheel on the opposite side 
of the vehicle.

 Springs 

Check condition of brake shoes, brake shoe retracting spring, brake 
shoe hold-down springs and drum for signs of overheating. If shoes have a 
slight blue coloring indicating overheating, brake shoe retracting spring and 
brake shoe hold-down springs should be replaced. Overheated springs lose their 
tension and could allow new lining to drag and wear prematurely if not replaced.

 Brake Backing Plate 

Clean the ledge pads on the brake backing plate. Sand lightly to bare 
metal.

Apply a light coating (0.80 mm [1/32-inch] thick) of 
high temperature lithium-base grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C 
or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B or Disc Brake 
Caliper Lubricant D7AZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C172-A at the points where the rear brake shoe and lining touch the 
brake backing plate.

================================================================================
PAGE 4697
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 06-02B: Brake, Hydraulic Drum

1997 LN-7000 Equipped with Hydraulic Drum Brakes Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake Shoe, Initial Setting 

With automatic adjusting brakes, it is important to set the 
shoe-to-drum clearance prior to driving the vehicle. This makes sure that 
excessive movement of the wheel cylinder piston is avoided and that the 
correct and stabilized running clearance of the auto-adjuster is quickly 
achieved.

After servicing the brake, initial brake shoe-to-drum clearance should 
be set to 0.51-0.76 mm (0.020-0.030 inch).

To adjust, use the recommended Rear Brake Adjustment Tool D90T-2588-AR 
or equivalent, and using the backing plate as a fulcrum, turn the manual 
override wheel in a counterclockwise direction as viewed when looking down the 
piston.

For detailed procedure, refer to Brake Shoes and Lining in the Removal 
and Installation portion of this section.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Caliper, Heavy-Duty Rail Slider 

The disc brake caliper is a rail slider design with dual pistons on the 
same side of the rotor. The pistons and cylinder bores are protected by boot 
seals fitted to a groove in the piston and in the caliper housing.

The brake assembly consists of a caliper, which slides on the rails of 
the adapter support assembly, containing identical inner and outer brake pads. 
Both the caliper and brake pads are common for right and left assemblies.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Service Precautions

 WARNING: DO NOT INHALE DUST FROM BRAKES, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. 
INHALATION OF DUST CAN BE HAZARDOUS TO YOUR HEALTH AND COULD CAUSE CANCER OR 
ASBESTOSIS. COMPRESSED AIR OR BRUSHES MUST NOT BE USED TO CLEAN BRAKES, BRAKE 
DRUMS, CLUTCHES AND ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. USE ROTUNDA BRAKE/CLUTCH/SERVICE 
VACUUM 164-R3600 OR EQUIVALENT EQUIPPED FOR THIS PURPOSE TO REMOVE ANY DUST. 
ADHERENT DUST SHOULD BE REMOVED WITH A DAMP RAG. ANY DUST SHOULD BE CONTAINED 
IN A SEALED AND LABELED BAG FOR DISPOSAL. WEAR AN APPROVED HIGH EFFICIENCY 
CARTRIDGE OR AIR LINE RESPIRATOR AND USE EXTRA CAUTION TO AVOID BREATHING THIS 
DUST. USE NON-ASBESTOS REPLACEMENT PARTS WHENEVER POSSIBLE.

 Removal 

To avoid fluid overflow when the caliper pistons are pressed into the 
caliper cylinder bores, remove part of the brake fluid from the master 
cylinder reservoir (connected to the front disc brakes). Do not drain 
completely. Discard the drained brake fluid.

Raise the vehicle and install safety stands. Remove the front wheel 
assembly. Refer to Section 04-04 .

Remove the key retaining bolt.

[FIGURE: H40321C.gif]

Using a brass rod and light hammer, drive out the key and spring.

[FIGURE: H40331C.gif]

 NOTE: It is not necessary to disconnect the hydraulic line when replacing 
brake lining pad assemblies. However, DO NOT let the caliper hang on the 
hydraulic hose. Lay the caliper on the suspension or support it with a length 
of wire. If the caliper is being overhauled or replaced, then disconnect the 
hydraulic hose.

Remove the caliper from its support assembly by rotating the key and 
spring end out and away from the rotor. Lift the opposite end of the caliper 
clear of the slide in the support and off the rotor. Lay the caliper on the 
suspension or support it with a length of wire.

Remove the pad retaining spring.

Slots are provided in the lining abutment rails of the caliper through 
which the brake lining pads will pass and permit the removal of the brake 
lining pad assemblies. Remove the outer lining pad, farthest from the piston, 
first, followed by the inner assembly (contacting the pistons).

Inspect the inside of the caliper, particularly the areas around the 
pistons and boots for leaks. Wipe the inside of the caliper. Clean and check 
the dust boots for cuts, cracks or other damage. If damage is noted or 
evidence of leakage is found, the caliper should be overhauled.

Clean caliper retaining key and spring.

Clean caliper and support rails, removing any rust buildup by filing 
lightly with fine file.

 Installation 

Place a block of wood across the face of the pistons. Using a C-clamp, 
push the pistons back to the bottom of the piston bores to provide clearance 
for the caliper to fit over the rotor when new brake lining pad assemblies are 
installed.

[FIGURE: H40341B.gif]

Lubricate rails at both ends of the caliper using Disc Brake Caliper 
Slide Grease D7AZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C72-A.

Install the new brake lining pad assemblies in the caliper by inserting 
them through the slots in the lining abutment rails. Install the inboard brake 
lining pad assembly first with the metal side against the pistons. 
Installation of the outboard brake lining pad follows with the lining side 
facing the inboard lining.

Position the caliper rail into the lower rail on the support and rotate 
the upper end of the caliper into position on the upper support rail over the 
rotor.

Install the pad retaining spring so that the ends are seated in the 
groove at the caliper rails, and the sides extend over the top of the lining 
backing plates.

 NOTE: The spring is between the key and caliper and the spring tangs overlap 
the ends of the key.

Position the key and spring, and start the subassembly between the 
caliper and support by hand. Use a brake adjusting tool or screwdriver to hold 
up the caliper, if required, against the support assembly.

[FIGURE: H4063G.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

Caliper

Using a hammer, drive the key and spring into position, aligning the 
correct notch with the existing hole in the support.

Secure the key to the support with the key retaining bolt. Tighten the 
bolt to 19-29 Nm (14-21 lb-ft).

After new brake lining pad assemblies and wheel assemblies have been 
installed on both front wheels, lower the vehicle. Check the master cylinder 
reservoirs, and fill if necessary with clean High Performance DOT-3 Brake 
Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT-3 fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A.

Depress the brake pedal firmly several times to seat the linings on the 
rotor. Do not move the vehicle until the pedal is firm.

If any hydraulic lines were disconnected, bleed the hydraulic system. 
Refer to Section 06-06 . Check for leakage at all connections under maximum 
pressure. Refill reservoir as required.

Reinstall front wheels. Refer to Section 04-04 . Lower vehicle to the 
ground and road test the vehicle.

Section 06-03A: Brake, Hydraulic Disc, Rail Slider

1997 LN-7000 with 7000-Pound Front Axles and Hydraulic Brakes Workshop Manual

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Caliper

 Disassembly 

Remove the caliper assembly. Refer to Caliper, Heavy-Duty Rail 
Slider in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Disconnect the hydraulic hose and cap or tape the fittings to prevent 
dirt from entering the hydraulic line.

Check the brake hose for worn spots, cracks or other signs of 
deterioration. Replace the hose if damaged.

Drain the brake fluid from the caliper.

 CAUTION: Do not use mineral base cleaning solvents such as gasoline, kerosene, 
carbon tetrachloride, acetone or paint thinner to clean the caliper. These 
solvents will damage the rubber parts. 

Thoroughly clean the caliper exterior with clean isopropyl alcohol or 
brake fluid.

Remove the boot protectors.

 WARNING: DO NOT USE AN EXCESSIVE AMOUNT OF AIR PRESSURE TO REMOVE THE PISTONS. 
EXCESSIVE PRESSURE CAN FORCE THE PISTONS OUT OF THE BORE WITH ENOUGH FORCE TO 
CAUSE PERSONAL INJURY. NEVER ATTEMPT TO CATCH THE PISTONS AS THEY COME OUT OF 
THE BORE. 

Place a small block of wood under caliper pistons. Pad caliper exterior 
with a clean shop towel. Remove the pistons by directing compressed air into 
the caliper fluid outlet.

[FIGURE: H40641A.gif]

Remove and discard the piston boots.

 NOTE: The piston outside diameter is the primary sealing surface in the 
caliper assembly. The piston must not be refinished by any means, and 
abrasives should not be used.

Carefully examine the piston outer diameter for scoring, nicks, 
corrosion and worn or damaged plating. Replace if any wear or damage is 
detected.

 CAUTION: Do not use a metal tool for this operation as it may damage the caliper 
bore. 

Use a pointed piece of wood or plastic to remove piston seals from the 
groove in the caliper bore and discard seals.

[FIGURE: H40651A.gif]

 Assembly 

 CAUTION: Do not use mineral base cleaning solvents such as gasoline, kerosene, 
carbon tetrachloride, acetone or paint thinner to clean the caliper. These 
solvents will damage the rubber parts. 

Clean all other parts in clean isopropyl alcohol or brake fluid. Use 
dry, filtered low-pressure compressed air to dry parts and blow out all 
passages in the caliper and bleeding valve.

Place caliper assembly on a clean bench area, over clean cloth or 
paper, with the open end of cylinder facing up.

Dip the new piston seal in clean High Performance DOT-3 Brake Fluid 
C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT-3 fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A, and install it in the cylinder groove. Gently work the seal 
around the cylinder bore with a finger until it is properly seated into the 
seal groove. Be sure the seal is not twisted or rolled in the groove.

[FIGURE: H40661B.gif]

Install the dust boot in its cylinder groove in the same manner as the 
piston seal.

Coat the outside diameter of the piston with clean High Performance 
DOT-3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT-3 fluid meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M6C25-A. Use a small flat plastic or wood tool to gradually 
work the dust boot around the piston.

[FIGURE: H40671A.gif]

Press the piston straight into the caliper piston bore until it 
bottoms. The boot internal diameter should slide up the piston as the piston 
is pushed into the caliper bore, and comes to rest in the boot groove in the 
piston.

Install the boot protector.

[FIGURE: H40681A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Caliper

 NOTE: When raising the vehicle, make sure that the hoist lift points do not 
rest on the caliper pins.

Raise vehicle on hoist. 

Remove the wheel.

Visually check the front disc brake caliper. If the front disc brake 
caliper housing is leaking, it should be replaced. If a piston seal is 
leaking, the front disc brake caliper must be disassembled and new piston 
seals installed. If a caliper piston is seized in the bore, a new front disc 
brake caliper housing is required.

If a caliper piston is removed for any reason, the piston seal must be 
replaced. 

Clean all metal parts with isopropyl alcohol. Then, clean out and dry 
the grooves and passageways with compressed air. Make sure that caliper bore 
and component parts are thoroughly clean and dry prior to assembly.

Check the cylinder bore and caliper piston for excessive scoring or 
corrosion.

================================================================================

================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 06-03A: Brake, Hydraulic Disc, Rail Slider

1997 LN-7000 with 7000-Pound Front Axles and Hydraulic Brakes Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Brake Pad and Linings

Inspect brake pads and lining for wear. If the lining is worn to within 
3 mm (1/8 inch) of the pad, replace all (four) pad and lining assemblies 
(complete axle set) on front wheels as required.

Do not attempt to clean or restore any oil- or grease-soaked brake pad 
and lining. When contaminated brake pad and lining are found, they must be 
replaced in complete axle sets.

1997 L-Series

Section 06-03A: Brake, Hydraulic Disc, Rail Slider

1997 LN-7000 with 7000-Pound Front Axles and Hydraulic Brakes Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Rotor

Grease or any other foreign material must be kept off the brake shoe 
and lining surfaces of the front disc brake rotor and external surfaces of the 
hub during service operations. In handling the front disc brake rotor and disc 
brake caliper assemblies, avoid deformation of the front disc brake rotor and 
nicking or scratching of brake shoes and linings.

Each time the brakes are serviced, the disc brake rotor should be 
checked for scoring, runout, parallelism and thickness.

Rotor scoring and runout can be checked on most brakes with the caliper 
either on or off. To check parallelism and thickness, the caliper must be 
removed.

Rotor specifications are listed in the Specifications 
portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Service Precautions

 WARNING: DO NOT INHALE DUST FROM BRAKES, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. 
INHALATION OF DUST CAN BE HAZARDOUS TO YOUR HEALTH AND COULD CAUSE CANCER OR 
ASBESTOSIS. COMPRESSED AIR OR BRUSHES MUST NOT BE USED TO CLEAN BRAKES, BRAKE 
DRUMS, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. USE ROTUNDA BRAKE/CLUTCH/SERVICE 
VACUUM 164-R3600 OR EQUIVALENT EQUIPPED FOR THIS PURPOSE TO REMOVE ANY DUST. 
ADHERENT DUST SHOULD BE REMOVED WITH A DAMP RAG. ANY DUST SHOULD BE CONTAINED 
IN A SEALED AND LABELED BAG FOR DISPOSAL. WEAR AN APPROVED HIGH EFFICIENCY 
CARTRIDGE OR AIR LINE RESPIRATOR AND USE EXTRA CAUTION TO AVOID BREATHING THIS 
DUST. USE NON-ASBESTOS REPLACEMENT PARTS WHENEVER POSSIBLE.

 Removal 

To avoid fluid overflow when the caliper pistons are pressed into the 
caliper cylinder bores, drain a portion of the brake fluid from the master 
cylinder reservoir, connected to the front disc brakes. Do not drain 
completely. Discard the fluid that is drained from the cylinder.

Raise the vehicle evenly and support on safety stands. Remove the front 
wheel and tire assembly or rim and tire assembly. Refer to Section 04-04 .

Remove the two bolts and the spring plate retainer assembly.

[FIGURE: H3637C.gif]

Remove the bolt at the bottom end of the caliper support and slide the 
key out from between caliper and support rails.

[FIGURE: H3638F.gif]

 NOTE: It is not necessary to disconnect the hydraulic line when replacing 
brake lining pad assemblies. However, DO NOT let the caliper hang on the 
hydraulic hose. Lay the caliper on the suspension or support it with a length 
of wire. If the caliper is being overhauled or replaced, then disconnect the 
hydraulic line.

Rotate the upper end of the caliper up and away from the upper support 
rail and lift assembly off the rotor.

[FIGURE: H3639D.gif]

Remove the pad retaining spring.

Slots are provided in the lining abutment rails through which the brake 
lining pads will pass permitting removal of the brake lining pad assemblies. 
Remove the outer lining pad (farthest from the piston) first, followed by the 
inner pad assembly (contacting the pistons).

[FIGURE: H36401C.gif]

Inspect the inside of the caliper, particularly the areas around the 
pistons and boots for leaks. Wipe the inside of the caliper. Clean and check 
the dust boots for cuts, cracks or other damage. If damage is noted or 
evidence of leakage is found, the caliper should be overhauled.

[FIGURE: H36411A.gif]

Clean caliper retaining key and spring plate retainer assembly.

Clean caliper and support rails, removing any rust buildup by filing 
lightly with a fine file.

 Installation 

Place a block of wood across the face of the pistons. Using a C-clamp, 
push the pistons back to the bottom of the piston bores to provide clearance 
for the caliper to fit over the rotor when new brake lining pad assemblies are 
installed.

[FIGURE: H36421A.gif]

Lubricate rails at both ends of the caliper using Disc Brake Caliper 
Slide Grease D7AZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C172-A.

Install the new brake lining pad assemblies in the caliper by inserting 
them through the slots in the lining abutment rails. Install the inboard brake 
lining pad assembly first with the metal side against the pistons. 
Installation of the outboard brake lining pad assembly follows with the brake 
lining side facing the inboard lining.

Place caliper assembly over the rotor and rest on lower support rail. 
Rotate upper end of caliper down into position on upper support rail. Install 
key from inboard side and lock in place with bolt. Tighten to 19-29 Nm
 (14-21 lb-ft).

Install the pad retaining spring so that the ends are seated in the 
grooves of the caliper and the sides extend over the top of the lining backing 
plates.

 CAUTION: After performing this step, examine installation to determine that 
springs are seated properly against shoulder on caliper and support rails. 

Install spring plate retainer at opposite end of caliper assembly with 
two bolts. Tighten bolts to 33-47 Nm (24-35 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: H3644C.gif]

Add clean heavy-duty brake fluid, such as Ford High Performance DOT 3 
Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A, into the master cylinder reservoir to bring the fluid level to 
6.35 mm (0.25 inch) from the top of the reservoir.

If any hydraulic lines were disconnected, bleed the hydraulic system. 
Refer to Section 06-06 . Pump the brake pedal several times to make sure the 
brake linings are adjusted. Check for leakage at all connections under maximum 
pressure. Refill master cylinder reservoir as necessary.

Reinstall front wheels, lower to ground and road test the vehicle. 
Refer to Section 04-04 for wheel installation.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Caliper, Dual Piston

 Disassembly 

Remove the caliper assembly. Refer to Caliper, Heavy-Duty Rail 
Slider in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Disconnect the hydraulic hose and cap or tape the fittings to prevent 
dirt from entering the hydraulic line.

Check the brake hose for worn spots, cracks or other signs of 
deterioration. Replace the hose if damaged.

Drain the brake fluid from the caliper.

 CAUTION: Do not use mineral base cleaning solvents such as gasoline, kerosene, 
carbon tetrachloride, acetone or paint thinner to clean the caliper. These 
solvents will damage the rubber parts. 

Thoroughly clean the caliper exterior with clean isopropyl alcohol or 
brake fluid.

Remove the boot protectors.

 WARNING: DO NOT USE AN EXCESSIVE AMOUNT OF AIR PRESSURE TO REMOVE THE PISTONS. 
EXCESSIVE PRESSURE CAN FORCE THE PISTONS OUT OF THE BORE WITH ENOUGH FORCE TO 
CAUSE PERSONAL INJURY. NEVER ATTEMPT TO CATCH THE PISTONS AS THEY COME OUT OF 
THE BORE. 

Place a small block of wood approximately 51 mm (2 inches) thick under 
caliper pistons. Pad caliper exterior with a clean shop towel. Remove the 
pistons by directing compressed air into the caliper fluid outlet.

[FIGURE: H36451A.gif]

Remove and discard the piston boots.

 NOTE: This piston outside diameter is the primary sealing surface in the 
caliper assembly. The piston must not be refinished by any means, and 
abrasives should not be used.

Carefully examine the piston outer diameter for scoring, nicks, 
corrosion and worn or damaged plating. Replace if any wear or damage is 
detected.

 CAUTION: Do not use a metal tool for this operation as it may damage the caliper 
bore. 

Use a pointed piece of wood or plastic to remove piston seals from the 
groove in the caliper bore and discard seals.

[FIGURE: H36461A.gif]

 Assembly 

 CAUTION: Do not use mineral base cleaning solvents such as gasoline, kerosene, 
carbon tetrachloride, acetone or paint thinner to clean the caliper. These 
will damage the rubber parts. 

Clean all other parts in clean isopropyl alcohol or brake fluid. Use 
dry, filtered low-pressure compressed air to dry parts and blow out all 
passages in the caliper and bleeding valve.

Place caliper assembly on a clean bench area, over clean cloth or 
paper, with the open end of cylinder facing up.

Dip the new piston seal in clean Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake 
Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A and install it in the cylinder groove. Gently work the seal around 
the cylinder bore with a finger until it is properly seated into the seal 
groove. Be sure the seal is not twisted or rolled in the groove.

[FIGURE: H36471A.gif]

Install the dust boot in its cylinder groove in the same manner as the 
piston seal.

Coat the outside diameter of the piston with clean Ford High 
Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A. Use a small flat plastic or wood tool to 
gradually work the dust boot around the piston.

[FIGURE: H36481A.gif]

Press the piston straight into the caliper piston bore until it 
bottoms. The boot internal diameter should slide up the piston as the piston 
is pushed into the caliper bore and comes to rest in the boot groove in the 
piston.

[FIGURE: H36491A.gif]

Install the boot protectors.

Section 06-05A: Brake, Air, Parking/Emergency System

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Parking/Emergency System 

 WARNING: IN THE EVENT OF PARKING BRAKE SYSTEM DAMAGE, THE VEHICLE SHOULD NOT BE 
OPERATED UNTIL THE SYSTEM IS SERVICED. 

The parking brake system is composed of a parking brake control valve, 
a modulating valve (trucks) or double check valve (tractors), quick release 
valves and spring brakes. The spring brake chambers use a powerful spring to 
mechanically apply the brakes when air pressure is not available (provided the 
brakes are properly adjusted). 

Air pressure compresses the spring in the brake air chamber when the 
parking brake control is in the release position. The air pressure is 
delivered to the brake air chamber by modulating valve or a double check 
valve. The modulating valve is controlled by an air pressure signal from the 
parking brake control valve on the instrument panel. The modulating valve or 
double check valve also functions to prevent the application of the spring 
brakes and service brakes at the same time, thus preventing brake system 
damage. 

 Emergency Stopping, Tractors 

For emergency stopping, tractors use a vertically split brake system. 
If an air pressure loss occurs somewhere in the front brake system (hose, air 
line, etc.), the rear (primary) brake system will continue to operate until 
the supply air is depleted by several brake applications. An air pressure loss 
in the rear brake system makes the front (secondary) brake system responsible 
for stopping the vehicle until the air supply in the reservoir(s) is depleted. 

 WARNING: IN THE EVENT OF BRAKE SYSTEM DAMAGE, THE VEHICLE SHOULD NOT BE OPERATED 
UNTIL THE SYSTEM IS SERVICED. 

 Emergency Stopping, Trucks 

Emergency brake systems on trucks are different than brake systems on 
tractors. The rear (primary) brake system operates similarly to a tractor-type 
system when there is a failure in the front brake system. A failure in the 
rear brake system leaves the front brakes continuing to function, but 
additional braking power is provided by the modulation of the rear spring 
brakes application. This is done by the modulating valve. 

For either truck or tractor emergency systems, the stopping 
capabilities of the brakes are reduced during a brake failure since not all of 
the brakes are functional. Upon service of the component, the system should 
return to normal operation.

 WARNING: IN THE EVENT OF BRAKE SYSTEM DAMAGE, THE VEHICLE SHOULD NOT BE OPERATED 
UNTIL THE SYSTEM IS SERVICED. 

The brake air chamber assembly consists of two separate air chambers, 
each having its own application and release mechanism. The only difference 
between the two chambers is that the service chamber applies the brake by air 
pressure and releases it by spring pressure; the spring brake chamber applies 
the brake by spring pressure and releases it by air pressure. 

 Parking/Emergency Stopping 

During normal driving (brakes released), the service brakes are held in 
the released position by the diaphragm return spring in the service air 
chamber assembly. Air reservoir pressure against the spring brake chamber 
piston and diaphragm keeps the parking-emergency spring compressed. 

During normal braking (service brakes applied), air pressure from the 
foot control valve pressing on the service brake diaphragm applies the brakes. 
Air reservoir pressure in the spring brake chamber keeps the parking-emergency 
spring compressed. Normal service brake operation is not affected by the 
spring brake. 

During parking or an emergency brake application, air is exhausted from 
the spring brake chamber permitting the parking-emergency spring to expand, 
moving the spring brake piston and the brake air chamber push rod against the 
slack adjuster assembly to apply the brakes. 

Loss of air pressure at the spring brake chamber will result in 
automatic application of the brakes. If it is necessary to move the vehicle 
before air pressure can be restored, the parking-emergency spring must be 
manually compressed. The procedure for manually releasing and then resetting 
the spring brake after service has been performed is described in Section 06-08E or Section 06-08F . The vehicle should not be driven until the brake 
system is serviced.

Two types of spring brake chambers are used: Maxi-Brake II and MGM.

================================================================================
PAGE 4733
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 06-05A: Brake, Air, Parking/Emergency System

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Maxi-Brake II 

The Midland Maxi-Brake II brake air chambers are standard. The Maxi has 
an emergency chamber, a service chamber and a bulkhead assembly. 

The service chamber applies the brake by air pressure and releases it 
by spring pressure when air is exhausted from the service brake chamber. The 
emergency brake in the end cap is applied by spring pressure and released by 
air pressure. 

A safe level of air pressure within the system holds spring brakes 
released, but always ready for parking or emergency application.

[FIGURE: H8914B.gif]

Since the service section and spring brake section are isolated from 
each other by seals, the spring brake cannot interfere with the operation of 
the normal service brake.

[FIGURE: H9702A.gif]

A hand operated parking brake control valve in the cab to exhaust air 
pressure from the spring brake air chamber gives the driver foolproof and 
positive parking brakes.

[FIGURE: H9703A.gif]

For Maxi-Brake II brake chamber service procedures, refer to Section 06-08E .

Brake Assembly, MGM

The MGM brake air chamber assembly used on rear wheel service brakes is 
a spring-applied parking brake which acts as an emergency brake in case of air 
pressure loss.

Section 06-05A: Brake, Air, Parking/Emergency System

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Valve, Parking Brake Control 

The parking brake control valve is a push-pull, manually operated air 
control valve. It is pressure- sensitive and will automatically move from the 
parking brake released position to the apply position if both primary and 
secondary air reservoirs are reduced to below 241-310 kPa (35-45 psi).

Air pressure is constantly supplied to the supply port from the air 
reservoirs. As the parking brake control valve is pushed in, air is supplied 
to the spring chambers releasing the parking brakes. This air pressure also 
acts on the surface area of the inlet and exhaust valve to keep the valve in. 
If the air supply pressure to the valve is reduced to a pressure of 241-310 
kPa (35-45 psi), a spring will overcome the force created by the air pressure 
on the inlet and exhaust valve and the valve will pop out. This will apply the 
parking brakes by releasing the air from the brake air chambers out through 
the parking brake control valve exhaust port. 

The parking brakes are normally applied by manually pulling out the 
parking brake control valve and releasing the air from the spring chambers.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Valve, Modulating

The modulating valve is used on the parking system for truck-type 
vehicles only. 

The modulating valve is used in conjunction with a dual air brake 
system and spring brakes and performs four functions: 

limits hold-off pressure to the spring brake air chambers to 655-724 
kPa (95-105 psi)

provides for quick release of air pressure from the spring cavity of 
the spring brake air chamber allowing a fast application of the spring brake

modulates spring brake application should a failure occur in the 
service brake system

prevents compounding of service and spring forces

Brake Air Chamber

 NOTE: The force of the spring below the balance piston is adjustable by an 
external screw on the modulating valve. The adjustment is set at the factory 
so the inlet valve will close at a slightly greater pressure, 655 kPa (95 
psi), than the hold-off pressure of the spring brake actuator, but below the 
maximum system pressure. 

When air pressure in the spring brake compartment of the brake air 
chamber has released the spring brake and when air pressure on top of the 
balance piston is sufficient to overcome the force of the balance piston 
spring, the balance piston moves. When the balance piston moves, it allows the 
inlet valve spring to close the inlet valve, shutting off further air pressure 
from the reservoir that supplies the modulating valve.

When the parking brakes are released and a normal service brake 
application is made by actuating the foot control valve, air from the primary 
circuit is delivered to the lower side of the control piston through the 
balance port. Air from the secondary circuit is delivered to the top of the 
control piston through the control port. Because air pressure from the primary 
and secondary circuits are not equal, there will be a slight movement of the 
control piston but the modulating valve does not operate.

The pressure differential between the primary and secondary circuits 
regulates the amount of air pressure released from the spring cavity of the 
spring brake air chamber. This results in a brake application on the rear axle

air pressure would be delivered to the top of the control piston. However, the 
inlet and exhaust valve and balance piston would not move and the braking on 
the rear axle(s) is made sure by the primary circuit supplying rear axle 
service brakes. The spring brakes would not be actuated.

Brake Air Chamber 

When the knob of the parking brake control valve is pulled to the park 
(exhaust) position, the modulating valve's supply air pressure and the air 
pressure in the brake air chamber is exhausted. The single check valve speeds 
the exhaust of air from the brake air chamber cavities by allowing the air on 
top of the balance piston to exhaust by the double check valve through the 
supply port to the atmosphere. When air pressure drops sufficiently, the 
balance piston opens the inlet valve, opening the larger passage in the 
modulating valve. This makes sure the balance of air pressure in the spring 
cavity of the brake air chamber exhausts rapidly.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Valve, Quick Release 

The quick release valve is used for several functions in the brake 
system. It is mounted near the brake air chambers to provide a close exit 
point for exhausted air. The nearer the air exhaust port, the quicker the 
application of the spring brake or release of the service brake.

It is used in tractors to release air pressure in the service line. It 
is used in the parking brake system to provide a faster brake application and 
to eliminate the undesirable exhausting of large quantities of air into the cab.

[FIGURE: H4959E.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

2A095

Quick Release Valve

2

—

Supply Port (Part of 2A095)

3

—

Delivery Port (Part of 2A095)

4

—

Exhaust Port (Not Threaded) (Part of 2A095)

When a brake application is made, air pressure enters the supply port. 
The diaphragm moves down and seals the exhaust. At the same time, air pressure 
forces the edges of the diaphragm down and air flows out the delivery port. 

When air pressure being delivered (beneath the diaphragm) equals the 
pressure being delivered by the brake valve (above the diaphragm), the 
diaphragm outer edge will seal against the body seat. The exhaust port is 
still sealed by the center portion of the diaphragm when the foot control 
valve application is released. When the air pressure above the diaphragm is 
released back through the foot control valve exhaust port, air pressure 
beneath the diaphragm forces the diaphragm to rise, opening the exhaust port 
and allowing air to exhaust.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Valve, Double Check 

The double check valve is used in an air brake system to direct a flow 
of air into a common line from either of two sources, whichever is at the 
higher pressure. It can be used for directing airflow for specific functions 
or to select the higher pressure of either of two sources of air as a supply 
source. 

 Double Check Valve 

[FIGURE: H4167D.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Inlet Port (Part of 2K119)

2

—

Delivery Port (Part of 2K119)

3

—

Shuttle (Part of 2K119)

4

—

Body (Part of 2K119)

5

—

Shuttle Guide (Part of 2K119)

6

—

O-Ring (Part of 2K119)

The double check valve is used in several parts of the brake system. It 
is used in the brake system for tractors to make sure both the service brake 
force and the spring force of a brake air chamber are not applied at the same 
time, which could damage the brake system. If the parking brakes are applied, 
the air is released from the spring hold-off side of the brake air chamber to 
provide spring application of the brakes. To make sure that the service 
chamber force is not applied at the same time, the double check valve routes 
air pressure to the spring brake hold-off side of the brake air chamber during 
a service brake application, relieving the spring force proportional to the 
service brake application. 

The double check valve used in the parking brake supply line serves to 
make sure that if a failure occurs in either the primary or secondary air 
supply system, the remaining system will provide sufficient air for control of 
the spring brake release. It is used with the tractor hand control valve to 
allow either foot control valve control or tractor control valve application 
of the trailer brakes. 

The double check valve operates as follows: air under pressure enters 
either of the double check valve inlet ports. The moving shuttle is pushed 
away from a higher pressure inlet port to seal a lower pressure inlet port. 
The airflow continues out the delivery port of the double check valve. The 
position of the shuttle will reverse if the pressure levels are reversed.

Section 06-05A: Brake, Air, Parking/Emergency System

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Low-Pressure Indicator Switch 

The low air pressure switch is a safety device designed to give an 
automatic warning to the driver whenever air pressure in the air brake system 
is below 414 kPa (60 psi), the safe minimum for normal vehicle operation. It 
is used to operate an electrical buzzer and warning lamp, which are audible 
and visible to the driver. The low air pressure switch is located on the 
parking brake control valve. 

The low air pressure switch is also used in the primary and secondary 
air supply lines. 

The low air pressure switch is designed so that the electrical contacts 
remain closed by the spring force until the air brake system pressure is above 
the spring set point (force). The setting and piece number are marked on a 
label on the low air pressure switch body. If a label is not present, the 
vehicle manual should be consulted for the proper setting. The minimum setting 
of the low air pressure switch is 511-593 kPa (74-86 psi). 

The low air pressure switch operates as follows: when air pressure at 
the supply port and under the diaphragm is above 552 kPa (80 psi), the 
electrical contacts remain open because the force exerted by air pressure 
underneath the diaphragm overcomes the force exerted by the spring above the 
diaphragm. 

When air pressure below the diaphragm drops below 552 kPa (80 psi), the 
spring exerts a force that is greater than the force exerted by the air 
pressure below the diaphragm. This causes a piston to move and allows the 
electrical contacts to close. When the ignition switch is on, this closes the 
electrical circuit to the warning device, warning the driver of low air 
pressure in the system.

 Low Air Pressure Switch 

[FIGURE: H8324B.gif]

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

 WARNING: BEFORE ATTEMPTING TO WORK ON AN AIR BRAKE SYSTEM, CERTAIN PRECAUTIONS 
SHOULD BE OBSERVED. AIR UNDER COMPRESSION MAY BE COMPARED TO THE ENERGY IN A 
COILED SPRING AND WHEN RELEASED, MAY PRESENT A HAZARD IF NOT PROPERLY 
RECOGNIZED. 

Follow the safety measures listed below.

The wheels of the vehicle should always be blocked by some means other 
than the air brake system so that depletion of air will not permit the vehicle 
to roll.

In draining the system, do not look into the air jets or direct them 
toward a person as dirt or sludge particles may be carried in the air stream. 
Hoses which contain air pressure should not be disconnected under pressure 
since they will whip as air escapes from the line.

Follow the manufacturers' recommended procedures in working on any air 
device so as to avoid injury or damage from parts which, when released, are 
subject to mechanical (spring) or pneumatic propulsion.

As system pressure is drained and the emergency brakes applied, hands 
should be away from brake air chamber push rods and slack adjusters which will 
apply automatically with the loss of pressure. This also applies when checking 
a service brake system.

Reservoirs that are closest to the source of compressed air (compressor 
or auxiliary source) should contain a safety valve in known working order and 
sufficient capacity to limit the reservoir pressure to a safe maximum level.

Old, used reservoirs should not be used as replacements. The safety 
valves should not be reset higher than specified by the reservoir 
manufacturer, vehicle manufacturer, or code to which the reservoir had been 
manufactured.

Brake air chambers contain large internal steel springs that require 
special disassembly procedures. Note and be guided by the warning tags on such 
units.

Action

Braking Is Uneven. Vehicle Pulls to One Side

 NOTE: Brake-pull evaluation should be conducted on a smooth, level surface.

Low tire pressure or worn tires.

INFLATE tires to recommended pressure. REPLACE worn tires. REFER to 
 Section 04-04 .

Improperly adjusted brakes.

 NOTE: VERIFY that the air chamber push rod clevis position is to
