PAGE 4913
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 06-08D: Brake, Air, Cam-Type

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Manual Adjustment

Rotate the slack adjuster hex extension clockwise until the brake shoe 
and lining contacts the brake drum.

Back off the slack adjuster by rotating the hex extension 1/2 turn 
counterclockwise. A loud clicking will be heard during counterclockwise 
rotation.

[FIGURE: DH0175A.gif]

With the brakes released, measure and record the distance from the face 
of the brake air chamber to the center of the large clevis pin. Distance "A."

Have an assistant make and hold a 586 kPa (85 psi) brake application. 
Allow the air chamber push rod its full travel.

Make and record the same measurement as in Step 3. Distance "B." The 
difference between "A" and "B" is the air chamber stroke.

The air chamber stroke must be within the DOT Adjusted Air Chamber 
Stroke specifications.

 DOT ADJUSTED AIR CHAMBER STROKE LIMITS

550-620 kPa (80-90 psi) Pressure in Air Chamber

 Clamp Type Air Chamber

Chamber Type (Size)

Adjust the stroke as short as possible without the brakes dragging. The
vehicle may be put out of service if the stroke is not:

9

less than 34.9 mm (1-3/8 inches)

12

less than 34.9 mm (1-3/8 inches)

16

less than 44.4 mm (1-3/4 inches)

20

less than 44.4 mm (1-3/4 inches)

24

less than 44.4 mm (1-3/4 inches)

24 long stroke

less than 50.8 mm (2 inches)

30

less than 50.8 mm (2 inches)

36

less than 57.1 mm (2-1/4 inches)

If the air chamber stroke is not within specifications, inspect the 
foundation brake system to locate loose, broken, worn, missing or improperly 
installed parts. Service or replace as necessary.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake, Air Chamber, Maxi-Brake II

 WARNING: BEFORE ATTEMPTING DISASSEMBLY, MAKE SURE THE SPRING IS MECHANICALLY 
CAGED. REMOVE THE PLUG AND INSTALL THE EXTERNALLY STORED T-BOLT. TURN THE 
T-BOLT 90 DEGREES CLOCKWISE UNTIL IT CONTACTS THE INTERNAL STOP. INSTALL THE 
T-BOLT RELEASE NUT AND HAND-TIGHTEN THE NUT OVER THE WASHER. DO NOT USE IMPACT 
WRENCHES AS THEY CAN DAMAGE THE ALUMINUM DIE CASTINGS AND PREVENT PROPER 
CAGING OF THE SPRING. 

The Midland Maxi-Brake II brake air chamber (used on the rear axles 
only) is much like a conventional brake air chamber. It consists of an 
emergency chamber, a service chamber and a bulkhead assembly. 

The service chamber applies the brake by air pressure and releases it 
by spring pressure when air pressure in the service brake chamber is released. 
The emergency brake in the end cap is applied by spring pressure and released 
by air pressure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Brake Air Chamber 

 Removal 

Chock the wheels to prevent vehicle movement.

 CAUTION: To avoid damage to the brake air chamber aluminum housing, do not use 
impact tools to tighten the T-bolt nut. Turn down the T-bolt nut and tighten 
it against the washer. 

Cage the main spring with the following procedure:

Remove the T-bolt from its storage position on the brake air chamber 
housing.

Pull the weather seal plug from the end of the brake air chamber.

Insert and turn the T-bolt until the T head locks in the internal slot.

Release all air pressure from the system.

Disconnect the clevis from the slack adjuster. Discard the cotter pins.

Disconnect the air lines from the brake air chamber.

Remove the brake air chamber mounting nuts and remove the brake air 
chamber from the vehicle.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: To avoid cutting the push rod too short, make sure that the main spring 
is fully caged before cutting the push rod. If installing a new air chamber, 
cut the new push rod to the same length as the old one. 

Install the brake air chamber on the mounting bracket. Tighten the 
mounting nuts to 136-197 Nm (100-145 lb-ft).

 Disassembly 

 WARNING: BEFORE ATTEMPTING DISASSEMBLY, MAKE SURE THE SPRING IS MECHANICALLY 
CAGED. REMOVE THE PLUG AND INSTALL THE EXTERNALLY STORED T-BOLT. TURN THE 
T-BOLT 90 DEGREES CLOCKWISE UNTIL IT CONTACTS THE INTERNAL STOP. INSTALL THE 
T-BOLT RELEASE NUT AND HAND-TIGHTEN THE NUT OVER THE WASHER. DO NOT USE IMPACT 
WRENCHES AS THEY CAN DAMAGE THE ALUMINUM DIE CASTINGS AND PREVENT PROPER 
CAGING OF THE SPRING. 

Scribe a mark on the non-pressure housing and bulkhead and across the 
clamp band for alignment purposes during assembly.

[FIGURE: H3774C.gif]

Remove the non-pressure housing clamp band nuts and bolts. Separate the 
clamp band halves by prying the bands off with a screwdriver. 

Remove the clevis, if still installed. 

Remove the non-pressure housing from the bulkhead. Place the housing 
down on a bench and push down on the housing. Remove the jam nut from the push 
rod and slowly allow the return spring to push up the non-pressure housing. 
Remove the return spring and push rod.

[FIGURE: H37751A.gif]

Remove the diaphragm from the bulkhead.

[FIGURE: H3776B.gif]

Inspect all components for rust and wear. If the spring shows signs of 
rust, clean with a wire brush and coat with a rust inhibitor. Replace any worn 
or damaged parts. 

 Assembly 

 WARNING: TO MAINTAIN EVEN BRAKING, DIAPHRAGMS AND SPRINGS MUST BE REPLACED IN 
AXLE SETS. 

Install a new diaphragm in the bulkhead. 

Position the push rod and return spring in the non-pressure housing. 
Push down on the housing and install the jam nut. Run the jam nut down as far 
as it will go on the push rod to make sure the return spring is properly 
seated. This will prevent return spring force from pushing apart the bulkhead 
and non-pressure housing while installing the clamp bands. A spacer may be 
used between the jam nut and non-pressure housing if necessary.

[FIGURE: H37771A.gif]

Place the assembly on the bulkhead and align the scribe marks made at 
disassembly. Install the clamp bands in alignment with the scribe marks. 
Install nuts and bolts and tighten to 22-26 Nm (16-19 lb-ft). 
Make sure the clamp bands are evenly spaced.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Emergency Chamber

 WARNING: TO MAINTAIN EVEN BRAKING, DIAPHRAGMS AND SPRINGS MUST BE REPLACED IN 
AXLE SETS. 

 Disassembly 

 WARNING: BEFORE ATTEMPTING DISASSEMBLY, MAKE SURE THE SPRING IS MECHANICALLY 
CAGED. REMOVE THE PLUG AND INSTALL THE EXTERNALLY STORED T-BOLT. TURN THE 
T-BOLT 90 DEGREES CLOCKWISE UNTIL IT CONTACTS THE INTERNAL STOP. INSTALL THE 
T-BOLT RELEASE NUT AND HAND-TIGHTEN THE NUT OVER THE WASHER. DO NOT USE IMPACT 
WRENCHES AS THEY CAN DAMAGE THE ALUMINUM DIE CASTINGS AND PREVENT PROPER 
CAGING OF THE SPRING. 

Scribe a mark on the emergency chamber and bulkhead and across the 
clamp band for alignment purposes during assembly. 

[FIGURE: H3778B.gif]

Carefully remove the nuts, bolts and band clamps. Slide the end cap 
sideways on the bulkhead and remove the end cap.

[FIGURE: H3779B.gif]

Remove the diaphragm from the end cap. 

Place the end cap in a press capable of at least 1134 kg (2500 lbs.) 
pressure. The press should have an opening at its base allowing operator 
access to the T-bolt while under pressure.

Bring the press down firmly (not to exceed 11120-11564 Nm
 [2500-2600 lb-ft] pressure). This will 
allow access to remove the nut on the T-bolt far enough to allow pushing the 
T-bolt inward until a quarter turn counterclockwise can be made and the T-bolt 
removed.

[FIGURE: H3780B.gif]

Slowly release the press, allowing the main spring to expand and spring 
support to rise. Remove the main spring and spring support. If the main spring 
shows signs of rust or corrosion, clean with a wire brush and coat with a rust 
inhibitor.

[FIGURE: H3781B.gif]

 Assembly 

Place the main spring and spring support into the end cap, making sure 
the main spring and spring support are properly seated.

[FIGURE: H3782B.gif]

Place the assembly in a suitable press and bring the press down to 
compress the main spring and spring support into the end cap. Insert T-bolt 
and give a quarter turn clockwise and hand tighten T-bolt nut to cage the main 
spring. 

Remove the assembly from the press and install diaphragm in end cap. 

Place the end cap over the bulkhead. 

Align bulkhead, end cap and band clamp with the scribe marks made at 
disassembly. Install nuts and bolts on each side of the band clamps and 
tighten evenly to 22-26 Nm (16-19 lb-ft).

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Bulkhead 

 Disassembly 

Remove the service brake diaphragm and emergency chamber. Refer to Service Brake Diaphragm 
 and refer 
to Emergency Chamber in the Disassembly and 
Assembly portion of this section. 

Turn the bulkhead assembly so that the main spring side faces downward. 
Push down on the assembly and compress the push rod return spring. This will 
force the adapter rod upward from the bulkhead.

[FIGURE: H37831A.gif]

Grasp the adapter rod with a pair of pliers or locking pliers (with a 
protective surface to avoid scratching the adapter rod surface). Remove the 
lower adapter plate screw.

[FIGURE: H37841A.gif]

While maintaining pressure on the bulkhead, release the pliers or 
locking pliers and slowly let the adapter rise. Pull out the adapter rod and 
return spring guide. The return spring and lower adapter plate will fall away. 
Inspect the return spring and adapter rod for wear or corrosion. If they show 
signs of rust or corrosion, clean with a wire brush and coat with a rust 
inhibitor. If the adapter rod is worn or damaged, it should be replaced.

[FIGURE: H37851A.gif]

To replace the O-ring in the bulkhead, it must be picked out with a 
sharp instrument. Replace with a new O-ring coated with Motorcraft Premium 
Long Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B. The nylon bushing is not replaceable. If bushing has been 
damaged, a new bulkhead must be installed.

[FIGURE: H37861A.gif]

 Assembly 

Place the push rod return spring into position on the main spring side 
of the bulkhead. 

Push the adapter rod through the center boss of the bulkhead and turn 
the unit over with the bulkhead facing downward on the bench. 

Clamp the adapter rod with protected locking pliers or pliers to avoid 
surface damage to the rod. Reinstall the lower adapter plate with a new screw. 
Coat the screw with Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSK-M2G349-A1 and tighten to 4.5-5.5 Nm 
(40-49 lb-in). Install a new locking pellet above the screw. 

While maintaining downward pressure on the bulkhead, remove the locking 
pliers or pliers from the adapter rod and allow the bulkhead to rise. This 
will complete the reassembly of the bulkhead. 

Install the service and emergency chambers, making sure the bulkhead, 
service and emergency chambers and clamp bands are all aligned with the scribe 
marks made at disassembly.

Section 06-08F: Brake, Air Chamber, MGM

1997 L-Series Equipped with Cam-Type Air Brakes Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake Assembly 

The MGM double diaphragm brake air chamber assembly, used on rear wheel 
brakes, contains a spring applied parking brake which acts as an emergency 
brake in case of air pressure loss. This assembly is used with S-cam brakes 
only. 

The brake air chamber assembly consists of two separate air chambers, 
each having its own application and release mechanism. The only difference 
between the two chambers is that the service chamber applies the brake by air 
pressure and releases it by spring pressure; the spring brake chamber applies 
the brake by spring pressure and releases it by air pressure. 

During normal driving (brakes released), the service brakes are held in 
the released position by the diaphragm return spring in the service air 
chamber assembly. Air reservoir pressure against the spring brake chamber 
piston and diaphragm keeps the parking-emergency spring compressed.

 Normal Driving 

[FIGURE: H9915A.gif]

During normal braking (service brakes applied) air pressure from the 
brake valve working against the service brake diaphragm applies the brakes. 
Air reservoir pressure in the spring brake chamber keeps the parking-emergency 
spring compressed. Normal service brake operation is not affected by the 
spring brake. 

 Normal Service Brakes 

[FIGURE: H9916A.gif]

During parking or an emergency brake application, air is exhausted from 
the spring brake chamber permitting the parking-emergency spring to expand, 
moving the spring brake piston and the service brake push rod against the 
slack adjuster assembly to apply the brakes. 

 Parking Brake 

[FIGURE: H9917A.gif]

Loss of air pressure at the spring brake chamber will result in 
automatic application of the brakes. If it is necessary to move the vehicle 
before air pressure can be restored, the parking-emergency spring must be 
manually compressed. The procedure for manually releasing and then resetting 
the spring brake after service has been performed is described below. Do not 
drive vehicle until the air system is serviced.

 Manual Release 

[FIGURE: H9918A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Chamber, Complete Unit 

 Removal 

Place chocks under the wheels to prevent the vehicle from moving. 

Manually cage the spring brake as described in Manual 
Release in the Adjustments portion of this section. 

Loosen the jam nut above the clevis. 

After releasing system air pressure, disconnect the air lines and the 
clevis pins. Discard the cotter pins.

Remove the mounting stud nuts and remove the unit from the mounting 
bracket. 

 Installation 

If a new unit is being installed, make sure the push rod and the clevis 
are the correct length and all ports are aligned with the air lines. New units 
are equipped with a 203 mm (8-inch) push rod. Cut the push rod the same length 
as the old unit. When cutting the piston rod, the spring brake must be fully 
compressed (release bolt fully extended) as described in Manual 
Release in the Adjustments portion of this section.

[FIGURE: H4038D.gif]

If necessary, remove the clevis/snap nut assembly and the jam nut from 
the old air chamber and install them on the new unit. Tighten jam nut to 45-67 Nm
 (33-50 lb-ft). 

 NOTE: When installing brake air chambers to brake assemblies, chambers must 
be placed to top of slots in brake assembly bracket in normal vehicle position.

Install the unit in position on the bracket. Make sure the washers are 
on the outside of the bracket and not against the service chamber housing. 
Install the nuts and tighten to 136-196 Nm (100-145 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Service Diaphragm or Service Chamber 

 Removal 

Chock the wheels to prevent vehicle movement.

Manually cage the spring brake. Refer to Manual Release in the 
Adjustments portion of this section.

 CAUTION: Pad the jaws of the locking pliers to prevent push rod damage. 

Extend the service brake push rod by applying the brake pedal or by 
pushing the slack adjuster. Clamp and hold the push rod with locking pliers.

Release system air pressure.

Disconnect the clevis from the slack adjuster. Discard the cotter pins.

[FIGURE: H4042C.gif]

Disconnect the air lines from the brake air chamber.

Remove the air chamber-to-air chamber bracket nuts and remove the air 
chamber from the vehicle.

Pull the one end of the breather tube out of the rubber elbow.

Make a mark across the two chamber assemblies and the clamp ring to aid 
reassembly alignment.

Remove the two clamp ring nuts and bolts. Remove the clamp ring.

Separate the non-pressure housing from the spring brake chamber assembly.

Remove the service brake diaphragm from the spring brake chamber 
assembly.

Inspect all components for cracks, corrosion or other damage. Replace 
as necessary. 

 Installation 

 WARNING: TO INCREASE BRAKING BALANCE, AIR CHAMBER DIAPHRAGMS AND SPRINGS MUST BE 
REPLACED IN AXLE SETS ONLY. 

Install the new diaphragm into the spring brake chamber assembly.

 NOTE: To help seat the clamp ring, tap around the ring with a hammer. 

Using the alignment marks made at disassembly, position the spring 
brake chamber and clamp ring on the non-pressure housing. Install the clamp 
ring bolts and nuts. Tighten the clamp ring nuts to 41-47 Nm 
(30-35 lb-ft).

Insert the breather tube into the rubber elbow.

Position the air chamber on the air chamber bracket and install the air 
chamber-to-air chamber bracket washers and nuts. Tighten the nuts to 136-196 Nm
 (100-145 lb-ft).

Apply Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A on the 
air line fittings. Install the fittings and tighten to 33 Nm 
(24 lb-ft) maximum. Position the fittings by turning in the tightening 
direction only.

Using new cotter pins, attach the clevis to the slack adjuster. 

Remove the locking pliers from the push rod.

Build up air system pressure and test for leaks.

With air system at normal pressure, uncage the spring brake. Remove and 
store the T-bolt and nut.

Press the weather seal into the hole in the spring brake chamber.

Adjust the brakes. Refer to Section 06-08D .

ADJUSTMENTS

Manual Release 

Place chocks under the wheels to keep the vehicle from moving. 

Remove the weatherseal plug. 

Remove the T-head bolt from the air chamber storage slot.

Insert the T-bolt through the opening in the spring brake chamber and 
engage the T-head in the slot in the piston. Turn the bolt 90 degrees 
clockwise until it stops and locks. 

Pull the T-bolt out as far as possible by hand and install the washer 
and nut. 

 CAUTION: Do not tighten the T-bolt nut over 67 Nm (50 lb-ft). 

 NOTE: Caging of the spring brake is easier with the air system at normal 
pressure.

With a 3/4-inch wrench, turn the T-bolt nut clockwise until the spring 
brake is caged. If T-bolt binds, apply Rust Penetrant and Inhibitor 
F2AZ-19501-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C56-A and allow 
it to soak into threads.

[FIGURE: H4037B.gif]

When the spring has been fully caged, the release bolt will extend 76 
mm (3.0 inch) for Model 30 and 114 mm (4.5 inch) for Model 36 (heavy-duty) air 
chambers.

Section 06-09: Brake System, Anti-Lock, Front and Rear

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Description 

The anti-lock brake system (ABS) is used on L-Series tractors with air 
brake systems. ABS provides precise axle braking control during aggressive 
braking and prevents wheel lockup. On vehicles equipped with ABS, steering 
control, stability and safety are maintained when the brakes are applied. In 
addition, the stopping distance can be reduced.

The particular system covered in this section is called the full 
vehicle ABS system, or two-channel system. The full vehicle ABS system 
provides ABS braking on the front and rear axles.

The major components of a two-channel (full vehicle ABS) system are a 
control module, two front wheel speed sensors, two drive axle wheel speed 
sensors, a rear modulator/relay valve and a front modulator valve. 

[FIGURE: H9484C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

2C204

Front Wheel ABS Speed Sensors

2

4B409

Rear Wheel ABS Speed Sensor

3

— 

Rear Modulator/Relay Valve (Part of 2C219)

4

2C219

ABS Module Assy

5

2B273

ABS Modulator Valve

The control module is the computer or "brain" controlling the ABS 
system. It is an electronic device that receives electrical input signals from 
several anti-lock system components. Based on these signals, the control 
module is programmed to send output signals to control other ABS components 
during aggressive braking. The control module has a diagnostics window that 
helps to troubleshoot the system. The ABS system uses an MC-14 control module. 

[FIGURE: H9485B.gif]

Wheel speed sensors send wheel speed signals to the control module. ABS 
systems have four wheel speed sensors: two for the front axle and two for the 
drive axle. 

[FIGURE: H9486B.gif]

The rear axle brakes on the ABS system are controlled by the M-12 rear 
modulator/relay valve. Inside the rear modulator/relay valve there are two 
solenoids. These solenoids are controlled by the control module.

[FIGURE: H9487B.gif]

The control module is mounted on top of the M-12 rear modulator/relay 
valve.

[FIGURE: H9488E.gif]

The front modulator is designed to prevent lockup of the brakes on the 
front axle. This modulator is called the M-21. Like the rear modulator, it has 
two solenoids which are controlled by the MC-14 control module.

[FIGURE: H9489B.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Inputs/Outputs

All components in the ABS system either send or receive a signal from 
the control module. Components that send signals to the control module are 
module inputs and components that receive signals are module outputs.

 ABS Component Layout 

[FIGURE: H8786C.gif]

[FIGURE: H8787A.gif]

 Module Inputs 

Module inputs are the components of an anti-lock brake system that send 
signals to the control module. Wheel speed sensors are an example of 
components that provide input signals. In addition to wheel speed sensors, ABS 
inputs to the control module include electrical power and the stoplight switch.

 Electrical Power 

Vehicle power is continually input to the control module from the 
ignition switch through a fuse or circuit breaker. The electrical ground for 
the control module is the vehicle chassis.

 Stoplight Switch 

The stoplight switch sends a 12-volt signal to the MC-14 that indicates 
that the brakes have been applied. If the signal is not available, the MC-14 
will still function. 

 Module Outputs 

Module outputs are the components of an anti-lock brake system that 
receive signals from the control module. Modulators are an example of an 
output component. In addition to modulators, ABS output signals from the 
control module include the anti-lock warning light and LEDs (diagnostic window).

 Anti-Lock Warning Light 

The main components in the anti-lock warning light electrical circuit 
consist of:

dash-mounted amber ABS warning light

ABS warning light relay

control module

The amber ABS warning light is located in the instrument cluster. When 
the key is turned to RUN, the amber light blinks twice and stays on as the 
control module performs a self test.

If the amber light does not blink it means that a fault has been 
detected. The self test is completed when vehicle speed exceeds 16 km/h (10 
mph) and the light goes out. To eliminate false anti-lock, the control module 
will shut down and turn on the amber light if it sees too much variation in 
wheel speed sensor signals after 15 seconds (front to rear or left to right). 
This condition could be caused by towing, dynamometer or accelerating on an 
icy surface. If this occurs, the vehicle must slow down or stop and then 
accelerate normally. When the control module receives uniform wheel speed 
signals, the anti-lock function will be reactivated and the amber light will 
be turned off.

The ABS warning light relay is located near the circuit breaker panel. 
Voltage is supplied to the relay through the fuse and ignition switch.

When the key is turned to RUN, current flows through the relay and ABS 
warning light.

To turn the ABS warning light off, the control module grounds the relay 
coil. This allows current to flow through the relay coil winding and creates a 
magnetic field. The magnetic field around the coil opens the relay contacts 
and turns the amber warning light off.

 LEDs, Diagnostic Window 

A self test is performed each time the key is turned to RUN. The 
flashing amber warning light indicates that the self test is in progress. 
During this time the control module sends out an electrical signal to each of 
the windings in the wheel speed sensors and modulator valves and brake switch. 
Excessive electrical resistance, opens, shorts or grounds in any of these 
circuits (including the wiring harness) will affect the self test signal and 
turn on a combination of LED (light emitting diode) lights on the control 
module.

If any single ABS component fails, the dash-mounted anti-lock warning 
light will illuminate. A troubleshooting LED on the control module will also 
light. Depending on the type of failure and where it occurs, the control 
module will continue anti-lock function, but at a lower performance level, or 
it will disable all or some of the anti-lock functions on the vehicle. When 
the anti-lock function is disabled, the affected axle(s) will revert to 
standard air braking.

If a single speed sensor fails on one axle, the system will not be 
disabled. The remaining sensor will be used to continue anti-lock operation, 
but with slightly less efficiency.

The ABS will try to provide the vehicle with the best possible braking 
and stability, even after a failure has occurred. Standard air braking will 
still be available on those brakes where the anti-lock has been disabled.

The ABS system will completely shut down if:

electrical power is below or above the 10 to 17 volt operating range.

a control module failure is detected.

two or more failures are detected, regardless of where the problem 
exists, or the modulator fails.

If a failure is detected on the front modulator, only the front ABS 
will be disabled.

When servicing an ABS system, observe the following precautions:

It is generally advisable to replace a wire harness rather than repair 
individual wires in the harness. If a splice repair must be made, it is 
important that the splice be properly soldered with a rosin flux (not acid 
based) and made waterproof. 

Do not pierce wire insulation when checking for continuity. Check for 
power, ground or continuity by disconnecting the connector and testing the 
individual pins or sockets in the connector(s). 

Always check the Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual City Delivery

or Fleet & Full 
for wiring and connector identification. 

While the retarder disable and serial link connections (three total) 
are present on all control modules, they are not always used.

Section 06-09: Brake System, Anti-Lock, Front and Rear

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Operation

The wheel speed sensors send signals to the control module. These 
signals tell the control module how fast each wheel is rotating. When the 
driver applies the brakes, the control module uses these signals to detect if 
one or more wheels on the front or rear axle is about to lock up. The control 
module signals the front and rear modulators to adjust air pressure to the 
service brakes to control wheel lockup. The control module and modulator are 
able to apply and exhaust air the same way as if the driver was pumping the 
brakes.

 Rear Brake Application 

The rear brakes on the ABS system are controlled by the control module 
and the M-12 rear modulator/relay valve. The M-12 rear modulator/relay valve 
delivers equal brake application pressure to the service chambers on the rear 
axles during normal braking. Two wheel speed sensors in the rear axle send 
changes in wheel acceleration and deceleration to the control module. Based on 
this information, the control module activates two solenoids in the M-12 rear 
modulator/relay valve. When the solenoids are activated air is exhausted from 
the service brakes to prevent wheel lockup.

 Front Brake Application 

The front axle (steering axle) brakes are controlled by the control 
module and the M-21 front modulator. During normal braking when the brakes are 
applied, air passes through the M-21 front modulator to the front axle service 
chambers. Two wheel speed sensors on the front axle send changes in wheel 
acceleration and deceleration to the control module. When ABS braking is 
required, the control module activates the M-21 front modulator solenoids to 
control the air pressure to the front service brakes.

 Control Module, Anti-Lock Brake 

Wheel speed information is provided to the control module (MC-14) by a 
wiring harness from individual wheel speed sensors. The control module 
receives and interprets all speed signals at the same time. During aggressive 
braking, the control module uses the modulator to regulate air pressure to the 
service brakes based on information from the wheel speed sensors. The brake 
switch also provides braking information.

The MC-14 control modules has self-test capabilities and a diagnostic 
display window for troubleshooting.

The MC-14 self test and diagnostic circuitry continuously checks for 
proper operation of the entire anti-lock system. If a circuit or component 
problem is detected, one or more LEDs (light emitting diodes) in the 
diagnostic window will be turned on along with the dash-mounted warning light.

 Multiple Faults 

The LEDs will only show one fault at a time. After correcting the first 
fault (and clearing the first fault code with the RESET function) the second 
fault will be displayed. Intermittent faults, however, must be recreated in 
order to reactivate second fault display.

 MC-14 Control Module 

The MC-14 has a 30-pin connector. It monitors the speeds of four wheels 
and controls the braking on two axles.

The MC-14 has the following nine LEDs:

FRONT (front component)

MID (middle) (see following note)

REAR (rear component)

RIGHT (right component)

LEFT (left component)

MOD (modulator)

SENS (wheel speed sensor)

ECU (control module)

VOLT (voltage to control module)

 NOTE: The MID LED is not used in the diagnostic process for the MC-14. It 
will, however, light when a magnet is placed on the RESET switch in the 
diagnostic window.

[FIGURE: H8790B.gif]

 M-12 Rear Modulator/Relay Valve 

The purpose of the M-12 rear modulator/relay valve is to modify driver 
applied air pressure to the service brakes. It is a combination valve that has 
two components: a standard relay valve and solenoids (inlet and exhaust) which 
rapidly apply and exhaust air during an ABS stop. It is located between the 
brake pedal and the rear brake air chambers. It replaces the standard drive 
axle relay valve used to speed up the application and release of the rear axle 
brakes. The M-12 has the following three air connections:

SUP — supply air from the reservoir

DEL — delivery to the rear brake actuators

CON — air pressure from the brake valve

 NOTE: Do not remove or tamper with plugged port on solenoid body. It will 
disable the anti-lock system.

[FIGURE: H8788C.gif]

 M-21 Front Modulator Valve 

The M-21 is a high capacity, on/off air valve that has two electrical 
solenoids that are controlled by the MC-14. The M-21 has one exhaust and one 
supply solenoid. Each solenoid winding has between 3.5 and 5 ohms of 
resistance. The solenoids are connected to the MC-14 by a three-wire 
connector. One wire supplies source voltage (+) to both 
windings. The remaining two wires are used by the MC-14 to control the supply 
and exhaust solenoids. The M-21 has the following three air connections:

SUP — air pressure from the brake valve

DEL — delivery to the front brake actuators

EXH — air exhaust during anti-lock control

[FIGURE: H8789C.gif]

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Brake System, Anti-Lock

 Inspection and Verification 

 General 

While the diagnostic display locates a specific area, it is still 
necessary to confirm whether the concern resides in the component itself or 
the wiring. Basically, the troubleshooting procedure that follows is devoted 
to narrowing the problem to either the wiring or a specific anti-lock 
component. It should be noted however that all troubleshooting begins by 
observing the anti-lock warning light on the dash. All troubleshooting should 
begin by first performing Pinpoint Test A: Dash Warning Light Comes 
On and following the directions contained in it. 

To assist the troubleshooting technician in keeping track of the 
procedure and also to provide a record of the service performed, use a 
troubleshooting record sheet. Refer to Troubleshooting Tips in the Diagnosis 
and Testing portion of this section.

 Troubleshooting Tips 

No voltage or resistance tests are performed at the control module. All 
voltage and resistance tests are performed by beginning at the wire harness 
half of the connector and moving away from the control module toward an 
anti-lock system component (modulator, wheel speed sensor, etc.). 

Record all findings and the action taken while troubleshooting on a 
troubleshooting record sheet. The troubleshooting sheet should be filed in the 
vehicle maintenance folder for future reference and comparison. 

 Troubleshooting Record Sheet 

[FIGURE: CH8792A.gif]

 Safety 

 WARNING: WHERE CIRCUMSTANCES REQUIRE THAT THE ENGINE BE IN OPERATION, EXTREME 
CAUTION SHOULD BE USED TO PREVENT PERSONAL INJURY RESULTING FROM CONTACT WITH 
MOVING, ROTATING, LEAKING, HEATED, OR ELECTRICALLY CHARGED COMPONENTS. 

When working in the engine compartment, the engine should be shut off.

Park the vehicle on a level surface. Apply the parking brakes, then 
chock the wheels. Stop the engine when working around the vehicle. 

Exhaust the air pressure from all reservoirs before beginning any work 
on the vehicle. 

Never connect or disconnect a hose or line containing pressure; it may 
whip. Never remove a component or plug unless you are certain all system 
pressure has been exhausted.

Never exceed recommended pressures and always wear safety glasses. 

Do not attempt to install, remove, disassemble or assemble a component 
until you have read and thoroughly understand the recommended procedures. Use 
only the proper tools and observe all precautions pertaining to use of those 
tools. 

Replacement hardware, tubing, hose fittings, etc., should be of 
equivalent size, type and strength as original equipment and be designed 
specifically for such applications and systems. 

Components with stripped threads or damaged parts should be replaced 
rather than serviced. Service requiring machining or welding should not be 
attempted. 

Prior to returning the vehicle to service, make sure all components and 
systems are restored to their proper operating condition. Repeat initial 
check-out procedure. 

 Pin Tests 

When performing checks at the control module connector pins, be careful 
not to damage the pins. Also, check the pins for corrosion and damage. Make 
sure the terminals and pins make good contact.

 Ground Tests 

Make sure all ground connections are tight and that all ground voltage 
measurements are zero volts.

 Resistance Tests 

Make sure the wiring harnesses are tight and in good condition without 
any damaged insulation or frayed wires. Measure resistance or continuity at 
the control module to verify the condition of the wiring harness and component.

[FIGURE: H9501C.gif]

 Component Resistance 

If the resistance or continuity test results are not within 
specifications, measure the resistance of each component at the connector. If 
the resistance is not correct, check the component and service or replace the 
parts as necessary.

[FIGURE: H9502A.gif]

 Checking Continuity, Power and Ground 

When checking for continuity, do not pierce the wire insulation. Check 
for power, ground or continuity by disconnecting the connector and testing the 
individual pins or sockets in the connector(s).

 Retarder Disable and Serial Link Connections 

The retarder disable and serial link connections are on all control 
modules but are not always used.

 Symptom Chart — Two-Channel ABS System

 Pinpoint Tests 

There are nine LEDs plus a magnetically actuated reset switch in the 
control module diagnostic window. The first five LEDs locate a concern to a 
specific area of the vehicle while the last four indicate the component or its 
wiring. The LEDs are controlled by the control module and are either on or off 
depending upon their monitor function. 

 NOTE: Right and left, front and rear are determined from the driver's seat. 
Left front is therefore the corner closest to the driver. 

 NOTE: The MID LED shown in the chart is not used in the diagnostic process 
for the control module. However, it will light when a magnet is placed on the 
RESET switch in the diagnostic window.

 Front LED 

This red LED illuminates and latches on in order to indicate the 
location of a worn or damaged component or its wiring. It will light in 
conjunction with either the RIGHT or LEFT LED and the SENS LED when indicating 
a speed sensor malfunction. The FRONT LED will also light in conjunction with 
the MOD LED to indicate that the front modulator or its wiring has 
malfunctioned. 

 Mid LED 

This red LED is not used in troubleshooting the control module and 
should light only when a magnet is held on the RESET switch. 

 Rear LED 

This red LED illuminates and latches on in order to indicate the 
location of a worn or damaged component or its wiring. It will light in 
conjunction with either the RIGHT or LEFT LED and the SENS LED when indicating 
a speed sensor malfunction. The REAR LED will also light in conjunction with 
the MOD LED to indicate that the rear modulator/controller has malfunctioned. 

 Right LED 

This red LED illuminates and latches on in order to indicate the 
location of a worn or damaged component or its wiring. It will light in 
conjunction with either the FRONT or REAR LED and SENS LED. This LED should 
not light when a MOD LED is on. 

 Left LED 

This red LED illuminates and latches on in order to indicate the 
location of a worn or damaged component or its wiring. It will light in 
conjunction with either the FRONT or REAR LED and SENS LED. This LED should 
not light when a MOD LED is on. 

 Mod LED 

This red LED illuminates and latches on to indicate a permanent or 
intermittent open or short circuit in the solenoids of one of the two 
modulators or the wiring connecting them to the system. The MOD LED will 
illuminate in conjunction with either the FRONT or REAR LED. 

 Sens LED 

This red LED illuminates and latches on to indicate permanent or 
intermittent failure. The failures indicated are open or shorted wheel speed 
sensor, open or shorted wheel speed sensor wiring, wheel speed signal not 
present or not to specification. The SENS LED will illuminate in conjunction 
with either the FRONT or REAR LED and either the RIGHT or LEFT LED. 

 ECU LED 

This red LED, when illuminated, indicates that the control module has 
failed. It is latched on for all control module failures except low voltage. 
For voltages less than 10, the LED illuminates to indicate the controller is 
inoperative. However, when the voltage again exceeds 11 volts the LED will 
turn off automatically. 

 Volt LED 

This green LED illuminates and remains on during vehicle operation to 
indicate that vehicle power is reaching the control module. If vehicle power 
is out of range for proper operation (below 10 or above 17 volts) this LED 
will flash until power is brought into range. The VOLT LED will also flash if 
a marginal low voltage condition existed at the time of an anti-lock event. 

 Reset 

Beneath the RESET area of the window display is a magnetically 
sensitive switch that is used to reset the diagnostic system. The device will 
respond to a magnet which has strength sufficient to lift a 3-ounce weight. 
Holding a magnet against the RESET will cause all LEDs to light during the 
time the mag

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Control Module, Anti-Lock Brake

 Removal 

Make sure all system air pressure has been exhausted. Identify and 
remove all air lines connected to the rear modulator. 

Disconnect the electrical connector from the control module. 

Note and mark the mounting position of the modulator controller 
assembly on the vehicle. Loosen, remove and save the nuts on the mounting 
hardware that attaches the modulator control assembly bracket to the vehicle. 
Remove the modulator controller assembly from the vehicle. 

Remove any contamination from the exterior of the assembly, making sure 
to keep the contamination away from the open ports. 

 NOTE: If a gasket is damaged during removal, replace it with a new gasket.

Note and mark the position of the control module relative to the rear 
modulator. Remove and retain the four hex capscrews that secure the control 
module to the modulator. Carefully separate the control module from the 
modulator enough to expose the wire harness that connects both units 
electrically. Disconnect the wire harness by separating the four-pin connector 
at the control module. Peel the gasket from the modulator and retain for 
reuse. 

 Installation 

After noting the positioning marks made prior to disassembly, reconnect 
the modulator wire harness to the control module. Position the gasket on the 
control module and secure the control module to the modulator using the four 
capscrews. Tighten the capscrews to 6-9 Nm (53-80 lb-in).

Mount the modulator controller assembly on the vehicle and orient it in 
the position marked prior to removal. 

Reconnect all air lines. 

Reconnect the electrical connector to the modulator controller. 

Test the modulator controller assembly for operation and air leakage 
prior to placing the vehicle in service. 

Perform Pinpoint Test A: Dash Warning Light Comes On in the Diagnosis 
and Testing portion of this section. Make sure the anti-lock system is 
operating properly.

Wheel Speed Sensor, Front

 Removal

Remove the sensor from the steering knuckle, using a twisting motion if

Disconnect the sensor cable from the chassis harness.

[FIGURE: H9705A.gif]

 Installation 

Connect the sensor cable to the chassis harness.

Install any fasteners used to hold the sensor cable in place.

 NOTE: Make sure the sensor spring clip is installed with the flange stops on 
the inboard side (vehicle inboard).

Push the sensor spring clip into the bushing in the steering knuckle 
until it stops.

Push the sensor completely into the sensor spring clip until it stops 
against the tooth wheel.

Remove the chocks from the rear tires.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Brake Sensors, Rear

The rear wheel speed sensors are in-axle type sensors. They are mounted 
to the differential bearing adjuster. To service these sensors, the 
differential carrier must be removed. Refer to Section 05-02A for differential 
carrier and wheel speed sensor removal and installation.

To avoid unnecessary service, the sensor operation can be verified with 
an AC voltmeter. Connect the voltmeter leads to each wheel speed sensor pin. 
Rotate the wheel fast enough to get a good signal (one-half revolution per 
second or faster). Sensor output should be 0.25 volt or more.

MAINTENANCE

Preventative Maintenance 

Every three months, 25,000 miles or 900 operating hours, perform the 
following: 

Check all wiring and connectors to make sure they are secure and free 
from visible damage. 

Although the control module incorporates a diagnostic routine, the LED 
display should be inspected to make sure they are functional. With the vehicle 
ignition on, a magnet (800 gauss; capable of picking up 3 ounces) held to the 
diagnostic window reset switch, should cause all of the LEDs to illuminate. If 
one or more of the LEDs does not illuminate and the anti-lock warning light on 
the dash indicates the system is functioning properly, the non-illuminated 
LED(s) should be noted for future reference. Although the diagnostic 
capabilities will be limited, the system will continue to function as 
designed. 

Road test the vehicle by making an anti-lock stop from a vehicle speed 
of 32 km/h (20 mph). When an anti-lock stop is made, the modulator solenoids 
pulsate and an audible burst of air can be heard from outside of the cab. The 
wheels should not enter a prolonged "lock" condition.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Fluid Drain and Refill Procedure

If the fluid is cold, operate the transmission until a normal operating 
temperature of 71°-93°C (160°
-200°F) is reached. 

Disconnect the drain plug from the transmission pan and allow the fluid 
to drain. 

When the fluid has stopped draining, reconnect the drain plug and 
tighten the fitting to 20-27 Nm (15-20 lb-ft). 

Replace fluid filter. Refer to Section 07-02 .

Remove the dipstick and pour approximately 17.5 liters (37 pints) of 
transmission fluid into the transmission through the filler tube. 

With the vehicle standing level, apply the parking brake and place the 
selector lever in N. Operate the engine at idle speed. 

Shift the selector lever through all the range positions to make sure 
that warm fluid is distributed throughout the transmission. Return the 
selector lever to N. 

Check the fluid level on the dipstick. The safe operating level is 
between the two COLD marks on the dipstick. If fluid level is low, add 
sufficient fluid to bring level to the lower of the two COLD marks. If level 
is too high, drain excess fluid to proper level. Fluid temperature should be 
16-49°C (60-120°F) for cold check.

Section 07-01A: Transmission, Automatic, AT-542 and AT-545

1997 LN-7000 Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission 

 Removal 

From inside the vehicle, remove the right and left door sill scuff 
plate screws and remove the plates. Position the floor covering out of the 
way. Remove the bolts securing the transmission access cover to the floor pan 
and remove the cover. 

On a one-piece driveshaft, disconnect the shaft from the yoke at the 
transmission. On a two-piece driveshaft, disconnect the coupling shaft from 
the yoke at the transmission, and remove the center support bearing bracket. 
Move the forward end of the driveshaft, or coupling shaft, out of the way. 
Refer to Section 05-01 .

Place a drain pan under the transmission. Disconnect the drain plug 
from the transmission pan and allow the fluid to drain. 

Disconnect the fluid filler tube. 

Disconnect the speedometer sensor from the rear of the transmission. 

Disconnect the fluid cooler lines at the transmission. 

Remove the modulator retainer bolt and remove the retainer. Remove the 
modulator and valve actuating rod from the case. 

Disconnect the shift cable from the control arm at the transmission.

Remove the two bolts securing the shift cable bracket to the 
transmission and position the cable and bracket out of the way. 

Remove the cover from front face of flywheel housing. 

Remove six adapter ring-to-flexplate retaining bolts. If required, turn 
the crankshaft manually. 

Remove four upper and two lower converter housing-to-flywheel housing 
retaining bolts. 

Remove the bolts and nuts securing the two rear engine supports to the 
crossmember. Remove the lower insulators and flatwashers. 

Loosen the front engine support bolts. 

Position a transmission jack such as Rotunda Truck Transmission Jack 
164-R3510 or equivalent under the transmission and secure the transmission to 
the jack with a safety chain. 

Place a jack under the engine, then raise both jacks to take the weight 
off the crossmember. 

Remove the two upper engine rear support insulators from the 
crossmember. 

Remove the bolts securing the engine rear support brackets to the 
transmission and remove the brackets, if so equipped. 

With both jacks supporting the engine and transmission, remove the 
remaining converter housing-to-flywheel housing retaining bolts. 

Pull the transmission rearward until the converter housing contacts the 
body sheet metal. Then tilt the rear of the transmission up until the bottom 
of the converter housing clears the crossmember. Lower the assembly and remove 
it from under the vehicle. If necessary, raise the rear of the truck to permit 
the transmission to clear the frame. 

 Transmission Installation, FD-1060 Engine with AT-545 and AT-542

 Installation 

 NOTE: Prior to installing the transmission, the flexplate must be checked for 
runout. The maximum TIR (total indicated runout) should be 0.762 mm (0.030 
inch). Also, flywheel housing transmission mounting face alignment inspection 
should be made of the engine flywheel housing transmission surface. The face 
and bore runout should not exceed 0.203 mm (0.008 inch) TIR. 

Position the torque converter to the transmission, engaging the turbine 
shaft with the converter turbine, the stator shaft with the stator, and the 
hub with the oil pump drive gear. 

With the converter properly installed, place the transmission on a jack 
such as Rotunda Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510. Secure the transmission to 
the jack with a safety chain. 

Raise the converter and transmission on the jack, then move the 
assembly into position over the crossmember. Align the holes in the converter 
with the holes in the flywheel. 

Install 12 converter housing-to-flywheel housing retaining bolts. 
Tighten the bolts to 49-57 Nm (36-42 lb-ft). 

Lower the engine jack and remove it from under the vehicle. 

Position the engine rear support brackets to the sides of the 
transmission and secure with the retaining bolts. 

Position the two upper engine rear support insulators on the 
crossmember. Position the lower insulators and flatwashers to the crossmember 
and install the rear support-to-crossmember bolts and nuts. Tighten the bolts 
to 102-142 Nm (75-105 lb-ft). 

Lower the transmission jack and remove it from under the vehicle. 

Install the four upper and two lower converter housing-to-flywheel 
housing retaining bolts. 

Tighten the front engine support-to-crossmember bolts to 102-142 Nm
 (75-105 lb-ft). 

Install the six adapter ring-to-flexplate retaining bolts. Tighten the 
bolts to 47-54 Nm (35-40 lb-ft). If required, turn the 
crankshaft manually. 

Install the cover to the front face of the flywheel housing. 

Position the shift cable bracket to the transmission and install the 
retaining bolts. 

Connect the shift cable to the manual lever at the transmission. 

Install the modulator actuating rod and modulator into the case. 
Install the modulator retainer and secure with the retaining bolt. Tighten the 
bolt to 16-23 Nm (12-17 lb-ft). 

Connect the fluid cooler lines to the transmission case. 

Connect the speedometer sensor. 

Connect the fluid filler tube to the transmission pan. Tighten the nut 
to 95-108 Nm (70-80 lb-ft). 

Install the driveshaft, or the center support bearing bracket and the 
coupling shaft, if so equipped. Connect the driveshaft or coupling shaft to 
the yoke. Tighten all bolts and nuts to specification. Refer to Section 05-01 . 

Position the transmission access covers to the floorpan and secure with 
the retaining bolts. Reposition the floor covering. Install the door sill 
scuff plates and secure with the retaining screws. 

Fill transmission. Refer to Transmission Fluid Drain and Refill 
Procedure in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Replace fluid filter. Refer to Section 07-02 .

Add enough automatic transmission fluid to the converter and 
transmission to bring the fluid up to a level between the two COLD marks on 
the dipstick, with engine at idle and transmission in neutral. 

Check the transmission, converter assembly and fluid cooler lines for 
leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Universal Joint Flange 

 Removal 

The transmission may be placed in a horizontal position sump pan. 

Remove flange retaining bolt, with washer and O-ring seal. Do not 
remove washer and O-ring from the bolt. 

Remove the flange. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Do not allow the output shaft to turn until the flange is installed, 
seated and the retaining bolt has been tightened. If the output shaft is 
allowed to rotate, damage to the pilot tube or governor will result. 

Lubricate the output seal with Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M1C159-A and ESB-M1C93-A. 

Install the output flange, using a 1/2-20-inch UNF bolt, flange 
retaining plate, spacer, and nut as installation tools. The length of the bolt 
and spacer will vary depending on the type of flange being installed. 

During installation, exercise care to avoid damage to the seal journal 
or the oil seal. Inspect the flange seal journal for nicks or scratches and 
seal for cuts and tears. 

Seat the flange by tightening the 1/2-20-inch nut. Remove the 
installation bolt, nut, plate and spacer. Install retaining bolt including 
O-ring seal and washer. 

Tighten the bolt to 139-164 Nm (103-121 lb-ft). 

Rotate flange by hand to check for binding or interference.

ADJUSTMENTS

Selector Lever Linkage 

With the engine stopped, position the transmission selector lever in 
the R position, fully rearward. 

Disconnect the shift cable sleeve at the transmission control arm. 

Shift the transmission control arm to R (fully forward). 

With the transmission control arm in the R position, adjust the sleeve 
until it freely enters into the hole of the control arm. 

Connect the sleeve to the control arm with the flatwashers, spring 
washer and cotter pin. 

Operate the selector lever in all positions to make sure that the 
control arm at the transmission is in full detent in all gear ranges. Readjust 
the sleeve slightly to obtain the detent position in all drive ranges.

ADJUSTMENTS

Flywheel Housing Alignment 

Whenever the flywheel housing has been replaced, or when the original 
housing is to be used on another engine, check the alignment of the housing 
bore and rear face with the engine crankshaft. 

Check the mating surfaces of the engine and the flywheel housing for 
raised metal, paint, nicks, or burrs. Remove any marks or material that would 
affect alignment. 

Position the flywheel housing on the two dowel pins in the engine, then 
bolt the housing in place. 

Check the runout of the flywheel housing bore and rear face with Dial 
Indicator/Magnetic Base D78P-4201-B or equivalent mounted on the engine 
crankshaft. If the total indicator reading of the bore runout exceeds 0.203 mm 
(0.008 inch), or if the total indicator reading of the rear face runout 
exceeds 0.203 mm (0.008 inch), repeat the check with another housing. 

 CAUTION: Be careful not to drill the upper dowel pin too deeply as the dowel pin 
is in a blind hole which may break through into the water jacket or cylinder 
wall. 

If either runout on the housing checked is not within limits, remove 
the two dowel pins from the engine. 

Bolt the flywheel housing in place without dowel pins, then adjust the 
housing to get the correct bore runout. Tighten the bolts and ream the dowel 
pin holes large enough for oversize dowel pins. 

Check the runout with the new oversize dowel pins in place, and with 
the mounting bolts tightened to 55-61 Nm (41-45 lb-ft).

 Installation

transmission fluid and fit on neck of modulator control.

lever and fuel pump lever. Readjust at idle if clearance does not exist.

 (44-62 lb-in).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Fluid Drain and Refill Procedure

The transmission should be at normal operating temperature 71°
-93°C (160°-200°
F) when the fluid is drained.

Remove the drain plug from the oil pan and allow the fluid to drain. 

After draining is completed, reinstall the drain plug. Tighten to 20-27 Nm
 (15-20 lb-ft). 

Replace fluid filter. Refer to Section 07-02 .

Slowly pour 16.5 liters (35 pints) of Motorcraft MERCON®
 ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent into 
the transmission. Apply the parking brake securely, then start the engine. 

With the hand throttle, set engine speed at idle speed rpm with the 
selector lever at N. Apply the service brakes, and shift the transmission 
through all ranges. 

Check the transmission fluid level with the engine running and the 
selector lever at N. If necessary, add fluid to bring the level to the lower 
COLD mark. Fluid temperature should be between 16-49°C (60-120°
F) for cold check.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission 

Nothing fastens the torque converter to the transmission. A retaining 
strap must be used for handling. 

The torque converter and transmission must be removed from and 
installed in the vehicle as a unit. The transmission cannot be removed from or 
installed on the converter in the vehicle. 

Except where noted, these removal and installation procedures apply 
generally to all vehicles. 

The transmission should be at operating temperature 71°
-93°C (160°-200°F) when the 
fluid is drained. This will make sure drainage is more efficient. 

 Removal 

From inside the vehicle, remove the right and left door sill scuff 
plate screws and remove the plates. 

Position the floor covering out of the way. Remove the bolts securing 
the transmission access cover to the floorpan and remove the cover. 

Remove the drain plug from the fluid pan and allow the fluid to drain.

Disconnect the fluid filler tube. 

Install a protective plug in the drain hole and the fluid filler tube.

 NOTE: In the following step do not remove the bolt that attaches the flange 
on the transmission output shaft.

On a one-piece driveline, disconnect the shaft from the pinion flange 
and from the yoke. On a two-piece drive line, disconnect the coupling shaft 
from the yoke. Remove the center support bearing bracket. Move the forward end 
of the driveshaft, or coupling shaft, out of the way. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Disconnect the speedometer, neutral start switch, backup lamp switch, 
and fluid temperature switch wires from the transmission. 

Disconnect the selector lever cable from the transmission control arm 
and the throttle control rod to the lever on the left side of the transmission 
housing. Remove the cable clamp bracket from the housing. Disconnect the 
vacuum line, if so equipped, from the modulator. 

Disconnect the fluid cooler lines from the fittings on the 
transmission, then remove the fittings. Plug the lines and transmission 
openings. If desired, the lines and transmission can be drained, but they 
should be plugged before removing the converter and transmission from the 
vehicle. 

If necessary, disconnect or remove exhaust manifold to exhaust pipe.

For the FD-1060 and FD-1460 engines remove the cover from front face of 
flywheel housing. 

For the FD-1060 and FD-1460 engines remove the bolts holding the 
flexplate to the converter ring. 

Place an engine support under the rear end of the engine, then raise 
the engine to take the weight off the crossmember. 

Support the transmission with a 454-kg (1,000-pound) transmission jack, 
such as Rotunda Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or equivalent. 
The jack should be placed so that the fluid pan does not support the entire 
weight of the transmission. Fasten a safety chain over the top of the 
transmission and to both sides of the jack.

 Installation 

If the engine, flywheel, or flywheel housing has been replaced, check 
the flywheel housing alignment and flywheel shim adjustment before installing 
the torque converter and transmission. Refer to Flywheel Housing 
Alignment in the Adjustments portion of this section. 

 NOTE: Prior to installing the transmission, it is mandatory that the 
flexplate be checked for runout. The maximum total indicated runout (TIR) 
should be 0.762 mm (0.030 inch). Also, flywheel housing transmission mounting 
face alignment inspection should be made on the engine flywheel housing 
transmission surface. The face and bore runout should not exceed 0.203 mm 
(0.008 inch) TIR. 

Raise the converter and transmission on the jack, then move the unit 
into position over the crossmember that supports the converter. Align the 
studs in the converter cover with the holes in the flywheel. Install two guide 
studs in the flywheel housing, then push the unit forward so that the 
converter studs enter the holes in the flywheel. 

Install six new self-locking nuts that hold the converter on the engine 
flywheel, and tighten to 23-31 Nm (17-23 lb-ft) for 3/8-24 
and 28-33 Nm (21-24 lb-ft) for M10-1.5 x 40. 

Install the transmission on the flywheel housing and tighten as follows:

3/8-16 x 1.5 bolts, MT-643/653 gasoline engines: 23-31 Nm
 (17-23 lb-ft)

M10-1.5 x 40, MT-643/653 FD-1060 and FD-1460 diesel engines: 51-61 Nm
 (38-45 lb-ft)

M10-1.5 x 65, MT-654 FD-1460 diesel engine: 51-61 Nm 
(38-45 lb-ft)

Install the dust shield on the bottom front side of the flywheel 
housing for the 7.0L gasoline engine. For the FD-1060 and FD-1460 diesel 
engines, install cover to front face of flywheel housing. 

Position the transmission under the transmission rear support. Align 
the holes in the support bracket with the threaded holes in the converter 
housing. Install the two bolts and washers. Tighten the bolts to 203-278 Nm
 (150-205 lb-ft). 

Lower the Rotunda Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or 
equivalent, remove it from under the vehicle, then remove the engine support 
from under the rear end of the engine. 

Install the selector lever cable bracket on the left side of the 
transmission housing, and tighten the screws to 11-13 Nm 
(8-10 lb-ft). 

Connect the selector lever cable to the transmission control arm, and 
the throttle control rod to the lever on the left side of the transmission 
housing. Connect the vacuum line, if so equipped, to the modulator. 

Remove the protective plug and connect the fluid filler tube to the 
fluid pan, then install the tube support strap bolt. 

If the exhaust manifold to exhaust pipe was removed or disconnected 
during removal, install and connect it. 

Install the driveshaft, or the center bearing support bracket, and the 
coupling shaft. Connect the shaft to the parking brake drum. Tighten all nuts 
and bolts to specifications given in Section 05-01 . 

Connect the speedometer, backup lamp switch, neutral start switch, and 
fluid temperature switch wiring. 

Adjust the selector lever linkage. Refer to Selector Lever 
Linkage in the Adjustments portion of this section.

Check all fluid line connections for tightness, then lower the vehicle 
to the floor. 

Replace fluid filter. Refer to Section 07-02 .

Fill transmission. Refer to Transmission Fluid, Drain and Refill 
Procedure in the Removal and Installation portion of this section for 
procedure. 

Add enough automatic transmission fluid to the converter and 
transmission to bring the fluid level to between the two COLD marks on the 
dipstick, while the engine idles after running at 1000-1200 rpm for one minute 
with transmission in neutral. 

Position the transmission access covers to the floorpan and secure with 
the retaining bolts. Reposition the floor covering. Install the door sill 
scuff plates and secure with the retaining screws.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Universal Joint Flange, MT-643 and MT-653

 Removal 

The transmission can be placed in either a vertical or horizontal 
position on the input drive cover or sump pan. Remove flange retaining bolt, 
with washer and O-ring seal. Do not remove washer and O-ring from the bolt. 
Remove the flange. 

Do not allow the output shaft to turn until the flange is installed, 
seated and the retaining bolt or nut has been tightened. If the output shaft 
is allowed to rotate, damage to the pilot tube or governor will result. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: During installation, care should be exercised to avoid damage to the 
seal journal or the oil seal. Inspect the flange seal journal for nicks or 
scratches and seal for cuts and tears. 

Install the universal joint flange, using a 1/2-20-inch UNF bolt, 
flange retaining plate, spacer, and nut as installation tools. The length of 
the bolt and spacer will vary depending on the type of flange being installed. 

Seat the flange by tightening the 1/2-20-inch nut. Remove the 
installation bolt, nut plate and spacer. Install retaining bolt including 
O-ring seal and washer. Tighten the bolt to 139-164 Nm 
(102-121 lb-ft).

ADJUSTMENTS

Selector Lever Linkage

Proper adjustment of the manual selector lever linkage is important as 
the shift detents must correspond exactly to those in the transmission. 
Periodic inspections should be made for bent or worn parts, loose threaded 
connections, loose bolts, and accumulation of grease and dirt. All moving 
joints must be kept clean and well lubricated.

The following procedures are applicable to most vehicles.

The selector lever should move easily and give a crisp detent feel in 
each position. The linkage should be adjusted so that the stops in the column 
(selector lever and bracket) match the detents in the transmission.

When the linkage is correctly adjusted, the pin that engages the 
control arm at the transmission can be moved freely in each range.

 CAUTION: Proper installation of the control arm is imperative to the function of 
the transmission. Excessive torque applied to the external selector lever 
retaining nut can damage the internal selector lever arm. 

With the engine stopped, position the transmission selector lever in 
the R (reverse) position, fully rearward.

Disconnect the shift cable sleeve at the transmission control arm.

Shift the transmission control arm to R (all the way forward and upward).

With the transmission control arm in the R position, adjust the sleeve 
until it freely enters into the hole of the control arm.

Connect the sleeve to the control arm with the flatwashers, spring 
washer and cotter pin.

Operate the selector lever in all positions to make sure that the 
control arm at the transmission is in full detent in all gear ranges. It may 
be necessary to readjust the sleeve slightly to obtain the detent position in 
all drive ranges.

ADJUSTMENTS

Flywheel Housing Alignment 

Whenever the flywheel housing has been replaced, or when the original 
housing is to be used on another engine, check the alignment of the housing 
bore and rear face with the engine crankshaft. 

Check the mating surfaces of the engine and the flywheel housing for 
raised metal, paint, nicks, or burrs. Remove any marks or material that would 
affect alignment. 

Position the flywheel housing adapter on the two dowel pins in the 
engine, then bolt the housing in place. 

Face and bore runouts must not exceed 0.203 mm (0.008 inch) as measured 
with a dial indicator mounted to the crankshaft. 

 CAUTION: Be careful not to drill the upper dowel pin too deeply as the dowel pin 
is in a blind hole which can break through into the water jacket or cylinder 
wall. 

If either runout on the housing checked is not within limits, remove 
the two dowel pins from the engine. 

Bolt the flywheel housing adapter in place without dowel pins, then 
adjust the housing to get the correct bore runout. Tighten the bolts and ream 
the dowel pin holes large enough for oversize dowel pins. 

Check the runout with the new oversize dowel pins in place, and with 
the mounting bolts tightened to 55-61 Nm (41-45 lb-ft).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fluid Cooler, Integral

The transmission fluid cooler (heat exchanger) is mounted in the right 
radiator tank (7000 and 8000-Series) or under the radiator crossmember. Engine 
coolant passes through tubes in the element of the cooler to absorb heat from 
the transmission fluid circulating around the tubes. The cooled fluid passes 
through a filter in the return line to the transmission.

================================================================================
PAGE 4979
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 07-02: Transmission, Automatic, Cooling

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Operating Temperatures 

The transmission should not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent 
operating temperatures to 149°C (300°F) will 
not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures above 120°C 
(250°F) increase the lubricant's rate of oxidation and 
shorten its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 120°
C (250°F), the transmission may require 
more frequent fluid changes or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F):

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

================================================================================
PAGE 4980
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 07-02: Transmission, Automatic, Cooling

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Transmission Temperature Indicator Light 

The instrument panel-mounted TRANS TEMP warning light comes on to 
indicate maximum transmission-to-cooler fluid temperature of 149°
C (300°F). Should the light come on, stop 
the vehicle and shift the transmission to neutral. Accelerate the engine to 
1200-1500 rpm to allow the transmission to return to normal, 71-104°
C (160-220°F), before resuming operation. 
Check transmission fluid level.

================================================================================
PAGE 4981
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 07-02: Transmission, Automatic, Cooling

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Transmission Cooler Line Filter 

Normal transmission wear may cause debris which can move around within 
the transmission fluid cooling system and become trapped in the transmission 
fluid cooler, preventing efficient cooling. In most cases there is no 
effective method to completely remove this material from the transmission 
fluid, yet it must be eliminated as much as possible. Transmission fluid 
cooler systems use an external filter in the fluid return circuit to remove 
any debris present in the fluid, providing protection against excessive 
transmission wear, overheating, or damage due to contamination.

 Removal

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Transmission Fluid Cooler

When internal wear or damage has occurred in the transmission, metal 
particles, clutch plate material, or band material may have been carried into 
the converter and transmission fluid cooler. These contaminants are a major 
cause of recurring transmission troubles and must be removed from the system 
before the transmission is put back into service.

Whenever a transmission has been disassembled to replace worn or 
damaged parts or because the valve body sticks due to foreign material, the 
converter and transmission fluid cooler must be cleaned by using a 
mechanically agitated cleaner, such as Rotunda Torque Converter/Oil Cooler 
Cleaner 014-00028 or equivalent.

The lack of a drain plug in the converter increases the amount of 
residual flushing solvent retained in the converter after cleaning. This 
retained solvent is not acceptable and a method of diluting it is required. 
The following procedure is to be used after removal of the torque converter 
from the cleaning equipment.

Thoroughly drain remaining solvent through hub.

Add 1.9 liters (2.0 qts.) of clean transmission fluid to converter. 
Agitate by hand.

Thoroughly drain solution through converter hub.
