REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Output Yoke, Auxiliary Section and Clutch Housing 

 Removal 

Lock the transmission by engaging the two mainshaft gears with the 
mainshaft sliding clutches.

[FIGURE: C100571A.gif]

Use a large breaker bar to turn the nut from the output shaft. Pull the 
yoke straight to the rear and off the output shaft.

Remove the six nuts with lockwashers that hold the clutch housing to 
the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100581A.gif]

Remove the two capscrews that hold the clutch housing to the 
transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100591A.gif]

Jar the clutch housing with a rubber mallet to break the gasket seal. 
Pull the clutch housing from the transmission case and remove the gasket.

 NOTE: There are three capscrew lengths. Note their locations. 

Remove the 15 capscrews that hold the auxiliary section to the 
transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100601A.gif]

Insert three capscrews in the housing flange tapped holes. Tighten 
evenly to move the auxiliary section back; leave a space wide enough to attach 
a chain hoist.

[FIGURE: C100611A.gif]

Remove the puller capscrews and attach a chain hoist to the auxiliary 
section. Pull the auxiliary section off and remove the gasket.

[FIGURE: C100621A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Make sure the synchronizer is in neutral, and the auxiliary front 
countershaft bearings are installed in the front case. 

Position a new gasket on the auxiliary housing. Attach a chain hoist to 
the auxiliary section. Move the assembly evenly into the front case rear, 
piloting it on the dowel pins. As the assembly is moved forward, the 
countershaft drive gears will mesh with the auxiliary drive gear. 

 NOTE: There are three capscrew lengths. Make sure the capscrews are in their 
proper locations. 

Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install the 15 capscrews in the 
auxiliary housing flange and tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

Position the corresponding new gasket on the clutch housing mounting 
surface. Install the clutch housing on the case front, piloting on the six 
studs and the front bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C100631A.gif]

Install the six nuts with lockwashers. Tighten to 244-271 Nm
 (180-200 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12973A.gif]

Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install and tighten the 
capscrews to 108-136 Nm (80-100 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12974A.gif]

Install the yoke on the output shaft splines and move it into the rear 
bearing cover. 

Lock the transmission by engaging two mainshaft gears with their 
sliding clutches. 

Lightly oil output shaft threads. Then, install the nut on the output 
shaft. Tighten the nut to 542-610 Nm (400-450 lb-ft).

Input Shaft 

 Special Procedure for Changing Input Shaft 

Some cases of service can require replacement of the input shaft 
because of clutch wear on the splines. In these instances the input shaft can 
be removed without disassembling the transmission other than removing the 
shift bar housing. Removal of the clutch housing is optional.

[FIGURE: C10066C.gif]

 Removal 

Remove the shift bar housing from the transmission case. Refer to Shift 
Bar Housing in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Remove the retaining capscrews, front bearing cover and gasket. Service 
the oil seal of model covers so equipped. 

Remove the bearing retaining snap ring from the shaft groove. 

Push down on the input shaft to cock the bearing in the bore. Drive the 
input shaft toward the transmission rear through the bearing as far as 
possible. Pull the input shaft forward to expose the bearing. 

Use pry bars or screwdrivers to complete removal of the bearing. 

Remove the spacer and the snap ring. 

Pull the input shaft forward and out of the drive (fourth) gear and 
case. 

 Installation

input shaft into drive (fourth) gear.

Install the snap ring in the snap ring groove inside the drive (fourth) 
gear. 

Install the spacer on the input shaft. 

Install the bearing on the input shaft. 

Install the bearing retainer snap ring. 

Install the front bearing cover and gasket. Make sure to align the oil 
return hole in the case with the hole in the cover. Lightly oil capscrew 
threads. Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

Install the shift bar housing. Refer to Shift Bar 
Housing in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Auxiliary Section 

 Bearing Cover, Rear, Removal 

Remove the capscrews and the rear bearing cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C100671A.gif]

If necessary, remove the oil seal from the rear bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C100681A.gif]

Remove the speedometer rotor or replacement spacer from the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C100691A.gif]

Remove the washer from the output shaft.

 Auxiliary Countershafts, Removal 

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershafts forward through the 
countershaft bearings and remove them from the auxiliary housing.

[FIGURE: C100701A.gif]

Remove the countershaft bearings from the auxiliary case bearing bores.

[FIGURE: C100711A.gif]

 NOTE: The vise should be equipped with soft jaws or wood blocks to prevent 
damage to the countershaft. 

If necessary, secure assembly in a vise and remove the auxiliary 
countershaft front bearing race from the countershaft with a jaw puller and 
clamp.

If necessary, secure assembly in a vise and remove the auxiliary 
countershaft rear bearing race. 

 Range Cylinder Assembly, Synchronizer Assembly, LO Range Gear and 
Output Shaft, Disassembly 

Secure the auxiliary housing in a vise. Remove the capscrews and the 
range cylinder cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C100721A.gif]

Remove the yoke bar nut and washer.

[FIGURE: C100731A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not damage the piston. 

Push range yoke bar to the transmission rear. Use a screwdriver to 
remove the piston.

Remove the copper gasket from the yoke bar.

[FIGURE: C100741A.gif]

 NOTE: The following step will damage the bearing and should not be attempted 
unless bearing replacement is planned. 

Use pullers and a clamp to remove the bearing from the output shaft 
front.

Move the synchronizer assembly, shift yoke and yoke bar forward and out 
of the housing assembly.

[FIGURE: C100751A.gif]

Remove the yoke bar and shift yoke from the synchronizer assembly. Cut 
the lockwire and remove the two lock screws. Remove the shift yoke from the 
yoke bar.

[FIGURE: C100771A.gif]

[FIGURE: C100761A.gif]

Remove the dust seal and air port extension from the range cylinder 
housing top.

[FIGURE: C100781A.gif]

Remove the cylinder housing. If necessary, remove the O-ring from the 
small bore in the cylinder.

[FIGURE: C100791A.gif]

 LO Range Gear and Output Shaft, Removal 

 NOTE: When applying force to the output shaft rear, do not damage threads. 

Using a soft bar and maul, drive or press against the output shaft rear 
to move assembly forward and out of the rear bearing.

Remove the rear washer and LO range gear from the shaft rear.

[FIGURE: C100801A.gif]

Remove the spline washer from the LO range gear hub. 

[FIGURE: C100811A.gif]

Move the output shaft rear bearing to the rear and out of the housing.

 Synchronizer 

 Disassembly 

Place the larger LO range synchronizer ring on the bench. Cover the 
assembly with a shop towel to prevent losing the three springs released from 
the HI range synchronizer at the pin locations. Pull the HI range synchronizer 
from the blocker pins.

[FIGURE: C100821A.gif]

Remove the synchronizer springs from the HI range synchronizer ring bore.

[FIGURE: C100831A.gif]

Remove the sliding clutch from the synchronizer LO range pins.

[FIGURE: C100841A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Pins on the LO range synchronizer must be lined up with the chamfered 
holes on the sliding clutch bottom. 

Place the larger LO range synchronizer ring race down on the bench with 
the pins up. Place the sliding clutch, recessed side up on the pins of the LO 
range synchronizer.

[FIGURE: C100851A.gif]

Install the three springs in the HI range synchronizer ring bore. 

Place the HI range synchronizer ring, seating springs against the pins. 

Apply downward pressure to the HI range synchronizer ring while 
twisting counterclockwise to compress the springs and fully seat the ring on 
the LO range synchronizer blocker pins.

[FIGURE: C100861A.gif]

 LO Range Gear and Output Shaft, Assembly 

 NOTE: Make sure the magnetic discs are installed in the auxiliary housing. 

 NOTE: Mark timing teeth on the LO range gear. A highly visible color of 
toolmaker's dye is recommended. 

Mark any two adjacent gear teeth. Then mark two adjacent teeth that are 
directly opposite the first set marked. There should be the same number of 
teeth between the markings on each gear side.

[FIGURE: C100871A.gif]

Place splined washer on the output shaft, with shoulder facing up as 
shown.

[FIGURE: C100881A.gif]

Install the LO range gear over the output shaft rear and against 
shoulder of splined washer.

[FIGURE: C100891A.gif]

Install the LO range gear rear washer on the output shaft and against 
the gear, with the chamfer side facing up.

[FIGURE: C100901A.gif]

Stand the output shaft on end with the shaft rear facing up. Place the 
auxiliary housing over the shaft so the output shaft extends through the rear 
bore.

[FIGURE: C100911A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not heat the bearing above 135°C (275°
F). 

Using a heat lamp or hot plate and oil, heat the output shaft rear 
bearing and install on the output shaft. Seat the bearing securely on the 
shaft and in the bore.

[FIGURE: C100921A.gif]

Install the bearing in the housing bore with the appropriate driver.

[FIGURE: C100931A.gif]

 Range Cylinder, Assembly 

If removed, install the O-ring in the cylinder small bore slot. 
Lubricate the O-ring with Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A. 

Install the range cylinder in the housing with the cylinder air port 
aligned with the air port in the auxiliary housing.

[FIGURE: C100941A.gif]

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to air port extension 
threads. Install the dust seal and air port extension through housing and into 
the air cylinder bore.

[FIGURE: C100781A.gif]

 Range Cylinder Assemblies and Synchronizer, Installation 

Place the shift yoke on the yoke bar, with the long hub toward the bar 
front. Align slots in the yoke bar and install the two lock screws. Tighten 
lock screws to 68-88 Nm (50-65 lb-ft) and secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C12975A.gif]

Place the yoke in the sliding clutch slot, threaded end of the yoke bar 
toward the larger LO range synchronizer. Place the entire assembly in the 
auxiliary housing, engaging the sliding clutch splines with the output shaft 
and inserting the yoke bar through the cylinder bore.

[FIGURE: C100751A.gif]

Install the copper gasket on the yoke bar threaded end.

[FIGURE: C100741A.gif]

Install the O-ring on the piston outer diameters. Apply a light coat of 
Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESR-M13P4-A to the O-ring.

[FIGURE: C100951A.gif]

Install the piston on the yoke bar and against the copper gasket, 
piston flat side out.

[FIGURE: C100961A.gif]

Install the lockwasher and nut on the yoke bar and tighten to 81-95 Nm
 (60-70 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12976A.gif]

Install the gasket and cylinder cover with the HI range port to the 
right. Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install and tighten the four 
capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12977A.gif]

 Auxiliary Countershafts 

 Assembly 

Install the bearing inner race on the countershaft front.

[FIGURE: C100971A.gif]

Install the bearing inner race on the countershaft rear.

[FIGURE: C100981A.gif]

 NOTE: Countershaft gear teeth must be marked for timing the auxiliary 
section. Mark with a highly visible color of toolmakers' dye. 

Mark the tooth on the countershaft gear which is stamped with an O.

[FIGURE: C100991A.gif]

 Installation 

Seat the outer races of the countershaft rear bearing only partially in 
the housing bores, just far enough to stay in place.

[FIGURE: C101001A.gif]

 NOTE: Time the countershaft gear with the LO range gear. As the countershaft 
is installed, mesh the marked LO range gear tooth on each countershaft between 
each set of marked gear teeth on the LO range gear. 

Place the countershaft into position in the auxiliary housing, 
inserting the inner race into the partially installed rear bearing. 

[FIGURE: C101011A.gif]

With the countershaft in position, complete the installation of the 
countershaft rear bearings on the shaft and into the case bore. Seat securely. 

Install the washer with flat side to the rear on the output shaft and 
against the bearing. 

Install the speedometer rotor or replacement spacer on the output shaft. 

 NOTE: Use the proper seal driver to install the seal. 

If previously removed, install the oil seal in the rear bearing cover, 
with seal lip to the rear.

Install the rear bearing cover with the speedometer bore up and to the 
left. Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to capscrew threads. Then, 
install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12978A.gif]

Install the bearing on the output shaft front, with chamfered side to 
race rear.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Front Section 

 Input Shaft, Removal 

Remove the four capscrews retaining the front bearing cover. Remove the 
bearing cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C101021A.gif]

Remove the bearing retaining snap ring from the shaft groove.

[FIGURE: C101031A.gif]

Push down on the input shaft to cock the bearing in the bore. Drive the 
input shaft toward the transmission rear, through the bearing as far as 
possible. Pull the input shaft forward to expose the bearing. 

Use pry bars to complete the bearing removal.

[FIGURE: C101041A.gif]

Remove spacer from the input shaft. 

Remove snap ring from the groove inside the drive (fourth) gear.

[FIGURE: C101051A.gif]

Pull the input shaft forward and out of the drive (fourth) gear and 
case. 

Check the bushing in the input shaft pocket, replace if worn.

[FIGURE: C101061A.gif]

 Auxiliary Drive Gear 

 Removal 

Straighten the lock tangs. Remove the four capscrews and two bearing 
retainers from the case.

[FIGURE: C101071A.gif]

Remove the snap ring from the mainshaft rear, located inside the 
auxiliary drive gear bore.

[FIGURE: C101081A.gif]

With two screwdrivers, pry the auxiliary drive gear off the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C101091A.gif]

 Disassembly 

Remove the snap ring from the auxiliary drive gear. 

Press or use a driver to remove the bearing from the auxiliary drive 
gear. 

 Assembly 

Press the bearing on the auxiliary drive gear. 

Install the bearing retaining snap ring in the auxiliary drive gear 
shoulder groove. 

 Upper Countershaft Bearings, Removal 

Remove the upper countershaft snap ring from the case rear bearing bore.

[FIGURE: C101101A.gif]

Use a soft bar and maul against the countershaft rear and move the 
countershaft assembly forward as far as possible until the snap ring groove in 
the front bearing is exposed. 

Install the snap ring removed from the rear bearing bore in the exposed 
snap ring groove.

[FIGURE: C101111A.gif]

 NOTE: Steps four and five may have to be repeated several times to unseat the 
front bearing. 

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft assembly to the rear 
as far as possible. This will move the front bearing forward on the 
countershaft. 

From the case rear, use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft 
forward to unseat the front bearing from the case bore.

Use puller or pry bars to remove the front countershaft bearing. 

 NOTE: Removal procedure damages the bearings. Removal should not be attempted 
unless bearing replacement is planned. 

Block the countershaft and use a maul and punch from inside the case to 
drive the rear countershaft bearing from the case bore and countershaft.

[FIGURE: C101121A.gif]

 Upper Reverse Idler Gear Assembly, Removal 

Use inside jaw pullers or an impact puller to remove the auxiliary 
countershaft front bearing from the left reverse idler gear bore. 

Remove the plug from the reverse idler gear shaft rear.

[FIGURE: C101131A.gif]

Use a socket wrench to remove the stop nut from the reverse idler gear 
shaft front. Remove the washer.

[FIGURE: C101141A.gif]

Use an impact puller with a 1/2-inch 13-threaded end to remove the 
reverse idler gear shaft from the case bore.

[FIGURE: C101151A.gif]

As the reverse idler gear shaft is moved to the rear, remove the thrust 
washer and reverse idler gear from the case. 

If necessary, remove the bearing from the reverse idler gear bore.

[FIGURE: C101161A.gif]

 Mainshaft Assembly 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: After performing this step, note that the drive gear will be free and 
can fall from the shaft. 

Block the right countershaft assembly against the case wall. Slide the 
drive gear to the rear and engage with the sliding clutch splines. Use a hook 
around first/second sliding clutch. Tilt the mainshaft front up and lift the 
assembly from the case.

[FIGURE: C101171A.gif]

 Disassembly 

Secure the mainshaft, with drive (fourth) gear up, in a vise. Remove 
the drive (fourth) gear and the third/fourth speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C101181A.gif]

Remove third gear hub snap ring from the mainshaft groove.

[FIGURE: C101191A.gif]

Remove tolerance washer and third gear.

[FIGURE: C101201A.gif]

Remove second gear and tolerance washer.

[FIGURE: C101211A.gif]

Remove first/second speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C101221A.gif]

Remove mainshaft key from mainshaft keyway.

[FIGURE: C101231A.gif]

Remove tolerance washer and first gear.

[FIGURE: C101241A.gif]

Remove LO speed gear and tolerance washer.

[FIGURE: C101251A.gif]

Remove LO/reverse speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C101261A.gif]

Remove tolerance washer and reverse gear.

[FIGURE: C101271A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: If previously removed, install the corresponding snap rings in the 
inside diameter of the mainshaft gears. 

Secure the mainshaft in a vise equipped with brass jaws or wood blocks, 
shaft pilot-end down. If previously removed, install the roll pin in the 
keyway. 

Install the reverse gear tolerance washer in the groove near the 
mainshaft rear.

[FIGURE: C101281A.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure the mainshaft key is positioned with the word TOP to the 
outside. 

Rotate the tolerance washer in the mainshaft groove to align the washer 
splines with the mainshaft splines. Install the mainshaft key in keyway to 
lock the washer in place.

[FIGURE: C101291A.gif]

Install the reverse gear on the tolerance washer with clutching teeth 
facing down.

[FIGURE: C101301A.gif]

Install the auxiliary drive gear on the mainshaft with clutching teeth 
facing up.

[FIGURE: C101311A.gif]

Install the snap ring in the mainshaft rear groove.

[FIGURE: C101321A.gif]

Insert two screwdrivers between the reverse gear hub and the auxiliary 
drive gear. Apply slight downward pressure on the screwdriver handles to 
spread the gears evenly apart. Make sure the gear hubs are parallel. Insert a 
feeler gauge between the hubs. The gap must be between 0.127-0.305 mm 
(0.005-0.012 inch). If the clearance is less than the minimum 0.127-mm 
(0.005-inch) tolerance, the tolerance washer in the reverse gear should be 
replaced by a thinner tolerance washer. This increases the axial clearance 
between gears. If the clearance checked is greater than the maximum 0.305-mm 
(0.012-inch) tolerance, a thicker tolerance washer should be installed in the 
reverse gear. This would decrease the axial clearance between the gears.

[FIGURE: C101331A.gif]

Washers are available in the following thicknesses to obtain the 
correct limits. Select the appropriate washer as required.

After proper reverse gear clearance has been set, remove the snap ring 
from the mainshaft rear. Remove the auxiliary drive gear and the reverse gear 
from the mainshaft. The tolerance washer and key remain on the mainshaft. 

Reposition the mainshaft with the reverse gear minus its snap ring in 
the vise, with pilot end up, and the keyway accessible. 

Install the LO/reverse speed sliding clutch on the mainshaft, against 
the reverse gear tolerance washer. Align sliding clutch slot with mainshaft key.

[FIGURE: C101341A.gif]

Remove the mainshaft key. Install LO speed gear tolerance washer on the 
mainshaft. Install the key to lock the tolerance washer to the shaft. 

Install LO speed gear on the mainshaft, clutching teeth down and 
engaged with the washer external splines.

[FIGURE: C101351A.gif]

Install first gear on the mainshaft, clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: C101361A.gif]

 CAUTION: When the key is removed, the mainshaft gears can drop to the bottom. 

Remove the mainshaft key from the keyway. Install first gear tolerance 
washer on the mainshaft and into first gear hub.

[FIGURE: C101371A.gif]

Install the mainshaft key to lock the tolerance washer to the shaft.

[FIGURE: C101381A.gif]

Check axial clearances and make adjustments if necessary. 

Install the first/second speed sliding clutch, aligning sliding clutch 
slot with key; engage with first gear.

[FIGURE: C101391A.gif]

 NOTE: Pull the mainshaft key up slightly to fit in keyway. 

Move the mainshaft key upward and install second gear tolerance washer. 
Install mainshaft key.

[FIGURE: C101401A.gif]

Reposition the key so it rests on the mainshaft grooved shoulder. 

Install the second gear on the mainshaft with clutching teeth down. 
Engage gear with the tolerance washer external splines. 

Install the third gear on the mainshaft with clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: C101411A.gif]

Install a tolerance washer in the third gear bore. 

Install the snap ring in the snap ring groove.

[FIGURE: C101421A.gif]

Check axial clearance and make adjustments if necessary. 

Install the third/fourth speed sliding clutch on the mainshaft. Align 
sliding clutch slot with key and engage clutch with third gear.

[FIGURE: C101431A.gif]

 NOTE: Mark timing teeth on drive (fourth) gear with a highly visible color of 
toolmakers' dye. 

Mark two adjacent teeth on the drive (fourth) gear. Th

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Mainshaft Assembly, Input Shaft, Drive Gear Assembly and Upper 
Countershaft Assembly, Installation 

Place the upper countershaft assembly into position in the case. 
Support the countershaft assembly against the case wall as far as possible. 

Place the mainshaft assembly into position in the case. 

Mesh the lower countershaft marked tooth with either of the two marked 
teeth on the main drive (fourth) gear.

[FIGURE: C101591A.gif]

If previously removed, install the input shaft bushing. 

Install input shaft through case bore and into the drive (fourth) gear 
splines. Installation of the input shaft prevents the mainshaft from dropping 
to the case bottom.

[FIGURE: C101601A.gif]

Center the mainshaft in the case rear bore and install the auxiliary 
drive gear. 

Seat the auxiliary drive gear bearing in the case rear bore.

[FIGURE: C101611A.gif]

Install the bearing lower retainer plates. Lightly oil threads of 
capscrews. Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

Bend the lock tangs. 

Install the top retainer plates and bend the lock tangs.

[FIGURE: C101621A.gif]

Move the mainshaft assembly to the rear to expose the mainshaft snap 
ring groove. Install the snap ring.

[FIGURE: C101631A.gif]

Install snap ring into drive (fourth) gear groove.

[FIGURE: C101641A.gif]

Install the spacer on the input shaft, chamfered side to the front.

[FIGURE: C101651A.gif]

Install the drive gear bearing.

[FIGURE: C101661A.gif]

Install the bearing retainer snap ring.

[FIGURE: C101671A.gif]

Install the front bearing cover and gasket, making sure oil return hole 
aligns with cover hole. 

Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install the bearing cover 
capscrews and tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12979A.gif]

Engage the third/fourth speed sliding clutch into third mainshaft gear. 
This prevents drive (fourth) speed gear from dropping to cause a timing error.

[FIGURE: C101691A.gif]

Mesh the upper countershaft marked timing tooth with the main drive 
(fourth) gear two marked timing teeth, making sure the lower countershaft 
remains in time.

[FIGURE: C101701A.gif]

 NOTE: Use a large screwdriver or bar to block the countershaft from moving.

Hold the countershaft in position and partially install the rear 
countershaft bearing.

[FIGURE: C101711A.gif]

Install the case rear bore snap ring into the groove.

[FIGURE: C101721A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not shift the transmission into two gears at the same time. This 
prevents the transmission from rotating. 

Shift the mainshaft sliding clutches into all the gear positions with a 
screwdriver. The front box is properly timed if the sliding clutches can be 
shifted into all the mainshaft gears.

[FIGURE: C101731A.gif]

Use a flanged driver to complete installation of the front countershaft 
bearing.

[FIGURE: C101741A.gif]

 Upper Reverse Idler Gear Assembly, Installation 

 NOTE: Since the upper and lower reverse idler gear assemblies are identical, 
installation of the upper reverse idler gear assembly should be made using the 
procedure described under Lower Reverse Idler Gear Assembly, 
Installation in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Subassemblies 

 Shift Lever Housing 

 Disassembly 

 WARNING: SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. USE CARE TO PROTECT EYES WHEN REMOVING SPRING. 

Remove the boot from the shift lever and secure assembly in a vise with 
the housing bottom up. Use a large screwdriver to twist between the spring and 
housing, forcing the spring from under the lugs in the housing. Do one coil at 
a time.

[FIGURE: C101751A.gif]

Remove the tension spring, washer and shift lever from the housing.

[FIGURE: C101761A.gif]

Remove the spade pin from the housing bore tower. If necessary, remove 
the O-ring from the tower groove.

[FIGURE: C101771A.gif]

 Assembly 

Secure the shift lever housing in a vise. Install the spade pin in the 
housing tower bore. If previously removed, install the O-ring in the tower 
groove. 

Position the shift lever in the housing with the spade pin in the lever 
ball slot. Install the tension spring washer over the ball, dished-side up.

[FIGURE: C101781A.gif]

Install the tension spring under the housing lugs, seating one coil at 
a time. Use a spring driving tool.

[FIGURE: C101791A.gif]

Remove the assembly from the vise. Install the rubber boot over the 
shift lever and against the housing.

[FIGURE: C101801A.gif]

 Shift Bar Housing 

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: During disassembly, lay all parts on a clean bench in the order of 
removal to facilitate reassembly. Shift bars not being removed must be kept in 
the neutral position or interlock parts will lock bars.

Remove the two capscrews and remove the detent spring cover from 
housing top. Remove the three tension springs installed under the cover.

[FIGURE: C101811A.gif]

Tilt the assembly and remove the three detent balls from the housing 
bores.

[FIGURE: C101821A.gif]

Secure the assembly in a vise with the air valve actuating shaft up. 
The housing front will be to the right.

[FIGURE: C101831A.gif]

 NOTE: When removing the shift bars, start with the upper shift bar. Move all 
the bars to the right and out the rear boss bore. Cut the lockwire and remove 
the lock screws from each bar just before their removal. 

Move the LO/reverse shift bar to the right and out of the housing, 
removing shift yoke from bar.

[FIGURE: C101841A.gif]

Move the first/second shift bar to the right and out of housing, 
removing shift yoke from bar. As the neutral notch in bar clears the front 
web, remove the interlock pin from the neutral notch bore.

[FIGURE: C101851A.gif]

[FIGURE: C101861A.gif]

Remove the air valve actuating shaft from rear web.

[FIGURE: C101871A.gif]

Move the third/fourth shift bar to the right and out of housing, 
removing shift yoke from bar. As yoke is removed, remove the two interlock 
balls from front web.

[FIGURE: C101881A.gif]

If necessary, remove the plug, spring and reverse plunger stop from 
bore in LO/reverse shift yoke.

[FIGURE: C101891A.gif]

 Assembly 

If previously removed, place plunger stop in LO/reverse shift yoke, and 
install spring in bore of yoke and onto shank of plunger. Install the plug and 
tighten to compress spring. 

Back the plug out 1-1/2 turns and stake plug through the small hole in 
yoke.

[FIGURE: C101901A.gif]

 NOTE: Keep bar in neutral position during installation. Do not exceed the 
recommended torque rating for yoke lock screws as overtightening may distort 
shift bars. 

Place the housing in a vise with the front of housing to the right as 
shown. Install the third/fourth shift bar in bottom bore with detent notches 
to the front. Install yoke and lock screw and tighten to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft). Secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C12980A.gif]

Install interlock ball in front web vertical bore.

[FIGURE: C101921A.gif]

Install air valve actuating shaft in rear web vertical bore.

[FIGURE: C101931A.gif]

Install the first/second speed shift bar in center bore, and install 
shift yoke on bar; insert interlock pin in detent notch. Install lock screw. 
Tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C101941A.gif]

Install interlock ball in front web vertical bore.

[FIGURE: C101951A.gif]

Install LO/reverse shift bar in upper bore, detent notches to the 
front. Install yoke on bar, fork to the rear. Install lock screw and tighten 
to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C101961A.gif]

Remove assembly from vise and install the three detent balls, one in 
each bore in housing top. Keep yokes in neutral.

[FIGURE: C101971A.gif]

Install the three tension springs, one in each bore, in housing top.

[FIGURE: C101981A.gif]

Install the detent spring cover. Lightly oil threads of capscrews. 
Then, install and tighten the two capscrews to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12982A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification

The RTLO-12713, 14713 and 16713 transmissions are low inertia 
transmissions. In a low inertia transmission, there is a sliding clutch that 
separates the front box from the rear box whenever there is a gearshift, a 
range shift or a split shift. This enables the front box to slow down quickly 
to make shifting easier. With a low inertia transmission, preselection during 
a split shift is possible. The RTLO 13-speed transmissions have twin 
countershafts and helical auxiliary gears.

[FIGURE: C12178A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 5121
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 07-03L: Transmission, Manual, RTLO-12713, 14713 and 16713 13-Speed

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow

 LO Range "L" 

 NOTE: The numbers on the following illustrations correspond to the following 
numbered steps.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

The input shaft external splines engage the main drive gear internal 
splines.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged mainshaft 
gear. The following cross-section view illustrates a first/fifth speed gear 
engagement.

The external clutching teeth of the sliding clutch engage with the 
internal clutching teeth of the mainshaft gear which transfers torque to the 
mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12179A.gif]

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear 
sliding clutch which is in the forward position.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the LO range gear in 
the auxiliary section.

The LO range gear delivers torque to the output shaft through the range 
synchronizer sliding clutch.

The output shaft delivers torque to the driveline components.

[FIGURE: C12180A.gif]

 HI Range "L" 

 NOTE: The numbers on the illustration correspond to the following numbered 
steps.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

The input shaft external splines engage the main drive gear internal 
splines.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged mainshaft 
gear. The following cross-section view illustrates a first/fifth speed gear 
engagement.

The external clutching teeth of the sliding clutch engage with the 
internal clutching teeth of the mainshaft gear which transfers torque to the 
mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12179A.gif]

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the front auxiliary drive 
gear sliding clutch which is in the forward position.

The front auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the rear auxiliary 
drive gear.

Torque is transferred to the range synchronizer sliding clutch which is 
in the forward position delivering torque directly to the output shaft.

The output shaft delivers torque to the driveline components.

[FIGURE: C12181A.gif]

 HI Range "H" 

 NOTE: The numbers on the following illustrations correspond to the following 
numbered steps.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

The input shaft external splines engage the main drive gear internal 
splines.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged mainshaft 
gear. The following cross-section view illustrates a first/fifth speed gear 
engagement.

The external clutching teeth of the sliding clutch engage with the 
internal clutching teeth of the mainshaft gear which transfers torque to the 
mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12179A.gif]

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the rear auxiliary drive 
gear sliding clutch which is in the rearward position.

Torque is delivered to the back of the rear auxiliary drive gear. The 
range synchronizer sliding clutch is in the forward position, transferring 
torque directly to the output shaft.

The output shaft delivers torque to the driveline components.

[FIGURE: C12182A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

Proper lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program.

Eaton Fuller Transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in an oil circulating bath created by the motion of the gears and 
shafts.

All parts are amply lubricated if these procedures are closely followed:

Maintain oil level and inspect regularly.

Follow maintenance interval chart.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 Maintain Proper Oil Level 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. 

 NOTE: If your vehicle has a transmission oil filter, you must change the 
filter when fluid or lubricant is changed.

Make sure oil is level with the filler opening. Because you can reach 
oil with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. An oil level of 25 
mm (one inch) is equivalent to approximately 3.7 liters (one gallon) of oil.

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Transmission Operating Angles 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication will occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

For operating angles over 12 degrees, the transmission must be equipped 
with an oil pump or cooler kit to make sure transmission is properly lubricated.

 Operating Temperatures with Oil Coolers 

The transmission must not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 121°C (250°F). However, intermittent 
operating temperatures to 149°C (300°F) do 
not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures above 121°C 
(250°F) increase the lubricant's oxidation rate and shorten 
its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 121°
C (250°F), the transmission can require 
more frequent oil changes or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 121°C (250°F):

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

exhaust system too close to transmission

high horsepower operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

Transmission oil coolers are recommended with the following engines:

350 HP and above

Transmission oil coolers are required with the following engines:

399 HP and above and GCW's over 40 900 kg (90,000 lb)

399 HP and above and 1898 Nm (1400 lb-ft) or greater 
torque

450 HP and above

Auxiliary Section

 Removal (Horizontal) 

 CAUTION: Auxiliary countershaft retaining straps can be installed to hold the 
countershafts in place. However, the auxiliary section can be removed without 
straps. Use care. 

 NOTE: Auxiliary sections can be removed either with the transmission in the 
horizontal position or the vertical position.

 NOTE: To facilitate installation, note the capscrew lengths and their 
locations.

Remove the four capscrews and the auxiliary countershaft rear bearing 
cover, gasket, and rear bearing shim.

[FIGURE: C12186A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an air gun. Tighten by hand until the capscrews are snug. 

Install the auxiliary countershaft retaining covers with two 3/8-inch 
NC x 1-inch and one 3/8-inch NC x 1-1/2-inch clean capscrews.

[FIGURE: C12187A.gif]

 NOTE: To facilitate installation, note the capscrew lengths and their 
locations.

From the auxiliary section housing, remove the retaining capscrews that 
attach the front section to the auxiliary section.

Insert the two longest capscrews in the housing flange tapped holes. 
Tighten capscrews evenly, separating the auxiliary section from the front box 
enough to break the gasket seal.

[FIGURE: C12188A.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the tapped holes.

Attach an auxiliary section hanger bracket to the auxiliary section top.

Attach a lifting chain to the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

[FIGURE: C12320A.gif]

Move assembly to the rear until auxiliary section is free.

Remove the gasket and clean all mounting surfaces of gasket material.

 Removal (Vertical) 

 CAUTION: Place blocks under the clutch housing to prevent input shaft damage. 

Place transmission in the vertical position, clutch housing down.

 NOTE: To facilitate installation, note the capscrew lengths and their 
locations.

Remove the four capscrews and the auxiliary countershaft rear bearing 
cover, gasket, and rear bearing shim.

[FIGURE: C12189A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an air gun. Tighten by hand until the capscrews are snug. 

Install the auxiliary countershaft retaining straps with two 3/8-inch 
NC x 1-inch and one 3/8-inch NC x 1-1/2-inch clean capscrews.

[FIGURE: C12190A.gif]

 NOTE: To facilitate installation, note the capscrew lengths and their 
locations.

From the auxiliary section housing, remove the capscrews that retain 
the auxiliary section to the front box.

Install a steel bar through the yoke.

Attach a lifting chain to the steel bar.

[FIGURE: C12191A.gif]

Lift assembly from the front section.

Remove the gasket and clean all mounting surfaces of gasket material.

 NOTE: Auxiliary sections can be installed either with the transmission in the

Position a new gasket on the transmission mounting surface.

Attach a lifting chain to the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

[FIGURE: C12320A.gif]

front section back.

Remove the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

Loosen the retaining covers.

Slide the auxiliary section the rest of the way into position.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or

 NOTE: Install capscrews into their proper locations noted during removal.

 (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12718A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Clutch Housing

 Removal 

 NOTE: Removal of the clutch housing is done in the horizontal position.

 NOTE: The clutch release mechanism must be removed.

From inside the clutch housing, remove the nuts and washers.

From inside the clutch housing, remove the capscrews.

[FIGURE: C12330A.gif]

Jar clutch housing to break gasket seal.

Pull the clutch housing from the studs and transmission case.

[FIGURE: C12331A.gif]

Remove the gasket and clean all mounting surfaces of gasket material.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Installation of the clutch housing is done in the horizontal position.

Position a new gasket on the housing mounting surface.

Install the clutch housing on the front box, pilot it on the six studs 
and drive gear bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C12331A.gif]

Install the nuts with washers or lockwashers on the studs, tighten to 
244-256 Nm (180-190 lb-ft).

Install the capscrews with lockwashers, tighten to 122-136 Nm
 (90-100 lb-ft).

Reverse Idler Gear Assembly

 NOTE: The following instructions are used to remove upper and lower reverse

 Removal 

The mainshaft reverse gear must be moved in order to remove the upper 
reverse idler gear. Refer to Mainshaft Assembly , Steps 1-3 in the Removal and

From the idler shaft, loosen and remove the locknut and washer.

[FIGURE: C12204A.gif]

From the idler shaft rear, remove the pipe plug. From the reverse idler

bearing race.

[FIGURE: C12205A.gif]

 NOTE: While removing the reverse idler shaft, the thrust washer can drop to 
the transmission case bottom.

Install an impact puller, 1/2 inch-13 threaded end, and remove the 
shaft from case bore. As the idler shaft and idler plate are removed, remove

[FIGURE: C12206A.gif]

Inspect the reverse gear assembly and remove the inner race and needle 
bearing, if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12207A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: If you are installing the bottom reverse idler gear assembly, make sure

Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification

 NOTE: The upper reverse idler is positioned in the case during mainshaft 
installation.

If reverse gear assembly is disassembled, position the needle bearing 
and inner race into the reverse idler gear.

[FIGURE: C12207A.gif]

Place the rear thrust washer on the idler shaft.

[FIGURE: C12208A.gif]

Insert the idler shaft into the case bore, threaded-end to the front. 
As the shaft passes through the case bore position the reverse idler gear on 
the shaft, long hub to the front. Insert the thrust washer between the reverse 
idler gear and the case support boss. Finish inserting the idler shaft.

Make sure the reverse idler shaft is seated in the support boss bore.

Install the washer and locknut on shaft front. Tighten the stop nut to 
68-81 Nm (50-60 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12209A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12210A.gif]

Thread the pipe plug into the reverse idler shaft and tighten.

[FIGURE: C12211A.gif]

Use a bearing driver and maul and install the auxiliary countershaft 
front bearing race against the idler plate.

[FIGURE: C12347A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Countershaft Bearings

 CAUTION: Performing the following instructions will damage the bearings and 
should not be done unless bearing replacement is planned. 

 NOTE: The following instructions are used to remove the upper and lower 
countershaft bearings. To remove the mainshaft assembly, only the upper 
countershaft bearings need to be removed.

 Removal 

From each countershaft rear groove, remove the snap ring. From inside 
the case, use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft rear bearings from 
the case bores.

[FIGURE: C12212A.gif]

From each countershaft front, remove the capscrew and front retainer 
plate.

[FIGURE: C12213A.gif]

Use the soft bar and maul to drive each countershaft to the rear as far 
as possible. This partially unseats the front bearings. Return to the case 
rear, and drive each countershaft forward as far as possible. This exposes the 
bearing snap rings.

[FIGURE: C12214A.gif]

 NOTE: The bearing inner race remains pressed on the countershaft after 
removal of the front bearings.

Use a bearing puller or pry bars to remove the countershaft front 
bearings. If a bearing puller is used, the front bearing cover has to be 
removed.

[FIGURE: C12215A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: The front bearing inner race must be pressed on the countershaft front.

Move the countershaft to the rear and insert the countershaft support 
tool to center shaft in rear case bore.

[FIGURE: C12216A.gif]

 NOTE: The flanged-end driver must cover the bearing outer race for proper 
installation.

Use a flanged-end driver to start the front bearing in case bore.

Use a screwdriver inserted in the countershaft capscrew bore to help 
center the countershaft.

Move the countershaft forward into the bearing.

Use a flanged-end bearing driver and maul to completely seat the front 
bearing in case bore.

[FIGURE: C12217A.gif]

On the countershaft front, position the retainer plate with roll pin in 
shaft end hole.

Secure with capscrew. Tighten to 122-163 Nm (90-120 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12218B.gif]

From the rear, remove the countershaft support tool.

With the larger inside diameter lead chamfer to the shaft front, use a 
flanged-end bearing driver and install the rear bearing. On each countershaft 
rear groove, install the snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12219A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mainshaft Assembly

 Removal 

From the mainshaft, remove the reverse gear retaining snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12222A.gif]

Move the mainshaft reverse gear as far to the rear as possible and 
remove reverse gear inside diameter snap ring.

Move the reverse gear forward and against the next gear, engaging the 
mainshaft sliding clutch spline.

[FIGURE: C12223A.gif]

 NOTE: The upper reverse idler gear assembly shaft must be removed. Roll the 
gear to the outside. Refer to Reverse Idler Gear Assembly in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section.

Use a large screwdriver and block the upper countershaft assembly 
against the case wall.

Position the hook or rope around the mainshaft.

Pull the mainshaft to the rear to free the pilot from the input shaft 
pocket.

[FIGURE: C12224A.gif]

 CAUTION: Be careful when removing the mainshaft assembly. The sliding clutch on 
the end can slip off the mainshaft. 

 CAUTION: Reverse gear is also free and can fall off the shaft. 

 NOTE: The upper countershaft must be kept forward against the case front 
wall. After the mainshaft is free of the pilot, move it as far forward as 
possible.

Tilt the mainshaft front up and lift assembly from the case.

[FIGURE: C12225A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: The lower countershaft bearings and the input shaft must be installed, 
but for higher torque ratings do not install the front bearing cover.

 NOTE: Check to make sure the lower countershaft drive gear marked tooth is in 
time with main drive gearset of marked teeth.

Block the upper countershaft forward and as close to the case wall as 
possible.

With reverse gear forward against the next speed gear and mainshaft 
pilot end over the integral oil pump gear, lower the mainshaft assembly while 
pulling the shaft rear through the case bore.

[FIGURE: C12225A.gif]

Pull the input shaft forward until the drive gear is against the case.

After the mainshaft drops into the case, slide the countershaft back 
and the mainshaft should fall down between the countershafts.

Move the mainshaft pilot-end into the input shaft pilot bushing. Mesh 
the mainshaft gears with the corresponding countershaft assembly gears.

[FIGURE: C12224A.gif]

Install the upper reverse idler gear in case. Refer to Reverse Idler 
Gear Assembly in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Mesh the reverse gear teeth with the reverse idler gear teeth and move 
the reverse gear to the rear as far as possible.

[FIGURE: C12226A.gif]

Align the reverse gear spacer external splines with the reverse gear 
and move the spacer into the reverse gear.

Install the reverse gear inside diameter snap ring and move the reverse 
gear forward on the mainshaft and against the reverse gear limit washer.

[FIGURE: C12222A.gif]

To finish the input shaft/front bearing cover installation, refer to Input Shaft 
 in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 NOTE: Replace the pilot bushing, if worn.

[FIGURE: C12337A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12196A.gif]

Push the input shaft bearing back into the case bore.

Position a new gasket on the bearing cover mounting surface, making

[FIGURE: C12197A.gif]

Position the front bearing cover, making sure to align the cover oil

Secure the front bearing cover with six capscrews and tighten to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Timing Procedures

 CAUTION: It is essential that both countershaft assemblies of the front and 
auxiliary sections are timed. This makes sure proper tooth contact is made 
between mainshaft gears seeking to center on the mainshaft during torque 
transfer and mating countershaft gears that distribute the load evenly. If not 
properly timed, serious damage to the transmission is likely to result from 
unequal tooth contact causing the mainshaft gears to climb out of equilibrium. 

Timing is a simple procedure of marking the appropriate teeth of a 
gearset prior to installation and placing them in proper mesh while in the 
transmission. In the front section, it is necessary to time only the drive 
gearset. And depending on the model, only the LO range, deep reduction, or 
splitter gearset is timed in the auxiliary section.

 Front Section 

Marking countershaft drive gear teeth.

Prior to placing each countershaft assembly into the case, clearly mark 
the tooth located directly over the drive gear keyway as shown. This tooth is 
stamped with an O to aid identification.

[FIGURE: C8921B.gif]

Marking main drive gear teeth.

Mark any two adjacent teeth on the main drive gear.

Mark the two adjacent teeth located directly opposite the first set 
marked on the main drive gear. There should be an equal number of unmarked 
gear teeth on each side between the marked sets.

[FIGURE: C8922B.gif]

Meshing marked countershaft drive gear teeth with marked main drive 
gear teeth.

After placing the mainshaft assembly into the case, the countershaft 
bearings are installed to complete installation of the countershaft assemblies.

When installing the bearings on the left countershaft, mesh the 
countershaft drive gear marked tooth with either set of main drive gear two 
marked teeth.

Repeat the procedure when installing the bearings on the right 
countershaft, make use of the remaining set of main drive gear two marked 
teeth to time assembly.

[FIGURE: C8923B.gif]

 Auxiliary Section 

Mark any tooth on the LO range auxiliary mainshaft gear. Then mark a 
tooth located directly opposite the first marked.

Prior to placing each auxiliary countershaft assembly into housing, 
mark the two teeth on each auxiliary countershaft assembly LO range gear 
stamped with the two Os. Repeat the procedure on each auxiliary countershaft 
reduction gear.

Splitter Cylinder Assembly

 Removal 

 NOTE: To remove the splitter cylinder assembly, you must be able to access 
the front and rear of the auxiliary case.

From the splitter cylinder cover, remove the retaining capscrews. 
Remove the cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: DC0061A.gif]

Remove the 3/4-inch nut on the splitter yoke bar.

[FIGURE: DC0062A.gif]

From the auxiliary front, pull the sliding clutch and shift yoke 
straight out to remove them.

[FIGURE: DC0063A.gif]

From the auxiliary rear, remove the splitter cylinder housing.

[FIGURE: DC0064A.gif]

 NOTE: When removing the splitter cylinder cover insert valve, note the 
direction the insert valve was positioned (nipple in or out).

From the splitter cylinder cover, remove the insert valve retaining nut 
and insert valve.

[FIGURE: DC0065A.gif]

Inspect the insert valve and the cover bore for damage.

Inspect the piston O-rings. Remove if necessary.

Inside the cylinder housing bore, inspect the small O-ring and remove 
if damaged.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Apply Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M13P4-A to shift cylinder assembly and insert valve O-rings 
so a film covers the entire surface of each O-ring.

 NOTE: Apply Rust Penetrant and Inhibitor F2AZ-19A501-A or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESR-M99C56-A to all shift cylinder walls and yoke bars. 
Cover the entire yoke bar surface that comes in contact with the shift 
cylinder O-ring.

If previously removed, install the small O-ring in the cylinder housing 
bore.

[FIGURE: DC0066A.gif]

If previously removed, install the piston O-ring on the piston outer 
diameter.

Place the shift yoke in the splitter sliding clutch slot.

Position the sliding clutch and yoke in the auxiliary housing. One hand 
will need to hold the sliding clutch against the rear auxiliary drive gear 
until the splitter yoke nut has been installed.

Position a new gasket on the cylinder housing mounting surface. With 
the air passage toward the rear bearing cover, install the cylinder housing.

[FIGURE: DC0067A.gif]

If previously removed, install the insert valve in the cylinder cover 
bore with nipple in the proper direction. Install the insert valve retaining 
nut. Tighten the retaining nut to 54-68 Nm (40-50 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: DC0068A.gif]

Inside the cylinder housing, install the O-ring over the yoke bar end. 
With the recessed side up, install the splitter cylinder piston. Install the 
3/4-inch lock nut. Tighten the lock nut to 95-115 Nm (70-85 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: DC0069A.gif]

Position a new gasket on the cylinder housing cover mounting surface. 
The gasket air passage must align with the housing air passage. Position the 
splitter cylinder cover over the gasket.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining 
capscrews. Install and tighten the retaining capscrews to 27-34 Nm
 (20-25 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: DC0070A.gif]

 Auxiliary Section Fixture 

[FIGURE: C12054A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12234A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12382A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12236A.gif]

Place the auxiliary housing over the output shaft assembly, and the

[FIGURE: C12237A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12238A.gif]

Position the rear bearing cover.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or

Install the six retaining capscrews. Tighten to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: DC0071A.gif]

Install the bearing races.

[FIGURE: DC0072A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an air gun. Tighten by hand until the capscrews are snug.

Install the cylinder housing.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the capscrews. Tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 
lb-ft).

Insert the piston. Push it in as far as it will go.

[FIGURE: C12288A.gif]

Secure the piston with the retaining nut. Tighten to 95-115 Nm
 (70-85 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12289B.gif]

Position a new gasket on the cylinder housing cover mounting surface.

Over the gasket, position the range cylinder cover.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the capscrews. Tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12290B.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Shift Lever Housing

 NOTE: If total disassembly is needed, the Roadranger® valve 
must be removed first.

 Disassembly 

Slide the boot up the shift lever shaft and remove.

[FIGURE: C12387A.gif]

With housing bottom facing up, secure the assembly in a vise.

 CAUTION: Spring is under tension. Use care to protect eyes when removing spring. 

 NOTE: Release the spring one coil at a time.

Use large screwdriver to twist between the spring and housing, forcing 
the spring from under the housing lugs.

[FIGURE: C12388A.gif]

From inside the housing tower, remove the tension spring, washer, and 
shift lever.

In models so equipped, remove the nut and washer from the housing bore.

From the housing tower spade pin bore, remove and inspect the spade 
pin. Discard if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12389A.gif]

From the housing tower inside groove, inspect the O-ring. Discard if 
damaged.

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Inspect tension spring and washer for wear.

 NOTE: Apply Rust Penetrant and Inhibitor F2AZ-19A501-A or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESR-M99C56-A to the shift lever pivot ball. A rust 
preventative lubricant film should cover all surfaces between and including 
the pivot ball.

With housing bottom facing up, secure the assembly in a vise.

If the spade pin is damaged, replace and install the spade pin in 
housing tower bore.

[FIGURE: C12389A.gif]

In models so equipped, install the nut and washer in the housing bore.

If the O-ring is damaged, replace. Lubricate the O-ring with Silicone 
Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A. 
Install the O-ring in the housing tower inside groove.

Align the lever ball slot with the spade pin and position the shift 
lever in the housing tower.

With dished-side up, install the washer over the ball.

[FIGURE: C12390A.gif]

 NOTE: Seat the tension spring one coil at a time.

Use a tension spring driver to install the tension spring under the 
housing lugs.

[FIGURE: C101791A.gif]

Remove the assembly from the vise.

Install a rubber boot over the shift lever and against the housing.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Shift Bar Housing

 NOTE: The shift bar housing must be removed from the transmission.

 NOTE: During disassembly, lay all parts on a clean bench in order of removal 
to facilitate assembly.

 NOTE: Shift bars not being removed must be kept in the neutral position or 
the interlocking parts lock the bars.

 NOTE: Start with the bottom shift bar.

 NOTE: Cut the lockwire and remove the lock screws from each bar just before 
their removal.

 Disassembly 

If the three sets of tension springs and balls from housing bores have 
not been removed, place the shift bar housing on its side to remove them.

[FIGURE: C12241A.gif]

With the housing rear to the right, lay the assembly on a flat surface.

Remove the oil trough retaining capscrews and oil trough (16713 does 
not have an oil trough).

[FIGURE: DC0074A.gif]

While removing the top yoke bar to the right, remove the two shift 
blocks.

[FIGURE: DC0075A.gif]

From the middle yoke bar, remove the shift yoke and shift block. As the 
neutral notch in the bar clears the rear boss, remove the small interlock pin 
from the notch bore.

[FIGURE: DC0076A.gif]

Remove the actuating plunger from the center top bore boss.

[FIGURE: DC0077A.gif]

From the bottom yoke bar, remove the two shift yokes.

[FIGURE: DC0078A.gif]

As the shift bar clears the last boss, two 3/4-inch interlock balls 
drop from the bottom rear boss bore.

[FIGURE: C12247A.gif]

If damaged, remove the plug, spring, and plunger from the first and 
reverse shift yoke.

[FIGURE: C12248A.gif]

Inspect the yoke or block parts, replace the worn parts.

If the yoke actuator parts are damaged, replace the parts.

[FIGURE: C12249A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Keep yoke bars in neutral while assembling.

 NOTE: Inspect shift blocks and shift yokes for wear.

 NOTE: Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the shift bar housing 
plugs which are used to plug oil cooler provision holes. The sealant should be 
applied so that at least 5 complete threads are covered.

 NOTE: Apply Eaton Lockwire No. 1819 or equivalent to all shift bar housing 
assembly set screws in both blocks and yokes. The wire should anchor the 
capscrew at least two complete 360-degree turns. The lockwire ends should be 
trimmed and bent out of the way of any part interference.

Assemble the yoke actuator assembly as follows:

From the shift bar housing bottom, install the actuator pin and yoke 
actuator.

[FIGURE: C12250A.gif]

On the shift bar housing top, install the washer and nut.

[FIGURE: C12251A.gif]

Assemble the first and reverse shift yoke assembly as follows:

Install the plunger in the first and reverse shift yoke bore, plunger 
shank to the outside.

Install the spring into the bore over the plunger shank.

Install the plug and tighten to compress the spring.

After plug bottoms out, back the plug out 1-1/2 turns.

Complete the block assembly process by staking the plug through the 
small hole in block.

[FIGURE: C12248A.gif]

With the housing rear to the right, lay the assembly on a flat surface.

Start installation of the bottom shift bar, as the bar passes the 
bosses, install the two bottom shift yoke assemblies. Finish installation.

[FIGURE: DC0078A.gif]

Install the shift yoke lock screw. Tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft). Tighten the lockwire securely.

Place the actuating plunger in the top center bore.

[FIGURE: DC0077A.gif]

Place one 3/4-inch interlock ball in the interlock bore, against the 
bottom bar.

Holding the middle bar notched-end, start installation. As the bar 
passes the rear boss, position the shift block.

As the bar passes the center boss, position the shift yoke on bar, long 
hub to the housing front.

Just prior to inserting notched-end of bar in rear boss, install the 
small interlock pin vertically in the neutral notch bore.

[FIGURE: C12252A.gif]

Install the shift block and shift yoke lock screws. Tighten to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

Place on 3/4-inch interlock ball in the interlock bore, against the 
middle bar.

Holding the top bar notched-end, start installation. As the bar passes 
the rear boss, position the shift block.

As the bar passes the center boss, position the shift yoke on bar, long 
hub to the housing rear.

[FIGURE: DC0075A.gif]

Install the shift block and shift yoke lock screws. Tighten to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft). Tighten the lockwire securely.

Install the oil trough. Tighten the retaining capscrews to 11-16 Nm
 (8-12 lb-ft) (16713 does not have an oil trough).

[FIGURE: DC0079A.gif]

Install the three tension balls, one in each housing top bore. Install 
the three detent springs, one over each tension ball.

[FIGURE: DC0080A.gif]

Make sure interlocking system is working by verifying it cannot be 
shifted into two gears at the same time.

Make sure all lock screws are lockwired.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Countershaft Assembly, Front Section

 Disassembly 

From each countershaft front remove the drive gear retaining snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12254A.gif]

 CAUTION: Never use the PTO gear as a pressing base. The narrow width of this 
gear can cause breakage. 

Using the rear face of the fourth speed gear as a base, press the drive 
gear, PTO gear, and fourth speed gear from each countershaft. This removes the 
front bearing inner race.

[FIGURE: C12255A.gif]

Using the rear face of second speed gear as a base, press third speed 
gear and second speed gear from each countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12256A.gif]

Inspect the keys and remove if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12257A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Except for the PTO gears, the upper and lower countershaft assemblies 
are the same.

To avoid confusion during installation, mark the upper countershaft 
(45-tooth PTO gear) with a U. The lower countershaft has a 47-tooth PTO gear.

If previously removed, install the keys in each countershaft keyway.

[FIGURE: DC0081A.gif]

Align second speed gear keyway with the countershaft key, long hub to 
countershaft front, and press the gear on the countershaft.

[FIGURE: DC0082A.gif]

Align third speed gear keyway with the countershaft key, long hub 
against second speed gear, and press the gear on the countershaft.

[FIGURE: DC0083A.gif]

Align fourth speed gear keyway with the countershaft key, long hub to 
countershaft front, and press the gear on the countershaft.

[FIGURE: DC0084A.gif]

Align PTO gear keyway with the countershaft key, bullet-nose of teeth 
facing up (shaft rear). Align drive gear keyway with the countershaft key, 
long hub against PTO gear, and press both gears on the countershaft.

[FIGURE: DC0085A.gif]

On each countershaft front, install the drive gear retaining snap ring 
in groove.

[FIGURE: DC0086A.gif]

Use a flanged-driver or the press to install the bearing inner race on 
the countershaft front against the drive gear.

[FIGURE: C12261A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Mainshaft Assembly, Procedure 1

 NOTE: During disassembly, lay all parts on a clean bench in order of removal 
to facilitate reassembly.

 NOTE: When removing limit washers, spacers and gears, note their location. 
Keep the internal-splined washers and external-splined spacers with the gear 
from which they were removed. There is only one limit washer and one spacer 
belonging to each gear.

 Disassembly 

Remove reverse gear and reverse gear spline spacer.

[FIGURE: DC0087A.gif]

Tilt the mainshaft up, and from the opposite end, remove the sliding 
clutch.

[FIGURE: DC0088A.gif]

Place the mainshaft in a vertical position.

From the mainshaft rear, pull the mainshaft key from the mainshaft 
keyway.

[FIGURE: DC0089A.gif]

Turn the reverse gear limit washer to align its splines with the 
mainshaft and remove the washer. Remove the first/reverse-speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: DC0090A.gif]

Lift and turn first gear to align the limit washer splines.

[FIGURE: DC0091A.gif]

Remove the limit washer, spacer and first gear.

[FIGURE: DC0092A.gif]

Turn the second gear limit washer to align its splines with the 
mainshaft. Remove second gear and its limit washer. Remove the second/third 
sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: DC0093A.gif]

Remove each remaining gear, limit washer, and spacer.

[FIGURE: DC0094A.gif]

Inspect the roll pin and remove if damaged.

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Each mainshaft gear must have its inside diameter snap ring installed 
before placement on the mainshaft. Do not replace reverse gear inside diameter 
snap ring.

 NOTE: Gear limit washers are internally splined and locked to the mainshaft 
by the key. Gear spacers are externally splined to engage with gear hub 
clutching teeth. There is one limit washer and one spacer for each mainshaft 
gear.

 NOTE: Axial clearance (end play) limits are 0.152-0.381 mm (0.006-0.015 inch) 
for all mainshaft gears.

 NOTE: If the axial clearance is less than the minimum 0.152-mm (0.006-inch) 
tolerance, the limit washer should be replaced with a thinner limit washer. 
This will increase the axial clearance between the gears. If the axial 
clearance is greater than the maximum 0.381-mm (0.015-inch) tolerance, a 
thicker limit washer should be installed. This will decrease the axial 
clearance between the gears.

With mainshaft pilot-end down, secure the mainshaft in a vise equipped 
with brass jaws or wood blocks.

If previously removed, install the roll pin in keyway.

[FIGURE: C12406A.gif]

With the washer flat side up, position the fourth speed gear limit 
washer (white) in the mainshaft first or bottom groove. Rotate the washer 
until the washer splines and mainshaft splines align.

Start at the mainshaft bottom and install a plastic line in the keyway 
to lock the washer in place. As limit washers and gears are installed, 
continue to push the plastic line up.

[FIGURE: C12266A.gif]

Against the fourth speed gear washer, position the fourth speed gear 
spacer. With clutching teeth down and engaged with the spacer external 
splines, position the fourth speed gear on the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: DC0095A.gif]

With clutching teeth up and against fourth speed gear, install the 
third speed gear and spacer.

[FIGURE: DC0096A.gif]

With the washer flat-side down, position the limit washer against the 
spacer. Rotate the washer until the washer splines and mainshaft splines align.

[FIGURE: DC0097A.gif]

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Between the gear hub and mainshaft spacer, insert 0.152-mm (0.006-inch) 
feeler gauge and 0.381-mm (0.015-inch) feeler gauge. If out of tolerance, 
change the limit against the mainshaft spacer. Refer to the shimming chart in 
the Specifications portion of this section for further information.

[FIGURE: DC0098A.gif]

With the missing internal splines aligned with the plastic line, 
install the second/third speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: DC0099A.gif]

With the washer flat side up, position the second speed gear limit 
washer in the next available groove. Rotate the washer until the washer 
splines and mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Install second gear spacer.

[FIGURE: DC0100A.gif]

With clutching teeth down, position the second speed gear on the 
mainshaft engaging with spacer external splines.

[FIGURE: DC0101A.gif]

With clutching teeth up, install first speed gear on shaft against 
second speed gear.

[FIGURE: C12279A.gif]

Position first speed gear spacer against first speed gear, engaging the 
spacer external splines with gear clutching teeth. 

With washer flat side down, position the limit washer against the 
spacer. Rotate the washer until the washer splines and mainshaft splines align.

[FIGURE: DC0102A.gif]

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Between the gear hub and mainshaft spacer, insert 0.152-mm (0.006-inch) 
feeler gauge and 0.381-mm (0.015-inch) feeler gauge. If out of tolerance, 
change the limit against the mainshaft spacer. 

[FIGURE: DC0103A.gif]

Align the sliding clutch missing internal spline with the mainshaft key 
and install the first/reverse speed sliding clutch.

With the flat side up, position the reverse speed gear limit washer 
(white) in the next available groove. Rotate the washer until the washer 
splines and mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Against the limit washer, position reverse speed gear spacer.

[FIGURE: DC0104A.gif]

Install reverse gear on the mainshaft. Engage the gear clutching teeth 
with spacer external splines and sliding clutch. Move the reverse gear down 
against the first speed gear.

[FIGURE: DC0105A.gif]

 CAUTION: Be careful not to move the gears while doing this procedure, the limit 
washers are unlocked and can rotate which would cause the gears to drop. 

At this time remove the air line and insert the mainshaft key.

[FIGURE: C12273A.gif]

Remove the mainshaft from the vise.

On the shaft front, align the sliding clutch missing internal spline 
with the mainshaft key and install the fourth-drive gear sliding clutch. 
Engage the sliding clutch external splines with the fourth speed gear 
clutching teeth.

[FIGURE: C12274A.gif]

Mainshaft Assembly, Procedure 2

 NOTE: This mainshaft procedure differs from the previous in that this 
procedure is for mainshafts with three grooves and a flatwasher between

 NOTE: When removing limit washers, spacers and gears, note their location.

belonging with each gear. No external splined washer under fourth or second.

[FIGURE: DC0087A.gif]

clutch.

[FIGURE: DC0088A.gif]

Remove the mainshaft key snap ring.

keyway.

[FIGURE: DC0089A.gif]

[FIGURE: DC0090A.gif]

[FIGURE: DC0091A.gif]

Remove the limit washer, spacer and first gear.

[FIGURE: DC0092A.gif]

Turn the second gear limit washer to align its splines with the 
mainshaft. Remove second gear and its limit washer. Remove the second/third

[FIGURE: DC0093A.gif]

Remove each remaining gear, limit washer, and spacer.

[FIGURE: DC0106A.gif]

Inspect the roll pin, remove if damaged.

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Each mainshaft gear that has an I.D. snap ring must have its I.D. snap

I.D. snap ring.

 NOTE: Gear limit washers are internally splined and locked to the mainshaft 
by the key. Gear spacers are externally splined to engage with gear hub 
clutching teeth. There is one limit washer and one spacer for each mainshaft 
gear.

 NOTE: Axial clearance (end play) limits are 0.152-0.381 mm (0.006-0.015 inch) 
for all mainshaft gears.

 NOTE: If the axial clearance is less than the minimum 0.152-mm (0.006-inch) 
tolerance, the limit washer should be replaced with a thinner limit washer. 
This will increase the axial clearance between the gears. If the axial 
clearance is greater than the maximum 0.381-mm (0.015-inch) tolerance, a 
thicker limit washer should be installed. This will decrease the axial 
clearance between the gears.

With mainshaft pilot-end down, secure the mainshaft in a vise equipped 
with brass jaws or wood blocks.

If previously removed, install the roll pin in keyway.

[FIGURE: C12406A.gif]

With the washer flat side up, position the fourth speed gear washer in 
the mainshaft first or bottom groove. Rotate the washer until the washer 
splines and mainshaft splines align.

Start at the mainshaft bottom and install a plastic line in the keyway 
to lock the washer in place. As limit washers and gears are installed, 
continue to push the plastic line up.

[FIGURE: C12266A.gif]

With clutching teeth down, position the fourth speed gear on the 
mainshaft. Install the flatwasher.

[FIGURE: DC0107A.gif]

With clutching teeth up and against the flat-washer, install the third 
speed gear.

[FIGURE: DC0096A.gif]

With the washer flat side down, position the washer against the spacer. 
Rotate the washer until the washer splines and mainshaft splines align.

[FIGURE: DC0097A.gif]

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

With the missing internal splines aligned with the plastic line, 
install the second/third speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: DC0099A.gif]

With the washer flat side up, position the second speed gear limit 
washer in the next available groove. Rotate the washer until the washer 
splines and mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Install second gear spacer.

[FIGURE: DC0100A.gif]

With clutching teeth down, position the second speed gear on the 
mainshaft engaging with spacer external splines.

[FIGURE: DC0101A.gif]

With clutching teeth up, install first speed gear on shaft against 
second speed gear.

[FIGURE: C12279A.gif]

Position first speed gear spacer against first speed gear, engaging the 
spacer external splines with gear clutching teeth. 

With washer flat-side down, position the limit washer against the 
spacer. Rotate the washer until the washer splines and mainshaft splines align.

[FIGURE: DC0102A.gif]

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Between the gear hub and mainshaft spacer, insert 0.152-mm (0.006-inch) 
feeler gauge and 0.391-mm (0.015-inch) feeler gauge. If out of tolerance, 
change the limit against the mainshaft spacer. 

[FIGURE: DC0103A.gif]

Align the sliding clutch missing internal spline with the mainshaft key 
and install the first/reverse speed sliding clutch.

With the flat-side up, position the reverse speed gear limit washer 
(white) in the next available groove. Rotate the washer until the washer

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Against the limit washer, position reverse speed gear spacer.

[FIGURE: DC0104A.gif]

Install reverse gear on the mainshaft. Engage the gear clutching teeth

[FIGURE: DC0105A.gif]

At this time remove the air line and insert the mainshaft key.

[FIGURE: C12273A.gif]

On the shaft front, align the sliding clutch missing internal spline

Engage the sliding clutch external splines with the fourth speed gear
