DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Output Shaft Assembly

 Disassembly 

From the auxiliary housing rear, remove the rear bearing retaining 
capscrews.

[FIGURE: DC0108A.gif]

 CAUTION: When removing the rear bearing cover, the rear bearing cone drops from 
the housing bore. 

From the auxiliary housing rear, remove the rear bearing cover, rear 
bearing, and bearing race.

[FIGURE: DC0109A.gif]

Clean the gasket mounting surface of gasket material.

Inspect the rear bearing cover oil seal for damage and remove if damaged.

[FIGURE: DC0110A.gif]

From the output shaft, remove the bearing inner spacer.

[FIGURE: C12292A.gif]

Use the output shaft assembly gear front face as a base and press the 
output shaft through the bearing and gear.

[FIGURE: C12293A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Output shaft stack up should be done on a clean, flat surface.

Using toolmaker's dye, mark any two adjacent teeth on the LO range gear 
for timing purposes. Repeat the procedure for the two adjacent teeth directly 
opposite the first set marked.

[FIGURE: C12294A.gif]

Place the splined washer on the output shaft shoulder. With LO range 
gear clutching teeth down, position LO range gear on the output shaft, engage 
the washer splines.

[FIGURE: C12295A.gif]

With the smooth side up, position the LO range gear rear washer on the 
output shaft against the LO range gear. Move LO gear around to center the 
washer.

[FIGURE: C12296A.gif]

 CAUTION: When heating the bearings, do not heat bearings above 136°
C (275°F). 

With tapered side up, use heat or appropriate driver and install the 
output shaft front rear bearing (the larger bearing).

[FIGURE: C12297A.gif]

On the output shaft, position the bearing inner spacer. Set aside.

[FIGURE: DC0111A.gif]

 NOTE: When installing the rear bearing race, the proper depth is when the 
race shoulder is seated on bearing bore top.

Lay the auxiliary housing front face down on a clean, flat surface. 
Install the bearing race in the bearing bore.

[FIGURE: DC0112A.gif]

Follow assembly procedures under Countershaft Assembly, Auxiliary 
Section in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Synchronizer Assembly

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: Place the synchronizer assembly on a clean, flat surface. Cover the 
synchronizer assembly with a shop rag to prevent losing the three springs 
under pressure from the HI range synchronizer pin locations.

Place the larger LO range synchronizer ring on the bench.

Grab both sides of the HI range synchronizer and pull.

[FIGURE: C12438A.gif]

From the synchronizer ring LO range pins, remove the sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C12439A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Assembly should be done on a clean, flat surface slightly lower than 
your waist.

On the bench place the larger LO range synchronizer ring face down with 
pins up.

 NOTE: Pins on the LO range synchronizer must line up with the chamfered holes 
on the sliding clutch bottom.

With the sliding clutch recessed side up, place the sliding clutch on 
the LO range synchronizer pins.

[FIGURE: C12439A.gif]

In the HI range synchronizer bores, install the three springs.

[FIGURE: C12440A.gif]

Place the HI range synchronizer ring over the LO range synchronizer 
ring. Rotate the HI range synchronizer until the springs are seated against 
the pins.

[FIGURE: C12441A.gif]

 NOTE: When compressing the HI range synchronizer springs, cover with a shop 
rag. In the event compression is not achieved the first time, this prevents 
the springs from leaving the bench area.

With the shop rag, cover the assembly. Apply downward pressure to the 
HI range synchronizer ring while twisting counterclockwise. This compresses 
the springs to fully seat HI range on the LO range synchronizer.

[FIGURE: C12442A.gif]

Make sure there are three springs and the springs are fully compressed.

Make sure the sliding clutch can be moved from HI to LO range and back.

ADJUSTMENTS

Shimming Procedure for Tapered Bearings

 CAUTION: Shims must be aligned properly or the rear bearing cover can be damaged 
when final torque is applied. 

 NOTE: The shimming procedure can be done in the horizontal or vertical 
position. The procedure is done the same.

Remove the countershaft straps. Make sure a 0.100 countershaft rear 
bearing shim is installed. Be sure the countershaft rear bearing races are 
seated in the bearing bores.

[FIGURE: C12456A.gif]

Install two clean 3/8-inch x 1-inch capscrews without washers directly 
across from each other in each bearing cover. Tapped holes in auxiliary case 
must be free of thread adhesive.

[FIGURE: C12457A.gif]

Tighten the capscrews to 0.8 Nm (7 lb-in). Do not 
install the countershaft rear bearing cover gasket.

[FIGURE: C12458B.gif]

Rotate the output shaft six times clockwise, then six times 
counterclockwise to seat the countershaft rear bearings. Use a feeler gauge, 
as close to each capscrew location as possible, and measure the gap between 
the countershaft rear bearing cover and the auxiliary case. Record the 
measurements. Using the average measurement, refer to the shimming chart in Specifications 
 to identify the proper shim.

[FIGURE: DC0113A.gif]

Remove the countershaft rear bearing cover and gauging shim.

Place the selected shim on the rear countershaft bearing race.

[FIGURE: DC0114A.gif]

Position a new gasket on countershaft rear bearing cover mounting 
surface.

Position the countershaft rear bearing cover over the new gasket.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the retaining capscrews, tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12460B.gif]

Repeat Steps 1-8 for the other countershaft rear bearing cover.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification

The Fuller RT-8608-L, RT-11609A, RTX-11609-B/R, RT-12609A, 
RTX-12609-B/R, RT-13609-A, RTX-13609-B/R, RT-14609-A and RTX-14609-B/R 
transmissions feature the twin-countershaft principal of operation.

The twin-countershaft design, which splits torque equally between the 
two shafts, provides a high torque capacity-to-weight ratio.

Because of torque splitting, each gear set carries only half the load, 
greatly reducing the face width of each gear. The mainshaft gears, when not 
engaged, float between the countershaft gears, eliminating the need for gear 
sleeves and bushings. All gears are in constant mesh and have spur-type teeth.

The RT-8608-L, RT-11609A, RTX-11609-B/R, RTX-13609-B/R, RT-12609A, 
RTX-12609-B/R, RT-13609-A, RT-14609A and RTX-14609-B/R series transmissions 
have nine forward speeds and two reverse speeds consisting of a five-speed 
front section and a two-speed auxiliary section.

[FIGURE: C11084C.gif]

In operation the transmission transfers torque from the engine to the 
driveshaft throughout the following route.

================================================================================

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow, Front Section

 NOTE: These numbered steps correspond to the numbers on the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

Splines of input shaft engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to mating countershaft 
gears of engaged mainshaft gear.

Internal clutching teeth in hub of engaged mainshaft gear transfers 
torque to mainshaft through sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow, Auxiliary Section

 Low Range 

 NOTE: These numbered steps correspond to the numbers on the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

Splines of input shaft engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to mating countershaft 
gears of engaged mainshaft gear.

Internal clutching teeth in hub of engaged mainshaft gear transfers 
torque to mainshaft through sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged low range gear 
on range mainshaft or output shaft.

Torque is transferred to range mainshaft or output shaft through 
sliding clutch.

Torque is delivered to driveline as LOW RANGE 1st.

 High Range 

These numbered steps correspond to the numbers on the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

Splines of input shaft engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to mating countershaft 
gears of engaged mainshaft gear.

Internal clutching teeth in hub of engaged mainshaft gear transfers 
torque to mainshaft through sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear transfers torque directly to the range 
mainshaft or output shaft through engaged sliding clutch.

Torque is delivered through range mainshaft or output shaft to 
driveline as HIGH RANGE 5th.

 Underdrive/Overdrive 

 NOTE: These numbered steps correspond to the numbers on the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the vehicle's engine is transferred to the 
transmission input shaft.

Splines of input shaft engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to mating countershaft 
gears of engaged mainshaft gear.

Internal clutching teeth in hub of engaged mainshaft gear transfers 
torque to mainshaft through sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both auxiliary countershafts to mating 
countershaft gears of engaged underdrive or overdrive splitter gear on output 
shaft.

Torque is transferred to output shaft through sliding clutch.

Output shaft delivers torque to driveline as 5th UNDERDRIVE or OVERDRIVE.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

Proper lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program. If the oil is not doing its job, or if the oil level is 
ignored, all the maintenance procedures in the world are not going to keep the 
transmission running or ensure long transmission life.

Eaton Fuller transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in an oil circulating bath by the motion of the gears and shafts.

All parts are amply lubricated if these procedures are closely followed:

Maintain oil level. Inspect regularly.

Change oil regularly.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 CAUTION: The use of mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil is not 
recommended, but if these gear oils are used, be sure to adhere to the 
following limitations. 

 CAUTION: Do not use mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil when operating 
temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). Many 
of these gear oils, particularly 85W140, break down above 110°
C (230°F) and coat seals, bearings, and gears with deposits 
that can cause premature failures. If these deposits are observed (especially 
a coating on seal areas causing oil leakage), change to Eaton Roadranger®
 CD50 transmission fluid, heavy-duty engine oil or mineral 
gear oil to ensure maximum component life and to maintain your warranty with 
Eaton. Refer to Section 07-02 . 

Additives and friction modifiers are not recommended for use in Eaton 
Fuller transmissions.

First 30 hours

Change transmission lubricant on new units.

Every 40 hours

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission lubricant where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission lubricant. (Normal off-highway use.)

 Proper Oil Level 

Make sure oil is level with the filler opening. Because you can reach 
oil with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level (an oil level of 25 
mm [one inch] is about 3.7 liters [one 
gallon] of oil).

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Draining Oil 

Drain transmission while oil is warm. To drain oil remove the drain 
plug at case bottom. Clean the drain plug before reinstalling.

 Refilling 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. 

Clean case around filler plug and remove plug from case side. Fill the 
transmission to the level of the filler opening. If the transmission has two 
filler openings, fill to the level of both openings.

The exact amount of oil depends on the transmission inclination and 
model. Do not overfill — this causes oil to be forced out of 
the case through the front bearing cover.

 Proper Lubrication Levels as Related to Transmission 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication can occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

The chart below illustrates the safe percent of upgrade on which the 
transmission can be used with various chassis mounting angles. For example: if 
you have a four-degree transmission mounting angle, then eight degrees (or 14 
percent of grade) is equal to the limit of 12 degrees. If you have a 
zero-degree mounting angle, the transmission can be operated on a 12-degree 
(21 percent) grade.

Anytime the transmission operating angle or 12 degrees is exceeded for 
an extended period of time the transmission should be equipped with an oil 
pump or cooler kit to make sure transmission is properly lubricated.

Note on the chart the effect low oil levels can have on safe operating 
angles. Allowing the oil level to fall one half inch below the filler plug 
hole reduces the degree of grade by approximately three degrees (5.5 percent). 
Proper lubrication levels are essential.

[FIGURE: C11746A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Shift Bar Housing

 Removal 

Remove the capscrews from the shift bar housing. Jar the housing to 
break the gasket seal and lift the housing up and off.

[FIGURE: C95691A.gif]

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: For models equipped with an oil pump or cooler assemblies, make sure to 
disconnect the lube line at fitting on shift bar housing prior to proceeding 
with the following instructions.

 Shift Bar Housing 

[FIGURE: C11079B.gif]

7230

Shift Yoke, Second-Third

Tilt the assembly and remove the three sets of tension springs and 
balls from the housing bores.

[FIGURE: C99271A.gif]

 NOTE: When removing the shift bars, start with the upper shift bar. Move all 
the bars to the right and out the rear boss bore. Cut the lockwire and remove 
the lock screws from each bar just before their removal.

Place the housing in a vise with the plunger-side up. Cut the lockwire, 
remove the capscrews and the oil trough, if so equipped, from the housing.

Move the fourth-fifth speed yoke bar to the shift bar housing rear, 
remove the shift yoke and shift block from the yoke bar.

[FIGURE: D9940A.gif]

Move the second-third speed yoke bar to the shift bar housing rear. 
Remove the shift yoke and shift block from the yoke bar. As the neutral notch 
in the shift bar clears the rear boss, remove the small interlock pin from the 
notch bar.

[FIGURE: D9941A.gif]

Remove the actuating plunger from the center boss bore.

[FIGURE: D9942A.gif]

Move the short first-reverse speed yoke bar to the shift bar housing 
rear. Remove the shift yoke from the yoke bar. As the yoke bar is removed from 
the shift bar housing, two interlock balls will drop from the rear boss bottom 
bore.

[FIGURE: D9943A.gif]

If necessary, remove the plug, spring and reverse-stop plunger from the 
first-reverse speed shift yoke bore.

[FIGURE: D9944A.gif]

 Assembly 

If previously removed, install the reverse-stop plunger in 
first-reverse shift yoke. Make sure the plunger is fully seated in the yoke 
slot bore.

[FIGURE: D9945A.gif]

Install the spring in the yoke bore and on the plunger shank.

[FIGURE: D9946A.gif]

Install the plug and tighten to compress the spring. Back the plug out 
one and one-half turns and stake plug through the small hole in the yoke.

 NOTE: Start with the lower shift bore of the rear boss and move to the left 
(front of the housing). Keep bars in the neutral position during installation. 
Do not exceed the recommended torque ratings for the yoke lock screws as 
overtightening can distort the yoke bars.

Secure the shift bar housing in a vise. Hold the notched-end of the 
short first-reverse speed yoke bar. Install the bar in the lower bore of the 
shift bar housing bosses. Position the yoke on the bar between the bosses. 
Install the yoke lock screw, tighten, and wire securely.

[FIGURE: D9947A.gif]

Install the actuating plunger in the center bore.

[FIGURE: C99411A.gif]

Install one interlock ball in the rear top bore.

[FIGURE: C99401A.gif]

 NOTE: The interlock pin must remain in a vertical position during reassembly 
as rotation of the bar causes the pin to jam in the tension spring bores.

While holding the notched-end of the bar, install the second-third 
speed shift bar in the housing boss middle bore. Position the shift block on 
the bar between the center and the rear bosses and the yoke on the bar between 
the front and center bosses, the long hub to the front of the housing. Just 
before inserting the notched end of the rear boss bar, install the small 
interlock pin vertically in the neutral notch bore. Install the block and yoke 
lock screws, tighten screws and lockwire securely. Install actuating plunger 
in center boss bore.

[FIGURE: D9948A.gif]

Install the second interlock ball in the rear top bore.

While holding notched end of the bar, install the fourth-fifth speed 
yoke bar in the housing boss upper bore. Position the shift block on the bar 
between the center and the rear bosses and the shift yoke on the bar between 
the front and center bosses, long hub to the rear of housing. Install the 
shift block and yoke bar lock screws. Tighten and wire securely.

[FIGURE: D9949A.gif]

For models so equipped, install the oil trough on the housing. Tighten 
the capscrews and lockwire securely.

Remove the assembly from the vise. Install the three tension balls, one 
in each bore on the housing top.

Install the three tension springs, one over each ball in the housing 
bores.

[FIGURE: D9950A.gif]

 Installation 

Make sure the shift bars are in the neutral position.

[FIGURE: C95701A.gif]

Place the sliding clutches on the mainshaft in the neutral position. 
Install a new shift bar housing gasket in position on the case.

[FIGURE: C95711A.gif]

 NOTE: Avoid tilting the assembly during installation as the three sets of 
tension springs and balls are free to be released from bores in top of housing.

Install the shifting bar housing on transmission, fitting yokes into 
slots of corresponding clutch gears.

[FIGURE: C95721A.gif]

Install the retaining capscrews. Tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C95731A.gif]

Capscrew

 Removal 

Lock the transmission by engaging two gears with the mainshaft sliding 
clutches.

[FIGURE: C95591A.gif]

Use a large breaker bar to turn output shaft nut from the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C95601A.gif]

Pull the companion flange or yoke from splines of output shaft.

[FIGURE: C95611A.gif]

 NOTE: Temporarily reinstall output shaft nut to protect the threads during 
auxiliary removal.

Remove the speedometer drive gear from hub of flange or yoke or from 
the inside rear bearing cover remaining on output shaft. For some models it is 
necessary to remove the snap ring in groove of output shaft prior to removal 
of the speedometer gear.

[FIGURE: C95621A.gif]

Remove the capscrews retaining the auxiliary section to the 
transmission. Insert three puller screws in the tapped holes of housing flange.

[FIGURE: C95631A.gif]

Tighten puller screws evenly to move auxiliary section to the rear and 
just far enough from front section to break gasket seal.

[FIGURE: C95641A.gif]

Attach lifting eye to auxiliary section and attach a hoist into 
position before sliding auxiliary section completely off dowels. Remove the 
gasket from the front section.

For models so equipped, remove the clutch release mechanism.

Remove the four capscrews, six nuts and lockwashers from studs securing 
the clutch housing to transmission case.

Jar the clutch housing with a rubber mallet to break gasket seal and 
pull from transmission case. Remove the gasket.

 Installation 

Position the new gasket on housing mounting surface and install the 
clutch housing on front case, piloting on the six studs and drive gear bearing 
cover.

[FIGURE: C95651A.gif]

Install the six nuts with washers or lockwashers and tighten to 244-258 Nm
 (180-190 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C10938A.gif]

Install the four capscrews with lockwashers and tighten to 122-135 Nm
 (90-100 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C10939A.gif]

Install clutch release mechanism, if so equipped.

 NOTE: When installing a low-low auxiliary, the deep reduction clutch must be 
moved to the rear, engaging the deep reduction gear.

Install a new auxiliary mating surface gasket. Lower the auxiliary 
section into position with a hoist and align on the dowel pins.

[FIGURE: C95661A.gif]

Slide the auxiliary part way onto the dowels and remove the lifting eye.

Slide the auxiliary the rest of the way into position. Assembly will be 
easier if the input shaft is slowly rotated during installation.

 NOTE: Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 (Type II) to capscrews.

Fasten the auxiliary to the front section, drawing the capscrews down 
evenly. Tighten the capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C95671A.gif]

Install speedometer rotor on hub of flange or yoke or on the inside 
rear bearing cover on output shaft.

Install snap ring, if so equipped.

Lock the transmission by engaging two gears with the mainshaft sliding 
clutches. Slide the companion flange or yoke onto the output shaft. Install 
the output shaft nut and washer. Tighten the nut to 610-678 Nm
 (450-500 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C95681A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Input Shaft

 Special Procedure for Changing Input Shaft 

 NOTE: Some cases of service can require replacement of the input shaft 
because of clutch wear on the splines. In these instances the input shaft can 
be removed without disassembling the transmission other than removing the 
shifting bar housing. Removal of the clutch housing is optional.

 NOTE: The following instructions are only for changing the input shaft. To 
change the drive gear, complete disassembly of the front section is required.

 Input Shaft 

[FIGURE: C11766A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

7051

Gasket

2

7030

Snap Ring

3

7025

Bearing

4

7064

Snap Ring

5

7005

Case

6

7120

Bushing

7

7017

Input Shaft

8

7158

Drive Gear

9

7A059

Spacer

10

7050

Front Bearing Cover (Pull-Type)

 Removal 

Remove the shift lever housing from shift bar housing, if necessary, 
and the shift bar housing assembly from transmission case. Refer to Shift Bar 
Housing in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

[FIGURE: C95751A.gif]

Remove the retaining capscrews, front bearing cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C97011A.gif]

Remove the bearing nut (left-hand threads). Engagement of two mainshaft 
sliding clutches into gear will prevent the input shaft from rotating and 
assist nut removal. This procedure is for nut removal only.

[FIGURE: C97021A.gif]

Drive the input shaft as far forward as possible.

[FIGURE: C97031A.gif]

Tap the input shaft down to tilt the input shaft bearing in its bore.

[FIGURE: C97041A.gif]

 NOTE: If this procedure does not free the bearing in its bore, repeat Steps 4 
through 6.

Drive the input shaft back through the bearing and into the case as far 
as possible. Drive the shaft forward again to free the input shaft bearing 
from the bore in the case.

[FIGURE: C97051A.gif]

Pry the bearing from the input shaft with two large screwdrivers.

[FIGURE: C97061A.gif]

Remove spacer from input shaft.

From the front of transmission, remove the snap ring from inside 
diameter of main drive gear using two small screwdrivers. If mainshaft was 
previously locked in two gears it may be necessary to place sliding clutches 
in the neutral position to rotate input shaft and mainshaft for removal of 
snap ring.

Pull the input shaft forward from the splines of the drive gear.

[FIGURE: C97071A.gif]

 Installation 

Replace bushing in pocket of input shaft if necessary.

Install new input shaft into splines of main drive gear just far enough 
to expose snap ring groove in the inside diameter of the drive gear.

Install snap ring in groove of drive gear.

[FIGURE: C97081A.gif]

Install spacer on input shaft.

[FIGURE: C97091A.gif]

Move the clutch gear forward to contact end of input shaft in hub of 
drive gear. Block between rear of sliding clutch and front of the overdrive 
gear. When installing bearing, this will hold input shaft in position to seat 
the bearing properly.

[FIGURE: C97101A.gif]

Using a bearing driver, install the bearing on shaft and into case 
bore. When applying force to driver, use caution to prevent damage to the 
bearing shield. Remove blocking from the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C97111A.gif]

Apply Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSK-M2G349-A1 to the cleaned threads of input shaft and nut, 
using caution to prevent bearing contamination with sealant.

 CAUTION: Do not reuse old nut in this procedure. 

Engage two mainshaft sliding clutches into gear to prevent the 
mainshaft from rotating and install the new bearing nut (left hand threads), 
on input shaft. Tighten nut to 339-407 Nm (250-300 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C97121A.gif]

With a punch and maul, peen the nut into the two milled slots of input 
shaft. Use caution to prevent distorting the outside diameter of nut.

[FIGURE: C97131A.gif]

To facilitate proper reinstallation of the shift bar housing assembly 
on case, make sure mainshaft sliding clutches are placed in the neutral 
position.

Reinstall the shift bar housing, the front bearing cover and shift 
lever housing if removed, making sure to replace gaskets. Refer to Shift Bar Housing 
 in Removal and Installation portion of this section.

[FIGURE: C97141A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Auxiliary Countershaft Disassembly

 Countershaft Rear Bearings 

[FIGURE: C11086A.gif]

 Removal 

Remove countershaft rear bearing covers and gaskets.

[FIGURE: C10940A.gif]

Remove the snap ring from the groove at rear of each countershaft.

[FIGURE: C97661A.gif]

 CAUTION: Support the countershafts from the gear side to prevent them from 
dropping. 

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershafts forward far enough 
to partially unseat rear bearings.

[FIGURE: C97701A.gif]

Using caution so as not to damage the bearing inner race on front of 
each countershaft, drive the shafts to the rear to expose the bearing snap 
rings.

[FIGURE: C11087A.gif]

 NOTE: The auxiliary countershaft assembly cannot be removed from housing 
until splitter shift yoke is removed.

Use a puller to remove the countershaft rear bearings from housing bores.

 Installation 

 NOTE: The splitter gear set must remain in time during the installation of 
rear bearings.

 NOTE: Check the synchronizer assembly for springs that may have been released 
from bores in high range ring during bearing installation.

Center the rear of either countershaft assembly in bearing bore and use 
a soft bar to start rear bearing in bore. Complete installation with a 
flanged-end bearing driver and maul. Repeat the procedure with other auxiliary 
countershaft assembly. Make sure the splitter gear set has remained in time.

[FIGURE: C11058A.gif]

Install the snap ring in groove at rear of each countershaft.

[FIGURE: C97661A.gif]

Position the corresponding new gasket on cover mounting surface and 
install both rear bearing covers. Tighten capscrews to secure covers to 
auxiliary housing.

[FIGURE: C11059A.gif]

 Auxiliary Countershaft Assemblies 

If previously removed, install the bearing inner race on front of each 
countershaft.

On the low range gear of each auxiliary countershaft assembly, use a 
highly visible color of toolmaker's dye to mark the tooth stamped with an O 
for timing purposes.

 NOTE: Check synchronizer assembly for springs that may have been released 
from bores in high range ring during bearing installation.

Place one of the assemblies into position in the rear plate, meshing 
the marked tooth of countershaft low range gear with either set of two marked 
teeth of low range gear on output shaft (inset). Center rear of countershaft 
in bearing bore, start rear bearing in bore and complete installation with a 
flanged-end driver and maul. Repeat the procedure with other auxiliary 
countershaft assembly, making sure the low range gear set remains in time 
during bearing installation.

[FIGURE: C11058A.gif]

Install the snap ring in groove at rear of each countershaft.

[FIGURE: C11772A.gif]

Position the corresponding new gasket on cover mounting surface and 
install both rear bearing covers. Tighten capscrews to secure covers to 
auxiliary plate.

 Removal 

Secure the auxiliary section housing in a vise. Remove the range 
cylinder cover capscrews and remove the cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: D9841A.gif]

Remove the nut from the end of the yoke bar.

[FIGURE: C97181A.gif]

Cut the lockwire and remove two yoke lock screws.

[FIGURE: C97191A.gif]

Pull yoke bar from the cylinder housing bore.

[FIGURE: C97221A.gif]

Remove range yoke from sliding clutch of synchronizer assembly.

[FIGURE: C97211A.gif]

Remove the range piston from cylinder bore. If necessary remove the 
O-rings from piston inside diameter and outside diameter (inset).

[FIGURE: C10947A.gif]

Remove the capscrews and the range cylinder housing and gasket. If 
necessary, remove the small O-ring from groove in housing bore (inset).

[FIGURE: C10948A.gif]

 Installation 

If previously removed, lubricate the O-ring with Silicone Lubricant 
COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A and install 
in the small bore of the range cylinder housing.

[FIGURE: C11060A.gif]

 NOTE: The air port should be located in the 10 o'clock position.

 NOTE: Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 (Type II) to bolts.

Bolt the cylinder housing into place using a new gasket. Tighten bolts 
to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C97571A.gif]

Place the range yoke into position with sliding clutch of synchronizer 
assembly, long hub of yoke to the front. Insert threaded-end of yoke bar 
through yoke and into bore of range cylinder housing, aligning the notches in 
bar with yoke lock screw holes.

[FIGURE: C97581A.gif]

Install the yoke capscrews with safety wire.

[FIGURE: C97591A.gif]

If previously removed install O-rings on the outside diameter and 
inside diameter of piston and apply a light coat of Silicone Lubricant 
COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A. Install 
the piston with the flat side to the rear.

[FIGURE: C97601A.gif]

Install a new locknut on the yoke bar to secure the piston. Tighten nut 
to 95-115 Nm (70-85 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C97611A.gif]

 NOTE: Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 (Type II) to capscrew 
threads.

Install the cylinder cover using a new gasket. Tighten capscrews to 
47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C97621A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Synchronizer Assembly, Mainshaft Assembly and Range Air Cylinder

 Removal 

Slide the synchronizer assembly off the mainshaft.

Drive the output shaft assembly out using a soft bar and maul. Support 
front of shaft to avoid damaging the mainshaft quill once output shaft is free 
of bearing assembly.

[FIGURE: C97261A.gif]

Remove the bearing inner spacer from output shaft.

[FIGURE: C97331A.gif]

 CAUTION: Support the mainshaft from below so it does not drop and sustain damage 
during the pressing operation. 

Using the front face of low range gear as a base, press the output 
shaft through the gear and bearing. Remove the bearing and washer from hub of 
low range gear.

[FIGURE: C97341A.gif]

If necessary, remove the snap ring from low range gear of models so 
equipped.

[FIGURE: D9836A.gif]

Remove the rear bearing cover and gasket. The rear bearing cone will 
drop from bore in auxiliary plate when cover is removed. If necessary, remove 
the oil seal from cover.

[FIGURE: C97271A.gif]

Remove the two bearing cups and outer spacer from bore in auxiliary 
plate.

[FIGURE: C97881A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Synchronizer

[FIGURE: C97361A.gif]

 Disassembly 

 CAUTION: There are three springs which will be released as the high range 
synchronizer is removed from the pins. Cover the assembly with a rag to 
prevent losing springs. 

Pull upward to remove the high range synchronizer from pins.

[FIGURE: C97371A.gif]

Remove the sliding clutch from low range synchronizer pins.

[FIGURE: C97381A.gif]

 Assembly 

Place the larger low range synchronizer face down on the bench with 
pins up. Install the sliding clutch (recessed side up) down over the pins on 
the synchronizer. Install the three springs into their bores.

[FIGURE: C97391A.gif]

Position the high range synchronizer ring so that the springs contact 
the side of the low speed synchronizer pins. Seat the ring by pushing down and 
twisting counterclockwise to compress springs.

[FIGURE: C97401A.gif]

Install the synchronizer assembly on splines of output shaft, low range 
ring in recess of low range gear.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Auxiliary Drive Gear 

 Removal 

Remove the snap ring from groove at rear of mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C9831C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

7064

Snap Ring

2

7065

Bearing

3

Retainer

4

7A079

Auxiliary Drive Gear

5

6

42998-S

Capscrew

[FIGURE: C101081A.gif]

Cut lockwire and remove the capscrews from bearing retainer ring.

[FIGURE: C11063A.gif]

Insert three puller screws in the specially tapped holes of retainer 
ring. Tighten screws evenly to pull the auxiliary drive gear assembly from 
case bore.

[FIGURE: C11064A.gif]

 Disassembly 

Using the rear face of retainer ring as a base, press the drive gear 
through bearing.

[FIGURE: C98351A.gif]

If necessary, remove the O-rings from hub outside diameter of auxiliary 
drive gear.

[FIGURE: C11065A.gif]

Remove the snap ring from hub of auxiliary drive gear.

[FIGURE: C11066A.gif]

 Assembly 

If previously removed, install the O-rings on extended front hub of 
auxiliary drive gear.

Install the retainer ring on auxiliary drive gear, snap ring groove 
facing front hub and away from gear teeth.

[FIGURE: D9859A.gif]

Start the auxiliary drive gear bearing on front hub, bearing snap ring 
facing groove in retainer ring. Using both the inner and outer race of bearing 
as a base, press the bearing on gear with snap ring in groove of retainer ring 
or use a bearing driver.

[FIGURE: D9860A.gif]

Install the snap ring in gear hub groove to retain the bearing.

[FIGURE: D9861A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Input Shaft and Drive Gear Nut, Removal

Remove the four capscrews retaining the front bearing cover. Remove the 
bearing cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C101021A.gif]

If necessary, remove the oil seal from cover of models so equipped.

[FIGURE: C11061A.gif]

Lock the transmission by engaging the two mainshaft gears with the 
mainshaft sliding clutches. Remove nut (left-hand thread) with drive gear nut 
removing tool.

[FIGURE: C11062A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Reverse Idler Gear

 Removal 

Move the mainshaft reverse gear as far to the rear as possible and 
remove the snap ring from ID of gear.

[FIGURE: C4620B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

377850-S

Nut

2

7482

Washer

3

7B369

7140

7

Idler Plate

7728

Thrust Washer

Move the reverse gear forward and against the first speed gear, 
engaging the splines of mainshaft sliding clutch.

Using inside jaw pullers or impact puller, remove the auxiliary 
countershaft front bearing from left reverse idler gear bore. If necessary, 
repeat the procedure for removing the auxiliary countershaft front bearing 
from right reverse idler gear bore.

Remove the stop nut and washer from the idler shaft front.

[FIGURE: D9865A.gif]

Remove the pipe plug from the idler shaft rear.

As the idler shaft and the retainer washer are moved to the rear, 
remove the thrust washer and gear from the case. If necessary, remove the 
inner race from bearing bore and press the needle bearing from the idler gear.

[FIGURE: D9866A.gif]

 Installation 

If any of the magnets in the bottom of the case were damaged during 
disassembly, chip them out and glue new magnets into place using Gasket and 
Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESR-M11P17-A and ESE-M2G52-A.

If previously removed, thread pipe plug in rear of reverse idler shaft 
and tighten. Install the washer on shaft, flat side to the front (inset).

[FIGURE: C11074A.gif]

If removed, press the needle bearing in reverse idler gear bore.

[FIGURE: D9916A.gif]

Install the bearing inner race on idler shaft and insert shaft into 
case bore, threaded-end of shaft to the front. As the idler shaft is moved 
forward, install the reverse idler gear on shaft, long hub to the front and 
seating on bearing inner race. Position the thrust washer on shaft between the 
gear and support boss in case. Continue with movement of idler shaft forward 
into bore of support boss.

[FIGURE: D9917A.gif]

Make sure the idler shaft is seated in the bore of the support boss as 
far forward as possible.

Install the washer and the stop nut on front of the idler shaft. 
Tighten the nut to 67-81 Nm (50-60 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: D9918A.gif]

 NOTE: The bearing inner race is installed on the auxiliary countershaft front 
and never with the outer race.

Install the outer race of the auxiliary countershaft front bearing with 
a driver into the transmission case bore and against the retaining washer.

[FIGURE: D9920A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Countershaft Bearings, Removal

 NOTE: The front and rear countershaft bearings are removed in the following 
procedure. However, for removal of the mainshaft, remove the right 
countershaft bearings only.

Remove the snap ring from groove at rear of each countershaft.

[FIGURE: C11069A.gif]

 NOTE: This step will damage the bearings and should not be attempted unless 
replacement of the bearings is planned.

From inside the case, use a soft punch and maul to drive the 
countershaft rear bearings to the rear and from case bores.

[FIGURE: D9867A.gif]

Remove the capscrew and the front bearing retainer plate from the 
countershaft.

[FIGURE: C11070A.gif]

 NOTE: The soft bar used should have a flattened end that is large enough so 
as not to damage holes for the roll pin and capscrew.

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft to the rear as far as 
possible. This partially underseats the front bearing.

[FIGURE: D9868A.gif]

From the rear of case, use a soft bar and maul to drive each 
countershaft forward to unseat the front bearings from case bores and expose 
the bearing snap rings.

[FIGURE: C11071A.gif]

 NOTE: The bearing inner race remains pressed on the countershaft.

Use a bearing puller or pry bars to remove the countershaft front 
bearing.

Block the right countershaft assembly against case wall and pull the 
mainshaft assembly to the rear to free pilot from pocket of input shaft. Tilt 
front of mainshaft up and lift the assembly from case (inset). Use caution as 
the reverse gear is free and can fall from shaft.

[FIGURE: C98481A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mainshaft

 Mainshaft Assembly 

[FIGURE: D9869B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

7B341

Sliding Clutch

2

7173

7064

Reverse

7

Splined Mainshaft

10

7100

Second

11

7158

Third

12

7B340

Fourth (RT), Overdrive (RTO)

 Removal 

Block the right countershaft assembly against case wall and pull the 
mainshaft assembly to the rear to free pilot from pocket of input shaft. Tilt 
front of mainshaft up and lift the assembly from case (inset). Use caution as 
the reverse gear is free and can fall from shaft.

[FIGURE: D9902A.gif]

Remove the fourth-fifth speed sliding clutch from front of mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C98661A.gif]

Remove the snap ring from groove at rear of mainshaft.

[FIGURE: D9870A.gif]

Remove the reverse gear and spacer from rear of mainshaft.

[FIGURE: D9871A.gif]

 NOTE: When removing limit washers, spacers and gears note their location on 
mainshaft to facilitate reassembly. Keep the internal-splined washers and 
external-splined spacers with the gear from which they were removed. There is 
only one limit washer and one spacer belonging to each gear.

From rear of mainshaft pull the key from mainshaft keyway.

[FIGURE: C98691A.gif]

Turn the reverse gear limit washer to align its splines with those of 
the mainshaft and remove washer.

[FIGURE: D9872A.gif]

Remove the first-reverse speed sliding clutch from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: D9873A.gif]

Using a small screwdriver, turn the limit washer in hub of first speed 
gear to align its splines with those of the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: D9874A.gif]

Pull the first speed gear from rear of mainshaft to remove limit 
washer, spacer and gear. If necessary, remove the snap ring from the inside 
diameter of gear.

[FIGURE: D9875A.gif]

Remove each remaining gear, limit washer, spacer, and sliding clutch 
from mainshaft. If necessary, remove the snap ring from the inside diameter of 
each gear.

[FIGURE: D9876A.gif]

 Assembly 

If previously removed, install the corresponding snap rings in inside 
diameter of mainshaft gears.

Secure the mainshaft in a vise equipped with brass jaws or wood blocks, 
pilot-end of the shaft down. If removed, install the roll pin in the keyway.

[FIGURE: D9877A.gif]

Install the third speed gear limit washer on mainshaft, flat side of 
washer up. Rotate washer in the first or bottom groove of mainshaft to align 
the splines of washer with those of the mainshaft. Install the key in 
mainshaft keyway to lock washer in place.

Install the spacer on the shaft against the washer.

[FIGURE: D9878A.gif]

Install the third speed (or overdrive) gear limit washer on the 
mainshaft, flat side of washer up. Rotate washer in the first or bottom groove 
of the mainshaft to align the splines of the washer with those of the 
mainshaft. Install the key in the mainshaft keyway to lock washer in place.

Install the spacer on shaft against washer.

 NOTE: Gear tolerance washers are internally splined and locked to the 
mainshaft by the key. Gear spacers are externally splined to engage with 
clutching teeth in the gear hubs. There is one tolerance washer and one spacer 
for each gear in the mainshaft assembly.

Install the fourth speed (or overdrive) gear on mainshaft, clutching 
teeth down and engaged with external splines of spacer.

[FIGURE: D9879A.gif]

Install the second speed gear on the shaft against the overdrive (or 
third) gear, clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: D9880A.gif]

Install the spacer in second speed gear, engaging the external splines 
of spacer with clutching teeth of the gear.

[FIGURE: D9881A.gif]

Remove the key from the keyway and install the second speed gear 
tolerance washer on the mainshaft, flat side of the washer down and against 
the spacer. Rotate the washer in the second groove of the mainshaft to align 
the splines of the washer with those of the mainshaft and reinsert the key in 
the keyway to lock the washer in place.

[FIGURE: D9882A.gif]

Insert two large screwdrivers between the second and overdrive (or 
third) gears to check axial clearances. Apply slight downward pressure on the 
screwdriver handles to spread the gears evenly. Make sure the gear hubs are 
parallel. Insert a feeler gauge between the hubs. Correct axial clearance 
should be from 0.152-0.381 mm (0.006-0.015 inch). If the clearance is less 
than the minimum 0.152 mm (0.006 inch) tolerance, the tolerance washer in the 
second speed gear should be replaced by a thinner tolerance washer. This 
increases the axial clearance between the gears. If the clearance checked is 
greater than the maximum 0.381 mm (0.012 inch) tolerance, a thicker tolerance 
washer should be installed in the second speed gear. This would decrease the 
axial clearance between the gears.

[FIGURE: D9883A.gif]

Install the first-second speed sliding clutch, aligning the missing 
internal spline of the sliding clutch with the key in the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: D9884A.gif]

Remove the key from the keyway. Install the first speed gear tolerance 
washer on the mainshaft, flat side of the washer up. Rotate the washer in the 
second groove of the mainshaft to align the splines of the washer with those 
of the mainshaft, and reinsert the key in the keyway to lock the washer in 
place.

Washers are available in the following thicknesses to obtain the 
correct limits.

6.30-6.35 mm (0.248-0.250 inch)

6.43-6.48 mm (0.253-0.255 inch)

6.55-6.60 mm (0.258-0.260 inch)

6.68-6.73 mm (0.263-0.265 inch)

6.81-6.86 mm (0.268-0.270 inch)

6.93-6.98 mm (0.273-0.275 inch)

[FIGURE: D9885A.gif]

Install the spacer on the shaft against the washer.

[FIGURE: D9886A.gif]

Install the first speed gear on the mainshaft, clutching teeth down and 
engaged with external splines of the spacer.

[FIGURE: D9887A.gif]

Install the low speed gear on the shaft against first speed gear, 
clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: D9888A.gif]

Install the spacer in low speed gear, engaging the external splines of 
the spacer with clutching teeth of gear.

[FIGURE: D9889A.gif]

Remove the key from the keyway. Install the low speed gear tolerance 
washer on the mainshaft, flat side of the washer down and against the spacer. 
Rotate the washer in the fourth groove of the mainshaft to align the splines 
of the washer with those of the mainshaft and insert the key in the keyway to 
lock washer in place.

[FIGURE: D9890A.gif]

Check the axial clearance between low and first speed gears and adjust 
as required. Refer to Step 11 for this procedure.

[FIGURE: D9891A.gif]

Install the first and reverse speed sliding clutch, aligning the 
missing internal spline of sliding clutch with the key in the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: D9892A.gif]

Remove the key from the keyway and install the reverse gear tolerance 
washer on the mainshaft, flat side of washer up. Rotate washer in the fifth 
groove of the mainshaft to align the splines of the washer with those of the 
mainshaft and insert key in the keyway to lock the washer in place.

[FIGURE: D9893A.gif]

Install the spacer on the shaft against the washer.

[FIGURE: D9894A.gif]

Install the snap ring in the mainshaft groove to retain key in the 
keyway.

[FIGURE: D9897A.gif]

Install the snap ring on reverse hub only to check axial clearance 
limits.

[FIGURE: D9896A.gif]

Install the reverse gear on the mainshaft, clutching teeth down and 
engaged with the spacer external splines.

[FIGURE: D9895A.gif]

Install the auxiliary drive gear assembly in its proper position on the 
rear of the mainshaft. Install the auxiliary retaining snap ring in the 
mainshaft snap ring groove.

[FIGURE: D9898A.gif]

 NOTE: This check is made without spreading the gears with screwdrivers.

Force both the reverse gear and auxiliary drive gear downward on the 
shaft to flatten their respective snap rings. Making sure the gear hubs are 
parallel, insert a feeler gauge between the reverse gear and auxiliary drive 
gear hubs. Correct axial clearance should be from 0.152-0.381 mm (0.006-0.015 
inch). If clearance is less than the minimum 0.152 mm (0.006 inch) tolerance, 
the reverse gear limit washer should be replaced by a thinner limit washer. 
This will increase the axial clearance between the gears. If the clearance 
checked is greater than the maximum 0.381 mm (0.015 inch) tolerance, a thicker 
limit washer should be installed in the reverse gear. This would decrease the 
axial clearance between the gears.

[FIGURE: D9899A.gif]

With the proper reverse gear limit washer installed on the mainshaft, 
remove the auxiliary drive gear assembly and reverse gear.

 NOTE: Do not replace the reverse gear internal snap ring at this time.

Install the reverse gear on the mainshaft. Engage the gear clutching 
teeth with the spacer splines and sliding clutch. Move the reverse gear 
against the low speed gear.

[FIGURE: D9900A.gif]

Remove the mainshaft assembly from the vise. Align the missing internal 
spline of third-fourth speed sliding clutch with key in the mainshaft and 
install on the shaft front, engaging the external splines of the sliding 
clutch with the clutching teeth of the fourth speed (or overdrive) gear.

[FIGURE: D9901A.gif]

Block the right countershaft assembly against the transmission case 
wall and lower the mainshaft assembly into position with the reverse gear held 
against the low speed gear and the shaft rear moved into the transmission case 
bore.

[FIGURE: D9902A.gif]

Move the pilot-end of the mainshaft into the input shaft pocket bushing.

With the reverse gear remaining against low speed gear, mesh the 
corresponding forward speed gears of the left countershaft assembly. Check to 
make sure that the marked tooth on the left countershaft drive gear has 
remained in mesh with the marked set of teeth on the main drive gear.

Center rear of mainshaft in case bore and install the auxiliary drive 
gear assembly on shaft, partially seating the bearing in bore. Do not complete 
installation at this time.

Main Drive Gear

 Removal 

Remove the input shaft bearing retaining snap ring from the input shaft 
groove.

[FIGURE: D9903B.gif]

Item

Part Number

1

[FIGURE: D9904A.gif]

Drive the input shaft back through bearing with a soft bar and maul. 
Remove input shaft from case.

Move upper countershaft to right and remove drive gear and spacer from 
case. Remove the snap ring from drive gear.

[FIGURE: D9906A.gif]

Drive the input shaft bearing out the front of case.

[FIGURE: C11072A.gif]

Check the bushing in pocket of input shaft and replace if worn or

[FIGURE: C11073A.gif]

 Installation 

If removed, install the snap ring in the main drive gear inside diameter.

teeth on the drive gear and repeat the procedure for the two adjacent teeth 
directly opposite the first set marked. Use a highly visible color of 
toolmaker's dye to make the timing marks.

[FIGURE: D9925A.gif]

Mesh the marked tooth of the left countershaft drive gear with either 
set of the two marked teeth on the main drive gear. Slide the input shaft 
through the main drive gear.

[FIGURE: D9926A.gif]

Install the drive gear spacer and the bearing on the input shaft with 
the external snap ring to the outside.

[FIGURE: D9927A.gif]

Install the drive gear bearing on the input shaft, seat bearing into 
case bore with the proper bearing driver.

[FIGURE: D9928A.gif]

Temporarily install the front bearing cover.

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the input shaft through the bearing. 
Remove the front bearing cover.

[FIGURE: D9929A.gif]

Install the bearing retainer snap ring.

 NOTE: Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 (Type II) to capscrew 
threads.

Install the front bearing cover and gasket, and make sure to align the 
oil return hole in the case with the cover hole. Secure the front bearing 
cover on case with the six capscrews. Tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Countershaft

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: Except for the power takeoff gears, the left and right countershaft 
assemblies are identical and are disassembled in the same manner.

Move the right countershaft assembly to the rear as far as possible so 
the front of the shaft can be removed from the transmission case bore and 
moved to the center of the transmission case. Lift the assembly from the 
transmission case and repeat the procedure for the left countershaft assembly.

 Countershaft Assemblies 

[FIGURE: C11121B.gif]

Snap Ring

Remove the drive gear retaining snap ring from each countershaft front.

[FIGURE: D9908A.gif]

 CAUTION: Never use the PTO gear as a pressing base. The narrow face width of 
this gear makes it very susceptible to breakage. 

Using the rear face of third speed gear as a base, press the drive 
gear, PTO gear and fourth speed (or overdrive) gear from each countershaft 
(left). This will also remove the front bearing inner race from countershafts 
of models so equipped.

[FIGURE: D9909A.gif]

 NOTE: Always use caution when pressing a cluster of gears from countershaft. 
Press these gears off in a cluster of three and then in a cluster of two.

Using the rear face of first speed gear as a base, press the second 
speed and first speed gears from each countershaft.

[FIGURE: D9910A.gif]

Remove the key and roll pin from the countershaft.

[FIGURE: D9911A.gif]

Remove the right reverse idler gear assembly. Steps for removal are 
identical to the left reverse idler gear assembly removal procedure.

 Assembly 

Except for the power takeoff gears, the right and left countershaft 
assemblies are identical and are assembled in the same manner.

If removed, install the roll pin and key in the countershaft keyway.

Align keyway of gear with key in countershaft and press the second 
speed gear on shaft, long hub of gear to the front of countershaft.

[FIGURE: D9912A.gif]

Press the third speed gear on the countershaft, long gear hub against 
second speed gear hub.

Press the fourth speed (or overdrive) gear on the countershaft, long 
gear hub to countershaft front.

[FIGURE: D9913A.gif]

 NOTE: The left countershaft assembly has a 47-tooth power takeoff gear; the 
right countershaft assembly has a 45-tooth power takeoff gear.

Start the power takeoff gear onto the countershaft, bullet-nose side of 
teeth facing up and toward countershaft rear. Align the drive gear keyway with 
the countershaft key and both press gears onto the shaft with the drive gear 
long hub against the power takeoff gear.

To avoid confusion during installation, mark the end of the left 
countershaft with an L; the end of the right countershaft with an R.

[FIGURE: D9914A.gif]

Install the drive gear retaining snap ring in the countershaft front 
groove.

[FIGURE: D9908A.gif]

 NOTE: Mark the countershaft drive gear for timing purposes. On each 
countershaft drive gear, mark the tooth aligned with the gear keyway and 
stamped with an O for easy identification. Use a highly visible color of 
toolmaker's dye to make timing marks.

Use a flanged-end driver to install the bearing inner race on the 
countershaft, shoulder of race against shoulder of countershaft.

[FIGURE: D9915A.gif]

 Left Countershaft Bearing, Installation 

Place the left countershaft assembly into position in the transmission 
case. Make sure the L-marked assembly has the larger 47-tooth power takeoff 
gear.

Place the right countershaft assembly into position in the transmission 
case. Make sure the R-marked assembly has the smaller 45-tooth power takeoff 
gear.

[FIGURE: D9921A.gif]

Move the left countershaft assembly to the rear, and insert the 
countershaft support tool or blocking to center shaft in the transmission case 
rear bore.

[FIGURE: D9922A.gif]

 NOTE: The inner race of roller-type front bearing is pressed on front of 
countershaft.

Use a flanged-end bearing driver to start the bearing in case bore.

Center the front of left countershaft in bearing and move the assembly 
forward.

[FIGURE: C11075A.gif]

Use a flanged-end bearing driver to completely seat the front bearing 
or bearing outer race in the transmission case bore.

[FIGURE: D9923A.gif]

Position the retainer plate on the left countershaft front. Roll pin in 
hole at shaft end. Install the capscrew and tighten to 122-163 Nm
 (90-120 lb-ft).

Remove the countershaft support tool or blocking from the transmission 
case rear bore. Install the left countershaft rear bearing with the larger 
inside diameter chamfer to the shaft front. Install the snap ring in the left 
countershaft rear groove.

[FIGURE: D9924A.gif]

 Right Countershaft Bearing, Installation 

 NOTE: The left countershaft assembly must remain in time with the main drive 
gear when timing the right countershaft assembly.

Remove blocking from the right countershaft assembly and place it 
parallel to the mainshaft assembly. Mesh the marked tooth of the right 
countershaft drive gear with the remaining set of two marked teeth on the main 
drive gear.

Insert the countershaft support tool or blocking in the rear bearing 
bore.

[FIGURE: D9931A.gif]

Position the front countershaft bearing in front bearing bore. Use the 
proper bearing driver to set the bearing.

[FIGURE: D9932A.gif]

Install the retainer washer and capscrew. Make sure to match roll pin 
in the retainer with the inner bearing hole. Tighten the capscrew to 122-163 Nm
 (90-120 lb-ft).

Position the countershaft rear bearing in the rear bearing bore. Use 
the proper bearing driver to seat bearing in bore. Install the snap ring in 
the right countershaft rear groove.

[FIGURE: D9933A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not engage the sliding clutches with more than one gear at a time. 
This locks the gearing and prevents the mainshaft and the countershaft 
assemblies from rotating.

Move the reverse gear to the mainshaft rear and use a screwdriver to 
engage the sliding clutches with all the forward speed gears. A sliding clutch 
that does not engage with a gear indicates the gear set is not in proper mesh. 
The bearings of the right countershaft would need to be removed and the drive 
gear set timed.

[FIGURE: D9934A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mainshaft and Auxiliary Drive Gear

 Installation 

Install the left reverse idler gear assembly using the same sequence as 
used for the right reverse idler gear assembly.

 CAUTION: Block the mainshaft so it does not move when removing the auxiliary 
drive gear. 

Remove the auxiliary drive gear assembly from the mainshaft and the 
rear bearing bore. 

[FIGURE: D9935A.gif]

Move the reverse gear to the rear as far as possible, meshing teeth of 
the reverse gear with those of the reverse idler gears.

[FIGURE: D9936A.gif]

Align the external splines of the spacer with the clutching teeth of 
the reverse gear and move the spacer forward on the mainshaft and into the 
reverse gear.

Install the snap ring in the reverse gear hub and move the reverse gear 
forward on the mainshaft and into the proper position in the transmission case.

[FIGURE: D9937A.gif]

Install the auxiliary drive gear assembly on mainshaft rear. Use a 
flanged-end driver and maul to seat the bearing in the transmission case bore.

 NOTE: Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 (Type II) to capscrew.

Align the six capscrews holes in retainer with the tapped holes in the 
transmission case. Install the capscrews. Tighten the capscrews to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft) and lockwire the capscrews in groups of three.

Install the snap ring in the mainshaft end groove.

[FIGURE: D9938A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Input Shaft and Drive Gear Nut, Installation

 CAUTION: Do not reuse old nut. 

 NOTE: For models equipped with a snap ring to retain bearing, install the 
snap ring in groove of input shaft.

Apply Stud and Bearing Mount EOAZ-19554-BA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSK-M2G349-A1 to cleaned threads of new drive gear bearing nut. 

[FIGURE: C11076A.gif]

Install the nut on shaft (left hand threads). Using a drive gear nut 
installer, tighten to 339-407 Nm (250-300 lb-ft). Use a punch 
and maul to peen the nut into the milled slots of input shaft.

If previously removed, install the oil seal in drive gear housing 
bearing cover of models so equipped.

[FIGURE: C11077A.gif]

Install the drive gear bearing cover and gasket, making sure to align 
the oil hole in case. Secure cover on case with retaining capscrews (inset).

[FIGURE: C11078A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Shift Lever Housing

 Disassembly 

Secure the assembly in a vise with the bottom of housing up. Use a 
large screwdriver to twist between the spring and housing, forcing the spring 
from under the three lugs. Do one coil at a time. Remove the spring.

[FIGURE: C71671A.gif]

Remove the washer and shift lever.

[FIGURE: C11080A.gif]

Remove the spade pin from the bore in the housing. If necessary, remove 
the O-ring from the housing.

[FIGURE: C11081A.gif]

 Assembly 

Install the spade pin in the bore of the housing. Install the O-ring in 
the groove.

Install the shift lever in the housing, fitting the slot in the lever 
ball over the spade pin.

Seat the tension spring under the lugs in the housing, seating one coil 
at a time. Use of a spring driving tool is recommended.

[FIGURE: C71711A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification

The Fuller RTO-11709MLL and RTO-14709MLL are eleven speed 
transmissions. In addition to nine forward speeds, there are two additional 
speeds for low and low-low reduction. These transmissions use the Roadranger®
 air system, have twin countershafts, helical auxiliary 
gearing and overdrive with a direct shift pattern.

[FIGURE: C12542A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 5180
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 07-03N: Transmission, Manual, RTO-11709MLL and 14709MLL

1997 L-9000 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow

 Deep Reduction 

 NOTE: The numbers on the following illustrations correspond to the following 
numbered steps.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

The input shaft external splines engage the main drive gear internal 
splines.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the mating countershaft 
gears of the engaged mainshaft gear. The following cross section view 
illustrates a first/fifth speed gear engagement.

The external clutching teeth of the sliding clutch engage with the 
internal clutching teeth of the mainshaft gear which transfers torque to the 
mainshaft.

 Front Section 

[FIGURE: C12543A.gif]

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear 
sliding clutch which is in the forward position.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the deep reduction gear 
in the auxiliary section.

The deep reduction gear delivers torque to the output shaft through the 
range synchronizer sliding clutch.

The output shaft delivers torque to the driveline components.

 Auxiliary Section 

[FIGURE: C12544A.gif]

 LO Range 

 NOTE: The numbers on the following illustrations correspond to the following 
numbered steps.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

The input shaft external splines engage the main drive gear internal 
splines.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the mating countershaft 
gears of the engaged mainshaft gear. The following cross section view 
illustrates a first/fifth speed gear engagement.

The external clutching teeth of the sliding clutch engage with the 
internal clutching teeth of the mainshaft gear which transfers torque to the 
mainshaft.

 Front Section 

[FIGURE: C12543A.gif]

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the front auxiliary drive 
gear sliding clutch which is in the forward position.

The front auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged LO range 
gear.

Torque is transferred to the sliding clutch which is in the forward 
position delivering torque directly to the output shaft.

The output shaft delivers torque to the driveline components.

 Auxiliary Section 

[FIGURE: C12545A.gif]

 HI Range 

 NOTE: The numbers on the following illustrations correspond to the following 
numbered steps.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

The input shaft external splines engage the main drive gear internal 
splines.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the mating countershaft 
gears of the engaged mainshaft gear. The following cross section view 
illustrates a first/fifth speed gear engagement.

The external clutching teeth of the sliding clutch engage with the 
internal clutching teeth of the mainshaft gear which transfers torque to the 
mainshaft.

 Front Section 

[FIGURE: C12543A.gif]

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear 
sliding clutch which is in the rearward position.

Torque is delivered to the sliding clutch in the forward position, 
transferring torque directly to the output shaft.

The output shaft delivers torque to the driveline components.

 Auxiliary Section 

[FIGURE: C12546A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

 Proper Oil Level 

Make sure oil is level with the filler opening. Because you can reach 
oil with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. (An oil level of 25 
mm [1 inch] is about 3.7 liters [1 
gallon] of oil.)

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. 

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Draining Oil 

Drain transmission while oil is warm. To drain oil remove the drainplug 
at bottom of case. Clean the drainplug before reinstalling.

 Refilling 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, types and brands of oil must not be mixed because of 
possible incompatibility. 

Clean case around filler plug and remove plug from side of case. Fill 
transmission to the level of the filler opening. If transmission has two 
filler openings, fill to level of both openings.

The exact amount of oil will depend on the transmission inclination and 
model. Do not overfill — this will cause oil to be forced out 
of the transmission.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission lubricant (normal off-highway use).

 Operating Temperatures with Oil Coolers 

The transmission must not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent 
operating temperatures to 149°C (300°F) do 
not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures above 120°C 
(250°F) increase the lubricant's oxidation rate and shorten 
its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 120°
C (250°F), the transmission can require 
more frequent oil changes or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F):

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

exhaust system too close to transmission

high horsepower operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

Transmission oil coolers are recommended with the following engines:

350 HP and above

Transmission oil coolers are required with the following engines:

399 HP and above and GCWs over 40 824 kg (90,000 lb)

399 HP and above and 1898 Nm (1400 lb-ft) or greater 
torque

450 HP and above

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Output Yoke

 Removal 

Engage two (2) mainshaft sliding clutches into two (2) mainshaft gears 
to lock the transmission.

[FIGURE: C12313A.gif]

Use a large breaker bar or air impact wrench to remove the output shaft 
nut.

[FIGURE: C12550A.gif]

 NOTE: After removal of the output yoke or companion flange, temporarily 
replace the output shaft nut to protect the output shaft threads during 
auxiliary section disassembly.

Pull the yoke or flange straight to the rear and off the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C12626A.gif]

Remove the slinger.

[FIGURE: C12627A.gif]

Remove the speedometer gear or spacer.

[FIGURE: C12628A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: You must remove the shift bar housing in order to lock the transmission.

Engage two (2) mainshaft sliding clutches into two (2) mainshaft gears 
to lock the transmission.

[FIGURE: C12313A.gif]

Install the speedometer drive gear rotor or replacement spacer on the 
output shaft inside the rear bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C12628A.gif]

If the slinger on the yoke is damaged, replace using a slinger/seal kit.

[FIGURE: C12627A.gif]

Slide the companion flange or yoke onto the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C12626A.gif]

Install the output shaft nut, tighten to 610-678 Nm 
(450-500 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12629A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Auxiliary Section

 Removal, Vertical Position 

 CAUTION: Place blocks under the clutch housing to prevent input shaft damage. 

Place transmission in the vertical position, clutch housing down.

Remove the four (4) capscrews and the auxiliary countershaft rear 
bearing cover, gasket, and rear bearing shim.

[FIGURE: C12326A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an air gun. Tighten by hand until the capscrews are snug. 

Install the auxiliary countershaft retaining straps with two 3/8-inch 
NC x 1-inch and one 3/8-inch NC x 1-1/2-inch clean capscrews.

[FIGURE: C12633A.gif]

From the auxiliary section housing, remove the retaining capscrews that 
attach the front box to the auxiliary section.

[FIGURE: C12634A.gif]

Install a steel bar through the yoke.

Attach a lifting chain to the steel bar.

[FIGURE: C12635A.gif]

Lift assembly from the front section.

Remove the gasket and clean all mounting surfaces of gasket material.

 Removal, Horizontal Position 

Remove the four (4) capscrews and the auxiliary countershaft rear 
bearing cover, gasket, and rear bearing shim.

[FIGURE: C12630A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an air gun. Tighten by hand until the capscrews are snug. 

Install the auxiliary countershaft retaining covers with two 3/8-inch 
NC x 1-inch and one 3/8-inch NC x 1-1/2-inch clean capscrews.

[FIGURE: C12631A.gif]

From the auxiliary section housing, remove the retaining capscrews that 
attach the front section to the auxiliary section.

Insert the two (2) longest capscrews in the housing flange tapped 
holes. Tighten evenly to move the auxiliary section away from the front box. 
Go far enough to break the gasket seal.

[FIGURE: C12632A.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the tapped holes.

Attach an auxiliary section hanger bracket to the auxiliary section top.

Attach a lifting chain to the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

[FIGURE: C12320A.gif]

Move assembly to the rear until auxiliary section is free.

Remove the gasket and clean all mounting surfaces of gasket material.

 Installation, Vertical Position 

 CAUTION: Place blocks under the clutch housing to prevent input shaft damage. 

Place the transmission in the vertical position, clutch housing down.

Position a new gasket on the transmission mounting surface.

Install a steel bar through the yoke.

Attach a lifting chain to the steel bar.

[FIGURE: C12635A.gif]

Position the auxiliary section over the two (2) dowel pins.

Slide the auxiliary section down the dowels.

Loosen the retaining covers.

Slide the auxiliary section the rest of the way into position.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the retaining capscrews, tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12636A.gif]

Remove the steel bar and chain.

To finish installation, refer to Shimming Procedure for Tapered 
Bearings in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 Installation, Horizontal Position 

Position a new gasket on the transmission mounting surface.

Attach an auxiliary section hanger bracket to the auxiliary section top.

Attach a lifting chain to the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

[FIGURE: C12320A.gif]

Position the auxiliary section on the two (2) dowel pins.

Slide the auxiliary section on until the hanger bracket contacts the 
front section back.

Remove the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

Loosen the retaining covers.

Slide the auxiliary section the rest of the way into position.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the retaining capscrews, tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12637A.gif]

To finish installation, refer to Shimming Procedure for Tapered 
Bearings in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Shimming Procedure for Tapered Bearings

Remove the countershaft straps. Make sure a 0.100 countershaft rear 
bearing shim is installed. Make sure the countershaft rear bearing races are 
seated in the bearing bores.

[FIGURE: C12326A.gif]

Install two (2) clean 3/8-inch x 1-inch capscrews without washers 
directly across from each other in each bearing cover. Tapped holes in 
auxiliary case must be free of thread adhesive.

[FIGURE: C12638A.gif]

Tighten the capscrews to 0.8 Nm (7 lb-in). Do not 
install the countershaft rear bearing cover gasket.

[FIGURE: C12639A.gif]

Rotate the output shaft six (6) times clockwise, then six (6) times 
counterclockwise to seat the countershaft rear bearings. Use a feeler gauge, 
as close to each capscrew location as possible, and measure the gap between 
the countershaft rear bearing cover and the auxiliary case. Record the 
measurements. Using the average measurement, refer to the Shimming Chart to 
identify the proper shim.

[FIGURE: C12640A.gif]

Remove the countershaft rear bearing cover and gauging shim.

[FIGURE: C12326A.gif]

Place the selected shim on the rear countershaft bearing race.

Position a new gasket on countershaft rear bearing cover mounting 
surface.

Position the countershaft rear bearing cover over the new gasket.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the retaining capscrews, tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12641A.gif]

Repeat Steps 1-8 for the other countershaft rear bearing cover.

 Removal 

From inside the clutch housing, remove the nuts and washers.

From inside the clutch housing, remove the bolts.

[FIGURE: C12330A.gif]

Pull the clutch housing from the studs and transmission case.

[FIGURE: C12331A.gif]

Remove the gasket and clean all mounting surfaces of gasket material.

 Installation 

Position a new gasket on the housing mounting surface.

Install the clutch housing on the front box, pilot it on the six studs 
and drive gear bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C12331A.gif]

244-258 Nm (180-190 lb-ft).

equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to retaining capscrews.

Install the capscrews with lockwashers, tighten to 122-136 Nm
 (90-100 lb-ft).
