DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Auxiliary Section

 Auxiliary Countershafts 

 Disassembly 

To hold the auxiliary countershafts from turning, place a shop rag or 
equivalent between the auxiliary drive gear and one countershaft.

From the output shaft, loosen the 15/16-inch capscrew and retainer. Do 
not remove the capscrew.

[FIGURE: C12643A.gif]

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the output shaft forward far enough to 
partially unseat the bearing.

[FIGURE: C12644A.gif]

Support the auxiliary countershaft while removing the auxiliary 
countershaft retaining strap.

Remove the auxiliary countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12645A.gif]

Remove the auxiliary countershaft bearing race from bore.

If necessary, secure the countershaft assemblies in a vise and remove 
both the front and rear bearings with a bearing separator and jaw pullers.

[FIGURE: C12646A.gif]

 NOTE: To make auxiliary section assembly easier, you can make an auxiliary 
section fixture out of a 2-inch x 12-inch template.

[FIGURE: C12054A.gif]

 Assembly 

Place the countershaft assembly vertical on a clean, flat surface. If 
previously removed, use the proper driver and maul to install the countershaft 
bearings.

Mark each countershaft for correct timing. Locate the O stamped on the 
countershaft and mark the tooth with highly visible toolmaker's dye or paint.

[FIGURE: C12647A.gif]

Place the countershafts in the fixture or on a flat surface for 
reassembly. Turn the countershafts so that the two teeth marked on each LO 
range gear are towards the middle.

Align the output shaft between the countershafts, match the timing marks.

[FIGURE: C12648A.gif]

Install range yoke, offset side facing down, into the synchronizer 
sliding slot. Install the reduction yoke in the sliding clutch on the output 
shaft.

[FIGURE: C12649A.gif]

Lay the auxiliary housing front face down on a clean, flat surface. 
Install the bearing race in the bearing bore.

[FIGURE: C12650A.gif]

Temporarily install the rear bearing cover with two (2) capscrews.

[FIGURE: C12651A.gif]

Place the auxiliary housing over the countershaft assemblies and the 
output shaft assembly.

[FIGURE: C12652A.gif]

Install the bearing races.

[FIGURE: C12935A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an air gun. Tighten by hand until the capscrews are snug. 

Install each auxiliary countershaft retaining strap with two 3/8-inch 
NC x 1-inch and one 3/8-inch NC x 2-1/2-inch clean capscrews.

Remove the rear bearing cover.

Make sure the output shaft bearing spacer is on the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C12936A.gif]

Heat the rear output bearing cone and install the bearing, tapered side 
down, on the shaft.

Position a new gasket on the rear bearing cover mounting surface.

Position the rear bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C12937A.gif]

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the six (6) retaining capscrews in the nonchamfered holes, 
tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12938A.gif]

Tighten the 15/16-inch capscrew and retainer to 258-285 Nm
 (180-210 lb-ft). Do not remove the capscrew.

[FIGURE: C12643A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Range Cylinder Assembly

 Disassembly 

From the combination cylinder cover, remove the capscrews, cover, and 
gasket.

[FIGURE: C12657A.gif]

Clean the gasket mounting surfaces of all gasket material.

From the combination cylinder housing bore, remove the 15/16-inch nut 
from the range yoke bar.

From the combination cylinder housing bore, remove the 3/4-inch nut 
from the reduction yoke bar.

[FIGURE: C12658A.gif]

Remove the cylinder housing and gasket.

[FIGURE: C12659A.gif]

From the auxiliary housing, remove the synchronizer shift yoke and the 
synchronizer assembly.

[FIGURE: C12660A.gif]

From the cylinder housing bore, remove the range piston.

Inspect the range piston O-rings, remove if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12661A.gif]

From the cylinder housing bore, remove the reduction piston.

[FIGURE: C12662A.gif]

Inspect the reduction piston O-rings, remove if damaged.

Clean the gasket mounting surface of all gasket material.

Inspect the O-rings inside the combination cylinder housing bores, 
remove if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12663A.gif]

Inspect the insert valve retaining nut from the cylinder cover, remove 
if damaged.

If necessary, remove and inspect the insert valve from the valve bore.

[FIGURE: C12664A.gif]

 Assembly 

If previously removed, install the insert valve, flat side to the 
inside, and retaining nut. Tighten to 54-68 Nm (40-50 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12665A.gif]

If previously removed, in the combination cylinder housing bores, 
install the O-rings.

[FIGURE: C12663A.gif]

If previously removed, on the two (2) pistons, install the O-rings.

[FIGURE: C12661A.gif]

Position a new gasket on the combination cylinder housing mounting 
surface.

Install the cylinder housing.

[FIGURE: DC0014A.gif]

Install the range yoke bar piston, flat side to the rear.

Secure the piston with the retaining nut (must have nylon locking 
patch), tighten to 95-115 Nm (70-85 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: DC0015A.gif]

Install the reduction yoke bar piston, flat side to the rear.

Secure the piston with the retaining nut, tighten to 102-115 Nm
 (75-85 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: DC0016A.gif]

Position a new gasket on the cylinder housing cover mounting surface.

Over the gasket, position the range cylinder cover.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the capscrews, tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12669A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Synchronizer

 Disassembly 

 CAUTION: Cover the synchronizer assembly with a shop rag to prevent losing the 
three springs from the HI range synchronizer pin location. 

Place the larger LO range synchronizer ring on the bench.

Grab both sides of the HI range synchronizer and pull.

[FIGURE: C12438A.gif]

From the synchronizer ring LO range pins, remove the sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C12439A.gif]

 Assembly 

On the bench place the larger LO range synchronizer ring face down with 
pins up.

With the sliding clutch recessed side up, place the sliding clutch on 
the LO range synchronizer pins.

[FIGURE: C12439A.gif]

In the HI range synchronizer bores, install the three (3) springs.

[FIGURE: C12670A.gif]

Place the HI range synchronizer ring over the LO range synchronizer 
ring. Rotate the HI range synchronizer until the springs are seated against 
the pins.

[FIGURE: C12671A.gif]

With a shop rag, cover the assembly.

Apply downward pressure to the HI range synchronizer ring while 
twisting counterclockwise. This compresses the springs to fully seat HI range 
on the LO range synchronizer.

[FIGURE: C12438A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

LO Range Gear Assembly

 Disassembly 

Temporarily install the output yoke on the output shaft. Insert a 
breaker bar to keep the output shaft from turning.

[FIGURE: C12672A.gif]

From the auxiliary housing front, remove the 1-1/2-inch range coupler 
nut.

[FIGURE: C12673A.gif]

From the output shaft, remove the output yoke.

From the auxiliary mainshaft, remove the washer and dowel pin.

[FIGURE: C12674A.gif]

Remove the LO range gear with the coupler.

With a punch and hammer drive the two coupler pins from the coupler.

[FIGURE: C12675A.gif]

Align the coupler splines with the washer splines and remove the range 
coupler from the LO range gear.

[FIGURE: C12676A.gif]

If necessary, remove the bushings from inside the coupler.

[FIGURE: C12677A.gif]

From inside the LO range gear, remove the splined washer.

[FIGURE: C12678A.gif]

From the auxiliary housing, remove the sliding clutch and the reduction 
yoke assembly.

[FIGURE: C12679A.gif]

 Assembly 

Use toolmaker's dye to mark the LO range gear for timing purposes.

Mark any two (2) adjacent teeth on the LO range gear. Repeat the 
procedure for the two (2) adjacent teeth directly opposite the first set marked.

[FIGURE: C12680A.gif]

If previously removed, insert the bushings in the coupler.

[FIGURE: C12677A.gif]

Install the splined washer in the LO range gear hub.

[FIGURE: C12678A.gif]

Install the LO range gear over the coupler matching the coupler 
external splines with the LO range gear internal splines.

[FIGURE: C12681A.gif]

Rotate the splined washer in the coupler groove to engage the external 
splines with the LO range gear clutching teeth.

[FIGURE: C12682A.gif]

To lock LO range gear to the coupler, align the washer splines and 
install the pins in the coupler with a punch and hammer.

[FIGURE: C12683A.gif]

From auxiliary mainshaft, install washer and dowel pin.

From output shaft, install output yoke temporarily and insert breaker 
bar to keep output shaft from turning.

From auxiliary housing front, install the 1-1/2-inch range coupler nut.

Remove output yoke.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Output Shaft Assembly

 Disassembly 

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the output shaft forward and through 
the rear bearing assembly.

[FIGURE: C12684A.gif]

From the auxiliary housing rear, remove the rear bearing retaining 
capscrews.

[FIGURE: C12685A.gif]

From the auxiliary housing rear, remove the rear bearing cover, rear 
bearing, and bearing race.

[FIGURE: C12686A.gif]

Clean the gasket mounting surface of gasket material.

Inspect the rear bearing cover oil seal for damage, replace with new 
seal if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12687A.gif]

If so equipped, remove the bearing inner spacer from the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C12688A.gif]

Use the output shaft assembly gear front face as a base, press the 
output shaft through the bearing and gear.

[FIGURE: C12689A.gif]

 Assembly 

Use toolmaker's dye to mark the LO range gear for timing purposes.

Mark any two (2) adjacent teeth on the LO range gear. Repeat the 
procedure for the two (2) adjacent teeth directly opposite the first set marked.

[FIGURE: C12690A.gif]

Place the splined washer on the output shaft shoulder.

With LO range gear clutching teeth down, position LO range gear on the 
output shaft, engage the washer splines.

[FIGURE: C12691A.gif]

With the smooth side up, position the LO range gear rear washer on the 
output shaft against the LO range gear. Move LO gear around to center the 
washer.

[FIGURE: C12692A.gif]

 NOTE: When heating the bearings, do not heat bearings above 136°
C (275°F). When installing the rear bearing 
race, the proper depth is when the race shoulder is seated on bearing bore top.

With tapered side up, use heat or appropriate driver and install the 
output shaft front rear bearing (the larger bearing).

[FIGURE: C12693A.gif]

Turn the assembly upside down on a table. Install the reduction yoke 
sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C12694A.gif]

Install the LO range gear and coupler assembly on the output shaft with 
the reduction gear clutching teeth upward.

[FIGURE: C12695A.gif]

Insert the dowel pin through the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C12696A.gif]

Place the retainer washer on the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C12697A.gif]

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the threads of the 
coupler retaining nut.

Install the coupler retaining nut on the output shaft. Tighten to 
122-163 Nm (90-120 lb-ft). Set aside.

[FIGURE: C12698A.gif]

If so equipped, position the bearing inner spacer on the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C12699A.gif]

Lay the auxiliary housing front face down on a clean, flat surface. 
Install the bearing race in the bearing bore.

[FIGURE: C12700A.gif]

To reinstall output shaft into auxiliary housing, refer to Auxiliary 
Countershafts assembly in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Front Section

 Input Shaft 

 Removal 

From the front bearing cover, remove the six (6) retaining capscrews 
and cover. Remove any remaining gasket material from the case and cover.

[FIGURE: C12373A.gif]

From the input shaft groove, remove the bearing retaining snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12371A.gif]

Use a soft bar and maul and drive the input shaft toward the case rear 
as far as possible. Pull the input shaft forward.

[FIGURE: C12701A.gif]

Use pry bars or screwdrivers to complete removal of the bearing. From 
the drive gear front, remove the drive gear spacer.

[FIGURE: C12702A.gif]

Remove the drive gear internal snap ring.

Pull the input shaft forward and out of the drive gear.

[FIGURE: C12703A.gif]

From inside the case, remove the drive gear.

Inspect the bushing in the input shaft pocket, remove if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12365A.gif]

 Installation 

In inside diameter of main drive gear, install the snap ring.

Use toolmaker's dye to mark the main drive gear for timing purposes.

Mark any two (2) adjacent teeth on the drive gear. Repeat the procedure 
for the two (2) adjacent teeth directly opposite the first set marked.

[FIGURE: C12366A.gif]

Inside the case, mesh the lower countershaft drive gear marked tooth 
with either set of marked teeth on the main drive gear.

From the front, slide the input shaft into the main drive gear.

[FIGURE: C12703A.gif]

Over the input shaft, install the drive gear spacer.

With the bearing internal snap ring to the outside, position the 
bearing on the input shaft.

[FIGURE: C12702A.gif]

Use a flanged-end driver and maul to seat the input shaft bearing.

[FIGURE: C12369A.gif]

Install the bearing retainer snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12371A.gif]

Push the input shaft bearing back into the case bore.

Position a new gasket on the bearing cover mounting surface, making 
sure to align the gasket oil return hole with case oil return hole.

[FIGURE: C12372A.gif]

Position the front bearing cover, making sure to align the cover oil 
return hole with case oil return hole.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA meeting 
Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to retaining capscrews.

Secure the front bearing cover with six (6) capscrews, tighten to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Reverse Idler Gear Assembly

 NOTE: Before the upper reverse idler gear assembly can be removed, mainshaft 
reverse gear must be positioned forward against the next gear.

While removing the reverse idler shaft, the thrust washer can drop to 
the transmission case bottom.

The mainshaft reverse gear must be moved in order to remove the upper 
reverse idler gear. Refer to Mainshaft Assembly, Removal in the Disassembly 
and Assembly portion of this section.

 Removal 

From the idler shaft, loosen the lock nut and washer.

[FIGURE: C12709A.gif]

The mainshaft reverse gear must be moved in order to remove the upper 
reverse idler gear. See Mainshaft Assembly, Removal , Steps 1-3 in the 
Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section.

Remove the loosened lock nut and washer.

[FIGURE: C12710A.gif]

From the idler shaft rear, remove the pipe plug.

From the reverse idler gear bore, use an impact puller to remove the 
auxiliary countershaft front bearing race.

[FIGURE: C12205A.gif]

Install an impact puller, 1/2 inch-13 threaded end, and remove the 
shaft from case bore.

As the idler shaft and idler plate are removed, remove the thrust 
washers and gear.

[FIGURE: C12206A.gif]

Inspect the reverse gear assembly. Remove the inner race and needle 
bearing, if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12207A.gif]

 Installation 

If reverse gear assembly is disassembled, position the needle bearing 
and inner race into the reverse idler gear.

[FIGURE: C12207A.gif]

Place the rear thrust washer on the idler shaft.

[FIGURE: C12208A.gif]

Insert the idler shaft into the case bore, threaded end to the front. 
As the shaft passes through the case bore position the reverse idler gear on 
the shaft, long hub to the front. Insert the thrust washer between the reverse 
idler gear and the case support boss. Finish inserting the idler shaft.

[FIGURE: C12209A.gif]

Make sure the reverse idler shaft is seated in the support boss bore.

Install the washer and lock nut on shaft front. Tighten the stop nut to 
68-81 Nm (50-60 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12711A.gif]

Thread the pipe plug into the reverse idler shaft and tighten.

[FIGURE: C12211A.gif]

Use a bearing driver and maul and install the auxiliary countershaft 
front bearing race against the idler plate.

[FIGURE: C12347A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Countershaft Bearings

 NOTE: The following instructions are used to remove the upper and lower 
countershaft bearings. To remove the mainshaft assembly, only the upper 
countershaft bearings need to be removed.

Performing the following instructions will damage the bearings and 
should not be done unless bearing replacement is planned.

The bearing inner race remains pressed on the countershaft after 
removal of the front bearings.

 Removal 

From each countershaft rear groove, remove the snap ring.

From inside the case, use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft 
rear bearings from the case bores.

[FIGURE: C12212A.gif]

From each countershaft front, remove the capscrew and front retainer 
plate.

[FIGURE: C12082A.gif]

Use the soft bar and maul to drive each countershaft to the rear as far 
as possible. This partially unseats the front bearings.

[FIGURE: C12712A.gif]

Return to the case rear, and drive each countershaft forward as far as 
possible. This exposes the bearing snap rings.

[FIGURE: C12713A.gif]

Use a bearing puller or pry bars to remove the countershaft front 
bearings. If a bearing puller is used, the front bearing cover has to be 
removed.

[FIGURE: C12215A.gif]

 Installation 

Move the countershaft to the rear and insert the countershaft support 
tool to center shaft in rear case bore.

[FIGURE: C12216A.gif]

Use a flanged-end bearing driver and maul to position the front bearing 
in case bore.

[FIGURE: C12217A.gif]

Use a screwdriver inserted in the countershaft capscrew bore to help 
center the countershaft.

Move the countershaft forward into the bearing.

Use a flanged-end bearing driver and maul to completely seat the front 
bearing in case bore.

[FIGURE: C12217A.gif]

On the countershaft front, position the retainer plate with roll pin in 
shaft end hole.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA meeting 
Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to retaining capscrews.

Secure with capscrew, tightening to 122-163 Nm (90-120 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12714A.gif]

From the rear, remove the countershaft support tool.

With the larger inside diameter lead chamfer to the shaft front, use a 
flanged-end bearing driver and install the rear bearing.

In the countershaft rear groove, install the rear snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12219A.gif]

Countershaft Assemblies

 Removal 

Move the upper countershaft assembly to the rear as far as possible.

Swing the countershaft front to case middle.

Lift the countershaft assembly from the case.

[FIGURE: C12220A.gif]

 Installation

[FIGURE: C12356A.gif]

Place the upper, 45-tooth PTO gear countershaft assembly in the case, 
the drive gear end to the front.

Position as far to the right as possible (the same side as the lower 
reverse idler gear assembly).

[FIGURE: C12220A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Timing Procedures

It is essential that both countershaft assemblies of the front and 
auxiliary sections are timed. This ensures proper tooth contact is made 
between mainshaft gears seeking to center on the mainshaft during torque 
transfer and mating countershaft gears that distribute the load evenly. If not 
properly timed, serious damage to the transmission is likely to result from 
unequal tooth contact causing the mainshaft gears to climb out of equilibrium.

Timing is a simple procedure of marking the appropriate teeth of a gear 
set prior to installation and placing them in proper mesh while in the 
transmission. In the front section, it is necessary to time only the drive 
gear set. And depending on the model, only the LO range, deep reduction, or 
splitter gear set is timed in the auxiliary section.

 Front Section 

Marking countershaft drive gear teeth.

Prior to placing each countershaft assembly into the case, clearly mark 
the tooth located directly over the drive gear keyway as shown. This tooth is 
stamped with an O to aid identification.

[FIGURE: C8921B.gif]

Marking main drive gear teeth.

Mark any two adjacent teeth on the main drive gear.

Mark the two adjacent teeth located directly opposite the first set 
marked on the main drive gear. As shown to the left, there should be an equal 
number of unmarked gear teeth on each side between the marked sets.

[FIGURE: C8922B.gif]

Meshing marked countershaft drive gear teeth with marked main drive 
gear teeth.

(After placing the mainshaft assembly into the case, the countershaft 
bearings are installed to complete installation of the countershaft assemblies.)

When installing the bearings on the left countershaft, mesh the 
countershaft drive gear marked tooth with either set of main drive gear two 
marked teeth.

[FIGURE: C8923B.gif]

Repeat the procedure when installing the bearings on the right 
countershaft, make use of the remaining set of main drive gear two marked 
teeth to time assembly.

 Auxiliary Section 

Mark any tooth on the LO range auxiliary mainshaft gear. Then mark a 
tooth located directly opposite the first marked.

Prior to placing each auxiliary countershaft assembly into housing, 
mark the two teeth on each auxiliary countershaft assembly LO range gear 
stamped with the two Os. Repeat the procedure on each auxiliary countershaft 
reduction gear.

Follow the assembly procedures under Auxiliary Section in the 
Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Mainshaft Assembly

 Removal 

From the mainshaft, remove the reverse gear retaining snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12222A.gif]

Move the mainshaft reverse gear as far to the rear as possible and 
remove reverse gear inside diameter snap ring.

 NOTE: If not removing the upper reverse idler gear assembly, you must remove 
the upper reverse idler gear assembly shaft and roll the gear to the outside. 
Refer to Reverse Idler Gear Assembly , Steps 1-4 in the Disassembly and 
Assembly portion of this section.

Move the reverse gear forward and against the next gear, engaging the 
mainshaft sliding clutch spline.

[FIGURE: C12223A.gif]

Use a large screwdriver and block the upper countershaft assembly 
against the case wall.

 NOTE: If removing the upper reverse idler gear assembly, refer to Reverse 
Idler Gear Assembly in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section at 
this time.

Position the hook or rope around the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12224A.gif]

 NOTE: The upper countershaft must be kept forward against the case front 
wall. Pull the mainshaft rearward and to the right as far as possible.

Pull the mainshaft to the rear to free the pilot from the input shaft 
pocket.

Tilt the mainshaft front up and lift assembly from the case.

[FIGURE: C12225A.gif]

 Installation 

Block the upper countershaft forward and as close to the case wall as 
possible.

With reverse gear forward against the next speed gear and mainshaft 
pilot end over the integral oil pump gear, lower the mainshaft assembly while 
pulling the shaft rear through the case bore.

[FIGURE: C12225A.gif]

Pull the input shaft forward until the drive gear is against the case.

After the mainshaft drops into the case, slide the countershaft back 
and the mainshaft should fall down between the countershafts.

Move the mainshaft pilot end into the input shaft pilot bushing. Mesh 
the mainshaft gears with the corresponding countershaft assembly gears.

[FIGURE: C12224A.gif]

Position the upper reverse idler gear in case.

Mesh the reverse gear teeth with the reverse idler gear teeth and move 
the reverse gear to the rear as far as possible.

[FIGURE: C12226A.gif]

Align the reverse gear spacer external splines with the reverse gear 
and move the spacer into the reverse gear.

Install the reverse gear inside diameter snap ring and move the reverse 
gear forward on the mainshaft and against the reverse gear limit washer.

Install reverse gear retaining snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12222A.gif]

To finish the input shaft/front bearing cover installation, refer to Input Shaft, Installation 
, Steps 9-12 in the Disassembly and Assembly portion 
of this section.

 Disassembly 

Remove reverse gear.

Remove reverse gear spline spacer.

Tilt the mainshaft up, and from the opposite end, remove the sliding 
clutch.

[FIGURE: C12262A.gif]

Place the mainshaft in a vertical position.

Remove the mainshaft key snap ring.

From the mainshaft rear, pull the mainshaft key from the mainshaft 
keyway.

Turn the reverse gear limit washer to align its splines with the 
mainshaft and remove the washer.

Remove the first/reverse-speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C12263A.gif]

Lift and turn first gear to align the limit washer splines.

Remove the limit washer, spacer and 1st gear.

[FIGURE: C12264A.gif]

Turn the second gear limit washer to align its splines with the 
mainshaft. Remove second gear and its limit washer.

Remove the second/third sliding clutch.

Remove each remaining gear, limit washer, and spacer.

Inspect the roll pin, remove if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12275A.gif]

 Assembly 

With mainshaft pilot end down, secure the mainshaft in a vise equipped 
with brass jaws or wood blocks.

If previously removed, install the roll pin in keyway.

[FIGURE: C12406A.gif]

With the washer flat side up, position the fourth speed gear washer in 
the mainshaft first or bottom groove. Rotate the washer until the washer 
splines and mainshaft splines align.

[FIGURE: C12266A.gif]

Start at the mainshaft bottom and install a plastic line in the keyway 
to lock the washer in place. As limit washers and gears are installed, 
continue to push the plastic line up.

With clutching teeth down, position the fourth speed gear on the 
mainshaft.

Install the flatwasher.

With clutching teeth up and against the flatwasher, install the third 
speed gear.

[FIGURE: C12276A.gif]

With the washer flat side down, position the washer against the spacer. 
Rotate the washer until the washer splines and mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

With the missing internal splines aligned with the plastic line, 
install the second/third speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C12277A.gif]

With the washer flat side up, position the 2nd speed gear limit washer 
in the next available groove. Rotate the washer until the washer splines and 
mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Install second gear spacer.

With clutching teeth down, position the second speed gear on the 
mainshaft engaging with spacer external splines.

[FIGURE: C12278A.gif]

With clutching teeth up, install first speed gear on shaft against 
second speed gear.

[FIGURE: C12279A.gif]

Position first speed gear spacer against first speed gear, engaging the 
spacer external splines with gear clutching teeth.

With washer flat side down, position the limit washer against the 
spacer. Rotate the washer until the washer splines and mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Between the gear hub and mainshaft spacer, insert 0.076-mm (0.003-inch) 
feeler gauge and 0.178-mm (0.007-inch) feeler gauge. If out of tolerance, 
change the limit against the mainshaft spacer. Refer to Axial Clearance (End 
Play) Limits in the Specifications portion of this section.

[FIGURE: C12271A.gif]

Align the sliding clutch missing internal spline with the mainshaft key 
and install the first/reverse speed sliding clutch.

With the flat side up, position the reverse speed gear limit washer 
(white) in the next available groove. Rotate the washer until the washer 
splines and mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Against the limit washer, position reverse gear spline spacer.

Install reverse gear on the mainshaft. Engage the gear clutching teeth 
with spacer external splines and sliding clutch. Move the reverse gear down 
against the first speed gear.

[FIGURE: C12272A.gif]

 NOTE: Be careful not to move the gears while doing this procedure. The limit 
washers are unlocked and can rotate, causing the gears to drop.

At this time remove the air line and insert the mainshaft key. 

[FIGURE: C12273A.gif]

Remove the mainshaft from the vise.

On the shaft front, align the sliding clutch missing internal spline 
with the mainshaft key and install the fourth drive gear sliding clutch. 
Engage the sliding clutch external splines with the fourth speed gear 
clutching teeth.

Install mainshaft key snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12274A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Gearshift Lever

 NOTE: If total disassembly is needed, the Roadranger® valve 
must be removed first. Refer to Section 07-06 .

 Disassembly 

Slide the boot up the shift lever shaft and remove.

[FIGURE: C12387A.gif]

With housing bottom facing up, secure the assembly in a vise.

Use large screwdriver to twist between the spring and housing, forcing 
the spring from under the housing lugs.

[FIGURE: C12388A.gif]

From inside the housing tower, remove the tension spring, washer, and 
gearshift lever.

In models so equipped, remove the nut and washer from the housing bore.

From the housing tower spade pin bore, remove and inspect the spade 
pin, discard if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12389A.gif]

From the housing tower inside groove, inspect the O-ring, discard if 
damaged.

 Assembly 

With housing bottom facing up, secure the assembly in a vise.

If the spade pin is damaged, replace and install the spade pin in 
housing tower bore.

[FIGURE: C12389A.gif]

In models so equipped, in the housing bore install the nut and washer.

If the O-ring is damaged, replace; lubricate the O-ring with Silicone 
Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A. 
Install the O-ring in the housing tower inside groove.

Align the lever ball slot with the spade pin and position the gearshift 
lever in the housing tower.

With dished side up, install the washer over the ball.

[FIGURE: C12390A.gif]

Use a tension spring driver to install the tension spring under the 
housing lugs.

[FIGURE: C12388A.gif]

Remove the assembly from the vise.

Install a rubber boot over the gearshift lever and against the housing.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Shift Bar Housing

 Disassembly 

If the three (3) sets of tension springs and balls from housing bores 
have not been removed, place the shift bar housing on its side to remove them.

[FIGURE: C12241A.gif]

If so equipped, remove the oil trough retaining capscrews and oil trough.

[FIGURE: C12242A.gif]

With the housing rear to the right, lay the assembly on a flat surface.

While removing the top yoke bar to the right, remove the two (2) shift 
blocks.

[FIGURE: C12243A.gif]

From the middle yoke bar, remove the shift yoke and shift block. As the 
neutral notch in the bar clears the rear boss, remove the small interlock pin 
from the notch bore.

[FIGURE: C12244A.gif]

Remove the actuating plunger from the center top bore boss.

[FIGURE: C12245A.gif]

From the bottom yoke bar, remove the two (2) shift yokes.

[FIGURE: C12246A.gif]

As the shift bar clears the last boss, two (2) 3/4-inch interlock balls 
drop from the bottom rear boss bore.

[FIGURE: C12247A.gif]

If damaged, remove the plug, spring, and plunger from the first/reverse 
shift yoke.

[FIGURE: C12248A.gif]

Inspect the yoke or block parts, replace the worn parts.

If the yoke actuator parts are damaged, replace the parts.

[FIGURE: C12249A.gif]

 Assembly 

Assemble the yoke actuator assembly:

From the shift bar housing bottom, install the actuator pin and yoke 
actuator.

On the shift bar housing top, install the washer and nut. Tighten to 
102-115 Nm (75-85 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12250A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12715A.gif]

Assemble the first/reverse shift yoke assembly:

Install the plunger in the first/reverse shift yoke bore, plunger shank 
to the outside.

Install the spring into the bore over the plunger shank.

Install the plug and tighten to compress the spring.

After plug bottoms out, back the plug out 1-1-1/2 turns.

Complete the block assembly process by staking the plug through the 
small hole in block.

[FIGURE: C12248A.gif]

With the housing rear to the right, lay the assembly on a flat surface.

Start installation of the bottom shift bar, as the bar passes the 
bosses, install the two (2) bottom shift yoke assemblies. Finish installation.

[FIGURE: C12246A.gif]

Install the shift yoke lock screw. Tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft). Tighten lockwire securely.

Place the actuating plunger in the top center bore.

[FIGURE: C12245A.gif]

Place one 3/4-inch interlock ball in the interlock bore, against the 
bottom bar.

Holding the middle bar notched end, start installation. As the bar 
passes the rear boss, position the shift block.

As the bar passes the center boss, position the shift yoke on bar, long 
hub to the housing front.

Just prior to inserting notched end of bar in rear boss, install the 
small interlock pin vertically in the neutral notch bore.

[FIGURE: C12252A.gif]

Install the shift block and shift yoke lock screws. Tighten to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft). Tighten lockwire securely.

Place one 3/4-inch interlock ball in the interlock bore, against the 
middle bar.

Holding the top bar notched end, start installation. As the bar passes 
the rear boss, position the shift block.

As the bar passes the center boss, position the shift yoke on bar, long 
hub to the housing rear.

[FIGURE: C12243A.gif]

Install the shift block and shift yoke lock screws. Tighten to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft). Tighten lockwire securely.

If so equipped, install the oil trough. Tighten the retaining capscrews 
to 11-16 Nm (8-12 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12716A.gif]

Install the three (3) tension balls, one in each housing top bore. 
Install the three (3) detent springs, one over each tension ball.

[FIGURE: C12241A.gif]

Section 07-03P: Transmission, Manual, Eaton 8-Speed and 15-Speed Deep Reduction

1997 LT, LTS, LNT, LTL, LTLS, LTLA, LTA-9000 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification

[FIGURE: D9292B.gif]

The Fuller RTO-11708LL, RTO-14708LL, RT-14715, RTO-14715, RT-15715 and 
RTX-15715 series transmissions are designed for heavy-duty vehicles, for both 
on-highway and off-highway use.

The twin countershaft design, which splits torque evenly between the 
two countershafts, provides a high torque capacity-to-weight ratio. Because of 
torque splitting, each gearset carries only half of the load, greatly reducing 
the face width of each gear.

The design employs the floating gear principle. The mainshaft gears, 
when not engaged, float between the countershaft gears, eliminating the need 
for gear sleeves and bushings.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow

 Front Section 

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
illustration.

The transmission transfers torque from the engine to the driveshaft 
through the following route:

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear.

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

 Auxiliary Section 

 Deep Reduction 

The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear.

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both auxiliary countershafts to the engaged 
deep reduction gear on output shaft.

Torque is transferred to the output shaft through the sliding clutch.

Output shaft delivers torque to driveline as deep reduction first.

 Power Flow — Front Section and Auxiliary Section (Deep 
Reduction) 

[FIGURE: D9293B.gif]

 LO Range 

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear.

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged LO Range gear 
on range mainshaft or output shaft.

Torque is transferred to range mainshaft or output shaft through the 
sliding clutch.

Torque is delivered to driveline as LO Range first.

 Power Flow — Auxiliary Section (LO Range) 

[FIGURE: D9294B.gif]

 HI Range 

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear.

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear transfers torque directly to the range 
mainshaft or output shaft through engaged sliding clutch.

Torque is delivered through range mainshaft or output shaft to 
driveline as HI range sixth.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

 CAUTION: The use of mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil is not 
recommended, but if these gear oils are used, be sure to adhere to the 
following limitations. 

 CAUTION: Do not use mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil when operating 
temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). Many 
of these gear oils, particularly 85W140, break down above 110°
C (230°F) and coat seals, bearings, and gears with deposits 
that can cause premature failures. If these deposits are observed (especially 
a coating on seal areas causing oil leakage), change to Eaton Roadranger®
 CD50 transmission fluid, heavy-duty engine oil, or mineral 
gear oil to ensure maximum component life and to maintain your warranty with 
Eaton. Refer to Operating Temperatures in this section. 

 CAUTION: Additives and friction modifiers are not recommended for use in Eaton 
Fuller transmissions. 

Proper lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program. If the oil is not doing its job, or if the oil level is 
ignored, all the maintenance procedures in the world are not going to keep the 
transmission running or ensure long transmission life.

Eaton Fuller transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in an oil circulating bath by the motion of the gears and shafts.

All parts are amply lubricated if these procedures are closely followed:

Maintain oil level. Inspect regularly.

Change oil regularly.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 LUBRICATION CHANGE AND INSPECTION

 Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid 

 HIGHWAY USE 

Every 16 093 km (10,000 miles)

Check fluid level. Check for leaks.

Every 402 325 km (250,000 miles)

Change transmission fluid.

 OFF-HIGHWAY USE 

Every 40 hours

Inspect fluid level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission fluid where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission fluid (normal off-highway use).

 Heavy-Duty Engine Lubricant or Mineral Gear Lubricant 

 HIGHWAY USE 

First 4 828 to 8 047 km (3,000 to 5,000 miles)

Factory fill initial drain.

Every 16 093 km (10,000 miles)

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 80 465 km (50,000 miles)

Change transmission lubricant.

 OFF-HIGHWAY USE 

First 30 hours

Change transmission lubricant on new units.

Every 40 hours

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission fluid where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission fluid (normal off-highway use).

 Proper Oil Level 

Make sure oil is level with the filler opening. Because you can reach 
oil with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. An oil level of 
25.4 mm (1 inch) is equal to approximately 3.7 liters (1 gallon) of oil.

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Draining Oil 

Drain transmission while oil is warm. To drain oil remove the drain 
plug at case bottom. Clean the drain plug before reinstalling.

 Refilling 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. 

Clean case around filler plug and remove plug from case side. Fill the 
transmission to the level of the filler opening. If the transmission has two 
filler openings, fill to the level of both openings.

The exact amount of oil depends on the transmission inclination and 
model. Do not overfill — this causes oil to be forced out of 
the case through the front bearing cover. 

 Proper Lubrication Levels As Related to Transmission Operating Angles 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication can occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

The chart below illustrates the safe percent of upgrade on which the 
transmission can be used with various chassis mounting angles. For example: if 
you have a four-degree transmission mounting angle, then eight degrees (or 14 
percent of grade) is equal to the limit of 12 degrees. If you have a 
zero-degree mounting angle, the transmission can be operated on a 12-degree 
(21 percent) grade.

Anytime the transmission operating angle or 12 degrees is exceeded for 
an extended period of time the transmission must be equipped with an oil pump 
or cooler kit to ensure proper lubrication.

Note on the chart the effect low oil levels can have on safe operating 
angles. Allowing the oil level to fall one-half inch below the filler plug 
hole reduces the degree of grade by approximately three degrees (5.5 percent). 
Proper lubrication levels are essential.

[FIGURE: C11746A.gif]

 Operating Temperatures 

 Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid, 
Heavy-Duty Engine Oil and Mineral Oil 

The transmission must not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent 
operating temperatures to 149°C (300°F) will 
not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures above 120°C 
(250°F) increase the lubricant's rate of oxidation and 
shorten its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 120°
C (250°F), the transmission may require 
more frequent oil changes or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F).

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

exhaust system too close to transmission

high horsepower, overdrive operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

Transmission oil coolers are recommended with the following engines:

350 HP and above with overdrive transmissions

Transmission oil coolers are required with the following engines:

399 HP and above with overdrive transmissions and GCWs over 40,824 kg 
(90,000 lb).

399 HP and above and 1,898 Nm (1400 lb-ft) or greater 
torque

450 HP and above

 With EP or Multipurpose Gear Oil 

Mild EP gear oil and multipurpose gear oil are not recommended when 
lubricant operating temperatures are above 110°C (230°
F). In addition, transmission oil coolers are not 
recommended with these gear oils, since the oil cooler materials can be 
attacked by these gear oils. The lower temperature limit and oil cooler 
restriction with these gear oils generally limit their success to milder 
applications.

 Removal 

Clean the area around the shift lever housing. Remove the capscrews, 
then jar the housing lightly. Remove the shift lever housing and cover the 
opening in the shift bar housing.

[FIGURE: C95541A.gif]

 Disassembly 

 WARNING: SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. USE CARE TO PROTECT EYES WHEN REMOVING SPRING. 

Secure the shift lever housing assembly in a vise with the bottom of 
the housing up. Use a large screwdriver to twist between the spring and 
housing, forcing the spring from under the three lugs. Do one coil at a time. 
Remove the spring.

[FIGURE: C71671A.gif]

Remove the washer and shift lever.

Remove the spade pin from the bore in the housing. If necessary, remove 
the O-ring from the housing.

 Assembly 

Install the spade pin in the bore of the housing. Install the O-ring in 
the groove. 

Install the shift lever in the housing, fitting the slot in the lever 
ball over the spade pin.

Seat the tension spring under the lugs in the housing, seating one coil 
at a time. Use of a spring driving tool is recommended.

[FIGURE: C71711A.gif]

 Installation 

Make sure that the three tension springs and balls are in the shift bar 
housing bores.

[FIGURE: C95551A.gif]

Install the gasket and the shift lever housing on the shift bar 
housing, fitting the lever into shift block and yoke notches.

[FIGURE: C95561A.gif]

Lightly oil capscrew threads, then install the four capscrews and 
tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C9557B.gif]

Fourth/Fifth Shift Yoke

 Removal 

For models equipped with an oil pump or cooler assembly, disconnect the 
lube line at fitting on shift bar housing.

Remove the retaining capscrews. Jar the top with a mallet to break the 
gasket seal and lift the shift bar housing from the transmission case. Remove 
the gasket.

[FIGURE: C95691A.gif]

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: During disassembly, lay all parts on a clean bench in order of removal 
from housing to facilitate reassembly. Yoke bars not being removed must be 
kept in the neutral position or interlock parts will lock bars.

Tilt the assembly and remove the three sets of tension springs and 
balls from the housing bores.

[FIGURE: C99271A.gif]

Place the housing in a vise with the air valve shaft up. Cut the 
lockwire, remove the capscrews and the oil trough from the housing.

 NOTE: When removing the yoke bars, start with the upper yoke bar, move all 
the bars to the right and out the rear boss bore. Cut the lockwire and remove 
the lock screws from each bar just before their removal.

Move the fourth/fifth yoke bar to the shift bar housing rear, remove 
the shift yoke and shift block from the yoke bar.

[FIGURE: D9940A.gif]

Move the second/third yoke bar to the shift bar housing rear, remove 
the shift yoke and shift block from the yoke bar. As the neutral notch in the 
shift bar clears the rear boss, remove the small interlock pin from the notch 
bar.

[FIGURE: D9941A.gif]

Remove the air valve shaft from the center boss bore.

[FIGURE: D9942A.gif]

Move the short first/reverse yoke bar to the shift bar housing rear. 
Remove the shift yoke from the yoke bar. As the yoke bar is removed from the 
shift bar housing, two interlock balls will drop from the rear boss bottom bore.

[FIGURE: D9943A.gif]

If necessary, remove the plug, spring and reverse-stop plunger from the 
first/reverse shift yoke bore.

[FIGURE: D9944A.gif]

 Assembly 

If previously removed, install the reverse-stop plunger in 
first/reverse shift yoke. Make sure the plunger is fully seated in the yoke 
slot bore.

[FIGURE: D9945A.gif]

Install the spring in the yoke bore and on the plunger shank.

[FIGURE: D9946A.gif]

Install the plug and tighten to compress the spring. Back the plug out 
one and one-half turns and stake plug through the small hole in the yoke.

 NOTE: Start with the lower shift bore of the rear boss and move to the left 
(front of the housing). Keep bars in the neutral position during installation. 
Do not exceed the recommended torque ratings for the yoke lock screws as 
overtightening can distort the yoke bars.

Secure the shift bar housing in a vise. Hold the notched-end of the 
first/reverse yoke bar. Install the bar in the lower bore of the shift bar 
housing bosses. Position the yoke on the bar between the bosses. Install the 
yoke lock screw and tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Secure 
with lockwire.

[FIGURE: D9947A.gif]

Install the air valve shaft in the center bore.

[FIGURE: C99411A.gif]

Install one interlock ball in the rear top bore.

[FIGURE: C99401A.gif]

 NOTE: The interlock pin must remain in a vertical position during reassembly 
as rotation of the bar causes the pin to jam in the tension spring bores.

While holding the notched end of the bar, install the second/third yoke 
bar in the housing boss middle bore. Position the shift block on the bar 
between the center and the rear bosses, and the yoke on the bar between the 
front and center bosses, the long hub to the front of the housing. Just before 
inserting the notched end of the rear boss bar, install the small interlock 
pin vertically in the neutral notch bore. Install the block and yoke lock 
screws and tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Secure with 
lockwire.

[FIGURE: D9948A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Auxiliary Countershaft Assemblies

 Timing Procedures 

It is essential that both countershaft assemblies of the front and 
auxiliary sections are timed. This ensures proper tooth contact is made 
between mainshaft gears seeking to center on the mainshaft during torque 
transfer, and mating countershaft gears that distribute the load evenly. If 
not properly timed, serious damage to the transmission is likely to result 
from unequal tooth contact causing the mainshaft gears to climb out of 
equilibrium.

Timing is a simple procedure of marking the appropriate teeth of a 
gearset prior to installation and placing them in proper mesh while in the 
transmission. In the front section, it is necessary to time only the drive 
gearset. And depending on the model, only the LO range, deep reduction, or 
splitter gearset is timed in the auxiliary section.

 Front Section 

Marking countershaft drive gear teeth.

Prior to placing each countershaft assembly into case, clearly mark the 
tooth located directly over the keyway of drive gear as shown. This tooth is 
stamped with an O to aid identification.

[FIGURE: C8921B.gif]

Marking main drive gear teeth.

Mark any two adjacent teeth on the main drive gear.

Mark the two adjacent teeth located directly opposite the first set 
marked on the main drive gear. As shown below, there should be an equal number 
of unmarked gear teeth on each side between the marked sets.

[FIGURE: C8922B.gif]

Meshing marked countershaft drive gear teeth with marked main drive 
gear teeth. After placing the mainshaft assembly into case, the countershaft 
bearings are installed to complete installation of the countershaft assemblies.

When installing the bearings on left countershaft, mesh the marked 
tooth of countershaft drive gear with either set of two marked teeth on the 
main drive gear.

Repeat the procedure when installing the bearings on right 
countershaft, making use of the remaining set of two marked teeth on the main 
drive to time assembly.

[FIGURE: C8923B.gif]

 Auxiliary Section 

The auxiliary section is different from the standard because of the 
helical gear design; therefore, review this procedure before reassembly.

Mark any tooth on the LO range gear. Then mark a tooth located directly 
opposite the first marked.

Mark any tooth on the reduction gear. Then mark a tooth located 
directly opposite the first marked.

Prior to placing each auxiliary countershaft assembly into housing, 
mark the two teeth on the LO range gear of each auxiliary countershaft 
assembly stamped with the two Os. Repeat procedure on the reduction gear of 
each auxiliary countershaft.

Install the auxiliary countershaft in the auxiliary housing, aligning 
the timing marks on the countershaft with the LO range gear and the reduction 
gear.

Seat the auxiliary countershaft bearings.

Install an auxiliary countershaft retaining strap in each countershaft.

 Installation 

If previously removed, install the countershaft bearings on each of the 
countershafts.

[FIGURE: C12731A.gif]

Locate the two Os stamped in each countershaft and mark the adjoining 
teeth with a highly visible print or dye. Repeat the procedure on each 
auxiliary countershaft reduction gear.

[FIGURE: C12647A.gif]

To assist in assembly of the auxiliary section, you can make this 
auxiliary section fixture out of a section of 2 x 12.

[FIGURE: C12054A.gif]

Place the two countershafts in the fixture or on a flat bench with the 
large HI range gears down.

[FIGURE: C12732A.gif]

Position the auxiliary mainshaft assembly between the two 
countershafts. Make sure the timing marks on each countershaft are aligned 
with the LO range gear and the reduction gear on the mainshaft. Install 
bearing inner spacer, if so equipped, on output shaft.

[FIGURE: C12648A.gif]

Install the reduction yoke in either the sliding clutch or output 
shaft. Install the range yoke in the synchronizer sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C12649A.gif]

Auxiliary Housing and Range and Reduction Cylinder Assemblies, Assembly

Install the complete bearing race in the auxiliary housing bearing bore.

[FIGURE: C12650A.gif]

Temporarily install the rear bearing cover with two capscrews.

[FIGURE: C12651A.gif]

Place the auxiliary housing assembly over the output shaft and

[FIGURE: C12652A.gif]

If removed, lubricate the range cylinder and reduction cylinder O-rings 
with Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification

specification ESR-M13P4-A. Install the cylinder assembly housing in the

[FIGURE: C12666A.gif]

Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification

Install the nut and tighten to 95-115 Nm (70-85 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12733A.gif]

Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A 
and install.

(70-85 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12734A.gif]

Install the insert valve with flat side to the side. Install and 
tighten the insert valve retaining nut.

[FIGURE: D9851A.gif]

Install the cylinder cover gasket and cylinder cover. Apply Threadlock®
 and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to capscrew threads. Then, install and tighten the 
five capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

Install the countershaft bearing race, with the tapered side forward, 
into the auxiliary bores. Complete installation with a flanged-end driver and 
maul.

 NOTE: Do not use an air wrench. Tighten only until the bolts are snug.

Install an auxiliary countershaft retaining strap or new Eaton Tool 
T-65514-S with two capscrews that were removed from the auxiliary countershaft 
bearing covers. Install a 0.375 x 2.50-inch capscrew through the center of the 
auxiliary countershaft retaining strap, then thread capscrew into auxiliary 
countershaft. Repeat this step for other auxiliary countershaft, and make sure 
the reduction gears are still in time.

[FIGURE: C12735A.gif]

Remove the rear bearing cover.

Heat the rear bearing cone and install on the output shaft, taper side 
down and inside the bearing cup. Do not heat the bearing above 136°
C (277°F). If possible, use heat lamps as 
the source.

[FIGURE: C12655A.gif]

Position gasket on the mounting surface and install the rear bearing 
cover on the auxiliary housing. Apply Threadlock® and Sealer 
EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to 
capscrew threads. Then, install and tighten the capscrews to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Countershaft Bearings, Removal

 NOTE: The front and rear countershaft bearings are removed in the following 
procedure; however, for removal of the mainshaft, remove the right 
countershaft bearings only.

Temporarily install the auxiliary drive gear on the mainshaft. Remove 
the snap ring from each countershaft rear groove.

Remove the six capscrews from the front bearing cover, and remove the 
cover.

 NOTE: This procedure damages the bearings and should not be done unless 
replacement of the bearings is planned.

From inside the transmission case, use a soft bar and maul to drive the 
countershaft rear bearings to the rear and from the transmission case bores.

[FIGURE: D9867A.gif]

Remove the capscrew and the front bearing retainer plate from the 
countershaft.

 NOTE: The soft bar used must have a flattened end that is large enough so as 
not to damage holes for the roll pin and capscrew.

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft to the rear as far as 
possible. This partially underseats the front bearing.

[FIGURE: D9868A.gif]

From the rear of the transmission case, use a soft bar and maul to 
drive the upper countershaft forward to unseat the front bearing from the 
transmission case bore and expose the bearing snap ring.

 NOTE: The bearing inner race remains pressed on the countershaft.

Use a bearing puller or pry bars to remove the countershaft front 
bearing.

 Removal 

 CAUTION: The reverse and fifth gear is free and can fall from the mainshaft. 

Block the right countershaft assembly against case wall and pull the 
mainshaft assembly to the rear to free pilot from pocket of input shaft. Tilt 
front of mainshaft up and lift the assembly from case. Use caution as the 
reverse gear is free and can fall from shaft.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Special Procedure for Changing Input Shaft

 NOTE: Some cases of service repair may require replacement of the input shaft 
because of clutch wear on the splines. In these instances, the input shaft can 
be removed without disassembling the transmission other than removing the 
shift bar housing. Removal of the clutch housing is optional. The detailed 
procedure is as follows.

 Input Shaft 

[FIGURE: C11766B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

7051

Gasket

2

7030

Snap Ring

3

7025

Bearing

4

7064

Snap Ring

5

7005

Case

6

7120

Bushing

7

7017

Input Shaft

8

7158

Drive Gear

9

7A059

Spacer

10

7050

Front Bearing Cover (Pull-Type)

 Removal 

Remove the shift bar housing from transmission case. Refer to Shift Bar 
Housing in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 NOTE: To prevent lubricant leakage during shipment, a small rubber lip seal 
is installed on the transmission input shaft under the front cover. This seal 
should be removed and discarded during transmission repair.

Remove the remaining capscrews, front bearing cover and gasket. If 
necessary, service the oil seal of model covers so equipped.

Remove the bearing retaining snap ring from input shaft groove.

Push down on the input shaft to cock the bearing in the bore. Drive the 
input shaft toward the transmission rear through the bearing as far as 
possible. Pull the input shaft forward to expose the bearing.

Use pry bars or screwdrivers to complete removal of the bearing.

Remove the spacer and the snap ring.

Pull the input shaft forward and out of the drive gear and case.

 Installation 

If necessary, replace the bushing in the input shaft pocket. Install 
input shaft into drive gear.

Install the snap ring in the snap ring groove inside the drive gear.

Install the spacer on the input shaft.

Install the bearing on the input shaft.

Install the bearing retainer snap ring.

Install the front bearing cover and gasket. Make sure to align the oil 
return hole in the case with the hole in the cover. Lightly oil capscrew 
threads. Then, install capscrews and tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft)

Install the shift bar housing. Refer to Shift Bar 
Housing , Installation in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 Removal and Disassembly 

 NOTE: Except for the power takeoff gears, the left and right countershaft 
assemblies are identical and are disassembled in the same manner.

Move the right countershaft assembly to the rear as far as possible so 
the front of the shaft can be removed from the transmission case bore and 
moved to the center of the transmission case. Lift the assembly from the 
transmission case and repeat the procedure for the left countershaft assembly.

Remove the drive gear retaining snap ring from each countershaft front.

[FIGURE: D9908A.gif]

 NOTE: Never use the power takeoff gear (fourth gear on RT-RTO-14715 
transmissions) as a pressing base. The narrow face width of this gear makes it 
very susceptible to breakage.

Using the rear face of the overdrive gear as a base, press the drive 
gear, power takeoff gear (fourth gear on RT-RTO-14715 transmissions) and the 
overdrive gear from each countershaft. This will also remove the front bearing 
inner race from the countershafts.

[FIGURE: D9909A.gif]

Using the rear face of third gear as a base, press the third gears from 
each countershaft.

RT-RTO-14715 and RT-RTX-15715 transmissions: using the rear face of 
second gear as a base, press the third and second gears from each countershaft.

[FIGURE: D9910A.gif]

Remove the key and roll pin from the countershaft. Using the rear face 
of second gear as a base, press the second gear from the countershaft.

Remove the key from the countershaft. No other gears can be pressed 
from the countershaft.

[FIGURE: D9911A.gif]

Remove the right reverse idler gear assembly. Steps for removal are 
identical to the left reverse idler gear assembly removal procedure.

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Except for the power takeoff gears, the right and left countershaft 
assemblies are identical and are assembled in the same manner.

If removed, install the roll pin and key in the countershaft keyway.

Align the keyway with the countershaft key. Press the second gear on 
the countershaft, long hub to the countershaft front.

[FIGURE: D9912A.gif]

Install the long key in the countershaft keyway. Press the third gear 
on the countershaft, long gear hub against second speed gear hub.

Press the overdrive gear on the countershaft, long gear hub to 
countershaft front.

RT-RTO-14715 transmissions: press the fourth gear on the countershaft, 
long gear hub to countershaft front.

[FIGURE: D9913A.gif]

Start the power takeoff gear onto the countershaft, bullet-nose side of 
teeth facing up and toward countershaft rear. Align the drive gear keyway with 
the countershaft key and press BOTH gears onto the shaft with the drive gear 
long hub against the power takeoff gear.

 NOTE: The left countershaft assembly has a 47-tooth power takeoff gear; the 
right countershaft assembly has a 45-tooth power takeoff gear.

To avoid confusion during installation, mark the end of the left 
countershaft with an L; mark the end of the right countershaft with an R.

[FIGURE: D9914A.gif]

Install the drive gear retaining snap ring in the countershaft front 
groove.

[FIGURE: D9908A.gif]

 NOTE: Mark the countershaft drive gear for timing purposes. On each 
countershaft drive gear, mark the tooth aligned with the gear keyway and 
stamped with an O for easy identification. Use a highly visible color of 
toolmaker's dye to make timing marks.

Use a flanged-end driver to install the bearing inner race on the 
countershaft, shoulder of race against shoulder of countershaft.

[FIGURE: D9915A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Right Reverse Idler Gear Assembly, Installation

If any of the magnets in the bottom of the case were damaged during 
disassembly, chip them out and glue new magnets into place using Gasket and 
Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESR-M11P17-A and ESE-M2G52-A.

If removed, press the needle bearing in reverse idler gear bore.

[FIGURE: D9916A.gif]

Install the washer on the idler shaft.

Position the reverse idler bearing, gear, and washer in the 
transmission case. Install the idler shaft through the idler gear and into the 
transmission case bore. Make sure the idler shaft is seated in the bore of the 
support boss as far forward as possible.

[FIGURE: D9917A.gif]

Install the washer and the stop nut on front of the idler shaft. 
Tighten the nut to 68-81 Nm (50-60 lb-ft) with threads oiled.

[FIGURE: D9918B.gif]

Install the pipe plug in the reverse idler shaft.

[FIGURE: D9919A.gif]

 NOTE: The bearing inner race is installed on the auxiliary countershaft front 
and never with the outer race.

Install the outer race of the auxiliary countershaft front bearing with 
a driver into the transmission case bore and against the retaining washer.

[FIGURE: D9920A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Countershaft Bearing, LH, Installation

Move the left countershaft assembly to the rear, and insert the 
countershaft support tool or blocking to center shaft in the transmission case 
rear bore.

[FIGURE: D9922A.gif]

Use a flanged-end bearing driver to completely seat the front bearing 
or bearing outer race in the transmission case bore.

[FIGURE: D9923A.gif]

Position the retainer plate on the left countershaft front. Roll pin in 
hole at shaft end. Lightly oil capscrew threads. Then, install and tighten 
3/8-24 capscrew to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft), 1/2-20 capscrew to 
34-47 Nm (25-35 lb-ft) or 5/8-18 capscrew to 122-163 Nm
 (90-120 lb-ft). Secure with lockwire.

Remove the countershaft support tool or blocking from the transmission 
case rear bore. Install the left countershaft rear bearing with the larger 
inside diameter chamfer to the shaft front. Install the snap ring in the left 
countershaft rear groove.

[FIGURE: D9924A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Input Shaft and Main Drive Gear Assembly, Installation and Timing

If removed, install the snap ring in the main drive gear inside diameter.

Mark the main drive gear for timing purposes. Mark any two adjacent 
teeth on the drive gear and repeat the procedure for the two adjacent teeth 
directly opposite the first set marked. A highly visible color of toolmaker's 
dye is recommended for making the timing marks.

[FIGURE: D9925A.gif]

Mesh the marked tooth of the left countershaft drive gear with either 
set of the two marked teeth on the main drive gear. Slide the input shaft 
through the main drive gear.

[FIGURE: D9926A.gif]

Install the drive gear spacer and the bearing on the input shaft with 
the external snap ring to the outside.

[FIGURE: D9927A.gif]

Install the drive gear bearing on the input shaft, seat bearing into 
case bore with the proper bearing driver.

[FIGURE: D9928A.gif]

Temporarily install the front bearing cover (RT models only). For 
RTX-RTO models leave bearing cover off. 

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the input shaft through the bearing. 
Remove the front bearing cover.

[FIGURE: D9929A.gif]

Install the bearing retainer snap ring.

[FIGURE: D9930A.gif]

Install the front bearing cover and gasket, and make sure to align the 
oil return hole in the case with the cover hole. Lightly oil capscrew threads. 
Then, install six capscrews and tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 
lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mainshaft Assembly, Assembly and Partial Installation

If removed, install the corresponding snap rings in the inside diameter 
of the mainshaft gears.

Secure the mainshaft in a vise equipped with brass jaws or wood blocks, 
pilot end of the shaft down. If removed, install the roll pin in the keyway.

[FIGURE: D9877A.gif]

Install the overdrive gear (fourth gear on RT-RTO-14715 and 
RT-RTX-15715 transmissions) limit washer on the mainshaft, flat side of washer 
up. Rotate washer in the first or bottom groove of the mainshaft to align the 
splines of the washer with those of the mainshaft. Install the key in the 
mainshaft keyway to lock washer in place.

Install the spacer on the shaft against the washer.

[FIGURE: D9878A.gif]

 NOTE: Gear tolerance washers are internally splined and locked to the 
mainshaft by the key. Gear spacers are externally splined to engage with 
clutching teeth in the gear hubs. There is one tolerance washer and one spacer 
for each gear in the mainshaft assembly.

Install the overdrive (fourth) gear on the mainshaft, clutching teeth 
down and engaged with the external splines of the spacer.

[FIGURE: D9879A.gif]

Install the third gear on the shaft against the overdrive (fourth) 
gear, clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: D9880A.gif]

Install the spacer in third gear, engaging the external splines of 
spacer with clutching teeth of the gear.

[FIGURE: D9881A.gif]

Remove the key from the keyway and install the third gear tolerance 
washer on the mainshaft, flat side of the washer down and against the spacer. 
Rotate the washer in the second groove of the mainshaft to align the splines 
of the washer with those of the mainshaft, and reinsert the key in the keyway 
to lock the washer in place.

[FIGURE: D9882A.gif]

 NOTE: New style tolerance washers come in a full range of tolerances as 
corresponding colors listed below "plus red." (Example: "Orange plus red" 
tolerance washer has an inch tolerance thickness of 6.55-6.60 mm [
0.258-0.260 inch].) Refer to Selective Tolerance Washers 
chart in the Specifications portion of this section for available thickness.

Insert two large screwdrivers between the third and overdrive (fourth) 
gears to check axial clearances. Apply slight downward pressure on the 
screwdriver handles to spread the gears evenly. Make sure the gear hubs are 
parallel. Insert a feeler gauge between the hubs. Correct axial clearance is 
0.152-0.381 mm (0.006-0.015 inch). If the clearance is less than the minimum 
0.152-mm (0.006-inch) tolerance, the tolerance washer in the third gear must 
be replaced by a thinner tolerance washer. This increases the axial clearance 
between the gears. If the clearance checked is greater than the maximum 
0.381-mm (0.015-inch) tolerance, a thicker tolerance washer must be installed 
in the third gear. This will decrease the axial clearance between the gears.

[FIGURE: D9883A.gif]

Install the second/third speed sliding clutch, aligning the missing 
internal spline of the sliding clutch with the key in the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: D9884A.gif]

Remove the key from the keyway. Install the second gear tolerance 
washer on the mainshaft, flat side of the washer up. Rotate the washer in the 
third groove of the mainshaft to align the splines of the washer with those of 
the mainshaft, and reinsert the key in the keyway to lock the washer in place.

[FIGURE: D9885A.gif]

Install the spacer on the shaft against the washer.

[FIGURE: D9886A.gif]

Install the second gear on the mainshaft, clutching teeth down and 
engaged with external splines of the spacer.

[FIGURE: D9887A.gif]

Install the first gear on the shaft against second gear, clutching 
teeth up.

[FIGURE: D9888A.gif]

Install the spacer in first gear, engaging the external splines of the 
spacer with clutching teeth of gear.

[FIGURE: D9889A.gif]

Remove the key from the keyway. Install the first gear tolerance washer 
on the mainshaft, flat side of the washer down and against the spacer. Rotate 
the washer in the fourth groove of the mainshaft to align the splines of the 
washer with those of the mainshaft and insert the key in the keyway to lock 
washer in place.

[FIGURE: D9890A.gif]

Check the axial clearance between first and second gears and adjust as 
required. Refer to Step 9 for this procedure.

[FIGURE: D9891A.gif]

Install the first/reverse speed sliding clutch, aligning the missing 
internal spline of sliding clutch with the key in the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: D9892A.gif]

Remove the key from the keyway and install the reverse gear tolerance 
washer on the mainshaft, flat side of washer up. Rotate washer in the fifth 
groove of the mainshaft to align the splines of the washer with those of the 
mainshaft and insert key in the keyway to lock the washer in place.

[FIGURE: D9893A.gif]

Install the spacer on the shaft against the washer.

[FIGURE: D9894A.gif]

Install the reverse gear on the mainshaft, clutching teeth down and 
engaged with the spacer external splines.

[FIGURE: D9895A.gif]

Install the snap ring on reverse hub only to check axial clearance 
limits.

[FIGURE: D9896A.gif]

Install the snap ring in the mainshaft groove to retain key in the 
keyway.

[FIGURE: D9897A.gif]

Install the auxiliary drive gear assembly in its proper position on the 
rear of the mainshaft. Install the auxiliary retaining snap ring in the 
mainshaft snap ring groove.

[FIGURE: D9898A.gif]

 NOTE: The following check is made without spreading the gears with 
screwdrivers.

Force both the reverse gear and auxiliary drive gear downward on the 
shaft to flatten their respective snap rings. Making sure the gear hubs are 
parallel, insert a feeler gauge between the reverse gear and auxiliary drive 
gear hubs. Correct axial clearance is 0.152-0.381 mm (0.006-0.015 inch). If 
clearance is less than the minimum 0.152-mm (0.006-inch) tolerance, the 
reverse gear limit washer must be replaced by a thinner limit washer. This 
will increase the axial clearance between the gears. If the clearance checked 
is greater than the maximum 0.381-mm (0.015-inch) tolerance, a thicker limit 
washer must be installed in the reverse gear. This will decrease the axial 
clearance between the gears.

[FIGURE: D9899A.gif]

With the proper reverse gear limit washer installed on the mainshaft, 
remove the auxiliary drive gear assembly and reverse gear.

Install the reverse gear on the mainshaft. Engage the gear clutching 
teeth with the spacer splines and sliding clutch. Move the reverse gear 
against the first gear.

[FIGURE: D9900A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not replace the reverse gear internal snap ring at this time.

Remove the mainshaft assembly from the vise. Align the missing internal 
spline of fourth/fifth speed sliding clutch with key in the mainshaft and 
install on the shaft front, engaging the external splines of the sliding 
clutch with the clutching teeth of the overdrive (fourth) gear.

[FIGURE: D9901A.gif]

Block the right countershaft assembly against the transmission case 
wall and lower the mainshaft assembly into position with the reverse gear held 
against the first gear and the shaft rear moved into the transmission case bore.

[FIGURE: D9902A.gif]

Move the pilot end of the mainshaft into the input shaft pocket bushing.

With the reverse gear remaining against first gear, mesh the 
corresponding forward gears of the left countershaft assembly. Check to make 
sure that the marked tooth on the left countershaft drive gear has remained in 
mesh with the marked set of teeth on the main drive gear.

Center the rear of the mainshaft in the transmission case bore. Install 
the auxiliary drive gear assembly on the shaft, partially seating the bearing 
in the bore. Do not complete installation at this time.

================================================================================
