REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Countershaft Bearing, RH, Installation and Timing of Right 
Countershaft Assembly

 NOTE: The left countershaft assembly MUST remain in time with the main drive 
gear when timing the right countershaft assembly.

Remove blocking from the right countershaft assembly and place it 
parallel to the mainshaft assembly. Mesh the marked tooth of the right 
countershaft drive gear with the remaining set of two marked teeth on the main 
drive gear.

Insert the countershaft support tool or blocking in the rear bearing 
bore.

[FIGURE: D9931A.gif]

Position the front countershaft bearing in front bearing bore. Use the 
proper bearing driver to seat the bearing.

[FIGURE: D9932A.gif]

Install the retainer washer and capscrew. Make sure to match roll pin 
in the retainer with the inner bearing hole. Lightly oil capscrew threads. 
Then, install and tighten 3/8-24 capscrew to 27-34 Nm (20-25 
lb-ft), 1/2-20 capscrew to 34-47 Nm (25-35 lb-ft) or 5/8-18 
capscrew to 122-163 Nm (90-120 lb-ft). Secure with lockwire.

Position the countershaft rear bearing in the rear bearing bore. Use 
the proper bearing driver to seat bearing in bore. Install the snap ring in 
the right countershaft rear groove.

[FIGURE: D9933A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not engage the sliding clutches with more than one gear at a time. 
This locks the gearing and prevents the mainshaft and the countershaft 
assemblies from rotating.

Move the reverse gear to the mainshaft rear and use a screwdriver to 
engage the sliding clutches with all the forward speed gears. A sliding clutch 
that does not engage with a gear indicates the gearset is not in proper mesh. 
The bearings of the right countershaft need to be removed and the drive 
gearset timed.

[FIGURE: D9934A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Complete Installation of Mainshaft and Auxiliary Drive Gear Assemblies

Remove the auxiliary drive gear assembly from the mainshaft and the 
rear bearing bore. Block the mainshaft so it does not move when removing the 
auxiliary drive gear.

[FIGURE: D9935A.gif]

Move the reverse gear to the rear as far as possible, meshing teeth of 
the reverse gear with those of the reverse idler gears.

[FIGURE: D9936A.gif]

Align the external splines of the spacer with the clutching teeth of 
the reverse gear and move the spacer forward on the mainshaft and into the 
reverse gear.

[FIGURE: D9937A.gif]

Install the snap ring in the reverse gear hub and move the reverse gear 
forward on the mainshaft and into the proper position in the transmission case.

Install the auxiliary drive gear assembly on mainshaft rear. Use a 
flanged-end driver and maul to seat the bearing in the transmission case bore.

Align the six capscrews holes in retainer with the tapped holes in the 
transmission case. Lightly oil capscrew threads. Then, install and tighten the 
capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Lockwire the capscrews 
in groups of three.

Install the snap ring in the mainshaft end groove.

[FIGURE: D9938A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Clutch Housing Installation

Position the new gasket on housing mounting surface and install the 
clutch housing on the front case, piloting on the six studs and drive gear 
bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C95651A.gif]

Models with cast iron housing, install six nuts with lockwashers and 
tighten to 244-271 Nm (180-200 lb-ft). Models with aluminum 
housing, install six nuts with flatwashers and tighten to 190-203 Nm
 (140-150 lb-ft) with threads oiled.

Install clutch release mechanism, if so equipped.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Auxiliary Section Installation

 NOTE: The front box sliding clutches must be in the neutral position.

Tighten the middle bolt on each countershaft strap until the 
countershafts are snug. Shift the reduction sliding clutch into reduction. 
Attach a chain hoist to the output shaft.

[FIGURE: D9508A.gif]

 NOTE: Shift the reduction sliding clutch into deep reduction before 
installing auxiliary.

With the transmission in the vertical position, block under the clutch 
housing to prevent damage to the input shaft, and position the new gasket on 
the transmission case. Lower the auxiliary assembly on the front case rear.

If the transmission is set in the horizontal position, install the new 
gasket. Set the auxiliary section into position with a hoist, and align on the 
dowel pins.

Install the retaining capscrews in the housing and tighten to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

Install the output shaft yoke to check for the proper auxiliary 
countershaft end play. Remove the countershaft end straps.

[FIGURE: D9299A.gif]

Install a 0.100 gauging shim, from the helical shim kit, in each 
countershaft rear bearing shim bore or use Eaton Tool T-65514-S. Make sure the 
old shim has been removed, and the countershaft rear bearing races are seated 
in the bearing bores.

[FIGURE: D9509A.gif]

Install the two countershaft rear bearing covers and two rear bearing 
capscrews in each cover. The capscrews must be located directly across from 
each other as shown. Tighten the capscrews to 0.8 Nm (7 
lb-in). Do not install the countershaft rear bearing cover gasket.

[FIGURE: D9510B.gif]

Rotate the output shaft six times clockwise, then six times 
counterclockwise to seat the countershaft rear bearings. Use a feeler gauge, 
as close to one capscrew location as possible, and measure the gap between the 
countershaft rear bearing cover and the auxiliary case. Record the 
measurement. Now measure the gap as close to the other capscrew location and 
record the measurement. Average the two measurements. Using the averaged 
measurement, refer to Helical End Play chart in the Specifications 
 portion of this section.

Select the numbers in the left column that compare to the average 
measurement recorded from the countershaft rear bearing cover. Follow the 
column to the right to identify the proper shim to be used in the countershaft 
shim bores. Duplicate this procedure for the other countershaft rear bearing 
cover.

[FIGURE: D9511A.gif]

Remove the countershaft rear bearing covers and gauging shims. Position 
new gaskets on the countershaft rear bearing cover mounting surface, and 
install both rear bearing covers. Apply Threadlock® and 
Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to 
capscrew threads. Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: D9298B.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Companion Flange Installation

Install the speedometer rotor or replacement spacer on the output 
shaft. Install the slinger.

[FIGURE: D9512A.gif]

Lock the transmission by engaging two mainshaft gears with their 
sliding clutches.

[FIGURE: C95591A.gif]

Install the yoke on the output shaft splines and move it into the rear 
bearing cover.

Lightly oil the threads on the output shaft. Install the washer, if 
equipped, and nut on the output shaft. Tighten the nut to 610-678 Nm
 (450-500 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Shift Bar Housing, Installation

Place all three mainshaft sliding clutches in the neutral position.

[FIGURE: C12736A.gif]

 NOTE: Avoid tilting the shift bar housing assembly during installation as the 
three sets of tension springs and balls are free to be released from the 
housing bores.

Position a new shift bar housing gasket on the transmission case. With 
all three shift bars in the neutral position, install the shift bar housing 
assembly fitting the shift yokes into the slots of the corresponding sliding 
clutches.

Lightly oil capscrew threads. Then, install and tighten the capscrews 
to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow

 Front Section 

 NOTE: These numbered steps correspond to the numbers on the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear.

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

 Auxiliary Section 

 LO Range 

 NOTE: These numbered steps correspond to the numbers on the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear. 

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged low range 
gear on range mainshaft or output shaft.

Torque is transferred to range mainshaft or output shaft through 
sliding clutch.

Torque is delivered to driveline as LO RANGE 1st.

 Power Flow — Front Section and Auxiliary Section (LO 
Range) 

[FIGURE: DC0280A.gif]

 HI Range 

 NOTE: These numbered steps correspond to the numbers on the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear.

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear transfers torque directly to the range 
mainshaft or output shaft through engaged sliding clutch.

Torque is delivered through range mainshaft and/or output shaft to 
driveline as HI RANGE 6th.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

 CAUTION: The use of mild EP gear oil or multipurpose gear oil is not 
recommended, but if these gear oils are used, be sure to adhere to the 
following limitations. 

 CAUTION: Do not use mild EP gear oil or multipurpose gear oil when operating 
temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). Many 
of these gear oils, particularly 85W140, break down above 110°
C (230°F) and coat seals, bearings and gears with deposits 
that can cause premature failures. If these deposits are observed (especially 
a coating on seal areas causing oil leakage), change to Eaton Roadranger®
 CD50 transmission fluid, heavy-duty engine oil or mineral 
gear oil to ensure maximum component life and to maintain your warranty with 
Eaton. Refer to Operating Temperatures in this section. 

 CAUTION: Additives and friction modifiers are not recommended for use in Eaton 
Fuller transmissions. 

Proper lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program. If the oil is not doing its job, or if the oil level is 
ignored, all the maintenance procedures in the world are not going to keep the 
transmission running or ensure long transmission life.

Eaton Fuller transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in a bath of oil circulated by the motion of gears and shafts.

All parts will be amply lubricated if these procedures are closely 
followed:

Maintain oil level and inspect regularly.

Change oil regularly.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 LUBRICATION CHANGE AND INSPECTION

Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid

HIGHWAY USE

Every 16 093 km (10,000 miles)

Check fluid level. Check for leaks.

Every 402 325 km) (250,000 miles)

Change transmission fluid.

 OFF-HIGHWAY USE 

Every 40 hours

Inspect fluid level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission fluid where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission fluid (normal off-highway use).

 HIGHWAY USE — Heavy-Duty Engine Lubricant or Mineral 
Gear Lubricant 

First 4 828 to 8 047 km (3,000 to 5,000 miles)

Factory fill initial drain.

Every 16 093 km (10,000 miles)

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 80 465 km (50,000 miles)

Change transmission lubricant.

 OFF-HIGHWAY USE 

First 30 hours

Change transmission lubricant on new units.

Every 40 hours

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission lubricant where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission lubricant (normal off-highway use).

 Proper Oil Level 

Make sure oil is level with filler opening. Because you can reach oil 
with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. An oil level of 25.4 mm 
(1 inch) is equal to approximately 3.7 liters (1 gallon) of oil.

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Draining Oil 

Drain transmission while oil is warm. To drain oil remove the drain 
plug at bottom of case. Clean the drain plug before reinstalling.

 Refilling 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. 

Clean case around filler plug and remove plug from side of case. Fill 
transmission to the level of the filler opening. If transmission has two 
filler openings, fill to level of both openings.

The exact amount of oil will depend on the transmission inclination and 
model. Do not overfill — this will cause oil to be forced out 
of the transmission.

 Proper Lubrication Levels as Related to Transmission Installation Angles 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication can occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

The chart below illustrates the safe percent of upgrade on which the 
transmission can be used with various chassis mounting angles. For example: if 
you have a four-degree transmission mounting angle, then eight degrees (or 14 
percent of grade) is equal to the limit of 12 degrees. If you have a 
zero-degree mounting angle, the transmission can be operated on a 12 degree 
(21 percent) grade.

Anytime the transmission operating angle of 12 degrees is exceeded for 
an extended period of time, the transmission must be equipped with an oil pump 
or cooler kit to ensure proper lubrication.

Note on the chart the effect low oil levels can have on safe operating 
angles. Allowing the oil level to fall one-half inch below the filler plug 
hole reduces the degree of grade by approximately three degrees (5.5 percent).

[FIGURE: C11746A.gif]

 Operating Temperatures 

 With Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid, 
Heavy-Duty Engine Oil and Mineral Oil 

The transmission must not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent 
operating temperatures to 149°C (300°F) will 
not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures above 120°C 
(250°F) increase the lubricant's rate of oxidation and 
shorten its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 120°
C (250°F), the transmission may require 
more frequent oil changes or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F).

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

exhaust system too close to transmission

high horsepower, overdrive operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

Transmission oil coolers are recommended with the following engines:

350 HP and above with overdrive transmissions

Transmission oil coolers are required with the following engines:

399 HP and above with overdrive transmissions and GCW's over 40,824 kg 
(90,000 lb).

399 HP and above and 1898 Nm (1400 lb-ft) or greater 
torque

450 HP and above

 With EP or Multipurpose Gear Oil 

Mild EP gear oil and multipurpose gear oil are not recommended when 
lubricant operating temperatures are above 110°C (230°
F). In addition, transmission oil coolers are not 
recommended with these gear oils, since the oil cooler materials can be 
attacked by these gear oils. The lower temperature limit and oil cooler 
restriction with these gear oils generally limit their success to milder 
applications.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission

 Removal 

Drain air system and disconnect air lines at Roadranger®
 valve and position out of way. Refer to Section 07-06 .

Drain transmission oil.

If required, remove seat belt and seat assembly. Refer to appropriate 
Group 01 section.

Remove shift lever. Refer to Shift Lever Housing procedure in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Disconnect wiring connectors.

Raise vehicle on hoist.

Disconnect and remove fuel lines and bracketry as required. Refer to 
 Section 10-01 .

Remove exhaust as required. 

Remove driveshaft assembly. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Disconnect air lines at transmission. Refer to Section 07-06 .

If so equipped, disconnect low oil level indicator sensor.

Disconnect clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

Remove clutch housing cover.

Position Rotunda 20-Ton Air/Hydraulic Truck Service Jack 164-R3506 or 
equivalent under the transmission and install jack.

Remove transmission clutch housing-to-engine retaining bolts and raise 
transmission slightly with jack.

Remove top engine support bracket retaining nut and insulators.

Remove both jam nuts and insulators.

Lower transmission from vehicle.

 Installation 

Use transmission jack to lift transmission into place.

Install insulator retainer assembly.

 NOTE: For installing and aligning clutch discs, plates, flywheel and shafts, 
refer to Section 08-01 .

Install and align clutch assembly and install clutch housing-to-engine 
retaining bolts. Tighten to 122-136 Nm (90-100 lb-ft).

Position rear engine support bracket on transmission. Install 
insulators and tighten jam nut to 203-278 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 
Tighten remaining jam nut finger-tight and apply two additional turns.

Install insulators and top rear engine support bracket retaining nut. 
Tighten nut to 203-278 Nm (150-205 lb-ft).

Remove transmission jack.

Install clutch housing cover.

Connect clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

Install fuel lines and bracketry. Refer to Section 10-01 .

If so equipped, connect low oil lever indicator sensor.

Connect air lines to transmission. Refer to Section 07-06 .

Install exhaust, if removed. 

Install driveshaft assembly. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Lower vehicle.

Reconnect all wiring connectors.

Install shift lever. Refer to Shift Lever Housing procedure in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Connect air lines to Roadranger® valve. Refer to 
 Section 07-06 .

Install seat belt and seat assembly, if removed. Refer to appropriate 
Group 01 section.

Refill transmission will appropriate type and quantity oil. Refer to Transmission Oil Drain and Refill 
 procedure in the Removal and Installation 
portion of this section.

[FIGURE: C11997A.gif]

 NOTE: During disassembly, lay all parts on a clean bench in order of removal 
from housing to facilitate reassembly. Yoke bars not being removed must be 
kept in the neutral position or interlock parts will lock bars.

Tilt the assembly and remove the three sets of tension springs and 
balls from bores in top of housing.

[FIGURE: C11998A.gif]

Secure the assembly in a vise with air valve shaft up and remove gasket 
material.

[FIGURE: C12000A.gif]

Remove the two capscrews from the oil trough and remove assembly. Cut 
the lockwire and remove the lock screws from each yoke bar and block.

[FIGURE: C12001A.gif]

 NOTE: When removing the yoke bars, start with the upper yoke bar; move all 
the bars to the right and out the rear boss bore.

Move the 4th/5th yoke bar to the rear of housing, removing the yoke and 
block from bar.

[FIGURE: C12002A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12003A.gif]

Remove the air valve shaft from bore at top of center boss.

[FIGURE: C12004A.gif]

Move the short 1st/Reverse yoke bar to the rear of housing, removing 
the yoke from bar. As the yoke bar is removed from housing, two 3/4-inch 
interlock balls will drop from bottom bore of rear boss.

[FIGURE: C12005A.gif]

If necessary, remove the plug, spring and reverse-stop plunger from 
bore in 1st/Reverse shift yoke.

[FIGURE: C12006A.gif]

 Assembly 

If previously removed, install the reverse-stop plunger and spring in 
1st/Reverse shift yoke, making sure plunger is fully seated in bore at yoke 
slot. Install the plug and tighten to compress the spring; back the plug out 1 
to 1-1/2 turns after it bottoms.

[FIGURE: C12007A.gif]

Complete the yoke assembly process by staking the plug through the 
small hole in yoke.

[FIGURE: C12008A.gif]

 NOTE: Start with the lower shift bore of rear boss and move to the left 
(front of housing). Keep bars in the neutral position during installation. Do 
not exceed the recommended torque ratings for yoke lock screws, as 
overtightening can distort shift bars.

Install 1st/Reverse yoke bar in the lower bore boss. Place the air 
valve shaft in its bore, and place one interlock ball in the interlock bore 
down against the 1st/Reverse bar.

[FIGURE: C12009A.gif]

 NOTE: Interlock pin must remain in a vertical position during reassembly, as 
rotation of the bar will cause pin to jam in tension spring bores.

Holding notched end of bar, install the 2nd/3rd yoke bar in middle bore 
of housing boss, positioning the shift block on bar between the front and 
center bosses, with long hub to the front of housing. Just prior to inserting 
notched end of bar in rear boss, install the small interlock pin vertically in 
bore at neutral notch. Install and tighten the block and yoke lock screws to 
47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Secure lock screws with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C12010A.gif]

Install the other 3/4-inch interlock ball in bore at top of rear boss. 
This ball rides between the 2nd/3rd and 4th/5th yoke bars.

[FIGURE: C12011A.gif]

Holding notched end of bar, install the 4th/5th yoke bar in upper bore 
of housing boss, positioning the shift block on bar between the center and 
rear bosses, and the yoke on bar between the front and center bosses, with 
long hub to the rear of housing. Install and tighten the block and yoke lock 
screws to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Secure lock screws with 
lockwire.

[FIGURE: C12012A.gif]

Install the oil trough on shift bar housing. Lightly oil capscrew 
threads. Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft). Secure capscrews with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C12013B.gif]

Remove the assembly from vise and install the three tension balls, one 
in each bore on top of housing. Place a detent spring over each ball to 
complete the assembly.

 Auxiliary Countershaft Assembly

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Auxiliary Countershaft Assemblies

 Timing Procedures 

It is essential that both countershaft assemblies of the front and 
auxiliary sections are timed. This ensures proper tooth contact is made 
between mainshaft gears seeking to center on the mainshaft during torque 
transfer, and mating countershaft gears that distribute the load evenly. If 
not properly timed, serious damage to the transmission is likely to result 
from unequal tooth contact causing the mainshaft gears to climb out of 
equilibrium.

Timing is a simple procedure of marking the appropriate teeth of a 
gearset prior to installation and placing them in proper mesh while in the 
transmission. In the front section, it is necessary to time only the drive 
gearset. And depending on the model, only the LO range, deep reduction, or 
splitter gearset is timed in the auxiliary section.

 Front Section 

Marking countershaft drive gear teeth.

Prior to placing each countershaft assembly into case, clearly mark the 
tooth located directly over the keyway of drive gear as shown. This tooth is 
stamped with an O to aid identification.

[FIGURE: C8921B.gif]

Marking main drive gear teeth.

Mark any two adjacent teeth on the main drive gear.

Mark the two adjacent teeth located directly opposite the first set 
marked on the main drive gear. As shown below, there should be an equal number 
of unmarked gear teeth on each side between the marked sets.

[FIGURE: C8922B.gif]

Meshing marked countershaft drive gear teeth with marked main drive 
gear teeth. After placing the mainshaft assembly into case, the countershaft 
bearings are installed to complete installation of the countershaft assemblies.

When installing the bearings on left countershaft, mesh the marked 
tooth of countershaft drive gear with either set of two marked teeth on the 
main drive gear.

Repeat the procedure when installing the bearings on right 
countershaft, making use of the remaining set of two marked teeth on the main 
drive to time assembly.

[FIGURE: C8923B.gif]

 Auxiliary Section 

The auxiliary section is different from the standard because of the 
helical gear design; therefore, review this procedure before reassembly.

Mark any tooth on the LO range gear. Then mark a tooth located directly 
opposite the first marked.

Prior to placing each auxiliary countershaft assembly into housing, 
mark the two teeth on the LO range gear of each auxiliary countershaft 
assembly stamped with the two O's. Repeat procedure on the reduction gear of 
each auxiliary countershaft.

Install the auxiliary countershaft in the auxiliary housing aligning 
the timing marks on the countershaft with the LO range gear and the reduction 
gear.

Seat the auxiliary countershaft bearings.

 Installation 

If previously removed, install the countershaft bearings on each of the 
countershafts.

[FIGURE: C12052A.gif]

Locate the O stamped in each countershaft and mark the adjoining teeth 
with a highly visible print or dye.

[FIGURE: C12053A.gif]

To assist in assembly of the auxiliary section, you can make this 
auxiliary section fixture out of a section of 2 x 12.

 Auxiliary Section Fixture 

[FIGURE: C12054A.gif]

Place the two countershafts in the fixture or on a flat bench with the 
large HI range gears down.

[FIGURE: C12055A.gif]

Position the output shaft, LO range and synchronizer assembly between 
the two countershafts.

[FIGURE: DC0046A.gif]

Check the timing marks on the LO range gear, making sure the 
countershaft gear timing marks are aligned between the LO range gear teeth.

[FIGURE: DC0047A.gif]

Place the range yoke assembly into the synchronizer sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C12058A.gif]

Place the auxiliary housing over the output shaft and countershaft 
assemblies.

[FIGURE: DC0048A.gif]

Install the two rear countershaft bearing races in the auxiliary 
section bores.

[FIGURE: DC0049A.gif]

Place the shim gauges over each bearing. Install one 2-1/2-inch x 
3/8-inch and two 1-inch x 3/8-inch capscrews. Tighten all capscrews only until 
snug. Straps can also be used.

[FIGURE: DC0050A.gif]

Install range cylinder into auxiliary section bore. Apply Threadlock®
 and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to capscrew threads. Then, install and tighten 
capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: DC0051A.gif]

Place range piston in cylinder bore. Tighten piston retaining nut to 
95-115 Nm (70-85 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: DC0052A.gif]

Position new gasket and range cylinder cover on the range cylinder. 
Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to capscrew threads. Then, install 
and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: DC0053A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not heat the bearing above 136°C (275°
F). Use a bearing heater if possible.

Install bearing inner spacer on the output shaft. Heat the rear bearing 
and place it on the output shaft until seated.

[FIGURE: DC0054A.gif]

 NOTE: One rear bearing capscrew's hole is chamfered. The nylon collar and 
brass washer must be installed at this location to correctly seal the rear 
bearing cover. Do not reuse old nylon collar.

 NOTE: Spacer must be installed between bearing and speedometer rotor.

Install the rear bearing gasket and cover on the housing. Apply 
Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to capscrew threads. Then, install and 
tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: DC0055A.gif]

Install yoke and nut on output shaft for installation of auxiliary 
section to the main case.

[FIGURE: DC0056A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12102A.gif]

gear makes it very susceptible to breakage.

hub.

[FIGURE: C12119A.gif]

Press the 4th (or overdrive) gear on countershaft, long hub of gear to 
the front of shaft.

[FIGURE: C12120A.gif]

 NOTE: The left (lower) countershaft assembly has a 47-tooth PTO gear; the 
right (upper) countershaft assembly has a 45-tooth PTO gear. Mark each shaft 
accordingly by L (left) and R (right).

Start the PTO gear onto countershaft, bullet-nose side of teeth facing 
up and toward rear of shaft. Align keyway of drive gear with key in 
countershaft, and press BOTH gears onto shaft, long hub of drive gear against 
PTO gear.

[FIGURE: C12121A.gif]

Install the drive gear retaining snap ring in groove on front of each 
countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12122A.gif]

Use the proper driver to install the bearing race on the countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12123A.gif]

Mark the countershaft drive gear for timing purposes. On the drive gear 
of each countershaft assembly, mark the tooth aligned with keyway of gear and 
stamped with an O for easy identification. A highly visible color of 
toolmaker's dye is recommended for making timing marks. Refer to Auxiliary 
Countershaft Assemblies, Timing Procedures in the Removal and Installation 
portion of this section.

[FIGURE: C12124A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Countershaft Assemblies, Partial Installation

Place the left countershaft assembly into position in case, making sure 
the "L"-marked assembly has the larger, 47-tooth PTO gear.

[FIGURE: C12101A.gif]

Place the right countershaft assembly into position in case, making 
sure that the "R"-marked assembly has the smaller, 45-tooth PTO gear.

[FIGURE: C12101A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Left Countershaft Bearing, Installation

Move the left countershaft assembly to the rear, and insert 
countershaft support tool or blocking to center shaft in rear case bore.

[FIGURE: C12125A.gif]

Use a flanged-end bearing driver to start the bearing in case bore. 
Center the countershaft in the bearing and complete the installation.

[FIGURE: C12126A.gif]

Position the retainer plate on front of left countershaft, then roll 
pin in hole at end of shaft. Lightly oil capscrew threads and install 
capscrew. When shaft can be secured, tighten capscrew to 122-136 Nm
 (90-100 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12127B.gif]

Remove countershaft support tool or blocking from rear case bore. 
Install the left countershaft rear bearing with larger I.D. lead chamfer to 
the front of shaft. Install the snap ring in groove at rear of left 
countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12128A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Main Drive Gear Assembly, Assembly, Installation and Timing

Mark the main drive gear for timing purposes. Mark any two adjacent 
teeth on drive gear. Repeat the procedure for the two adjacent teeth directly 
opposite the first set marked. A highly visible color of toolmaker's dye is 
recommended for making timing marks. Refer to Auxiliary Countershaft 
Assemblies, Timing Procedures in the Removal and Installation portion of this 
section.

[FIGURE: C12129A.gif]

Mesh the marked tooth of left countershaft drive gear with either set 
of two marked teeth on main drive gear. Slide the input shaft through the main 
drive gear.

[FIGURE: C12130A.gif]

Install spacer and bearing on the input shaft, with external snap ring 
to the outside.

[FIGURE: C12131A.gif]

Install the bearing into the bore with the proper driver. Temporarily 
install the front bearing cover, and drive the input shaft into the bearing 
from the rear.

[FIGURE: C12132A.gif]

================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 07-03Q: Transmission, Manual, 9-Speed and 10-Speed (Helical Gears)

1997 L, LA, LL, LLA, LLS, LN, LNT, LS, LT, LTA, LTL, LTLA, LTLS, LTS-9000 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mainshaft Assembly, Assembly and Partial Installation

Secure the mainshaft in a vise equipped with brass jaws or wood blocks, 
pilot end of shaft down. If previously removed, install the roll pin in keyway.

[FIGURE: C12133A.gif]

Install the 4th gear limit washer on mainshaft, flat side of washer up. 
Rotate washer in the 1st or bottom groove of mainshaft to align the splines of 
washer with those of the mainshaft. Feed a plastic line up from the bottom of 
the mainshaft to secure the washer.

[FIGURE: C12134A.gif]

 NOTE: Gear limit washers are internally splined and locked to mainshaft by 
the key. Gear spacers are externally splined to engage clutching teeth in gear 
hubs. There is one limit washer and one spacer for each gear in the mainshaft 
assembly.

Place 4th (or overdrive) spacer and gear on the mainshaft, clutching 
teeth down, with external splines of spacer engaged into the gear.

[FIGURE: C12135A.gif]

Install the 3rd gear and spacer on shaft against 4th (or overdrive) 
gear, clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: C12136A.gif]

Install the 3rd gear washer. Rotate the washer to align splines, and 
feed the plastic line up to hold washer in place.

[FIGURE: C12137A.gif]

Insert two large screwdrivers between the 3rd and 4th (or overdrive) 
gears to check axial clearance. Making sure the gear hubs are parallel, insert 
a feeler gauge between hubs. Correct axial clearance is 0.152-0.381 mm 
(0.006-0.015 inch). If the clearance is less than the minimum 0.152 mm (0.006 
inch) tolerance, the limit washer in the 3rd gear must be replaced by a 
thinner limit washer. This will increase the axial clearance between the 
gears. If the clearance checked is greater than the maximum 0.381 mm (0.015 
inch) tolerance, a thicker limit washer must be installed in the 3rd gear. 
This will decrease the axial clearance between the gears.

[FIGURE: C12138A.gif]

Install the 2nd/3rd speed sliding clutch, aligning the missing internal 
spline of sliding clutch with plastic line, feed line up.

[FIGURE: C12139A.gif]

Install the 2nd gear limit washer on mainshaft, flat side of washer up. 
Rotate washer in the 3rd groove of mainshaft to align the splines of washer 
with those of the mainshaft. Feed the plastic line up through the washer. Also 
install the spacer at this time.

[FIGURE: C12140A.gif]

Install the 2nd gear on mainshaft, clutching teeth down and engaged 
with external splines of spacer.

[FIGURE: C12141A.gif]

Install the 1st gear on shaft against 2nd gear, clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: C12142A.gif]

Install the spacer in 1st gear, engaging the external splines of spacer 
with clutching teeth of gear. Place the limit washer into 1st gear and rotate 
the washer to align the splines. Feed plastic line up the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12142A.gif]

Check axial clearance and make adjustments, if necessary, between the 
1st and 2nd gears as described in Step 6 of this procedure.

[FIGURE: C12143A.gif]

Install the 1st/Reverse speed sliding clutch, aligning the missing 
internal spline of sliding clutch with plastic line. Feed line up.

[FIGURE: C12144A.gif]

Install the reverse gear limit washer on mainshaft, flat side of washer 
up. Rotate washer in the 5th groove of mainshaft to align the splines of 
washer with those of the mainshaft. Feed the plastic line up and install the 
spacer.

[FIGURE: C12145A.gif]

Install the snap ring in 6th groove of mainshaft to retain key in keyway.

[FIGURE: C12146A.gif]

Install the snap ring in hub of reverse gear only to check axial 
clearance (end play) limits. Refer to Axial Clearance (End Play) Limits in the Specifications 
 portion of this section.

[FIGURE: C12147A.gif]

Install the reverse gear on mainshaft, clutching teeth down and engaged 
with external splines of spacer.

[FIGURE: C12148A.gif]

Install the auxiliary drive gear assembly in its proper position on 
rear of mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12149A.gif]

 NOTE: This check is made by spreading the gears with screwdrivers.

Separate the auxiliary drive gear and reverse gear by placing two 
screwdrivers 180° opposite each other between the gears. 
Allow the weight of the screwdrivers to separate the gears; do not apply 
downward pressure to screwdrivers. Check the clearance between the auxiliary 
drive gear and reverse gear. Select the proper limit washer that will allow 
the correct clearance of .006-.015 between the gears.

[FIGURE: C12150A.gif]

With the proper reverse gear limit washer installed on the mainshaft, 
remove the auxiliary drive gear assembly and reverse gear. Remove the snap 
ring from hub of reverse gear and reinstall the gear on mainshaft. Engage the 
clutching teeth of gear with the splines of the spacer and sliding clutch. 
Move the reverse gear against the 1st gear.

[FIGURE: C12151A.gif]

Remove the snap ring from the 6th groove of the mainshaft. Place the 
mainshaft key in line with the plastic line. While pulling the line out, 
follow it down with the mainshaft key. Reinstall the snap ring after key is 
seated.

[FIGURE: C12152A.gif]

 NOTE: Check to make sure that marked tooth on left countershaft drive gear 
has remained in mesh with marked set of teeth on main drive gear.

Block the right countershaft assembly against case wall. Lower the 
mainshaft assembly into position with the reverse gear held against 1st gear, 
and rear of shaft moved into case bore. Move the pilot end of mainshaft into 
pocket bushing of input shaft.

[FIGURE: C12153A.gif]

Center rear of mainshaft in case bore. Install the auxiliary drive gear 
assembly on shaft, partially seating the bearing in bore. Do not complete 
installation at this time.

[FIGURE: C12159B.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Right Countershaft Assembly and Bearings, Installation

 NOTE: The left countershaft assembly must remain in time with main drive gear 
when timing right countershaft assembly. Refer to Auxiliary Countershaft 
Assemblies, Timing Procedures in the Removal and Installation portion of this 
section.

Remove blocking from right countershaft assembly and place it parallel 
to mainshaft assembly. Mesh the marked tooth of right countershaft drive gear 
with remaining set of two marked teeth on main drive gear.

[FIGURE: C12155A.gif]

Insert countershaft support tool or blocking in rear bearing bore.

[FIGURE: C12156A.gif]

Position the front countershaft bearing in its bore and install it with 
proper bearing driver. Lightly oil capscrew threads and install the retaining 
washer and capscrew, making sure to align pin in shaft. Tighten capscrew to 
122-163 Nm (90-120 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12157B.gif]

 NOTE: Do not engage sliding clutches with more than one gear at the same 
time. This will lock the gearing and prevent the mainshaft and countershaft 
assemblies from rotating.

Move the reverse gear to the rear on mainshaft. Use a screwdriver to 
engage sliding clutches with all forward speed gears. A sliding clutch that 
will not engage with a gear indicates the gearset is not in proper mesh. The 
bearings of the right countershaft need to be removed and the drive gearset 
retimed.

[FIGURE: C12158A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Left Reverse Idler Gear Assembly, Assembly and Installation

 NOTE: Since the left and right reverse idler gear assemblies are identical, 
reassembly and installation of the left reverse idler gear assembly should be 
performed at this time. Refer to Right Reverse Idler Gear Assembly, Assembly 
and Installation in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Remove the auxiliary drive gear assembly from mainshaft and rear 
bearing bore. Do not allow mainshaft to move to rear when removing auxiliary 
drive gear.

[FIGURE: C12159B.gif]

Move the reverse gear to the rear as far as possible, meshing teeth of 
gear with those of the reverse idler gears.

[FIGURE: C12158A.gif]

Align the external splines of spacer with clutching teeth of reverse 
gear. Move spacer forward on mainshaft and into gear. Install the snap ring in 
hub of reverse gear. Move the reverse gear forward on mainshaft and into 
proper position in case.

[FIGURE: C12160A.gif]

Reinstall the auxiliary drive gear assembly on rear of mainshaft. Use a 
flanged-end driver and maul to seat bearing in case bore.

[FIGURE: C12159B.gif]

Align the six capscrew holes in retainer with the tapped holes in case. 
Lightly oil capscrew threads. Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft). Lockwire the capscrews in groups of three.

[FIGURE: C12161B.gif]

Install the snap ring in groove at end of mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12162A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Clutch Housing Installation

Position the corresponding new gasket on housing mounting surface. 
Install the clutch housing on front case, piloting on the six studs and drive 
gear bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C12024A.gif]

Install the six nuts with washers or lockwashers on studs and tighten 
to 244-258 Nm (180-190 lb-ft) or to 230-237 Nm
 (170-175 lb-ft) for aluminum housing. Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, 
install the four capscrews with lockwashers and tighten to 122-136 Nm
 (90-100 lb-ft) or to 95-102 Nm (70-75 
lb-ft) for aluminum housing.

[FIGURE: C12023B.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Auxiliary Section Installation

 NOTE: The following procedure can be completed in both the horizontal and 
vertical positions. Care must be taken when the procedure is completed in the 
horizontal, as parts can shift and cause damage to the auxiliary countershaft 
bearing covers.

 NOTE: Front box sliding clutches must be in the neutral position.

 NOTE: The shim gauge tool print is available from Eaton Corp. Tool Print 
Number T-65514-S.

 NOTE: The auxiliary section should be engaged in gear so the yoke can be 
rotated.

Place the transmission in the vertical position. Place two blocks of 
wood under the clutch housing to prevent transmission from tipping or causing 
damage to the input shaft. Lower the auxiliary section onto the rear of the 
front case.

[FIGURE: C12163A.gif]

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to threads of capscrews. 
Install the retaining capscrews in flange of auxiliary housing and tighten to 
47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12164B.gif]

Remove the center bolt from each shim gauge. Loosen the two cover 
capscrews.

[FIGURE: C12165A.gif]

Each capscrew (3/8 x 1 inch) must have clean threads (no thread 
adhesive applied to threads) with no lockwasher. Threads in case must also be 
free of thread adhesive.

[FIGURE: C12166A.gif]

 CAUTION: Rear countershaft bearing cover gaskets must not be installed at this 
time. 

Turn capscrews until they contact the shim gauge surface, then evenly 
apply .79 Nm (7 lb-in) of torque to each capscrew.

[FIGURE: C12167B.gif]

Rotate the output shaft six times clockwise then six times 
counterclockwise to properly seat the countershaft bearings. Use a feeler 
gauge to measure the clearance between the shim gauge and the auxiliary 
housing surface next to each capscrew location. Record each measurement and 
average the two measurements. Refer to Helical End Play chart in the Specifications 
 portion of this section, and select the number in the 1st 
column which corresponds to the average measurement achieved. Follow the 
column to the right to determine the proper shim required by thickness, part 
number and shim color. Repeat this procedure for the remaining countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12168A.gif]

 NOTE: This procedure can be performed with a .100 gauging shim and the 
existing rear bearing covers. Follow the same procedure.

 NOTE: There is a separate shim requirement when an auxiliary countershaft oil 
pump is being installed.

After the correct shim has been selected, place the shim on the rear 
countershaft bearing race. Install the countershaft rear bearing cover and 
gasket. Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to threads of capscrews. 
Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 
lb-ft). Check for cover shim alignment. If misaligned the bearing cover can be 
damaged when final torque is applied to cover capscrews. Perform the same 
procedure on the remaining rear countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12169B.gif]

With threads of output shaft lightly oiled, install and tighten the 
output shaft nut to 610-678 Nm (450-500 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12172A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12173A.gif]

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to threads of capscrews. 
Install the capscrews in housing and tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12174B.gif]

Install shift tower gasket and the three detent balls and springs.

[FIGURE: C12175A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification

The Eaton RTLO Transmissions are low inertia transmissions. A low 
inertia transmission utilizes a sliding clutch that disengages the front box 
of the transmission from the back box during split-shifts, range shifts and 
regular gear shifts which allows the front box to slow down faster than the 
back box. This makes shifting much easier since the gears to be shifted are no 
longer being spun by the inertia of the back box. This also allows 
preselection of gears during split-shifts which is a feature not found on the 
other transmissions.

The low inertia transmissions used by Ford are the RTLO-11610B, 
-12610B, -13610B, -14610A/B, -15610B and -16610B. These transmissions also 
utilize Roadranger® valves and twin countershafts and have 
Multi-Mesh (spur-type) auxiliary gears.

[FIGURE: C12299A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow

 NOTE: The numbers of the procedures correspond to the numbers on the 
illustrations.

 One Gear 

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

The input shaft external splines engage the main drive gear internal 
splines.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the mating countershaft 
gears of the engaged mainshaft gear. The following cross-section view 
illustrates a one-speed gear engagement.

The external clutching teeth of the sliding clutch engage with the 
internal clutching teeth of the mainshaft gear which transfers torque to the 
mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12300A.gif]

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the rear auxiliary drive 
gear sliding clutch which is in the rearward position.

The rear auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the LO range gear in 
the auxiliary section.

The LO range gear delivers torque to the output shaft through the range 
synchronizer sliding clutch.

The output shaft delivers torque to the driveline components.

[FIGURE: C12301A.gif]

 Two Gear 

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

The input shaft external splines engage the main drive gear internal 
splines.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the mating countershaft 
gears of the engaged mainshaft gear. The following cross-section view 
illustrates a two-speed gear engagement. 

The external clutching teeth of the sliding clutch engage with the 
internal clutching teeth of the mainshaft gear which transfers torque to the 
mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12302A.gif]

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear 
sliding clutch which is in the forward position.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the LO range gear in 
the auxiliary section.

The LO range gear delivers torque to the output shaft through the range 
synchronizer sliding clutch.

The output shaft delivers torque to the driveline components.

[FIGURE: C12303A.gif]

 Seven Gear 

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

The input shaft external splines engage the main drive gear internal 
splines.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the mating countershaft 
gears of the engaged mainshaft gear. The following cross-section view 
illustrates a seven-speed gear engagement.

The external clutching teeth of the sliding clutch engage with the 
internal clutching teeth of the mainshaft gear which transfers torque to the 
mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12304A.gif]

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the rear auxiliary drive 
gear sliding clutch which is in the rearward position.

Torque is delivered to the back of the rear auxiliary drive gear. The 
range synchronizer sliding clutch is in the forward position, transferring 
torque directly to the output shaft.

The output shaft delivers torque to the driveline components.

[FIGURE: C12305A.gif]

 Eight Gear 

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission input 
shaft.

The input shaft external splines engage the main drive gear internal 
splines.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the mating countershaft 
gears of the engaged mainshaft gear. The following cross-section view 
illustrates an eight-speed gear engagement.

The external clutching teeth of the sliding clutch engage with the 
internal clutching teeth of the mainshaft gear which transfers torque to the 
mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12306A.gif]

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the front auxiliary drive 
gear sliding clutch which is in the forward position.

The front auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the rear auxiliary 
drive gear.

Torque is transferred to the range synchronizer sliding clutch which is 
in the forward position delivering torque directly to the output shaft.

The output shaft delivers torque to the driveline components.

[FIGURE: C12307A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

Proper lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program.

Eaton Fuller transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in an oil circulating bath created by the motion of the gears and 
shafts.

All parts are amply lubricated if these procedures are closely followed:

Maintain oil level. Inspect regularly.

Follow maintenance interval chart.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 Maintain Proper Oil Level 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, types and brands of oil should not be mixed because of 
possible incompatibility. 

Make sure oil is level with the filler opening. Because you can reach 
oil with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. An oil level of 25 
mm (one inch) is about 3.7 liters (one gallon) of oil.

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 CAUTION: If your vehicle has a transmission oil filter, you must change the 
filter when fluid or lubricant is changed.

 Additives and friction modifiers must not be introduced. 

 Transmission Operating Angles 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication will occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

For operating angles over 12 degrees, the transmission must be equipped 
with an oil pump or cooler kit to make sure transmission is lubricated properly.

 Operating Temperatures with Oil Coolers 

The transmission must not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent 
operating temperatures to 149°C (300°F) do 
not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures above 120°C 
(250°F) increases the lubricant's oxidation rate and shortens 
its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 120°
C (250°F) the transmission can require more 
frequent oil changes or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F): 

operating consistently at slow speeds 

high ambient temperatures 

restricted airflow around transmission 

exhaust system too close to transmission 

high horsepower operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

 Oil Coolers 

Transmission oil coolers are recommended:

with engines of 350 H.P. and above

Transmission oil coolers are required:

with engines 399 H.P. and above and GCW's over 40 824 kg (90,000 lb)

with engines 399 H.P. and above and 1898 Nm (1400 
lb-ft) or greater torque

with engines 450 H.P. and above

the transmission.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Auxiliary Section Without Tapered Bearings

 NOTE: There can be different capscrew lengths, note their location.

 NOTE: Auxiliary sections can be removed either with the transmission in the 
horizontal position or the vertical position.

 Removal (Horizontal) 

From the auxiliary section housing, remove the retaining capscrews that 
attach the front section to the auxiliary section.

[FIGURE: C12318A.gif]

Insert the two longest capscrews in the housing flange tapped holes. 
Tighten evenly to move the auxiliary section away from the front box. Go far 
enough to break the gasket seal.

[FIGURE: C12319A.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the tapped holes.

Attach an auxiliary section hanger bracket to the auxiliary section top.

Attach a lifting chain to the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

[FIGURE: C12320A.gif]

Move assembly to the rear until auxiliary section is free.

Remove the gasket and clean all mounting surfaces of gasket material.

 Removal (Vertical) 

 CAUTION: Place blocks under the clutch housing to prevent input shaft damage. 

Place transmission in the vertical position, clutch housing down.

From the auxiliary section housing, remove the retaining capscrews that 
attach the front box to the auxiliary section.

[FIGURE: C12321A.gif]

Install a steel bar through the yoke.

Attach a lifting chain to the steel bar.

Lift assembly from the front section.

[FIGURE: C12322A.gif]

Remove the gasket and clean all mounting surfaces of gasket material.

 Installation (Horizontal) 

 NOTE: There are different capscrew lengths. Install in the correct location.

 NOTE: Auxiliary sections can be installed either with the transmission in the 
horizontal position or the vertical position.

Position a new gasket on the transmission mounting surface.

Attach an auxiliary section hanger bracket to the auxiliary section top.

Attach a lifting chain to the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

Position the auxiliary section on the two dowel pins.

[FIGURE: C12320A.gif]

Slide the auxiliary section on until the hanger bracket contacts the 
front case back.

Remove the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

Slide the auxiliary section the rest of the way into position.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the retaining capscrews. Tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12722A.gif]

 Installation (Vertical) 

 NOTE: To install in the vertical position, the clutch housing must be 
installed.

 CAUTION: Place blocks under the clutch housing to prevent input shaft damage. 

Place the transmission in the vertical position, clutch housing down.

Position a new gasket on the transmission mounting surface.

Install a steel bar through the yoke.

Attach a lifting chain to the steel bar.

Position the auxiliary section over the two dowel pins.

[FIGURE: C12322A.gif]

Slide the auxiliary section down the dowels.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the retaining capscrews. Tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12723A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an air gun. Tighten by hand until the capscrews are snug. 

Install the auxiliary countershaft retaining straps with 2-3/8 inch NC 
x 1 inch and 1-3/8 inch NC x 2-1/2 inch clean capscrews.

[FIGURE: C12327A.gif]

From the auxiliary section housing, remove the retaining capscrews that 
attach the front box to the auxiliary section.

[FIGURE: C12328A.gif]

Install a steel bar through the yoke.

Attach a lifting chain to the steel bar.

[FIGURE: C12329A.gif]

Lift assembly from the front section.

Remove the gasket and clean all mounting surfaces of gasket material.

 Installation (Horizontal) 

 NOTE: There are different capscrew lengths. Install in the correct location.

 NOTE: Auxiliary sections can be installed either with the transmission in the 
horizontal position or the vertical position.

 NOTE: To install in the vertical position, the clutch housing must be 
installed.

Position a new gasket on the transmission mounting surface.

Attach an auxiliary section hanger bracket to the auxiliary section top.

Attach a lifting chain to the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

Position the auxiliary section on the two dowel pins.

[FIGURE: C12320A.gif]

Slide the auxiliary section on until the hanger bracket contacts the 
front section back.

Remove the auxiliary section hanger bracket.

Slide the auxiliary section the rest of the way into position.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the retaining capscrews. Tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12724A.gif]

To finish installation, refer to Shimming Procedure for Tapered 
Bearings in the Adjustment portion of this section.

 Installation (Vertical) 

 CAUTION: Place blocks under the clutch housing to prevent input shaft damage. 

Place the transmission in the vertical position, clutch housing down.

Position a new gasket on the transmission mounting surface.

Install a steel bar through the yoke.

Attach a lifting chain to the steel bar.

Position the auxiliary section over the two dowel pins.

[FIGURE: C12329A.gif]

Slide the auxiliary section down the dowels.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the retaining capscrews. Tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12328B.gif]

Remove the steel bar and chain.

To finish installation, refer to Shimming Procedure for Tapered 
Bearings in the Adjustment portion of this section. Make sure the input shaft 
rotates.

Input Shaft

 Special Procedure for Changing Input Shaft 

 NOTE: This procedure is a way of removing the input shaft without

Remove the bearing retainer snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12332A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12333A.gif]

Pull the input shaft forward to expose the bearing.

To complete bearing removal, use pry bars.

Remove the spacer.

[FIGURE: C12334A.gif]

Remove the snap ring.

Pull the input shaft forward, out of the drive gear and transmission

[FIGURE: C12335A.gif]

 Installation 

Install the new input shaft into main drive gear splines.

Position the input shaft just far enough into the gear to expose the 
drive gear snap ring groove.

[FIGURE: C12336A.gif]

Install the drive gear snap ring.

Install the spacer on the input shaft.

[FIGURE: C12334A.gif]

With the snap ring to the outside, slide the bearing on the input shaft 
and position into the case bore.

With the input shaft bearing driver, seat the bearing.

[FIGURE: C12337A.gif]

Install the bearing retaining snap ring.

Position a new gasket on the transmission mounting surface.

Position the front bearing cover on the input shaft. Align the oil

[FIGURE: C12332A.gif]

equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

(35-45 lb-ft). Make sure the input shaft turns freely.

Reverse Idler Gear Assembly

 NOTE: Before the upper reverse idler gear assembly can be removed, mainshaft

 NOTE: While removing the reverse idler shaft, the thrust washer can drop to

 NOTE: The mainshaft reverse gear must be moved in order to remove the upper

[FIGURE: C12342A.gif]

From the idler shaft, remove the loosened lock nut and washer.

[FIGURE: C12343A.gif]

From the idler shaft rear, remove the pipe plug.

[FIGURE: C12344A.gif]

 NOTE: If you are installing the bottom reverse idler gear assembly, make sure

Thread the pipe plug into the reverse idler shaft and tighten.

[FIGURE: C12345A.gif]

idler shaft.

[FIGURE: C12346A.gif]

Make sure the reverse idler shaft is seated in the support boss bore.

Install the washer and lock nut on shaft front. Tighten the stop nut to 
68-81 Nm (50-60 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12343A.gif]

front bearing outer race against the reverse idler plate.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Countershaft Bearings

 NOTE: The following instructions are used to remove the upper and lower 
countershaft bearings. To remove the mainshaft assembly, only the upper 
countershaft bearings need to be removed.

 NOTE: Performing the following instructions will damage the bearings and 
should not be done unless bearing replacement is planned.

 NOTE: The bearing inner race remains pressed on the countershaft after 
removal of the front bearings.

 Removal 

To keep the mainshaft pilot from falling out of the input shaft pocket, 
temporarily install the auxiliary drive gear on the mainshaft.

From each countershaft rear groove, remove the snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12348A.gif]

From inside the case, use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft 
rear bearings from the case bores.

[FIGURE: C12349A.gif]

From the front of each countershaft, remove the capscrew and front 
retainer plate.

[FIGURE: C12350A.gif]

Use the soft bar and maul to drive each countershaft to the rear as far 
as possible. This partially unseats the front bearings.

Return to the case rear, and drive each countershaft forward as far as 
possible. This exposes the bearing snap rings.

Use a bearing puller or pry bars to remove the countershaft front 
bearings. If a bearing puller is used, the front bearing cover has to be 
removed.

[FIGURE: C12351A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: The front bearing inner race must be pressed on the countershaft front.

 NOTE: The flanged-end driver must cover the bearing outer race for proper 
installation.

Move the countershaft to the rear and insert the countershaft support 
tool to center shaft in rear case bore.

[FIGURE: C12352A.gif]

Use a flanged-end driver to start the front bearing in case bore.

[FIGURE: C12353A.gif]

Use a screwdriver inserted in the countershaft capscrew bore to help 
center the countershaft.

Move the countershaft forward into the bearing.

Use a flanged-end bearing driver and maul to completely seat the front 
bearing in case bore.

On the countershaft front, position the retainer plate with roll pin in 
hole at shaft end.

[FIGURE: C12350A.gif]

Secure with capscrew. Tighten to 122-163 Nm (90-120 
lb-ft).

From the rear, remove the countershaft support tool.

With the larger inner diameter lead chamfer to the shaft front, use a 
flanged-end bearing driver and install the rear bearing.

On each countershaft rear groove, install the snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12354A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Timing Procedures

 Front Section 

It is essential that both countershaft assemblies of the front and 
auxiliary sections are timed. This makes sure proper tooth contact is made 
between mainshaft gears seeking to center on the mainshaft during torque 
transfer and mating countershaft gears that distribute the load evenly. If not 
properly timed, serious damage to the transmission is likely to result from 
unequal tooth contact causing the mainshaft gears to climb out of equilibrium.

Timing is simply a procedure of marking the appropriate teeth of a gear 
set prior to installation and placing them in proper mesh while in the 
transmission. In the front section, it is necessary to time only the drive 
gear set. And depending on the model, only the LO range, deep reduction, or 
splitter gear set is timed in the auxiliary section.

 Marking countershaft drive gear teeth 

Prior to placing each countershaft assembly into the case, clearly mark 
the tooth located directly over the drive gear keyway as shown. This tooth is 
stamped with an O to aid identification.

[FIGURE: C8921B.gif]

 Marking main drive gear teeth 

Mark any two adjacent teeth on the main drive gear.

Mark the two adjacent teeth located directly opposite the first set 
marked on the main drive gear. As shown to the left, there should be an equal 
number of unmarked gear teeth on each side between the marked sets.

[FIGURE: C8922B.gif]

 Meshing marked countershaft drive gear teeth with marked main drive 
gear teeth 

After placing the mainshaft assembly into the case, the countershaft 
bearings are installed to complete installation of the countershaft assemblies.

When installing the bearings on the left countershaft, mesh the 
countershaft drive gear marked tooth with either set of main drive gear two 
marked teeth.

Repeat the procedure when installing the bearings on the right 
countershaft, make use of the remaining set of main drive gear two marked 
teeth to time assembly.

 Auxiliary Section 

Mark any two teeth on the LO range gear. Then mark two teeth located 
directly opposite the first marked.

Prior to placing each auxiliary countershaft assembly into housing, 
mark the tooth on each auxiliary countershaft assembly LO range gear stamped 
with the O.

Follow the assembly procedures in the appropriate Auxiliary Section 
procedure in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Countershaft Assemblies, Front Section

Except for the PTO gears, the upper and lower countershaft assemblies 
are the same. Make sure to mark each as they are removed.

 Removal 

Move the upper countershaft assembly to the rear as far as possible.

Swing the countershaft front to middle of the case.

Lift the countershaft assembly from the case.

[FIGURE: C12355A.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure the countershaft assemblies have been marked for proper 
position, 47-tooth PTO gear in the lower position.

 NOTE: On the drive gear of each countershaft assembly, mark the tooth aligned 
with the gear keyway and stamped with an O for easy identification. Use a 
highly visible color of toolmaker's dye to make timing marks. Refer to Timing 
Procedures in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 Installation 

Mark the countershaft drive gear for timing purposes.

[FIGURE: C12356A.gif]

Place the lower 47-tooth PTO gear assembly in the case, with the inner 
bearing race end to the front.

Position as far to the left as possible (the opposition side as the 
lower reverse idler gear assembly).

Place the upper 45-tooth PTO gear assembly in the case, with the inner 
bearing race end to the front.

[FIGURE: C12355A.gif]

Position as far to the right as possible (the same side as the lower 
reverse idler gear assembly).

Make sure the upper and lower countershafts are in the right place.

Make sure the timing marks are visible.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mainshaft Assembly

 NOTE: Be careful when removing the mainshaft assembly. The sliding clutch on 
the end can slip off the mainshaft.

 NOTE: Reverse gear is also free and can fall off the shaft.

 Removal 

From the mainshaft, remove the reverse gear retaining snap ring.

Move the mainshaft reverse gear as far to the rear as possible and 
remove reverse gear inside diameter snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12357A.gif]

 NOTE: If not removing the upper reverse idler gear assembly, you must remove 
the upper reverse idler gear assembly shaft and roll the gear to the outside. 
Refer to Reverse Idler Gear Assembly in the Removal and Installation portion 
of this section.

Move the reverse gear forward and against the next gear, engaging the 
mainshaft sliding clutch spline.

[FIGURE: C12358A.gif]

Use a large screwdriver and block the upper countershaft assembly 
against the case wall.

If removing the upper reverse idler gear assembly, refer to Reverse 
Idler Gear Assembly in the Removal and Installation portion of this section at 
this time.

[FIGURE: C12359A.gif]

Position the hook or rope around the mainshaft.

Pull the mainshaft to the rear to free the pilot from the input shaft 
pocket.

 NOTE: The lower countershaft bearings and the input shaft must be installed.

 NOTE: Check to make sure the lower countershaft drive gear marked tooth is in 
time with main drive gear set of marked teeth.

Tilt mainshaft front up and lift assembly from the case.

 Installation 

Block the upper countershaft against the case wall.

With reverse gear forward against the next speed gear, lower the 
mainshaft assembly while pulling the shaft rear through the case bore.

Move the mainshaft pilot-end into the input shaft pilot bushing. Mesh 
the mainshaft gears with the corresponding forward countershaft assembly gears.

[FIGURE: C12360A.gif]

 NOTE: At this time other components of the front section must be installed 
before the mainshaft installation can be completed, refer to Countershaft 
Bearings in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Center the mainshaft rear in case bore and temporarily position the 
auxiliary drive gear on the mainshaft. Partially seat the bearing in the bore.

Mesh the reverse gear teeth with the reverse idler gear teeth and move 
the reverse gear to the rear as far as possible.

Remove the auxiliary drive gear.

[FIGURE: C12361A.gif]

Align the reverse gear spacer external splines with the reverse gear 
and move the spacer into the reverse gear.

Install the reverse gear inside diameter snap ring and move the reverse 
gear forward on the mainshaft and against the reverse gear limit washer.

Install the reverse gear snap ring in the mainshaft second snap ring 
groove.

[FIGURE: C12357A.gif]

 NOTE: For ease of disassembly, mount the auxiliary section upright in a vise.

 NOTE: Both countershafts are removed the same.

 NOTE: As the countershaft strap is removed, the countershaft can fall.

[FIGURE: C12382A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Shift Lever Housing

 NOTE: If total disassembly is needed, the Roadranger® valve 
must be removed first.

 NOTE: Release the spring one coil at a time.

 Disassembly 

Slide the boot up the shift lever shaft and remove.

[FIGURE: C12387A.gif]

With housing bottom facing up, secure the assembly in a vise.

Use large screwdriver to twist between the spring and housing, forcing 
the spring from under the housing lugs.

[FIGURE: C12388A.gif]

From inside the housing tower, remove the tension spring, washer, and 
shift lever.

In models so equipped, from the housing bore, remove the nut and washer.

From the housing tower spade pin bore, remove and inspect the spade 
pin, discard if damaged.

From the housing tower inside groove, inspect the O-ring, discard if 
damaged.

[FIGURE: C12389A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Inspect tension spring and washer for wear.

 NOTE: Apply Rust Penetrant and Inhibitor F2AZ-19A501-A or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESR-M99C56-A to the shift lever pivot ball. A rust 
preventative lubricant film should cover all surfaces between and including 
the pivot ball.

 NOTE: Seat the tension spring one coil at a time.

With housing bottom facing up, secure the assembly in a vise.

If the spade pin is damaged, replace and install the spade pin in 
housing tower bore.

In models so equipped, install the nut and washer in the housing bore.

If the O-ring is damaged, replace; lubricate the O-ring with Silicone 
Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A. 
Install the O-ring in the housing tower inside groove.

[FIGURE: C12389A.gif]

Align the lever ball slot with the spade pin and position the shift 
lever in the housing tower.

With dished-side up, install the washer over the ball.

[FIGURE: C12390A.gif]

Use a tension spring driver to install the tension spring under the 
housing lugs.

[FIGURE: C12462A.gif]

Remove the assembly from the vise.

Install a rubber boot over the shift lever and against the housing.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Shift Bar Housing

 NOTE: The shift bar housing must be removed from the transmission.

 NOTE: During disassembly, lay all parts on a clean bench in order of removal 
to facilitate assembly.

 NOTE: Shift bars not being removed must be kept in the neutral position or 
the interlocking parts lock the bars.

 NOTE: Start with the bottom shift bar.

 NOTE: Cut the lockwire and remove the lock screws from each bar just before 
their removal.

 Disassembly 

If the two sets of tension springs and balls from housing bores and the 
anti-rotating pin have not been removed, place the shift bar housing on its 
side to remove them.

[FIGURE: C12391A.gif]

With the housing rear to the right, lay the assembly on a flat surface.

While removing the top yoke bar, remove the shift yoke.

[FIGURE: C12392A.gif]

While removing the top yoke bar, remove the shift yoke assembly and 
block assembly.

[FIGURE: C12393A.gif]

Remove the interlock pin.

From the middle yoke bar, remove the jam nut, plain nut, and washer.

[FIGURE: C12394A.gif]

Remove the range interlock bar.

[FIGURE: C12395A.gif]

From the middle yoke bar, remove the select interlock bar to the right.

Pull the select tube to the left and remove the shift select block.

[FIGURE: C12396A.gif]

Remove the select tube with key to the left.

[FIGURE: C12397A.gif]

From the 1st and reverse shift yoke, remove the snap ring, washer, 
spring, and plunger. From the 3rd speed block, remove the plug, spring, and 
plunger.

[FIGURE: C12398A.gif]

Inspect the yoke or block parts, replace the worn parts.

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Inspect shift blocks and shift yokes for wear.

 NOTE: Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the shift bar housing 
plugs which are used to plug oil cooler provision holes. The sealant should be 
applied so that at least five complete threads are covered.

 NOTE: Apply Eaton Lockwire No. 1819 or equivalent to all shift bar housing 
assembly setscrews in both blocks and yokes. The wire should anchor the 
capscrew at least two complete 360-degree turns. The lockwire ends should be 
trimmed and bent out of the way of any part interference.

 NOTE: Keep yoke bars in neutral while assembling.

Assemble the 1st and reverse shift yoke assembly:

Install the plunger in the 1st and reverse shift yoke bore, plunger 
shank to the outside.

Install the spring into the bore over the plunger shank.

Position the washer over the plunger shank.

Install the snap ring.

Assemble the 3rd speed block assembly:

Install the plunger in the 3rd shift block bore, plunger shank to the 
outside.

Install the spring into the bore over the plunger shank.

Install the plug and tighten to compress the spring.

After plug bottoms out, back the plug out 1 to 1-1/2 turns.

Complete the block assembly process by staking the plug through the 
small hole in block.

[FIGURE: C12398A.gif]

With the housing rear to the right, lay the assembly on a flat surface.

Install the select tube in the middle boss with key in the key slot.

As the select tube passes through the first boss, install the shift 
select block.

[FIGURE: C12399A.gif]

From the right, install the select interlock bar.

[FIGURE: C12396A.gif]

Install the range interlock bar, chamfered end in, notched side down.

[FIGURE: C12395A.gif]

At the middle yoke bar front end, install the washer, plain nut, and 
jam nut.

Install the interlock pin, centered between bosses.

[FIGURE: C12394A.gif]

While installing the top yoke bar, position the shift yoke assembly and 
block assembly. The block assembly aligns with shift select block ear.

[FIGURE: C12393A.gif]

Install the lock screws. Tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 
lb-ft). Tighten the lockwire securely.

While installing the bottom yoke bar, position the shift yoke. The 
block assembly aligns with shift select block ear.

[FIGURE: C12392A.gif]

Install the lock screw. Tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 
lb-ft). Tighten the lockwire securely.

Make sure interlocking system is working and cannot shift into two 
gears at the same time.

Make sure all capscrews are lockwired.
