DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Mainshaft Assembly

 NOTE: During disassembly, lay all parts on a clean bench in order of removal 
to facilitate reassembly.

 NOTE: When removing limit washers, spacers and gears, note their location. 
Keep the internal-splined washers and external-splined spacers with the gear 
from which they were removed. There is only one limit washer and one spacer 
belonging to each gear.

 Disassembly 

Remove reverse gear.

Remove reverse gear spline spacer.

[FIGURE: C12403A.gif]

Tilt the mainshaft up, and from the opposite end, remove the sliding 
clutch.

[FIGURE: C12404A.gif]

Place the mainshaft in a vertical position.

Remove the mainshaft key snap ring.

From the mainshaft rear, pull the mainshaft key from the mainshaft 
keyway.

[FIGURE: C12405A.gif]

Turn the reverse gear limit washer to align its splines with the 
mainshaft and remove the washer.

Remove the reverse-1st speed sliding clutch.

Remove 1st gear and spline spacer.

Remove 1st gear spacer.

Turn the 1st gear limit washer to align its splines with the mainshaft 
and remove the washer.

Turn the 3rd gear limit washer to align its splines with the mainshaft 
and remove the washer.

Remove the 3rd gear spacer.

Remove 3rd gear.

Remove 3rd gear spline spacer.

Turn the 3rd gear limit washer to align its splines with the mainshaft 
and remove the washer.

Inspect the roll pin, remove if damaged.

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Each mainshaft gear must have its I.D. snap ring installed before 
placement on the mainshaft. Do not replace reverse gear I.D. snap ring.

 NOTE: Gear limit washers are internally splined and locked to the mainshaft 
by the key. Gear spacers are externally splined to engage with gear hub 
clutching teeth. There is one limit washer and one spacer for each mainshaft 
gear.

 NOTE: Axial clearance (end play) limits are .152-.381 mm (.006-.015 inch) for 
all mainshaft gears.

 NOTE: If the axial clearance is less than the minimum .152 mm (.006-inch) 
tolerance, the limit washer should be replaced with a thinner limit washer. 
This will increase the axial clearance between the gears. If the axial 
clearance is greater than the maximum .381 mm (.015-inch) tolerance, a thicker 
limit washer should be installed. This will decrease the axial clearance 
between the gears.

With mainshaft pilot-end down, secure the mainshaft in a vise equipped 
with brass jaws or wood blocks.

If previously removed, install the roll pin in keyway.

[FIGURE: C12406A.gif]

With the washer flat side up, position the 3rd speed gear limit washer 
(white) in the mainshaft 1st or bottom groove. Rotate the washer until the 
washer splines and mainshaft splines align.

Start at the mainshaft bottom and install the air line in the keyway to 
lock the washer in place. As limit washers and gears are installed, continue 
to push the air line up.

[FIGURE: C12407A.gif]

Against the 3rd speed gear washer, position the 3rd speed gear spacer.

With clutching teeth down and engaged with the spacer external splines, 
position the 3rd speed gear on the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12408A.gif]

Against 3rd speed gear, position a mainshaft spacer.

With the washer flat side down, position the limit washer against the 
spacer. Rotate the washer until the washer splines and mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12409A.gif]

Between the gear hub and mainshaft spacer, insert 0.152-mm (0.006-inch) 
feeler gauge and 0.381-mm (.015-inch) feeler gauge. If out of tolerance, 
change the limit against the mainshaft spacer.

With the flat side up, position the 1st speed gear limit washer (white) 
in the next available groove. Rotate the washer until the washer splines and 
mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12410A.gif]

Against the limit washer, position the mainshaft spacer.

With clutching teeth up, position the 1st speed gear on the mainshaft 
against the spacer.

Position 1st speed gear spacer against 1st speed gear, engaging the 
spacer external splines with gear clutching teeth.

With washer flat side down, position the limit washer against the 
spacer. Rotate the washer until the washer splines and mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C12411A.gif]

Between the gear hub and mainshaft spacer, insert 0.152-mm (0.006-inch) 
feeler gauge and 0.381-mm (0.015-inch) feeler gauge. If out of tolerance, 
change the limit against the mainshaft spacer.

Align the sliding clutch missing internal spline with the mainshaft key 
and install the 1st-reverse speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C12412A.gif]

With the flat side up, position the reverse speed gear limit washer 
(white) in the next available groove. Rotate the washer until the washer 
splines and mainshaft splines align.

Push the air line up to lock the washer on the mainshaft.

Against the limit washer, position reverse speed gear spacer.

[FIGURE: C12413A.gif]

Install reverse gear on the mainshaft. Engage the gear clutching teeth 
with spacer splines and sliding clutch. Move the reverse gear down against the 
1st speed gear.

 CAUTION: Be careful not to move the gears while doing the following procedure. 
The limit washers are unlocked and can rotate which would cause the gears to 
drop. 

At this time remove the air line and insert the mainshaft key.

Install the mainshaft key snap ring.

Remove the mainshaft from the vise.

On the shaft front, align the sliding clutch missing internal spline 
with the mainshaft key and install the 3rd-drive gear sliding clutch. Engage 
the sliding clutch external splines with the 3rd speed gear clutching teeth.

[FIGURE: C12414A.gif]

Make sure reverse gear is against 1st speed gear. Make sure the 
mainshaft key is in the keyway. Make sure the 3rd speed sliding clutch is 
engaged into 3rd speed gear.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Output Shaft Assembly

 NOTE: When using the soft bar and maul on the output shaft, be careful not to 
damage the threads.

 NOTE: When removing the rear bearing cover, the rear bearing cone drops from 
the housing bore.

 Disassembly 

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the output shaft forward and through 
the rear bearing assembly.

From the auxiliary housing rear, remove the rear bearing retaining 
capscrews, cover, and gasket.

[FIGURE: C12415A.gif]

Clean the gasket mounting surface of gasket material.

Inspect the rear bearing cover oil seal for damage. Remove if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12416A.gif]

From the auxiliary housing rear, remove the bearing cup and spacer.

[FIGURE: C12417A.gif]

From the auxiliary housing front, remove the remaining bearing cup.

From the output shaft, remove the bearing inner spacer.

[FIGURE: C12418A.gif]

[FIGURE: C12419A.gif]

Use the output shaft assembly gear front face as a base, press the 
output shaft through the bearing and gear.

[FIGURE: C12420A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Make sure the magnetic plugs are installed in the auxiliary housing.

 NOTE: Output shaft stack up should be done on a clean, flat surface.

 NOTE: When heating the bearings, do not heat bearings above 136°
C (275°F).

 NOTE: When installing the rear bearing race, the proper depth is when the 
race shoulder is seated on bearing bore top.

 NOTE: Because the collar becomes distorted when compressed, do not use an old 
nylon collar in the rear bearing cover.

Use toolmaker's dye to mark the LO range gear for timing purposes.

Mark any two adjacent teeth on the LO range gear. Repeat the procedure 
for the two adjacent teeth directly opposite the first set marked.

With splined washer facing up, place the washer on the output shaft 
shoulder.

[FIGURE: C12421A.gif]

With LO range gear clutching teeth down, position LO range gear on the 
output shaft. Engage the washer splines.

[FIGURE: C12422A.gif]

With chamfer side up, position the LO range gear rear washer on the 
output shaft against the LO range gear.

[FIGURE: C12423A.gif]

With tapered side up, use heat or appropriate driver and install the 
output shaft front rear bearing.

[FIGURE: C12424A.gif]

On the output shaft, position the bearing inner spacer. Set aside.

[FIGURE: C12419A.gif]

Lay the auxiliary housing front face up on a clean, flat surface. 
Install the front bearing cup.

[FIGURE: C12425A.gif]

Turn the auxiliary housing over, install the rear bearing spacer and 
rear bearing race in the bearing bore.

[FIGURE: C12426A.gif]

To finish procedure, refer to Auxiliary Section, Countershaft 
Assembly Installation in Removal and Installation portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Synchronizer Assembly

 NOTE: Place the synchronizer assembly on a clean, flat surface. Cover the 
synchronizer assembly with a shop rag to prevent losing the three springs 
under pressure from the HI range synchronizer pin locations.

 Disassembly 

Place the larger LO range synchronizer ring on the bench.

Grab both sides of the HI range synchronizer and pull.

[FIGURE: C12438A.gif]

From the synchronizer ring LO range pins, remove the sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C12439A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Assembly should be done on a clean, flat surface slightly lower than 
your waist.

Pins on the LO range synchronizer must line up with the chamfered holes 
on the sliding clutch bottom.

When compressing the HI range synchronizer springs, cover with a shop 
rag. In the event compression is not achieved the first time, this prevents 
the springs from leaving the bench area.

On the bench place the larger LO range synchronizer ring face down with 
pins up.

With the sliding clutch recessed side up, place the sliding clutch on 
the LO range synchronizer pins.

[FIGURE: C12439A.gif]

In the HI range synchronizer bores, install the three springs.

[FIGURE: C12440A.gif]

Place the HI range synchronizer ring over the LO range synchronizer 
ring. Rotate the HI range synchronizer until the springs are seated against 
the pins.

[FIGURE: C12441A.gif]

With a shop rag, cover the assembly.

Apply downward pressure to the HI range synchronizer ring while 
twisting counterclockwise. This compresses the springs to fully seat HI range 
on the LO range synchronizer.

[FIGURE: C12442A.gif]

Make sure there are three springs and are fully compressed.

Make sure you can move the sliding clutch from HI to LO range and back.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Countershaft Assembly

 NOTE: Never use the PTO gear as a pressing base. The narrow width of this 
gear can cause breakage.

 Disassembly 

From each countershaft front, remove the drive gear retaining snap ring.

[FIGURE: C12449A.gif]

Using the rear face of 3rd speed gear as a base, press the drive gear, 
PTO gear, and 3rd speed gear from each countershaft. This removes the front 
bearing inner race.

[FIGURE: C12450A.gif]

Inspect the key and roll pin, remove if damaged.

[FIGURE: C12451A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Except for the PTO gears, the upper and lower countershaft assemblies 
are the same. To avoid confusion during installation, mark the upper 
countershaft (45-tooth PTO gear) with a "U". The lower countershaft has a 
47-tooth PTO gear.

If previously removed, install the roll pin and key in countershaft 
keyway.

Align 3rd speed gear keyway with the countershaft key and press the 
gear on the countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12452A.gif]

Align PTO gear keyway with the countershaft key and press the gear on 
the countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12453A.gif]

Align drive gear keyway with the countershaft key and press the gear on 
the countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12454A.gif]

On each countershaft front, install the drive gear retaining snap ring 
in groove.

Use a flanged-driver or the press to install the bearing inner race on 
the countershaft front against the drive gear.

[FIGURE: C12455A.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

Shimming Procedure for Tapered Bearings

 NOTE: The shimming procedure can be done in the horizontal or vertical 
position. The procedure is done the same.

 NOTE: Shims must be aligned properly or the rear bearing cover can be damaged 
when final torque is applied.

Remove the countershaft straps. Make sure a 3.175-mm (0.125-inch) 
countershaft rear bearing shim is installed. Be sure the countershaft rear 
bearing races are seated in the bearing bores.

[FIGURE: C12456A.gif]

Install two clean 3/8-inch x 1-inch capscrews without washers directly 
across from each other in each bearing cover. Tapped holes in auxiliary case 
must be free of thread adhesive.

[FIGURE: C12457A.gif]

Tighten the capscrews to 0.8 Nm (7 lb-in). Do not 
install the countershaft rear bearing cover gasket.

[FIGURE: C12458B.gif]

Rotate the output shaft six times clockwise, then six times 
counterclockwise to seat the countershaft rear bearings. Use a feeler gauge, 
as close to each capscrew location as possible, and measure the gap between 
the countershaft rear bearing cover and the auxiliary case. Record the 
measurements. Using the average measurement, refer to the shimming chart in 
the Specifications portion of this section to identify the proper shim.

Remove the countershaft rear bearing cover and gauging shim.

Place the selected shim on the rear countershaft bearing race.

Position a new gasket on countershaft rear bearing cover mounting 
surface.

[FIGURE: C12459A.gif]

Position the countershaft rear bearing cover over the new gasket.

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the retaining capscrews.

Install the retaining capscrews. Tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12460B.gif]

Repeat Steps 1-8 for the other countershaft rear bearing cover.

Make sure the input shaft rotates.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Shift Selectors

Vehicle manufacturers may choose different types of shift selectors for 
their equipment. The shift selector in an Allison-equipped vehicle will be 
similar to one of those shown below.

[FIGURE: D13161A.gif]

 Push-Button Shifter 

The push-button shift selector has reverse, neutral, drive, up and down 
arrows, a mode button, and a digital display. When a range button has been 
pressed, a tone will sound, the SELECT indicator will display the chosen 
operation (if the ECU determines the shift is acceptable), and the 
transmission will shift to the starting range as indicated on the monitor 
display. In DRIVE, selection of a specific gear can be accomplished by 
pressing the up or down arrow buttons. Conditions resulting in the DO NOT 
SHIFT light located on the instrument panel will disable the pad and no tones 
will be heard.

 Shift Lever Selector 

The lever selector is an electromechanical control. The pattern of 
positions can vary according to the shift selector installed. Positions R, N, 
and D are selected by pressing a hold override button and choosing the desired 
gear. It is possible to move between forward drive positions without pressing 
the hold override button. A mode button (a dash-mounted switch can be used) is 
located on lever and push-button shift selectors to activate a second shift 
schedule or specialized function when desirable. The mode being utilized is 
identified above the mode button. The display will indicate MODE ON for most 
programmed functions.

 Mode Button 

This feature is located on the shift lever and push-button shifters and 
can be used to activate a second shift schedule (this is typically programmed 
for "economy," which will enable the transmission to shift at a lower engine 
rpm to conserve fuel).

 Display Mode 

A display mode button is included on the lever selector to allow access 
to diagnostic code information. The capability is included on the push-button 
selector by pressing the up and down arrow buttons at the same time.

This button is included on the shift lever selector to allow access to 
diagnostic code information. The capability is included on the push-button 
selector by pressing the up and down arrow buttons at the same time.

 Allison MD3060 and MD3560 

With an Allison MD-equipped vehicle, selecting the right moment to 
upshift or downshift during changing road and traffic conditions is not 
necessary. The Allison MD does it for you. However, knowledge of the gear 
ranges and when to select them will make vehicle control and driving even 
easier.

 WARNING: THESE TRANSMISSIONS HAVE NO PARK POSITION. BEFORE LEAVING THE DRIVER 
SEAT EVEN MOMENTARILY, WHETHER THE ENGINE IS RUNNING OR SHUT OFF, ALWAYS SHIFT 
INTO N (NEUTRAL) AND SET THE PARKING BRAKE OR EMERGENCY BRAKE. ALWAYS USE 
WHEEL CHOCKS. UNEXPECTED AND POSSIBLY SUDDEN VEHICLE MOVEMENT MAY OCCUR IF 
THESE PRECAUTIONS ARE NOT TAKEN. 

 NOTE: The vehicle must be completely stopped before shifting from forward to 
reverse or from reverse to forward. The select indicator will display R and 
the monitor will display R when reverse is attained.

The MD3060 and MD3560 automatics are six-speed transmissions that have 
five forward driving ranges, as described below. These transmissions are 
electronically controlled and are available with a push-button or shift lever 
shifter.

Reverse: The vehicle must be completely stopped before shifting from 
forward to reverse or from reverse to forward. The select indicator will 
display R and the monitor will display R when reverse is attained.

Neutral: Place the transmission in neutral before starting the engine. 
The engine will not start in any other gear (if it does, the neutral start 
circuit must be serviced immediately). Neutral is also used during stationary 
operation of the power takeoff (if so equipped).

 WARNING: DO NOT ALLOW THE VEHICLE TO COAST IN NEUTRAL. TRANSMISSION BRAKING IS 
NOT AVAILABLE IN NEUTRAL. THIS PRACTICE CAN RESULT IN TRANSMISSION DAMAGE. 

Drive: The vehicle will attain first gear when drive is selected, and 
as the speed increases, the transmission will automatically upshift through 
each gear. As the vehicle slows down, the transmission will automatically 
downshift.

5-2: Occasionally, the road conditions, load, or traffic conditions 
will make it desirable to restrict the automatic shifting to a lower gear. 
These positions also provide progressively greater engine braking for going 
down grades (the lower the gear, the greater the braking effect).

First gear: Use this gear when pulling through mud and deep snow, when 
maneuvering in tight spaces, or while driving up or down grades. Low gear 
provides the vehicle with its maximum driving power and maximum engine braking 
power.

 NOTE: The MD3060 and MD3560 transmissions incorporate a hold feature to 
prohibit upshifting above the gear selected during normal driving. For 
downhill operation, the transmission may upshift above the highest gear 
selected when the engine governed speed is exceeded, and damaging the engine 
is a possibility.

 NOTE: In case of engine shutdown (i.e., running out of fuel) while the 
transmission is in gear, the transmission will remain in gear until the 
ignition key is turned to the OFF position. After the ignition key has been 
turned to the OFF position, the transmission will automatically shift to 
neutral and the monitor on the shift pad will display NEUTRAL when the 
ignition key is in the ON position. If the vehicle is equipped with a shift 
lever shifter, the transmission will return to neutral (when the ignition key 
is turned to OFF) but the engine cannot be restarted until the shift lever has 
moved to the NEUTRAL position.

Power takeoff operation: The PTO drive gear on these transmissions is 
engine-driven and provides direct engine power. The power takeoff can be 
operated when the vehicle is moving or stopped.

The PTO gear is in constant mesh with the drive gear in the converter 
housing. A friction clutch or constant drive is used to transmit power to the 
PTO output.

DO NOT SHIFT: If this light illuminates (accompanied by eight seconds 
of short beeps from the shift selector) while the vehicle is in operation, it 
indicates the ECU has detected the transmission operating parameters have been 
exceeded and the shifts are being restricted (i.e., upshifts and downshifts 
may be restricted). Also, the SELECT digit on the shifter display will be 
blank. A diagnostic code will be recorded in the ECU if this happens. The 
transmission will continue to operate in order to seek service assistance. If 
the vehicle is equipped with a push-button shifter, it will not operate. If 
equipped with a shift lever and the lever is moved, a continuous alarm will 
sound until the original shift lever position is restored.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Throttle Linkage Check 

 NOTE: Whenever the throttle linkage has been adjusted, adjust the throttle 
modulator linkage. 

When the throttle linkage is properly adjusted, maximum engine 
performance starting and accelerating a heavily loaded truck is obtained 
automatically. The driver need only press the accelerator pedal to the WOT 
position and hold it there. With the accelerator pedal held at the WOT 
position, the transmission will stay in the starting gear until engine 
crankshaft speed approaches the engine governed speed (maximum engine 
performance), then it will shift into the next higher gear. The automatic, 
full throttle (at detent) shifting just under governed speed will continue 
until the highest gear or desired road speed is reached.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Diagnostic Codes, MD-Series

The following is a list of some of the most common diagnostic codes. 
For a complete listing accompanied by service information, see the Allison 
MD-Series Troubleshooting Manual.

The diagnostic codes are broken down into a two-digit main code and a 
two-digit sub-code.

 CODES 13/12 AND 13/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

13

12

Battery voltage to electronic control unit (ECU) is too low

13

23

Battery voltage to the ECU is too high

If the condition is intermittent, closely inspect the vehicle wiring 
for transmission system power and grounds. Check for loose, dirty or painted 
connections. Check the vehicle interface module (VIM) for loose, incorrect or 
overheating relays or fuses. Check for wires that are chafed and touching 
other components.

 CODES 21/12 AND 21/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

21

12

Throttle position sensor failed low

21

23

Throttle position sensor failed high

This code indicates the throttle position sensor has been released or 
pulled by its linkage into an error zone, a fault with the sensor or the 
wiring to the sensor of the ECU. Perform Pinpoint Test A .

 NOTE: Main Code 21 in conjunction with Main Code 33 indicates the potential 
loss of common ground between the throttle and temperature sensors.

 CODES 24/12 AND 24/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

24

12

Oil temperature cold

24

23

Oil temperature hot

This code indicates the ECU has detected a high or low temperature in 
the transmission sump. All shifts are inhibited when Code 24/12 is set. No 
upshifts are allowed above a calibration range when code 24/23 is set. All 
inhibits are cleared when the temperature conditions are normal.

Should the hot oil code appear (24/23), shift the transmission to 
neutral and accelerate the engine to 1200-1500 rpm to allow the transmission 
to return to normal temperature 71°-104°C (160°
-220°F) before operation can take place. 
Check the transmission oil level.

 CODES 33/12 AND 33/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

33

12

Oil temperature sensor low

33

23

Oil temperature sensor high

This code indicates the ECU has diagnosed a fault with the sump 
temperature sensor or associated circuitry. This indicates the sensor failed 
showing abnormally high or low temperature readings.

 CODES 35/00 AND 35/16

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

35

00

Power interruption (this would occur only after the power has been
restored). During power interruption, the DO NOT SHIFT light will illuminate
but the transmission will shift.

35

Power interruption at the same time the ECU is recording a critical code

This code indicates the ECU has detected a complete power loss before 
the ignition was turned off.

Air is supplied to the system at the air supply port by the vehicle's

supply air line to the supply ports of the range valve and the slave valve. 
Depending upon the position of the knob on the range valve, air will pass 
through either the low range air line or the high range air line to the range 
shift cylinder.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Slave Valve, Preselection 

An air valve shaft protruding from the shift bar housing prevents the 
actuating piston in the slave valve from moving while the shift lever is in a 
gear position and releases the piston when the lever is moved to or through 
neutral.

[FIGURE: C9523B.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 5330
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 07-06: Shift Controls, Manual Transmission, Air

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Range Cylinder 

In low range, air pressure is supplied from the slave valve to the low 
range port in the range cylinder. This air pressure forces the range cylinder 
piston to the rear, engaging the low range gearing. Air pressure on the back 
of the piston and in the high range air line is exhausted out the slave valve. 

In high range, air pressure is supplied from the slave valve to the 
high range port of the range cylinder cover. This air pressure forces the 
range cylinder piston forward, engaging the high range gearing. The air 
pressure that was on the front side of the piston and in the low range air 
line during low range operation is exhausted out the slave valve.

[FIGURE: C95241A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 5331
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 07-06: Shift Controls, Manual Transmission, Air

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Roadranger® Valve A-5010 

Constant air pressure is supplied from the slave valve to the S port of 
the Roadranger® valve. In low range (ranger lever down), air 
passes through the lever and out the P port of the Roadranger®
 valve. This air returns to the slave valve to the end port or P port 
depending on the type of slave valve used. In high range (control lever up) 
the lever prevents the air from passing through the Roadranger®
 valve. Air pressure that was in the outlet line is 
exhausted out the bottom of the Roadranger® valve.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Intermediate Shift Cylinder 

Constant, regulated air is channeled through the cover to the front 
side of shift piston. Air is always on the side of piston. 

The shift piston is moved by removing or applying air (from constant 
supply) to the backside of piston. This piston area is larger and can overcome 
the area of front side of piston. The removal or application of air on 
backside of piston is controlled by the insert valve in cylinder cover; this 
valve in turn is controlled by the Roadranger® valve.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Deep Reduction Air System

 Roadranger® Valve A-5015 

In addition to the various components of the range shift air system, 
the deep reduction air system utilizes a reduction cylinder and a Roadranger®
 valve A-5015. 

Constant air from the air filter/regulator assembly is supplied to the 
Roadranger® valve A-5015. Air is supplied to the built-in 
deep reduction valve only while in low range from tee fitting at the low range 
or L port of slave valve. The insert valve is installed in the cylinder cover 
to provide the proper airflow needed to move the reduction piston in the 
cylinder. 

With the deep reduction button in the rearward position, the SP port of 
Roadranger® valve is closed and no air is supplied to the 
center port of cylinder cover. 

While in low range, the button can be moved forward to operate in deep 
reduction. The SP port of valve is opened when deep reduction selection is 
made, supplying air to the center port of cylinder cover. 

While in high range, the mechanical interlock of the Roadranger®
 valve prevents movement of deep reduction button to the 
forward position.

Slave Valve (19470 or A-5000)

Travel of the small insert valve piston is only 0.794 mm (0.031 inch). 
As shown in the illustrations below, when no air is applied to the top side of

freely through the insert valve and to the backside of cylinder piston, moving

range). When air is applied to the top side of valve piston through the signal 
line, the piston moves down to cut off air supplied to the backside of 
cylinder piston. This air is exhausted out bottom port of the cover when 
constant air supplied from the regulator is directed to the front side of 
cylinder piston, moving the yoke bar rearward to engage deep reduction gearing 
(deep reduction).

 Insert Valve 

The insert valve located in the shift cylinder cover is a small 
30.163-mm (1.19-inch) valve. It is installed with the flat surface to the

bore of cover.

The insert valve is self-contained and cannot be disassembled except 
for the three O-rings on the outer diameter. These three O-rings are a 
stationary seal and do not move in cylinder. 

Travel of the small piston in insert valve is approximately 0.794 mm 
(0.03 inch). The insert valve is a normally open valve.

piston, the constant air from regulator passes through the insert valve and to 
the backside of the piston and moves the yoke bar forward (direct).

of shift piston. Air in the shift cylinder is exhausted out through the insert 
valve and bottom bore of cover.

front side of shift piston moves the shift bar to the rear.

Shift Controls

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the vehicle owner's original concern by operating the air shift 
system to duplicate the concern.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Slip out (splitter or range)

Slow shift (splitter or range)

Does not shift (range)

Burned synchronizer

Overlapping gear ratios

Air leaks in system or transmission case

 NOTE: Before installing any screws, coat the threads with Threadlock®
 and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSK-M2G315-A5.

proceed to the following symptom chart.

 Component Tests 

 Air Filter 

The air filter contains a replaceable filter element that can be 
removed by turning out the end cap. This element must be cleaned or replaced 
at each oil change, or more often under high humidity conditions. 

 Air Regulator 

With normal vehicle air pressure and the gearshift lever in neutral, 
check the breather port on the side of the regulator. There should be no air 
leaking from the port. If there is a steady leak of air from this port, this 
indicates a damaged regulator that must be replaced. 

Cut off the vehicle air pressure and install an air gauge in the output 
port of the regulator. Bring the vehicle air pressure back to normal. 
Regulated air pressure range is 396-431 kPa (57-62 psi). 

 Slave Valve, Poppet-Type (19470) 

The poppet-type slave valve is a nonserviceable valve. If the valve is 
damaged, the complete assembly must be replaced. Perform the following 
preliminary checks prior to valve replacement. 

Check air fittings and air lines between the slave valve and range 
valve for restrictions. A restriction in the line between the outlet port of 
the range valve and the P port of slave valve can cause a constant air leak 
out the exhaust port of the slave valve. 

Check the torque of the four 1/4-inch slave valve mounting capscrews. 
Tighten to 11 Nm (97 lb-in) and determine if the valve 
functions properly. If the capscrews are not tightened correctly an air leak 
between the slave valve and the transmission case can result. 

If retightening the four slave valve capscrews eliminates the air 
leaks, remove the valve from the transmission and tighten the three No. 10 
Phillips head base plate screws on the back of the valve to 61 Nm
 (45 lb-ft). If the four slave valve retaining capscrews 
are equipped with star washers, install flatwashers under the star washers to 
prevent them from fretting into the valve. Reinstall the valve and tighten 
capscrews to 11 Nm (97 lb-in). 

If the valve continues to leak after the above checks have been made, 
the valve must be replaced. 

<a name="extract_837

Section 07-06: Shift Controls, Manual Transmission, Air

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Roadranger® Valve 

 Removal 

Drain the air from the system. 

Remove the screws in the side of the shift handle skirt, and slide the 
skirt down on the shifter shaft.

[FIGURE: C91471A.gif]

 NOTE: If you experience difficulty removing the air line from the fitting, a 
slight impact to the tool used on the release sleeve helps remove the secured 
line. 

Remove the air line fittings from under the valve. 

The release sleeve must be depressed to remove the air line. A plastic 
tube cutter, a 5/32-inch open-end wrench, or equivalent can be used to depress 
the sleeve. 

To remove the air line, apply pressure evenly to both sides of the 
release sleeve and pull the tubing from the fitting. 

Loosen the lock nut and unscrew the valve from the shifter shaft.

[FIGURE: C9149B.gif]

 Installation 

Install the shift control valve on the shifter shaft and tighten the 
lock nut. 

Install the air lines to the valve. 

The air line cut end must be smooth and square. Use a plastic tubing 
cutter or a sharp razor knife. Do not use diagonal cutters; they deform the 
tubing. If the air line end is deformed or burred, the internal O-ring can be 
damaged, which causes leaks. 

To install the air line, insert the cut tubing into the fitting. Make 
sure the tubing is seated fully (approximately 19 mm [3/4 
inch]. Give a slight tug to make sure the air line is secured. 

 NOTE: Before installing screws, coat the threads with Threadlock®
 and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Slave Valve, Piston-Type (A-5000) 

 Disassembly 

Disconnect all air lines, turn out the four capscrews and remove the 
slave valve from the transmission. 

Turn out the three capscrews and remove the side cap. 

Remove the seal from the piston and remove the O-ring from the seal. 

Remove the spring from the piston. 

Turn out the end cap from the valve body and remove the piston from the 
bore. 

Remove the U-seal from the piston. 

Remove the nylon plug from the piston and remove the O-ring from the 
plug. 

Remove the snap ring from the bore in front of the valve body. 

Remove plug, spring, washer and U-seal from valve body bore. Remove 
O-ring from plug. 

Lubricate all O-rings and U-seals with silicone lubricant and 
reassemble the slave valve. 

 Assembly 

Follow disassembly procedure in reverse order. When reinstalling the 
end cap, do not use more than 54 Nm (40 lb-ft) of torque. 
Overtightening can result in binding the piston in the valve bore.

Section 08-00: Clutch System, Service

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch System

The purpose of the clutch is to transfer power from the engine to the 
drivetrain. It connects and disconnects a manually-operated transmission and 
the remainder of the drivetrain system from the engine. This permits starting 
and stopping the vehicle, shifting and changing speeds that correspond to the 
engine speed through gear reductions for both forward and reverse directions.

Check clutch and clutch linkage for proper adjustment.

Clutch Dragging 

Intermediate plate not retracting (separator pins not set correctly) 
(Two-Plate Clutch).

Intermediate pressure plate separator pin not set correctly. With 
clutch in release position, PRY intermediate plate with separator pin towards 
transmission. (Pins will reset when clutch is engaged.)

Driven disc distorted or warped.

REPLACE disc. GO to Pinpoint Test C .

Internal clutch adjustment not correct.

READJUST clutch for standard release travel. GO to Pinpoint Test G .

Splines worn on input shaft of transmission.

REPLACE input shaft and CHECK driven disc hubs for excessive wear. If 
worn, REPLACE disc. CHECK flywheel housing alignment of engine and 
transmission. MAKE SURE driven discs slide freely on drive gear splines.

Flywheel pilot bearing fitting too tightly in flywheel or on end of 
drive gear.

CHECK flywheel bore diameter or input shaft pilot diameter. FIT in 
flywheel and on drive gear pilot. If bearing is rough, REPLACE.

Facings gummed with oil or grease.

REPLACE facings or entire driven disc assembly. Cleaning not recommended.

Damaged clutch release bearing.

REPLACE bearing. If bearing is grease type, LUBRICATE with engine 
running.

Clutch release shaft projecting through release yoke.

RELOCATE release shaft so it does not project.

Broken intermediate plate.

REPLACE intermediate plate/driven disc assembly.

Clutch Pedal Binding

Check pedal shaft and bushings.

REPLACE pedal bushings if worn. LUBRICATE pedal shaft and bushings in

equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. CHECK pedal support bracket 
bore. REPLACE pedal support bracket if bore is elongated. REPLACE transmission 
input shaft retainer if worn.

Release bearing and hub assembly binding on transmission input shaft 
retainer.

LUBRICATE bearing hub with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C 
or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B.

Clutch linkage binding due to linkage misadjustment.

ALIGN clutch linkage.

Worn equalizer bar assembly spherical ball bearings.

REPLACE spherical ball bearings.

Linkage binding no grease — or worn parts.

GREASE linkage or REPLACE worn parts.

Excessive Engine Crankshaft End Play

SERVICE engine per specifications. REFER to Section 03-00 , or

Clutch Vibration (Torsional), Vehicle Moving at Road Speed 49-88 km/h

INSTALL specified clutch disc.

Aftermarket (off-brand) clutch disc installed.

INSTALL specified clutch disc.

Engine not functioning properly.

CHECK engine performance, TUNE UP engine.

Incorrect installation of coupling shaft or drive shaft assembly.

Pressure plate imbalance.

GO to Pinpoint Test E .

Transmission-Related Problems

Insufficient clutch reserve (excessive clutch pedal free play).

Gear Clash

Clutch housing misalignment.

REALIGN clutch housing.

Pressure plate release hang-up.

Pinpoint Tests

PINPOINT TEST A: CLUTCH SLIPPAGE

 A1 VERIFY CLUTCH SLIPPAGE 

Chock the wheels and set the parking brake.

Start the engine, shift into fourth gear and increase engine speed to 
2,000 rpm.

Slowly release the clutch pedal.

 Does the engine stall within five seconds?

Yes

No

Clutch is not slipping. RETURN to the Symptom Chart .

GO to A2 
 .

 A2 INSPECT CLUTCH PEDAL 

Inspect the clutch pedal pivot point for proper lubrication.

 Is the clutch pedal pivot point properly lubricated?

Yes

No

GO to A3 
 .

LUBRICATE the clutch pedal pivot point.

 A3 INSPECT CLUTCH ASSEMBLY (DISC/PRESSURE PLATE) 

Inspect clutch disc for oil or grease.

 Is clutch disc contaminated with oil or grease?

Yes

No

REFER to Section 08-01 .

INSPECT clutch disc, clutch pressure plate and flywheel for wear. REFER 
to Clutch Disc/Discs, Clutch Pressure Plate, or Flywheel Runout Check in the Cleaning and Inspection 
 portion of this section. REPLACE as necessary. REFER 
to Section 08-01 for replacement procedures.

 B1 CHECK CLUTCH CHATTER OR SHUDDER 

Start engine, press clutch pedal and shift into first gear.

Shift into reverse and increase engine speed between 1200 and 1500 rpm.

 Is clutch chatter or shudder noise evident?

Yes

No

GO to B2 
 .

Clutch OK.

 Is clutch assembly tight and free of oil?

Yes

No

 .

PINPOINT TEST C: CLUTCH DRAG

 C1 CHECK FOR CLUTCH DRAG 

Start engine, press clutch pedal and shift into first gear.

Wait five seconds and shift into reverse.

 Are gears clashing or dragging?

Yes

No

to Section 08-01 .

Clutch OK.

PINPOINT TEST D: CLUTCH PEDAL PULSATION

 D1 CHECK CLUTCH PEDAL PULSATION

 Does clutch pedal pulsate?

Yes

No

REFER to Section 08-01 .

Clutch pedal OK.

PINPOINT TEST E: CLUTCH-RELATED VIBRATIONS

 E1 CHECK VIBRATIONS 

Raise vehicle on hoist.

Check engine mount interlocks for grounding.

Check for any other engine component (e.g., exhaust manifold, valve 
cover, etc.) grounding on body or frame.

Lower vehicle.

Discontinue accessory drive belts one at a time and check for vibration.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Pressure Plate 

 CAUTION: Do not use cleaners with a petroleum base, and do not immerse the 
pressure plate in the solvent. 

 NOTE: If a substantial difference in lever wear exists, the heavily worn 
lever is binding. Replace the pressure plate.

Inspect friction surface of the pressure plate for scoring, burring, 
heat checking or distortion. If friction surface is badly scored, heat 
checked, warped or dished in excess of 0.254 mm (0.010 inch), replace with new 
cover assembly. Smooth and flat pressure plate surfaces must be used for 
satisfactory clutch life. 

Clean the pressure plate and flywheel surfaces with a suitable 
commercial solvent to be sure that surfaces are free from any oil film. 

Using a straightedge and a feeler gauge, check the face runout of the 
pressure plate. If the runout is greater than the service limit, replace the 
clutch cover assembly.

Service limit: 0-0.50 mm (0-0.02 inch)

[FIGURE: C11476A.gif]

 NOTE: Always check the condition of the engine flywheel for cracks, heat 
checks or other damage whenever the clutch is inspected, removed or replaced.

Clutch Disc(s)

 NOTE: For adjustment-free clutch, go to Step 2.

Block the release bearing with wood blocks (1/2 x 1/2 x 3 inches for 
two-plate and 1/2 x 1-3/4 x 3 inches for single plate), using the tool 
provided in Spicer Clutch Service Kit (CSK1) or equivalent tool as shown. 

[FIGURE: C10321A.gif]

Remove the clutch from the flywheel. Refer to Section 08-01 for service 
details. 

 NOTE: For dual clutch disc assemblies, the front and rear disc may have 
different thickness. 

Check the driven disc. 

Using a vernier caliper, measure the gauge (facing) thickness in three 
or four areas around each clutch disc. If less than service limit, replace 
clutch disc.

356-mm (14-inch) Super Duty

Standard: 9.14 mm (0.360 inch)

Service: 7.37 mm (0.290 inch)

356-mm (14-inch) Stamped Angle-Spring or 394-mm (15.5-inch) Cast 
Angle-Spring

Standard: 11.4 mm (0.450 inch)

Service: 9.65 mm (0.380 inch)

[FIGURE: C11477A.gif]

If the thickness varies by more than 0.203 mm (0.008 inch) on the 
facing surface, replace the disc. Measurements are taken on pad (clutch disc) 
in similar locations and distances from outer edge of clutch disc.

[FIGURE: C10322A.gif]

evident, replace the disc. 

Using a feeler gauge, measure the clearance between the clutch disc 
spline and the transmission input shaft spline. If the clearance is greater 
than the service limit, replace the clutch disc.

Standard: 0.05-0.15 mm (0.002-0.006 inch)

Service Limit: 0.5 mm (0.02 inch)

[FIGURE: C11478A.gif]

concavity 

convexity 

runout 

allowable grind for a reground flywheel

Refer to Flywheel in the Cleaning and Inspection portion of this section.

Check the pilot bearing. If the bearing is rough, replace it. 

 NOTE: When installing a new disc, be careful not to drop it or contaminate it 
with oil or grease.

Perform the following checks:

Check the clutch disc facing for oil or grease (eliminate the source of 
any contamination).

Check the clutch disc for worn or loose facings.

Check the clutch disc for loose rivets in the hub.

Check the clutch disc for distortion.

Check for broken springs, (springs loose enough to rattle will not 
cause noise when vehicle is operating).

Replace the clutch disc if any of these conditions are present.

 Two-Disc Clutch with Positive Separator, 356-mm (14-Inch), 356-mm 
(14-Inch) Stamped Angle Spring and 394-mm (15.5-Inch) Cast Angle Spring

Flywheel

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Flywheel Runout Check

Position Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent to the 
engine flywheel housing with gauge finger on the face of the flywheel near the 
outer edge. Rotate flywheel, making sure to hold it in the full forward or 
rearward position so that the crankshaft end play will not be indicated as 
flywheel runout. Maximum allowable runout is 0.127 mm (0.005 inch) per inch of 
the flywheel diameter. For example, 0.178-mm (0.007-inch) runout is allowable 
for a 356-mm (14-inch) clutch.

[FIGURE: C9451C.gif]

If the clutch face runout exceeds specification, remove the flywheel 
and check for burrs between the flywheel and face of the crankshaft mounting 
flange. If no burrs exist, check the runout of the crankshaft mounting flange. 
Replace the flywheel or machine the crankshaft flywheel mounting face 
sufficiently to correct the surface if the mounting flange runout exceeds the 
specification of 0.203 mm (0.008 inch).

If the crankshaft mounting flange is not the cause of the runout, 
resurface or replace the flywheel as necessary. To resurface, refer to Section 03-00 . To remove or replace the flywheel, refer to Section 03A-01 or Section 03B-01 . For the Cummins engine, refer to the Cummins Engine Service Manual, 
for the CAT engine, refer to the CAT Diesel Engine Service Manual, and for DDC 
engines, refer to the Detroit Diesel Engine Service Manual.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Pilot Bearing, Ball Type

Check the fit and rotation of the clutch pilot bearing in the bore of

lithium-base grease. 

 CAUTION: Avoid using too much lubricant because it may contaminate the clutch 
disc when the clutch revolves.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Release Bearing

Wipe all oil and dirt off the release bearing. The bearing is 
prelubricated and should not be cleaned with solvent.

Inspect the release bearing as follows:

 NOTE: A light intermittent clicking noise may result during pedal application 
(to limit of pedal free-travel) and upon further pedal depression, a normal 
bearing noise may be audible. Some noise under these situations will not 
adversely affect clutch function and does not necessarily indicate a failed 
release bearing or out-of-plane pressure plate release levers. Inspection of 
these components is not required unless the noise is excessive.

Hold the bearings, hub and back plate and rotate the outer race while 
applying pressure. If the bearing rotation is rough, replace the bearing.

Inspect/remove any surface scoring or burrs that may affect the sliding 
motion of the release bearing on the transmission input shaft. Any scoring or 
burrs should be polished off with a fine grade emery paper.

Inspect release bearing hub groove for freedom from nicks and burrs or 
lever wear. Replace the bearing only if there is excessive wear on lever 
groove or yoke contact surface.

The following are failure situations for release bearing operation:

Too little clutch pedal free play may allow contact of clutch fingers 
on bearing, resulting in a continuous running bearing.

Riding the clutch pedal has the same effect as above.

Misalignment of clutch release lever.

Misalignment between engine and the transmission will exhibit symptoms 
such as transmission jumping out of gear, driveshaft vibration, excessive spin 
time resulting in gear clash, and clutch chatter on start-up.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Release Lever/Shaft

shaft as required.

Check that the release lever fork tips are not excessively worn and 
that the curved portion of the lever is curved with no flat spots. Also, check 
that the locating flats do not show signs of excessive wear or grooving and 
replace as necessary.

ADJUSTMENTS

Clutch Adjustment Procedures

Various service tips have been developed to help the heavy truck 
service technician troubleshoot and adjust Spicer stamped angle-spring clutch. 
These include the following: 

recognizing symptoms of potential concerns

inspecting and checking the affected clutch components

determining which clutch parts actually require replacement

adjusting procedures for synchronized and non-synchronized transmissions

If service is required, use the following service procedure to adjust 
and check the clutch components. 

 Clutch, Spicer Disc Pull-Type, Cast Angle Spring and Stamped Angle 
Spring with Kwik-Adjust Adjustment 

The linkage on a 356-mm (14-inch) stamped angle spring single or 
multiple-disc clutch and 356-mm (14-inch) or 394-mm (15.5-inch) cast angle 
spring (CAS) multiple disc clutch should not be adjusted to compensate for 
clutch face wear. Linkage should only be reset to provide proper pedal free 
play upon installation of a new clutch and not every time the clutch is 
adjusted internally. If linkage is adjusted for proper pedal free play, it 
should be done after specified bearing release travel is obtained. Proper 
linkage settings are given in Section 08-02 . 

To make an internal clutch adjustment, remove the clutch housing cover 
from the bottom of the clutch housing. 

Remove the pedal free play by lightly placing the clutch release lever 
against the release bearing. Measure the distance between the release bearing 
and the clutch brake (non-synchronized transmission) or input shaft cover 
(synchronized transmission). The dimension between the release bearing and the 
clutch brake or input shaft cover (bearing release travel) should be 12.7-14.2 
mm (0.500-0.560 inch).

[FIGURE: C9196D.gif]

Adjust the clutch assembly by rotating the engine flywheel until the 
Kwik-Adjust adjustment bolt is exposed.

[FIGURE: C11140C.gif]

Hold or block the clutch pedal in the released position. 

Use a 5/8-inch (6-point) socket. Apply an inward pressure on adjusting 
bolt (hex-head). A clockwise adjustment will move release bearing housing 
toward the transmission, a counterclockwise adjustment will move release 
bearing housing toward the flywheel. Rotation will move the release bearing 
approximately 0.51 mm (0.020 inch). 

Remove the clutch pedal block to engage the clutch. 

Recheck the clearance as outlined in previous steps. Readjust if 
necessary. Check clutch pedal free play travel (inches). If it is not within 
specification, then a linkage adjustment should be made. Refer to Section 08-02 . 

Install the clutch housing cover on the clutch housing.

 Clutch, Spicer Disc Pull-Type, Cast Angle Spring with Self-Adjuster 

The linkage on a 356-mm (14-inch) or 394-mm (15.5-inch) CAS 
multiple-disc clutch should not be adjusted to compensate for clutch face 
wear. Linkage should only be reset to provide proper pedal free play after the 
internal clutch adjustment has been made. If linkage is adjusted for proper 
pedal free play, it should be done after specified bearing release travel is 
obtained. For proper linkage settings, refer to Section 08-02 . Internal clutch 
adjustment is necessary only after clutch replacement.

To make an internal clutch adjustment, remove the inspection cover from 
the bottom of the clutch housing.

Remove the pedal free play by placing the clutch release lever against 
the release bearing. Measure the distance between the release bearing and the 
clutch brake of the non-synchronized transmission. The dimension between the 
release bearing and the clutch brake or input shaft cover (bearing release 
travel) should be 12.7-14.2 mm (0.500-0.560 inch).

[FIGURE: C9196D.gif]

Adjust the clutch assembly by rotating the engine flywheel until the 
self-adjustment bolts are exposed.

Loosen left bolt and remove right bolt.

[FIGURE: C12752A.gif]

Rotate adjuster upward. This will disengage worm gear from the 
adjusting ring to allow manual adjustment. Hold adjuster, disengage and 
tighten left bolt.

[FIGURE: C12753A.gif]

Rotate adjusting ring as required to attain 13-14 mm (0.500-0.560 inch) 
of release bearing gap.

[FIGURE: C12754A.gif]

Loosen left bolt. Rotate adjuster downward to engage worm with 
adjusting ring teeth. Adjusting ring may have to be rotated slightly to allow 
worm to mesh.

[FIGURE: C12755A.gif]

Tighten left bolt to 41-47 Nm (30-35 lb-ft).

Install right bolt and tighten to 41-47 Nm (30-35 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12756A.gif]

Install the cover (inspection) on the clutch housing.

 Clutch Brake Adjustment 

 Non-Synchronized Transmissions 

Adjust the external linkage rod so that the clutch brake squeeze begins 
about 12.7-33 mm (0.5-1.3 inch) from the end of the end of the pedal stroke. 

[FIGURE: DC0018A.gif]

Check the adjustment results by placing a business card (or similar 
device) behind the clutch release bearing and depressing the clutch pedal. The 
card should be held tight. 

Release the clutch pedal. See if the card slips out when the pedal is 
approximately 12.7-33 mm (0.5-1.3 inch) from the end of the pedal stroke. 

 Stamped Angle-Spring with Adjustment Free Clutch 

No adjustment is needed for this type of clutch. As the clutch wears, 
the internal self-adjuster will automatically adjust for free play and travel.

If the clutch is not releasing properly, the clutch assembly may need 
to be replaced. Refer to Section 08-01 . After replacement of the clutch, 
actuate the clutch by pushing the pedal all the way to the floor five to ten 
times. This will set the release bearing gap to specification of 13-14 mm 
(0.500-0.560 inch). Set free play (initially after replacement) by adjusting 
the clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

 Clutch Free Travel 

 Non-Synchronized Transmissions 

Adjust the clutch internally to get about 38.1-50.8 mm (1.5 to 2.0 
inch) free play at the top of the pedal stroke or 3.2 mm (0.126 inch) as shown 
below between yoke and wear pads. Visually check both free travel and release 
travel as shown below. This is the clutch pedal up.

[FIGURE: DC0019B.gif]

Adjust the Spicer clutch assembly by rotating the engine flywheel until 
the Kwik-Adjust adjustment bolt is exposed. 

Use a 5/8-inch (6-point) socket. Apply an inward pressure on adjusting 
bolt (hex-head). A clockwise adjustment will move release bearing housing 
toward the transmission, a counterclockwise adjustment will move release 
bearing housing toward the flywheel. Rotation will move the release bearing 
approximately 0.51 mm (0.020 inch). 

The clutch pedal must be pushed to the floor to turn the adjusting ring 
using Kwik-Adjust adjustment bolt. 

[FIGURE: C11140C.gif]

Remove clutch pedal free play. Check the distance from the clutch 
release bearing to the transmission input shaft cover or clutch brake. There 
must be 12.7-14.2 mm (0.50-0.56 inch) movement of the release bearing for 
proper clutch release. Adjust the clutch internally to obtain this. 

Whenever clutch pedal free play becomes 1/2 inch or less, readjustment 
is recommended. 

 Synchronized Transmissions 

Check measurement with clutch pedal up. Refer to Section 08-02 .

 NOTE: When checking release bearing gap, remove pedal free play.

Adjust Kwik-Adjust bolt to obtain a 12.7-14.2-mm (0.50-0.56-inch) gap 
between input shaft cover and release bearing, as shown in the illustration. 
(47.625 mm [1.875 inch] and 19.05 mm [
0.75 inch] shown are reference values.) 

[FIGURE: DC0020B.gif]

To set 12.7-14.2 mm (0.50-0.56 inch) dimensions as shown, proceed as 
follows: 

With pedal depressed, turn the adjusting ring to obtain a 12.7-14.2-mm 
(0.50-0.56-inch) release bearing gap.

Turn the adjusting ring clockwise to move the release bearing toward 
transmission. 

Turn the adjusting ring counterclockwise to move the release bearing 
toward the engine. 

To set 3.2 mm (0.126 inch) dimensions as shown, proceed as follows: 

Adjust the external linkage by shortening or lengthening to obtain 3.2 
mm (0.126 inch) between the release yoke fingers and the wear pads on the 
release bearing housing. 

Check to see that this adjustment provides approximately 38.1 mm (1.5 
to 2.0 inch) of free travel at the pedal. 

Tighten all lock nuts. 

Whenever clutch pedal free play becomes 12.7-mm (0.5-inch) or less, 
readjustment is recommended.

PAGE 5366
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 08-00: Clutch System, Service

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Clutch and Driven Disc Check 

If the release of the clutch is still not acceptable after the linkage 
and clutch adjustments have been made, proceed as follows: 

Adjust the clutch so that there is no free travel. 

 Kwik-Adjust Adjustment Bolt 

[FIGURE: C11140C.gif]

[FIGURE: C10319A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not adjust linkage. 

Turn the adjusting bolt counterclockwise to increase release bearing 
travel. 

This will create additional release bearing travel. 

It increases the internal pressure plate travel. 

Test drive and determine if the release of the clutch has been affected. 

If the release has improved, replace the driven discs only. Refer to 
 Section 08-01 for service details. 

Readjust the clutch after replacing the discs. 

 Clutch Brake Check (Non-Synchronized Transmissions) 

Clamp the clutch brake, on the outside diameter, in a vise. 

Slide a modified input shaft (a cut input shaft with a nut welded on it 
to accommodate a torque wrench) through the clutch brake. 

[FIGURE: C10320A.gif]

Connect the torque wrench to the nut and rotate two half turns. Take 
note of the torque reading. 

The torque should not read lower than 16.3 Nm (12 
lb-ft). 

If the reading is higher than 16.3 Nm (12 lb-ft), 
reuse the brake. 

If lower, replace it. 

If the reading is more than 47.5 Nm (35 lb-ft), 
replace the clutch brake to eliminate the possibility of tang breakage. 

 Clutch Release Bearing Adjustment 

Set the gap between the release bearing and the front cover of the 
input shaft (synchronized transmissions) or the clutch brake (non-synchronized 
transmissions) to 12.7-14.2 mm (0.500-0.560 inch).

Rotate the engine flywheel until the Kwik-Adjust bolt is exposed.

Release the clutch by holding the clutch pedal in the depressed position.

Remove the free play from the clutch linkage by bringing the release 
lever against the wear pads of the release bearing.

Check the distance as described in Step 1 of this procedure. If 
adjustment is necessary, engage the Kwik-Adjust bolt and adjust until desired 
setting is reached using 5/8-inch (6-point) socket. Counterclockwise rotation 
of the Kwik-Adjust bolt will move the release bearing towards the flywheel. A 
clockwise rotation will move the release bearing away from the flywheel.

Disengage the Kwik-Adjust bolt and engage the clutch and recheck as 
outlined in Step 1 of this procedure.

ADJUSTMENTS

Flywheel Housing Alignment 

Inspection or alignment of the flywheel housing is indicated when 
symptoms exist of excessive transmission gear wear, transmission jumping out 
of gear, driveline vibration, clutch pedal vibration or rough feel, pilot 
bearing noise, release bearing noise, or excessive clutch spin time. Common 
complaint areas or obvious misadjustment should always be checked and 
corrected prior to checking alignment, to be sure the basic system is in 
working order. 

Alignment of the flywheel housing bore and rear face with engine should 
be checked as a possible cause of any of the following troubles: excessive 
transmission gear wear, transmission jumping out of gear, clutch pedal 
vibration or scrubby pedal feel, driveline variation, excessive pilot bushing 
wear, or excessive clutch spin time. Whenever any of the above problems are 
identified, the clutch housing should be given a complete inspection. 

The engine and transmission must have a common axis. The following 
checks must be made to locate possible misalignment. Clean all surfaces 
thoroughly before taking readings or checking parts. 

 NOTE: When taking the following readings, rotate the engine by hand; do not 
crank the engine with the starter. Engine may be rotated by the pulley nut at 
the front end of the crankshaft, or from the flywheel mounting bolts, or 
starter ring gear on the flywheel. Release compression on the diesel engines.

 NOTE: Before taking dial indicator measurements of the engine flywheel or 
flywheel housing, make sure the engine crankshaft does not have excessive end 
play and excessive bearing clearance. If it does, accurate readings can not be 
obtained. 

Inspect for a worn or fretted pilot on both the transmission clutch 
housing and the engine flywheel housing. The 3.2-mm (0.126-inch) pilot lip of 
the transmission clutch housing can wear into the flywheel housing either by 
the transmission loosening up or after high mileage just from the road and 
engine vibration. Any appreciable amount of wear on either part will cause 
misalignment and the part should be replaced. The wear will generally be found 
between the 3 o'clock and 8 o'clock positions. 

[FIGURE: C35291A.gif]

 Common Housing Wear Areas 

[FIGURE: C35301A.gif]

Use Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent to measure 
the face of the engine flywheel housing. Secure the dial indicator to the 
engine flywheel with the gauge stylus against the housing face. Rotate the 
flywheel by hand and, with chalk or soap stone, mark the high and low points 
of the indicator as it is being rotated. 

[FIGURE: C9450C.gif]

The total runout mean will be the difference between the highest plus 
and minus readings. Maximum total runout for the flywheel housing pilot is 
0.203 mm (0.008 inch) with No. 1 and No. 2 housings. 

 Flywheel Housing Pilot Runout 

[FIGURE: C35321A.gif]

 NOTE: If you have to reposition the flywheel housing, it is necessary to mark 
your high and low runout readings in the clock positions. 

Use dial indicator to measure the bore of the engine flywheel housing. 
With the dial indicator secured to the flywheel, move gauge stylus against the 
bore of the flywheel housing. Mark the high and low points. SAE maximum total 
runout for the flywheel housing bore is 0.203 mm (0.008 inch) with No. 1 and 
No. 2 housings. 

[FIGURE: C9449C.gif]

Use dial indicator to measure the flywheel face. Secure the dial 
indicator to the engine flywheel housing with gauge finger against the face of 
the flywheel near the outer edge. Turn the flywheel to obtain readings. A 
runout or face wobble of 0.127 mm (0.005 inch) per inch of flywheel radius is 
allowed. For example, if the vehicle has a 356-mm (14-inch) clutch and 
readings are taken just off the outer edge of the clutch disc, maximum 
tolerance would be 0.178 mm (0.007 inch).

[FIGURE: C35341A.gif]

Use Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent to measure 
the pilot bearing bore of the flywheel. With the indicator secured to the 
flywheel housing, move gauge stylus to contact pilot bearing bore surface. 
Turn the flywheel and obtain readings. SAE maximum total runout for the pilot 
bearing bore is 0.127 mm (0.005 inch). 

[FIGURE: C35351A.gif]

The transmission clutch housing face and pilot cannot be checked 
accurately in the field, unless a set of case bore plugs and shaft are used. 
This setup consists of plugs with very close fits that are screwed into the 
front and rear bores of the transmission case. A shaft fits through the 
centers of the plugs and extends to the front far enough to secure the dial 
indicator and obtain reading on the clutch housing. SAE maximum runout for the 
transmission clutch housing face and pilot is 0.203 mm (0.008 inch) with No. 1 
and No. 2 housings. 

 NOTE: Exceeding these limits causes misalignment. If not corrected, 
misalignment causes premature wear of drivetrain components. 

Use dial indicator to measure the flywheel crankshaft face. Secure the 
dial indicator to the engine flywheel housing with the gauge finger against 
the crankshaft face near the outer edge. Turn the crankshaft to obtain 
readings. A runout of 0.0381 mm (0.0015 inch) on the crankshaft face is 
allowed. 

[FIGURE: C35361A.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment Correction

Since any change in face alignment will change bore alignment, it may 
be possible to correct bore alignment by changing the face alignment. Face 
alignment can be changed by shimming between the flywheel housing and engine. 
The following illustration shows the type of shim that can be fabricated. 

[FIGURE: DC0017A.gif]

The shim required is one half the maximum (minus) indicator reading, 
and should be located at the point of maximum (minus) indicator reading.

If both the bore and face alignment are out of limits, shim between the 
flywheel housing and engine to bring the face alignment within limits. Check 
the bore alignment.

If the bore alignment is out of limits and face alignment is within 
limits, shim the flywheel housing to the limit of face misalignment and check 
the bore alignment. If it is not within limits, replace the housing.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch System

The purpose of the clutch is to transfer power from the engine to the 
drivetrain. It connects and disconnects a manually-operated transmission and 
the remainder of the drivetrain from the engine. This permits starting and 
stopping the vehicle, shifting and changing speeds that correspond to the 
engine speed through gear reductions for both forward and reverse directions. 

The driven disc is either a 356-mm (14-inch) single or dual plate, or a 
394-mm (15.5-inch) dual plate. The cover assembly consists of a cover, 
pressure plate, pressure springs and a release bearing assembly. There are 
four clutch models available: the 356-mm (14-inch) Stamped Angle Spring (SAS) 
single and dual plate types, the 356-mm (14-inch) and 394-mm (15.5-inch) Cast 
Angle Springs (CAS), which are dual plate-type clutch assemblies. Current 
releases utilize the Kwik-Adjust adjuster on the 356-mm (14-inch) and 394-mm 
(15.5-inch) with assist springs. The self-adjusting clutch does not contain 
assist springs. All model clutches are pull-type and function by pulling on 
the release bearing, which is engaged to the release lever. 

When the clutch is in the engaged position, the pressure springs load 
the pressure plate holding the clutch disc clamped firmly between the flywheel 
and the pressure plate. 

When the clutch pedal is depressed, movement is transmitted to the 
clutch mechanical linkage which turns the release shaft and actuates the 
clutch release lever. 

As the release shaft turns, the clutch release lever pulls back on the 
release bearing, unloading the levers and pressure springs, permitting the 
pressure plate to move away from the clutch disc. The clutch disc is 
disengaged from the engine/flywheel and the transmission may be shifted to 
another gear. 

Another internal part is a pilot ball bearing mounted in the flywheel 
which supports the end of the input shaft. The bearings are designed for long 
life and require no periodic maintenance. 

The Spicer clutch discs are available with either organic or primarily 
ceramic facings which provide long life. Damper-style hubs, self-adjusting and 
adjustment-free clutches are also available.

Spicer clutches utilize angle springs and are a dry disc, adjustable, 
pull-type design using centrally located pressure springs isolated from the 
heat of the pressure plate. The 356-mm (14-inch) and 394-mm (15.5-inch) CAS 
clutches use drive straps to hold the pressure plate in position. The clutch 
release bearing rotates continuously and only carries a thrust load when the 
clutch is released. On all L-Series vehicles, the release bearing can be 
lubricated through the transmission lower inspection opening in the clutch 
housing. Anti-friction bushings are used in the release lever system to help 
provide low release load at the pedal.

================================================================================
PAGE 5372
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 08-01: Clutch/Pressure Plate

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Brake 

The purpose of the clutch brake is to slow down or stop the 
transmission input shaft from rotating on non-synchronized transmissions. This 
permits a clean engagement of either first or reverse gears when starting the 
vehicle from a standstill. 

Non-synchronized transmissions use a torque limiting clutch brake. The 
brake is a steel hub with two tangs, encased in a cover that has a facing 
material bonded to both sides. The torque limiting feature is provided by an 
internal slip washer, loaded by a wave spring washer, that is then driven by 
the hub. The spring washer reacts against the clutch brake cover on the one 
side and the internal slip washer on the other, providing a clamping force and 
creating a breakaway torque within the brake. This feature is called torque 
limiting. The hub and spring washer combination slips with respect to the 
covers after approximately 24 Nm (18 lb-ft) load has been 
exceeded. This protects the outer facings.

When the operator depresses the clutch pedal beyond the normal clutch 
disengage position, the clutch release bearing comes in contact with the 
clutch brake and the transmission input shaft bearing cover. Because the tangs 
on the brake hub are engaged in the transmission input shaft splines, the 
transmission is slowed down or stopped. The driver can then shift from first 
to reverse or from reverse to first without clashing or putting undue strain 
on the gears.

[FIGURE: C94821A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Clutch Preassembly Procedures

 WARNING: DO NOT INHALE THE DUST FROM BRAKES, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. 
INHALATION OF DUST FROM THESE COMPONENTS COULD BE INJURIOUS TO YOUR HEALTH. 
COMPRESSED AIR OR BRUSHES MUST NOT BE USED TO CLEAN BRAKES, BRAKE DRUMS, 
CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. USE A VACUUM CLEANER SUCH AS ROTUNDA BRAKE, 
CLUTCH, SERVICE VACUUM 164-R3600 OR EQUIVALENT EQUIPPED FOR THIS PURPOSE TO 
REMOVE ANY DUST. ADHERENT DUST SHOULD BE REMOVED WITH A DAMP RAG. ANY DUST 
SHOULD BE CONTAINED IN A SEALED AND LABELED BAG FOR DISPOSAL. WEAR AN APPROVED 
HIGH EFFICIENCY CARTRIDGE OR AIR LINE RESPIRATOR AND USE EXTRA CAUTION TO 
AVOID BREATHING THIS DUST. 

Clean the following components by scraping them and soaking them in a 
suitable solvent.

flywheel housing face and bore 

clutch housing face 

transmission input shaft

front face

Check for any damage or excessive wear and service as necessary. Clean 
the clutch housing interior with a suitable solvent. 

Clean the transmission input shaft with a wire brush, then polish the 
shaft and clean with a suitable solvent. Check condition of the transmission 
input shaft. Use a crocus cloth or file to dull sharp edges of the splines. If 
splines are worn excessively or notched, the clutch disc will not slide on the 
shaft. Replace the input shaft as required. 

Clean the flywheel face with a suitable solvent. 

Clean the clutch release lever with a wire brush. Smooth the clutch 
release lever fingers locating faces with a carborundum stone and then clean 
with a suitable solvent. Apply a light coating of Motorcraft Premium Long-Life 
Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to 
the clutch release lever finger tips and locating faces. If clutch release 
lever is worn excessively, replace it. 

Apply Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to the cross-shaft bushings until clean 
grease appears from all four bushings. Remove the excess grease. 

If reinstalling the old clutch, clean the pressure plate with a 
suitable solvent. 

If the shaft/fork assembly has not been dismantled, check that the 
shafts do not protrude into the fork locating space and make sure that the 
non-operating shaft end is flush with the outside of the clutch housing. Make 
sure that the assembly turns freely.

Install four shipping bolts (adjustment-free clutch only).

 CAUTION: Whenever the clutch is removed, spacer blocks must be installed to 
prevent release bearing from moving forward and bottoming. If the release 
bearing is allowed to move too far forward, the internal levers in the clutch 
cover may partially come out of the groove in the retainer. If the cover is 
reinstalled, internal binding of the clutch or loss of levers can occur. Both 
are detrimental to the performance of the clutch. 

Install two 1/2 x 1-3/4 x 3-inch spacer blocks between the clutch cover 
and the release bearing assembly to relieve the heavy internal spring load in 
the clutch assembly. If there is inadequate clearance to install the spacers, 
use the release fork tool provided in the Spicer Clutch Service Kit (CSK1) to 
pull back the release bearing assembly evenly and then install the spacer 
blocks.

[FIGURE: C9442C.gif]

flywheel and install two 3/8-16 x 2-inch guide studs to help support the 
weight of the clutch.

[FIGURE: C11141A.gif]

[FIGURE: C9443C.gif]

prevent cocking and bending of the clutch mounting bolts. Remove all of the 
mounting bolts and remove the clutch cover. 

Remove the alignment tool and the clutch disc from the flywheel. 

Inspect the engine flywheel housing and flywheel. Refer to Section 08-00 . If flywheel is heat-checked or warped, refer to Flywheel Clutch Surface 
Machining in Section 03-00 . To replace flywheel or flywheel housing, refer to

Check condition of the transmission input shaft. Use a stone to dull
