Inspect the pilot bearing. Refer to Section 08-00 . If required, remove 
the pilot bearing using a suitable puller. 

Check wear on fingers of the clutch release lever, cross-shaft and 
cross-shaft bushings. Replace any of the components if excessive wear is 
noted. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: If a new clutch is to be installed, a new pilot bearing must also be 
installed. 

If removed, install the pilot bearing using Pilot Bearing Replacer 
T93T-7025-EH for 44.45-mm (1.75-inch) input shaft or T93T-7025-BH for 38.1-mm 
(1.5-inch) input shaft and Driver Handle T80T-4000-W.

Install two guide studs (3/8-16 x 2-inch) at the 11 and 1 o'clock 
positions of the flywheel. 

 CAUTION: Clutch will not function correctly if disc is installed backwards. Make 
sure the side marked PRESSURE PLATE SIDE faces the pressure plate. 

Install the disc by inserting the aligning tool through the splines and 
into the pilot bearing.

With the alignment tool still in place, carefully slide the clutch 
cover assembly over the aligning tool and onto the guide studs. Align the 
Kwik-Adjust bolt or self adjuster with the opening in the clutch housing. 

 CAUTION: Use only Ford approved mounting bolts. 

Install the clutch cover mounting bolts and lock washers hand-tight. 
Tighten in the following sequence to 48-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C9444B.gif]

Replace the guide studs with the two mounting bolts, and tighten to 
48-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). 

 NOTE: Whenever an adjustment-free clutch assembly is removed, shipping bolts 
must be installed to prevent pressure plate from moving forward.

For adjustment-free clutch only, remove four shipping bolts from clutch 
cover. Save shipping bolts.

[FIGURE: DC0028A.gif]

For adjustment-free clutch only, check to make sure there is no visible 
gap between the spacer sleeve and the bolt head.

[FIGURE: C12985A.gif]

 NOTE: Save the spacer blocks installed during removal.

Remove the two spacer blocks from between the release bearing housing 
and the clutch cover assembly if they have not fallen out.

Remove the clutch aligning tool. Reinsert tool completely. Slowly move 
tool in and out to check for binding. If binding exists, reinstall clutch 
assembly. 

Install the clutch brake assembly on the transmission input shaft, if 
so equipped (non-synchronized transmission). Shift the transmission into gear. 

Rotate clutch release bearing housing so that flat section is on top. 

 NOTE: Clutch release bearings must be lubricated after adjustment and at 
regular maintenance intervals. Lubricate the release bearing with Motorcraft 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B. Clutches with a permanently sealed release bearing require no 
lubrication. 

Apply a small daub of grease to each of the clutch release lever 
fingers and the release bearing wear pads (both sides).

Install the transmission into the vehicle. Rotate clutch release lever 
so that release lever fingers clear the pads on the release bearing housing as 
the clutch housing is moved forward into position. 

Make sure the transmission is square to and aligned with the engine 
when it is raised into position. Use a transmission jack to support the 
transmission during installation.

Make sure the clutch release lever clears the bearing and is rotated 
over the wear pads as the clutch housing is moved forward. 

Align the splines by turning the transmission output shaft. Do not 
force the transmission onto the clutch or flywheel housing. If it does not 
enter freely, check the installation for a problem. 

 Engaging Clutch Release Lever 

[FIGURE: C9445B.gif]

Start all transmission retaining bolts and tighten progressively around 
the housing to recommended torque. Tighten clutch housing bolts to 48-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft). Refer to appropriate section in Group 07 to 
finalize transmission installation.

Connect clutch release linkage.

Check and adjust clutch.

For adjustment-free clutch, actuate the clutch assembly by depressing 
the clutch pedal five to ten times, releasing the clutch. Check release 
bearing travel. Release travel should be 13-14 mm (0.500-0.560 inch). Adjust 
clutch pedal free play with linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

For Kwik-Adjust clutch, check release bearing travel, clutch brake 
squeeze (non-synchronized transmission) and proper clutch pedal free play 
adjustment. Adjust as required according to instructions in the Adjustments 
 portion of this section and 
in Section 08-02 . 

Install clutch housing inspection cover.

cover may partially come out of the groove in the retainer. If the cover is 
reinstalled, internal binding of the clutch or loss of levers can occur. Both 
are detrimental to the performance of the clutch. 

Install two 1/2 x 1/2 x 3-inch spacer blocks between the clutch cover 
and the release bearing assembly to relieve the heavy internal spring load in 
the clutch assembly. If there is inadequate clearance to install the spacers, 
use the release fork tool provided in the Spicer Clutch Service Kit (CSK1) to 
pull back the release bearing assembly evenly and then install the spacer 
blocks.

[FIGURE: C9442C.gif]

Remove two top mounting bolts attaching the cover assembly to the 
flywheel and install two 3/8-16 x 2-inch guide studs to help support the 
weight of the clutch.

[FIGURE: C11141A.gif]

[FIGURE: C9443C.gif]

Loosen the remaining clutch cover bolts in a crisscross pattern to 
prevent cocking and bending of the clutch mounting bolts. Remove all of the 
mounting bolts and remove the clutch cover. 

Remove the alignment tool and the clutch rear driven disc. 

Remove the intermediate drive plate and adapter ring.

[FIGURE: C94461A.gif]

Remove the front driven disc. 

Inspect the engine flywheel housing and flywheel. Refer to Section 08-00 . If flywheel is heat-checked or warped, refer to Flywheel Clutch Surface 
Machining in Section 03-00 . To replace flywheel or flywheel housing, refer to 
 Section 03A-01 or Section 03B-01 .

Check condition of the transmission input shaft. Use a crocus cloth or 
file to dull sharp edges of the splines. If splines are worn excessively or 
notched, the clutch discs will not slide on the shaft. Replace the input shaft 
as required. 

Inspect the pilot bearing. Refer to Section 08-00 . If required, remove 
the pilot bearing using a suitable puller. 

Check wear on fingers of the clutch release lever, cross-shaft and 
cross-shaft bushings. Replace lever if necessary.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: If a new clutch is to be installed, a new pilot bearing must also be 
installed. 

If removed, install the pilot bearing using Pilot Bearing Replacer 
T93T-7025-EH and Driver Handle T80T-4000-W.

Install two guide studs (3/8-16 x 2-inch) at the 11 and 1 o'clock 
positions of the flywheel. 

 CAUTION: Clutch will not function correctly if disc is installed backwards. Make 
sure the side marked FLYWHEEL SIDE faces the flywheel. 

Install the front disc in the engine housing.

Check the condition of the clutch intermediate plate and adapter ring.

 CAUTION: The four holes at the drive straps are the pilot holes for the adapter 
ring. 

 CAUTION: Make sure the side marked FLYWHEEL SIDE faces the flywheel. 

 NOTE: The drive straps must face the pressure plate. 

Install the intermediate plate and adapter ring over the guide studs. 
Raise the front disc to fit into the intermediate plate opening. 

 CAUTION: Clutch will not function correctly if disc is installed backwards. Make 
sure the side marked PRESSURE PLATE SIDE faces the pressure plate. Make sure 
that both discs are properly installed. 

Install the rear disc by inserting the aligning tool through both 
splined hubs and into the pilot bearing bore. 

With the alignment tool still in place, carefully slide the clutch 
cover assembly over the aligning tool and onto the guide studs. Align the 
Kwik-Adjust bolt or self-adjuster with the opening in the clutch housing (at 6 
o'clock). 

 CAUTION: Use only Ford approved mounting bolts. 

Install the clutch cover mounting bolts and lockwasher hand-tight. 
Tighten in the following sequence to 48-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C9444B.gif]

Replace the guide studs with the two mounting bolts, and tighten to 
48-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). 

 NOTE: Whenever an ADJUSTMENT-FREE clutch assembly is removed, shipping bolts 
must be installed to prevent pressure plate from moving forward.

For adjustment-free clutch only, remove four shipping bolts from clutch 
cover. Save shipping bolts.

[FIGURE: DC0028A.gif]

For adjustment-free clutch only, check to make sure there is no visible 
gap between the spacer sleeve and the bolt head.

[FIGURE: C12986A.gif]

 NOTE: Save the spacer blocks installed during removal.

Remove the spacer blocks from between the release bearing housing and 
the clutch cover assembly.

Remove the clutch aligning tool. Reinsert tool completely. Slowly move 
tool in and out to check for binding. If binding exists, reinstall clutch 
assembly.

Install the clutch brake assembly, if so equipped, on the transmission 
input shaft. Shift the transmission into gear. 

Rotate clutch release bearing housing so that flat section is on top. 
If cross-shaft is below center, rotate bearing housing 180 degrees. 

 NOTE: Clutch release bearing must be lubricated after adjustment and at 
regular maintenance intervals. Lubricate the release bearing with Motorcraft 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B. Clutches with a permanently sealed release bearing require no 
lubrication.

Apply a small daub of grease to each of the clutch release lever 
fingers and the release bearing wear pads (both sides).

Install the transmission into the vehicle. Rotate clutch release lever 
so that release lever fingers clear the pads on the release bearing housing, 
as the clutch housing is moved forward into position. 

Make sure the transmission is square to and aligned with the engine 
when it is raised into position. Use a transmission jack to support the 
transmission during installation. 

Make sure the clutch release lever clears the bearing and is rotated 
over the wear pads as the clutch housing is moved forward. 

Align the splines by turning the transmission output shaft. Do not 
force the transmission onto the clutch or the flywheel housing. If it does not 
enter freely, check the installation for a problem. 

 Engaging Clutch Release Lever 

[FIGURE: C9445B.gif]

Start all transmission attaching bolts and tighten progressively around 
the housing to recommended torque. Tighten clutch housing bolts to 48-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft). Refer to appropriate section in Group 07 to 
finalize transmission installation.

Connect clutch release linkage.

Check and adjust clutch.

Remove clutch housing inspection cover.

For adjustment-free clutch, actuate the clutch assembly by depressing 
the clutch pedal five to ten times, releasing the clutch. Check release 
bearing travel. Release bearing travel should be 13-14 mm (0.500-0.560 inch). 
Adjust clutch pedal free play with clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

For Kwik-Adjust clutches, check release bearing travel, clutch brake 
squeeze and proper clutch pedal free play adjustment. Adjust as required 
according to instructions in the Adjustments 
portion of this section and in 
 Section 08-02 . 

Install clutch housing inspection cover.

Install a Truck Clutch Alignment Shaft D79T-7550-C or equivalent into 
the release bearing, discs and pilot bearing.

[FIGURE: C9453C.gif]

 CAUTION: Whenever the clutch is removed, spacer blocks must be installed to 
prevent release bearing from moving forward and bottoming. If the release 
bearing is allowed to move too far forward, the internal levers in the clutch 
cover may partially come out of the groove in the retainer. If the cover is 
reinstalled, internal binding of the clutch or loss of levers can occur. Both 
are detrimental to the performance of the clutch. 

Install two 5/8-inch spacer blocks between the clutch cover and the 
release bearing assembly to relieve the heavy internal spring load in the 
clutch assembly. If there is inadequate clearance to install the spacers, use 
the release fork tool provided in the Spicer Clutch Service Kit (CSK1) to pull 
back the release bearing assembly evenly and then install the spacer blocks.

[FIGURE: C94541A.gif]

Loosen the clutch cover bolts in a crisscross pattern to prevent 
cocking and bending of the clutch mounting bolts. 

Remove two top mounting bolts attaching the cover assembly to the 
flywheel and install two guide studs to help support the weight of the clutch.

[FIGURE: C11141A.gif]

[FIGURE: C9455B.gif]

Remove the remaining mounting bolts and remove the clutch cover. 

Remove the clutch rear driven disc. 

Remove the intermediate drive plate from the flywheel housing. 

Remove the front driven disc and alignment tool. 

Check wear on fingers of the clutch release lever, cross-shaft and 
cross-shaft bushings. Replace lever if necessary.

 CAUTION: If a new clutch is to be installed, a new pilot bearing must also be 
installed. 

Inspect and replace the pilot bearing as required. Refer to engine 
manufacturer's service information.

Check condition of the transmission input shaft. Use a crocus cloth or 
file to dull sharp edges of the splines. If splines are worn excessively or 
notched, the clutch discs will not slide on the shaft. Replace the input shaft 
as required. 

Inspect the engine flywheel housing and flywheel. If flywheel is 
heat-checked or warped, refer to the engine manufacturer's recommendations 
regarding machining or replacement. On models with the 14-2 flywheel, refer to 
the following steps for drive pin replacement.

 NOTE: The 14-2 flywheel contains drive pins.

 NOTE: The flywheel must first be removed from the engine to service the 
intermediate plate drive pins. 

Remove the two setscrews from each of the drive pin setscrew holes.

[FIGURE: C94561A.gif]

Remove the drive pins using a punch and hammer. 

 WARNING: TO AVOID SERIOUS INJURY TO EYES AND FACE, ALWAYS USE A BRASS HAMMER AND 
A DRIVE PIN ALIGNMENT TOOL (IF AVAILABLE) TO INSTALL THE DRIVE PINS. SAFETY 
GLASSES SHOULD BE WORN AT ALL TIMES. 

Install six new drive pins in the flywheel, equally spaced. Make sure 
the shanks of the drive pins are a press-fit in the flywheel rim, and that the 
heads are square with the friction face.

[FIGURE: C94571A.gif]

Position the intermediate drive plate over the drive pins. 

 CAUTION: Do not file or grind the drive pins to provide adequate clearance as 
this can cause uneven loading on the drive pins, which will result in clutch 
sticking, and possibly broken drive pins. 

Apply pressure to the intermediate drive plate in one direction and 
measure the clearance between the drive pins and the drive slots in the plate. 
The minimum clearance between the drive pins and the drive slots should be 
0.152mm (0.006 inch).

[FIGURE: C94581A.gif]

If the alignment and the clearance are correct, remove the intermediate 
plate and install new setscrews. The setscrews are 3/8 inch by 3/8 inch and 
two must be used to lock each drive pin. 

Install the flywheel to the crankshaft. Refer to the engine 
manufacturer's service information. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Clutch will not function correctly if disc is installed backwards. Make 
sure the side marked FLYWHEEL faces the flywheel. 

Install the front disc in the engine housing.

Check the condition of the clutch intermediate plate. 

Install the intermediate plate in the flywheel locating the drive slots 
over the drive pins. 

On 14-2 super duty clutch, make sure to use three anti-rattle springs 
equally spaced between the drive pins. Install with rounded sections toward 
the flywheel face (as indicated by arrow on anti-rattle spring).

[FIGURE: C94591B.gif]

 CAUTION: Clutch will not function correctly if disc is installed backwards. Make 
sure the side marked PRESSURE PLATE faces the transmission. 

Insert the clutch alignment tool into the hub of the rear clutch disc. 
Position the rear disc in place and push the alignment tool through the front 
disc and into the pilot bearing. 

With the alignment still in place, carefully slide the clutch cover 
assembly over the aligning tool and onto the guide studs. Align the 
Kwik-Adjust bolt or self adjuster with the opening in the clutch housing. 

 CAUTION: Use only Ford-approved mounting bolts. 

Install the clutch cover mounting bolts and washer hand-tight. Remove 
the guide studs and install the two bolts in their place. Tighten in the 
following sequence to 48-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C11142B.gif]

 NOTE: Save the spacer blocks installed during removal.

Remove the two spacer blocks from between the release bearing housing 
and the clutch cover assembly if they have not fallen out.

Remove the clutch aligning tool. Reinsert tool completely. Slowly move 
tool in and out to check for binding. If binding exists, reinstall clutch 
assembly. 

Install the clutch brake assembly on the transmission input shaft, if 
so equipped. Shift the transmission into gear. 

Rotate clutch release bearing housing so that flat section is on top. 
If cross-shaft is below center, rotate bearing housing 180 degrees.

flush against the flywheel.

ADJUSTMENTS

Clutch

 Internal Adjustment 

 Clutch, Spicer Disc Pull-Type, Stamped Angle Spring (Single and Double 
Disc with FD-1060 or FD-1460 Engine) 

 Manual Adjustment 

The linkage on a 356-mm (14-inch) single or multiple disc clutch should 
not be adjusted to compensate for clutch face wear. Linkage should only be 
reset to provide proper pedal free play at installation of a new clutch and 
not every time you adjust the clutch internally. If linkage is adjusted for 
proper pedal free play, it should be done after specified bearing release 
travel is obtained. For proper linkage settings refer to Section 08-02 . 

To make an internal clutch adjustment, remove the inspection cover from 
the bottom of the clutch housing. 

Remove the pedal free play by placing the clutch release lever against 
the release bearing. Measure the distance between the rear of the release 
bearing and the clutch brake or input shaft cover, depending on whether it has 
a synchronized or non-synchronized transmission. On vehicles equipped with 
356-mm (14-inch) Spicer clutches, the dimension between the release bearing 
and the clutch brake or input shaft cover (bearing release travel) should be 
13-14 mm (0.500-0.560 inch) for the FD-1060 and FD-1460 engines.

Adjust the clutch assembly by rotating the engine flywheel until the 
Kwik-Adjust bolt is exposed.

[FIGURE: C11140C.gif]

Hold or block the clutch pedal in the released position. 

Use a 5/8 (6-point) socket to turn the Kwik-Adjust bolt. Apply inward 
pressure on the spring and hex-head bolt, adjusting ring counterclockwise 
(looking from rear of vehicle) to move the release bearing toward the 
flywheel, or clockwise to move the release bearing away from the flywheel. 
Rotation or movement of one lug position will move the release bearing 
approximately 0.51 mm (0.020 inch). 

Remove the clutch pedal block to engage the clutch. 

Recheck the clearance as outlined in Step 2. Readjust if necessary. 
Check clutch pedal free travel (inches). If it is not within specification, 
then a linkage adjustment should be made. Refer to Section 08-02 . 

Install the inspection cover on the clutch housing. 

 Adjustment-Free 

The linkage on a 356-mm (14-inch) single- or multiple-disc clutch 
should not be adjusted to compensate for clutch face wear. Linkage should only 
be reset to provide proper pedal free play at installation of a new clutch. If 
linkage is adjusted for proper pedal free play, it should be done after 
specified bearing release travel is obtained. For proper linkage settings 
refer to Section 08-02 . Internal adjustment is only set at the installation of 
a new clutch. After installation, perform the following procedure.

 NOTE: The shipping bolts must be removed before adjusting clutch.

 NOTE: Perform Steps 1 and 2 only if shipping bolts were not removed during 
clutch installation.

Remove the inspection cover from the bottom of the clutch housing to 
access the four hex-head shipping bolts.

Remove shipping bolts.

Depress clutch pedal five to ten times in order to obtain the specified 
bearing release travel of 13-14 mm (0.500-0.560 inch).

Check free play (set clutch linkage). Refer to Section 08-02 .

Install inspection cover on the clutch housing.

 Clutch, Spicer Disc Pull-Type, Cast Angle Spring 

 Manual Adjuster 

The linkage on a 356-mm (14-inch) or 394-mm (15.5-inch) CAS 
multiple-disc clutch should not be adjusted to compensate for clutch face 
wear. Linkage should only be reset to provide proper pedal free play after the 
internal clutch adjustment has been made. If linkage is adjusted for proper 
pedal free play, it should be done after specified bearing release travel is 
obtained. For proper linkage settings, refer to Section 08-02 . 

To make an internal clutch adjustment, remove the cover (inspection) 
from the bottom of the clutch housing. 

Remove the pedal free play by placing the clutch release lever against 
the release bearing. Measure the distance between the release bearing and the 
clutch brake of the non-synchronized transmission. The dimension between the 
release bearing and the clutch brake or input shaft cover (bearing release 
travel) should be 13-14 mm (0.500 to 0.560 inch).

[FIGURE: C9196D.gif]

Adjust the clutch assembly by rotating the engine flywheel until the 
Kwik-Adjust adjustment bolt is exposed. 

[FIGURE: C11140C.gif]

Hold or block the clutch pedal in the released position. 

Use a 5/8 (6-point) socket. Apply an inward pressure on adjusting bolt 
(hex-head). A clockwise adjustment will move release bearing housing toward 
the transmission, a counterclockwise adjustment will move release bearing 
housing toward the flywheel. Rotation will move the release bearing 
approximately 0.51 mm (0.020 inch). 

Remove the clutch pedal block to engage the clutch. 

Recheck the clearance as outlined in previous steps. Readjust if 
necessary. Check clutch pedal free travel (inches). If it is not within 
specification, then a linkage adjustment should be made. Refer to Section 08-02 . 

Install the cover (inspection) on the clutch housing.

 Self-Adjuster 

The linkage on a 356-mm (14-inch) or 394-mm (15.5-inch) CAS 
multiple-disc clutch should not be adjusted to compensate for clutch face 
wear. Linkage should only be reset to provide proper pedal free play after the 
internal clutch adjustment has been made. If linkage is adjusted for proper 
pedal free play, it should be done after specified bearing release travel is 
obtained. For proper linkage settings, refer to Section 08-02 . Internal clutch 
adjustment is necessary only after clutch replacement.

To make an internal clutch adjustment, remove the inspection cover from 
the bottom of the clutch housing.

Remove the pedal free play by placing the clutch release lever against 
the release bearing. Measure the distance between the release bearing and the 
clutch brake of the non-synchronized transmission. The dimension between the 
release bearing and the clutch brake or input shaft (bearing release travel) 
cover should be 13-14 mm (0.500-0.560 inch).

[FIGURE: C9196D.gif]

Adjust the clutch assembly by rotating the engine flywheel until the 
self-adjustment bolts are exposed.

Loosen left bolt and remove right bolt.

[FIGURE: C12752A.gif]

Rotate adjuster upward. This will disengage worm gear from the 
adjusting ring to allow manual adjustment. Hold adjuster, disengage and 
tighten left bolt.

[FIGURE: C12753A.gif]

Rotate adjusting ring as required to attain 13-14 mm (0.500-0.560 inch) 
of release bearing gap.

[FIGURE: C12754A.gif]

Loosen left bolt. Rotate adjuster downward to engage worm with 
adjusting ring teeth. Adjusting ring may have to be rotated slightly to allow 
worm to mesh.

[FIGURE: C12755A.gif]

Install right bolt and tighten to 41-47 Nm (30-35 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12756A.gif]

Install the clutch housing inspection cover.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Control System, Mechanical

The mechanical clutch linkage is a system of leverage necessary to 
multiply the relatively small force at the clutch pedal to a larger force at 
the clutch pressure plate fingers.

ADJUSTMENTS

Clutch Pedal

A common pedal is used on all L-Series vehicles, except those equipped 
with FD-1060 and FD-1460 diesel engines. Instructions on adjusting pedal total 
travel and dimension locations for installation and free pedal measurements 
are shown below.

 NOTE: All adjustments are to be made with the engine off, and the parking 
brake engaged.

 NOTE: Adjustment of the linkage is only required after clutch replacement. Do 
not adjust the linkage to reset pedal free play after normal clutch facing 
wear has reduced it to less than 12.7 mm (0.50 inch).

 NOTE: The following linkage adjustments can only be made after verifying the 
clutch release bearing gap is within specification. Refer to Section 08-00 .

There are two independent adjustments that may need to be made: total 
travel and free play.

 Total Travel, All Except FD-1060 and FD-1460 Engines 

To adjust total pedal travel, loosen jam nut on pedal stop and press 
pedal enough so the rubber head on pedal stop can be hand-turned in or out 
until the required travel of 260-272 mm (10.25-10.75 inches) is achieved.

 Free Play 

 NOTE: The practice of using a ruler to measure free play from the pedal 
straight down to the floor board is not acceptable. This method does not take 
the arc of pedal travel into account and measures only the straight line 
distance and will always read less than the actual free play distance.

Using a suitable measuring tape, hook the end of the tape to the middle 
of the clutch pedal as shown in the following illustration. Pull the tape case 
back to the middle of the driver's seat so that it can be easily held in one 
hand and the initial measurement read.

[FIGURE: DC0044A.gif]

Use the other hand to push on the clutch pedal (following the pedal 
arc) using no more than three pounds of force, and read the distance of free 
play travel on the measuring tape. The difference between initial and final 
measurement readings is the free play travel, which should be between 
38.1-50.8 mm (1.5-2.0 inches). 

Use the following procedures if free play travel is not within 
specification.

 Free Play, All Except FD-1060 and FD-1460 

 NOTE: Refer to illustrations under Clutch Linkage in the Adjustments portion 
of this section for component location and orientation.

Install all parts as shown in the illustrations, except the trim rod 
and the clutch release rod assemblies.

Install 0.25-inch gauge pin through a hole in clutch vertical control 
lever and clutch release shaft bracket to retain lever.

Install release rod into release lever.

Rotate clutch lever counterclockwise until zero bearing lash is 
achieved and adjust clutch release rod assembly until clevis pin fits freely 
in bellcrank lever. Install clevis pin and tighten jam nut.

Install trim rod into pedal. With pedal held against the stop, adjust 
clevis on trim rod until it can be installed into lever. Turn clevis another 4 
turns to lengthen the rod and install into the lever. Tighten jam nut to 16-23 Nm
 (12-16 lb-ft). Remove gauge pin.

Verify free travel is within 38.1-50.8 mm (1.5-2.0 inches). If not, 
adjust clevis on trim rod until free play is within specification. The pedal 
free play in the cab is directly proportional to the 3.2 mm (0.126) free play 
measured between the release fork and release bearing.

 Free Play, FD-1060 and FD-1460 

 NOTE: Refer to illustration under Clutch Linkage in the Adjustments portion 
of this section for component location and orientation.

Install all parts.

Adjust trim rod until pedal exhibits free play shown in the 
illustration under Clutch Linkage. Tighten jam nut to 16-23 Nm
 (12-16 lb-ft).

Verify free travel is within 38.1-50.8 mm (1.5-2.0 inches). If not, 
adjust clevis on trim rod until free play is within specification. The pedal 
free play in the cab is directly proportional to the 3.2 mm (.120) free play 
measured between the release fork and release bearing.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Exhaust Brake

An exhaust brake is an auxiliary braking system that attaches to the 
engine exhaust system on vehicles equipped with diesel engines. The exhaust 
brake functions by partially closing off the exhaust manifolds, creating an 
increase in exhaust back pressure. 

During vehicle deceleration the engine must turn against the back 
pressure and this creates a braking effect on the driving wheels. The effect 
of the exhaust brake is to make the engine act as a compressor. 

The exhaust brake system is composed of the following components: 

dash-mounted control switch 

dash-mounted warning light 

one or more relays

accelerator switch 

clutch switch 

pneumatic solenoid control valve 

actuating cylinder 

exhaust brake body 

The following guidelines must be followed when installing an exhaust 
brake on Ford diesel engines or the warranty can be voided. 

Exhaust brake assembly must be mounted a minimum of 1.7 meters (5.5 
feet) downstream from the turbocharger. 

Maximum allowable exhaust back pressure is 241 kPa (35 psi) at 2860 rpm. 

The effect of an exhaust brake is not felt as a normal braking force as 
with service brakes, but is more of a gradual decelerating effect, as if the 
service brakes were lightly applied. 

The exhaust brake is used to aid the engine and the service brakes in 
slowing the vehicle, reducing service brake wear.

Muffler Inlet Pipe

With the dash-mounted switch on, accelerator pedal released and the 
clutch pedal in the UP (clutch engaged) position, the exhaust brake will be 
activated. The accelerator and clutch switches are closed and current is 
applied to the control valve. The control valve allows system air pressure to 
be applied to the actuating cylinder, which shifts the brake body butterfly 
valve to the closed position.

When the accelerator or clutch pedal is pressed, or when the anti-lock 
brake system (ABS) is activated, the switch will open and interrupt current to 
the control valve. The control valve will stop air pressure from going to the 
actuating cylinder, and will exhaust existing air from the cylinder. The 
return spring in the actuating cylinder will then open the exhaust brake 
butterfly valve.

When the exhaust brake switch is in the ON position, the exhaust brake 
unit will operate whenever the following conditions are met:

The clutch pedal must be in the UP (clutch engaged) position. 

The accelerator pedal must be in the idle position. 

The vehicle air supply system must be up to operating pressure.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Exhaust System

 Inspection and Verification 

Exhaust system performance complaints such as excessive back pressure 
are usually noticeable by their effect on engine performance. 

Other inoperative components can have similar effects on engine 
performance and be characterized by the same symptoms or complaints. Refer to 
the engine diagnosis and service procedures in the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual 
when attempting to diagnose engine performance concerns.

For general exhaust system concerns, refer to the symptom chart listed 
in this section. 

 Exhaust Leakage or Noise 

Noise can be caused by exhaust leaks. Inspect exhaust system for holes, 
openings, cracks or gaps. Clamp bolts must be tightened to specifications. 
Clamps must be visually inspected to ensure they are drawn tight.

 Exhaust Brake, Preliminary Inspection 

 CAUTION: Never operate the exhaust brake if engine condition is in doubt. Do not 
operate the vehicle if the exhaust brake is stuck in the on position or engine 
damage may result. 

Before testing the operation of the exhaust brake: 

inspect the exhaust system for leaks. 

the engine must be fully warmed up. 

the vehicle air system must be up to full operating pressure.

Follow standard back pressure test procedures if a chassis dynamometer 
is available. A chassis dynamometer is the preferred and most accurate method 
of achieving rated speed and load. If a chassis dynamometer is not available, 
use the following procedure:

Install pressure gauge to the back pressure test port found on either 
the muffler inlet pipe near the turbocharger outlet or the inlet side of the 
muffler and catalytic converter assembly. Use a gauge that has at least 3 
percent of full scale accuracy between zero and 10 in-Hg (140 in-H 2 
O).

If the vehicle does not have a tachometer, install a temporary one on 
the engine.

Run engine until it is warmed up and at normal operating temperatures.

Select a location and gear where an acceleration to wide-open throttle 
can be accomplished safely.

Drive vehicle at wide-open throttle and peak engine power. If possible, 
drive vehicle up a long hill or load vehicle to the maximum gross vehicle 
weight to attain maximum engine load and speed. Record the maximum exhaust 
back pressure when engine is at maximum RPM and load.

 Does exhaust back pressure reading exceed 6 in-Hg (82 in-H 2 
O)?

Yes

No

REPLACE muffler and catalytic converter assembly.

REFER to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

 Component Tests 

 Exhaust Brake Test 

With the accelerator and clutch pedals released and the transmission in 
gear from a speed of 33-48 km/h (20-30 mph), check for the following 
conditions: 

Road speed should decrease unless descending a steep grade or carrying 
a heavy load. 

Slight change in the sound of the engine when the exhaust brake is in 
use. 

When descending a grade, the vehicle speed increases slightly if the 
exhaust brake switch is turned to the OFF position. 

Engine exhaust smoke appears normal. 

When the accelerator is applied again, the exhaust brake is deactivated 
and the following conditions should exist: 

Throttle response is normal. 

There is a quick hissing noise from the exhaust brake control valve as 
it releases air pressure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Exhaust Brake Assembly

 Removal 

Disconnect the air line from actuating cylinder. 

Loosen the two clamps retaining the exhaust brake body to the inlet and 
outlet pipes. Slide the clamps onto the adjoining pipes. 

Remove the exhaust brake. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: The exhaust brake body must be installed in a specific direction. Make 
sure the arrow on the brake body is pointing in the direction of exhaust flow. 

Position the exhaust brake assembly to the inlet and outlet pipes. 

Install the clamps and tighten to specifications. 

Connect the air line to the cylinder. 

Start the vehicle and check for exhaust leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Actuating Cylinder 

 Removal 

Disconnect the air line from the actuating cylinder. 

Using a suitable drift, tap the roll pin from the cylinder mounting 
bracket pivot pin bushing. Remove the bushing from the pivot pin. 

Tap the roll pin from the exhaust valve lever pin bushing. Remove the 
bushing from the pin. 

 CAUTION: Actuating cylinder is under spring pressure. Use care when removing. 

Remove the actuating cylinder from the mounting bracket. 

 Installation 

Position the actuating cylinder on the mounting bracket pivot pin and 
on the exhaust valve lever pin. 

Position the bushings on the two pins, lining up the roll pin holes. 

Tap the roll pins through the bushings and pins. 

Connect the air line.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Actuating Cylinder 

 Disassembly 

Mount the air supply end of the cylinder in a vise, using care to 
prevent cylinder damage. 

Measure and record the assembled length of the cylinder. 

Loosen the jam nut and remove the nut and clevis from the end of the 
cylinder push rod. 

Using a pair of Channel Lock® pliers, loosen the 
center portion of the cylinder from the air supply end of the cylinder. 

Remove the cylinder from the vise and remove the air supply end of the 
cylinder from the end of the cylinder. 

Remove the push rods, springs, spring retainer and push rod locator 
from the cylinder. Remove the O-ring from the air supply end of the cylinder. 

 Assembly 

Lubricate seals and O-rings with Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A. 

Install the push rod, springs, spring retainer and push rod locator in 
the cylinder. Install the O-ring in the air supply end of the cylinder. 

Install the air supply end of the cylinder on the cylinder and push rod 
assembly. 

 CAUTION: Use care not to overtighten the cylinder and compress to O-ring. 

Position the cylinder in a vise, and tighten the cylinder to the 
cylinder air supply end until it contacts the O-ring. Then tighten the 
cylinder slightly more. 

Install the jam nut on the push rod and install the clevis on the push 
rod. Position the clevis and push rod so that the length of the assembled 
actuating cylinder and push rod equals the dimension recorded in the 
disassembly procedure. Tighten the jam nut against the clevis.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Engine Air Cleaner

 WARNING: DO NOT SMOKE OR CARRY LIGHTED TOBACCO OR OPEN FLAME OF ANY TYPE WHEN 
WORKING ON OR NEAR ANY FUEL-RELATED COMPONENT. HIGHLY FLAMMABLE MIXTURES ARE 
ALWAYS PRESENT AND CAN BE IGNITED, RESULTING IN POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY. 

Refer to Section 03A-12 (FD-1060 diesel engine), Section 03B-12 
(FD-1460 diesel engine) and Section 03C-12 (Cummins, CAT and DDC engines).

Refer to vehicle owner guide for the recommended air cleaner assembly 
maintenance mileage interval.

Cleaning the air cleaner or crankcase ventilation filter elements is 
not recommended. Replace at the specified mileage intervals.

Clean the air cleaner body and the cover with a solvent or compressed 
air. Wipe the air cleaner body and cover dry if a solvent is used. Inspect the 
air cleaner body and cover for distortion or damage at the gasket mating 
surfaces. Replace cover or body if they are damaged beyond service.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tanks

All fuel tanks used on diesel engine-equipped L-Series vehicles are 
outside-frame mounted and are made of steel or aluminum. 

Some vehicles are equipped with dual fuel tanks. The fuel crossover 
tube that extends from tank to tank is a balance tube for the dual tanks and 
has a shutoff valve on each end.

================================================================================
PAGE 5419
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tank Filler Cap

 NOTE: Use of an aftermarket fuel tank filler cap other than an authorized 
Ford service part can result in damage to the fuel tank if not properly 
designed and manufactured.

The fuel tank filler cap is sealed and is the threaded screw-on, 
screw-off type, some of which are equipped with a chain retainer.

================================================================================
PAGE 5420
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 10-01: Fuel Tank, Filters, Tubes and Fuel Pump, Diesel Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Selector Valve — Vehicles with Dual Tanks Only

Some vehicles are equipped with dual fuel tanks. The fuel crossover 
tube which extends from tank to tank on some vehicles is a balance tube for 
the dual tanks and has a fuel selector valve on each end. These valves must 
always be in the ON (open) position during vehicle operation. The fuel is 
drawn from the left tank (normally) and returned to the right tank. If the 
valves on one or both ends are closed, the return fuel will pressurize the 
right-hand tank. In extreme cases, the fuel tank ends may expand or appear to 
bulge.

PAGE 5421
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Filter

 In-Line 

The in-line fuel filter provides filtration to protect the small 
metering orifices of the fuel injector nozzles.

 NOTE: The fuel filter should be changed at 24,000 km (15,000 miles) or 
15-month intervals, and each time a fuel tank sending unit and pump is 
replaced. When the fuel filter requires replacement, proceed to Fuel 
Filter(s), In-Line, in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

If contamination of fuel is suspected, refill tank with clean fuel, not 
fuel from fuel tanks.

The fuel filter will prevent dirt and other particulate matter from 
entering the system. Water in the fuel tank can pass through the filter 
without restriction.

================================================================================
PAGE 5422
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 10-01: Fuel Tank, Filters, Tubes and Fuel Pump, Diesel Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel/Water Separator

Filtration and separation of water from the fuel is important for 
trouble-free operation and long life of the fuel system. Some of the 
clearances between the fuel injection pump parts are very close. For this 
reason, the parts can easily be damaged by corrosion, contaminants or loss of 
the lubricating film of fuel.

Be sure to use the correct element. The element has a valve which must 
be opened daily to drain the collected water.

 Fuel/Water Separator, Typical 

[FIGURE: V10280A.gif]

A dual fuel/water separator-filter adapter provides additional 
filtering capacity. The fuel flows through the adapter to a larger combination 
fuel/water separator-filter, and back to the fuel filter for final filtering.

Regular maintenance, including draining moisture from the fuel/water 
separator-filter and supply tanks, is essential to keep water out of the fuel.

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tubes

 WARNING: TANK-TO-INJECTOR FUEL TUBES REMAIN UNDER HIGH PRESSURE AFTER THE SYSTEM 
IS SHUT OFF. DEPRESSURIZE THE FUEL TUBE SYSTEM AT THE SCHRADER VALVE LOCATED 
ON THE ENGINE FUEL RAIL BEFORE DISCONNECTING ANY FUEL TUBES. DISCONNECTING 
FUEL TUBES WITHOUT DEPRESSURIZING THE SYSTEM AS DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION CAN 
RESULT IN INJURY FROM FUEL BEING SPRAYED UNDER PRESSURE. ALSO, FUEL SPRAYED 
UNDER PRESSURE IS AN OBVIOUS FIRE HAZARD. 

 CAUTION: Only Ford Motor Company approved fuel tubes and O-rings should be used 
for repair or replacement because substitute materials can leak or deteriorate 
rapidly from contact with fuel. Never substitute hose clamps for approved 
fittings on nylon fuel tubes as they can pull loose because of the fuel 
pressure. 

Disconnect vehicle battery.

Keep all flame, burning tobacco products, and sparks from grinders and 
other power tools away from vehicle when servicing fuel system.

Keep the front end of the vehicle higher than the rear when servicing 
fuel tubes. If the fuel tubes are disconnected with the front of the vehicle 
lower than the rear, fuel can syphon out through the tubes.

================================================================================
PAGE 5424
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 10-01: Fuel Tank, Filters, Tubes and Fuel Pump, Diesel Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Dual Draw/Dual Return System

Some vehicles are equipped with a dual draw/dual return fuel system. 
The dual draw/dual return system is designed to provide accurate and reliable 
equalization of fuel levels in dual tanks without utilizing crossover tubes, 
and to dissipate to both tanks the heat added to fuel by electronic engines. 
The supply tubes and fittings are designed to ensure RH and LH symmetry and 
smooth, upward flow paths throughout the fuel system.

================================================================================

================================================================================

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Flow Splitter Valve

A flow splitter valve on the return side of the fuel system ensures 
equal distribution of the return flow between the fuel tanks for all operating 
conditions.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Level Sending Unit, Diesel

The fuel level sending unit consists of a variable resistor 
(potentiometer) which is attached to a float in the fuel tank and varies 
according to fluid level in the tank. When the fuel level is low, resistance 
in the sending unit is high and allows only a low current to flow through the 
indicator gauge windings, causing the pointer to move a short distance. When 
the fuel level is high, the resistance in the sending unit is low and allows a 
higher current flow and a greater heating effect, causing the pointer to move 
a greater distance.

fuel tube connection) and drain the fuel tank.

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Filling

 WARNING: FUEL CAN BE UNDER PRESSURE. ALWAYS REMOVE THE FUEL CAP CAREFULLY AND 
SLOWLY. IF THE CAP IS VENTING FUEL OR A HISSING SOUND IS HEARD, WAIT UNTIL THE 
CONDITION STOPS BEFORE REMOVING THE CAP. IF THESE PRECAUTIONS ARE NOT 
FOLLOWED, FUEL CAN SPRAY AND CAUSE PERSONAL INJURY. 

 WARNING: USE OF AN AFTERMARKET FUEL FILLER CAP OTHER THAN AN AUTHORIZED SERVICE 
PART OR THE EQUIVALENT IS NOT RECOMMENDED AND CAN RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE FUEL 
SYSTEM. IT CAN ALSO CAUSE IMPROPER SYSTEM OPERATION DUE TO PRESSURE OR VACUUM 
BUILDUP, WHICH CAN COMPROMISE THE PERFORMANCE OF THE FUEL SYSTEM IN THE EVENT 
OF A COLLISION. 

 CAUTION: The fuel crossover tube (tank to tank) is a balance tube for the dual 
tanks and has a shutoff valve on both ends. 

You can prevent excessive condensation in the fuel tank by keeping it 
over half full. Some vehicles are equipped with dual fuel tanks with a 
crossover tube.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tank(s)

Typical fuel tank installations are shown in the following 
illustrations. Refer to these illustrations and remove damaged or worn parts 
as required. 

 Removal 

To avoid electrical sparking, disconnect the battery ground cable. 

Drain the fuel into an OSHA-approved container by either removing the 
drain plug, if so equipped, or by siphoning through the filler cap opening. 
Then disconnect the fuel tube and the fuel gauge sending unit wire. 

Disconnect the fuel return tube. 

On a vehicle with dual fuel tanks, disconnect the fuel tube connecting 
the tanks. 

 CAUTION: Use a suitable jack to support the tank. 

If the tank is equipped with a filler neck and connecting hose, loosen 
the hose retaining clamp at the tank and pull the hose away from the tank. 

Remove the fuel tank strap retaining bolts and remove the straps. 
Remove the tank. Replace all worn or damaged parts. 

If the fuel tank is to be replaced, remove the fuel level sending unit 
and gasket from the tank. Remove the shutoff valve assembly, if so equipped. 
Remove the vent valve. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Use a suitable jack to support the tank. 

If the fuel tank has to be replaced, install the fuel level sending 
unit and a new gasket on the tank. Install the transfer valve assembly, if so 
equipped. Install the vent valve. Position new insulating strips on the fuel 
tank brackets. Install the drain plug (if it was removed) in the fuel tank. 

Install the fuel tank on the mounting brackets. 

 CAUTION: Do not crush tank by overtightening tank straps. 

Install the retaining straps, but do not tighten the mounting bolts. 
Align the tank. Make sure insulators are properly centered under the straps 
and brackets. Tighten the retaining strap mounting bolts. 

Connect the fuel tubes to the tank. Connect the fuel gauge sending unit 
wire. 

On a vehicle with dual fuel tanks, connect the fuel tubes connecting 
the tanks. 

Connect the fuel return tubes. 

Fill the tank with fuel and install the filler cap.

Connect the battery ground cable.

Start the engine and check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tank Support Straps

 Removal 

Support the fuel tank, using a suitable jack, before removing one or 
both fuel tank straps.

Remove the lower fuel tank retaining strap nut(s).

Remove the upper fuel tank retaining strap nut(s).

 NOTE: When removing upper fuel tank strap, use caution not to let holding 
bolt fall out of frame hole. If fuel tank strap bolt falls out of frame hole, 
use a length of wire to pull strap bolt back into position.

Remove the strap(s) from the fuel tank.

If a new strap is being installed, the rubber insulator must be removed 
from the tank strap for installation of the new strap.

 Installation 

If a new strap is being installed, position rubber insulator(s) to strap.

Position fuel tank strap to fuel tank.

Install upper strap stud retaining nut and hand-tighten.

Install lower strap stud retaining nut and hand-tighten.

Make sure strap is properly positioned and tighten upper and lower 
strap(s) stud nuts to 43-56 Nm (31-42 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Cooler Assembly

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable.

Drain fuel from fuel tank. Refer to Fuel Draining in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section.

Remove fuel hose tube nuts from the fuel cooler assembly.

Remove two fuel cooler assembly retaining bolts from the fuel cooler 
lower mounting bracket.

Remove the nuts and bolts retaining the fuel cooler assembly to the 
fuel cooler upper mounting bracket.

Remove the fuel cooler assembly.

 Installation 

Position fuel cooler assembly for installation.

Insert and tighten the nuts and bolts retaining the fuel cooler 
assembly to the upper mounting bracket.

Insert and tighten the two bolts retaining the fuel cooler assembly to 
the lower mounting bracket.

Connect fuel hose tube nuts to the fuel cooler assembly and tighten to 
specifications.

Connect the battery ground cable.

Refill the fuel tank with fuel. Check for leaks while filling.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Sending Unit, Fuel Tank

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable.

Remove fuel from tank.

Disconnect the wiring from the fuel sending unit.

Remove and discard the mounting screws.

Remove the fuel sending unit and mounting gasket from the fuel tank 
opening and discard the gasket.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Prior to installation of sender unit, new gasket and screws, remove and 
discard old shipping plate, gasket and screws. Sender flange area must be 
clean of debris.

Clean the fuel sending unit mounting surface of the fuel tank. Do not 
allow foreign material to enter the tank opening

Position the new mounting gasket at the fuel tank opening and carefully 
align holes in gasket to screw holes in tank.

Position the fuel sending unit in the tank and carefully align holes in 
sending unit flange-to-gasket holes with screw holes in tank.

Install the new mounting screws and tighten to 2.0-2.7 Nm
 (18-24 lb-in). Then check all mounting screw torques.

Connect the wiring to the fuel sending unit.

Connect battery ground cable.

Refill the tank with fuel. Check for proper fuel gauge operation and 
for leaks while refilling.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tube Organizer

 Removal 

Either single tubes and hoses can be removed from the organizer 
assemblies or the entire assembly can be removed.

Disconnect the battery ground cable.

To remove a single tube or hose, snap open the organizer-to-frame clips.

Disconnect tube or hose ends if necessary.

Snap tube or hose out of organizer core and remove. It may be necessary 
to remove some other tubes to remove one.

To remove the entire assembly, use the following additional steps.

Disconnect all tubes, hoses and electrical connections going through 
the organizer if necessary.

Remove nuts retaining the organizer assembly to the frame.

Remove the fuel tube organizer assembly.

 Installation 

Position fuel tube organizer assembly for installation on frame.

Install organizer clip nuts and tighten to 8-10 Nm 
(71-89 lb-in).

Connect all hoses, tubes and wires.

Connect the negative battery cable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tubes, Flexible Hose

Flexible fuel tubes must be serviced with bulk tubing and reusable 
swivel sockets. The appropriate bulk tubing and socket replacements must 
satisfy SAE J1402 requirements. Ford Trucks use Aeroquip tubing and sockets. 
Refer to the following Conversion Chart. 

 CONVERSION CHART

Tube Assembly Base

Bulk Tubing No. a 

Socket Part No. a 

-2C037-

FC350-06

401-6S

-2C038-

FC350-08

401-8S

-2C039-

FC350-10

401-10S

 a Aeroquip part numbers.

 Removal 

Disconnect fuel tubes at both ends. If removing crossover tube, shut 
off valves. Remove units from holding clips and remove from vehicle. 

Slide looms, if used, off tubes. Replace all worn or damaged parts. 

 Installation 

Use bulk tubing, according to preceding chart, as determined from tube 
assembly base numbers shown in service manual. 

Cut hose square with either a cut-off wheel or fine-toothed hacksaw. 

 NOTE: For long tube lengths, it may be preferred to place the tube in the 
vise and screw socket until tight. Then, back off one-quarter turn.

Put socket in vise. Screw tube counterclockwise into socket until tight 
and then back off one-quarter turn. Thoroughly lubricate nipple threads and 
inside of tube with heavy oil or tube assembly lubrication. 

Screw nipple clockwise into socket and tube, being careful to leave 
1/32-inch to 1/16-inch clearance between nipple hex and socket. 

Clean tube assembly by blowing out with clean compressed air. Then 
rinse inside of tube assembly with diesel fuel. 

Install connecting tubes and clamps, if required, on fuel tubes. 
Position tubes in clips on vehicle. Tighten connecting hose clamps, if so 
equipped.

Fuel Return System

A fuel return system is used to maintain fuel flow at the fuel charging

The fuel return system is serviced in the same manner as the fuel tubes.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fuel Tubes, Filters and Water Separator

With the engine stopped, examine the fuel tube connections for wetness, 
washed or stained areas that might indicate a fuel leak. Start the engine and 
observe all the connections for fuel seepage. Tighten or replace fuel tubes as 
necessary.

Drain the water reservoir by turning valve to open drain. The filter 
and separator assembly is located on the right side of the engine. After the 
water has been drained, close the valve.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fuel Sediment Bowl and Filter

On tanks equipped with check ball, check drain valves. Remove plug and 
dislodge check ball with small Allen-head wrench. Contents of tank will slowly 
drain, allowing water and sediment to escape. On tanks equipped with drain 
plugs, first reduce fuel level by using Rotunda Fuel Storage Tanker 164-R3201 
or equivalent on the fuel hose, or by siphoning fuel. After fuel is reduced to 
a residual amount, the drain plug can be removed to allow water and sediment 
to escape.

Check drainage for sediment. If sediment is obvious, remove and 
thoroughly clean the fuel tank using an approved steam cleaner.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fuel Tanks

Fuel tanks do not require special service procedures and can be 
steam-cleaned and serviced using standard procedures. After steam cleaning, 
allow them to thoroughly air dry. Replace dual tank strap bolts. Remove fuel 
tank sending unit before cleaning tank.

Inspect the fuel tank mounting brackets and straps to be ensure fuel 
tanks are securely attached to the vehicle. Inspect the fuel tubes at the 
tanks to be ensure they do not leak.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Fuel System Pressure Relief

 CAUTION: Fuel supply tubes can remain pressurized for some period of time after 
the engine is shut off. This pressure must be relieved before servicing the 
fuel system. 

 CAUTION: The pressure of the fuel in the tubes is sufficient to penetrate the 
skin and cause serious bodily harm. 

 CAUTION: Do not bleed a hot engine as this can cause fuel to spill onto a hot 
exhaust manifold, creating a danger of fire. 

Before opening the fuel system, relieve the fuel pressure as follows:

Disconnect the negative battery cable.

Loosen the fittings at the injector slowly and carefully until all 
residual pressure is relieved. Use a shop towel to absorb any escaping fuel.

After the fuel system is serviced, the fuel tubes should be vented as 
follows:

 CAUTION: The pressure of the fuel in the tube is sufficient to penetrate the 
skin and cause serious bodily harm. 

 CAUTION: Do not bleed a hot engine as this can cause fuel to spill onto a hot 
exhaust manifold, creating a danger of fire. 

Reconnect the negative battery cable.

Loosen the fittings at the injector, and crank the engine to allow 
entrapped air to bleed from the tube. Use a shop towel to absorb any escaping 
fuel. Tighten the fittings to specifications.

Start the engine and vent one tube at a time until the engine runs 
smoothly.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Fuel System — Pressurized

 Fuel and Vapor Return Tubes 

 CAUTION: Ford-approved nylon fuel tubing is made from material which has been 
tested and proven to be acceptable for use with commercially available fuels. 
It is also resistant to most environmental conditions. Avoid using alternate 
tubing materials. Use of non-approved tubing could pose a hazard in service. 

 CAUTION: Plastic fuel tubes cannot be repaired. If damaged, the component must 
be replaced. 

 NOTE: Formed sections (i.e., bends) of nylon fuel tubes cannot be repaired 
using straight tubing. Straight service tubing will kink if bent. Formed nylon 
fuel tube is required to replace the damaged section.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

The throttle is controlled by an accelerator rod and cable type 
linkage, and a pedal assembly. The accelerator pedal should travel smoothly 
from the idle to the wide-open throttle positions. Hesitation on return or 
prevention of return to the idle position must not occur. Surrounding 
components, such as wiring, hoses, sound insulator and floor covering, must 
not contact the sliding inner member of the cable, rod or the accelerator 
pedal assembly. 

On vehicles equipped with electronic engine controls, an electronic 
accelerator pedal is used instead of the mechanical pedal and linkage. The 
electronic pedal sends a pedal reference signal to the engine control module 
(ECM) to indicate pedal position. The engine control module (ECM) then 
controls fuel delivery to the engine equal to the throttle demand. This system 
eliminates the need for any linkage or adjustments.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

 Inspection and Verification 

 WARNING: SURROUNDING ENGINE COMPARTMENT COMPONENTS, SUCH AS WIRING OR HOSES, 
MUST NOT CONTACT ANY MOVING MEMBER OF THE ACCELERATOR CONTROLS. CHECK ALL 
VEHICLES FOR RETURN TO IDLE. PERCEPTIBLE HESITATION OR PREVENTION OF RETURN TO 
IDLE POSITION MUST NOT OCCUR DURING SLOW REMOVAL OF THE FOOT FROM THE 
ACCELERATOR PEDAL AND SHAFT, STARTING AT THE FULLY DEPRESSED, WIDE-OPEN 
THROTTLE (WOT) POSITION. 

Verify the customer's concerns by inspecting the condition. Check for 
any resistance in accelerator pedal action. Inspect the accelerator pedal and 
linkage if a high engine idle speed condition exists. After inspection and 
verification, refer to the symptom chart for the condition, and perform the 
appropriate action to correct the condition.

Operate the accelerator pedal and linkage by hand, observing and 
feeling that the full range of travel is not restricted by wiring, hoses, dash 
panel insulation, carpet, mat, padding or any other components.

 Symptom Chart — Accelerator Pedal to Throttle Body 

 ACCELERATOR PEDAL TO THROTTLE BODY 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Accelerator Pedal Is Hard to Push Down or Has a Rough/Raspy or Sticky 
Feel

 NOTE: Accelerator cable should not be lubricated and it is not serviceable.

Accelerator cable and spring contact surrounding parts.

DISCONNECT the accelerator cable from the throttle body lever. If 
vehicle is equipped with speed control, disconnect the speed control actuator 
cable from the accelerator cable. VERIFY that the disconnected end of the 
accelerator cable or its spring does not come into contact with any of the 
surrounding parts.

Insulation or trim interferes with pedal travel.

OPERATE the accelerator pedal by hand, observing and feeling that the 
full pedal range of travel is not restricted by the dash panel insulator or 
carpet/mat/padding. If full pedal travel to WOT is restricted, ADJUST 
insulator and/or trim items as required.

Shaft not moving.

OPERATE the accelerator pedal and shaft by foot.

Internal components other than cable not working properly.

If accelerator cable operation is smooth, REFER to the throttle body 
diagnosis procedures in the appropriate section in the Powertrain 
Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

Cable is worn.

If the condition recurs (making sure disconnected end of accelerator 
cable has not come into contact with anything), CHECK the accelerator pedal 
for free operation. If the pedal operation is free, REPLACE accelerator cable.

High Engine Idle Speed

Internal components interacting improperly.

If the accelerator cable ball socket extends beyond the throttle lever 
ball stud, REFER to the throttle body diagnosis procedures in the appropriate 
section in the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

Component, trim or insulation interference.

If the socket does not extend beyond the stud, CHECK the accelerator 
pedal for free operation (no contact with carpet, mats, wiring, etc.). If the 
pedal operation is free, REPLACE the accelerator cable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Accelerator Cable, Hand

 WARNING: SURROUNDING ENGINE COMPARTMENT COMPONENTS, SUCH AS WIRING OR HOSES, 
MUST NOT CONTACT ANY MOVING MEMBER OF THE ACCELERATOR CONTROLS. CHECK ALL 
VEHICLES FOR RETURN TO IDLE. PERCEPTIBLE HESITATION OR PREVENTION OF RETURN TO 
IDLE POSITION MUST NOT OCCUR DURING SLOW REMOVAL OF THE FOOT FROM THE 
ACCELERATOR PEDAL AND SHAFT, STARTING AT THE FULLY DEPRESSED, WIDE-OPEN 
THROTTLE (WOT) POSITION. 

Refer to the illustrations in this section for component location and 
orientation.

 Removal 

Loosen setscrew at accelerator pedal lever.

Remove retainer screw and clip at throttle control bracket. Remove 
accelerator cable from lever.

Unscrew the jam nut from the back of the steering column support 
bracket. Remove the accelerator cable.

 Installation 

Position the accelerator cable through the steering column support 
bracket.

Install the washer and jam nut.

Attach the accelerator cable to the throttle control bracket and 
tighten the retainer screw.

Loosely attach the accelerator cable to the accelerator pedal lever.

With the accelerator pedal at the closed throttle position, and the 
hand accelerator knob pushed all the way in, tighten the setscrew on the pedal 
lever.

bolt. Tighten to 10-13 Nm (7-10 lb-ft).

Connect accelerator linkage to accelerator pedal assembly.

ADJUSTMENTS

Accelerator Linkage

Instructions for adjusting accelerator linkages used on all diesel 
engines are contained in the following procedures by vehicle and engine 
application. Refer to the appropriate illustration in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section. 

Whenever possible, the engine should be at operating temperature when 
accelerator linkage adjustments are made. 

Be sure to install throttle return springs in the manner shown on the 
illustrations in this section. After adjustment, the accelerator must return 
to idle on slow release of foot pressure, without binding or dragging.

"Slow release" means movement no faster than approx. 2 seconds per inch 
at the pedal pivot on suspended pedal installations or at a point 25.4 mm (1 
inch) from top edge of floor-mounted pedals.

Surrounding engine compartment components (hoses, wiring) must not 
contact any moving part of the accelerator controls.

================================================================================
PAGE 5454
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 10-02: Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Accelerator Linkage, LNT-9000 with Cummins L10 Engine 

Verify that governor lever assembly is in proper position shown in 
second illustration in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 
Correct if necessary. 

Install rod assemblies and return springs. 

With pedal assembly held against pedal stop bolt, adjust length of rod 
assembly until governor shaft is rotated to wide-open throttle position. Then 
decrease length of rod assembly 2.0 mm (0.08 inches) (2 turns). Tighten jam 
nuts to 5-7 Nm (45-65 lb-in). 

With engine running, depress accelerator pedal to its full extent and 
slowly release the pedal. The pedal must return completely from wide-open 
throttle position to idle position without any indication of drag or binding.

Section 10-02: Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Accelerator Linkage, Caterpillar 3306 Engine 

With pedal assembly held against stop bolt, adjust length of rod 
assembly until governor lever provides 1.52 mm (0.06 inch) breakover at the 
detent travel stop. 

Tighten jam nuts to 10-13 Nm (7-10 lb-ft).

Install two throttle return springs. 

With governor lever in idle position install hand accelerator lever 
assembly. Position hand throttle assembly so that approximately 1.52 mm (0.06 
inch) clearance exists between hand throttle and instrument panel. 

With engine running, depress accelerator pedal to its full extent, 
slowly release the pedal. The pedal must return completely from wide-open 
throttle position to idle position without any indication of drag or binding. 

Tighten jam nuts to 10-13 Nm (7-10 lb-ft).

ADJUSTMENTS

Accelerator Linkage, Caterpillar 3406 Programmable Electronic Engine 
Controls (PEEC) and Caterpillar 3176 Engines 

Automatic transmission modulator adjustment: 

After accelerator components have been installed and adjusted, install 
all modulator linkage leaving the slip link transmission kickdown control 
unconnected from the accelerator lever stud. 

With the accelerator pedal set at wide-open throttle and the modulator 
linkage pushed rearward the full extent of its travel 38 mm (1.5 inches), 
adjust adjuster transmission kickdown until the slip link just fits over the 
accelerator lever stud with the stud at the rear of the slip link slot.

Install washer and cotter pin over slip link on accelerator lever stud 
and tighten nut on adjuster transmission kickdown against slip link to 16-23 Nm
 (12-17 lb-ft).

ADJUSTMENTS

Accelerator Linkage, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Engines

In-line injection pump accelerator system

Install all parts.

Hold pedal to wide-open throttle to stop bolt.

Adjust turnbuckle on rod assembly until rod extends approximately 1/16 
inch.

Tighten jam nut to 10-13 Nm (7-10 lb-ft).

Exhaust brake

Install all parts, but do not tighten fasteners for the switch and 
bracket assembly.

Slide the switch and bracket assembly toward the pump shaft lever until 
a click is heard.

Tighten fasteners to 10-13 Nm (7-10 lb-ft).

With engine running, depress accelerator pedal to its full extent, 
slowly release the pedal. "Slowly release" means movement no faster than 
approximately two seconds per inch at the top of the pedal. The pedal must 
return completely from wide-open throttle position to idle position without 
any indication of drag or binding.

Surrounding engine compartment components (hoses, wiring, etc.) must 
not contact any moving part of the accelerator controls.

Modulator adjustment:

With governor shaft rotated to the wide-open throttle position, push 
modulator cable end to stop and adjust clevis until it can be installed on 
transmission control shift lever assembly.

Section 10-03A: Speed Control System, Caterpillar PEEC III Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Speed Control System

The speed control system is comprised of the on/off switch, a 
set-accel/resume-coast switch, an instrument panel-mounted warning indicator 
light, a vehicle speed pickup, a throttle position sensor, the PEEC III 
(Programmable Electronic Engine Control) module, a clutch pedal switch and a 
brake pedal switch. 

To activate speed control: 

Vehicle speed must be above the low speed control limit, typically 48 
km/h (30 mph). 

Set the on/off switch to the ON position. 

Bring vehicle up to desired road speed. 

Place the set/resume switch momentarily into the SET position. The PEEC 
III system will maintain the speed that the vehicle is traveling when the set 
switch is released. 

 NOTE: If the set switch is held for more than one second, the vehicle speed 
will continue to increase until the set switch is released. The speed control 
will then be set to the speed the vehicle is traveling when the set switch is 
released. 

To disengage the speed control: 

Move the on/off switch to the OFF position, or 

Depress the clutch, or 

Depress the brake. 

To resume speed control operation: 

Return the on/off switch to the ON position. 

Place the set/resume switch momentarily into the RESUME position. 

 NOTE: The PEEC III control system remembers the last speed control set speed 
as long as the engine is running. The PEEC III system may have a maximum 
controlled speed which has been programmed by the operator of the vehicle. The 
speed control will only function between the low and high settings that are 
programmed into the engine control module. The high cruise speed limit is also 
generally set at a lower km/h (mph) than the vehicle speed limit. 

If the resume switch position is held for more than one second, the 
PEEC III system will decrease the vehicle speed and a new set speed will be 
established when the switch is released. 

The accelerator pedal can be used to exceed the speed control set speed 
if the high speed control limit is lower than the vehicle speed limit. 
Releasing the accelerator will return the vehicle to the previous controlled 
speed. The accelerator pedal override can be used to anticipate hills or for 
passing situations. 

To shift gears, the on/off switch can be moved to the OFF position or 
disengage the clutch to deactivate the speed control. 

After shifting gears, the speed control can be reactivated by moving 
the on/off switch to the ON position and momentarily setting the switch to the 
RESUME position. 

Locations of the PEEC components are shown in the following 
illustration for those L-Series vehicles equipped with speed control. For more 
information on the PEEC system and service procedures for PEEC components, 
refer to the Caterpillar 3406E PEEC or Caterpillar 3176 PEEC engine service 
manual.

[FIGURE: L5745C.gif]

Section 10-03A: Speed Control System, Caterpillar PEEC III Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Speed Control

 Inspection and Verification 

A visual inspection is an important part of the system diagnosis, and 
must be performed before conducting any diagnostic procedures. When performing 
a visual inspection, check all items for abnormal conditions, such as bare, 
broken or disconnected wires. The speed control servo (throttle actuator) and 
throttle linkage must operate freely and smoothly. The speed control actuator 
is preadjusted. If readjustment is required, the speed control actuator must 
be adjusted as tight as possible without opening the throttle plate or 
increasing the idle speed. Electrical connections must be complete and tight. 
The wiring harness must be properly routed. Look for frayed wiring insulation 
or evidence of shorts. Any problems revealed by the visual inspection must be 
corrected before further tests of the speed control system are made.

Section 10-03B: Speed Control System, Cummins CELECT Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Speed Control System

 WARNING: THE SPEED CONTROL SYSTEM MUST NOT BE USED WHEN DRIVING CONDITIONS DO 
NOT PERMIT MAINTAINING A CONSTANT SPEED, SUCH AS HEAVY TRAFFIC OR ON ROADS 
THAT ARE WINDING, ICY, SNOW-COVERED, SLIPPERY OR WITH A LOOSE DRIVING SURFACE. 
THIS CAN RESULT IN A LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL. 

The speed control system is comprised of the on/off and set/resume 
switches, two instrument panel-mounted warning indicator lights, a vehicle 
speed pickup, a throttle position sensor, the CELECT electronic control module 
and data link, and clutch and brake switches. 

The speed control systems for all electronic engines function in a 
similar manner. The minimum and maximum speed control speeds, however, vary 
from vehicle to vehicle.

 Cummins Engine, Typical 

[FIGURE: L7301D.gif]

The speed control will only work with the on/off switch in the ON 
position, and if the minimum speed setting has been reached. The speed control 
can be manually disengaged with on/off switch and is automatically disengaged 
by depressing the clutch or applying the brakes. 

With the speed control switch on, moving the set/resume switch to the 
SET position and releasing it engages the speed control system at the speed 
currently being driven. 

If the speed control has been disengaged by depressing the clutch or 
applying the brakes, moving the set/resume switch into the RESUME position and 
releasing it will return the vehicle to the last set speed. Holding the switch 
in the resume position longer than one second will decelerate (coast) the 
vehicle until the switch is released. 

The resume speed is lost when the vehicle is shut off.

Each CELECT engine includes a standard engine protection system to 
prevent damage to the engine. This system monitors the following five inputs: 

coolant level 

coolant temperature 

oil pressure 

oil temperature 

intake manifold temperature 

If any of these inputs goes outside of a limit set by Cummins, the 
engine will be gradually derated to protect the engine. If the CELECT system 
is derating the engine, the red CHECK FLUIDS warning light in the instrument 
cluster will come on. When the input returns to acceptable limits, the engine 
will return to full power and the warning light will turn off.
