SERVICE PROCEDURES

A/C-Heater System Deodorizing 

The A/C system deodorizer, product No. EP-1710-FF, is a full-strength 
deodorizer that requires no dilution or mixing. Each vehicle treated will 
require 10 fluid ounces to complete the procedure.

The A/C system deodorizer can be applied using Rotunda A/C Disinfectant 
Sprayer Unit 134-R0055 or equivalent, a siphon-type sprayer, a refillable 
aluminum or stainless steel aerosol paint sprayer (touch-up guns provide 
better access).

Set the function control switch to the NORM A/C position. Move the 
temperature control lever to full cold position.

With the heater blower motor operating in high speed, spray three 
ounces of the deodorizer product into the outside air inlet.

Set the function control switch to the MAX A/C position. Move the 
temperature control lever to the full cold position. 

With the heater blower motor operating in high speed, spray 1-1/2 
ounces of the deodorizer product into the recirculate air opening (located in 
the passenger side foot area of the vehicle). Set the temperature control to 
provide full heat and spray an additional 1-1/2 ounces into the recirculate 
air opening.

Shut the heater blower motor off.

Spray equal amounts of the remaining 4 ounces of the deodorizer product 
into each of the air outlet openings (defroster, instrument panel registers, 
and floor ducts).

Allow the vehicle to sit for approximately 30 minutes before returning 
to the customer.

Refrigerant Reclaiming/Recovery/Recycling Equipment

 CAUTION: The A/C refrigerant of all vehicles must be identified and analyzed 
prior to refrigerant charging. Failure to due so can contaminate the shop bulk 
refrigerant and other vehicles. 

Ford Motor Co. recommends the use of U.L.-approved recovery/recycling 
equipment. Refer to Special Service Equipment under Refrigerant System in the 
Service Procedures portion of this section for a list of recommended equipment.

If a refrigerant recovery or recycling station is used, the following 
general procedures must be observed, in addition to the operating instructions 
provided by the equipment manufacturer:

 CAUTION: Use extreme care and observe all safety and service precautions related 
to the use of refrigerants. 

 NOTE: Hoses must have shutoff devices or check valves within 305 mm (12 
inches) of the hose end to minimize the introduction of noncondensable gases 
(air) into the recycling station and to minimize the amount of refrigerant 
released when the hose(s) is (are) disconnected.

Connect the refrigerant recycling station hose(s) to the vehicle air 
conditioning service ports and the recovery station inlet fitting.

Turn on the power to the recycling station to start the recovery 
process. Allow the recycling station to pump the refrigerant from the system 
until the station pressure goes into a vacuum. On some stations the pump will 
be shut off automatically by a low-pressure switch in the electrical system. 
On other units it may be necessary to manually turn off the pump.

Once the recycling station has evacuated the vehicle air conditioning 
system, close the station inlet valve (if so equipped). Switch off the 
electrical power.

Allow the vehicle air conditioning system to remain closed for about 
two minutes. Observe system vacuum level as shown on the gauge. If the 
pressure does not rise, disconnect the recycling station hose(s).

If the system pressure rises, repeat the above three steps until the 
vacuum level remains stable for two minutes.

Perform required service operations, evacuate and recharge the air 
conditioning system.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Refrigerant Identification and Analysis

Use the A/C refrigerant analyzer to identify the refrigerant type and 
purity. Refer to the manufacturer's operating instructions.

If the purity percentage of the R-134a or R-12 is 98% or greater by 
weight, a green "PASS" LED will light. Proceed with the refrigerant recovery. 
Refer to System Discharging and Recovery in the Service Procedures portion of 
this section.

If the R-134a or R-12 does not meet 98% purity, a red "FAIL" LED will 
light. Proceed with the refrigerant recovery. Refer to System Discharging and 
Recovery in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Levels of R-22 and flammable hydrocarbons above 2% will light the red 
"FAIL" LED. Refer to Recovery of Contaminated A/C Systems in the Service 
Procedures portion of this section.

If a flammable hydrocarbon is detected above 5%, both the "FAIL" and 
"HYDROCARBON" LEDS will light and a horn will sound. Refer to Recovery of 
Contaminated A/C Systems in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Recovery of Contaminated A/C Systems

Repeat the refrigerant identification. Refer to Refrigerant 
Identification and Analysis in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

 NOTE: The customer might want to return to the facility responsible for the 
last A/C system service.

Advise the customer of the contaminated A/C system and any additional 
costs to repair the system.

 CAUTION: This equipment must only be used to recover contaminated refrigerant to 
prevent the spread of contaminated refrigerant to other vehicles. As an 
alternative, contact an A/C service facility in your area that is equipped to 
handle contaminated A/C systems. 

Recover the contaminated refrigerant using suitable recovery equipment 
designed only for the recovery of contaminated refrigerant.

Determine the cause of the failure.

Determine which parts will need to be replaced.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with an auxiliary A/C and heater system, the 
evaporator core in the unit must also be flushed to prevent system 
recontamination.

Flush the heat exchangers. Refer to System Flushing in the Service 
Procedures portion of this section.

Install a new suction accumulator/drier. Refer to Section 12-03A .

Add the necessary amount of refrigerant oil. Refer to Refrigerant Oil 
Addition in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Evacuate the A/C system for 45 minutes. Refer to System 
Evacuating in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Recharge the A/C system. Refer to System Charging in the Service 
Procedures portion of this section.

 NOTE: Contact your current hazardous waste disposal company to determine if 
it is capable of disposing of contaminated refrigerant.

Dispose of the contaminated refrigerant in accordance with all Federal, 
State, and Local laws and regulations.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

System Evacuating

Discharge refrigerant system, using an approved recovery unit.

Make sure that the gauge set is connected as follows:

Low-pressure hose connected to low-pressure service gauge port on top 
center of the accumulator/drier assembly.

High-pressure hose to high-pressure gauge port on compressor discharge 
line at connection. 

Connect gauge set center hose to a vacuum pump.

Open gauge set valves and start vacuum pump.

Evacuate system with vacuum pump until low-pressure gauge reads at 
least 84 kPa (25 in-Hg) (vacuum) and as close to 101 kPa (30 in-Hg) as 
possible. Continue vacuum pump operation for 15 minutes. If part of system has 
been replaced, continue vacuum pump operation for an additional 20-30 minutes.

When evacuation of system is complete, close gauge set valves and turn 
vacuum pump off.

Observe low side gauge to make sure system holds vacuum for five 
minutes. If vacuum is held for five minutes, proceed to charging the system. 
If vacuum is not held for five minutes, leak test system, repair leak(s) and 
again evacuate system.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

System Charging Setup

 CAUTION: The A/C refrigerant of all vehicles must be identified and analyzed 
prior to refrigerant charging. Failure to do so can contaminate the shop bulk 
refrigerant and other vehicles. 

Ford Motor Company recommends using a charging station to perform 
evacuation and charging of the refrigerant system. Follow the instructions 
provided with the charging station.

If a charging station is not available, system charging can be 
accomplished using a separate vacuum pump, charging cylinder and manifold 
gauge set.

If the charging cylinder method is used, the center port of the 
manifold gauge set should have two refrigerant hoses with integral shutoff 
valves built into the gauge set manifold. If the gauge set is the type that 
does not have shutoff valves and two hoses at the center port, a tee fitting 
and two hoses must be installed at the center port. In addition, the hoses 
attached to the center port must have shutoff valves at the other ends of the 
two center hoses to prevent air from entering the hoses when not connected to 
the vacuum pump and charging cylinder.

System Charging

 Charging with a Charging Cylinder 

Ford Motor Company supports the efficient use, recovery, and recycling 
of R-134a used in modern air conditioners. Ford Motor Company recommends the 
use of a U.L.-approved recovery/recycling device that meets SAE Standard J1991 
during any air conditioning system repair and recharge procedure which 
requires the air conditioning system to be discharged.

Connect the manifold gauge set. Refer to A/C Manifold Gauge Set 
Connection in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Discharge the refrigerant system using the refrigerant recovery method. 
Refer to System Discharging and Recovery in the Service Procedures portion of 
this section.

Evacuate the refrigerant system. Refer to System 
Evacuating in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Connect the center hose of the manifold gauge set to a refrigerant 
cylinder. If a charging station is used, follow the instructions of the 
manufacturer.

 WARNING: LIQUID-CHARGE INTO THE VEHICLE A/C DEHYDRATOR AND RECEIVER TANK ONLY. 
TO PREVENT A/C COMPRESSOR SLUGGING, DO NOT LIQUID-CHARGE INTO A REFRIGERANT 
HOSE WHILE THE ENGINE IS OPERATING. 

Open the low-pressure valve on the manifold gauge set to allow 
refrigerant to enter the system. Continue to add refrigerant until 
approximately 1.3 kg (3.0 lb) is drawn into the system.

 NOTE: Keep the refrigerant cylinder in the upright position.

Close the low-pressure valve.

 CAUTION: Do not open the high-pressure valve while the engine is running. 

Start the engine and turn on the air conditioning.

Open the low-pressure valve on the manifold gauge set to allow 
refrigerant to enter the system. Continue to add refrigerant until 
approximately 1.3 kg (3.0 lb) is drawn into the system.

Close the low-pressure valve.

Check the air conditioning system for proper operation.

Stop the engine.

Disconnect the manifold gauge set.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

System Flushing

 WARNING: R134A IS CLASSIFIED AS A SAFE REFRIGERANT, BUT MISUSE CAN MAKE IT 
DANGEROUS. THE FOLLOWING PRECAUTIONS MUST BE OBSERVED:

ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GOGGLES WHEN SERVICING AN AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM.

AVOID CONTACT WITH LIQUID REFRIGERANT R-134A. R-134A VAPORIZES AT 
APPROXIMATELY -20°F UNDER ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE AND IT WILL 
FREEZE SKIN TISSUE.

NEVER ALLOW REFRIGERANT R-134A GAS TO ESCAPE IN QUANTITY IN AN OCCUPIED 
SPACE. R-134A IS NON-TOXIC, BUT IT WILL NOT FURNISH THE OXYGEN NEEDED TO 
SUPPORT LIFE.

NEVER USE A TORCH IN AN ATMOSPHERE CONTAINING R-134A GAS. R-134A IS 
NON-TOXIC UNDER ALL NORMAL CONDITIONS, BUT WHEN IT IS EXPOSED TO HIGH 
TEMPERATURES, SUCH AS A TORCH FLAME, IT DECOMPOSES. ONE OF THE PRODUCTS OF THE 
CHEMICAL BREAKDOWN IS A PHOSGENE GAS WHICH IS HIGHLY TOXIC.

CARE SHOULD BE EXERCISED SO AS NOT TO OVERHEAT ANY PORTION OF THE 
CHARGED AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM. THE PRESSURE IN AN AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM 
RISES AS THE TEMPERATURE RISES AND TEMPERATURES OF APPROXIMATELY 200°
F CAN BE DANGEROUS. 

 CAUTION: Only an A/C flushing kit which includes the A/C flusher, A/C flusher 
fitting kit and Ford A/C system flushing solvent, such as Rotunda A/C Flusher 
Kit 014-00990 and Rotunda A/C Flushing Fitting Kit 014-00992 or equivalent, is 
approved for use on Ford vehicles. No other flushing device or solvent is 
approved for flushing heat exchangers. Use of any other flusher or solvent can 
cause damage to the A/C system and the flushing unit. 

 CAUTION: Do not flush the A/C evaporator core orifice or hoses. The internal 
plumbing and material make-up of these items make it impossible to properly 
remove the debris and residual flushing fluid which can cause premature system 
failure. 

 CAUTION: The flushing solvent and flushing unit filter are intended for one 
vehicle use only. They can be used to flush one or all of the heat exchangers 
in the A/C system. Failure to change the flushing solvent and filter can 
spread A/C system contamination. 

 NOTE: The A/C system filtering as described in this section is optional if 
A/C system flushing is performed. However, filter kit use after flushing is 
recommended if the A/C system contamination is extensive.

Recover the refrigerant. Refer to System Discharging and 
Recovery in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Disconnect the refrigerant lines from the heat exchanger(s) to be 
flushed. Refer to Section 12-03A .

Connect Rotunda A/C Flusher Kit 014-00990 and A/C Flushing Fitting Kit 
014-00992 or equivalents to the heat exchanger to be flushed. Refer to the 
equipment manufacturer's procedures and instructions.

Flush the heat exchanger, using 4 liters (1 gallon) of Ford A/C 
Flushing Solvent F4AZ-19597-A. Back-flush for a minimum of 15 minutes.

 CAUTION: The failure to successfully remove all of the residual solvent within 
the component can result in A/C system damage when it is reconnected and 
operated. 

 NOTE: Dispose of the flushing solvent and filter in accordance with all 
Federal, State, and Local laws.

Purge the heat exchanger. Apply 621-862 kPa (90-125 psi) of pressurized 
air for 30 minutes.

 NOTE: Replacement of the suction accumulator/drier is not required
when repairing the air conditioning system except when there is
physical evidence of system contamination from a failed A/C
compressor or damage to the suction accumulator/drier.

Replace the suction accumulator/drier and A/C evaporator core orifice 
on any vehicle being serviced for A/C compressor or desiccant failure. Refer 
to Section 12-03A .

Replace any refrigerant hoses that are clogged with debris. Refer to 
 Section 12-03A .

Reconnect the heat exchanger being serviced. Refer to Section 12-03A .

Add additional refrigerant oil as required. Refer to Refrigerant Oil 
Addition in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Evacuate, charge, and leak test the A/C system. Refer to the Service 
Procedures portion of this section.

Check the A/C system for proper operation.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Refrigerant System Filtering After A/C Compressor Replacement

 CAUTION: Follow all refrigerant system safety and service precautions as outlined. 

An A/C service kit has been released to provide the necessary equipment 
and information to perform the new, mandatory A/C system filtering procedure. 
The filter kit with the service part number suffix "A" is to be used on 
vehicles that have a nylon-lined evaporator to compressor suction line between 
the suction accumulator/drier and the A/C compressor.

[FIGURE: M4546A.gif]

To determine that the A/C compressor has failed and must be replaced, 
remove the A/C evaporator core orifice and condenser to evaporator tube if 
necessary. Look for a dirty A/C evaporator core orifice or a condenser to 
evaporator tube containing black refrigerant oil and particles.

Remove the damaged A/C compressor and drain the oil into a calibrated 
container.

 NOTE: The proper amount of refrigerant oil must be added to the new A/C 
compressor before it can be installed.

If the amount of oil drained from the removed A/C compressor is between 
85 and 142 ml (3 oz to 5 oz), pour the same amount of clean oil into the new 
A/C compressor. If the amount of oil drained from the old A/C compressor is 
greater than 142 ml (5 oz), pour only 142 ml (5 oz) of clean refrigerant oil 
into the new A/C compressor. If the amount of refrigerant oil drained from the 
old A/C compressor is less than 85 ml (3 oz), pour 85 ml (3 oz) of clean 
refrigerant oil into the new A/C compressor.

 NOTE: It will be necessary to transfer the A/C clutch from the old A/C 
compressor to the new A/C compressor.

Install the new A/C compressor. Make sure the compressor mounting bolts 
are tightened to the proper specification. Check the tension of the drive 
belt. Adjust if necessary.

Remove the suction accumulator/drier assembly and drain the oil into a 
calibrated container.

Add clean refrigerant oil to the new suction accumulator/drier in the 
same amount that was removed from the old unit, plus an additional 60 ml of 
new refrigerant oil.

Install the suction accumulator/drier in the vehicle.

Obtain the proper service kit for the vehicle on which you are working. 
Filter kits with the service part number suffix "A" are to be used on vehicles 
with a nylon-lined evaporator to compressor suction line. The label on the 
filter shows which evaporator to compressor suction line it is to be used with.

[FIGURE: M3730A.gif]

Remove a length of evaporator to compressor suction line to accommodate 
the suction filter and install the filter using the clamps provided with the 
kit. Be sure filter is correctly oriented for refrigerant system flow. Check 
the label on the filter. On the filter for nylon-lined evaporator to 
compressor suction line, install O-rings (two on each filter tube, making sure 
they are properly seated in the grooves on the tube). Tighten the clamps 
securely.

Install a new A/C evaporator core orifice. The A/C evaporator core 
orifice is located in the condenser to evaporator tube between the A/C 
condenser core and the A/C evaporator core. Replace the condenser to 
evaporator tube.

Install a pancake filter in the condenser to evaporator tube between 
the A/C condenser core and the A/C evaporator core orifice. Be sure the filter 
inlet is toward the A/C condenser core. Connections can be made using A/C Test 
Adapter Kit D88P-19703-B or equivalent and flexible refrigerant hose of 2500 
psi burst rating. Individual fittings are also available.

 Pancake Filter 

[FIGURE: M3878A.gif]

Evacuate, charge and leak test the system.

Check all refrigerant system hoses, lines and the positioning of the 
newly installed filters to be sure they do not interfere with other engine 
compartment components. If necessary, use tie straps to make adjustments.

Provide adequate airflow to the front of the vehicle (with a fan, if 
necessary), and set the air conditioner control at MAX A/C. Set the A/C blower 
motor speed control on HIGH and temperature control at full cool. Start the 
engine and let it idle briefly. Make sure the A/C system is operating properly.

Gradually bring the engine up to 1200 rpm by running it at lower rpms 
for short periods (first at 800 rpm, then at 1000 rpm). Set the engine at 1200 
rpm and run it for an hour with the A/C system operating.

Stop the engine.

Allow the engine to cool sufficiently to remove the fittings, flexible 
hoses and pancake filter from the condenser to evaporator tube. (It will be 
necessary to discharge and recover the refrigerant in the system first.)

Discard the pancake filter. It can be used ONE TIME ONLY.

Reconnect the condenser to evaporator tube back into the system.

Evacuate, charge and leak test the system. Make any necessary 
adjustments.

Check the operation of the system in all functions.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

A/C Evaporator Core Orifice Replacement Kit Installation

The fixed orifice tube is constructed with a plastic body, two screens 
and a small brass tube down the center of the orifice body. Two O-rings are 
installed around the orifice tube body to seal against leakage.

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to remove the fixed orifice tube with pliers or by 
twisting the tube. To do so will break the fixed orifice tube body in the 
evaporator core tube. Use only the recommended tool and follow the recommended 
service procedures. 

 Removal 

Discharge and recover the refrigerant from the air conditioning system. 
Observe all safety precautions.

Disconnect the liquid line from the evaporator core. Cap the liquid 
line to prevent the entry of dirt and excessive moisture.

Squirt a small amount of clean specified refrigerant oil into the 
evaporator core inlet tube to lubricate the tube and orifice O-rings during 
removal of the fixed orifice tube from the evaporator core tube.

Engage the Fixed Orifice Tube Tool D80L-19990-A or equivalent with the 
two tangs on the fixed orifice tube. Extract the orifice tube from the 
evaporator core tube.

If the orifice tube should break, hold the T-handle of Broken Orifice 
Tube Extractor D80L-19990-B or equivalent to keep the orifice tube from turning.

Run the nut on the tool down against the evaporator core tube until the 
orifice is pulled from the tube.

To remove a broken segment of an orifice tube, insert the screw end of 
the extractor into the evaporator core tube and thread the screw end of the 
tool into the brass tube in the center of the fixed orifice tube. Then, pull 
the fixed orifice tube from the evaporator core tube.

If only the brass center is removed during Step 7, insert the screw end 
of the extractor tool into the evaporator core tube and turn it into the end 
of the fixed orifice tube body. Then, pull the fixed orifice tube body from 
the evaporator core tube.

 Installation 

Lubricate the O-rings on the fixed orifice tube body liberally with 
clean refrigerant oil.

Place the fixed orifice tube in the Fixed Orifice Tube Tool 
D80L-19990-A or equivalent and insert the fixed orifice tube into the 
evaporator core tube until the orifice is seated at the stop.

Remove the tool from the fixed orifice tube.

Connect the liquid line to the evaporator core. Use only specified 
green O-ring seals.

Leak test, evacuate and charge the system. Observe all safety 
precautions.

Check the system for proper operation.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Suction Accumulator/Drier Replacement Guidelines 

 NOTE: Replacement of the suction accumulator/drier is not required
when repairing the air conditioning system except when there is
physical evidence of system contamination from a failed A/C
compressor or damage to the suction accumulator/drier.

 NOTE: When replacing the suction accumulator/drier, the procedure given here 
must be followed to make sure that the total oil charge in the system is 
correct after the new accumulator/drier is installed.

Drain the oil from the removed suction accumulator/drier into a 
suitable measuring container. If necessary, drill one or two 12.7-mm 
(1/2-inch) holes in the bottom of the old suction accumulator/drier to make 
sure that all the oil has drained out.

Add the same amount of clean new refrigerant oil plus two fluid ounces 
to the new suction accumulator/drier. Use only the oil specified for the 
specific vehicle being serviced.

PAGE 5591
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 12-00: Climate Control System, Service

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Refrigerant Oil Addition

The compressor uses a unique high-quality refrigerant oil Sanden SP-20 
or an equivalent refrigerant oil meeting Ford specification WST-M1C231-B2. An 
oil charge of 240 ml (8 oz) is used in a new system. It is extremely important 
that only the specified type and quantity of refrigerant oil be used in the 
compressor. If there is a surplus of oil in the system, it will circulate with 
the refrigerant, reducing the cooling capacity of the system. Using too little 
oil or oil not meeting the Ford specification will result in poor lubrication 
of the compressor.

When replacing a component of the refrigerant system, the procedures in 
this section must be followed to ensure that the total oil charge in the 
system is correct after the new part is installed.

When the compressor is operated, oil gradually leaves the compressor 
and is circulated through the system with the refrigerant. Eventually, a 
balanced condition is reached in which a certain amount of oil is retained in 
the compressor and a certain amount is continually circulated. If a component 
of the system is removed after the system has been operated, some oil will go 
with it. To maintain the original total oil charge, add oil as required to the 
new replacement part.

The procedures for replacing oil are as follows:

 During A/C Compressor Replacement 

 NOTE: The orifice tube must be replaced when the compressor is replaced.

 NOTE: Replacement of the suction accumulator/drier is not required
when repairing the air conditioning system except when there is
physical evidence of system contamination from a failed A/C
compressor or damage to the suction accumulator/drier.

A new service replacement compressor contains no refrigerant oil. Prior 
to installing the replacement compressor, drain the refrigerant oil from the 
removed compressor into a calibrated container. Then, drain the refrigerant 
oil from the new compressor into a clean calibrated container. Rotate the 
shaft about six to eight revolutions while pouring the oil from the ports. 
This effectively empties the compressor of oil.

Obtain a clean container that can also be used as a measuring device.

Place the disc and hub assembly on the compressor shaft so the shaft 
can be rotated.

Rotate the shaft by hand six to eight revolutions, collecting the oil 
in a clean measuring device.

If the amount of oil drained from the old compressor was between 85 and 
142 ml (3 and 5 oz), pour the same amount of clean specified refrigerant oil 
into the new compressor.

If the amount of oil that was removed from the old compressor is 
greater than 142 ml (5 oz), pour 142 ml (5 oz) of clean specified refrigerant 
oil into the new compressor.

If the amount of refrigerant oil that was removed from the old 
compressor is less than 85 ml (3 oz), pour 85 ml (3 oz) of clean specified 
refrigerant oil into the new compressor.

 R-134a Refrigerant Oil 

The refrigerant oil required for R-134a A/C systems is a polyalkalylene 
glycol (PAG) oil, Sanden SP-20, Ford specification WST-M1C231-B2 or 
equivalent. This type of refrigerant oil is made specifically for heavy truck 
R-134a systems. Never use R-12 or YN-12 refrigerant oil in R-134a systems.

 During Component Replacement 

When replacing other components of the air conditioning system, 
measured quantities of the specified refrigerant oil must be added to the 
component to make sure that the total oil charge in the system is correct 
before the system is operated.

Clean refrigerant oil should be poured directly into the replacement 
components as follows:

A/C evaporator core: add 90 ml (3 oz).

A/C condenser core: add 30 ml (1 oz).

Suction accumulator/drier: drain oil from removed accumulator/drier. 
Add same amount plus 60 ml (2 oz) of clean refrigerant oil to new suction 
accumulator/drier.

If any other component such as an A/C evaporator core orifice or a hose 
is replaced, 59 ml (2 oz) of refrigerant oil is necessary unless a hose bursts 
with a fully charged system. Then, the addition of refrigerant oil may be 
necessary with the amount to be determined by the technician. 

 Other Refrigerant System Components 

Replacement of other refrigerant system components such as hoses, A/C 
compressor valves, and pressure switches requires the addition of 59 ml (2 oz) 
of refrigerant oil.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Suggested Brazing Procedures:

Only cleaned parts should be joined; any rust, dirt, oil or grease must 
be removed.

The recommended braze alloy is a silver base alloy; the amount of 
silver content in the alloy is 35-45 percent.

The melting temperature of these alloys is 622°C (1150°
F) to 635°C (1175°F).

It is recommended that a flux, suitable for use with the alloy chosen, 
be used.

When fitting the tube to the counterbore, make sure that the wall 
section of the tube is not thinned excessively by grinding, filing, etc.

Use ordinary brazing procedures. After completion of brazing, the 
subassembly must be cleaned thoroughly to ensure no foreign particles will be 
introduced into the fluid system.

 NOTE: The new fitting is reuseable. Any further hose damage requires only 
replacement of hose.

Using a hacksaw, cut off the special fitting where it is attached to 
the socket.

[FIGURE: K21970A.gif]

Place the special tube end into the counterbored end of the service kit 
fitting. Weld or braze the tube into the nipple, which will provide a new 
nipple with the special end fitting required.

[FIGURE: K21971A.gif]

Assemble the new nipple and its matching socket to new hose cut to the 
proper length.

[FIGURE: K21972A.gif]

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Cleaning a Badly Contaminated Refrigerant System

A refrigerant system can become badly contaminated for a number of 
reasons.

The compressor may have failed due to damage or wear.

Use of wrong refrigerant oil.

The compressor may have been operated for some time with a bad leak or 
there may have been an opening in the system.

The system may have been damaged by a collision and left open for a 
long time.

The system may not have been cleaned properly after a previous failure.

The system may have been operated for a time with water or moisture in 
it.

Clutch cycle rate is fast.

Clutch ON time is short.

Clutch OFF time is short.

If preliminary inspection shows that the system is badly contaminated 
with water, carbon and other decomposition products from the failure, it will 
be necessary to remove all these contaminants and to clean and repair or 
replace the compressor and replace the suction accumulator/drier.

After servicing and correcting a refrigerant system problem, take 
additional pressure readings and observe the clutch cycle rate while meeting 
the conditional requirements to make sure the problem has been corrected.

In ambient temperatures above 38°C (100°
F), the compressor clutch will not normally cycle off and in 
many instances, the clutch will not cycle off when temperatures are above 32°
C (90°F).

Poor system performance can also result if the airflow through the unit 
is restricted by leaves or other debris which have entered through the cowl 
air inlet and plugged the evaporator core.

This condition can be detected by checking the center register 
discharge temperature. An abnormally low temperature indicates the air is 
spending more time in the evaporator and is very cold when discharged, but the 
volume is not enough to cool the vehicle properly.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Climate Control Assembly

Outside air heater systems are available for various vehicles, 
depending on model and engine usage.

 Heater or Heater-A/C Assembly 

[FIGURE: K17753C.gif]

The outside air heater unit is a blend air-type which is mounted to the 
dash panel and is connected to the right side cowl air duct. This allows the 
heater to draw in outside air for ventilation, heating and defrosting.

The heater control assembly is located in the instrument panel to the 
right of the steering column. It includes a blower switch with four operating 
speeds (LO, MED-LO, MED-HI, HI) and two levers. One lever selects the 
temperature (cool to warm) and the other selects the desired function (PANEL, 
FLOOR or DEFROST).

Ventilation is delivered through the instrument panel registers when 
the function lever is set on PANEL or through the floor outlets when the 
function lever is set on FLOOR. The quantity of air may be adjusted by means 
of the blower switch. The temperature may also be controlled by the 
temperature selector.

In the DEFROST position, air is discharged through the defrosters with 
a small amount going to the floor outlets. To provide maximum defrost air 
flow, the panel registers must be in the closed position.

In the OFF position, the outside air door is in the OFF position, no 
outside air enters the cab and the blower motor is off.

When the temperature control lever is moved between COOL and WARM, a 
temperature control cable moves the temperature blend door to direct a given 
portion of the total air input through the heater core. As the percentage of 
air exposed to the core increases, the air temperature at the outlets to the 
passenger compartment also increases.

The air conditioning/heater control system uses air pressure to 
activate pneumatic actuators, which control the position of the outside 
air/recirculated, panel/floor and defrost doors. The heater control system 
uses air pressure from the braking system on vehicles equipped with air brakes 
or air pressure from a separate pump located under the passenger's seat on 
vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes. The system logic is shown in the 
following illustration.

19980

A/C and Heater Control Assy

The heater control system uses air pressure to activate pneumatic 
actuators which control the position of the outside air/off, panel/floor, and 
defrost doors. The heater control system uses air pressure from the braking 
system on vehicles equipped with air brakes or air pressure from a separate 
pump located under the passenger's seat on vehicles equipped with hydraulic 
brakes.

 Airflow Control 

When the airflow or the heater system is turned on, the air circulation 
to the cab interior is obtained by means of airflow direction grilles.

 Temperature Control 

The air is heated as it passes through the heater core (connected to 
the engine cooling system).

The temperature is controlled by a lever which adjusts the temperature.

The temperature door control cable uses two snap-in fittings, one near 
each end. The blue fitting engages a square hole on the control bracket after 
the Z-bend engages the lever, while the white fitting engages a square hole on 
a bracket secured to the rear of the case (toward the passenger seat). The 
white fitting is not engaged into the bracket until the cable pigtail is first 
installed on the temp door crank post. Another feature of the cable is that it 
does have some adjustment capability. This is accomplished by displacing the 
white clip relative to its internal red bit. Only two discrete readjustment 
positions on each side of center are provided. Cable will be non-functional 
beyond the second readjustment position.

 Blower Motor Control 

Airflow volume through the system is controlled by a four-position 
blower switch. The blower switch, used with a resistor assembly, provides four 
blower speeds to control airflow through the system. The blower can be shut 
off only by moving the function selector lever to OFF.

 Recirculation/Fresh Air Control 

The heating and defrosting system allows for both fresh and 
recirculated air to be used. Fresh or recirculated air is governed through the 
use of air pressure to activate a pneumatic actuator on the outside air 
fresh/recirculated door. Outside air is allowed to pass through the system in 
all positions except OFF and, if equipped with air conditioning, the MAX A/C 
positions.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor

The blower motor is installed in the heater case located in the engine 
compartment. The motor is connected to the electrical circuit with two 
hardshell connectors located near the motor.

================================================================================

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor Resistor

The electrical system consists of the blower motor, blower speed 
switch, blower motor on-off switch (part of the nine-port vacuum selector 
valve), blower motor resistor with a thermal limiter and the fuse and wiring 
to complete the circuit.

The blower motor resistor is installed in the heater case near the 
blower motor. The resistor is used with the blower speed switch to provide 
four blower operating speeds.

 Heater Blower Motor Resistor 

The blower motor resistor assembly is attached to the blower housing. 
When the various blower speeds are selected with the blower switch, the 
appropriate resistance value in the blower motor resistor assembly is selected 
to provide the desired blower speed.

================================================================================
PAGE 5605
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor Thermal Limiter

The resistor assembly also contains a thermal limiter which is used as 
a temperature protecting fuse. The thermal limiter is located a preset 
distance from the resistor coils. If the temperature of the thermal limiter 
reaches approximately 121°C (250°F) the 
limiter contacts will open, interrupting the blower motor circuit for all 
blower speeds except high speed. The thermal limiter will not reset and the 
resistor assembly must be replaced if the thermal limiter opens.

Instrument Panel Registers

allow for independent control of airflow from the instrument panel. They can 
adjust airflow up, down, left and right. These registers also allow for an OFF 
position. However, the individual register OFF positions are not true 
functioning ON/OFF controls. In the OFF position, there will be a slight 
amount of air passing through these registers unless the function selector 
lever is moved to the OFF, DEFROST or FLOOR positions.

Pneumatic Hose Harnesses

The tubing bundle is made up of four black plastic 5/32-inch O.D. tubes 
of which three are color-coded with colored tape strips at each end or a thin 
colored stripe along the length of the tubing. The color coding is as follows:

Black (no tape or stripe) connects black port on control to "source" 
pressure manifold (at driver's side toeboard).

Red (tape or stripe) connects red port on control to plenum door 
(defrost door) air cylinder.

White (tape or stripe) connects white port on control to outside 
air/off door (on case) air cylinder.

Blue (tape or stripe) connects blue port on control to case's panel 
door air cylinder.

================================================================================

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Safety Precautions

 WARNING: CARBON MONOXIDE IS COLORLESS, ODORLESS AND DANGEROUS. IF IT IS 
NECESSARY TO OPERATE THE ENGINE WITH THE VEHICLE IN A CLOSED AREA SUCH AS A 
GARAGE, ALWAYS USE AN EXHAUST COLLECTOR TO VENT THE EXHAUST GAS OUTSIDE THE 
CLOSED AREA. 

Whenever components in the engine compartment or instrument panel areas 
are being serviced, the battery ground cable must be disconnected to eliminate 
the possibility of electrical shorts. Extreme care must be exercised when 
performing electrical tests where the battery must be connected to operate the 
system.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Climate Control Assembly

 Removal 

Remove access panel that surrounds the control and remove the two 
fasteners which secure the climate control assembly to the instrument panel.

Carefully pull climate control assembly back to expose the temperature 
door cable anchor point. With needle-nosed pliers or blade-type screwdriver, 
pinch the blue fitting snap-in tangs and push the fitting out of the square 
hole. Hold control firmly with one hand to preclude any type of bending of the 
plastic bracket when applying force of any kind.

 NOTE: Each port has a metal insert or sleeve which engages the tubing inside 
diameter. Should this insert pull out of the port with the tubing, make sure 
it is re-engaged into the replacement tubing upon reassembly.

With the blue fitting free, it will now be possible to disengage the 
Z-bend at the end of the wire from the control temp lever hole. Some 
articulation of the cable end is required.

Set the selector lever to OFF. Remove each tube from the air actuator 
on the control, making sure to depress and hold each mating collar while 
pulling on the tubing. Also, hold the actuator firmly while pulling off the 
tubing. Refer to Pneumatic Hoses in the Removal and Installation portion of 
this section.

Carefully disconnect the blower switch wiring harness connector as well 
as the control bulb/socket wiring harness connector.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Upon tube insertion, colored identification collars are not to be 
depressed. A bottoming out of the tubing can be felt upon insertion. Also, 
each tube end has a position identification line as a visual check for correct 
insertion. Lines on all the tubes will not be visible if all are properly 
inserted.

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Climate Control Assembly Illumination Bulbs

 Removal 

Remove access panel that surrounds the climate control assembly and 
remove the two fasteners which secure the control to the instrument panel.

Place temperature control lever in the full cool position and carefully 
pull the control back to expose the illumination bulb socket and wires.

Remove illumination bulb socket by carefully pulling straight out of 
the control. A slight rocking motion may be required to assist in the removal.

Remove the illumination bulb by grasping in fingers and carefully 
pulling bulb out of socket.

 Installation

 Removal

 Installation

is felt between the shaft and knob. All climate control knobs remove and 
install in the same manner.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Climate Control Cables

 Temperature Control Cable 

 Removal 

Place temperature control lever in full cool position.

Remove the heater housing cover trim panel four screws and Velcro®
 fastener (where used). Remove panel.

Locate the cable-to-housing bracket attachment point. With needle-nosed 
pliers or blade-type screwdriver, pinch the white fitting's snap-in tangs and 
push the fitting out of the square hole in the steel bracket.

After white fitting is free, articulate cable conduit and wire end to 
disengage the wire pigtail from the plastic post on the crank arm of the blend 
air door.

Remove instrument panel access panel that shields the control assembly 
and remove the two fasteners that hold the control to the instrument panel.

Carefully pull control assembly back to expose cable anchor point. 
Disengage the blue snap-in fitting as described previously. Hold control 
firmly with one hand to preclude any type of bending of the plastic bracket, 
while applying force of any kind.

With the blue fitting free, disengage the Z-bend at the end of the wire 
from the temperature control lever hole. Some articulation of the cable end is 
required. When cable is totally free, carefully remove the cable taking care 
not to snag, pull out or otherwise adversely affect the control tubing routed 
nearby.

 Installation 

Follow the removal procedure in reverse order.

In each case prior to engaging the snap-in fitting, it is necessary 
that the Z-bend be connected (control end) or that the pigtail be connected 
(case end).

In each case, an audible click must be heard upon fitting insertion. 
Proper seating can be checked by pulling on the conduit in a direction 
perpendicular to the mount surface (close to the anchor point).

Should the reassembled system require cable adjustment, refer to Temperature Control Cable 
 in the Adjustments portion of this section. In 
general, adjustment is not required if the temperature control lever is 
centralized in its slot (equal distance to slot edges from lever centerline 
between full warm and full cool).

Position the heater housing trim cover panel and install the four 
retaining screws and attach the Velcro® fastener (where used).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Climate Control Spool Valve Assembly

 Removal 

Remove access panel surrounding the control and remove the two 
fasteners which secure the control to the instrument panel.

Carefully pull control assembly back to expose the temperature door 
cable anchor point. With needle-nosed pliers or blade-type screwdriver, pinch 
the blue fitting snap-in tangs and push the fitting out of the square hole. 
Hold control firmly with one hand to prevent bending of the plastic bracket 
when applying force of any kind.

With the blue fitting free, disengage the Z-bend at the end of the wire 
from the control temperature lever hole. Some articulation of the cable end is 
required.

 NOTE: Each port has a metal insert or sleeve which engages the tubing inside 
diameter. Should this insert pull out of the port with the tubing, make sure 
it is re-engaged into the replacement tubing upon reassembly.

Disconnect the tube harness by pressing and holding in the colored 
release buttons while pulling out the tubing.

Remove the fastener securing the aluminum cover plate.

Remove the two screws retaining the electrical mode switch to the 
bracket.

Remove the two Phillips' head screws retaining the spool valve assembly 
to the bracket.

 CAUTION: Do not pull the spool out of the spool body. If the spool is removed, 
it can become contaminated, resulting in a control assembly failure. 

Lift the spool body gently from the mounting recess by sliding the 
spool to the lower end of the spool guide track. Take care not to damage the 
spool guide fingers.

[FIGURE: DM0246A.gif]

 Installation 

Apply a small amount of Teflon® Lubricant 
E7FZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M1C111-A to the 
spool guide track.

Gently position the spool slider into the guide track and locate the 
spool body into its recess.

Reinstall the spool valve assembly and secure with the two Phillips' 
head screws.

Align the lever slot with the spool slide hole. Position the mode 
switch so the switch post passes through the lever slot and slide holes and 
install the mode switch fasteners.

Reinstall the aluminum cover plate and secure with fasteners.

Reconnect the tube harness to the appropriate color-coded ports. Each 
tube end has a positive identification line as a visual check for correct 
insertion. Lines on all the tubes will not be visible if properly inserted.

Reinstall the control assembly in the dash panel.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Evaporator Housing 

 Removal 

Drain the engine cooling system.

Discharge the air conditioning system. Refer to Section 12-00 .

Disconnect the battery ground cable.

Remove the suction accumulator/drier retaining bolts at the attachment 
to the mounting bracket.

Disconnect the liquid and suction lines from the A/C evaporator at the 
dash panel.

Disconnect the heater hoses at the dash panel.

Inside the vehicle, remove four screws and one Velcro®
 fastener (where used) and remove the evaporator housing (air 
conditioning/heater housing) trim panel.

Disconnect the blower motor resistor and the blower motor connectors.

Remove the control cable from the bracket and the temperature door arm 
pivot, using pliers to compress the cable clip locking tabs.

In the engine compartment, remove the four nuts that retain the 
evaporator housing mounting studs to the dash panel.

 CAUTION: Failure to remove the tubing and excessive pulling at the control end 
can cause damage to the control. 

Slide the evaporator housing unit rearward in the vehicle and remove 
the pressure tubing from the fresh air/recirculated and panel floor actuators. 

Remove the evaporator housing assembly from the vehicle.

Tape or plug all refrigerant and heater hose tube ends to make sure 
they are not damaged or that moisture or contaminants do not enter the system.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Prior to installation, make sure that evaporator and heater core tube 
ends are protected to make sure they are not damaged during installation. 

Position the housing assembly in the vehicle near its installed 
location and connect the pressure tubing to the fresh air/recirculated and 
panel/floor door actuators.

Slide the unit into the installed position, making sure that the 
housing assembly seal at the underside of the plenum is not damaged or pulled 
out of position. Make sure that the side cowl seal at the fresh air inlet is 
in position.

Attach the temperature control cable to the temperature door arm pivot 
and the bracket.

Install the four nuts that secure the housing mounting studs to the 
dash panel.

Connect the blower motor resistor and blower motor connectors.

Connect the heater hoses at the dash panel and tighten the clamps to 
specifications.

Install new O-rings on the liquid and suction line male ends, apply 
refrigerant oil liberally to the male and female fittings and couple the lines 
to the evaporator tubes.

Install the suction accumulator/drier retaining bolts.

Connect the battery ground cable.

Fill and bleed the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Leak test, evacuate and charge the air conditioning system. Refer to 
 Section 12-00 . Check system operation.

Install the evaporator housing (air conditioner/heater housing) trim 
panel (four screws and one Velcro® fastener where used).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Heater Core

 Removal 

Drain the engine cooling system.

Disconnect the heater hoses at the dash panel.

Inside the vehicle, remove the air conditioner/heater housing trim 
panel (four screws and one Velcro® fastener where used).

Remove the three heater core cover retaining screws and remove the 
cover from the housing.

Pull the heater core and seal assembly from the housing. If necessary, 
loosen the four housing-to-dash panel retaining nuts in the engine compartment 
to relieve the pressure on the heater core tube/dash seals and facilitate 
removal of the heater core.

 Installation 

Install plugs or tape on the heater tube ends to prevent cutting the 
dash panel seals and to prevent entry of foreign material into the heater core.

Apply silicone grease liberally to the tube ends and the inside of the 
dash seals, to allow the heater core tubes to easily pass through the seals at 
installation.

Install the heater core and seal assembly into the housing. Make sure 
that the core tubes pass through the dash seals and the dash seals are in the 
proper position.

Position the heater core cover and install the two upper and one lower 
left retaining screws. The lower right screw hole is used for retaining the 
trim cover panel.

Install the air conditioner heater housing cover trim panel (four 
screws and one Velcro® fastener where used).

Tighten the housing to dash panel retaining nuts in the engine 
compartment, if they were loosened.

Connect the heater hoses and tighten the clamps to the specified value.

Fill and bleed the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Windshield Defroster Door

 Removal

Remove the floor duct.

Remove the engine cover.

proper operation of the defrost door. If OK, install the instrument panel 
bolts. If not OK, repeat previous installation steps.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Pneumatic Hoses

 Removal 

Read entire procedure prior to servicing the harness.

Remove the four heater housing cover trim panel retaining screws and 
detach Velcro® fastener (where used). Remove panel.

Determine visually if it will be necessary to loosen the case and pull 
it rearward in the cab an inch or so, without disconnecting the air 
conditioner lines or heater hoses.

 NOTE: The special fittings employed require that the colored collar(s) on the 
air cylinders or on the control be pushed toward the cylinder(s) or control 
prior to attempting to remove the tubing. Failure to depress the collar can 
result in damage to the cylinders or control.

Disconnect tubing at fresh air/off door cylinder (white).

The white line has a routing clip above the case and a second clip on 
the dash behind the right-hand side of the case. The clip on the dash is not a 
slip-through type. This plastic fastener engages a 1/4-inch hole in the dash 
and the tubing has been pre-taped to the fastener. If necessary, the fastener 
can be cut off or pried out with a screwdriver.

Remove the red, blue and black tube ends.

Remove the access panel which shields the control and the panel to the 
left of the control. This will expose the control and the tube routing of the 
black (source pressure) tubing.

 NOTE: Each port has a metal insert or sleeve which engages the tubing inside 
diameter. Should this insert pull out of the port with the tubing, make sure 
it is re-engaged into the replacement tubing upon reassembly.

Set the function selector lever to off, then begin to remove each tube 
from the air actuator on the control, making sure to depress and hold each 
mating collar while pulling on the tubing. Hold the actuator firmly while 
pulling off the tubing.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Upon tube insertion, colored identification collars are not to be 
depressed. A bottoming-out of the tubing can be felt upon insertion. Also, 
each tube end has a position identification line as a visual check for correct 
insertion. Lines on all the tubes will not be visible if all are properly 
inserted.

Follow removal procedure in reverse order. 

Position the heater trim cover panel and install the four retaining 
screws. Attach the Velcro® fastener (where used).

correctly and that the heater hoses cannot come in contact with any part of

ADJUSTMENTS

Temperature Control Cable

Verify that a misadjustment exists:

Move temperature lever to full cool position and note distance from 
lever center to end of slot (count number of detents).

Repeat above for full warm position.

If there is a significant difference between the two observations, 
adjustment is necessary.

Locate the cable attachment clip at the case. Do not disengage white 
clip from bracket.

The white clip has a 1/2-inch long rectangular flag which, when pulled 
away from the body of the clip, allows the internal mating plastic bit to be 
moved in increments of approximately 1/8 inch. This movement is used to 
recenter the lever in its slot.

Do not exceed two movement increments from the center position. 
Movement is possible only as long as the flag is pulled back. Once adjustment 
is completed, let go of the flag. Push or pull on conduit to effect 
adjustment. Pushing the conduit towards the vehicle right-hand side will 
result in a lever motion toward WARM. Pulling the conduit to the vehicle 
left-hand side will result in a lever motion toward COOL.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

R-134a Refrigerant System

The refrigerant R-134a is a hydrofluorocarbon refrigerant. R-134a is 
non-corrosive, non-explosive, non-flammable and has a slight ether-type odor. 
R-134a is heavier than air. Although it is classified as a safe refrigerant, 
certain precautions must be observed to protect the parts involved and the 
person working on the unit.

To determine whether or not your vehicle is equipped with R-134a, look 
for the yellow R-134a tag located near the high and low side charge ports.

[FIGURE: K22587A.gif]

 WARNING: AVOID BREATHING A/C REFRIGERANT AND LUBRICANT VAPOR OR MIST. IF 
ACCIDENTAL SYSTEM DISCHARGE OCCURS, VENTILATE THE WORK AREA BEFORE RESUMING 
SERVICE. LIQUID R-134A, AT NORMAL ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURES AND TEMPERATURES, 
EVAPORATES SO QUICKLY THAT IT HAS THE TENDENCY TO FREEZE ANYTHING IT CONTACTS. 
FOR THIS REASON, EXTREME CARE MUST BE TAKEN TO PREVENT ANY LIQUID REFRIGERANT 
FROM COMING IN CONTACT WITH THE SKIN AND ESPECIALLY THE EYES. 

 WARNING: WEAR NON-POROUS GLOVES AND SAFETY GOGGLES AT ALL TIMES WHEN HANDLING 
LIQUID REFRIGERANT. SHOULD ANY LIQUID REFRIGERANT GET INTO THE EYES OR ON THE 
SKIN, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH EYES AND SKIN WITH WATER FOR AT LEAST 15 MINUTES. 
REMOVE CONTAMINATED CLOTHING AND SHOES. CALL A PHYSICIAN. 

 WARNING: REFRIGERANT R-134A IS ALWAYS UNDER PRESSURE. BECAUSE THE SYSTEM IS 
TIGHTLY SEALED, HEAT APPLIED TO ANY PART CAN CAUSE THIS PRESSURE TO BUILD UP 
EXCESSIVELY. TO AVOID A DANGEROUS EXPLOSION, KEEP AWAY FROM OPEN FLAMES, 
GLOWING METAL SURFACES, BLOW TORCHES, STEAM CLEANING AND WELDING. R-134A CAN 
BE DECOMPOSED AT HIGH TEMPERATURES. MAKE SURE THAT CONTAINERS ARE NEVER HEATED 
TO OVER 52°C (125°F). CONTAINERS MUST BE 
STORED AND INSTALLED IN ACCORDANCE WITH ALL STATE AND LOCAL ORDINANCES. 

 CAUTION: Use only R-134a refrigerant. Due to environmental concerns, when the 
air conditioning system is drained, the refrigerant must be collected using 
refrigerant recovery/recycling equipment. R-134a must never be removed without 
the appropriate equipment or released into the atmosphere. Use of a recovery 
machine dedicated for R-134a is necessary to reduce the possibility of oil and 
refrigerant incompatibility concerns. Refer to the instructions provided by 
the equipment manufacturer when removing refrigerant from or charging the air 
conditioning system. 

 CAUTION: When admitting R-134a into the refrigerant system, always keep the tank 
in an upright position. If the tank is on its side or upside down, liquid 
R-134a will enter the system and may damage the compressor. Refrigerant R-134a 
should not be mixed with air for leak testing or used with air for any other 
purpose above atmospheric pressure. R-134a is combustible when mixed with high 
concentrations of air and higher pressures. 

 CAUTION: A number of manufacturers are producing refrigerant products which are 
described as being direct replacements for R-134a. The use of any unauthorized 
substitute refrigerant can severely damage the A/C components. If service is 
required, use only new or recycled R-134a.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C-Heater System, Manual

The air conditioner-heater is an integral blend air system with the 
evaporator housing attached to the lower right side of the dash panel. The 
evaporator and heater cores are located inside the evaporator housing. The 
condenser is mounted in front of the radiator in the engine compartment.

Outside air is used for ventilating, heating and defrosting. 
Recirculated or outside air is used for air conditioner operation. The cool 
air is discharged through the instrument panel registers and floor directed 
outlets.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ventilation System

Ventilation is delivered through the instrument panel registers when 
the function lever in the control assembly is set in the PNL position, or 
through the floor outlets when the function lever is set in the FLR position. 
The quantity of air can be adjusted by means of the blower motor switch. The 
discharge air temperature can be controlled in all selected functions by the 
temperature control lever. The outside-recirc. door is in the outside air 
position when A/C, PNL, FLR, and DEF positions are selected.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Climate Control Assembly

The air conditioner and heater control assembly is located in the 
instrument panel at the right of the steering column. It includes a blower 
motor switch with four operating speeds: low, medium low, medium high and 
high. The control assembly also includes two levers. One is provided to allow 
temperature selection between the extremes of COOL and WARM; the other 
provides for functional selection between MAX A/C, A/C, PNL, OFF, FLR and DEF.

A/C and Heater Control Assy

The L-Series air conditioning and heater control system uses air 
pressure to activate pneumatic actuators, which control the position of the 
outside air-recirc., panel-floor and defrost doors. The control system uses 
air pressure from the braking system on vehicles equipped with air brakes or 
air pressure from a separate pump located under the passenger's seat on 
vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes. The system logic is shown in the 
following illustration.

[FIGURE: K16498B.gif]

—

Pressure Selector Valve (Part of 19980)

 Airflow Control 

The function selector lever, as it is moved to any of its six 
positions, actuates the appropriate ports in the pressure selector valve. This 
valve controls the distribution of pressure to the pneumatic actuators which 
operate the doors in the air conditioning/heater unit and plenum. The function 
selector lever actuates a pneumatic valve that controls pneumatic actuators at 
the defrost panel-floor and outside-recirc. air doors. The function selector 
lever also controls the blower switch on/off operation and activates the air 
conditioner clutch circuit in the MAX A/C and A/C positions.

 Temperature Control 

The temperature selector lever actuates a control cable which operates 
the temperature blend door. The blower motor will operate at low, medium low, 
medium high, or high speed. The function selector lever must be in the OFF 
position if no blower operation is desired.

The temperature door control cable uses two snap-in fittings, one near 
each end. The blue fitting engages a square hole on the control bracket after 
the Z-bend engages the lever, while the white fitting engages a square hole on 
a bracket secured to the rear side of the case nearest the passenger seat. The 
white fitting is not engaged into the bracket until the cable's pigtail first 
engages the temp door crank post. 

Another feature of the non-adjust cable is that it actually does have 
some adjustment capability. This is accomplished by displacing the white clip 
relative to its internal red bit. Only two minor readjustment positions on 
each side of center are provided. Cable will be non-functional beyond the 
second readjustment position.

 Blower Motor Control 

A four-speed blower control switch with a range between LO and HI is 
located at the bottom of the control assembly. To stop blower operation, it is 
necessary to move the function lever to its OFF position.

 A/C Switch 

The air conditioning system is turned on and off by the function 
selector lever. When the lever is set in A/C (MAX, A/C or PNL) positions, 
electrical current flows through the A/C cycling switch to the A/C compressor 
clutch field coil; the A/C clutch engages and the air conditioning system is 
on when the lever is in any of the A/C or DEFROST modes. Current also flows 
through the A/C cycling switch to the A/C compressor clutch field coil. This 
allows the operator to select fully cool air, if needed, for defogging the 
windshield. When the lever is moved to other functions, current is stopped to 
the A/C compressor clutch field coil and the air conditioning system is off.

 Pneumatic Hoses 

The tubing bundle is made up of four 5/32-inch OD black plastic tubes 
of which three are color-coded with colored tape strips at each end or a thin 
colored stripe along the length of the tubing. The color coding is as follows:

Black (no tape or stripe) connects black port on control to "source" 
pressure manifold (at driver's side toeboard).

Red (tape or stripe) connects red port on control to plenum door 
(defrost door) air cylinder.

White (tape or stripe) connects white port on control to fresh 
air/recirc. door (on case) air cylinder.

Blue (tape or stripe) connects blue port on control to case's panel 
door air cylinder.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor Speed Control

Blower speeds are controlled by a four-position blower switch and a 
resistor assembly located in the evaporator case upstream from the evaporator 
core. The switch is used to select low, two intermediate, or high blower 
speeds. The blower is turned off by the function selector lever when it is in 
the OFF position. This is accomplished by a switch integral with the vacuum 
selector attached to the control assembly.

The blower motor is installed in the blower housing which is part of 
the evaporator case. The motor is connected to the electrical circuit with two 
hardshell connectors located near the motor.

The blower speed switch is installed on the control assembly and, with 
the blower resistor, provides the selection of four blower operating speeds. 
This switch does not turn the blower off.

================================================================================

================================================================================

Section 12-03A: Air Conditioning

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor Resistor

The blower motor resistor is installed in the evaporator case between 
the blower motor and the evaporator core. The resistor is used with the blower 
speed switch to provide four blower speeds.

Section 12-03A: Air Conditioning

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor Switch Resistor

 Blower Motor Thermal Limiter 

The resistor assembly contains a thermal limiter which is used as a 
temperature protecting fuse. The thermal limiter is located a preset distance 
from the resistor coils. If the temperature of the thermal limiter reaches 
approximately 149°C (300°F), the limiter 
contacts will open interrupting the blower motor circuit for all blower speeds 
except high speed. The thermal limiter will not reset and the resistor 
assembly must be replaced if the thermal limiter opens.

[FIGURE: L32451A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Recirculating Air Duct and Blower Motor Housing

The air inlet duct is located between the blower housing portion of the 
evaporator case and the dash panel in the engine compartment. It is attached 
to the dash panel. The air inlet duct is attached to the evaporator housing.

The air inlet duct contains the recirculating air duct door and the 
recirculating air duct grille, and has the door pneumatic actuator motor 
installed on the top of the duct.

The plenum assembly is mounted to the dash panel in the passenger 
compartment. It contains the temperature blend door, the heater core, and the 
panel and floor-windshield defroster doors. The temperature door is cable 
controlled at the crank arm on top of the plenum. The panel and 
floor-windshield defroster doors are operated by pneumatic actuator motors 
mounted on the side of the plenum.

The heater core is located in the right end of the plenum behind the 
heater core cover. The heater core cover allows heater core removal without 
removing the plenum.

Electrical System

The electrical system consists of the blower motor, blower speed

limiter, A/C cycling switch, magnetic clutch, thermal protection switch with 
CHECK A/C indicator light and the fuse and wiring to complete the circuits.

Evaporator (Absorbs BTUs)

The boiling or condensing temperature of a refrigerant increases or 
decreases relative to the pressure exerted.

Heat can be transferred from a comparatively cooler passenger 
compartment to the hot outside air because of the difference between the 
refrigerant pressure in the evaporator and the pressure in the condenser. At 
the evaporator, the A/C evaporator core orifice tube reduces the pressure and 
thereby reduces the boiling point below the temperature of the passenger 
compartment. Heat transfers from the passenger compartment to the boiling 
refrigerant. In the condenser, the compressor raises the condensation point 
above the temperature of the outside air. The heat transfers from the 
condensing refrigerant to the outside air. The A/C evaporator core orifice 
tube and the compressor simply create pressure conditions that permit the laws 
of thermodynamics to provide the desired cooling effects.

In the L-Series air conditioning system, liquid refrigerant R-134a is 
delivered under high pressure from the condenser to the A/C evaporator core 
orifice tube located in the evaporator inlet tube. When the refrigerant passes 
through the orifice tube, its pressure drops and its temperature drops to the 
saturation temperature associated with the pressure in the evaporator. The 
evaporator pressure is determined by the compressor suction pressure or is 
controlled by the pressure switch. As the refrigerant flows through the 
evaporator, warm passenger compartment air or outside air passes over the 
finned surfaces of the evaporator causing the refrigerant to boil. As it 
boils, the colder refrigerant absorbs heat from the air and cools the 
passenger compartment. The heat from the air is absorbed by the boiling 
refrigerant which is converted to a gas. The refrigeration cycle is now under 
way. Use the following procedure to complete the cycle.

Dispose of the heat in the gas.

Convert the gas back to liquid for reuse.

Return the liquid to the starting point in the refrigerant cycle.

The compressor pumps the gas and liquid out of the evaporator into the 
suction line to the accumulator/drier which stores any liquid that has passed 
through the evaporator. The suction accumulator/drier then allows only gas to 
return to the compressor. The compressor pumps the gaseous refrigerant under 
high pressure and temperature into the condenser which is located in the 
outside air stream at the front of the vehicle. The temperature of the gas 
entering the condenser is higher than that of outside air. As the heat is 
transferred from the hot gas to the cooler air, the refrigerant condenses back 
to liquid. The liquid, under high pressure, returns to the orifice tube in the 
evaporator inlet line to repeat its flow cycle.

 A/C Evaporator Core Orifice 

The function of the orifice tube is to regulate the flow of refrigerant 
into the evaporator. It is the dividing point in the refrigerant system 
between high and low pressure.

L-Series vehicles are equipped with an orifice tube that is color-coded

mesh-screened surface of the orifice tube assembly.

 Suction Accumulator/Drier 

 NOTE: Replacement of the suction accumulator/drier is not required
when repairing the air conditioning system except when there is
physical evidence of system contamination from a failed A/C
compressor or damage to the suction accumulator/drier.

Refrigerant enters the suction accumulator/drier canister through the 
inlet tube and the heavier oil-laden refrigerant falls to the bottom of the 
canister. A small-diameter oil bleed hole is located in the side of the outlet 
tube near the bottom of the canister. This bleed hole is covered with a filter 
and allows a small amount of the heavier liquid refrigerant and oil mixture to 
re-enter the suction line at a controlled rate. When the heavier liquid 
refrigerant and oil mixture enters the compressor suction line, it has a 
second opportunity to vaporize and circulate through the compressor without 
causing damage to the compressor due to refrigerant slugging.

A desiccant bag is mounted inside the suction accumulator/drier 
canister to absorb any moisture which may be in the refrigerant system.

A fitting located on the top of the suction accumulator/drier is used 
to attach the A/C cycling switch. A long travel valve stem core is installed 
in the fitting opening to prevent refrigerant loss when the A/C cycling switch 
is removed.

 A/C Cycling Switch 

The primary function of the A/C cycling switch is to maintain as low an 
evaporator temperature as possible without allowing evaporator icing to occur.

The dual-function pressure switch is located on the top of the suction 
accumulator/drier and controls the compressor clutch cycling. When the 
evaporator pressure increases to approximately 276-324 kPa (40-47 psi), the 
switch closes. When the pressure drops below approximately 169 kPa ±
 10 kPa (24.5 psi ± 1.5 psi), the 
switch opens to stop compressor operation. In ambient temperatures below 
approximately 7.2°C (45°F) the pressure 
switch will not allow compressor operation because of low system pressures.

During compressor operation, the A/C cycling switch senses the pressure 
in the suction accumulator/drier and electrically controls the cycling of the 
clutch assembly and the compressor to prevent the refrigerant from freezing 
the condensate which occurs on the evaporator. If allowed to build up, the ice 
would block airflow. The cut-in pressure of the compressor clutch is 
approximately 43.5 psi (clutch is operative) and the cutout pressure is 
approximately 24.5 psi (clutch is inoperative).

 A/C Condenser Core 

The A/C condenser core is attached to the radiator support in front of 
the radiator with two brackets at the top and bottom of the A/C condenser 
core. The top mounting brackets attach to the front of the radiator support, 
and the lower brackets attach to the bottom of the radiator support.

A/C Condenser Core

 A/C Compressor 

The A/C compressor is an axial design compressor with mounting brackets 
for tangential mounting. The compressor shaft is driven by belt from the 
engine accessory drive. The pistons, positioned axially around the compressor 
shaft, are actuated by a swash plate that is pressed on the compressor shaft. 
The swash plate uses the rotating action of the shaft to provide a 
reciprocating driving force to each of the pistons.

The A/C compressor has seven cylinders. Reed-type suction and discharge 
valve plates are located between the cylinder assembly and the head. An 
integral clutch is used to drive the compressor shaft.

When voltage is applied to the field coil, the clutch plate and hub 
assembly (which is solidly coupled to the compressor shaft) is drawn by 
magnetic force toward the pulley which rotates freely on the compressor front 
head casting. The magnetic force locks the clutch plate and hub assembly 
together as one unit. The compressor shaft then turns with the pulley. When 
voltage is removed from the clutch field coil, a rubber bushing in the clutch 
plate and hub assembly moves the clutch plate away from the pulley, and the 
clutch plate and hub assembly and the compressor shaft cease to rotate.

The air conditioner compressor is equipped with a thermal protection 
switch to automatically shut down operation by interrupting the electrical 
power to the compressor clutch when the compressor temperature exceeds 
approximately 116°C (2

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Air Conditioning

 Inspection and Verification 

Refer to Section 12-00 to supplement the following procedures.

It is possible to detect problem causes by a careful visual inspection 
of the air conditioner refrigerant system. This includes broken drive belt, 
obstructed air passages, a loose A/C clutch, loose or broken mounting 
brackets, disconnected or broken wires and many refrigerant leaks.

A refrigerant leak will usually appear as an oily residue at the 
leakage point in the system. The oily residue soon picks up dust or dirt 
particles from the surrounding air and appears greasy. Through time, this will 
build up and appear to be a heavy dirt-impregnated grease.

Most common leaks are caused by damaged or missing O-ring seals at the 
various hose and component connections. When these O-rings are replaced, 
lubricate the new O-rings with refrigerant oil. Be careful to keep shop towel 
lint from contaminating the internal surfaces of the connection. Leakage can 
occur at a spring lock coupling if the wrong O-rings are used at the coupling. 
Use only the O-rings listed in the Ford Master Parts Catalog for the spring 
lock coupling.

If the system contains no refrigerant or is extremely low on 
refrigerant, the A/C clutch will not engage for compressor operation. A 
rapidly cycling A/C clutch is usually an indication that the system is low on 
refrigerant. Also, cycling will normally not occur when the engine is 
operating at curb idle speed.

Inspect the vehicle dash panel for missing or improperly fitting 
grommets, plugs or seals. Also inspect for correct sealing of the evaporator 
case-to-dash gaskets. Install any missing grommets, plugs or seals. Tighten 
the evaporator case-to-dash panel retaining nuts to correct a seal leak 
between the evaporator case and the dash panel.

Inspect the drain opening on the forward side of the dash panel when 
the air conditioning system is operating during humid conditions. Water must 
flow freely from the drain tube. If blockage of the drain tube is suspected, 
the drain can be carefully flushed with water to remove accumulated debris.
