REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Refrigerant Oil Addition

The Sanden-SD compressor uses a polyalkylene glycol (PAG) refrigerant 
oil meeting Ford specification WST-M1C231-B2. An oil charge of 300 ml (10 oz) 
is used in a new system. It is extremely important that only the specified 
type and quantity of refrigerant oil be used in the compressor. If there is a 
surplus of oil in the system, it will circulate with the refrigerant, reducing 
the cooling capacity of the system. Using too little oil or oil not meeting 
the Ford specification will result in poor lubrication of the compressor.

When replacing a component of the refrigerant system, the procedures in 
this section must be followed to ensure that the total oil charge in the 
system is correct after the new part is installed.

When the compressor is operated, oil gradually leaves the compressor 
and is circulated through the system with the refrigerant. Eventually, a 
balanced condition is reached in which a certain amount of oil is retained in 
the compressor and a certain amount is continually circulated. If a component 
of the system is removed after the system has been operated, some oil will go 
with it. To maintain the original total oil charge, add oil as required to the 
new replacement part.

Refer to the following procedures for replacing refrigerant oil during 
A/C compressor replacement and during component replacement.

 During A/C Compressor Replacement 

 NOTE: The orifice tube should be replaced when the compressor is replaced.

 NOTE: Replacement of the suction accumulator/drier is not required
when repairing the air conditioning system except when there is
physical evidence of system contamination from a failed A/C
compressor or damage to the suction accumulator/drier.

A new service replacement compressor contains 300 ml (10 oz) of 
refrigerant oil.

Obtain a clean container that can also be used as a measuring device.

Place the disc and hub assembly on the compressor shaft so the shaft 
can be rotated.

Rotate the shaft by hand six to eight revolutions, collecting the oil 
in a clean measuring device.

If the amount of oil drained from the old compressor was between 85 and 
142 ml (3 and 5 oz), pour the same amount of clean specified refrigerant oil 
into the new compressor.

If the amount of oil that was removed from the old compressor is 
greater than 142 ml (5 oz), pour 142 ml (5 oz) of clean specified refrigerant 
oil into the new compressor.

If the amount of refrigerant oil that was removed from the old 
compressor is less than 85 ml (3 oz), pour 85 ml (3 oz) of clean specified 
refrigerant oil into the new compressor.

 During Component Replacement 

When replacing other components of the air conditioning system, 
measured quantities of the specified refrigerant oil should be added to the 
component to ensure that the total oil charge in the system is correct before 
the system is operated.

Clean refrigerant oil should be poured directly into the replacement 
components in the following quantities:

A/C evaporator core: add 90 ml (3 oz).

A/C condenser core: add 30 ml (1 oz).

Accumulator: drain oil from removed accumulator/drier. Add same amount 
plus 60 ml (2 oz) of clean refrigerant oil to new accumulator.

If any other component such as an A/C evaporator core orifice or a hose 
is replaced, no additional refrigerant oil is necessary unless a hose bursts 
with a fully charged system. The addition of refrigerant oil may be necessary 
with the amount to be determined by the technician. The suction 
accumulator/drier should also be replaced under these circumstances.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Climate Control Assembly

 Removal 

Remove access panel which surrounds the control assembly and remove the 
two fasteners which secure the control assembly to the instrument panel.

Carefully pull control assembly back to expose the temperature door 
cable anchor point. Using pliers, pinch the blue fitting snap-in tangs and 
push the fitting out of the square hole. Hold control assembly firmly with one 
hand to prevent any type of bending of the plastic bracket when applying force 
of any kind.

With the blue fitting free, it will now be possible to disengage the 
Z-bend at the end of the wire from the control temp lever hole. Some 
articulation of the cable end is required.

 CAUTION: Each port has a metal insert or sleeve which engages the tubing inside 
diameter. Should this insert pull out of the port with the tubing, make sure 
it is re-engaged into the replacement tubing upon reassembly. 

Set the selector lever to OFF. Remove each tube from the air actuator 
on the control assembly, making sure that you depress and hold each mating 
collar while pulling on the tubing. Hold the actuator firmly while pulling off 
the tubing.

Carefully disconnect the blower switch wiring harness connector, the 
function selector electrical switch hardshell connector, as well as the 
control bulb/socket wiring harness connector.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order. Upon tube insertion, colored 
identification collars are not to be depressed. A bottoming out of the tubing 
can be felt upon insertion. Also, each tube end has a position identification 
line as a visual check for correct insertion. Lines on all the tubes will no 
longer be visible after proper insertion.

 Illumination Bulbs 

 Removal 

Remove access panel which surrounds the control and remove the two 
fasteners which secure the control to the instrument panel.

Place temperature control lever in the full COOL position and carefully 
pull the control back to expose the illumination bulb socket and wires.

Remove illumination bulb socket by carefully pulling straight out of 
the control. A slight rocking motion may be required to assist in the removal.

Remove the illumination bulb by grasping bulb in fingers and carefully 
pulling out of socket.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

 Switch Knobs 

 NOTE: All climate control knobs remove and install in the same manner.

 Removal 

Grasp knob in fingers.

Release spring lock clip on backside of knob using a flat-bladed 
screwdriver. Pull clip toward knob while pulling knob off shaft at the same 
time.

 Installation 

Align shaft, spring lock clip and knob.

Push until a bottoming is felt between shaft and knob.

Spool Valve Assembly

 Removal 

Remove access panel which surrounds the control and remove the two 
fasteners which secure the control to the instrument panel.

Carefully pull control assembly back to expose the temperature door 
cable anchor point. With needle-nosed pliers or blade-type screwdriver, pinch

Hold control firmly with one hand to prevent bending of the plastic bracket 
when applying force of any kind.

With the blue fitting free, it will now be possible to disengage the 
Z-bend at the end of the wire from the control temperature lever hole. Some

 NOTE: Each port has a metal insert or sleeve which engages the tubing inside 
diameter. Should this insert pull out of the port with the tubing, make sure

Disconnect the tube harness by pressing and holding in the colored 
release buttons while pulling out the tubing.

Remove the fastener securing the aluminum cover plate.

Remove the two screws securing the electrical mode switch to the bracket.

Remove the two Phillips head screws securing the spool valve assembly 
to the bracket.

 CAUTION: Do not pull the spool out of the spool body. If the spool is removed, 
it can become contaminated resulting in a control assembly failure.

[FIGURE: DM0246A.gif]

Reinstall the aluminum cover plate and secure with fasteners.

Reconnect the tube harness to the appropriate color-coded ports. Each 
tube end has a positive identification line as a visual check for correct 
insertion. Lines on the tubes will not be visible if properly inserted.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Blower Motor Switch

 Removal 

Remove access panel which shields the control. Remove the two fasteners 
that secure the control to the instrument panel (if necessary).

 WARNING: HOLD KNOB WITH ONE HAND DURING THE KNOB REMOVAL PHASE TO AVOID INJURY 
OR LOSS OF KNOB WHEN SPRING CLIP IS DISENGAGED. AS A PRECAUTION, SAFETY 
GLASSES ARE RECOMMENDED. 

Remove the blower switch knob by pushing on the underside of the knob 
spring clip with a blade-type screwdriver.

Disconnect blower switch wiring from mating harness in instrument panel.

Remove the single blower switch fastener and remove switch from control.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: When securing the blower switch fastener, do not overtighten screw. The 
plastic bracket's mounting hole may strip out if excessive torque is applied. 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Section 12-03A: Air Conditioning

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Cables

 Pneumatic Hoses 

 Removal 

 NOTE: Please read entire procedure prior to servicing the harness.

Determine visually if it will be necessary to loosen the case-to-dash 
panel retaining nuts to pull the case rearward in the cab an inch or so, 
without disconnecting the air conditioning lines or heater hoses.

 CAUTION: The special fittings employed require that the colored collar(s) on the 
air cylinders or on the control be pushed toward the cylinder(s) or control 
prior to attempting to remove the tubing. Failure to depress the collar could 
result in damage to the cylinder, control, etc. 

 NOTE: The white tube has a routing clip above the case and a second clip on 
the dash behind the right side of the case. Please note that the clip on the 
dash is not a slip-through type. This plastic rosebud engages a 6 mm 
(1/4-inch) hole in the dash and the tubing has been pretaped to the rosebud. 
If necessary, the rosebud may be cut off or pried out with a screwdriver.

Disconnect white tubing at fresh air-recirc. door cylinder.

Remove the red, blue and black tube ends.

Remove the access panel which shields the control assembly and the 
panel to the left of the control assembly. This will expose the control and 
the tube routing of the black (source pressure) tubing.

 CAUTION: Each port has a metal insert or sleeve which engages the tubing inside 
diameter. Should this insert pull out of the port with the tubing, make sure 
it is re-engaged into the replacement tubing upon reassembly. 

Set the function selector lever to MAX A/C. Then begin to remove each 
tube from the air actuator on the control, making sure to depress and hold 
each mating collar while pulling on the tubing. Hold the actuator firmly while 
pulling off the tubing.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order. Upon tube insertion, colored 
identification collars are not to be depressed. A bottoming out of the tubing 
can be felt upon insertion. Also, each tube end has a position identification 
line as a visual check for correct insertion. Lines on the tubes will not be 
visible after proper insertion.

 Temperature Control Cable 

 Removal 

Place the temperature control lever in MAX COOL position.

Remove the air conditioning/heater housing cover trim panel (four 
screws and one Velcro® fastener where used).

Locate the cable-to-housing bracket attachment point. Using pliers, 
pinch the white fitting snap-in tangs and push the fitting out of the square 
hole in the steel or plastic bracket.

After white fitting is free, articulate cable conduit and wire end so 
the wire pigtail disengages from the plastic post on the crank arm of the 
blend air door.

Remove instrument panel access panel shielding the control assembly and 
remove the two fasteners which hold the control assembly to the instrument 
panel.

Carefully pull control assembly back to expose cable anchor point. 
Using pliers, pinch the blue fitting snap-in tangs and push the fitting out of 
the square hole. Hold control assembly firmly with one hand to prevent any 
type of cantilever bending of the plastic bracket while applying force of any 
kind.

 NOTE: In each case prior to engaging the snap-in fitting, it is necessary 
that the Z-bend be connected (control end) or that the pigtail be connected 
(case end).

With the Z-bend at the end of the wire, disconnect it from the control 
temp lever hole. Some articulation of the cable end is required. When cable is 
totally free, carefully remove the cable, taking care not to snag, pull out or 
otherwise adversely affect the control tubing routed nearby.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order. In each case, a click must 
be heard upon fitting insertion. Proper seating can be checked by pulling on 
the conduit in a direction perpendicular to the mount surface (close to the 
anchor point).

Should the reassembled system require cable adjustment, refer to the Adjustments 
 portion of this section. In general, adjustment is not required if 
the temperature control lever is centralized in its slot (equal distance to 
slot edges from lever centerline in full warm vs. full cool).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Evaporator Housing Assembly

 Removal 

Discharge the air conditioning system.

Remove the accumulator mounting bolts at the attachment to the 
accumulator mounting bracket.

Disconnect the liquid and suction lines from the evaporator at the dash 
panel.

Loosen the four housing-to-dash panel retaining nuts to allow the 
housing to be pushed rearward in the vehicle approximately 3/4 inch to relieve 
the pressure on the dash panel seals.

Remove the air conditioning/heater housing trim panel cover panel (four 
screws and one Velcro® fastener, where used).

Remove the evaporator core cover retaining screws and remove the cover 
from the housing (seven screws).

Carefully pull the evaporator core rearward out of the housing. Check 
to see that the dash panel to housing seal was removed with the evaporator core.

 Installation 

Apply silicone grease liberally to the evaporator housing dash panel 
seal and to the housing where the seal will slide through the dash panel. 
Position the seal over the evaporator tubes and against the backing plate.

Use shipping plugs or tape to protect the edges of the female tube 
O-fittings during installation.

Carefully slide the evaporator core into the housing. At the point 
where the seal enters the opening in the forward side of the housing, check 
from the engine side of the dash panel to make sure the evaporator tubes are 
aligned with the dash holes and that the seal will pass through the forward 
opening in the housing to seal properly against the inside surface of the dash 
panel. Push the evaporator fully into the housing.

Position the housing cover on the housing and install the cover 
attaching screws.

Tighten the four housing-to-dash panel retaining nuts.

Check the evaporator to dash seals around the dash panel holes from the 
engine side.

 NOTE: A special captured O-ring is now used on the tube-O fittings for 1996 
and newer heavy trucks. These captured O-rings are not compatible with 
standard tube-O fittings.

Install new O-rings on the liquid and suction line male ends, apply 
refrigerant oil liberally to both the male and female fittings and engage the 
lines into the tubes.

Install the accumulator mounting bolts.

Leak test, evacuate and charge the air conditioning system. Check 
system operation.

Install the A/C-heater housing cover trim panel (four screws and one 
Velcro® fastener, where used).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Heater Core

 Removal 

Drain the engine cooling system.

Disconnect the heater hoses at the dash panel.

Inside the vehicle, remove the air conditioner/heater housing trim 
panel (four screws and one Velcro® fastener, where used).

Remove the three heater core cover retaining screws and remove the 
cover from the housing.

Pull the heater core and seal assembly from the housing. It may be 
necessary to loosen the four housing-to-dash panel retaining nuts in the 
engine compartment to relieve the pressure on the heater core tube/dash seals 
to facilitate removal of the heater core.

 Installation 

Install plugs or tape on the heater core tube ends to prevent cutting 
the dash panel seals and prevent entry of foreign materials into the heater 
core.

Apply silicone grease liberally to the tube ends and the inside of the 
dash panel seals to allow the heater core tubes to easily pass through the 
seals at installation.

Install the heater core and seal assembly into the housing. Make sure 
the core tubes pass through the dash seals and the dash seals are in the 
proper position.

Position the heater core cover and install the two upper and one lower 
left retaining screws. The lower right screw hole is used for retaining the 
trim cover panel.

Install the air conditioner heater housing cover trim panel (four 
screws and one Velcro® fastener, where used).

Tighten the housing-to-dash panel retaining nuts in the engine 
compartment if they were loosened.

Connect the heater hoses and tighten the clamps to 2-3 Nm
 (18-27 lb-in).

Fill and bleed the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Ducts

 Outlet Floor 

 Removal 

Remove the A/C-heater housing trim panel.

Remove the floor duct retaining screw.

Pull down on the left side of the duct to disengage the Velcro®
 fastener (where used) and remove the floor duct.

 Installation 

Position the floor duct in its approximate location under the floor 
opening of the A/C-heater assembly. Raise duct into position to engage the 
forward tab of the floor duct into the retaining groove on the forward edge of 
the floor opening of the air conditioning/heater assembly.

Lift the left side of the floor duct and engage the Velcro®
 fastener (where used).

Install the floor duct retaining screw.

Install the A/C-heater housing cover panel.

 A/C Recirculating Air Duct and/or Blower Motor Housing 

 Removal 

Drain the engine cooling system.

Discharge the air conditioning system. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe 
all safety precautions.

Disconnect the battery ground cable.

Remove the accumulator mounting bolts at the attachment to the 
accumulator mounting bracket.

Disconnect the liquid and suction lines from the evaporator at the dash 
panel.

Disconnect the heater hoses at the dash panel.

Inside the vehicle, remove four screws and one Velcro®
 fastener (where used) and remove the air conditioning/heater housing trim 
panel.

Disconnect the blower motor resistor and the blower motor connectors.

Remove the control cable from the bracket and the temperature door arm 
pivot with pliers to compress the cable clip locking tabs.

In the engine compartment, remove the four nuts that secure the 
A/C-heater housing mounting studs to the dash panel.

Slide the A/C-heater unit rearward in the vehicle and remove the 
pressure tubing from the outside air-recirc. and panel-floor actuators. 
Failure to remove the tubing and excessive pulling at the control end may 
cause damage to the control.

Remove the A/C-heater housing assembly from the vehicle.

Tape or plug all refrigerant and heater hose tube ends to make sure 
they are not damaged or that moisture or contaminants do not enter the system.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Prior to assembly to dash panel, make sure that evaporator and heater 
core tube ends are protected to prevent damage during installation. 

Position the housing assembly in the vehicle near its installed 
location and connect the pressure tubing to the outside air-recirc, and 
panel-floor door actuators.

Slide the unit into the installed position, making sure the housing 
assembly seal at the underside of the plenum is not damaged or pulled out of 
position. Make sure the side cowl seal at the fresh air inlet is in position.

Attach the temperature control cable to the temperature door arm pivot 
and the bracket.

Install the four nuts that secure the housing mounting studs to the 
dash panel.

Connect the blower motor resistor and blower motor connectors.

Connect the heater hoses at the dash panel and tighten the clamps to 
the proper torque.

 NOTE: A special captured O-ring is now used on the tube-O fittings for 1996 
and newer heavy trucks. These captured O-rings are not compatible with 
standard tube-O fittings.

Install new O-rings on the liquid and suction line male ends. Apply 
refrigerant oil liberally to the male and female fittings and couple the lines 
to the evaporator tubes.

Install the accumulator mounting bolts.

Connect the battery ground cable.

Fill and bleed the engine cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Leak test, evacuate and charge the air conditioning system. Refer to 
 Section 12-00 . Check system operation.

Install the A/C-heater housing trim panel (four screws and one Velcro®
 fastener, where used).

Actuators, Pneumatic

 Panel-Floor Door 

 Removal 

Remove the air conditioning-heater housing cover trim panel.

Remove the floor duct.

Remove the engine cover.

Loosen the four housing-to-dash panel retaining nuts.

Pull the housing assembly rearward in the vehicle to obtain working 
clearance to the actuator retaining screws.

Disconnect tubing.

Remove two screws attaching actuator to housing.

Slide actuator rod off door shaft arm.

 Installation 

Slide actuator rod onto door shaft arm.

Install two retaining screws. Do not overtighten.

Install pressure tubing.

Check for proper operation.

Push the housing assembly forward in the vehicle and tighten the 
housing-to-dash panel retaining nuts. Inspect to make sure the 
plenum-to-housing and side cowl air inlet seals are in the proper position.

Install the engine cover.

Install the floor duct.

Install the air conditioning/heater cover trim panel.

 Defrost Door 

 Removal 

Remove the A/C-heater housing cover trim panel.

Remove the floor duct.

Remove the engine cover.

Disconnect the pressure tubing from the actuator.

Remove the clevis pin clip, pull down on the pressure fitting nipple to 
relieve the actuator spring force on the clevis pin and remove the clevis pin.

Remove the instrument panel attaching bolts and pull the panel rearward 
to gain access to the plenum defrost opening. Remove the actuator-to-defrost 
door retaining latch pin.

Remove the actuator.

 Installation 

Install the actuator to the defrost door with the actuator-to-defrost 
door retaining latch pin. Make sure the pin is latched.

Pull down on the actuator to align the holes in the actuator and 
bracket. Insert the clevis pin and install the retaining clip. The pressure 
fitting nipple must face forward in the vehicle. 

Insert the pressure tubing.

Position the instrument panel in the installed location. Check for 
proper operation of the defrost door. If OK, install the instrument panel bolts.

Install the engine cover.

Install the floor duct.

Install the A/C-heater housing cover trim panel.

 Outside-Recirc. Door 

 Removal 

Remove the A/C-heater housing cover trim panel.

Disconnect tubing.

Remove two screws attaching actuator to housing.

Slide actuator rod off of door shaft arm.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order. Do not overtighten actuator 
retaining screws.

Check for proper operation before installing housing cover trim panel.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Suction Accumulator/Drier

 Removal 

 NOTE: Replacement of the suction accumulator/drier is not required
when repairing the air conditioning system except when there is
physical evidence of system contamination from a failed A/C
compressor or damage to the suction accumulator/drier.

Discharge the refrigerant from the air conditioning system. Refer to 
 Section 12-00 . Observe all safety precautions.

Disconnect the electrical connector from the A/C cycling switch.

Remove the A/C cycling switch by unscrewing it from the suction 
accumulator/drier.

Disconnect the suction line from the suction accumulator/drier.

Remove the two mounting screws holding the bracket for the 
accumulator/drier. Disconnect the accumulator/drier from the evaporator outlet 
tube and remove the accumulator/drier. Cap all open refrigerant connections to 
prevent the entry of dirt and moisture.

 Installation 

Inspect the inside surface of the fittings for damage or contaminants 
that would affect sealing. Inspect the fittings to make sure no damage exists 
that would affect proper coupling of the fitting.

 NOTE: A special captured O-ring is now used on the tube O-fittings for 1996 
and newer heavy trucks. These captured O-rings are not compatible with 
standard tube O-fittings.

Inspect the fittings on the two suction lines to be coupled to the 
accumulator. Install new specified O-rings. Lubricate both the male and female 
fittings liberally with refrigerant oil.

Hold the accumulator in its approximate installed position and couple 
the accumulator to the evaporator outlet tube. Couple the suction line to the 
accumulator outlet fitting. Make sure the connections are fully engaged. 

Install the two mounting screws on the bracket for the 
accumulator/drier. Tighten screws to 1.7 Nm (15 lb-in) minimum.

 NOTE: A special captured O-ring is now used on the tube-O fittings for 1996 
and newer heavy trucks. These captured O-rings are not compatible with 
standard tube-O fittings.

Use a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil on the pressure 
switch nipple of the suction accumulator/drier. Then, install the A/C cycling 
switch and tighten the switch to 7-13 Nm (62-115 lb-in) if 
the switch has a metal base, and hand-tight if the switch has a plastic base.

Leak test, evacuate and charge the air conditioning system. Refer to 
 Section 12-00 .

Check system operation.

A/C Cycling Switch

 Removal

Unscrew the A/C cycling switch from the top of the suction 
accumulator/drier.

 Installation

Screw the pressure switch onto the top of the suction 
accumulator/drier. Do not exceed the specified torque limits 7-13 Nm
 (62-115 lb-in). If A/C cycling switch has a plastic base, 
hand-tighten only.

Install the electrical connector.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Evaporator Core Orifice

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to remove the fixed orifice tube with pliers or by 
twisting the tube. To do so will break the fixed orifice tube body in the 
evaporator core tube. Use only the recommended tool and follow the recommended 
service procedures. 

The fixed orifice tube is constructed with a plastic body, two screens 
and a small brass tube down the center of the orifice body. Two O-rings are 
installed around the orifice tube body to seal against leakage.

 Removal 

Discharge the refrigerant from the air conditioning system. Refer to 
 Section 12-00 . Observe all safety precautions.

Disconnect the liquid line from the evaporator core. Cap the liquid 
line to prevent the entry of dirt and excessive moisture.

Squirt a small amount of clean refrigerant oil into the evaporator core 
inlet tube to lubricate the tube and orifice O-rings during removal of the 
fixed orifice tube from the evaporator core tube.

Engage Fixed Orifice Tube Tool D80L-19990-A or equivalent with the two 
tangs on the fixed orifice tube. Extract the orifice tube from the evaporator 
core tube.

If the orifice tube should break, hold the T-handle of Broken Orifice 
Tube Extractor D80L-19990-B or equivalent to keep the orifice tube from turning.

Run the nut on the tool down against the evaporator core tube until the 
orifice is pulled from the tube.

To remove a broken segment of an orifice tube, insert the screw end of 
the extractor into the evaporator core tube and thread the screw end of the 
tool into the brass tube in the center of the fixed orifice tube. Pull the 
fixed orifice tube from the evaporator core tube.

If only the brass center is removed, insert the screw end of the 
extractor tool into the evaporator core tube and turn it into the end of the 
fixed orifice tube body. Pull the fixed orifice tube body from the evaporator 
core tube. 

 Installation 

Lubricate the O-rings on the fixed orifice tube body liberally with 
clean refrigerant oil.

Place the fixed orifice tube in Fixed Orifice Tube Tool D80L-19990-A or 
equivalent and insert the fixed orifice tube into the evaporator core tube 
until the orifice is seated at the stop.

Remove the tool from the fixed orifice tube.

 NOTE: A special captured O-ring is now used on the tube-O fittings for 1996 
and newer heavy trucks. These captured O-rings are not compatible with 
standard tube-O fittings.

Install two new specified O-rings lubricated with clean refrigerant oil 
onto the tube-O fitting. Connect both halves of tube-O fitting, using a wrench 
on each side of fitting to tighten.

Leak test, evacuate and charge the system. Refer to Section 12-00 . 
Observe all safety precautions.

Check the system for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Condenser Core

 NOTE: Replacement of the suction accumulator/drier is not required
when repairing the air conditioning system except when there is
physical evidence of system contamination from a failed A/C
compressor or damage to the suction accumulator/drier.

 Removal 

Discharge refrigerant from system. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all 
safety precautions.

Disconnect liquid line from condenser. Cap liquid line to prevent 
entrance of dirt and moisture.

Disconnect compressor discharge line from condenser. Cap discharge line 
to prevent entrance of dirt and moisture.

Working under vehicle, remove four screws attaching two condenser lower 
mounting brackets to front radiator support.

Remove four screws attaching two condenser upper mounting brackets to 
front side of radiator support.

Lift condenser from vehicle.

 Installation 

Position condenser to vehicle with lower mounting brackets on front 
side of radiator support and upper brackets on rear side of radiator support.

Install eight screws attaching four mounting brackets to radiator 
support. Tighten screws to 14-18 Nm (11-13 lb-ft).

 NOTE: A special captured O-ring is now used on the tube-O fittings for 1996 
and newer heavy trucks. These captured O-rings are not compatible with 
standard tube-O fittings.

Using two new O-rings lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect 
compressor discharge line to condenser.

 NOTE: A special captured O-ring is now used on the tube-O fittings for 1996 
and newer heavy trucks. These captured O-rings are not compatible with 
standard tube-O fittings.

Connect liquid line to condenser, using two new O-rings lubricated with 
clean refrigerant oil.

Leak test, evacuate and charge system. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe 
all safety precautions.

Check system for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Refrigerant Lines

 Removal 

Discharge A/C system. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all safety 
precautions.

Disconnect and remove refrigerant line using a wrench on each side of 
fitting.

Plug all A/C system open fittings to prevent dirt and moisture from 
entering the system.

 Installation 

Route new refrigerant line (with protective caps installed).

 NOTE: A special captured O-ring is now used on the tube-O fittings for 1996 
and newer heavy trucks. These captured O-rings are not compatible with 
standard tube-O fittings.

Remove protective caps and/or plugs from A/C fittings and connect 
refrigerant line into system using new O-rings lubricated with clean 
refrigerant oil.

Connect tube-O fittings using a wrench on both halves of fitting to 
tighten.

Evacuate, leak test and charge A/C system. Refer to Section 12-00 . 
Observe all safety precautions.

 Liquid Lines 

 Removal 

Discharge A/C system. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all safety 
precautions.

Disconnect liquid line at A/C condenser core.

Disconnect liquid line at evaporator inlet.

Disconnect retainer bracket at cowl center.

Remove liquid line from vehicle. Pay particular attention to line 
routing for installation purposes.

Cap all refrigerant system fitting and line openings to prevent dirt 
and moisture from entering the A/C system.

 Installation 

Route replacement liquid line in same manner as line removed.

Remove all plugs and/or shipping caps from A/C system and replacement 
line as necessary.

 NOTE: A special captured O-ring is now used on the tube-O fittings for 1996 
and newer heavy trucks. These captured O-rings are not compatible with 
standard tube-O fittings.

Install new, specified O-rings on fittings/lines as required.

Lubricate all O-rings and line fittings liberally with clean 
refrigerant oil.

Connect liquid line to evaporator inlet.

Connect liquid line to A/C condenser core outlet.

Connect retainer bracket at cowl center.

Evacuate, leak test and charge A/C system. Refer to Section 12-00 . 
Observe all safety precautions.

 Condenser and Refrigerant Line Tube, 3306 Engine

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Heater Water Hoses

 Removal 

Drain the coolant and remove the hose.

Cut a new hose of the same diameter to the same length as the old hose.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Make certain that the heater hose connections to the block are 
installed correctly and that the heater hoses cannot come in contact with any 
part of the exhaust system, or cannot become pinched or otherwise restricted. 

 NOTE: Refer to Section 12-02 for the correct routing of heater hoses.

Install hose.

Replace coolant.

After the coolant has been replaced, bleed the air from the heater core.

Refill and bleed cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Belt 

 Removal 

Loosen the idler pulley or compressor.

Remove the belt. 

 Installation 

Place the new belt in position, and adjust the belt tension to 
specification using Rotunda Belt Tension Gauge 014-R1056 or equivalent. 
Tighten the idler pulley or compressor. 

Check the belt alignment, and adjust it if necessary.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Compressor 

All compressor replacement operations except belt replacement can be 
performed only after the unit has been relieved of its refrigerant charge. 
Discharge the entire refrigerant system. 

To reduce the amount of time needed to make a compressor replacement, 
the service compressors are dehydrated and the proper amount of the specified 
refrigerant oil is in the crankcase when received. 

When replacing a compressor, first check the oil level in the old 
compressor. Then remove oil from the new compressor in an amount that will 
make the new compressor oil level the same as that in the old compressor. This 
procedure will keep the amount of oil in the system constant. Failure to use 
this procedure is the most common reason for excessive oil in the system. 
Refer to Section 12-00 .

 Removal 

Discharge the system and disconnect the two hoses from the compressor.

Disconnect electrical connectors from the compressor.

Loosen the idler pulley or alternator and remove the drive belt and the 
clutch and then remove the mounting bolts and the compressor. Refer to the 
following illustration. 

 Installation 

Place the compressor on the mounting bracket and install the four 
mounting bolts. Tighten screws to 40-54 Nm (30-40 lb-ft). 

Install the belt and adjust and tighten the idler pulley. Tighten 
compressor mounting bolts.

Connect compressor electrical connectors.

Connect the two hoses to the compressor. Evacuate, charge, and leak 
test the system. Refer to Section 12-00 .

 Air Conditioning Compressor, L- and LN-Series with FD-1060 and FD-1460 
Engines

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C System Filtering

 WARNING: FOLLOW ALL REFRIGERANT SYSTEM SAFETY AND SERVICE PRECAUTIONS. REFER TO 
R-134A REFRIGERANT SYSTEM IN THE DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION PORTION OF THIS 
SECTION. 

An A/C service kit has been released to provide the necessary equipment 
and information to perform the new, mandatory A/C system filtering procedure. 
The filter kit with the service part number suffix "A" is to be used on 
vehicles that have a nylon-lined evaporator-to-compressor suction line between 
the suction accumulator/drier and the A/C compressor. 

[FIGURE: M4546A.gif]

To determine that the A/C compressor has failed and must be replaced, 
remove the A/C evaporator core orifice and condenser-to-evaporator tube, if 
necessary. Look for a dirty A/C evaporator core orifice or a 
condenser-to-evaporator tube containing black refrigerant oil and particles.

Remove the damaged A/C compressor and drain the oil into a calibrated 
container.

Add the proper amount of specified refrigerant oil to the new A/C 
compressor before compressor is installed.

If the amount of oil drained from the removed A/C compressor is between 
85 and 142 ml (3-5 oz), pour the same amount of clean specified refrigerant 
oil into the new A/C compressor.

If the amount of oil drained from the old A/C compressor is greater 
than 142 ml (5 oz), pour only 142 ml (5 oz) of clean specified refrigerant oil 
into the new A/C compressor.

If the amount of refrigerant oil drained from the old A/C compressor is 
less than 85 ml (3 oz), pour 85 ml (3 oz) of clean specified refrigerant oil 
into the new A/C compressor.

 NOTE: It will be necessary to transfer the A/C clutch from the old A/C 
compressor to the new A/C compressor.

Install the new A/C compressor. Check the tension of the drive belt. 
Adjust, if necessary.

Remove the suction accumulator/drier assembly and drain the oil into a 
calibrated container.

Add clean specified refrigerant oil to the new suction 
accumulator/drier in the same amount that was removed from the old unit, plus 
an additional 60 ml (2 oz.) of new refrigerant oil.

Install the suction accumulator/drier in the vehicle.

Obtain the proper service kit for the vehicle on which you are working. 
Filter kits with the service part number suffix A are to be used on vehicles 
with a nylon-lined evaporator-to-compressor suction line. The label on the 
filter shows which evaporator-to-compressor suction line it is to be used with.

[FIGURE: M3730A.gif]

Remove a length of evaporator-to-compressor suction line to accommodate 
the suction filter and install the filter using the clamps provided with the 
kit. Make sure filter is correctly oriented for refrigerant system flow. Check 
the label on the filter. On the filter for nylon-lined 
evaporator-to-compressor suction line, install O-rings (two on each filter 
tube, making sure they are properly seated in the grooves on the tube). 
Tighten the clamps securely.

Install a new A/C evaporator core orifice. The A/C evaporator core 
orifice is located in the condenser-to-evaporator tube between the A/C 
condenser core and the A/C evaporator core. Replace the 
condenser-to-evaporator tube. Refer to Section 12-00 .

Install a pancake filter in the condenser-to-evaporator tube between 
the A/C condenser core and the A/C evaporator core orifice. Make sure the 
filter inlet is toward the A/C condenser core. Connections can be made using 
A/C Test Adapter Set D88P-19703-B or equivalent and flexible refrigerant hose 
of 17,238 kPa (2500 psi) burst rating. Individual fittings are also available.

 Pancake Filter 

[FIGURE: M3878A.gif]

Evacuate, charge and leak test the system.

Check all refrigerant system hoses, lines and the positioning of the 
newly installed filters to ensure they do not interfere with other engine 
compartment components. If necessary, use tie straps to make adjustments.

Provide adequate airflow to the front of the vehicle (with a fan, if 
necessary) and set the air conditioner control at MAX A/C. Set the A/C blower 
motor speed control on HIGH and temperature control at full COOL. Start the 
engine and let it idle briefly. Make sure the A/C system is operating properly.

Gradually bring the engine up to 1200 rpm by running it at lower rpms 
for short periods (first at 800 rpm, then at 1000 rpm). Set the engine at 1200 
rpm and run it for an hour with the A/C system operating.

Stop the engine.

Allow the engine to cool sufficiently to remove the fittings, flexible 
hoses and pancake filter from the condenser-to-evaporator tube. It will be 
necessary to discharge and recover the refrigerant in the system first.

Discard the pancake filter. It can be used one time only.

Reconnect the condenser-to-evaporator tube.

Evacuate, charge and leak test the system. Refer to Section 12-00 . Make 
any necessary adjustments.

Check the operation of the system in all modes.

ADJUSTMENTS

Cables

 Temperature Control Cable 

Verify that a misadjustment exists by performing the following procedure:

Move temperature control lever to full COOL position; note distance 
from lever center to end of slot (count number of detents).

Repeat for full WARM position.

If there is a significant difference between the two observations, an 
adjustment may be necessary.

Locate the cable attachment clip at the case. Do not disengage white 
clip from bracket.

The white clip has a 5-mm (0.2-inch) long rectangular flag which, when 
pulled away from the body of the clip, allows the internal mating plastic bit 
to move in increments of approximately 3 mm (1/8 inch). This movement is used 
to recenter the lever in its slot.

Do not exceed two movement increments from the center position. 
Movement is possible only as long as the flag is pulled back. Once adjustment 
is completed, let go of the flag. Push or pull on conduit to affect 
adjustment. Pushing the conduit toward vehicle right side will result in a 
lever motion toward warm. Pulling the conduit to the vehicle left side will 
result in a lever motion toward cool.

Section 12-03B: Compressor and Clutch, SD-7H15

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Compressor

The SD-7H15 compressor is an axial design compressor with mounting 
brackets for tangential mounting. The compressor shaft is driven by belt from 
the engine accessory drive. The pistons, positioned axially around the 
compressor shaft, are actuated by a swash plate that is pressed on the 
compressor shaft. The swash plate uses the rotating action of the shaft to 
provide a reciprocating driving force to each of the pistons. 

The SD-7H15 has seven cylinders. 

Reed-type suction and discharge valve plates are located between the 
cylinder assembly and the head. 

An integral clutch is used to drive the compressor shaft. When voltage 
is applied to the clutch field coil, the clutch plate and hub assembly (which 
is solidly coupled to the compressor shaft) is drawn by magnetic force toward 
the pulley, which rotates freely on the compressor front head casting. The 
magnetic force locks the clutch plate and hub assembly and the pulley together 
as one unit. The compressor shaft then turns with the pulley. When voltage is 
removed from the clutch field coil, a rubber bushing in the clutch plate and 
hub assembly moves the clutch plate away from the pulley and the compressor 
shaft ceases to rotate.

[FIGURE: K13806D.gif]

19703

A/C Compressor Assy

The air conditioner compressor is equipped with a thermal protection 
switch to automatically shut down operation by interrupting the electrical 
power to the compressor clutch when the compressor temperature exceeds 
approximately 116°C (240°F). The compressor 
will automatically restart when it has cooled to approximately 99°
C (210°F). A CHECK A/C warning light is 
mounted on the instrument panel. Illumination of the CHECK A/C warning light 
is an indication the thermal protection system has been activated and air 
conditioning system service is required. 

This warning is provided to indicate that the system needs service 
(such as low on refrigerant, etc.) and with immediate attention, the potential 
for system damage will be reduced. Continued use of the air conditioning 
system with the warning light indication cycling periodically, can result in 
compressor damage.

[FIGURE: K15232C.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Clutch

 A/C Clutch and A/C Clutch Pulley 

 Removal 

Insert two pins of the front plate spanner into two threaded holes in 
the clutch front plate. 

Hold clutch plate stationary and remove hex nut.

[FIGURE: K138141A.gif]

Using clutch plate puller, align puller center bolt to compressor 
shaft. Tighten three puller bolts into the threaded holes and turn center bolt 
until clutch plate releases from shaft.

[FIGURE: K138151A.gif]

Remove bearing dust cover, using a screwdriver.

[FIGURE: K138161A.gif]

Remove shaft key by lightly tapping it loose with a slotted screwdriver 
and hammer.

[FIGURE: K138171A.gif]

Remove the internal bearing snap ring.

[FIGURE: K138181A.gif]

Remove the external front housing snap ring.

[FIGURE: K13819B.gif]

Insert puller jaws into the snap ring groove. 

Place rotor puller shaft protector over exposed shaft.

[FIGURE: K138201A.gif]

Align thumb head bolts to puller jaws and finger-tighten. 

Tighten center bolt until A/C clutch pulley is removed.

[FIGURE: K13821B.gif]

 Installation 

Support the compressor on the four mounting ears on the rear of the 
compressor. If using a vise, clamp only on mounting ears, not on compressor 
body. 

Align A/C clutch pulley squarely on the front housing hub.

[FIGURE: K13822B.gif]

Using installer ring set, place installer ring into bearing cavity. 
Make certain the outer edge rests firmly on the A/C clutch pulley bearing 
outer race. 

Place set tool driver into ring.

[FIGURE: K138231A.gif]

Tap driver with a hammer while guiding the A/C clutch pulley to prevent 
binding. Tap until the A/C clutch pulley bottoms against the compressor front 
housing hub. 

Install internal bearing snap ring. 

Install external front housing snap ring. 

Install front plate assembly. 

Install compressor shaft key. 

Align front plate keyway to compressor shaft key. 

Using shaft protector, tap front plate to shaft until it bottoms out on 
the shims.

[FIGURE: K138241A.gif]

Install shaft hex nut. Tighten to 34-40 Nm (25-30 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: K138251A.gif]

Check air gap, using a 0.016- to 0.031-inch feeler gauge between hub 
and mating pulley surface in three locations equally spaced around pulley. 
Record air gap readings. 

Rotate compressor pulley one-half turn (180 degrees) and again check 
air gap in three equally spaced locations. Smallest air gap must be within 
specified limits for air gap. Add or remove shims between hub and compressor 
shaft end as necessary until smallest air gap is within specification. 

 A/C Clutch Field Coil 

 Removal 

Remove A/C clutch hub and pulley.

Loosen coil lead wire clip from compressor front housing.

[FIGURE: K138261B.gif]

Remove snap ring and field coil.

[FIGURE: K138271A.gif]

 Installation 

Install field coil and snap ring. 

Tighten clip on field coil lead wire. 

Install pulley and hub on compressor.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Thermal Protection Switch 

 Removal 

Remove the screw securing the thermal protection switch retainer plate 
and lead wire clamp. 

 NOTE: Switch removal may be difficult to accomplish, due to the silicone RTV 
used in switch installation. NEVER reinstall old thermal protection switch. 
ALWAYS replace with a new switch unit, when required. 

Using a small bladed screwdriver, insert blade between switch and 
switch socket and remove switch.

 Installation 

Remove all of the old silicone RTV and thoroughly clean the thermal 
protection switch socket. 

Position the thermal protection switch so that the flat copper surface 
faces upward. Apply a small amount of silicone RTV to the flat copper switch 
surface to ensure outside air temperatures do not affect switch thermal 
sensing ability. 

Install the switch in the mounting socket. Position wire clamp, 
retainer and install retaining screw. Tighten to 5.4-8.1 Nm 
(48-72 lb-in).

A/C Clutch Air Gap

[FIGURE: K138251A.gif]

Check air gap, using a 0.016-0.031-inch feeler gauge between hub and

air gap readings. Air gap should measure between 0.41-0.79 mm (0.016-0.031 
inch).

Rotate compressor pulley one-half turn (180 degrees) and again check 
air gap in three equally spaced locations. Smallest air gap must be within 
specified limits for air gap. Add or remove shims between hub and compressor 
shaft end as necessary until smallest air gap is within specification.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Instrument Cluster and Panel Lighting

The main light switch controls instrument cluster and panel lighting. 
When the main light switch is in the HEAD or PARK position, the battery 
supplies voltage to the instrument cluster and panel illumination lamps. The 
lamps can be dimmed manually with the dimmer switch.

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Level Indication System 

The fuel indicating system for L-Series models is an electromagnetic 
system and consists of a fuel indicator gauge mounted in the instrument 
cluster and a sending unit located in the fuel tank. The system operates 
directly from fused battery voltage and indicates fuel level condition based 
on the variable resistance of the sending unit. 

 Fuel Gauge 

The magnetic gauge movement consists of three primary coils, one of 
which is wound at a 90-degree angle to the other two. The coils form a 
magnetic field which varies in direction according to the variable resistance 
of the sending unit which is connected between two of the coils. A primary 
magnet, to which a shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to align to this 
primary field, resulting in pointer position. 

 NOTE: There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for these 
gauges. 

 Fuel Tank Sending Unit 

The fuel tank sending unit consists of a variable-screened resistor 
made up of a ceramic substrate. It is controlled by the action of an attached 
float in the fuel tank. When the fuel level is low, resistance in the fuel 
tank sending unit is approximately 25 ohms (City) or 240 ohms (Fleet and 
Full). When the fuel level is high, the resistance in the fuel tank sending 
unit is approximately 145 ohms (City) or 34 ohms (Fleet and Full). As the 
float moves from empty to full, the resistance will gradually and continuously 
increase (City) or decrease (Fleet and Full).

================================================================================
PAGE 5696
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster, Conventional

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Coolant Temperature Indication System

The engine coolant temperature indication system is a magnetic gauge 
system. It consists of a magnetic engine coolant temperature gauge mounted in 
the instrument cluster and an engine coolant temperature sender unit.

 Instrument Cluster Temperature Gauge 

The magnetic gauge movement consists of two primary coils, one of which 
is wound at a 90-degree angle to the other. The coils form a magnetic field, 
which varies in direction according to the variable resistance of the sender 
unit which is connected between two of the coils. A primary magnet, to which a 
shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to align to this primary field, 
resulting in pointer position.

 NOTE: There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for the 
gauge. 

 High Coolant Temperature Warning 

This red light will come on to indicate a high engine coolant 
temperature. If the light comes on, operate the engine at a low rpm 
(approximately 1000 rpm) for five minutes, then low idle for 30-60 seconds. 
Stop the engine and let it cool. This procedure allows a hot engine to cool 
gradually. Check the coolant level, following the instructions about care in 
removing the filler cap. Refer to Section 03-03 for cooling system service.

 Water Temperature Indicator Sender Unit 

The water temperature indicator sensor changes resistance according to 
the engine coolant temperature. When the engine temperature is low, resistance 
in the water temperature indicator sensor is approximately 74 ohms (City) or 
550 ohms (Fleet and Full). When the engine temperature is high, resistance in 
the water temperature indicator sensor is approximately 9.7 ohms (City) or 
43.5 ohms (Fleet and Full). As the engine temperature moves from hot to cold, 
the resistance will gradually and continuously increase.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Oil Pressure Indication System

Oil pressure indication system consists of:

low oil pressure warning indicator

oil pressure switch

necessary circuitry

 Low Oil Pressure Warning 

A red indicator lamp glows and a buzzer sounds when the oil pressure is 
below a specified value.

The lamp is connected between the oil pressure switch unit (mounted on 
the engine) and the ignition switch START or RUN feed.

 Oil Pressure Switch 

The oil pressure switch will become a closed circuit when a low 
pressure exists.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charge Indication System

The voltmeter is a gauge that measures the voltage potential at the 
battery to indicate the battery state of charge. The voltmeter is not 
adjustable and must be replaced if inoperative. 

 Battery Voltage Gauge 

Voltage applied across the terminals of the battery voltage gauge 
causes a gauge movement response proportional to the input. This positions the 
gauge pointer to indicate the appropriate voltage.

 NOTE: There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for this 
gauge.

================================================================================
PAGE 5699
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster, Conventional

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Pressure Gauge

This gauge shows the amount of air pressure in the brake system 
(green/primary and red/secondary) in pounds per square inch. When the pressure 
is too low for normal brake operation (less than 414 kPa [
60 psi]), and when the ignition switch lock cylinder is turned to the START or 
RUN positions a warning buzzer sounds and the warning light comes on. All 
vehicles have a dual-pointer air pressure gauge to indicate the pressure in 
each of the two brake circuits.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Speedometer

The speedometer indicates the speed at which the vehicle is moving. The 
vehicle speed is sensed by a speedometer sensor mounted at the output shaft of 
the transmission. A ten- or twelve-position dip switch is necessary for speed 
calibration. Refer to Speedometer Calibration in the Adjustments portion of 
this section.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Odometer

The odometer indicates the total distance the vehicle has been driven.

 Odometer Replacement 

The mileage on replacement speedometer/odometers cannot be reset. If a 
replacement speedometer/odometer is installed, a label recording the vehicle's 
mileage and date at the time of the speedometer/odometer replacement must be 
attached to the driver's door jamb.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Tachometer 

The electric tachometer is standard on L-Series vehicles. The 
instrument features an analog air core meter — movement 
indicating engine speed in revolutions per minute (rpm). The tachometer has 
few moving mechanical parts. 

The tachometer receives an electrical signal from the tachometer sensor 
that is mounted near the flywheel of the engine. 

 NOTE: The tachometer pointer will not return to zero with the key off. This 
should never be interpreted as an inoperative condition. 

There is only one electrical adjustment. An eight-position dip switch 
is necessary for engine calibration. Settings are listed on the tachometer 
case label. Refer to Tachometer Calibration in the Adjustments portion of this 
section.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Indicators

 Brake System 

The brake system warning light should glow when the ignition switch 
lock cylinder is in the START position. With hydraulic brakes, a dual circuit 
(SPLIT) system is used. In case of a loss of hydraulic pressure in either 
brake circuit, the other brake will provide reduced braking capability. If 
this occurs, the BRAKE warning light will illuminate upon the first 
application of the brakes and remain on until hydraulic pressure is restored. 
The brake warning light will also illuminate if there is a malfunction in the 
engine driven hydraulic pump system (in combination with BRAKE E MOTOR light 
and buzzer).

 Anti-Lock Brakes 

The anti-lock brake system uses one amber ABS warning light to alert 
the driver of malfunctions in the system.

The amber ABS warning light will come on for numerous reasons. It warns 
the driver that the ABS has been disabled. Normal power-assisted braking 
remains but the wheels can lock during a panic stop while the indicator is on. 
Certain procedures must be followed to find the concern in this situation. 
Refer to Section 06-09 for diagnosis and testing of the system.

 Check Engine 

The ENG WARN indicator comes on when the electronic engine control 
system is not working properly.

The check engine warning indicator comes on briefly when the ignition 
switch lock cylinder is turned to RUN, and should turn off when the engine 
starts. If the ENG WARN indicator does not come on when the ignition switch 
lock cylinder is turned to RUN or if it comes on while the vehicle is moving, 
the system is malfunctioning.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with dual fuel tanks, the CHECK ENGINE light 
may come on if fuel is restricted to the engine or if the fuel flow is 
momentarily disrupted because of an empty fuel tank before switching to the 
auxiliary fuel tank. This condition is normal and the ENG WARN light should go 
off sometime after fuel flow is restored.

 Low Oil Pressure 

This red light will come on to indicate low engine oil pressure. If the 
light comes on while the engine is running, pull off the road as soon as it is 
safely possible, wait at least five minutes after turning the engine off to 
check oil level when vehicle is on level ground. If level is low, add oil, but 
do not overfill.

 Low Coolant 

All vehicles equipped with diesel engines have a low coolant warning 
system with a red indicator light (with Cummins CELECT this feature is 
incorporated in the engine fluids lamp). If this light comes on, correct the 
low coolant condition immediately, following the instructions about care in 
removing the filler cap. Refer to Section 03-03 for cooling system service.

 High Beam 

The high beam indicator comes on when the headlamps are actuated to the 
high beam position or when the high beam headlamps are flashed.

 LH/RH Turn 

The LH/RH turn signal indicators are located in the instrument cluster. 
If the turn signal indicator light in the instrument cluster does not 
illuminate or remains on (doesn't flash) when a turn is signaled, the turn 
signaling system is malfunctioning. Refer to Section 17-01 for exterior 
lighting system service.

 Water Temperature 

This red light will come on to indicate a high engine coolant 
temperature. If the light comes on, operate the engine at a low rpm 
(approximately 1000 rpm) for five minutes, then low idle for 30-60 seconds. 
Stop the engine and let it cool. This procedure allows a hot engine to cool 
gradually. Check the coolant level, following the instructions about care in 
removing the filler cap. Refer to Section 03-03 for cooling system service.

 Transmission Temperature/Check Transmission 

This light comes on to indicate maximum transmission-to-cooler oil 
temperature of 149°C (300°F). Should the 
light come on, stop the vehicle and shift the transmission to neutral. 
Accelerate the engine to 1200-1500 rpm to allow the transmission to return to 
normal temperature, 71-104°C (160-220°F) 
before resuming operation. Check transmission oil level.

 Wait to Start 

When this indicator is illuminated, it indicates the air intake (inlet 
manifold) heater is in operation.

 Check A/C 

This amber warning light is used on vehicles equipped with air 
conditioning systems to monitor and evaluate A/C compressor operating 
temperatures and shut the A/C system off if the temperature gets too high. If 
the in-cab warning light comes on while you are driving, it indicates that the 
compressor is shut off and there is a need for service. The A/C compressor 
will restart when the operating temperature returns to within the normal range.

 Brake Electric Motor 

Activation of the brake electric motor warning light and buzzer alert 
the operator to the operating condition of the reserve pump motor. With the 
engine running, the brake electric motor light and buzzer should not be on. If 
either the brake electric motor light illuminates and/or the buzzer sounds 
when the engine is running, the brake system is malfunctioning. Stop the 
vehicle safely as soon as possible, and seek service immediately. The brake 
electric motor warning light and buzzer should activate when the engine is off 
and the brakes applied, and when the ignition switch lock cylinder is in the 
START position.

 Low Air 

Vehicles with air brakes are equipped with a low air pressure warning 
buzzer. The air brake systems are split or dual systems. If there is a loss of 
air pressure to either system, to a level below 414 kPa (60 psi) the buzzer 
will sound. The remaining brake system is capable of stopping the vehicle. 
However, the stopping distance will be greater.

 Differential Lock 

This red indicator light will come on when the differential lockout 
control and/or wheel to wheel lock is in the LOCK position to indicate that 
the lockout mechanism in the tandem rear axle is engaged to provide extra 
traction, or if the single axle wheel lock is engaged.

 Do Not Shift 

If this light illuminates (accompanied by eight seconds of short beeps 
from the shift selector) while the vehicle is in operation, it indicates that 
the transmission operating parameters have been exceeded and that the shifts 
are being restricted (i.e., upshifts and downshifts may be restricted). Also, 
the SELECT digit on the shifter display will be blank. A diagnostic code will 
be recorded. If this should happen, the transmission will continue to operate. 
If the vehicle is equipped with shift lever and the lever is moved, a 
continuous alarm will be sounded until the original shift lever position has 
been restored. If equipped with a push-button shifter, it will not accept new 
commands.

 Oil Temp 

This red warning light will come on to indicate a high engine oil 
temperature. If the light comes on while the engine is running, stop the 
engine and correct the cause of high temperature immediately.

 Stop Engine 

This warning lamp is used in conjunction with the electronic engine 
control and will indicate one of the following conditions is present: low oil 
pressure, low coolant level, or high coolant temperature.

 Engine Fluids 

If this red light comes on it could mean one or more of the following: 
high engine oil temperature, high engine coolant temperature or low oil 
pressure. If this light comes on, stop the engine and correct the cause 
immediately.

 Parking Brake (Park) 

On vehicles with a hydraulic brake system the parking brake light will 
illuminate when the parking brakes are applied, and momentarily when the 
ignition switch lock cylinder is in the START position. Upon actuation of the 
parking brake, a buzzer will sound until brakes are fully applied.

 Daytime Running Lamps 

If this amber warning lamp is on, it indicates the high beam headlamps 
(Canadian DRL) or low beam headlamps (U.S.A. DRL) are illuminated at reduced 
intensity for daytime driving. Refer to Section 17-04 for more information on 
the Daytime Running Lamp system.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Instrument Cluster

 Inspection and Verification 

Visually inspect the components. Check for damaged components, blown 
fuses, loose or corroded connections. Check the wiring harness for obvious 
signs of shorts, opens, bad connections or damage.

Verify circuit operation. Verify speedometer and odometer operation by 
road testing the vehicle.

 Symptom Chart — Instrument Cluster Diagnosis 

Refer to the Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual for the 
connector numbers in the pinpoint tests.

Possible Source

Action

unit arm gently to correct position.

Improper fuel gauge sensor unit calibration.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Instrument Cluster

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery ground cable. 

Remove the instrument cluster retaining screws, tilt cluster toward the 
steering column and disconnect the speedometer and cluster/gauge electrical 
connectors. 

Disconnect all wiring connectors and air or oil lines, if so equipped, 
and remove the cluster assembly.

 Installation 

Position the instrument cluster assembly to the instrument panel and 
connect all wiring connectors and air or oil lines, if so equipped. 

Make sure that all wiring is moved away from the instrument panel 
opening. Install the instrument cluster assembly to the instrument panel with 
the retaining screws. 

Connect the battery ground cable. 

Check the operation of all gauges, lamps and signals.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Gauge, City Delivery 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable. Remove instrument cluster. 

Remove electrical connectors from back of cluster. Remove oil pressure 
tube, if necessary. 

Remove four screws that secure cluster to the finish plate. 

Carefully remove glass and gauge bezel from front of cluster. 

Remove the two gauge attaching screws and remove fuel gauge assembly. 

[FIGURE: K10519C.gif]

 Installation 

Position fuel gauge assembly in cluster housing. Verify that the three 
electrical contact clips are snapped in cluster. 

Secure fuel gauge using two attaching screws. Verify that fuel gauge 
pins are in contact with snap-in clips. 

Install glass and gauge bezel on finish plate and secure with four 
attaching screws. 

Connect all electrical connectors, and connect oil pressure tube, if 
removed. 

Install the instrument cluster assembly. 

Connect battery ground cable and check operation of fuel gauge.

 Removal

[FIGURE: K10519C.gif]

[FIGURE: K10518C.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Instrument Cluster Lenses

 CAUTION: The use of vinyl cleaners and other similar cleaning agents to clean 
the vehicle interior and/or instrument cluster lenses has resulted in damage 
to the instrument cluster lenses. The chemical content of these cleaning 
agents (O-dichlorobenzene, ethyl alcohol and/or cellosolve), has produced 
fogging, spotting, stain, or splotches of the lenses, either through overspray 
or direct use on the lenses. Therefore, extreme caution should be taken during 
interior cleanup to prevent overspray of cleaning agents which contain the 
chemical contents mentioned from contacting the instrument cluster lenses. 

 CAUTION: The instrument cluster lenses should be cleaned with Ultra Clear Spray 
Glass Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESR-M14P5-A using a clean, soft, lint-free cloth. The Ford Glass Cleaner has 
been specially formulated for cleaning windows in automotive vehicles and is 
approved for use in cleaning the plastic instrument cluster lenses. Follow the 
directions on the container for best results.

ADJUSTMENTS

Tachometer Calibration 

The tachometer is calibrated according to engine type, specifically, 
the number of flywheel teeth. The tachometer can be calibrated by setting 
eight dip switches on back of the tachometer. The switches have the numbers 1 
through 8 embossed on the switch. To calibrate the tachometer, the switches 
are set so each switch is either in the ON or OFF position, depending on the 
engine type. A switch is set to the ON position when the switch is depressed 
towards the number on top of the switch. A switch is set to the OFF position 
when the switch is depressed at the bottom of the switch, away from the switch 
number. (Settings are listed on the tachometer case label.) 

[FIGURE: K19634A.gif]

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster, Conventional

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Speedometer Calibration

To assure that the electronic speedometer system operates accurately, 
periodic inspection of the vehicle speedometer sensor is necessary. The 
speedometer sensor is to be inspected for metal filings accumulating on the 
sensor pole face at the following kilometer (mileage) intervals: 800 (500), 
20,000 (12,500), 40,000 (25,000), 60,000 (37,500), 80,000 (50,000). Scheduled 
maintenance beyond 80,000 kilometer (50,000 mile) should occur at subsequent 
80,000 kilometer (50,000 mile) intervals. Metal filings that have developed on 
the speedometer sensor pole face must be removed to maintain system integrity. 
The programmable electronic speedometer instrument requires no maintenance.

The electronic speedometer is calibrated by rocker switches on the back 
of the speedometer. The following procedure describes how to calculate the 
speedometer calibration frequency and set the speedometer rocker switches. The 
bank of switches that are located at the rear of the electronic speedometers 
require setting for proper operation of the speedometer and odometer unit. The 
transmission-mounted speed sensor transmits a signal to the 
speedometer/odometer which is dependent on:

rear axle ratio.

tire revolutions per mile (RPMi), which is based on tire height.

 Rear Axle Differential Ratio 

The axle ratio can be determined by referring to the information 
delivered with the vehicle or finding the metal tag attached to the 
differential. If the vehicle has a two-speed differential (e.g., 4.15/5.72:1), 
use the smaller number (4.15 in this case) in all calculations.

 Tire Size 

The revolutions per mile can be calculated as follows:

Measure the tire height (ground to top of tire) in inches with the 
vehicle on level ground, loaded, with the tires cold and inflated to the 
recommended pressure. Measure to the nearest 1/8 inch. Use the following table 
to convert eighths to decimal. (If calculation is done in centimeters, divide 
tire height by 2.54 to convert to inches).

Example: If tire height is 36-1/8 inch, use 36.125 in your revolutions 
per mile calculation.

Fraction

Decimal

1/8

0.125

1/4

0.25

3/8

0.375

1/2

0.5

5/8

0.625

3/4

0.75

7/8

0.875

Divide 20,168 (constant) by the tire height to get the revolutions per 
mile.

Example: 20,168 / 36.125 = 558.28

 Calibration Frequency 

Multiply the axle ratio times the revolutions per mile times 0.267 
(constant)

Example: 558.28 x 4.10 x 0.267 = 611.49 Round the 611.49 to the closest 
whole number, which is 611.

 Calibration Testing 

Determine which type speedometer/odometer you are installing. The 
following procedure applies for both stand-alone and gauge cluster type 
speedometer/odometer units. Replacement units are either the 12-switch Beede 
or 10-switch Ametek type. The 10-switch Beede has been discontinued for service.

If the unit you are calibrating is a 10-switch type, determine if it is 
an Ametek or Beede by looking at the type of electrical connection on the 
back. The Beede has four studs, while the Ametek has a single plug-in type 
connector. If your 10-switch Beede is replaced with a 10-switch Ametek, a 
simple electrical jumper wire will be included with the new speedometer.

There are two speedometer setting charts (Ametek 10-position and Beede 
12-position). Using the correct speedometer setting chart (attached), find the 
"Test Freq" in the left-hand column and read the switch settings in the next 
column. A number means that switch is to be placed in the ON or closed 
position and a period (.) means that switch is to be placed in the OFF or open 
position (e.g., using the Beede 12-Position chart and the 611 test frequency 
calculated in the example, the chart gives the switch settings as : 
(1.3456.8.0.B). This means that switches 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 are ON and 
switches 2, 7, 9, 11 are OFF. The letters A and B are used to represent 
switches 11 and 12. There are at least three different styles of switches with 
unique switch position labeling. Ignore the switch position labeling. Pushing 
the top of the switch IN turns the switch ON. Pushing the bottom of the switch 
IN turns the switch OFF.

ESB-M1C158-A.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Horn Contacts

The horn contacts are mounted to the steering column horn contact 
housing.

 Removal 

Remove bolt and lockwasher from horn contact housing using a 1/4-inch 
12-point socket.

Remove two screws from horn contact housing using a T25 Torx®
 socket.

Remove horn contact housing, horn contact assembly and horn wire.

[FIGURE: G7228C.gif]

 Installation 

Position horn contact housing onto jacket tube and align its bolt hole 
with the tapped jacket tube bolt hole that is in line with the tilt lever.

Install bolt and lockwasher finger-tight. Tighten bolt to 8-13 Nm
 (71-115 lb-in) using a 1/4-inch 12-point socket, after 
steering wheel is installed and horn contact housing is adjusted.

Adjust housing to 2.38-mm (0.094-inch) gap at steering wheel skirt.

Install upper end of horn wire assembly into horn contact housing wire 
hole from lower end and attach the two horn wire terminals to horn contact 
assembly terminals.

Attach horn contact assembly to turn signal housing with two screws. 
Tighten screws to 4-5 Nm (35-44 lb-in) using a T25 Torx®
 socket.

Section 13-09: Engine Protection System

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Protection System Components

The engine protection system (or engine shutdown system) is designed to 
prevent engine damage resulting from operation of the engine during prolonged 
periods of low oil pressure, high coolant temperature or low coolant level.

Switches or sensors provide information to the system's electronic 
engine alarm/shutdown module. When one of the monitored engine systems is not 
functioning properly, a warning lamp in the instrument panel will illuminate. 
Warning lamps are provided for the following:

low oil pressure

high coolant temperature

low coolant level

The low oil pressure, high coolant temperature, and low coolant level 
warning lamps are accompanied by an audible warning. In vehicles equipped with 
the engine shutdown option, the audible warning will be heard with the warning 
lamp illumination and, after 30-40 seconds, the engine will stop running. The 
30-40 second delay is provided to allow removal of the vehicle from the road. 
After the engine stops running, it can be restarted and operated for 
approximately 30-40 seconds more. There is no limit to how many times the 
shutdown system will allow the engine to be restarted. This feature is only 
provided to allow the vehicle to be driven off the road. Any attempt to use 
this feature to drive the vehicle very far will result in serious engine damage.

The engine protection and shutdown system consists of the following 
components:

Indicator lamps in the instrument panel for the following warnings:

low oil pressure

high coolant temperature

low coolant level

Oil pressure switch, located on the left side of engine.

Coolant temperature indicator switch, located on the right side of 
engine.

Low coolant level sensor, mounted in the radiator coolant supply tank.

Fuel shutoff relay.

Engine alarm/shutdown module.
