REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Lamps, Front Marker

To replace the marker lamp or bulb, remove three (or four [
depending on lamp]) screws and remove the lens from the 
lamp body. 

Press the bulb in and turn counterclockwise to remove it from the 
socket. After installing the new bulb, install the lens and retaining screws. 

To remove the lamp body, disconnect the lead wire at the connector 
plug, remove the mounting nuts from the two mounting studs and withdraw the 
lamp and wire assembly from the vehicle. 

The plug connection comes out of a wiring harness on the inner side of 
the dash panel. The wire has to be drawn through a grommet in the floorpan.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Indicator Flasher 

When replacing a flasher unit, be sure to install a new flasher unit 
having the same color code and number as the one removed.

Do not replace turn signal switch or wiring if: 

turn signal lamps do not flash on demand with ignition switch in lock 
cylinder RUN, and 

turn signal flasher makes normal pulsing noise, and 

turn signal lamps prove satisfactory when bench-tested or checked by 
activating brake stoplamp switch for rear only. 

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery ground cable.

Remove the screws retaining the flasher unit.

Disconnect the push-on terminals and remove the flasher unit.

 Installation 

To install, position the flasher unit in fuse panel (City Delivery) or 
to instrument panel near fuse or circuit breaker panel (all other models).

Connect the push-on connections.

Connect the battery ground cable. 

Check for power at the turn signal flasher output connector (pulsing 
noise indicates power is coming into the flasher). 

If there is no power or very weak power at the flasher output connector 
(12-volt test lamp will not light or is dim), replace the turn signal flasher.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Headlamps

Clean headlamp by spraying with Ford Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner 
E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P5-A and wiping 
with a clean, soft cloth.

Visually inspect the headlamp for damage. If the headlamp is found to 
be damaged, replace it. Refer to Headlamp Bulb, except Aeromax or Headlamp 
Bulb, Aeromax in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Headlamp 

Headlamp aim adjustment should be made with the Rotunda Headlamp Aiming 
Kit 196-00001 or equivalent. Use the latest instructions. The kit equipment 
can be calibrated to accommodate a slight slope in the floor.

The high beam is automatically adjusted when the low beam is adjusted. 

Before making any headlamp adjustments, perform the following 
preparatory steps: 

Remove ice or mud from underhood assembly fender area (or wheel 
housing). 

Make sure all tires are inflated to recommended pressures. 

Check springs for sag or broken leaves. 

Take into consideration faulty wheel alignment or improper tracking of 
the rear axle. 

Make sure there is no load in the vehicle other than the fuel tank 
one-half full. 

Check hood for correct locked down position and make sure hood latches 
are secure. 

Clean lenses and aiming pads. 

Check for bulb burn-out and proper beam switching. 

Make sure that light output is well toward normal new lamp value. 

 NOTE: Always bring each beam into final position by turning adjusting screws 
clockwise so that headlamp will be held against the tension springs when the 
operation is completed. 

When setup requirements are satisfied, perform the following steps for 
headlamp adjustment: 

Right headlamp: cover left headlamp and turn headlamps on in low beam 
position. 

Horizontal adjustment: turn adjustment screw (B) at left of sealed beam 
retainer ring. Clockwise moves the beam to the right. Counterclockwise moves 
the beam to the left. 

Vertical adjustment: turn adjustment screw (A) at top of sealed beam 
retainer ring. Clockwise moves the beam upward. Counterclockwise moves the 
beam downward. 

Turn off headlamps, allow lamps to cool, and remove left headlamp cover.

[FIGURE: K90631A.gif]

Left headlamps: cover the right headlamp and turn headlamps on in low 
beam position. 

Horizontal adjustment: turn adjustment screw (C) at right of sealed 
beam retainer ring. Clockwise moves the beam to the left. Counterclockwise 
moves the beam to the right. 

Vertical adjustment: turn adjustment screw (A) at top of sealed beam 
retainer ring. Clockwise moves the beam upward. Counterclockwise moves the 
beam downward. 

Turn off headlamps, allow lamps to cool, and remove right headlamp cover.

[FIGURE: K90641A.gif]

Section 17-04: Lamps, Daytime Running

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Daytime Running Lamp (DRL) System, Canadian Vehicles 

The daytime running lamp (DRL) system is designed to turn the high beam 
headlamps on (or the low beam headlamps, in the case of LL/LTL vehicles), with 
a reduced light output, and without illuminating the high beam indicator lamp 
in the instrument panel when the following conditions are met: 

The vehicle is running. 

The parking brake is fully released. 

The headlamp switch is in the OFF or PARK position. 

The daytime running lamps (DRL) control module is grounded through the 
low beam input when the DRL system is active.

 NOTE: When the DRL system is active, the pulsed voltage on the high beam 
circuit cannot be measured accurately. If the low beam headlamps are 
inoperative, refer to Section 17-01 .

================================================================================
PAGE 5873
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 17-04: Lamps, Daytime Running

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Daytime Running Lamp (DRL) System, U.S. Vehicles

The daytime running lamp (DRL) system is designed to turn the low beam 
headlamps on at a reduced light output when the following conditions are met:

The vehicle is running.

The parking brake is fully released.

The headlamp switch is in the OFF or PARK position.

The daytime running lamps (DRL) control module is grounded through the 
high beam input when the DRL system is active.

 NOTE: When the DRL system is active, the pulsed voltage on the low beam 
circuit cannot be measured accurately. If the high beam headlamps are 
inoperative, refer to Section 17-01 .

 Is battery voltage present?

Yes

No

 .

 C147

 A8 CHECK HIGH BEAM INDICATOR (CANADA)

connector 
 C147
 (City) or connector 
 C2061

 Did high beam indicator illuminate?

Yes

No

 .

 A9 CHECK PARKING BRAKE SWITCH 

With daytime running lamps control module removed, turn all accessories 
to the OFF position.

daytime running lamps control module connector 
 C147
 (City) or connector 
 C2061
 (Fleet and Full — LL and LTL) or

 C2068
 (Fleet and Full — except LL and

Yes

No

GO to A10 
 .

SERVICE ground connection at parking brake switch or SERVICE Circuit 
162 (GN/R) for an open or a short or REPLACE parking brake switch. RESTORE 
vehicle. RETEST system.

 A10 RECHECK DAYTIME RUNNING LAMPS CONTROL MODULE 

Reinstall daytime running lamps control module.

Key to RUN.

Parking brake fully released.

Headlamp switch OFF or in the PARK position.

 Are the high beams (low beams U.S.) on at reduced intensity?

Yes

No

System is functioning properly. No service required.

system.

 Removal

 Installation

module or DRL resistor assembly.

Install the two retaining screws that secure daytime running lamps 
control module or DRL resistor to bracket and tighten.

For engine identification and adjustment information, a label, or 
dataplate, is attached to the side of the front gear housing in front of the 
fuel pump. Always refer to the label when replacement parts are required or 
when checking engine calibrations. Some engine parts may vary with engine 
application and vehicle type. The identification codes will make sure that the 
proper parts are obtained. The codes contain all pertinent information 
relating to dates, optional equipment and revisions. The Ford Master Parts 
Catalog contains a complete listing of the codes and their application. In 
addition, there is an engine serial number located on a pad at the lower right 
side of the block.

[FIGURE: A17169A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 6160
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cylinder Head

The cylinder head is a one-piece, crossflow design with two valves per 
cylinder. The head has integrally cast valve guides and hardened valve seat 
surfaces which can be serviced using the appropriate service parts. 

The cylinder head has a cast intake manifold, fuel filter head, 
thermostat housing and an internal water bypass. The injectors are mounted in 
the head for direct injection into the cylinders. Separate pedestals for each 
cylinder are used to support and route oil to the rocker levers. 

The cylinder head gasket is a laminated design with print-o-seal on 
both sides around the water holes. A fire ring in the gasket seals the 
cylinder bores. The gasket also provides orifices to control coolant 
circulation past and around the cylinder bores.

================================================================================
PAGE 6161
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Manifolds

The intake manifold is integral with the cylinder head. The exhaust 
manifold mounts to the right side of the cylinder head and is designed to 
maintain exhaust velocity to provide maximum input to the turbocharger. 
Exhaust exits via the exhaust pipe, through the muffler and tail pipe.

================================================================================
PAGE 6162
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Exhaust Brake 

 CAUTION: Exceeding maximum exhaust pressure will result in engine damage. 

The following guidelines must be followed when installing an exhaust 
brake on Ford FD-1060 diesel engines or the warranty may be voided.

Exhaust brake assembly must be mounted a minimum of 1.7 meters (5.5 
feet) downstream from the turbocharger. 

Maximum allowable exhaust back pressure is 35 psi for blue striped 
standard exhaust valve springs (36 psi for white standard exhaust valve 
springs), and 60 psi for white striped heavy-duty exhaust valve springs, all 
at 2750 rpm.

================================================================================
PAGE 6163
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cylinder Block

The cylinder block has provisions for the oil cooler housing, 
thermostat seats, coolant bypass line, water pump volute, oil pump housing, 
water pump inlet and bored piston cylinders with spacing between cylinders to 
provide room for dry liners, if needed for service. 

The six-cylinder crankshaft is a balanced, forged steel, full fillet 
hardened unit with seven main bearing journals. The lower crankshaft main 
bearing halves are all the same. All of the upper crankshaft main bearing 
halves are the same except for the No. 6 journal which uses a flanged upper 
bearing shell. The flanges on the bearing shell control the end thrust of the 
crankshaft. Oversize main bearings and thrust bearings are available for 
service. 

All crankshaft seals are the Teflon® lay-down lip 
(scroll) type. The Teflon® lay-down lip type seal does not 
contain a spring on the back of the sealing lip. The sealing lip is a thin, 
stiff piece of Teflon®. 

Teflon® seals must be dry before installation. Do not 
lubricate the seal lip or the shaft. After the first few turns of the shaft, a 
thin film of Teflon® is transferred from the seal lip to the 
shaft. If the shaft is not clean and dry, this transfer will not occur and the 
seal will leak. 

The pistons have a cast aluminum body, high swirl combustion bowl and 
three ring grooves. The top ring groove has a ni-resist insert with a Keystone 
profile. The piston pin end of the connecting rod is angle cut to provide 
additional bearing surface. The rod end is fitted with a bronze bushing. Steel 
backed tri-metal bearings are used in production for the additional loading 
resulting from turbocharging and aftercooling. 

Oversize service rod bearings are available for use with reground 
crankshafts. 

A free-floating, hollow piston pin is used to attach the piston to the 
connecting rod. Lubrication of the pin and journal is accomplished by residual 
spray from piston cooling. 

The camshaft is gear driven from the crankshaft. A replaceable bushing 
is used for the front journal to carry the side loading from the accessory 
drive. The remainder of the journals operate in cast iron bores in the 
cylinder block. The camshaft has lobes to operate the intake and exhaust 
valves and a special lobe to drive the lift pump. The camshaft lobes contact 
mushroom-shaped valve tappets which operate the push rods. The operating arm 
of the lift pump rides directly on the special lobe on the camshaft.

================================================================================
PAGE 6164
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lubrication System 

 Lubricating System Flow 

[FIGURE: A17164A.gif]

 Lubricating Oil Pump 

FD-1060 engines use a gerotor-type lubricating oil pump (1) located in 
the lower right area of the front face of the block.

 Pressure Regulating Valve 

The pressure regulating valve (2) is designed to keep the oil pressure 
from exceeding 483 kPa (70 psi). When the oil pressure from the pump is 
greater than 483 kPa (70 psi), the pressure regulating valve opens uncovering 
the dump port so part of the oil is routed to the oil pan. Because of 
manufacturing tolerances of the components and the oil passages, the oil 
pressure can differ between engines. 

 Oil Cooler 

The engine uses full flow, plate-type lubricating oil coolers (3). The 
oil flows through a cast passage in the cooler cover and through the element 
where it is cooled by engine coolant flowing past the plates of the element. 
The six-cylinder engine uses an element with seven plates. 

 Oil Filters 

After the oil is cooled, it flows through the full flow filter (4). 

 Oil Filter Bypass Valve 

The oil cooler cover contains an oil filter bypass valve (5) that will 
let the oil flow bypass a plugged filter. The oil filter bypass valve is 
designed to open when the pressure drop across the filter is more than 172 kPa 
(25 psi), as with a plugged filter, and lets the oil continue on through the 
engine. When a filter becomes plugged, an oil pressure decrease of 60 kPa (10 
psi) or less from the normal operating pressure can be observed on the vehicle 
oil pressure gauge. 

 Lubrication for the Turbocharger 

The turbocharger receives filtered, cooled and pressurized lubricating 
oil through a supply line from the oil filter head. A drain line connected to 
the bottom of the turbocharger housing returns the oil to the oil pan through 
a fitting in the cylinder block. 

 Turbocharger Lubrication 

[FIGURE: A17165A.gif]

 Lubrication for the Power Components 

The main bearings and the valve train are lubricated by pressurized oil 
directly from the main oil rifle. The other power components, connecting rods, 
pistons, and camshaft receive pressurized oil indirectly from the main oil 
rifle. 

The drillings in the crankshaft supply oil to the connecting rod 
bearings. The oil is supplied to the camshaft journals through drillings in 
the crankshaft main bearing saddle. Smaller drillings in the crankshaft main 
bearing saddle supply oil to the piston cooling nozzles. The spray from the 
nozzles provides cooling for the pistons and also provides lubrication for the 
piston pins. 

The number one crankshaft main bearing saddle does not contain a piston 
cooling nozzle. Cylinder No. 1 receives the lubricating and cooling spray from 
the nozzle located in the No. 2 crankshaft main bearing saddle. Cylinder No. 2 
receives the spray from the No. 3 crankshaft main bearing saddle, etc. 

 Power Component Lubrication

 Lubrication for the Overhead 

Lubrication for the valve train is supplied through separate drillings 
in the cylinder block. The oil flows through the drillings and across the oil 
transfer slot in the cylinder head gasket. From the transfer slot, the oil 
flows around the outside diameter at the cylinder head capscrew, across a slot 
in the bottom of the rocker lever support, and up a vertical drilling in the 
support. From these drillings, oil flows through drillings in the rocker lever 
shaft to lubricate the rocker levers. Oil flows through a drilling in the 
rocker levers to fill a channel cast into the top of the levers. The oil from 
the channel lubricates the intake and exhaust valve stems, push rods and 
tappets.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cooling System 

Coolant is drawn from the radiator by the integrally mounted water 
pump. The output from the water pump empties into the oil cooler cavity of the 
cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A21465A.gif]

The coolant then circulates around each cylinder and crosses the block 
to the fuel pump side of the engine.

[FIGURE: A21466A.gif]

Coolant then flows up into the cylinder head, crosses over the valve 
bridges and down the exhaust manifold side of the engine to the integral 
thermostat housing.

[FIGURE: A21467A.gif]

As the coolant flows across the head toward the thermostat housing, it 
provides cooling for the injector nozzle. When the engine is below operating 
temperature, the thermostat is closed, and the coolant flow bypasses the 
radiator and goes to the water pump inlet via internal drillings in the block 
and cylinder head.

[FIGURE: A21468A.gif]

Bypass Closed

6

—

Coolant Flow Back to Radiator

 CAUTION: Never operate the engine without a thermostat. Without a thermostat, 
the coolant will not flow to the radiator and the engine will overheat. 

When operating temperature is reached, the thermostat opens, blocking 
the bypass passage to the water pump and opening the outlet to the radiator.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air System 

Air is pulled into the engine from an air filter. Clean air is very 
important to the life of the engine. Ingested dust and dirt can damage the 
cylinders very quickly. 

On turbocharged engines, the intake air flow is from the air cleaner to 
the turbocharger and then routed to the charge air cooler located in front of 
the radiator. Air leaves the charge air cooler and is routed to the intake 
manifold where it is forced into the cylinders and used for combustion. The 
cooler reduces the temperature of the air, which lowers combustion chamber 
temperatures, and in turn reduces NOx emissions. Also, cooling the air makes 
it more dense allowing more fuel to be injected into the engine to increase 
the power-to-weight ratio.

 Removal

 Removal

Connect the air duct assembly to the turbocharger inlet.

Install the air cleaner assembly.

Fill the cooling system.

Connect the battery ground cable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Valve Spring, Valve Spring Retainer and Valve Stem Seal

Broken valve springs or damaged valve stem seals and retainers may be 
replaced without removing the cylinder head, provided damage to the valve or 
valve seal has not occurred.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Valve Spring Compressor

T83T-6513-A

 Removal 

Remove the valve cover and rocker arm assembly.

Remove the fuel injectors.

Install an air line using the Compression Test Adapter D92T-6600-A or 
equivalent in the injector nozzle hole and turn on the air supply.

 CAUTION: Take care not to drive the valve into the piston. Doing so could damage 
the valve and/or piston. Make sure the piston is not at TDC when loosening the 
retainers from the locks. 

 NOTE: It may be necessary to break the retainer loose from the valve locks. 
This can be done by tapping the edge of the retainer with a plastic hammer or 
by placing a socket (of approximately the same outside diameter) on the 
retainer and tapping the socket with a plastic hammer. Do not strike the tip 
of the valve stem.

Use Valve Spring Compressor T83T-6513-A to compress the valve spring.

[FIGURE: A21985A.gif]

Use a pencil magnet to remove the valve collets. Discard the valve 
collets.

Slowly release the pressure on the valve spring.

Remove the valve spring retainer and the valve spring.

Remove the valve spring seat/valve seal assembly.

 NOTE: If air pressure has forced the piston to the bottom of the cylinder, 
any removal of air pressure will allow the valve(s) to fall into the cylinder. 
A rubber band, tape or string wrapped around the end of the valve stem will 
prevent this condition and will still allow enough travel to check the valve 
for binding.

Remove the valve stem seal.

[FIGURE: A90331A.gif]

[FIGURE: A23419A.gif]

 Installation 

Inspect the cylinder head and valve assembly as described in this 
section. Inspect the valve stem for damage. Rotate the valve and check valve 
stem tip for eccentric (out-of-round) movement. Check for binding by moving 
the valve up and down through its normal travel in the valve guide checking 
for binds. If valve has been damaged, it will be necessary to remove cylinder 
head for service. Inspect the retainer locks for excessive wear, and replace 
in pairs, as necessary.

If the valve is OK, hold it in the closed position and apply air 
pressure within the cylinder. This will hold the valve in the closed position.

Lubricate the valve stem with recommended quality engine oil.

Install the valve spring seat/valve seal assembly over the valve stem. 
To prevent oil carry-over, the seals are color coded and must be installed as 
follows:

Exhaust valve: orange (with 64 grooves per inch)

Intake valve: black (with 40 grooves per inch)

[FIGURE: A18316A.gif]

Install the valve springs.

Install the valve spring retainers.

[FIGURE: A18317A.gif]

Use Valve Spring Compressor T83T-6513-A to compress the valve springs.

[FIGURE: A21985A.gif]

 NOTE: Use new valve spring retainer collets when rebuilding the cylinder head.

Install the new valve spring retainer collets.

 WARNING: WEAR EYE PROTECTION. IF THE COLLETS ARE NOT CORRECTLY INSTALLED, THEY 
CAN FLY OUT WHEN THE STEMS ARE HIT WITH A HAMMER. 

Use a plastic hammer to gently hit the top of the valve stems to make 
sure the valve collets are correctly seated in the spring retainer.

[FIGURE: A18319A.gif]

Remove the compressor tool. Turn off the air and remove the air line 
adapter.

Install the rocker arm assembly, push rods and valve cover.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Oil Seal, Crankshaft, Front 

 Removal 

 NOTE: Removal is easier if the crankshaft pulley is loosened before removing 
the belt. 

Remove the drive belt.

[FIGURE: A17366A.gif]

Remove the crankshaft pulley.

[FIGURE: A17373A.gif]

Remove the front cover.

[FIGURE: A17374A.gif]

Remove the oil seal from the front cover. Drive the oil seal from the 
back side of the cover toward the front side of the cover, while supporting 
the front cover.

[FIGURE: A17375A.gif]

Clean the crankshaft front seal bore in the front cover and the 
crankshaft surface free of all oil and crankshaft front seal residue.

[FIGURE: A17376A.gif]

 NOTE: If the crankshaft has excessive wear, a service wear sleeve is

Inspect the crankshaft for excessive wear.

[FIGURE: A17377A.gif]

Clean the gasket sealing surfaces of the block and front cover of all

 Installation 

Apply a bead of Loctite® 227 or equivalent to the 
outside diameter of the seal.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the crankshaft front seal carrier, hit the 
installation tool alternately at the 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock positions. 

Use the installation tool and a hammer to install the seal to the 
correct depth while supporting the back side of the cover.

[FIGURE: A17379A.gif]

 CAUTION: Always use a seal pilot when installing a seal. 

Install the pilot from the seal kit onto the crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A17380A.gif]

Install the front cover and gasket, making sure the seal slides over 
the pilot. Remove the pilot.

[FIGURE: A17381A.gif]

Install the front cover mounting capscrews and tighten to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17382A.gif]

Install the crankshaft pulley. Do not tighten the capscrews to the 
correct torque value at this time.

[FIGURE: A17367A.gif]

Install the drive belt. Check torque of belt tensioner mounting bolts. 
Correct torque value is 43 Nm (32 lb-ft).

Tighten the crankshaft vibration damper capscrews to 119-131 Nm
 (89-96 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17383A.gif]

 Wear Sleeve, Front Crankshaft Replacement 

 Removal 

Remove the fan drive belt, vibration damper, gear cover and seal. Refer 
to Oil Seal, Crankshaft, Front 
in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 CAUTION: Do not nick or gouge the crankshaft with the chisel. If the crankshaft 
is damaged, it must be replaced. 

Use a hammer and dull chisel only as wide as the wear sleeve. Make one 
or two soft blows across the wear sleeve. This will expand the wear sleeve 
allowing the sleeve to be removed.

[FIGURE: A23643A.gif]

Clean and inspect the crankshaft at the oil seal area for dirt, nicks, 
chisel marks, scratches, rust or corrosion, or other damage that would prevent 
a proper wear sleeve installation.

 Installation 

Use Cummins Engine Company Part No. 3823908, Crankshaft Front Wear 
Sleeve Installation Tool, to install the wear sleeve to the correct position 
on the crankshaft.

 Crankshaft Front Wear Sleeve Installation Tool 

[FIGURE: A23644A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Spacer (Part of 3823908)

2

—

Hairpin, Cotter (Part of 3823908)

3

—

Driver (Part of 3823908)

4

—

Capscrew, M14-1.5 x 60 mm (Part of 3823908)

Apply a thin coat of engine oil 15W40 to the driver inside diameter and

[FIGURE: A23645A.gif]

Position the chamfered end of the wear sleeve onto the end of the

[FIGURE: A23646A.gif]

Position the counterbore end of the driver onto the wear sleeve.

[FIGURE: A23647A.gif]

Install two capscrews (without spacers or hairpin cotters) through the 
driver and onto the crankshaft capscrew holes. Align the wear sleeve and 
driver perpendicular with the crankshaft. Tighten the capscrews finger-tight.

[FIGURE: A23648A.gif]

 NOTE: To prevent damage to the wear sleeve, do not exceed 1/2 revolution of 
each capscrew. Alternately tighten the capscrews until the sleeve is installed 
to a depth of approximately 16 mm (0.625 inch). Approximate torque value 20 Nm
 (15 lb-ft).

Remove the capscrews and install a spacer on each capscrew. Install the 
two capscrews again.

[FIGURE: A23649A.gif]

Continue to alternately tighten the capscrews until the bottom of the 
driver contacts the end of the crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A23650A.gif]

Remove the driver. Use the hairpin cotters to secure the capscrews and 
spacers to the tool during storage.

[FIGURE: A23651A.gif]

 NOTE: The wear sleeve and oil seal mating surface must be clean and dry to be 
sure of proper oil sealing.

Clean the wear sleeve and crankshaft of any lubricant.

Install the oil seal, crankshaft front cover, vibration damper and fan 
drive belt. Refer to Oil Seal, Crankshaft, Front in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft Drive Gear and Thrust Plate, In-Vehicle

 Removal 

Remove the following components as described in this section:

valve cover

rocker arm assemblies

push rods

crankshaft vibration damper

front cover

fuel lift pump (refer to Section 03A-04A )

 NOTE: It is necessary to partially remove the camshaft to replace the 
camshaft gear; therefore, the tappets must be raised and secured with the 
dowel rods.

Insert Lifter Holders, part of Lifter Holder Set D94T-6500-A, or 
equivalent, such as wooden dowels securely into each tappet. Use a soft face 
hammer if necessary.

[FIGURE: A17395A.gif]

Pull each valve tappet up until it makes contact with the cylinder 
block. Put a rubber band around two dowels to hold the tappets off the 
camshaft. 

[FIGURE: A18268A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft to align the timing marks before trying to remove 
the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A17397B.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the thrust plate.

 NOTE: Rotate the camshaft as it is being removed. Use extreme care to make 
sure the camshaft bushings are not damaged during the camshaft removal process.

Remove the camshaft from the cylinder block just enough to expose the 
first two camshaft lobes.

[FIGURE: A23421A.gif]

Install retainer to secure the camshaft in position. Secure the 
retainer between the second camshaft lobe and the second camshaft journal 
using an 8 mm x 1.25 capscrew in one of the holes used to secure the camshaft 
thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A23422A.gif]

Position the gear remover yoke over the first camshaft journal and 
assemble the rods through the access holes in the camshaft gear web. Assemble 
the remainder of the tool as shown. Gear installer yoke is not used for 
camshaft gear removal. Tighten the nuts and rods finger-tight.

[FIGURE: A23423A.gif]

Tighten the pressing screw by hand while positioning the gear remover 
mandrel between the screw press and the end of the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A23424A.gif]

 CAUTION: Hold the tool securely while tightening the pressing screw to prevent 
the tool and camshaft gear from falling during removal. 

Tighten the pressing screw in a "clockwise" direction while keeping the 
tool from rotating using the torque arm as shown.

[FIGURE: A23425A.gif]

Remove the tool and camshaft gear assembly from the vehicle. 
Disassemble the tool.

 Installation 

Assemble the Cam Gear Installer to the camshaft gear. Place the rods 
through the holes in the camshaft gear and screw the rods into the gear 
installer yoke. Secure the screw press to the rods with the nuts. The nuts and 
rods need only to be finger-tight. Turn the forcing screw counterclockwise as 
far as it will go.

Be certain the chamfer in the camshaft gear will be positioned towards 
the cylinder block during camshaft gear installation.

[FIGURE: A23426A.gif]

Lubricate the inside diameter of the camshaft gear and the end of the 
camshaft. Position the tool and camshaft gear assembly over the camshaft and 
slide the gear installer yoke over the front camshaft journal.

[FIGURE: A23427A.gif]

Engage the camshaft gear keyway with the camshaft locating pin and, by 
hand, turn the forcing screw clockwise until the camshaft gear, camshaft, and 
tool are all held firmly together and properly aligned with each other.

[FIGURE: A23428A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an impact wrench with this tool, otherwise damage may result 
to the camshaft gear, camshaft or the tool. 

Tighten the forcing screw in the clockwise direction while keeping the 
tool from rotating using the torque arm inserted in the screw press.

[FIGURE: A23425A.gif]

While turning the forcing screw, the effort required should increase 
steadily until the camshaft gear is against the camshaft shoulder.

When the camshaft gear is pressed firmly against the camshaft shoulder, 
the camshaft gear installation is complete.

[FIGURE: A23429A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not try to force the camshaft into the camshaft bore as damage to 
the camshaft bushing can result. 

Install the camshaft. While pushing in slightly, rotate the camshaft 
and carefully work the camshaft through the camshaft bushings. As each 
camshaft journal passes through a bushing, the camshaft will drop slightly and 
the camshaft lobes will catch on the bushings. Rotating the camshaft will free 
the lobe from the bushing and allow the camshaft to be installed.

[FIGURE: A17418A.gif]

Before the camshaft gear engages the crankshaft gear, check the 
camshaft for ease of rotation. When installed properly, the camshaft should 
rotate freely.

Align the timing marks on the camshaft with the timing mark on the 
crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A18275A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the camshaft assembly does not drop on your fingers when 
installing the thrust plate. 

Install the camshaft thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A18276A.gif]

Install the camshaft thrust plate capscrews and tighten to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft).

 NOTE: If the camshaft end clearance is greater than the stated limit, the 
thrust plate must be replaced.

Measure camshaft end clearance with a dial indicator. End clearance is 
controlled by the thickness of the thrust plate and the groove in the 
camshaft. Camshaft end clearance limits are 0.12-0.34 mm (0.005-0.013 inch).

 NOTE: The gears must be replaced if the backlash is greater than the above 
limit.

 NOTE: Excessive gear backlash can be caused by worn camshaft bushings.

Put a dial indicator on the camshaft gear and check the gear backlash 
between the camshaft gear and the crankshaft gear. Camshaft gear backlash 
limits are 0.076-0.330 mm (0.003-0.013 inch).

Remove the wooden dowel rods from the valve tappets.

Install all parts that were removed:

fuel lift pump

front cover

crankshaft vibration damper

push rods

rocker arm assemblies

valve cover

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft Drive Gear and Thrust Plate, Out-Of-Vehicle

 Removal 

Remove the following as outlined in this section: 

fan blade pulley

crankshaft pulley

front cover

camshaft

[FIGURE: A17422A.gif]

Set the camshaft, camshaft gear side up, in press and press off the 
camshaft gear.

[FIGURE: A17424A.gif]

Remove the camshaft key.

[FIGURE: A17425A.gif]

 NOTE: If the fretting, burrs or raised material cannot be removed with 
Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent, replace the gear. 

Visually inspect the camshaft gear for cracks, chipped or broken teeth. 
Inspect the bore of the gear for fretting or burrs.

[FIGURE: A17426A.gif]

 NOTE: If the keyway is damaged or the burrs cannot be removed, the gear must 
be replaced. 

Inspect the camshaft sprocket keyway for burrs. Remove burrs with 
Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent.

[FIGURE: A17427A.gif]

 NOTE: If fretting or burrs cannot be removed with Scotch-Brite®
 7448 or equivalent, replace the camshaft. 

Visually inspect the camshaft nose for fretting or burrs.

[FIGURE: A17428A.gif]

 Installation 

Install the key.

[FIGURE: A17429A.gif]

Lubricate the camshaft surface with Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

[FIGURE: A17430A.gif]

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE GLOVES TO HANDLE THE HOT GEAR. 

 CAUTION: The gear will be permanently distorted if overheated. The oven 
temperature should never exceed 177°C (350°
F). 

Heat the camshaft gear in Rotunda Gear/Bearing Heater 164-R3900 or 
equivalent at 149°C (300°F) for 45 minutes. 

 NOTE: Be sure the gear is seated against camshaft shoulder. 

 NOTE: Do not stop once you have begun to install the gear onto the camshaft. 
Do not turn the gear while you are installing it. The gear will get stuck on 
the camshaft once you stop or if you turn the gear while installing it. If 
this occurs, remove the gear and start again. 

Install the gear with the timing marks away from the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A17432A.gif]

Using a .001-inch feeler gauge, check to see if the feeler gauge can be 
inserted between the gear and the shoulder on the camshaft. If the feeler 
gauge can be inserted, the gear is not properly seated.

[FIGURE: A17433A.gif]

Install the following as outlined in this section: 

camshaft

front cover

crank pulley

fan blade pulley

[FIGURE: A17422A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Crankshaft Gear

 Removal 

Remove crankshaft from engine. 

Using Bearing Pulling Attachment D84L-1123-A, Push-Puller Set 
D80L-927-A and Shaft Protector D80L-625-5 or equivalents, remove gear from 
crankshaft. 

[FIGURE: A17880C.gif]

Remove all burrs and make sure the crankshaft sprocket surface on the 
end of the crankshaft is smooth. 

 Installation 

If previously removed, install the alignment pin until it bottoms in 
the bore. 

 CAUTION: The gear will be permanently distorted if overheated. The oven 
temperature should never exceed 177°C (350°
F). 

Heat the crankshaft gear in Rotunda Gear/Bearing Heater 164-R3900 or 
equivalent for 45 minutes as 149°C (300°F). 

Apply a thin coat of lubricant on the nose of the crankshaft. 

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE GLOVES TO PREVENT PERSONAL INJURY. 

 NOTE: Do not stop once you have begun to install the gear onto the 
crankshaft. Do not turn the gear while you are installing it. The gear will 
get stuck on the crankshaft once you stop or if you turn the gear while 
installing it. If this occurs, remove the gear and start again. 

Install the hot gear up to the crankshaft shoulder with the timing mark 
facing out. 

Install the crankshaft.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Geartrain Timing, Initial

 Removal 

The timing pin assembly is precisely located on the gear housing to 
correspond to Top Dead Center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1. Failure to locate the 
timing pin assembly to TDC for cylinder No. 1 prior to removal will result in 
incorrect fuel injection timing.

 NOTE: If the timing pin has been damaged and cannot be used to locate TDC, 
refer to Relocating Timing Pin Assembly in this section for procedure to 
locate top dead center with the cylinder head installed on the engine. If the 
cylinder head is removed, refer to Relocating Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder 
Head Removed in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Locate top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1 by barring engine 
slowly while pressing on the engine timing pin.

[FIGURE: A17171A.gif]

Remove the timing pin assembly and seal.

[FIGURE: A17435A.gif]

 Installation 

Install a new O-ring into the groove of the timing pin assembly. 
Lubricate the O-ring with 15W-40 engine oil.

With a coat of Threadlock® 262 E2FZ-19554-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 to the threads of the Torx®
 screws and install the timing pin assembly.

Push the pin into the hole in the cam gear to align the housing.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the pin and gear, be sure the timing pin is 
disengaged before rotating the crankshaft. 

Hold the pin in while tightening the Torx® screws to 5 Nm
 (44 lb-in).

[FIGURE: A17436B.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft and Valve Tappets

 NOTE: If camshaft gear is to be replaced, refer to procedure in this section. 

A replacement camshaft does not come with a new camshaft gear. If the 
camshaft is to be replaced and the original gear is in good condition, the 
gear must be pressed off and installed on the replacement camshaft. Refer to 
procedure in this section. 

 Removal 

 Preparatory Steps: 

Remove the following:

valve covers 

push rods 

drive belt 

crankshaft pulley 

front cover

fuel transfer pump

Using an appropriate dial indicator, measure camshaft sprocket 
backlash. If backlash is out of specifications, gear must be replaced. Refer 
to procedure in this section. 

[FIGURE: A17879A.gif]

Insert Lifter Holder Set D94T-6500-A or equivalent through the push rod 
holes and into the top of each tappet securely. When properly installed, the 
holders can be used to pull the tappets up and should not be able to be pulled 
out without considerable effort.

[FIGURE: A17395A.gif]

Pull the tappets up and wrap a rubber band around the top of the lifter 
holders. This will prevent the tappets from dropping down.

[FIGURE: A17396A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft engine to align the crankshaft to camshaft timing 
marks.

[FIGURE: A17397B.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A17398A.gif]

 CAUTION: Use care when removing camshaft so as not to nick camshaft journals, 
lobes or bores. 

Remove the camshaft and thrust plate. 

[FIGURE: A17399A.gif]

To aid in tappet removal and to prevent tappets dropping down into oil 
pan, fabricate a trough and insert the trough to the full length of the 
camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17400A.gif]

Make sure the trough is positioned so it will catch the tappet when the 
holder is removed.

[FIGURE: A17401A.gif]

Remove only one tappet at a time. Remove the rubber band from the two 
companion tappets, securing the tappet not to be removed with the rubber band.

[FIGURE: A17402A.gif]

Pull the lifter holder from the valve tappet bore allowing the tappet 
to fall into the trough.

[FIGURE: A17401A.gif]

When the tappet is dropped into the trough, most of the time it will 
fall over. However, if it doesn't, gently shake the trough just enough to 
allow the tappet to fall over before removing.

[FIGURE: A17404A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17405A.gif]

 NOTE: Special care should be taken when removing the No. 6 cylinder tappets, 
not to knock or shake the tappet over the end of the trough. 

Carefully pull the trough and tappet from the camshaft bore and remove 
the tappet. Repeat the process until all tappets are removed.

[FIGURE: A17406A.gif]

Inspect the tappets and camshaft. Refer to Camshaft and to Valve Tappets 
 in the Cleaning and Inspection portion of this section. 

 Installation 

Insert the fabricated trough the full length of the camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17400A.gif]

Lower the valve tappet installation tool down the push rod hole, 
through the valve tappet bore, and into the trough.

[FIGURE: A17407A.gif]

Feed the installation tool through the camshaft bores by carefully 
pulling the trough/installation tool out the front. The barrier at the rear of 
the trough will pull the tool out most of the time.

[FIGURE: A17408A.gif]

Lubricate the tappets with Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

[FIGURE: A17409B.gif]

Insert the installation tool into the tappet.

[FIGURE: A17410A.gif]

Slide the trough into the camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17400A.gif]

Pull the tool/tappet through the camshaft bore and up into the valve 
tappet bore.

[FIGURE: A17411A.gif]

If difficulty is experienced in getting the tappet to make the bend 
from the trough up to the valve tappet bore, pull the trough out enough to 
allow the tappet to drop down and align itself, then pull the tappet up into 
the bore.

[FIGURE: A17412A.gif]

After the tappet has been pulled up into position, slide the trough 
back into the camshaft bore and rotate it one-half turn. This will position 
the round side of the trough up, which will hold the tappet in place.

[FIGURE: A17413A.gif]

 NOTE: To aid in removing the installation tool after the tappet is installed, 
work the tool in and out of the tappet several times before installing the 
tappets. 

Remove the installation tool from the tappet.

[FIGURE: A21470A.gif]

Install Lifter Holder Set D94T-6500-A or equivalent into the top of the 
tappet. Wrap rubber bands around the lifter holders to secure the tappets. 

Repeat this process until all tappets have been installed. 

[FIGURE: A17415A.gif]

Before installing the camshaft, apply a coat of Engine Assembly 
Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A 
to the front camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17416A.gif]

Lubricate the camshaft lobes, journals and thrust washer with Engine 
Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESR-M99C80-A.

[FIGURE: A17417A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not try to force the camshaft into the camshaft bore as damage to 
the camshaft bushing can result. 

Install the camshaft. While pushing in slightly, rotate the camshaft 
and carefully work the camshaft through the camshaft bushings. As each 
camshaft journal passes through a bushing, the camshaft will drop slightly and 
the camshaft lobes will catch on the bushings. Rotating the camshaft will free 
the camshaft lobe from the bushing and allow the camshaft to be installed.

[FIGURE: A17418A.gif]

Before the camshaft gear engages the crankshaft gear, check the 
camshaft for ease of rotation. When installed properly, the camshaft should 
rotate freely.

[FIGURE: A17419A.gif]

Install the thrust washer. Align the timing marks as illustrated and 
finish installing the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A17397B.gif]

Install the thrust plate capscrews and tighten to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17420A.gif]

Measure to verify the camshaft has proper backlash and end play: 

A = 0.12 to 0.34 mm (0.005 to 0.013 inch) 

B = 0.076 to 0.330 mm (0.003 to 0.013 inch)

[FIGURE: A17421A.gif]

Complete the installation of the removed parts as outlined in this 
section: 

front cover 

vibration damper 

push rods

rocker levers and valve cover 

fuel transfer pump 

drive belt

Operate the engine at idle for 5 to 10 minutes and check for leaks and 
proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft Rear Cover

 Removal 

 NOTE: It is necessary to remove the rear camshaft cover when the camshaft 
bearings are being removed and replaced.

If the camshaft has not been removed from the block, pry the cover from 
the rear countershaft bore with a wide lipped screwdriver.

[FIGURE: A108141A.gif]

If camshaft removal is necessary or if the camshaft has been removed, 
insert a long rod through the camshaft bore and knock the cover out. Be 
careful not to damage the cam bearing surfaces.

 Installation 

Clean all of the old sealer from the cover. If the sealing edge is 
nicked or damaged, replace the cover.

Liberally coat the sealing edge of the rear cam cover with Perfect Seal 
Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

Tap the rear cam cover into place with a soft mallet until it is fully 
seated.

[FIGURE: A107771A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Piston and Piston Rings

 Removal 

Drain the engine coolant. 

Remove the cylinder head as outlined. 

Drain the lubricating oil. After oil is drained, reinstall drain plug 
and a new sealing washer. Tighten to 77-83 Nm (57-61 lb-ft). 

Remove the dipstick bayonet. 

Remove the oil pan and gasket. 

 NOTE: Each connecting rod cap and connecting rod should be marked from the 
factory with a four-digit number for identification. Each connecting rod 
cap/connecting rod identification number is different. This is done because 
each connecting rod cap/connecting rod is align bored. 

Mark each connecting rod cap according to cylinder.

[FIGURE: A17310A.gif]

Rotate the engine until the pistons are below the carbon deposits which 
are found above the piston ring travel area. 

Use a scraper or a blunt-edged instrument to loosen the carbon 
deposits. Do not damage the cylinder with the scraper.

[FIGURE: A17311A.gif]

Remove the remaining carbon with a Scotch-Brite® 
cleaning pad or equivalent.

 WARNING: TO PREVENT SERIOUS EYE DAMAGE WEAR EYE PROTECTION DURING THIS OPERATION. 

 CAUTION: Do not use the steel wire wheel in the piston travel area. Operate the 
wheel in a circular motion to remove the deposits. 

 NOTE: An inferior quality wire wheel will lose steel bristles during 
operation, thus causing additional contamination. 

An alternative method to remove the carbon ridge is to use a high 
quality steel wire wheel installed in a drill or die grinder.

[FIGURE: A17312A.gif]

 NOTE: On pistons with anodized coatings, do not stamp on the anodized coating 
or on the outer rim. 

Mark each piston according to the cylinder.

[FIGURE: A17313A.gif]

Remove the capscrews, connecting rod cap and rod bearings.

[FIGURE: A17314A.gif]

Push the connecting rod and piston assembly out of cylinder bore. Care 
must be taken not to damage the connecting rod or bearing during their removal.

[FIGURE: A17315A.gif]

Disassemble the piston and connecting rod. Refer to Piston and 
Connecting Rod in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section. 

 Installation 

Install the bearing halves into both the rod and the connecting rod 
cap. Make sure the tang on the bearing halves is in the slot of the connecting 
rod cap and rod.

[FIGURE: A17316A.gif]

Lubricate the rod bearings with a light film of Engine Assembly 
Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A. 

Lubricate the piston rings and piston skirts with clean engine oil. 

 CAUTION: If using a strap-type ring compressor, make sure the inside end of the 
strap does not hook on a ring gap and break the piston ring. 

Position the piston rings.

[FIGURE: A17317A.gif]

Compress the piston rings.

[FIGURE: A17318A.gif]

Lubricate the cylinder bore with clean engine oil. 

Position the crankshaft rod journal for the piston to be installed to 
bottom dead center (BDC). 

[FIGURE: A17319A.gif]

 NOTE: Take care not to damage the cylinder wall when inserting the connecting 
rod. 

Position the piston and connecting rod assembly into cylinder bore with 
the word "front" on piston toward the front of the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A17320A.gif]

Carefully push the piston into the bore while guiding the connecting 
rod to the crankshaft journal.

[FIGURE: A17321A.gif]

Lubricate the threads and underside of the connecting rod capscrew 
heads with engine oil.

 CAUTION: The four-digit number stamped on the rod and connecting rod cap at the 
parting line must match and be installed on the oil cooler side of the engine. 

Install the connecting rod cap and capscrews to the connecting rod.

[FIGURE: A17322A.gif]

Alternately, tighten the two capscrews in the following three steps: 

Step 1. 35 Nm (26 lb-ft)

Step 2. 70 Nm (51 lb-ft)

Step 3. 100 Nm (73 lb-ft)

[FIGURE: A17323A.gif]

Measure the side clearance between the connecting rod and crankshaft. 
Side clearance limits are 0.10 to 0.33 mm (0.004 to 0.013 inch). Do not 
measure the clearance between the connecting rod cap and crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A17324A.gif]

 CAUTION: The crankshaft must rotate freely. 

 CAUTION: If the connecting rod is not properly oriented (tang opposite the 
camshaft), it will contact the camshaft and prevent the crankshaft from 
rotating. 

Check for freedom of rotation as the connecting rod caps are installed. 
If the crankshaft does not rotate freely, check the installation of the rod 
bearings and the connecting rod bearing size.

[FIGURE: A17325A.gif]

Use Silicone Gasket and Sealant F6AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A6 to fill the joints between the pan rail, gear 
housing and rear cover.

[FIGURE: A17326A.gif]

Coat both sides of the oil pan gasket with Perfect Seal Sealing 
Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M18P2-A 
and ESE-M4G115-A.

[FIGURE: A17327A.gif]

Assemble the oil pan, gasket and capscrews as illustrated and install. 
Tighten capscrews to 21-27 Nm (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17328A.gif]

Install the oil level indicator.

Install the cylinder head. Refer to Cylinder Head in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section. Fill the cooling system and fill the 
engine with oil.

[FIGURE: A17329A.gif]

Prelube (prime) the engine prior to start-up by disconnecting the fuel 
shutoff solenoid and cranking the engine until the oil pressure gauge reads 
pressure, or no more than 30 seconds. Allow the starter to cool for two 
minutes between crank times.

Operate the engine to normal operating temperature and check for leaks.

[FIGURE: A17330A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Connecting Rod Bearings 

 Removal 

Drain the engine oil. 

Remove the oil pan and gasket. 

Rotate the crankshaft to position two of the connecting rods at bottom 
dead center (BDC).

[FIGURE: A17336A.gif]

Remove the connecting rod capscrews and connecting rod caps.

[FIGURE: A17314A.gif]

Remove the lower bearing shell from the connecting rod cap and mark it 
with the letter L (lower) and the cylinder number it was removed from.

[FIGURE: A17337A.gif]

Push the rod away from the crankshaft to allow the upper bearing shell 
to be removed.

[FIGURE: A17338A.gif]

Remove the upper bearing shell and mark it with the letter U (upper) 
and the cylinder number it was removed from.

[FIGURE: A17339A.gif]

Clean and inspect the bearings and connecting rod caps. Refer to the Cleaning and Inspection 
 portion of this section. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Used bearings must be installed in the same location from which they 
were removed. 

Use Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A to coat the inside diameter of the bearing shell halves.

[FIGURE: A17340A.gif]

Install the upper bearing shell in the connecting rod with the tang of 
the bearing in the slot of the rod.

[FIGURE: A21469A.gif]

Install the lower bearing shell in the connecting rod cap with the tang 
of the bearing in the slot of the connecting rod cap. Use Engine Assembly 
Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A 
to coat the inside diameter of the bearing shell.

[FIGURE: A17342A.gif]

Use clean engine oil to lubricate the threads and underside of the 
connecting rod capscrew head.

[FIGURE: A17343A.gif]

 NOTE: The four-digit number stamped on the rod and connecting rod cap at the 
parting line must match and be installed on the oil cooler side of the engine. 

Install the connecting rod cap and capscrews to the connecting rod.

[FIGURE: A17344A.gif]

Alternately tighten the two capscrews in the following three-step 
sequence: 

Step 1. 35 Nm (26 lb-ft) 

Step 2. 70 Nm (51 lb-ft) 

Step 3. 100 Nm (73 lb-ft)

[FIGURE: A17323A.gif]

Measure the side clearance between the connecting rod and crankshaft. 
Do not measure the clearance between the connecting rod cap and crankshaft. 
Side clearance limits are 0.10 to 0.33 mm (0.004 to 0.013 inch).

[FIGURE: A17345A.gif]

 CAUTION: The crankshaft must rotate freely. 

Check for freedom of rotation as the connecting rod caps are installed. 
If the crankshaft does not rotate freely, check the installation of the rod 
bearings and connecting rod bearing size. 

[FIGURE: A17325A.gif]

Install the engine lubricating oil pan and gasket. 

Fill the engine with oil.

[FIGURE: A17346A.gif]

Operate the engine to normal operating temperature and check for leaks.

[FIGURE: A17330A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Main and Thrust Bearings, Engine In-Vehicle

 Removal 

Drain the oil and remove the oil pan.

[FIGURE: A17347A.gif]

 NOTE: Before removing the crankshaft main bearing caps, make sure that the 
crankshaft main bearing caps are clearly marked for their location on the oil 
cooler side of the crankshaft main bearing cap. 

Perform a visual inspection of the main bearings and crankshaft main 
bearing journals. Remove the No. 2 and 3 crankshaft main bearing caps and 
check the crankshaft journals for signs of overheat, deep scratches or other 
damage. If there is no damage, there is no need to pull the other crankshaft 
main bearing caps at this time.

[FIGURE: A17348A.gif]

Inspect the crankshaft main bearing caps for dents, cracks, or other 
damage.

[FIGURE: A17349A.gif]

 NOTE: If the crankshaft main bearing journals or crankshaft main bearing caps 
are damaged, the engine will need to be removed to complete the overhaul. 

Inspect the crankshaft main bearing journals for deep scratches, 
indications of overheating and other damage.

[FIGURE: A17350A.gif]

Remove all crankshaft main bearing caps except the No. 1 and 7 
crankshaft main bearing cap for six-cylinder engine.

Use a pin to roll out the upper bearings from between the crankshaft 
and cylinder block. 

To make a pin, grind a 6 mm capscrew to the dimensions shown.

[FIGURE: A17352A.gif]

Install the pin into the oil hole in the crankshaft. Rotate the 
crankshaft so the pin pushes against the end of the bearing opposite the tang. 
Remove the bearing. 

Follow this procedure to remove the other bearings.

[FIGURE: A17353A.gif]

Inspect all crankshaft main bearing caps and crankshaft main bearing 
journals.

[FIGURE: A17350A.gif]

Determine the size of the bearing removed and obtain the same size for 
installation.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not lubricate the side of the bearing that is against the cylinder 
block. 

Apply a coat of Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A to the new upper bearings.

[FIGURE: A17355A.gif]

Position the new bearing on the crankshaft and install as far as 
possible by hand.

[FIGURE: A17356A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the pin does not slide under the bearing. 

Using the pin, finish pushing the bearing in slowly, making sure it is 
aligned with the block. Make sure the tang on the bearing sets into the notch.

[FIGURE: A17357A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17358A.gif]

Install the lower bearings into the crankshaft main bearing caps. Apply 
a coat of Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A to the bearings.

[FIGURE: A17359A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the crankshaft main bearing caps are correctly installed with 
the number toward the oil cooler side of the engine. 

Install a crankshaft main bearing cap after each upper bearing is 
installed to keep the bearing in place while the other uppers are installed. 
Tighten the capscrews to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft). Do not tighten to 
the final torque value at this time.

Use the same procedure to remove and install rear crankshaft main 
bearing cap, No. 5 or No. 7.

[FIGURE: A17361A.gif]

 CAUTION: Use care so the screwdriver does not damage the crankshaft or cylinder 
block. 

Use a flat-blade screwdriver. Gently bump the end of the bearing to 
loosen it from the block. Then, use finger pressure against the upper shell 
and rotate the crankshaft to roll the bearing out.

[FIGURE: A17362A.gif]

 NOTE: The front crankshaft main bearing journal, No. 1, does not contain a 
drilled oil passage. The pin cannot be used to replace the bearing. 

Lubricate and install the bearing. Use the screwdriver to push the 
bearing into position as you rotate the crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A17363A.gif]

 CAUTION: The crankshaft must rotate freely after each crankshaft main bearing 
cap is tightened. 

Tighten the main bearing capscrews evenly in the following three-step 
sequence: 

Step 1. 60 Nm (44 lb-ft) 

Step 2. 119 Nm (88 lb-ft) 

Step 3. 176 Nm (129 lb-ft) 

Check the bearing installation and the size of the bearings if the 
crankshaft does not rotate freely.

 NOTE: The dimensions of the thrust bearing and crankshaft main bearing 
journal determine end play. 

Measure the crankshaft end play. Following are dimension A end play 
limits: 

minimum 0.127 mm (0.005 inch) and maximum 0.355 mm (0.014 inch)

[FIGURE: A17365A.gif]

Install the oil pan and gasket. 

Fill the system with engine oil. Operate the engine at idle for 5 to 10 
minutes. Check for loose parts and leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Crankshaft Rear Oil Seal

 Removal 

Remove the transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07. 

Remove the flywheel.

[FIGURE: A17384A.gif]

Drill two holes 180 degrees apart into the crankshaft rear oil seal 
carrier.

[FIGURE: A17385A.gif]

Using a No. 10 sheet metal screw and a slide hammer dent puller, remove 
the rear seal.

[FIGURE: A17386A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: The crankshaft rear oil seal lip and the sealing surface on the 
crankshaft must be free from all oil residue to prevent oil leaks. 

Clean and dry the crankshaft sealing surface.

[FIGURE: A17387A.gif]

Install the seal pilot, provided in the replacement kit, onto the 
crankshaft. Push the seal onto the pilot and crankshaft. Remove the seal pilot.

[FIGURE: A17388A.gif]

Use the alignment tool to install the seal to the correct depth in the 
housing. Use a hammer to drive the seal into the housing until the alignment 
tool tops against the housing. Hit the tool at 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock 
positions to drive the seal evenly and to prevent bending the crankshaft rear 
oil seal carrier.

[FIGURE: A17389A.gif]

Install the flywheel. Tighten the capscrews in sequence as shown in the 
illustration, to 130-144 Nm (97-106 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17390A.gif]

Install the clutch, transmission and starter. Operate the engine and 
check for leaks. 

 Wear Sleeve, Rear Crankshaft Seal 

 Removal 

Remove the transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07.

Remove the clutch and flywheel, if so equipped. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Remove the flywheel housing. Refer to Flywheel Housing in the Removal 
and Installation portion of this section.

Remove the four lubricating oil pan mounting capscrews that secure the 
oil pan to the rear cover.

 CAUTION: Use extreme care when releasing the oil pan gasket from the rear cover 
to prevent damage to the gasket. If the gasket is damaged, the oil pan must be 
removed and the gasket replaced. 

Insert a feeler gauge or shim stock between the rear cover and the oil 
pan gasket. Move the feeler gauge or shim stock back and forth to release the 
gasket from the rear cover.

[FIGURE: A23652A.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the rear cover and remove the cover from the 
crankshaft flange. Remove the seal from the rear cover.

[FIGURE: A23653A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not nick or gouge the crankshaft with the chisel. If the crankshaft 
is damaged, it must be replaced. 

Use a dull chisel that is only as wide as the wear sleeve. Make one or 
two soft blows with a hammer across the wear sleeve. This will expand the wear 
sleeve allowing the sleeve to be removed.

[FIGURE: A23654A.gif]

Clean the gasket surface of the rear cover, crankshaft flange, and 
cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A23655A.gif]

Inspect the crankshaft flange and rear cover for dirt, nicks or other 
damage.

[FIGURE: A23656A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: The seal installation is used to properly align the rear cover. Do not 
push the cover in any direction to prevent irregular lip position after seal 
installation. 

 NOTE: Install the rear cover capscrews. Do not tighten. If the oil pan is 
installed, loosen the oil pan capscrews to allow clearance for rear cover and 
gasket clearance.

Install rear cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: A23657A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not use any kind of lubricant to install the oil seal. The oil seal 
must be installed with the lip of the oil seal and crankshaft clean and dry to 
ensure proper oil sealing.

 NOTE: The combination crankshaft oil seal and wear sleeve is installed on the 
crankshaft as an assembly.

 NOTE: The oil seal for a wet flywheel housing requires soap on the outside 
diameter of the seal case. Nothing is required on the outside diameter of the 
seal case for dry housings.

Use Cummins Engine Company Service Tool Part No. 3824078 to install the 
oil seal and wear sleeve assembly.

 Crankshaft Wear Sleeve Installation Tool 

[FIGURE: A23658A.gif]

Apply a small amount of clean engine oil to the crankshaft threaded 
studs and the inside diameter of the crankshaft rear seal and wear sleeve 
installation tool. Install two threaded studs into the crankshaft.

Position the chamfered end of the wear sleeve onto end of the 
crankshaft. Position the counterbore end of the installation tool over the 
threaded studs and align with wear sleeve, perpendicular to end of crankshaft.

 NOTE: Do not exceed 1/2 revolution of each nut to prevent wear sleeve binding 
and irregular stretch.

Install washers and nuts onto the threaded studs. Alternately tighten 
the nuts until the installation tool contacts the end of the crankshaft. 
Tighten to 20 Nm (15 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A23659A.gif]

Crankshaft

Remove the installation tool and the threaded studs.

Align the rear cover even with both sides of the oil pan rail on the 
cylinder block. Tighten the rear cover capscrews to 8-10 Nm 
(71-88 lb-in).

[FIGURE: A23660A.gif]

 NOTE: Be sure to fill the joint between the lubricating oil pan rail and rear 
cover with Silicone Gasket and Sealant F6AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A6.

Trim the gaskets even with the oil pan mounting surface.

[FIGURE: A23661A.gif]

 NOTE: The oil pan capscrews should be torqued within 15 minutes after 
applying sealant.

Install four capscrews that hold the oil pan to the rear cover. Tighten 
to 21-27 Nm (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A23662A.gif]

Install the flywheel housing. Refer to Flywheel Housing in the Removal 
and Installation portion of this section.

Install the clutch and flywheel, if so equipped. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Install the transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Gear Cover

 Removal 

 NOTE: If a new gear cover is to be installed, remove engine dataplate and 
attach to new gear cover.

Remove the following as described in this section: 

valve covers, rocker levers and push rods 

vibration damper 

camshaft

front cover

Remove the fuel injection pump. Refer to Section 03A-04A .

Remove the six front oil pan capscrews.

[FIGURE: A17438A.gif]

Remove the gear cover capscrews.

[FIGURE: A17439A.gif]

Using a feeler gauge, attempt to separate the oil pan gasket from the 
gear cover.

[FIGURE: A17440A.gif]

Remove the gear cover.

[FIGURE: A17441A.gif]

Clean the gasket material from the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A17442A.gif]

Inspect the oil pan gasket. If it is not torn, coat with Perfect Seal 
Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

[FIGURE: A17443A.gif]

If the gasket is torn, it may be repaired. Cut the torn gasket off, 
even with the front of the engine block.

[FIGURE: A17444A.gif]

Using the old gasket as a pattern, cut the front section of a new 
gasket to the same size.

[FIGURE: A17445A.gif]

Clean the sealing surfaces and coat the new gasket on both sides with 
Perfect Seal Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

[FIGURE: A17446A.gif]

Use common thread or a very fine wire to hold the new oil pan gasket 
splice in position as illustrated for the repair.

[FIGURE: A17447A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: When properly trimmed, the gear cover gasket should be even with the 
oil pan gasket when installed. 

Mark and trim 1.59 mm (1/16 inch) off the new gear housing gasket.

[FIGURE: A17448A.gif]

Coat both sides of the gear cover gasket with Perfect Seal Sealing 
Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M18P2-A 
and ESE-M4G115-A.

[FIGURE: A17449A.gif]

Position the gear cover gasket on the alignment dowels.

[FIGURE: A17450A.gif]

 CAUTION: If a new gear cover or other than the original gear housing is 
installed, the timing pin assembly must be accurately located. Refer to the 
appropriate procedure in this section. 

Carefully install the gear cover, making sure both gaskets are in 
place. Tighten screws to 21-27 Nm (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17451A.gif]

Start the oil pan capscrews in the holes not being used to tie the 
gasket in place.

[FIGURE: A17452A.gif]

Remove the thread or wire holding the gasket in place.

[FIGURE: A17453A.gif]

Install the remaining two capscrews and tighten the capscrews to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17454A.gif]

Lubricate the camshaft and thrust plate with Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

[FIGURE: A17455B.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure the alignment marks on the camshaft and camshaft gears are 
aligned. 

Install the camshaft/thrust plate. Refer to the Camshaft and Valve 
Tappets installation procedure if additional information is needed.

[FIGURE: A17456B.gif]

Install the camshaft thrust plate capscrews. Tighten to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17457A.gif]

Measure to verify the camshaft has proper backlash and end play: 

A = 0.12 to 0.34 mm (0.005 to 0.013 in.) 

B = 0.076 to 0.330 mm (0.003 to 0.013 in.)

[FIGURE: A17458A.gif]

Remove the lifter holders from the tappets.

[FIGURE: A17459A.gif]

Install and lubricate the push rods and complete the installation of 
the rocker levers as described in this section.

[FIGURE: A21471A.gif]

Complete the installation of the removed components as described in 
this section: 

Adjust the valves.

Install front cover. 

Install vibration damper. 

Install fuel injection pump (refer to Section 03A-04A ).

[FIGURE: A17461A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Relocating Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head Removed 

 CAUTION: The timing pin assembly is precisely located on the gear housing to 
correspond to TDC for cylinder No. 1. The timing pin assembly must be 
relocated if the gear housing is replaced. 

Remove the front cover.

Temporarily install the crankshaft damper and a pointer fabricated from 
No. 16 gauge wire. Put a flatwasher between the pointer and gear housing to 
prevent damage to gear housing.

[FIGURE: DA0285A.gif]

Cut a 5-inch long piece of 1/4-inch flat bar stock. Drill a 7/16-inch 
hole approximately 1/2-inch from one end. Using a flywheel bolt, attach the 
bar stock to the cylinder block extending over number one cylinder.

Rotate the crankshaft until number one piston touches the plate, then 
mark the damper. 

Rotate the crankshaft in the opposite direction until the piston 
touches the plate, and mark the damper again. 

Mark the damper exactly half way between the two marks. This is top 
dead center (TDC). 

Remove the bar and rotate the crankshaft until the wire pointer aligns 
with the new TDC mark. 

Look for the timing pin hole in the back of the camshaft gear. If the 
hole is not visible, rotate the crankshaft 360 degrees. 

Install a new O-ring into the groove of the timing pin assembly. 
Lubricate the O-ring with 15W-40 engine oil.

Apply a coat of Threadlock® 262 E2FZ-19554-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 to the threads of the Torx®
 screws and install the timing pin assembly.

Push the pin into the hole in the cam gear to align the housing.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the pin and gear, be sure the timing pin is 
disengaged before rotating the crankshaft. 

Hold the pin in while tightening the Torx® screws to 5 Nm
 (44 lb-in). Check the pin to be sure it did not slip out 
of the camshaft gear hole when the screws were tightened.

[FIGURE: A18289A.gif]

Remove the vibration damper and wire pointer.

[FIGURE: A18290A.gif]

Install the gear cover. Refer to Cover, Front in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section.

Install the vibration damper. Refer to Crankshaft 
Pulley/Damper in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Relocating Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head Installed 

 CAUTION: The timing pin assembly is precisely located on the gear housing to 
correspond to top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1. The timing pin 
assembly must be relocated if the gear housing is replaced. 

Remove the front cover as outlined in this section.

Locate top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1 by barring engine 
slowly while pressing on the engine timing pin.

[FIGURE: A17171A.gif]

[FIGURE: A18281A.gif]

 CAUTION: If a gear housing other than the original housing is installed, the 
timing pin assembly must be accurately aligned to correspond to TDC for 
cylinder No. 1. 

Remove the timing pin assembly and seal.

Verify the timing marks on the crankshaft and camshaft are aligned or 
the hole in the back of the camshaft gear is visible through the gear housing.

[FIGURE: A18282A.gif]

To align the assembly, temporarily install the vibration damper and a 
pointer fabricated from No. 16 gauge wire. Put a flatwasher between the 
pointer and gear housing to prevent damage to the gear housing.

[FIGURE: A18283A.gif]

Remove high pressure fuel lines.

 NOTE: This step is important to release cylinder pressure so the crankshaft 
can be rotated smoothly to locate TDC for cylinder No. 1.

Remove all injector nozzles.

Remove the valve cover.

Adjust the intake valve rocker lever on No. 1 cylinder to have zero 
valve clearance.

[FIGURE: A18284A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft 90 degrees in the direction of normal engine 
rotation.

[FIGURE: A18285B.gif]

 NOTE: Leave the adjusting screw in this position until TDC is established.

Tighten the adjusting screw for the No. 1 intake valve five complete 
turns of the screw.

 CAUTION: Use extreme care that the piston does not push against the exhaust 
valve with so much force that it bends the push rod, valve stem, or damages 
the valve head or piston. 

Rotate the crankshaft slowly in the direction opposite engine rotation 
until the piston just touches the intake valve.

Mark the vibration damper.

[FIGURE: A18286B.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the piston touches the valve with approximately the same 
amount of force as in the previous step. 

Rotate the crankshaft in the direction of engine rotation until the 
piston just touches the intake valve.

Mark the vibration damper.

Measure the distance and mark the damper at one-half the distance 
between the two marks. This mark is the TDC mark.

[FIGURE: A18287B.gif]

 CAUTION: Failure to loosen the No. 1 intake valve adjusting screw will result in 
bending the push rod, valve stem or damage to valve face or piston when the 
crankshaft is rotated. 

Completely loosen the No. 1 intake valve adjusting screw.

Rotate the crankshaft in the direction of engine rotation until the 
pointer is aligned with the TDC mark then an additional one full revolution 
(360 degrees).

[FIGURE: A18288A.gif]

Look through the back side of the gear housing for the timing pin hole 
in the camshaft gear. If the hole is not visible, the crankshaft must 
 be rotated one revolution.

Install a new O-ring into the groove of the timing pin assembly. 
Lubricate the O-ring with 15W-40 engine oil.

Apply a coat of Threadlock® 262 E2FZ-19554-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 to the threads of the Torx®
 screws and install the timing pin assembly.

Push the pin into the hole in the camshaft gear to align the housing.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the pin and gear, be sure the timing pin is 
disengaged before rotating the crankshaft. 

Hold the pin in while tightening the Torx® screws to 5 Nm
 (44 lb-in). Check the pin to be sure it did not slip out 
of the camshaft gear hole when the screws were tightened.

[FIGURE: A18289A.gif]

Remove the vibration damper and wire pointer.

Install the front cover. Refer to Cover, Front in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section.

Install the vibration damper. Refer to Crankshaft 
Pulley/Damper in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

[FIGURE: A18290A.gif]

Adjust the No. 1 intake valve clearance to 0.25 mm (0.010 inch). Refer 
to Valve Adjustment, Cold , in the Adjustments portion of this section.

Install the valve cover with a new seal.

Install the injector nozzles and high pressure fuel lines, then bleed 
fuel system. Refer to Section 03A-04A .
