REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Flywheel Housing 

 Removal 

Remove the transmission, clutch and all related components (if so 
equipped). Refer to the appropriate transmission section in Group 07 and to 
 Section 08-01 .

[FIGURE: A17466A.gif]

Remove the flywheel.

[FIGURE: A17384A.gif]

Adequately support the engine to prevent damage. Disconnect the battery 
cables and remove the starter motor.

[FIGURE: J5186B.gif]

Disconnect both rear engine supports.

Remove the flywheel housing capscrews.

[FIGURE: A17469A.gif]

 CAUTION: The component weighs 23 kg (50 lbs.) or more. To avoid personal injury, 
use a hoist or get assistance to lift the component. 

Use a rubber hammer to loosen the flywheel housing. Remove the flywheel 
housing and flywheel housing seal.

[FIGURE: A17470A.gif]

 WARNING: WHEN USING A STEAM CLEANER, WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES 
OR A FACE SHIELD. HOT STEAM CAN CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY. 

Use steam or solvent to clean the flywheel housing. Dry with compressed 
air.

[FIGURE: A17471A.gif]

Inspect the flywheel housing for cracks, especially in the bolt pattern 
area. Visually inspect all surfaces for nicks, burrs, or cracks. Use fine 
crocus cloth to remove small nicks and burrs.

[FIGURE: A17472A.gif]

Inspect for damaged threads commonly caused by cross-threaded capscrews 
or installing an incorrect capscrew. Heli-coils are available to service 
damaged threads.

[FIGURE: A17473A.gif]

 Installation 

Install flywheel housing seal and lubricate with Multi-Purpose Grease 
DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M1C159-A and 
ESB-M1C93-B.

[FIGURE: A17474B.gif]

 NOTE: Be sure the flywheel housing seal is not damaged during installation. 

Visually inspect the rear face of the cylinder block and flywheel 
housing mounting surface for cleanliness and raised nicks or burrs. Install 
the flywheel housing over the two ring dowels.

[FIGURE: A17475A.gif]

Tighten the flywheel housing capscrews in sequence shown to 75-81 Nm
 (56-59 lb-ft) for a cast iron housing, or 54-61 Nm
 (40-45 lb-ft) for an aluminum housing.

[FIGURE: A17476A.gif]

Check the flywheel housing bore and flywheel housing face alignments. 
Refer to Section 03-00 . 

Install the transmission, clutch and related components.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Oil Level Indicator and Tube Assembly

 Removal 

Clean the area around the oil level indicator tube.

Remove the oil level indicator tube and indicator assembly.

Remove any existing sealant from the hole in the engine block taking 
care to avoid contaminating the engine oil.

 Installation 

Remove any existing sealant from the knurled portion of the oil level 
indicator tube. Coat the knurled portion with Threadlock® 
262 E2FZ-19554-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6.

Insert the oil level indicator tube into the hole in the engine block 
making sure the shoulder on the tube seats against the machined surface of the 
engine block. The tube must be oriented as shown.

Install the oil level indicator in the tube.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Sending Unit

 Removal 

Disconnect the wire at the unit terminal.

Unscrew the unit from its mounting.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Be sure to use Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A 
or equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-A2 and ESR-M18P7-A or 
electrically conductive water-resistant sealer on the threads on the unit. The 
pressure switch-type unit used with the indicator lamp system is not 
interchangeable with the variable resistance-type sending unit, which is used 
with the gauge system. Refer to the Ford Truck Master Parts Catalog for proper 
parts usage. Installation of the wrong part will result in an inoperative oil 
pressure indicating system and a damaged sending unit or gauge. 

Install the new sending unit and tighten to 20-27 Nm 
(15-19 lb-ft).

Connect the wire to the unit terminal and check the operation of the 
unit.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Cylinder Head

 Removal 

 NOTE: It is easier and faster to remove the cylinder head as an assembly, and 
then remove additional components on the bench after the cylinder head is out 
of the vehicle. 

Disconnect the battery ground cables and drain the engine coolant.

Working from the right side of the engine compartment, remove the air 
cleaner assembly, air cleaner support and the turbocharger air inlet adapter. 
Cap the turbocharger air inlet. 

Disconnect the air-to-air tube from the charge air cooler and the 
turbocharger. Remove the air-to-air tube. Cap the charge air cooler inlet and 
turbocharger outlet. 

Disconnect the ether cold start line from the intake manifold (if so 
equipped). 

Remove the turbocharger oil supply and return lines. 

Disconnect the temperature sender wire on the thermostat housing. 

Remove the engine oil filter. 

Remove the exhaust pipe band clamp on the turbocharger exhaust outlet. 

Disconnect the upper radiator hose, the heater hoses to the thermostat 
housing and the heater hose from the heater hose tube assembly. 

Remove the generator drive belt, the upper generator bracket, and the 
bolt securing the generator lower support to the thermostat housing. 

Remove the bolt securing the heater hose tube to the cylinder head, 
loosen the flange nut and remove the heater hose tube. 

Working from the left side of the engine compartment, disconnect the 
air-to-air tube from the charge air cooler and the intake manifold. Remove the 
air-to-air tube. Cap the charge air cooler outlet. 

On vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes, remove the brake hydraulic 
pump belt, and remove the brake pump from the mounting bracket. Position the 
pump out of the way. 

On air brake equipped vehicles, remove the air compressor air inlet 
hose. 

Remove the bolts securing the engine cooling fan hub to the engine, and 
remove the fan and hub as an assembly.

[FIGURE: A17302A.gif]

Remove the wiring brackets from the rocker arm cover. 

Disconnect the injector high pressure lines from the injectors and the 
injection pump. Cap all lines to prevent contamination.

[FIGURE: A17303A.gif]

Disconnect the fuel supply hose at the fuel sediment bowl and the 
supply hose for the lift pump. Remove the fuel line from the lift pump to the 
fuel filter assembly. Cap all lines to prevent contamination. 

Remove the fuel filter. 

Disconnect the air inlet temperature sensor, remove the electrical 
bracket from the cylinder head and position the wiring harness out of the way. 

Remove the rocker arm covers and loosen all of the rocker arm adjusting 
nuts and screws. 

Mark the rocker arm pedestals for installation in the same locations. 
Remove the rocker arm shaft support bolts and remove the rocker arm and 
pedestal assemblies. Remove the push rods, noting their locations.

[FIGURE: A17304A.gif]

Remove the cylinder head bolts in the sequence shown.

[FIGURE: A17305A.gif]

Using a suitable lifting device, remove the cylinder head from the 
vehicle.

[FIGURE: A17306A.gif]

Remove additional components from the cylinder head as required for 
service. 

Inspect the cylinder head and block as detailed in Section 03-00 . 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Oversize service head gaskets are used when the cylinder head surface 
on the block or the cylinder head has been machined. Oversize service gaskets 
are available in either 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) oversize or 0.50 mm (0.020 inch) 
oversize. 

Install any components removed from the cylinder head after removal 
from the vehicle. 

Position a new cylinder head gasket on the engine block observing 
correct alignment with the holes in the engine block. Using a suitable lifting 
device, position the cylinder head on the engine and seat it onto the 
alignment dowels.

[FIGURE: A17307A.gif]

Position the push rods in their correct positions into the valve 
tappets. Lubricate the push rod sockets and the valve stem ends with fresh 
engine oil.

[FIGURE: A17308A.gif]

 CAUTION: Refer to Cleaning and Inspection in this section for guidelines on 
cylinder head bolt reuse. If they are too long, they will not properly clamp 
down the cylinder head. 

With the rocker arm adjusting screws completely loosened, position the 
rocker arm pedestals. Apply a light coating of fresh engine oil to the rocker 
arm shaft support bolt threads (long bolts), and under the bolt head, and 
install the retaining bolts (long bolts) hand-tight. 

Lightly lubricate the remaining cylinder head bolt threads and under 
the bolt heads, and install them hand-tight.

[FIGURE: A17309A.gif]

 CAUTION: The following procedure must be used for cylinder head bolt 
installation. 

Tighten the cylinder head bolts in the sequence shown using the Torque 
Plus Angle as follows: 

Tighten all cylinder head bolts in sequence to 90 Nm 
(66 lb-ft). 

Recheck all cylinder head bolt torques in sequence to 90 Nm
 (66 lb-ft). 

Tighten only the six long cylinder head bolts (4, 5, 12, 13, 20 and 21) 
in sequence to 120 Nm (90 lb-ft). 

Recheck the six long cylinder head bolts in sequence to 120 Nm
 (90 lb-ft). 

Following the sequence shown, turn all cylinder head bolts an 
additional 90 degrees. 

Recheck all cylinder head bolt torques by turning to 136 Nm
 (102 lb-ft). If any cylinder head bolts turn, loosen that 
cylinder head bolt and retighten it per Steps a through f above.

[FIGURE: A17305A.gif]

Install the remaining (short) rocker arm shaft support bolts and 
tighten to 21-27 Nm (16-19 lb-ft). 

Adjust the valve clearances as detailed under Adjustments in this 
section. 

Install the rocker arm covers. 

Connect the air inlet temperature sensor, and install the electrical 
bracket to the cylinder head. 

Install a new fuel filter. 

Connect the fuel supply hose to the fuel sediment bowl and the supply 
hose for the lift pump. Install the fuel line to the lift pump and the fuel 
filter assembly. 

Connect the injector high pressure lines to the injectors and the 
injection pump. 

Install the wiring brackets to the rocker arm covers. 

Position the engine cooling fan and hub to the engine and tighten the 
bolts to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft). 

On air brake-equipped vehicles, install the air compressor air inlet 
hose. 

On vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes, install the brake hydraulic 
pump assembly and adjust the belt to specifications. 

Working from the left side of the engine compartment, connect the 
air-to-air tube to the charge air cooler and the intake manifold. 

Install heater hose tube to cylinder head.

Install bolt securing generator lower support to thermostat housing. 
Install upper generator bracket and drive belt. Check torque of belt tensioner 
mounting bolts. Correct torque value is 43 Nm (32 lb-ft).

Connect upper radiator hose, the heater hoses to the thermostat housing 
and the heater hose to the heater hose tube assembly.

Install the exhaust pipe band clamp on the turbocharger exhaust outlet.

Install new oil filter.

Connect the temperature sender wire on the thermostat housing.

Install the turbocharger oil supply and return lines.

If so equipped, connect the ether cold start line to the intake manifold.

Connect the air-to-air tube to the charge air cooler and the 
turbocharger.

Install the turbocharger air inlet adapter, air cleaner support and the 
air cleaner assembly.

 CAUTION: New turbochargers must be pre-lubricated before start up. Pour 50-60cc 
(2-3 ounces) of clean engine oil into the oil supply fitting. Rotate the 
turbine wheel to allow the oil to enter the bearing housing. 

Fill the engine crankcase with engine oil. Add engine coolant.

Connect battery ground cable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Flywheel

 Removal 

Remove the vehicle driveline and transmission. Refer to the appropriate 
section in Group 07.

Remove the clutch discs and the pressure plate, if so equipped. Refer 
to Section 08-01 .

 NOTE: Use Engine Barring Tool D92T-6000-C or equivalent to hold the flywheel 
to prevent rotation.

Remove two capscrews 180 degrees apart. Install two M12 x 1.25 x 90 mm 
guide pins.

[FIGURE: A17462A.gif]

 NOTE: If a clutch is used in the equipment, the threads in the clutch 
pressure plate mounting capscrew holes can be metric or standard. Be sure to use the correct capscrews.

Determine the capscrew thread design and size and install two T-handles 
in the flywheel at points A and B.

Remove the remaining six flywheel mounting capscrews.

[FIGURE: A18294A.gif]

 CAUTION: The component weighs 23 kg (50 lbs.) or more. To avoid personal injury, 
use a hoist or get assistance to lift the component. 

Remove the flywheel from the guide pins.

[FIGURE: A18295A.gif]

If ring gear requires replacement, refer to procedure in this section.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Use a new pilot bearing when installing a new or rebuilt clutch.

Use a mandrel and a hammer to remove the pilot bearing.

Use a Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent to clean the 
pilot bore.

 NOTE: The pilot bearing must be installed even with the pilot 
bore surface.

Use a mandrel and hammer to install the pilot bearing.

[FIGURE: A18296A.gif]

Install two M12 x 1.25 x 90 mm guide pins into the crankshaft flange 
180 degrees apart.

 NOTE: If a clutch is used in the equipment, the threads in the clutch 
pressure plate mounting capscrew holes can be metric or standard. Be sure to use the correct capscrews.

Determine the capscrew thread design and size and install two T-handles 
into the flywheel at points A and B.

[FIGURE: A18297A.gif]

Visually inspect rear face of crankshaft and flywheel mounting flange 
for cleanliness and raised nicks or burrs.

 CAUTION: The component weighs 23 kg (50 lbs.) or more. To avoid personal injury, 
use a hoist or get assistance to lift the component. 

Install the flywheel on the guide pins.

Lubricate the threads of the capscrews and the surface of the washers 
with 15W-40 engine oil.

Install the six capscrews.

Remove the T-handles and guide pins.

Install the remaining capscrews into the holes from which the guide 
pins were removed.

Hold the crankshaft when tightening the flywheel capscrews.

Tighten the capscrews in the sequence shown (a star pattern) to 130-144 Nm
 (97-106 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17390A.gif]

Install the clutch discs and pressure plate. Refer to Section 08-01 . 

Install the vehicle transmission and driveline. Refer to the 
appropriate section in Group 07.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Flywheel Ring Gear 

 Removal

Remove the flywheel.

[FIGURE: A17462A.gif]

 WARNING: WEAR EYE PROTECTION WHEN YOU DRIVE THE GEAR FROM THE FLYWHEEL. DO NOT 
USE A STEEL DRIFT PIN. 

Use the drift pin to drive the ring gear from the flywheel.

[FIGURE: A17463A.gif]

Heat the new ring gear for 20 minutes in an oven preheated to 127°

Install the gear. The gear must be installed so the bevel on the teeth 
is toward the crankshaft side of the flywheel.

[FIGURE: A17465A.gif]

Use two capscrews in the front of the crankshaft, or similar device, to 
hold the crankshaft when the flywheel capscrews are being tightened.

[FIGURE: A17384A.gif]

Tighten the capscrews in the sequence shown to 130-144 Nm
 (97-106 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17390A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Oil Filter

 Removal 

Locate engine oil filter on engine. Place Oil Filter Wrench D79L-6731-A 
or equivalent on oil filter and remove by turning the filter in a 
counterclockwise direction.

 Installation 

Lubricate the oil filter gasket with the specified engine oil.

Install filter until gasket firmly contacts mating surface on the 
engine. Tighten filter one-half to three-quarters turn more.

Check engine oil level and add as required.

Operate engine and check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Oil Cooler

 Removal 

Drain engine coolant. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Remove the oil bypass filter.

[FIGURE: A24905A.gif]

Clean around the lubricating oil cooler cover.

[FIGURE: A24939A.gif]

Disconnect the turbocharger supply line.

[FIGURE: A24906A.gif]

Remove the lubricating oil cooler cover, gaskets and cooler element.

[FIGURE: A24907A.gif]

Clean the sealing surfaces between the oil cooler and cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A24908A.gif]

 Installation 

Assemble the oil cooler gaskets, element and cover. Tighten bolts to 
21-27 Nm (16-19 lb-ft).

Connect the turbocharger oil supply line.

Fill the oil bypass filter with clean engine oil and apply a light coat 
of oil to the sealing gasket. Install the oil bypass filter.

[FIGURE: A24910A.gif]

Fill the cooling system. Start engine and check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Piston Grading

 CAUTION: If a new cylinder block or crankshaft is used, a piston grading 
procedure must be used. 

Install the connecting rod and piston assembly into the No. 1 cylinder 
without the rings installed.

[FIGURE: A23634A.gif]

 CAUTION: The connecting rod bearing shells must be installed in the original 
connecting rod and cap. 

Install the upper bearing shell in the connecting rod with the tang of 
the bearing in the slot of the connecting rod. Use clean engine oil to coat 
the inside diameter of the connecting rod shell.

[FIGURE: A23635A.gif]

Install the bearing shell in the connecting rod cap with the tang of 
the bearing in the slot of the cap. Use clean engine oil to coat the inside 
diameter of the bearing shell.

[FIGURE: A23636A.gif]

The four-digit number stamped on the connecting rod and cap at the 
parting line must match and be installed on the oil cooler side of the engine. 
Install the connecting rod cap and capscrews to the connecting rod. Tighten 
capscrews to 35 Nm (26 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A23637A.gif]

Clean and remove all burrs from the cylinder block head deck. Zero Dial 
Indicator/Magnetic Base D78P-4201-B or equivalent.

[FIGURE: A23638A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not place the indicator tip on the anodized area.

Move the dial indicator over the piston, directly over the piston pin, 
to eliminate any side to side movement.

[FIGURE: A23665A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft to top dead center (TDC). Rotate the crankshaft 
clockwise and counterclockwise to find the highest dial indicator reading. 
Record the reading.

[FIGURE: A23666A.gif]

Remove the piston and connecting rod assembly from the No. 1 cylinder 
and install the assembly into the No. 2 cylinder. Repeat the procedure for 
every cylinder using the same piston and connecting rod.

[FIGURE: A23667A.gif]

Determine the grade of the piston being used for grading by referring 
to the chart. The four digits on top of the piston are the last four digits of 
the part number.

[FIGURE: A23668A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Cylinder Head 

 Disassembly 

The following disassembly and assembly procedure is provided for 
inspection purposes only. Refer to Cylinder Head in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section for complete rebuild instructions. 

Mark the intake valves and exhaust valves to identify their location.

[FIGURE: A17486A.gif]

Compress the valve spring and remove the valve stem collets.

[FIGURE: A17487A.gif]

Release valve spring. Remove the retainer and spring.

[FIGURE: A17403A.gif]

 CAUTION: Keep the valves in a labeled rack for a correct match with companion 
seats while making measurements. 

Remove the remaining collets, retainers and springs. Remove the intake 
valves and exhaust valves.

[FIGURE: A17488A.gif]

Remove the valve stem seals.

[FIGURE: A17489A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Clean all cylinder head components before assembling. 

Install the valve stem seals. The intake and exhaust seals are the same.

[FIGURE: A17490A.gif]

Lubricate the valve stems with SAE 90W engine oil before installing the 
intake valves and exhaust valves. 

Compress the valve spring, using a valve spring compressor tool, after 
assembling the spring and retainer.

[FIGURE: A17491A.gif]

Install new valve collets and release the valve spring compressor tool.

[FIGURE: A17492A.gif]

 CAUTION: Wear eye protection. If the collets are not correctly installed, they 
can fly out when the valve stems are hit with a hammer. 

After assembly, hit the valve stems with a plastic hammer to make sure 
that the collets are seated.

[FIGURE: A17493A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Piston and Connecting Rod 

 Disassembly 

Remove the retaining rings.

[FIGURE: A17494A.gif]

 NOTE: Heating the piston is not required.

Remove the piston pin.

[FIGURE: A17495A.gif]

Using a piston ring expander, remove the piston rings.

[FIGURE: A17496A.gif]

Clean and inspect the piston, pin and connecting rod as outlined under Cleaning and Inspection 
. 

 Piston-to-Cylinder Bore Fit 

Cylinder bore measurements are made from 25.4 mm (1.0 inch) below the 
cylinder to 144.3 mm (4.5 inch) below the cylinder. Orientation is parallel to 
the crankshaft. Record the measurements at these two places.

[FIGURE: A24931A.gif]

Measure piston diameter at right angles to the pin bore and 12 mm (0.47 
inch) from the bottom of the skirt.

[FIGURE: A24932A.gif]

Subtract the piston bore diameter from the cylinder bore diameter. 
Acceptable clearance is 0.113-0.293 mm (0.005-0.0115 inch).

 Assembly 

 CAUTION: If a piston ring expander tool is being used, be careful not to 
overexpand the piston ring. 

Be sure FRONT marking on piston and the numbers on the rod and 
connecting rod cap are oriented as illustrated.

[FIGURE: A17497A.gif]

Install the retaining ring in the piston pin retainer groove on the 
front side of the piston.

[FIGURE: A17498A.gif]

 NOTE: Pistons do not require heating to install the pin, however, the pistons 
do need to be at room temperature or above.

Lubricate the pin and piston pin bores with engine oil and install the 
pin. 

Install the second retaining ring.

[FIGURE: A17499A.gif]

Check the piston ring gap.

[FIGURE: A23677A.gif]

Position each piston ring in the cylinder and use a piston to square it 
with the bore. A = 89 mm (3.5 inch).

[FIGURE: A17501A.gif]

Use a feeler gauge to measure the piston ring gap.

[FIGURE: A17502A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Core Plugs

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Impact Slide Hammer

T59L-100-B

Impact Slide Hammer

T50T-100-A

 Removal 

To remove a large core plug, drill a 12.70-mm (0.5-inch) hole in the 
center of the plug and remove with Impact Slide Hammer T59L-100-B or 
T50T-100-A or pry it out with a large drift punch. On a small core plug, drill 
a 6.35-mm (0.25-inch) hole in the center of the plug and pry it out with a 
small pin punch.

Clean and inspect the plug bore. 

 Installation 

Inspect the plug bore for any damage that would interfere with the 
proper sealing of the plug. 

Coat the plug or bore lightly with an oil-resistant (oil galley) or 
Perfect Seal Sealing Compound B5A-19554-A or F2AZ-19554 or equivalent meeting 
Ford specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

Install the core plug in the bore following the procedure for cup-type 
or expansion-type below. 

 Cup-Type 

Cup-type core plugs are installed with the flanged edge outward. The 
maximum diameter of this plug is located at the outer edge of the flange. The 
flange on cup-type plugs flares outward with the largest diameter of the outer 
(sealing) edge.

 CAUTION: It is imperative to pull the plug into the machined bore by using a 
properly designed tool. Under no circumstances is the plug to be driven into 
the bore using a tool that contacts the flange. This method will damage the 
sealing edge and will result in leakage and/or plug blowout. 

[FIGURE: A3217E.gif]

Item

Sealing Edge Before Installation

 CAUTION: If the core plug replacing tool has a depth seating surface, do not 
seat the tool against a nonmachined (casting) surface. 

The flanged (trailing) edge must be below the chamfered edge of the 
bore to effectively seal the plugged bore. 

 Expansion-Type 

Expansion-type core plugs are installed with the flange edge inward. 
The maximum diameter of this plug is located at the base of the flange with 
the flange flaring inward.

 CAUTION: It is imperative to push or drive the plug into the machined bore using 
a properly designed tool. Under no circumstances is the plug to be driven 
using a tool that contacts the crowned portion of the plug. This method will 
expand the plug prior to installation and may damage the plug and/or plug 
bore. 

 CAUTION: If the core plug replacing tool has a depth seating surface, do not 
seat the tool against a nonmachined (casting) surface. 

When installed, the trailing (maximum) diameter must be below the 
chamfered edge of the bore to effectively seal the plugged bore. 

 Cylinder Block, Side 

 Removal 

Clean the area near the expansion plug of all debris.

[FIGURE: A24933A.gif]

Remove the large expansion plugs from the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A24934A.gif]

Thoroughly clean the expansion plug hole.

[FIGURE: A24935A.gif]

Visually inspect the core plug bore for damage.

[FIGURE: A24936A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Excessive sealant can run back into the engine and cause damage to 
other components. Allow the sealant to dry for a minimum of 2 hours before 
operating the engine. 

Apply a 2 mm (1/16 inch) bead of expansion plug lock 'N seal, Cummins 
part number 3375068 or equivalent to the outside diameter of the expansion 
plug and the inside diameter of the expansion plug bore.

[FIGURE: A24937A.gif]

 NOTE: The expansion plug must be installed with the edge of the expansion 
plug 0.5-1.0 mm (0.020-0.040 inch) deeper than the entrance chamfer of the bore.

Install the expansion plug.

[FIGURE: A24938A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Valve Tappets 

 CAUTION: Any time a new camshaft is installed, new tappets must also be installed. 

Clean the valve tappets with solvent and dry with compressed air.

Inspect the socket, stem and face for excessive wear, cracks and other 
damage. Visual limits: (A) normal contact (exaggerated); (B) and (C) irregular 
contact; do not reuse. 

[FIGURE: A17570C.gif]

Pit marks on the valve tappet face are acceptable. 

The following criteria define the size of the pits allowed. 

A single pit cannot be greater than 2 mm (0.078 inch). 

Interconnection of pits is not allowed. 

Total pits when added together should not exceed 6 mm (0.236 inch) 
diameter or a total of four percent of the valve tappet face. 

No pitting is allowable on the edges of the wear face of the valve 
tappet. 

[FIGURE: A17571A.gif]

Measure the valve tappet stem diameter for: minimum 15.936 mm (0.627 
inch) and maximum 15.977 mm (0.629 inch).

[FIGURE: A17572A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Camshaft Bearing

 Inspection 

Inspect the camshaft bearing for pitting or scoring. Measure the 
clearance between the internal diameter of the bearing and the outside 
diameter of the respective camshaft journal. If the clearance exceeds 0.184 mm 
(0.007 inch) remove and install a new bearing.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Camshaft Drive Gear and Thrust Plate

 Inspection 

Clean the gear, thrust plate and spacer in solvent. 

Check the gear and thrust plate for scores or nicks. Also, check the 
gear for the condition of the teeth wear pattern. Discard parts that show 
signs of excessive wear. 

Measure the thickness of the thrust plate. If the thrust plate is less 
than 9.340 mm (0.368 inch), discard the thrust plate and install a new one.

Check the keyway and key on the end of the camshaft. If the key is 
damaged, install a new key before installing the gear. Use a carborundum stone 
to remove minor gear teeth imperfections. If tooth wear or damage is severe, 
install a new gear.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Piston and Pin

 Cleaning 

 CAUTION: Be sure the cleaning solvent is approved for aluminum. Damage to the 
pistons can result. 

Allow the pistons to soak for a minimum of 30 minutes in a tank 
containing an approved cleaning solvent for aluminum.

 CAUTION: Do not clean the pistons and rods in an acid tank. 

 CAUTION: Do not use a metal brush. A metal brush will damage the piston ring 
grooves. Do not use glass beads to clean the grooves. Walnut shell or plastic 
bead blasting may be used on grooves with a ni-resist insert and on the dome 
or crown of the piston. Use the minimum effective pressure and do not 
concentrate the spray in one area for an extended period of time. The 
recommended blast pressure for plastic bead blasting is: 276 kPa (40 psi). Do 
not use glass beads or walnut shell blasting on the aluminum grooves or piston 
pin bores. This can cause the piston pin bore to crack or the piston rings to 
not seat. 

Wash the pistons and rods in a strong solution of laundry detergent in 
hot water. Use a non-metallic brush to remove carbon deposits.

 CAUTION: Do not use a piston ring groove cleaner. Be sure not to scratch the 
piston ring sealing surface in the piston ring groove. 

Clean the remaining deposits from the piston ring grooves with the 
square end of a broken piston ring. 

Wash the pistons again in a detergent solution or solvent. After 
rinsing, use compressed air to dry. 

 Inspection 

Inspect the piston for damage and excessive wear. Check the top, ring 
grooves, skirt and piston pin bore.

[FIGURE: A17533A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use pistons with cracks. 

Inspect the piston bowl, pin bore and skirt for cracks or other damage.

Measure the piston skirt diameter as illustrated: minimum 101.823 mm 
(4.0088 inch) and maximum 101.887 mm (4.0107 inch).

[FIGURE: A17534B.gif]

Use a new piston ring and feeler gauge to measure the clearance in the 
piston ring groove.

[FIGURE: A17535A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Piston Connecting Rods 

 WARNING: WHEN USING A STEAM CLEANER, WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES 
OR A FACE SHIELD. HOT STEAM CAN CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY. 

Use a nylon bristle brush to clean the oil drillings. 

Use steam or solvent to clean the connecting rods. Dry with compressed 
air. 

Inspect the connecting rods and connecting rod caps for damage. Replace 
the connecting rod if the I-beam portion is nicked or damaged.

[FIGURE: A17538A.gif]

Visually inspect the piston pin bore for damage or misalignment of the 
oil passage and bushing.

[FIGURE: A17539A.gif]

Measure the connecting rod piston pin bushing inside diameter (ID): 
minimum 40.019 mm (1.5756 inch) and maximum 40.033 mm (1.5761 inch).

[FIGURE: A17540A.gif]

Measure the connecting rod crank bore with the connecting rod bearing 
halves removed and the capscrews tightened to 100 Nm (73 
lb-ft). Minimum diameter should be no less than 72.987 mm (2.8735 inch) and 
maximum diameter should not exceed 73.013 mm (2.8745 inch). 

If the connecting rod crank bore measurements are not within 
specifications, replace the rod assembly.

[FIGURE: A17541A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Crankshaft

 CAUTION: A limited number of crankshaft main bearing or rod bearing journals 
will be ground 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) or 0.05 mm (0.002 inch) undersize in 
production. Engines equipped with undersize crankshafts will be identified 
with one of the following codes on the right front of the block near the 
engine code. 

 NOTE: If a new crankshaft is used, a piston grading procedure must be used. 
Refer to Piston Grading in the Removal and Installation portion in this section.

 Code 

 (M) — Undersize main bearing journals

 (P) — Undersize rod bearing journals

 (MP) — Undersize main and rod bearing 
journals.

 CAUTION: Handle the crankshaft with care to avoid possible damage to the 
finished surfaces. 

If the crankshaft gear teeth are excessively worn or chipped, install a 
new crankshaft gear which must be fully located on the shoulder of the 
crankshaft. Refer to Crankshaft Gear in the Removal and Installation portion 
of this section.

Clean the crankshaft with solvent, then blow out all oil passages with 
compressed air.

Measure the diameter of each journal in at least four places to 
determine an out-of-round, taper or undersize condition.

[FIGURE: A100941A.gif]

On an engine used with a manual transmission, check the fit of the 
clutch pilot bearing in the bore of the crankshaft. A needle roller bearing 
and adapter assembly is used as a clutch pilot bearing. It is press-fit 
directly into the engine crankshaft and should not be loose. Inspect the inner 
surface of the bearing for wear or a bell-mouth condition. Check the inside 
diameter of the bearing to see if it is worn or damaged. The bearing and 
adapter assembly cannot be serviced separately. The needle bearing clutch 
pilot can only be installed with the seal end of the bearing facing the 
transmission. The bearing and seal are pregreased and do not require 
additional lubrication. A new bearing must be installed whenever a bearing is 
removed.

Inspect the pilot bearing, when used, for roughness, evidence of 
overheating or loss of lubricant. Replace if any of these conditions are found.

Examine the rear oil seal journal for score marks, remove minor 
imperfections with fine emery cloth (600 grade). Clean journal around its 
circumference, not lengthwise. Clean the rear oil seal journal thoroughly with 
solvent after using emery cloth.

 Journals, Refinishing 

Dress minor imperfections such as scores, nicks or burrs with an oil 
stone. If the journals are severely marred or exceed the service limit, they 
should be refinished to size for the next undersize bearing. 

If required, machine the journals to give the proper clearance with the 
next undersize bearing. If the journals will not clean up to maximum undersize 
bearing available, replace the crankshaft. 

Always reproduce the same journal shoulder radius that existed 
originally. Too small a radius will result in fatigue failure of the 
crankshaft. Too large a radius will result in bearing failure due to radius 
ride of the bearing. 

After refinishing the journals, chamfer the oil holes. Polish the 
journal with a No. 320 grit polishing cloth and engine oil (crocus cloth may 
also be used as a polishing agent) to obtain a smooth finish.

 Cleaning

[FIGURE: A17512A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17516A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Flywheel 

 Automatic Transmission 

Inspect the flywheel for cracks or other damage that would make it 
unfit for further service. Inspect the flywheel ring gear for worn, chipped or 
cracked teeth. If the teeth are damaged, replace the ring gear and flywheel 
assembly. 

With the flywheel installed on the crankshaft, check the gear face 
runout. 

 Manual Transmission 

Inspect the flywheel for cracks, heat check, or other damage that would 
make it unfit for further service. Machine the friction surface of the 
flywheel if it is scored or worn. If it is necessary to remove more than 1.0 
mm (0.040 inch) of stock from the original thickness, replace the flywheel. 

Inspect the ring gear for worn, chipped or cracked teeth. If the teeth 
are damaged, replace the ring gear. 

With the flywheel installed on the crankshaft, check the flywheel face 
runout. Refer to Section 03-00 .

Oil Pan

 Cleaning

 Inspection

new oil pan if repairs cannot be made.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Oil Pump 

 Cleaning 

Wash all parts in a solvent and dry them thoroughly with compressed 
air. Use a brush to clean the inside of the pump housing and the pressure 
relief valve chamber. Make sure all dirt and metal particles are removed. 

 Inspection 

 NOTE: Internal components are not serviced. If any component is out of 
specification, the pump assembly must be replaced. 

Check the inside of the pump housing and the inner and outer gears for 
damage or excessive wear. 

Check the mating surface of the pump cover for wear. Minor scuff marks 
are normal, but if the cover, gears or housing surfaces are excessively worn, 
scored or grooved, replace the pump. Inspect the rotor for nicks, burrs or 
score marks. Remove minor imperfections with an oil stone. 

Measure the inner to outer rotor tip clearance with feeler gauge 
inserted 13 mm (0.5 inch) minimum. Inner and outer rotor tip clearance must 
not exceed 0.1778 mm (0.007 inch).

[FIGURE: A23430A.gif]

With the rotor assembly installed in the housing, place Straightedge 
D83L-4201-A or equivalent over the rotor assembly and the housing. 

Measure the vertical clearance (rotor end play) between the 
straightedge and both the inner rotor and the outer race. Maximum clearance 
must not exceed 0.127 mm (0.005 inch).

[FIGURE: A23431A.gif]

Measure clearance between outer rotor and housing in several areas 
around the circumference of the outer rotor. Clearance must not exceed 0.381 
mm (0.015 in.).

[FIGURE: A23432A.gif]

Measure backlash between oil pump drive gears. Backlash must not exceed 
0.33 mm (0.013 inch).

[FIGURE: A23433A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Head Deck 

 Cleaning 

 NOTE: Excessive deposits may be cleaned in an acid tank, but the camshaft 
bushings must first be removed to prevent damage.

Place clean lint-free rags over the pistons to prevent dirt from 
falling into the engine.

Plug or cover the coolant and oil passages in the cylinder block deck.

Use a gasket scraper to clean the cylinder block deck surface.

Use Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent and solvent to 
remove any residual gasket material from the cylinder block deck surface.

 WARNING: WHEN USING COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN CAPSCREW HOLES, ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY 
GLASSES OR A FACE SHIELD TO PROTECT THE EYES. PERSONAL INJURY CAN RESULT. 

 NOTE: Make sure the cylinder head capscrew holes are clean.

Use compressed air to clean debris from the capscrew holes.

Inspect the coolant passages. Buildup of deposits in the coolant 
passages can cause engine overheating. A large buildup of rust and lime will 
require removal of the cylinder block for cleaning in a hot tank.

Make sure the coolant passages are clean.

[FIGURE: A18331A.gif]

 Inspection 

 CAUTION: Do not proceed with the service if the cylinder block head deck is 
damaged or not flat. The engine will have to be removed for resurfacing the 
block. 

 NOTE: The cylinder block head deck can be resurfaced in a machine shop and a 
thicker surface head gasket installed to keep the piston-to-head clearance the 
same.

Use a straightedge and feeler gauge to measure the overall flatness of 
the cylinder head deck. The overall flatness, side-to-side, must not exceed 
0.075 mm (0.003 inch). The overall flatness, end-to-end, must not exceed 0.305 
mm (0.012 inch) with no more than 0.010 mm (0.0004 inch) variation within a 
50-mm (2-inch) diameter area. 

Visually inspect for any localized dips or imperfections. If present, 
the cylinder head deck must be reground.

[FIGURE: A17624A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Water Thermostat

 NOTE: If the problem being investigated is insufficient heat, the thermostat 
should be checked for leakage. This may be done by holding the thermostat up 
to a lighted background. Light leakage around the thermostat valve (thermostat 
at room temperature) is unacceptable and the thermostat should be replaced. On 
some thermostats, a slight leakage of light at one or two locations on the 
perimeter of the valve may be detected. This should be considered normal.

Remove the thermostat and immerse it in boiling water. Replace the 
thermostat if it does not open more than 6.35 mm (0.25 inch) after one minute 
in water.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cooling System 

 Rust or Dirt Contamination 

If the cooling system is contaminated by residual solids such as rust 
or dirt, the system should be cleaned by using Ford Premium Cooling System 
Flush F1AZ-19A503-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P7-A. 
Heavy rust or scale may require additional radiator cleaning service. 

 Oil Contamination 

If the cooling system is contaminated by oil: 

Determine the source or cause of the contamination and eliminate it. 

Drain the cooling system and fill with clean water containing two 
ounces per gallon of non-foaming automatic dishwasher detergent. 

Run the engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm. 

Drain the cooling system. Allow engine to cool. 

Refill with Ford Heavy Duty Diesel Engine Cooling System Fluid 
E6HZ-19549-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESE-M97B18-C.

================================================================================
PAGE 6243
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Lubrication System 

 NOTE: Also observe condition of coolant. If there is evidence of oil 
contamination in coolant, the cooling system should be cleaned following the 
directions outlined.

If the engine oil has been contaminated by coolant, the engine 
lubrication system must be cleaned. Determine the level/severity of 
contamination and proceed with the appropriate cleaning procedure.

 Contamination Slight to Moderate with No Sludging 

Defined as showing evidence of coolant in oil. 

Sludging is defined as gelled, slimy deposits attached to engine parts. 

 Contamination Heavy with Sludging 

Defined as showing heavy concentration of coolant in oil with sludging. 
Sludging is evidence of gelled, slimy deposits on parts under rocker cover and 
bottom end — oil pan area. 

Determine the source or cause of the contamination and eliminate it. 

 Cleaning — Slight to Moderate Contamination, No Sludge 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Remove 
crankcase breather element.

 WARNING: READ AND FOLLOW ALL STATEMENTS ON CLEANING SOLVENT CONTAINER TO MAKE 
SURE ENGINE OPERATES SAFELY. 

Mix 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) of kerosene with 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) 
of recommended engine oil and refill crankcase. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. 

Repeat Steps 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 one time. 

Fill crankcase with recommended engine oil. 

Replace crankcase breather element. 

 Cleaning — Heavy Contamination with Sludge 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

If sludge is heavy and built up, remove as much sludge deposit as 
possible from exposed engine parts, i.e., under rocker cover and lower end 
(oil pan removed) before proceeding further. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Remove 
crankcase breather element.

 WARNING: READ AND FOLLOW ALL STATEMENTS ON CLEANING SOLVENT CONTAINER TO MAKE 
SURE ENGINE OPERATES SAFELY. 

Mix 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) of commercially available cleaning solvent 
such as Butyl Cellosolve (Union Carbide) or Downol E-B (Dow Chemical) or 
Glycol Ether E-13 (Chem Central) or equivalent with 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) 
recommended engine oil and refill crankcase. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter.

 WARNING: READ AND FOLLOW ALL STATEMENTS ON CLEANING SOLVENT CONTAINER TO MAKE 
SURE ENGINE OPERATES SAFELY 

Mix 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) of commercially available cleaning solvent 
such as Butyl Cellosolve (Union Carbide) or Downol E-B (Dow Chemical) or 
Glycol Ether E-13 (Chem Central) or equivalent with 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) 
recommended engine oil and refill crankcase. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Fill the 
crankcase with the recommended engine oil. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove oil pan and inspect main and rod bearings for signs of distress. 
Replace bearings if necessary and replace oil pan. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Fill the 
crankcase with the recommended engine oil. Install new crankcase breather 
element.

ADJUSTMENTS

Valve Adjustment, Cold 

 CAUTION: Adjust the valves when the engine is cold — below 60°
C (140°F). 

 CAUTION: Be sure to disengage the pin after locating top dead center. 

 NOTE: Valve lash should be checked and adjusted at the first 32,000 km 
(20,000 miles) and thereafter at 64,000 km (40,000 mile) intervals. 

Use the timing pin to locate top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1, 
and then remove the valve covers.

[FIGURE: A17171A.gif]

 NOTE: The clearance is correct when some resistance is felt when the feeler 
gauge is slipped between the valve stem and the rocker lever. 

Valve lash is checked by inserting a feeler gauge between the rocker 
arm pad and the valve stem tip. Adjust the valves by loosening the lock nut 
and turning the adjusting screw.

[FIGURE: A17172A.gif]

Adjust the clearance for the valves shown in the illustration. 

Intake: 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) 

Exhaust: 0.51 mm (0.020 inch)

[FIGURE: A17173A.gif]

Tighten the lock nut to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft) and check the 
valve lash. 

 CAUTION: Be sure timing pin is disengaged before rotating the crankshaft. 

Mark the pulley and rotate the crankshaft 360 degrees.

[FIGURE: A17174A.gif]

Adjust the clearance for the valves shown in the illustration. 

Intake: 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) 

Exhaust: 0.51 mm (0.020 inch)

[FIGURE: A17175A.gif]

Tighten the lock nut to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft) and check the 
valve lash. 

Install the valve covers and gaskets. Tighten valve cover retaining 
bolts to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cooling System

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE THE RADIATOR CAP UNDER ANY CONDITIONS WHILE THE ENGINE IS 
OPERATING. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS CAN RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE 
COOLING SYSTEM OR ENGINE AND PERSONAL INJURY. 

TO AVOID HAVING SCALDING HOT COOLANT OR STEAM BLOW OUT OF THE RADIATOR, 
USE EXTREME CARE WHEN REMOVING THE CAP FROM A HOT RADIATOR. IF POSSIBLE, WAIT 
UNTIL THE ENGINE HAS COOLED, THEN WRAP A THICK CLOTH AROUND THE RADIATOR CAP 
AND TURN IT SLOWLY TO THE FIRST STOP. STEP BACK WHILE THE PRESSURE IS RELEASED 
FROM THE COOLING SYSTEM. WHEN YOU ARE SURE ALL THE PRESSURE HAS BEEN RELEASED, 
PRESS DOWN ON THE CAP (STILL WITH A CLOTH), TURN AND REMOVE IT. 

Refer to Section 03-03 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Thermostat, Water 

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to service the thermostat. It should be replaced if it 
is not operating properly. 

The poppet-type thermostat used in production is a high-temperature 
thermostat for use with a mixture of water and permanent-type coolant. Install 
a low-temperature thermostat if a nonpermanent type coolant and water solution 
is used (except on vehicles with automatic radiator shutters). 

Whenever changing the thermostat to a higher or lower temperature range 
on vehicles equipped with automatic shutters, always change the shutterstat to 
a corresponding higher or lower range. 

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery negative cables.

Drain the engine coolant. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Remove the air cleaner assembly.

Disconnect the air duct assembly at the turbocharger inlet.

Remove the accessory drive belt. Refer to Section 03A-05 .

Remove the bolts retaining the generator support strap (upper bracket) 
to the generator and the cylinder head, then remove the generator support strap.

Remove the generator pivot bolt, washers and nut, then reposition the 
generator away from the thermostat housing.

Remove retaining bolts, generator mounting bracket and water inlet 
support bracket.

Disconnect the upper radiator hose from the thermostat housing.

Remove the water outlet connection retaining bolts.

 Thermostat and Thermostat Housing 

[FIGURE: A24895A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

8592

2

8255

Thermostat Housing Gasket

3

8255

Water Outlet Connection Gasket

4

6E045

Lift Bracket

5

8575

Thermostat

Remove the thermostat housing, thermostat, and lift bracket from the 
cylinder head.

Remove the gasket and any residue from the thermostat housing.

 Installation 

Place the thermostat and a new gasket in the thermostat housing.

Position the thermostat housing and lift bracket on the cylinder head 
and install the retaining bolts. Tighten the water outlet connection retaining 
bolts to 21-27 Nm (15-20 lb-ft).

Connect the upper radiator hose to the thermostat housing.

Position the water inlet support bracket and generator mounting 
bracket, and install the retaining bolts. Tighten the bolt retaining both 
brackets to 55-65 Nm (41-48 lb-ft). Tighten the bolt 
retaining the water inlet support bracket to the thermostat housing to 30-40 Nm
 (22-30 lb-ft). Tighten the remaining bolt to 40-50 Nm
 (30-37 lb-ft).

Position the generator to the generator mounting bracket and install 
the generator pivot bolt, washers and nut. Do not tighten the pivot bolt at 
this time.

Install the generator support strap (upper bracket) and retaining 
bolts. Tighten the retaining bolts to 30-40 Nm (22-30 lb-ft).

Tighten the generator pivot bolt to 55-67 Nm (41-49 
lb-ft).

Install the accessory drive belt. Refer to Section 03A-05 .

Connect the air duct assembly to the turbocharger inlet.

Install the air cleaner assembly.

Fill the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Connect the battery negative cables.

Water Pump 

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery negative cables.

Drain the engine coolant. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Clean gasket sealing surfaces of cylinder block and water pump.

[FIGURE: A21473A.gif]

lb-ft).

Install the charge air cooler-to-intake manifold duct.

Fill the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Connect the battery negative cables.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator Lower Hose Tube 

The cooling system hoses must be replaced whenever they become cracked 
or deteriorated, or have a tendency to collapse. 

 Removal 

Partially drain the cooling system to replace cooling system upper 
(inlet) hose(s). Drain the cooling system to replace the lower radiator 
(outlet) hose. 

Loosen the clamps on each end of the hose(s) to be removed. Slide the 
hose(s) off the connections. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: If the connections have a single bead around the edges, make sure the 
clamps are located beyond the beads. If the connections have a double bead, 
make sure the clamp is located between the beads after assembly.

Position the clamps on each end of the new hose. Slide the hose onto 
the connections, then tighten the clamps. 

Fill the cooling system with coolant and bleed the system. Refer to 
 Section 03-03 . 

Operate the engine for several minutes, then check the hose(s) and 
connections for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator

When removing the radiator, place a support in front of the vehicle for 
the hood. Disconnect the hood support cables and swing the hood forward onto 
the support. This will give ample clearance for removing the radiator with the 
shroud attached. A hoist and sling are usually employed in lifting these 
radiators. 

 Removal 

Install hose on drain nipple and drain radiator coolant into a suitable 
container. 

Disconnect the spring-loaded hood support cables. 

 WARNING: USE EXTREME CARE AND OBSERVE ALL SAFETY AND SERVICE PRECAUTIONS RELATED 
TO THE USE OF REFRIGERANTS. REFER TO SECTION 12-00. 

Recover refrigerant from the air conditioning system (if necessary). 
Refer to Section 12-00 .

Remove transmission oil cooler (if so equipped) and set aside. Do not 
disconnect or drain oil cooler. 

Disconnect lower radiator hose. 

Remove the turbocharger-to-charge air cooler inlet pipe. 

Disconnect the radiator-to-radiator coolant recovery reservoir vent 
hose. 

Disconnect the radiator upper hose. 

Remove the charge air cooler-to-intake manifold tube. 

Disconnect the air conditioning compressor-to-condenser core hose (if 
necessary). 

Disconnect the air conditioning condenser core-to-orifice tube hose (if 
necessary). 

Remove seven plastic ties. 

Remove the hose and electrical support bracket.

Remove the two large (1/2-inch) lower mount retaining nuts and washers.

Remove the two radiator support-to-dash brace nuts, and position 
radiator support-to-dash brace out of way.

Attach lifting eyes and chain to two threaded studs in top of radiator 
assembly, and attach lifting equipment.

Remove the air conditioning condenser core retaining bolts (if so 
equipped).

Using lifting equipment and, with the aid of an assistant, remove 
radiator assembly from the vehicle.

Remove the screws and washers and remove shroud. 

Lower radiator to floor and remove lifting equipment and eye bolts.

Disassemble the module by removing the four bolts (manual) or two 
bolts/nuts (automatic), spring packs, steel plates and Teflon®
 pads that hold the charge air cooler to the radiator support frame.

Remove the charge air cooler.

Remove the nuts holding the gusset to vertical support at each other 
corner.

Remove the drain cock and de-aeration fitting as required.

The steel support members can now be removed by light tapping in a 
horizontal direction on the two vertical support members.

Remove the nuts on the two vertical strut rods.

Remove the radiator upper and lower frame supports.

Remove the rubber shock insulators from the four corners.

Service heat exchangers as required. Refer to Section 03-03 .

 Installation 

 NOTE: During the assembly process, use Ford Threadlock® 262 
E2FZ-19554-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 on all 
fasteners.

Install four corner rubber shock mounts on radiator.

Install radiator core to the lower frame.

Install upper radiator frame.

 NOTE: Do not tighten strut nuts.

Install vertical strut rods and two Nyloc nuts.

Install two radiator side frames by lightly tapping in a horizontal 
direction on the two vertical support members. Loosely install the fifteen 
nuts for the side frames and upper and lower frames. Insert a 6.4-mm 
(0.25-inch) drift into the eight assembly aid holes, to align marks in the 
frame member paint. Tighten the fifteen nuts to 34 Nm (25 
lb-ft). This will compress and secure the four corner shock mounts.

Tighten the vertical strut support nuts.

If removed, install the drain cock and de-aeration fitting.

Install the charge air cooler.

 NOTE: During the assembly process, use Ford Threadlock® 262 
E2FZ-19554-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 on all 
fasteners.

Assemble the module by installing the four bolts (manual) or two 
bolts/nuts (automatic), spring packs, steel plates and Teflon®
 pads that hold the charge air cooler to the radiator support frame. Tighten 
3/8-inch shoulder bolts to 34 Nm (25 lb-ft). Tighten 3/8-inch 
nuts to 34 Nm (25 lb-ft).

Position shroud and install retaining screws and washers.

Use suitable lifting equipment and with the aid of an assistant, lift 
radiator into position and install two (1/2-inch) lower mount retaining bolts 
and washers. After cleaning threads, apply Ford Threadlock® 
262 E2FZ-19554-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6. 
Tighten to 75-102 Nm (55-75 lb-ft). 

Position condenser on radiator and install retaining bolts.

Remove lifting equipment and lifting eyes. 

Install the charge air cooler-to-intake manifold tube. 

Install the turbocharger-to-charge air cooler inlet pipe. 

Connect radiator support-to-dash brace to radiator.

Connect the air conditioning condenser core-to-orifice tube (if 
necessary).

Connect the air conditioning compressor-to-condenser core hose (if 
necessary). 

Install the hose and electrical support bracket.

Connect the upper and lower radiator hoses. 

Connect vent hose to coolant recovery reservoir. 

Install the transmission oil cooler. 

Install the seven plastic ties for overflow hose and other hoses. 

With the aid of an assistant connect the spring-loaded hood support 
cables. 

Fill and purge coolant system. Refer to Section 03-03 . 

Evacuate and recharge air conditioning system. Refer to Section 12-00 . 

Check system for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator Coolant Recovery Reservoir 

 Removal 

 WARNING: DO NOT STAND IN LINE WITH OR NEAR RADIATOR COOLING FAN WHEN REVVING 
ENGINE. 

Drain the radiator until the coolant is out of the supply tank. 
Disconnect the radiator draw down hose at the supply tank. Disconnect the 
radiator vent tube at the supply tank, if so equipped. 

Remove the overflow tube from the supply tank. Remove the supply tank 
bracket retaining bolt(s) and remove the supply tank. 

 Installation 

Position the supply tank in the chassis and install the bracket 
retaining bolt(s). 

Connect the radiator draw down hose, overflow tube and vent tube, if so 
equipped, to the supply tank. 

Fill and bleed the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 . Check for 
coolant leaks and proper coolant level after the engine reaches normal 
operating temperatures.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fittings, Vehicles with Automatic Transmission and Radiator Bottom 
Tank Oil Coolers 

Use a waterproof sealer such as Pipe Sealant with Teflon®
 D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
WSK-M2G2350-A2 and ESR-M18P7-A when assembling fittings such as the drain cock 
to the radiator.

When installing a new radiator in a vehicle equipped with automatic 
transmission, transfer the oil cooler line fittings from the old radiator and 
install them in the new radiator, using oil-resistant sealer.

When installation of the radiator is complete, check the oil cooler 
line connections for leaks. Check the transmission fluid level and fill, if 
necessary.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel System Flow

Fuel from the tank (under suction) is routed to the prefilter and then 
to the transfer pump that is mounted on the left side of the engine. After 
going through the transfer pump, the fuel is pumped under pressure through the 
fuel filter and water separator. Once the fuel is filtered it goes to the fuel 
gallery of the fuel injection pump.

The FD-1060 and FD-1460 diesel engines use a fuel prefilter and a 
secondary filter/water separator assembly to make sure only clean fuel gets to 
the fuel injection pump. The use of properly filtered fuel cannot be 
overemphasized because of the tight clearances in the fuel injection pump and 
fuel injection nozzles. Never bypass the fuel filters.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Injection Pump

When the ignition key is turned to run, the rack inside the injection 
pump moves to the START position and allows fuel entering the injection pump 
to fill the pumping elements.

Fuel is distributed through individual pumping elements and on to each 
cylinder through high pressure fuel tubes. Fuel pressure and quantity is 
controlled by the action of the camshaft opening and closing the plungers and 
the control rack position of the individual pumping elements. Refer to Delivery Valve 
 in the Description and Operation portion of this section for 
further information.

A shutoff lever is used for engine shutdown. When the lever is moved in 
the direction to shut down the engine, the control rack is pulled to the stop 
position. At this time, no fuel is delivered to the engine.

Surplus fuel is provided to the fuel injection pump and injection 
nozzles for cooling and lubrication.

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to service the fuel injection pump. Service is to be 
performed only by authorized service centers. 

The fuel injection pump is mounted at the front left side of the 
engine. It is driven by a gear timed to the camshaft gear. The fuel injection 
pump is not a serviceable component and should not be tampered with. Tampering 
with the injection pump can void the warranty.

The fuel injection pump is of the constant stroke, in-line type, driven 
at half engine speed by the timing gears. There is one pumping element per 
cylinder actuated through roller tappets by a fully enclosed camshaft. The 
pumping elements are responsible for accurately metering and delivering the 
fuel to the fuel injectors.

Each of the pumping elements includes a barrel and plunger closely 
toleranced to give an accurate fit. Fuel is admitted to each pumping element 
by two bores on either side of the barrel. The barrel is splined, with a 
master spline for correct location within the pump body.

================================================================================
PAGE 6262
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-04A: Fuel Injection, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Delivery Valve

A delivery valve is located above each plunger on the Bosch P-7100 
In-Line Pump inside each high-pressure outlet fitting. The delivery valve 
allows fuel under injection pressure to move into the high-pressure tubes and 
also allows some drain-back to occur. The delivery valve also serves to 
rapidly reduce pressure in the injection tube once pressure from the plunger 
has ceased. Rapid pressure reduction is required to make certain the injector 
needle valve snaps shut to prevent fuel "dribble," a condition which can cause 
carbon formation on the injector tip and abnormal exhaust smoke.

Pumping element operation is detailed in the following steps and 
illustration.

With the plunger at the bottom of the stroke (A), fuel flows into the 
barrel through the spill port and fills the space above the plunger.

As the plunger (B) rises, the spill port in the barrel is covered and 
the fuel is trapped. This is the point of port closure. The continued upward 
movement of the plunger pressurizes the trapped fuel until the delivery valve 
(at the base of each high-pressure injection tube) is lifted from its seat. 
High-pressure fuel is transmitted through the tube to the injector and 
injection takes place through the injector nozzle.

Injection stops (C) when the upper edge of the helix uncovers the lower 
edge of the spill port. Pressure escapes to the fuel gallery. The drop in 
pressure causes the injector to close and injection to stop. After fuel 
delivery, the plunger continues to the top of the stroke and is returned by a 
spring for the next cycle.

Because the end of delivery is reached when the helix on the plunger 
uncovers the spill port (D), the amount of fuel delivered is varied by turning 
the pump plunger. If the plunger is turned until the vertical groove 
completely uncovers the spill port during the entire lift of the plunger, 
there will be no fuel delivered to the engine (E). This is because injection 
pressure cannot be reached, thereby shutting off the engine.

The plungers are rotated by a control rack splined to each plunger. 
Rack movement is determined by the control rod actuated by the throttle and 
governor.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Governor

An all-speed mechanical governor is used on the pump to regulate fuel 
at all engine speeds and loads. The governor also contains the boost control 
device (for starting) and the fuel shutoff solenoid. The governor is to be 
serviced only at authorized service centers. Tampering with the governor may 
void the warranty.

[FIGURE: A17764A.gif]

All engines are equipped with a boost control. This device limits the 
fuel during periods of low turbocharger boost. Smoke is kept to a minimum 
because the engine is provided with a fuel charge closely matched to the 
amount of air available in the combustion chamber. Operation of the device is 
quite simple. A diaphragm (which is connected via linkage to the control rack) 
inside the housing is exposed to boost pressure via a tube from the intake 
manifold. The other side of this diaphragm is exposed to reference spring 
pressure. When boost pressure drops, the spring forces the diaphragm back, 
pulling the control rack in a fuel decrease direction. This limits the amount 
of fuel available to the engine, which helps prevent excess smoke. This device 
is not to be adjusted or serviced except at authorized service centers.

[FIGURE: A17875A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Injector Nozzle Assemblies

The injector nozzles used in the six-cylinder diesel are of the 
inwardly opening, hydraulically operated, hole type. The injector nozzle 
assembly consists of two subassemblies: the nozzle body and nozzle holder. A 
section view of the injection nozzle assembly is shown.

[FIGURE: V43231A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Nozzle Holder

The nozzle holder is used to hold the nozzle in its correct position in 
the cylinder head and to provide channels for conducting diesel fuel to the 
nozzle valve.

================================================================================
PAGE 6266
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-04A: Fuel Injection, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Nozzle

The nozzle valve consists of two parts: needle valve and nozzle. These 
parts are precision machined and lapped to form an extremely close fitting 
matched set. The nozzle has a cone-shaped area on which the needle valve 
seats. There are holes in the nozzle through which fuel is injected into the 
engine combustion chamber. The use of multihole injectors is necessary in 
direct injection diesel engines because they provide a uniform distribution of 
fuel throughout the combustion chamber.

 CAUTION: The pressure of the fuel in the high pressure tube is sufficient to 
penetrate the skin and cause serious bodily harm. 

 NOTE: Fuel pressure generated by the fuel injection pump must overcome the 
counterforce of the pressure spring before the needle valve lifts off its seat.

The injector is operated by fuel pressure generated by the fuel 
injection pump. Fuel under high pressure acts on the exposed annular (ring 
shaped) area of the needle valve and lifts it from its seat.

The fuel is then injected through the nozzle orifices into the 
combustion chamber.

 NOTE: Opening pressure is adjustable by changing the initial tension on the 
pressure spring in the nozzle holder. This is accomplished by changing the 
shim thickness on the spring seat.

The opening pressure is determined by the initial tension of the 
pressure spring.

The needle valve lift is limited by the annular face at the base of the 
valve stem.

During injection, fuel takes the following path: fuel injection tubing 
to the fuel inlet passage of the nozzle holder, onto the inlet passages, 
pressure chamber and spray orifices of the nozzle, and then into the 
combustion chamber. Fuel leaking past the valve stem is returned to the fuel 
tank via the leak-off connection on the nozzle holder which is attached to the 
fuel return tube.

After injection of the fuel delivered by the injection pump, the 
pressure spring forces the needle valve back on its seat via the spindle and 
needle valve stem. The injection is then closed for the next pressure stroke. 
Fuel dribble should not occur, as might happen if the nozzle showed excessive 
wear.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Shutoff Solenoid

When the key is switched off, the fuel shutoff solenoid shuts off fuel 
by forcing the fuel pump control lever to the fuel-off position. When the key 
is switched to run, power applied to the solenoid pulls the fuel pump control 
lever to the fuel-open position, allowing fuel delivery and engine combustion. 
While the engine is running, power is continuously applied to the solenoid and 
continues to hold the control lever to the fuel-open position.

 NOTE: In instances of a no-start condition where the engine turns over 
normally and all correct starting procedures are being followed, inspect the 
fuel shutoff solenoid to make sure it is moving the fuel pump control lever 
when the key is turned to run and off. In some cases it may be necessary to 
adjust the length of the fuel shutoff solenoid rod. Refer to Fuel Shutoff 
Solenoid Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

 Disassembly 

 CAUTION: The hand-prime fitting and inlet fitting are spring-loaded. Sudden

[FIGURE: A17829A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Injection Pump

 CAUTION: Do not wash or steam clean the engine while it is running or still hot 
from running. Serious damage to the engine could occur. 

 NOTE: Before removing any fuel tubes, clean the exterior of the fuel 
injection pump with clean fuel oil or solvent to help prevent the entry of 
dirt or other contamination. The area can be steam cleaned, but this can only 
be done when the engine is cold and shut off.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Steering Wheel Puller

T67L-3600-A

 Removal 

Disconnect all fuel tubes (supply tube, high-pressure tubes and 
pressure relief valve) at injection pump.

Disconnect throttle control linkage.

Disconnect air fuel control tube from pump.

Disconnect wastegate control tube from pump.

For FD-1060, disconnect the external oil feed tube at the inboard side 
of the fuel injection pump and the main oil rifle.

 NOTE: Once top dead center (TDC) is located, make sure TDC timing pin is 
completely disengaged from camshaft sprocket.

Using Engine Barring Tool Kit D92T-6000-A or equivalent, locate top 
dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1. Slowly turn the engine while pushing on 
the TDC timing pin until timing pin drops into the hole in the camshaft 
sprocket.

Remove the fuel injection pump mounting bracket.

Remove the gear housing access cap. Remove the nut and washer from the 
fuel injection pump shaft.

Attach Steering Wheel Puller T67L-3600-A to the fuel injection pump 
drive gear and turn forcing screw until fuel injection pump drive gear comes 
loose from fuel injection pump shaft.

[FIGURE: A17780A.gif]

Remove the four mounting nuts. Remove the fuel injection pump.

[FIGURE: A17789A.gif]

 Installation 

Make sure the engine has cylinder No. 1 at TDC.

 NOTE: The fuel injection pump timing pin is located inside the access plug at 
the governor housing. To set fuel injection pump timing, the timing pin must 
be turned backwards inside the plug so the slot will fit into timing tooth of 
the pump. Refer to the following steps.

The fuel injection pump also has a timing pin, located in the governor 
housing. This pin is used to position the fuel injection pump shaft to 
correspond with top dead center for cylinder No. 1.

Remove the access plug from fuel injection pump governor housing.

[FIGURE: A17790A.gif]

Remove the timing pin from access plug.

[FIGURE: A17791A.gif]

If the timing tooth is not aligned with the timing pin hole, rotate the 
fuel injection pump shaft until the timing tooth aligns as shown.

[FIGURE: A17792A.gif]

Reverse the position of the timing pin so the slot of the timing pin 
will fit over the timing tooth in the fuel injection pump. Install and secure 
the timing pin with the access plug.

[FIGURE: A17793A.gif]

Use a 50/50 mixture of clean engine oil and STP® or 
equivalent to lubricate the gear housing bore to make sure the fuel injection 
pump will slide easily into the gear housing.

[FIGURE: A17794A.gif]

Lubricate the O-ring and mounting flange of the fuel injection pump.

[FIGURE: A17795A.gif]

 NOTE: The fuel injection pump shaft has a provision for a Woodruff key; 
however, it is not required. Timing mark alignment is not required for the 
fuel injection pump drive gear.

 NOTE: Make sure fuel injection pump shaft and gear taper is clean of oil and 
dry.

Slide the fuel injection pump shaft through the fuel injection pump 
drive gear and position the fuel injection pump flange onto the mounting studs.

[FIGURE: A17796A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to pull the fuel injection pump flange into the gear 
housing with the mounting nuts as damage to gear housing will occur. 

 NOTE: Push the fuel injection pump forward until the mounting flange and 
O-ring are properly fitted into the gear housing bore.

Install the mounting nuts. Tighten to 43 Nm (32 lb-ft).

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the timing pin, do not exceed the torque value 
given. This is not the final torque value for the fuel injection pump shaft nut. 

Install the fuel injection pump shaft nut and washer. Tighten to 10-15 Nm
 (7-11 lb-ft).

Disengage the engine timing pin.

Remove the fuel injection pump timing pin access plug. Reverse the 
position of the timing pin and reinstall the timing pin, access plug, and 
sealing washer. Tighten access plug to 40 Nm (30 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17797A.gif]

Tighten the fuel injection pump shaft nut to a final torque value of 165 Nm
 (122 lb-ft). Install the gear housing access cap hand-tight.

Install the fuel injection pump mounting bracket capscrews.

[FIGURE: A17798A.gif]

Connect all fuel tubes (supply tube, high-pressure tubes and pressure 
relief valve) to injection pump. Tighten low-pressure supply tube to 15 Nm
 (11 lb-ft). Tighten high-pressure tubes to 30 Nm
 (22 lb-ft).

Connect wastegate control tube.

On the FD-1060, install the external oil feed tube at the inboard side 
of the fuel injection pump and the main oil rifle. Connect wastegate tube to 
turbocharger.

Connect throttle control linkage. Check for stop-to-stop throttle 
travel, and proper operation of breakover mechanism.

 CAUTION: The governor housing must be prelubricated before engine operation. 
Failure to do so will result in premature governor wear. 

Add 750 ml (0.71 qt) of clean engine oil to the governor housing.

 WARNING: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES OR A PROTECTIVE FACE SHIELD WHEN WORKING WITH 
HIGH-PRESSURE FUEL. KEEP EYES AND HANDS AWAY FROM NOZZLE SPRAY. FUEL SPRAYING 
FROM THE NOZZLE UNDER HIGH PRESSURE CAN PENETRATE THE SKIN AND CAUSE BLOOD 
POISONING. MEDICAL ATTENTION SHOULD BE PROVIDED IMMEDIATELY IN THE EVENT OF 
SKIN PENETRATION. 

Vent the high-pressure fuel tubes. Loosen the fitting at the No. 1 
injector. Place the fuel injection pump control lever in the run position. 
Crank the engine so air can bleed from the fuel tubes. Then tighten the 
fitting to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft).

Vent each high-pressure tube separately until the engine runs smoothly.
