REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Injection Tubes

 Low-Pressure Fuel Injection Tube 

 Removal 

Remove fuel tube from fuel transfer pump.

[FIGURE: A17801A.gif]

Remove fuel drain manifold tube at filter adapter.

[FIGURE: A17802A.gif]

Remove low-pressure fuel tube from filter adapter.

[FIGURE: A17803A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: When replacing fuel tubes, replace banjo sealing washers each time they 
are removed. 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order. 

Bleed tube by opening banjo bleed screw and operate priming button on 
transfer pump until fuel flow from fitting is free of air. 

Tighten banjo bleed screw to 32 Nm (24 lb-ft).

 Injection Pump Supply Tube 

 Removal 

Remove banjo capscrew and sealing washers at filter adapter.

[FIGURE: A17806A.gif]

Remove banjo fitting capscrew and sealing washers at fuel injection 
pump inlet.

[FIGURE: A17807A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: When replacing fuel tubes, replace sealing washers each time they are 
removed. 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten fittings to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft).

 High-Pressure Fuel Tubes 

 Removal 

Fuel injection high-pressure tubes may be replaced one at a time, 
without having to remove the entire set from the engine. If all tubes are to 
be replaced, go to Step 4.

Remove clamping devices holding tubes together, then remove connections 
at delivery valves and injector nozzles.

Replace damaged tube(s), making connections at injector nozzles and 
delivery valves first, then reinstall clamping devices.

If all high-pressure tubes are to be removed, refer to the following 
procedure.

 WARNING: DO NOT BLEED A HOT ENGINE AS THIS COULD CAUSE FUEL TO SPILL ONTO A HOT 
EXHAUST MANIFOLD CREATING A DANGER OF FIRE. 

 WARNING: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES OR A PROTECTIVE FACE SHIELD WHEN WORKING WITH 
HIGH-PRESSURE FUEL. KEEP EYES AND HANDS AWAY FROM NOZZLE SPRAY. FUEL SPRAYING 
FROM THE NOZZLE UNDER PRESSURE CAN PENETRATE THE SKIN AND CAUSE BLOOD 
POISONING. MEDICAL ATTENTION SHOULD BE PROVIDED IMMEDIATELY IN THE EVENT OF 
SKIN PENETRATION. 

Clean area around fuel tubes at injection pump and nozzles.

Disconnect high-pressure tubes from injectors. Cap each tube and 
injector to prevent the entry of dirt into the system.

[FIGURE: A17808A.gif]

 NOTE: Use two wrenches to prevent delivery valve holder from turning.

Remove tube clamp capscrews from intake manifold.

[FIGURE: A17809A.gif]

Remove tubes from injection pump.

[FIGURE: A17811A.gif]

 Installation 

Follow the removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten fuel tube connections to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft). 
Start engine and vent one tube at a time until the engine runs smoothly.

 Injector Leak-Off Tube 

 Removal 

Clean area around injector leak-off tube.

Remove capscrews from hold-down clamps, where applicable.

Remove banjo fittings and washers from nozzle bodies.

[FIGURE: A17813A.gif]

Disconnect injector leak-off tube connections.

[FIGURE: A17814A.gif]

Remove injector leak-off tube.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Use new washers for fittings. 

 CAUTION: Be very careful to avoid cross-threading the banjo bolts into the 
nozzle body. 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten banjo fittings to 9 Nm (80 lb-in) and 
connections to 13 Nm (10 lb-ft). 

Once all connections are secure, start engine and check connections for 
fuel leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Filter/Water Separator

 Removal 

The fuel filter is a spin-on type filter mounted to a manifold located 
on the left side of the engine. The prefilter (sedimentor) is also mounted to 
the manifold. The filter/water separator is replaced as part of the scheduled 
maintenance unless it becomes plugged and must be replaced sooner. The fuel 
prefilter is unscrewed from the manifold and the filter screen is cleaned or 
replaced during scheduled maintenance or when it becomes plugged with sediment.

 Installation 

When installing a new filter, fill with clean, fresh diesel fuel and 
coat the seal with diesel fuel. Hand-tighten filter until it seats firmly 
against the mount, then hand-tighten an additional one-half to three-quarters 
turn. Start engine and check for leaks.

It may be necessary to bleed the system after installing fuel filters. 
Refer to Bleeding Fuel System or Restarting After 
Running Out of Fuel in the Adjustments portion of this section.

[FIGURE: A17815A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Filter/Water Separator Manifold

Perform the following only if manifold is leaking.

 Removal 

Remove fuel filter and water separator using suitable oil filter wrench.

Remove retainer nut from filter mount stud.

Using a large flat-bladed screwdriver, remove filter mount stud.

Remove manifold and O-rings. Clean manifold surfaces.

[FIGURE: A17816A.gif]

 Installation 

 WARNING: BE SURE TO ALIGN MARKS ON MANIFOLD AND CYLINDER HEAD. FAILURE TO DO SO 
MAY CAUSE ADAPTER TO CRACK AND FUEL TO LEAK. 

 NOTE: Be sure to use new O-rings to guard against leaks. Also, fill fuel 
filter and water separator with clean fuel prior to installation.

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten fuel filter mount stud with screwdriver and tighten retainer 
nut to 32 Nm (24 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Injector Nozzle

 NOTE: The injector nozzles are not to be disassembled. They are serviced as 
an assembly at an approved service center.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Impact Slide Hammer

T50T-100-A

Fuel System Protector Cap Set

T86T-9395-A

 Removal 

Before removing nozzle assemblies, clean the exterior of each nozzle 
assembly and the surrounding area with clean fuel oil or solvent to prevent 
the entry of dirt into the engine when the nozzle assemblies are removed. 
Also, clean the fuel inlet and fuel drain manifold connections. Blow dry with 
compressed air.

Loosen the high-pressure fuel tube going into the injection nozzle. It 
will pull off to the side enough to get the injector out. Place a cap on the 
high-pressure fuel tube opening to prevent the entry of dirt.

Remove the fuel drain manifold banjo bolt from the injection nozzle. 
There is an "earmuff"-type copper washer sealing both sides of banjo fitting. 
This washer must be discarded and replaced.

 CAUTION: When rust has formed on the hold-down nut, the injector can turn in the 
bore when the nut is loosened. This will cause severe damage to the head by 
the injector locating ball cutting a groove in the bore. 

Soak the hold-down nut with Penetrating Lubricant E8AZ-19A501-B or 
equivalent, for a minimum of 3 minutes.

[FIGURE: A17819A.gif]

Hit the injector body with the brass drift to loosen any rust.

[FIGURE: A17820A.gif]

 CAUTION: Damage to the cylinder head will result if the injector is allowed to 
turn while loosening the hold-down nut. 

Hold the injector body with an adjustable wrench while you loosen the 
hold-down nut with a 24-mm box wrench.

[FIGURE: A17821A.gif]

 NOTE: Injector Remover Adapter D92T-9000-A or equivalent can be used to 
remove injector nozzles from cylinders 2, 3 and 4. Use Injector Removal Tool 
Kit D92T-9000-B or equivalent to remove other injector nozzles.

Remove injector from bore. If injector is tight and will not come out 
by hand, attach Injector Remover Adapter D92T-9000-A or equivalent and Impact 
Slide Hammer T50T-100-A to the injector. Pull up on the slide hammer with 
enough force to free the injector. Remove copper washer from bore if it 
doesn't come out with injector.

[FIGURE: A17822A.gif]

Cover the nozzle tip with Fuel System Protector Cap Set T86T-9395-A to 
prevent the entry of dirt.

 Installation 

To install, refer to Stuck Fuel Injectors, Installation, in this section.

 Stuck Fuel Injectors 

 Removal 

If the injectors in cylinder Nos. 1, 5 and 6 are stuck and won't come 
out even after soaking, they may be removed using Injector Removal Tool Kit 
D92T-9000-B or equivalent. Refer to the following instructions.

Attach adapter to the threaded end of the forcing screw.

 CAUTION: Once all slack is taken up, do not turn the forcing screw. The injector 
may turn in its bore and damage to the cylinder head will result. 

Position bridge over the stuck injector and thread the adapter onto the 
injector and take up all slack by turning the hex nut.

Using a 1/2-inch open end wrench to hold the forcing screw, turn the 
hex nut using a 1-1/8 inch open end wrench until the injector is removed from 
the head.

 Installation 

 NOTE: All used nozzle assemblies should be tested for opening pressure, tip 
leakage and spray pattern before installation. Refer to the 1996 Powertrain 
Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual for the appropriate procedure.

Thoroughly clean the nozzle bore in the cylinder head before 
reinserting the nozzle assembly. Use Nozzle Cleaning Kit D83T-9000-G or 
equivalent to perform this job. Pay particular attention to seating surface, 
in order that no small particles of metal or carbon will cause the assembly to 
be cocked or permit blow-by of combustion gasses. Blow out the particles with 
compressed air.

Remove the protective cap from the nozzle tip and install a new copper 
gasket. Use a small daub of Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent 
grease meeting Ford specifications ESR-M1C159-A and ESB-M1C93-B to hold the 
washer in place during installation.

Apply a light coat of anti-seize compound to the threads of the 
injector hold-down nut and between the top of the nut and injector body.

[FIGURE: A17823A.gif]

 CAUTION: Align the injector's protrusion with the notch in the bore. 

Install the injector into the cylinder head injector bore. Tighten to 60 Nm
 (44 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17824A.gif]

Position the O-ring into the groove at the top of the hold-down nut.

 CAUTION: Do not overtighten banjo bolts. They are hollow and may break if 
overtightened. 

Install fuel drain manifold with banjo bolts and washers.

Remove the protective cap from the high-pressure fuel injection tube. 
Install the tube on the injector. Tighten the connecting nut to 30 Nm
 (22 lb-ft).

Start the engine.

If necessary, purge the high-pressure fuel tubes of air. Loosen the 
connectors of the serviced injectors one at a time, one-half to one turn while 
cranking the engine. Crank the engine until solid fuel, free from bubbles, 
flows from the connection.

 WARNING: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES OR A PROTECTIVE FACE SHIELD WHEN WORKING WITH 
HIGH-PRESSURE FUEL. KEEP EYES AND HANDS AWAY FROM NOZZLE SPRAY. FUEL SPRAYING 
FROM THE NOZZLE UNDER HIGH PRESSURE CAN PENETRATE THE SKIN AND CAUSE BLOOD 
POISONING. MEDICAL ATTENTION SHOULD BE PROVIDED IMMEDIATELY IN THE EVENT OF 
SKIN PENETRATION. 

Check for fuel leakage at the high-pressure connections.

ADJUSTMENTS

Bleeding Fuel System or Restarting After Running Out of Fuel

Restarting an engine that has run out of fuel is made difficult by the 
fact that after fuel is exhausted from the fuel tank, air then enters the 
sediment bowl, fuel filter/water separator and the fuel supply becomes 
insufficient to sustain engine firing. These assemblies must be refilled with 
fuel and the fuel tubes purged of air before the system can provide adequate 
fuel to the injectors to start the engine.

Follow these steps in restarting a fuel-depleted engine.

Fill the fuel tank with clean fuel. If only partial filling of the tank 
is possible, add a minimum of five gallons of fuel to make sure priming can be 
achieved and the engine can run for a short time.

Purge the air from the fuel system as follows:

 NOTE: If the primer will not pump fuel, either there is an air leak in the 
system, the primer is not functioning properly, or the plunger or arm is on 
the top of a cam lobe. Rotate engine 180 degrees and try to prime pump.

Depress primer button until effort to stroke primer increases, then 
stroke an additional 15 strokes (approximately 60 strokes total).

[FIGURE: V9976A.gif]

Open fuel filter vent screw until fuel and air bubbles appear. Allow 
1-1/2 to 2 minutes bleed time until air bubbles and fuel flow cease and the 
fuel system has lost its pressure. During this period, air is "back flowing" 
from the injection pump.

[FIGURE: A17827A.gif]

Close filter vent screw.

Stroke primer 10 times.

 CAUTION: Check filter vent screw after engine starts to make sure there are no 
fuel leaks. 

Start engine as follows:

Crank engine and while cranking, depress accelerator pedal to floor.

Engine should start in three to eight seconds of cranking, run rough 
for 5-10 seconds, and will either smooth out or stall. (Note: Keep accelerator 
to floor during rough running until clear and running smooth, then throttle 
back.)

If stall occurs, up to 15 seconds of additional cranking may be 
required to restart engine without additional priming.

If engine does not start, repeat Steps 2 and 3 to clear additional air 
from fuel system and start engine.

Venting High-Pressure Tubes

 WARNING: THE PRESSURE OF THE FUEL IN THE TUBE IS SUFFICIENT TO PENETRATE THE

 WARNING: DO NOT BLEED A HOT ENGINE AS THIS COULD CAUSE FUEL TO SPILL ONTO A HOT

smoothly.

ADJUSTMENTS

Fuel Shutoff Solenoid Adjustment

 NOTE: Do not turn the ignition key to the START position. The white (pull-in) 
wire will be energized.

Turn the ignition key to the ON position. This will energize the red 
(hold-in) wire and black (ground) wire.

[FIGURE: A17751A.gif]

Move the shutoff lever by hand to the full run (energized) position.

[FIGURE: A17752A.gif]

Adjust the solenoid linkage as necessary so that the plunger is 
magnetically held in with the shutoff lever in the absolute full run position. 
Turn the large hex on the end of the plunger to make adjustment as required.

[FIGURE: A17753A.gif]

With the solenoid energized, measure between the bottom of the solenoid 
bracket and the top of the horizontal pin on the lever. This measurement 
should equal 66.9 mm (2.64 inches). If not to specification, readjust linkage 
as required.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Turbocharger System

A turbocharger system uses the energy in the flow of exhaust gases to 
increase engine power and efficiency. These increases occur when the 
turbocharger converts the exhaust flow into a pressurized airflow on the 
intake side of the engine. Because more air is available to support 
combustion, additional fuel can be injected into the cylinders. It is the 
combination of additional fuel and a more complete scavenging of exhaust gases 
from the cylinders that produces the increased engine horsepower.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Turbine

The turbocharger consists of two operating elements, a turbine and a 
compressor, which are installed on opposite ends of a common shaft. The 
turbine is enclosed in a housing connected to the exhaust manifold. Exhaust 
gases entering the housing are directed against the turbine wheel blades, 
causing it to spin at more than 100,000 rpm (engine under load).

================================================================================
PAGE 6287
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-04B: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Compressor

Spinning at turbine speed, the compressor draws air through the intake 
filter and delivers it, under pressure, to the engine intake. The air is 
pressurized by the centrifugal force and the internal shape of the compressor 
housing. As air enters and is thrown outward against the housing, it flows 
through passages that narrow and compress the air as it approaches the 
turbocharger outlet. Air leaving the outlet is routed through a duct to the 
charge air cooler and then through another duct to the engine intake.

[FIGURE: V4308B.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wastegate Actuator

The wastegate regulates the amount of boost pressure developed by the 
turbocharger. When the boost pressure reaches a predetermined value, the 
wastegate opens and bypasses some of the exhaust gases directly into the 
exhaust manifold. Turbine speed is reduced, thereby reducing the speed of the 
compressor. This limits the amount of boost.

[FIGURE: A24460A.gif]

As pressure is reduced, the wastegate begins to close again. If boost 
is not controlled, engine components will be damaged from the excessive 
pressure.

[FIGURE: A24461A.gif]

The wastegate is a poppet-type valve operated by a turbocharger-mounted 
actuator. Air pressure from the compressor housing is applied to the actuator 
diaphragm. As pressure increases, the diaphragm moves against the spring 
pressure, holding the valve in the closed position. Movement of the actuator 
diaphragm is transferred to the poppet valve through an external rod and lever.

 CAUTION: The wastegate bracket is an integral part of the turbocharger. The 
turbocharger is a performance part and must not be tampered with after it is 
adjusted at the factory. Tampering with the wastegate components can reduce 
durability by increasing cylinder pressure and thermal loading due to 
incorrect inlet and exhaust manifold pressure, with a potential for poor fuel 
economy and failure to meet regulatory emission laws.

================================================================================
PAGE 6289
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-04B: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Center Housing

The center housing supports the compressor and turbine wheel shaft in a 
pair of identical bearings that contain oil, holes for directing oil to the 
bearing bores and shaft journals.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charge Air Cooler

As air in the turbocharger is compressed, it is also heated. To remove 
the heat, the air is routed through the charge air cooler. The charge air 
cooler is an air-to-air heat exchanger similar in construction and function to 
a radiator. By lowering the temperature of the air, it is made denser. The 
increased density of the air delivered to the engine cylinders permits a 
corresponding increase in the weight of fuel that can be injected into the 
cylinders while maintaining the air/fuel ratio required for proper combustion. 
Since engine power output is a function of the weight of fuel burned, the 
increase in the weight of fuel introduced as a result of turbocharger 
operation results in an increase in engine power output.

[FIGURE: A24462A.gif]

In addition to power increases, cooler air tends to lower stress on the 
engine by reducing detonation. It also reduces NOx emissions by lowering 
combustion chamber temperature.

================================================================================
PAGE 6291
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-04B: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Intake Manifold

The air intake manifold directs compressed air from the charge air 
cooler to the engine cylinders, where it is used for combustion.

PAGE 6292
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-04B: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air-Fuel/Exhaust Gas Flow

During operation of a turbocharged engine, exhaust gas from the engine 
exhaust manifold flows into the turbine. The exhaust gas pressure and the heat 
energy extracted from the gas cause the turbine wheel to rotate which, in 
turn, causes the compressor wheel to rotate.

The cooled and expanded exhaust gas leaving the turbine wheel is 
directed by the turbine housing to engine exhaust system, which expels it to 
atmosphere.

Rotation of the compressor wheel causes ambient air from the engine air 
cleaner to be drawn into the compressor housing, where it is compressed and 
delivered to appropriate ducting which delivers it to the engine intake 
manifold.

================================================================================
PAGE 6293
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-04B: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lubrication

Engine oil is used to lubricate the turbocharger bearings. The oil is 
routed to the turbocharger center housing through a pressure hose connected to 
the filter head located on the engine.

[FIGURE: A24463A.gif]

The center housing supports the compressor and turbine wheel shaft in a 
pair of identical bearings which contain oil holes for directing oil to the 
bearing bores and shaft journals. Split ring seals are installed at each end 
of the shaft between the bearing and the adjacent turbine or compressor wheel 
to prevent lubricating oil from entering the turbine and the compressor area. 
Passages drilled in the center housing provide for directing oil from the 
inlet port to oil grooves machined in the bearing bores, which align with 
holes in the bearings. Due to the high rotation speeds, the bearings are the 
full-floating type that have an oil film on both the inside diameter and 
outside diameter. The pumping action of the oil flow and the shaft rotation 
cause the bearings to rotate at approximately one-third of the shaft speed.

From the center housing, the oil drains to the engine crankcase through 
an oil return tube.

It is important that maximum oil flow is maintained whenever the engine 
is operating. Without lubrication, turbocharger failure can occur within 30 
seconds during operation. To prevent turbocharger damage, observe the 
following service guidelines.

Use only high-quality, recommended engine oil.

Do not accelerate the engine for one minute upon start-up. This allows 
for lubrication to reach the turbocharger bearings.

Do not switch off the engine while it is running at high speed. The 
turbocharger will continue to spin for a long time without oil pressure. 
Always allow the engine to idle and run for approximately 3 to 5 minutes to 
make sure that bearings have time to cool off before shutting off the engine.

Do not run the engine without an air cleaner; even minute particles of 
dirt can cause severe turbocharger damage.

If the turbocharger has been replaced, the center housing rotating 
assembly should be filled through the oil supply hole with clean engine oil. 
As the oil is poured into the housing, rotate the compressor wheel to 
distribute the oil onto the bearings. This will give the bearing the initial 
lubrication until normal engine oil flow is received.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler

Refer to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

 Inspection and Verification 

 Turbo Boost Pressure 

 NOTE: Turbo boost pressure is checked only on a dynamometer or where full 
load conditions can be achieved.

 Symptom Chart — Turbocharger 

 TURBOCHARGER 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Excessive Black Smoke Under Load/Low Power

 NOTE: Other engine systems may cause this condition. Refer to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

Air leak. Excess smoke and low power from a turbocharged engine can be 
caused by pressurized air leaking from loose connections or cracks in the 
crossover tube or intake manifold. This can also cause a noise problem.

CHECK entire system for leaks. PERFORM turbocharger system leak checks. 
REFER to Component Tests in this section.

Exhaust leak or restriction. Leaks or restrictions will cause the 
turbine and impeller to operate at a lower speed and reduce the amount of air 
being forced into the cylinders. Again, the symptom will be excess smoke, low 
manifold pressure and low power.

CHECK for leaks or restriction in exhaust system. SERVICE as required.

Airflow restriction. A restriction on the pressure side of the system 
will change the air-to-fuel ratio, reducing power and increasing smoke from 
the engine.

CHECK for restricted or leaking charge air cooler. PERFORM charge air 
cooler leak checks. REFER to Component Tests in this section.

Wastegate. Turbocharger wastegate failure of miscalibration of the 
turbocharger wastegate can result in excessively high or low boost pressures. 
Low boost pressures can cause excessive smoke and low power.

CHECK wastegate function and calibration. PERFORM turbocharger 
wastegate function check. REFER to Component Tests in this section.

Turbocharger. Failure of the internal components of the turbocharger 
can reduce its effectiveness and also cause excessive smoke and low power. A 
bearing failure can produce friction that will slow the speed of the rotor 
assembly. Failed bearings can also allow the blades of the rotor assembly to 
rub the housings, thus reducing the rotor assembly speed.

REPLACE turbocharger.

Air filter. Restriction increases as the filter removes contaminants 
from the intake air. Restricted airflow changes the air-to-fuel ratio, 
reducing power and increasing smoke from the engine.

REPLACE air filter.

High Oil Consumption

 NOTE: For procedure to confirm an excessive oil consumption
complaint, refer to Oil Consumption Test in Section 03-00 .

Restricted oil return line. Engine lubricating oil is used to lubricate 
the bearings and provide some cooling for the turbocharger. The oil supplied 
to the turbocharger through the supply line is at engine operating pressure. A 
return line connected to the bottom of the turbocharger routes the oil back to 
the engine oil pan. A restricted or damaged oil return line will cause the 
turbocharger housing to be pressurized, causing oil to migrate past the seals.

CLEAN or REPLACE oil return line.

Seal rings. Seal rings are used on each end of the rotor assembly. The 
primary function of the seals is to prevent exhaust gases and compressed air 
from entering the turbocharger housing. Oil leakage from the seals is rare, 
but it can occur. Do not consider a small amount of oil inside of the turbo 
housing a problem; this is normal. Since the turbo is increasing the amount of 
air into the cylinders, there will be an increase of blow-by. Blow-by carries 
oil vapors from the crankcase into the turbo housing where they condense. 
Suspect the carbon seal only if there is an excessive amount of oil in the 
turbo housing, and no other defects are found for excessive oil consumption.

REPLACE turbocharger.

Excessive blow-by.

 NOTE: Excessive crankcase pressure will not allow the oil to drain from the 
turbocharger. This will load the bearing housing and allow oil to leak past 
the compressor seals and into the engine.

REFER to the 1996 Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis
Manual, Test Step EPC 24, to check engine blow-by.

Boost Pressure High/Low

Wastegate. Turbocharger wastegate failure or miscalibration of the 
turbocharger wastegate can result in excessively high or low boost pressures. 
Low boost pressures can cause excessive smoke and low power. High boost 
pressures can cause major engine damage.

CHECK wastegate function and calibration. PERFORM turbocharger 
wastegate function check. REFER to Component Tests in this section.

Air leakage/restrictions.

REFER to Excessive Black Smoke Under Load/Low Power in this symptom 
chart.

Noise/Vibration

Air leaks. It is normal for the turbocharger to emit a whine sound that 
varies in intensity depending on engine speed and load. The sound is caused by 
the very high rotational speed of the rotor assembly. The sound will be more 
audible as engine speed increases. If possible, operate the engine at full 
speed to verify the maximum noise level. Leaks in the air system intake or 
exhaust components can produce additional noises.

CHECK system for leaks. PERFORM turbocharger system leak checks. REFER 
to Component Tests in this section.

Debris in system or rotor assembly contacting housing. Lower pitch 
sounds or rattles at slower engine speeds can indicate debris in the system or 
worn bearings are allowing the rotor assembly to touch the housings.

DISCONNECT exhaust pipe and outlet duct. INSPECT for debris, damage and 
signs of rotor contacting housing.

Rotor assembly imbalance. Because the rotor assembly speed is 100,000 
rpm or more, minor dents or nicks in the turbine or compressor wheel can 
result in an imbalance condition and vibration.

REPLACE turbocharger.

 Component Tests 

 Turbocharger Wastegate Functional Check 

Inspect wastegate lever pin. Replace turbocharger if worn excessively.

[FIGURE: A17632A.gif]

Check for excessive movement between shaft and bushing. Replace the 
turbocharger if shaft and bushing are damaged or seized.

[FIGURE: A17633B.gif]

Actuate lever by hand to make sure shaft rotates freely and is not 
seized.

[FIGURE: A17634A.gif]

Visually inspect wastegate actuator hose for cracks or holes. Replace 
hose if damaged.

[FIGURE: A17635A.gif]

Visually inspect wastegate mounting bracket, actuator rod and lever for 
damage. A bent wastegate actuator mounting bracket, actuator rod or lever can 
cause improper turbocharger operation.

If wastegate actuator mounting bracket is damaged, it must be replaced. 
If actuator rod is bent, replace wastegate actuator. If wastegate lever is 
bent, replace turbocharger.

[FIGURE: A17636A.gif]

Attach a dial indicator so that its shaft is in line with the wastegate 
actuator rod. Set the indicator to zero, with no air pressure applied to the 
wastegate actuator.

Loosen clamp and disconnect hose at wastegate actuator.

Connect clean, regulated air pressure supply and an accurate pressure 
gauge to the actuator.

Adjust pressure to actuator until axial travel of rod is 5 mm (0.200 
inch). Pressure reading at this point should be approximately 190-204 kPa 
(27.5-29.5 psi). The rod should not begin to move until air pressure reaches 
155-162 kPa (22.5-23.5 psi). Air must not leak through actuator. An air leak 
can be determined by listening for escaping air. Replace the actuator if it 
leaks or no movement/improper movement of the actuator rod and lever is 
detected.

[FIGURE: A17637A.gif]

 Turbocharger System Leak Checks 

 Air Pressure Leaks 

Air leaks on pressure side could cause excessive smoke and a loss of 
engine power, as well as a noise problem.

Visually inspect components for loose connections or damage. Apply 
liquid soap to duct connectors, air intake adapter and air intake manifold 
cover sealing surfaces to assist in detecting any air leakage. Any bubbles 
created will indicate the leak source.

 Exhaust Leaks 

Inspect for exhaust leaks at the exhaust manifold and turbocharger, 
gasket leaks or exhaust pipe restrictions. Exhaust leaks can usually be 
detected audibly or visually by a discoloration caused by the escaping hot 
gases.

Leaks or restrictions will cause the turbine and impeller to operate at 
a lower speed and reduce the amount of air being forced into the cylinders. 
The symptoms will be excessive smoke, low manifold pressure and low power.

 Charge Air Cooler Leak Checks 

Loss of engine power, low turbocharger boost pressure and higher than 
normal exhaust temperature may be caused by a leaking charge air cooler.

Look for two types of cracks: tube cracks or tank weld cracks. Tube 
cracks will usually occur first in the corners of the core and will be seen 
where the tube goes into the tank. Visual inspection will usually suffice to 
find most tube cracks. A better way to locate cracks is to pressurize the 
cooler to 276 kPa (40 psi). Apply a liquid soap film to all the tank joints. 
If bubbles form, there is a tube crack present.

If tube cracks are found, replace the cooler. Refer to the Master Parts 
Catalog for proper application.

[FIGURE: Q1810C.gif]

If there are no tube cracks, check for tank weld cracks. Tank weld 
cracks can usually be seen.

Refer to Service Procedures 
in this section to determine appropriate service for leaking or damaged charge air cooler.

 Bearing Clearance Inspection 

When there is reason to suspect that the turbocharger bearings are worn 
to the extent that the compressor or turbine wheel rubs the housing, perform 
the following procedures.

Remove the air cleaner tube boot from the compressor air inlet and 
remove the exhaust pipe from the turbine exhaust gas outlet.

With a powerful light, visually inspect the entire inlet and outlet 
surfaces for signs of wheel-to-housing rub. If scratching has occurred, the 
turbocharger center housing should be replaced. If scratches or damage to 
housing are severe, replace damaged housing.

If there is no sign of wheel-to-housing rubbing/interference, proceed 
to Step 2.

Measure the shaft end play using Dial Indicator/Magnetic Base 
D78P-4201-B or equivalent. End play is represented by dimension A in the 
illustration.

[FIGURE: A17630A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Service replacement turbocharger compressor outlet orientation may not 
be the same as the replaced turbocharger. If the compressor outlet orientation 
is the same, omit Steps 2, 5 and 6.

Clean turbocharger, exhaust manifold and oil drain tube gasket surfaces.

Loosen band clamp so compressor housing may be rotated.

Coat the turbocharger mounting studs with a high-temperature anti-seize 
compound and install new turbocharger-to-exhaust manifold gasket onto exhaust 
manifold mounting flange.

Install turbocharger onto exhaust manifold and install attaching nuts. 
Tighten nuts to 45 Nm (33 lb-ft).

Rotate compressor housing until outlet port aligns with air charge 
cooler inlet duct.

Tighten compressor housing band clamp to 8 Nm (71 
lb-in). Tap around the clamp with a plastic-tipped hammer and tighten again.

Using new gasket, install oil return line to turbocharger. Tighten 
return line retaining bolts to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft).

Fill turbocharger oil feed port with 50 to 60 cc (2-3 oz) of 
recommended engine oil. Rotate compressor wheel by hand to lubricate bearings.

[FIGURE: A17639A.gif]

Install the oil feed line to the turbocharger. Tighten fitting to 35 Nm
 (26 lb-ft).

If removed, install O-ring, outlet adapter and clamp.

Install air charge cooler inlet duct and exhaust outlet tube.

Install inside splash shield. Connect batteries.

Disconnect the fuel shutoff solenoid. Crank the engine to prime the 
turbocharger lubrication system.

Reconnect the fuel shutoff solenoid and start the engine. Check for air 
or oil leaks.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Charge Air Cooler, Aluminum

Listed in the following chart are the components of the air cooler 
system and the types of damage that occur. Some types of damage can be 
serviced while other types cannot. The corrective action is shown for each 
type of damage. In some cases, the cooler should be replaced not serviced.

 SERVICE PROCEDURES, CHARGE AIR COOLER, ALUMINUM

Condition

Action to Take

 · Tubes torn or cracked.

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Tubes dented, kinked or bent resulting in a round edge (radius less than 1
mm [1/32 in.]).

 · Weld or epoxy. Refer to Welding Procedures or Epoxy Procedures in the
Service Procedures portion of this section.

 · Tubes dented, kinked or bent resulting in a round edge (radius greater
than 1 mm [1/32 in.]).

 · No service required.

 · Holes in tubes less than 1 mm (1/32 in.) in all directions on tube surface.

 · Weld or epoxy to fill. Refer to Welding Procedures or Epoxy Procedures in
the Service Procedures portion of this section.

 · External fins crushed or bent; no more than 1 mm (1/32 in.) height
reduction per fin row and the sidemember-to-sidemember dimension is within
specification (687 mm [26-3/4 in.]).

 · No service required.

 · External fins pushed in with no tearing.

 · Straighten fins. Refer to Straightening in the Service Procedures portion
of this section.

 · External fins pushed in with tearing less than 10 mm (3/8 in.) deep from
core face. Also tearing is less than 20% of a given fin row and less than 5%
of the total fin rows.

 · Remove loose fin material and straighten. Refer to Straightening in the
Service Procedures portion of this section.

 · External fins pushed in with tearing of more than 10 mm (3/8 in.) from
face core or more than 20% of a given row or more than 5% of the total fin row.

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Sidemembers bent or dented.

 · Straighten sidemember to original form. If tubes are dented or fins
crushed, refer to appropriate service procedure in this section.

 · Sidemembers surface cracked or broken through.

 · Weld sidemember. Refer to Welding Procedures in the Service Procedures
portion of this section.

 · Headers bent or dented resulting in three or fewer tube or tube-to-header
leaks, and cracks are less than 2 mm (1/16 in.).

 · Weld header. Refer to Welding Procedures in the Service Procedures portion
of this section.

 Note: If crack is less than 1 mm (1/32 in.) service can be
performed using epoxy.

 · Headers bent or dented with more than three tube or tube-to-header leaks
or a crack width greater than 2 mm (1/16 in.).

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Headers cracked.

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Tank walls dented but not cracked or broken through and fit and function
of cooler is not affected.

 · No service required.

 · Tanks cracked. Crack is no more than 2 mm (1/16 in.) wide and 20 mm (3/4
in.) long.

 · Weld tanks. Refer to Welding Procedures in the Service Procedures portion
of this section.

 · Tanks cracked. Crack is more than 2 mm (1/16 in.) wide or 20 mm (3/4 in.)
long.

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Tanks punctured. Hole is no more than 5 mm (3/16 in.) in all directions on
tank surface.

 · Weld tanks. Refer to Welding Procedures in the Service Procedures portion
of this section.

 · Tanks punctured. Hole is more than 5 mm (3/16 in.) in any direction on
tank surface.

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Tank-to-header welds cracked or porous.

 · Weld. Refer to Welding Procedures in the Service Procedures portion of
this section.

 Caution: Service welds must not start or stop where a 
production weld ends. 

 · Threads stripped in tapped holes.

 · Drill out stripped threads and tap to accept proper helicoil insert of
same diameter and thread pitch of original hole.

 · Bosses and mounting brackets cracked or broken off, but crack or fractured
surface does not go into tank wall.

 · Weld. Refer to Welding Procedures in the Service Procedures portion of
this section.

 · Bosses or mounting brackets cracked or broken off, and crack goes into
tank wall.

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Mounting pins or other hardware cracked, broken or otherwise damaged, and
service will not affect fit, function or durability.

 · Service to original condition.

 · Mounting pins or other hardware cracked, broken or otherwise damaged, and
service will affect fit, function or durability.

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Straightening

 Straightening Fins 

Use a pointed object no more than 0.5 mm in diameter at the tip that 
will allow access to the apex of the fin. Straighten fins, taking care not to 
damage louvers or distort louver angle.

 Straightening Sidemembers 

Using pliers, vise-grips or similar tool, straighten side-member from 
sides only. Never pry against tubes or header. Care must be taken not to 
damage fins, tubes or headers when straightening sidemembers.

================================================================================
PAGE 6305
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-04B: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Welding Procedures

 Surface Preparation 

All surfaces to be welded must be free of all paint, oil, grease, water 
and other foreign matter in the area so the weld will adhere to the bare 
aluminum and will not be contaminated.

 Welding Tanks 

Prepare surfaces as outlined. Heat crack to chase ends until they stop. 
MIG weld to fill crack and continue bead past ends of crack approximately 25 
mm (1 in.). Wire brush and grind excess weld material to blend with tank 
surface.

 Welding Sidemembers 

Prepare surface as outlined. Cut a V-shaped groove along the length of 
the crack to a depth equal to the member thickness. MIG weld to fill the 
groove and grind excess material away to provide a flat surface.

 Welding Mounting Brackets 

Tack brackets in place so bracket will retain its correct orientation. 
MIG weld in place. Allow to air cool. Check alignment.

 CAUTION: Care must be taken not to melt fins of tube-to-header braze joint. If 
welding near core, core should be shielded with large steel plate. This 
protects it from sparks and weld splatter and will act as a heat sink. 

 Welding Tubes or Tube Header Joints 

TIG weld using aluminum wire designated Alcan MIG Electrode Wire, 1.20 
mm (3/16 in.) diameter, 4043 aluminum alloy or equivalent.

PAGE 6306
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-04B: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Epoxy Procedures

 Surface Preparation 

Remove all paint, oil, grease, water and other foreign matter in area 
of the epoxy so epoxy will adhere to the bare aluminum.

 Epoxying Tubes or Headers 

Use only high-temperature epoxy. The recommended epoxy is a resin (CIBA 
GEIGY ARALDITE AV 138M) and a hardener (CIBA GEIGY HV 998) or equivalent. Mix 
and cure instructions on product label must be strictly adhered to.

Section 03A-04B: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Cleaning After Weld or Epoxy Service

The cooler must be flushed after either weld or epoxy service to remove 
all debris that may have dropped into the cooler during service.

The recommended procedure for cleaning is to power flush the cooler 
with water at a rate of 1.5 mm (5 in.)/sec. for three minutes. To make sure 
that debris exits the cooler, orient the cooler so the tank containing the 
weld, or closest to the weld point, is at the bottom. The flushing water is to 
be introduced into the opposite tank at the top. When complete, invert the 
cooler and power flush in opposite direction.

If power flushing is not possible, flush cooler by hand. Lay cooler 
flat with inlet and outlet ports pointing up. Fill cooler to 40 percent of its 
volume with water, seal off both ports and agitate by hand so water flushes 
all internal surfaces at least ten times. Empty cooler and repeat flushing 
process until no debris is found in the flushing water.

After flushing (either power or by hand) drain cooler of all water and 
allow to air dry. Leak test cooler to check all service points prior to 
painting or installing cooler into vehicle.

================================================================================
PAGE 6308
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03A-04B: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, FD-1060 and FD-1460 Diesel Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Leak Testing Cooler After Service

 NOTE: To make sure cooler performs properly, serviced cooler must be 
leak-tested and pressure-checked prior to reinstalling it into vehicle.

Connect an air pressure gauge in one port of the cooler and a stop/air 
supply in the other port. Apply 345 kPa (50 psi) air pressure to cooler. 
Reduce pressure to 200 kPa (29 psi) and plug cooler to hold pressure. Let 
cooler stand a few minutes and note any loss of air pressure. Loss of air 
pressure should not exceed 10 kPa (1.5 psi) per minute. If leakage exceeds 
this limit, check cooler and perform any necessary service. Leak test cooler 
again and continue until cooler will hold pressure as stated.

ADJUSTMENTS

Actuator Calibration

 CAUTION: The wastegate is set accurately from the factory. Adjustment is not 
normally necessary unless the wastegate actuator is removed. The turbocharger 
is a performance part and must not be tampered with after it is adjusted at 
the factory. Tampering with the wastegate components can reduce durability by 
increasing cylinder pressure and thermal loading due to incorrect inlet and 
exhaust manifold pressure, with a potential for poor fuel economy and failure 
to meet regulatory emissions laws. 

Before checking actuator calibration procedure, perform Turbocharger 
Wastegate Functional Check . Refer to Component Tests in this section.

 CAUTION: Do not pull or push actuator rod to force alignment with clevis pin. 

Hole in actuator rod clevis should align with lever pin. If rod cannot 
be installed on lever, loosen clevis lock nut and turn clevis until hole 
aligns with pin.

[FIGURE: A17696A.gif]

Install retaining clip and tighten clevis lock nut.

Disconnect air supply at actuator.

Install hose on actuator and secure with clamp.

Section 03A-05: Drive Belts, Accessory, FD-1060 Diesel Engine

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Drive Belts, Accessory 

L-Series vehicles are equipped with two types of accessory drive belts. 
The drive belt type is selected for each engine based on performance 
requirements. To ensure maximum life, replacement belts should be of the same 
type as originally installed. These belts must be properly adjusted at all 
times. Loose belt(s) will result in slippage, which can cause a noise 
complaint or improper accessory operation (generator will not charge, etc.). 
Overly tight belts will place severe loads on accessory bearings. 

The poly-V (serpentine) drive belt tension is maintained by an 
automatic belt tensioner. Regular inspection is required to check belt 
condition to ensure excessive belt stretch does not occur. The vee drive belt 
is not automatically tensioned and requires periodic inspection for proper 
belt tension.

[FIGURE: Q1690E.gif]

Section 03A-05: Drive Belts, Accessory, FD-1060 Diesel Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Drive Belts, Accessory

 Inspection and Verification 

 Drive Belt Cracking/Chunking/Wear 

Under severe operating conditions (high temperatures, low humidity), 
drive belt rib cracking can occur at less than 96,000 km (60,000 miles). Drive 
belt rib cracking perpendicular to the belt ribs is not a reason for concern 
and has no detrimental effect on belt performance. Cracks parallel to ribs are 
not acceptable.

Drive belt "chunking" is the condition in which the rubber material 
actually chunks out between the cracks. The drive belt must be replaced if 
chunks are missing on two adjacent ribs or a chunked-out section is 13 mm (0.5 
inch) or longer in length.

[FIGURE: Q4077C.gif]

 Drive Belt Noise 

Drive belt chirp is a regularly occurring chirping noise that occurs 
due to pulley misalignment or excessive pulley runout. It can be a result of a 
damaged pulley or an improperly replaced pulley that was not properly aligned.

To correct, determine the area the noise comes from. Then check each of 
the pulleys in that area with a straightedge to the crankshaft pulley and look 
for the accessory pulleys to be out of position in the fore/aft direction or 
at an angle to the straightedge.

Belt squeal is an intermittent noise that occurs when the drive belt 
slips on a pulley during certain conditions, such as engine start-up, rapid 
engine acceleration or A/C clutch engagement.

Drive belt squeal can occur under the following conditions:

A/C discharge pressure goes above 2895 kPa (420 psi). This can occur if:

the A/C system is overcharged.

the A/C condenser core airflow is blocked.

the engine fan blade is not engaging fully at idle.

A/C OFF equalized pressure (the common discharge and suction pressure 
that occurs after several minutes) exceeds 965 kPa (140 psi), which is a rare 
occurrence at high ambient temperatures with a hot engine. Turn A/C off for a 
few seconds and then back on after fan blade begins to cool A/C condenser core.

Any of the accessories are damaged, or have a worn or damaged bearing 
or internal torsional resistance above normal for any reason. All of the 
accessories should be able to be rotated by hand in the unloaded condition. If 
any are not, the accessory should be inspected.

Fluid gets on the drive belt. Fluids include power steering fluid, 
engine coolant, engine oil or air conditioning system lubricant.

If fluid does get on the drive belt during service, clean the drive 
belt with soap and water and rinse thoroughly with clean water. The drive belt 
does not have to be replaced if no apparent damage has occurred.

Drive belt is too long. A drive belt that is too long will allow the 
drive belt tensioner arm to go all the way to drive belt tensioner arm travel 
stop under certain load conditions, which will untension the drive belt. If 
the drive belt tensioner is resting on the stop, replace the drive belt.

If the drive belt tensioner is worn or damaged. The drive belt 
tensioner arm should rotate freely without binding.

 Component Tests 

 Drive Belt Tension 

Check drive belt tension. Refer to Drive Belt Tension Adjustment in the 
Adjustments portion of this section. If tension is not within specification, 
check drive belt tensioner. Service components as required.

 Drive Belt Tensioner, Automatic 

The drive belt tensioner will maintain correct belt tension if the 
correct length drive belt is on the engine. The drive belt tensioner can be 
checked as follows:

With the engine running, observe drive belt tensioner movement. The 
drive belt tensioner should move (respond) when the A/C compressor cycles or 
when the engine is accelerated rapidly. If the drive belt tensioner movement 
is constant and excessive, a pulley or shaft is probably bent or a pulley is 
out of round. In rare cases, excessive belt rideout (uneven depth of grooves 
in belt) can cause excessive drive belt tensioner movement. This condition can 
be checked by replacing the suspect drive belt with a known good original 
equipment drive belt and repeating the observation.

With engine off, check for proper drive belt routing. Refer to the 
illustrations under Removal and Installation in this section. Service as 
required.

Visually inspect the condition of the drive belt. Replace the drive 
belt as required.

Rotate the drive belt tensioner and check for a binding or frozen 
condition. Replace components as required.

 Drive Belt Misalignment 

 CAUTION: Incorrect drive belt installation will cause excessive drive belt wear 
and can cause the drive belt to come off the drive pulleys. 

 NOTE: Original equipment drive belts are made of a special cord construction 
and are subjected to special testing before they are approved for use.

Replacement drive belts, other than O.E.M., can track 
differently/improperly. If a replacement drive belt tracks improperly, the 
drive belt must be replaced with an O.E.M. drive belt to avoid performance 
failure or loss of drive belt during cold operation.

With the engine running, check drive belt tracking (the position of the 
drive belt on the drive belt tensioner. If the edge of the drive belt rides 
beyond the edge of the drive bent tensioner, this can cause noise and 
premature wear.

If a drive belt tracking condition exists, visually check the drive 
belt tensioner for damage, especially the mounting pad surface. If the drive 
belt tensioner is not installed correctly with the locating pins in the 
locating holes, the mounting surface pad will be out of position. This will 
result in drive belt tension, chirp and squeal noises.

If the above procedures do not correct the drive belt noise, try 
replacing the drive belt with a known good original equipment drive belt. 
However, the drive belt noise might return (with mileage) if one of the above 
conditions still exists uncorrected.

With engine running, visually observe the grooves in the pulleys (not 
the pulley flanges) for excessive wobble. Replace components as required.

Check all accessories, mounting brackets and drive belt tensioner for 
any interference that would prevent the component from mounting properly. 
Correct any interference condition and recheck belt tracking.

Tighten all accessories mounting brackets and drive belt tensioner 
retaining hardware to specification. Recheck drive belt tracking.

Check drive belt tension. Refer to Drive Belt Tension 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Belt Replacement 

Conditions requiring drive belt replacement are rib chunk out, 
excessive wear, severe glazing and frayed cords. Replace any drive belt 
exhibiting any of these conditions. Minor cracks in the ribbed side of 
V-grooved portion of the drive belt are considered acceptable.

 Drive Belt, Serpentine (Poly-V) 

 Removal 

Remove Hydro-Max pump assembly drive belt, if so equipped.

Rotate automatic tensioner. 

Remove old belt. 

 Installation 

Install belt on crankshaft pulley. Make sure belt is completely seated 
in the pulley grooves and not touching the installation guide bolt (lower left 
side). 

With tensioner in free position, feed the belt over the tensioner 
pulley, under the A/C compressor or idler pulley and over the alternator 
pulley. 

Wrap the left side of belt over the fan pulley. Make sure belt is 
seated in all pulley grooves. 

Grab the remaining length of belt over the water pump pulley with one 
hand and activate the tensioner pulley outboard until the belt can be slipped 
over the water pump pulley. 

When belt is over the water pump pulley, carefully release the 
tensioner to tighten belt. Check again to make sure the belt is seated 
properly in all pulleys. 

Install Hydro-Max pump assembly vee drive belt.

Start engine and check for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Belt Tensioner, Automatic

 Removal 

Rotate automatic belt tensioner to release drive belt tension.

With tension released, remove poly-V (serpentine) drive belt from 
tensioner pulley.

Allow drive belt tensioner to slowly rotate to the relaxed position. Do 
not allow tensioner to snap back after the drive belt is removed or damage to 
the tensioner may occur.

Remove drive belt tensioner retainer belt and tensioner.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten drive belt tensioner bolt to 83 Nm (61 lb-ft).

ADJUSTMENTS

Drive Belt Tension Adjustment

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Belt Tension Gauge

T63L-8620-A

Install Belt Tension Gauge T63L-8620-A on vee drive belts or Rotunda 
Belt Tension Gauge 014-R1056 or equivalent on poly-V (serpentine) drive belts.

[FIGURE: Q4239C.gif]

If the belt(s) require adjustment, follow the applicable procedure 
below. 

 Vee Drive Belt 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Belt Tension Gauge

T63L-8620-A

Loosen the Hydro-Max pump assembly adjuster lock bolt. 

Loosen the pivot bolts and the adjustment bolt. 

Tighten or loosen adjustment bolt to achieve correct belt tension. 
Measure tension with Belt Tension Gauge T63L-8620-A following the instructions 
of the tool manufacturer.

With tension still applied, tighten the adjuster lock bolt. 

Tighten the pivot bolts. 

Tighten pivot bolts and tighten the adjuster lock bolt to 35-47 Nm
 (26-35 lb-ft). 

 Serpentine (Poly-V) Drive Belt 

The poly-V (serpentine) drive belt uses an automatic belt tensioner to 
automatically adjust and maintain the correct belt tension. No adjustment of 
the drive belt or driven components is required.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Starter Motor 

 Removal 

Open battery box and disconnect battery ground cable.

Remove starter motor upper mounting bolt.

Disconnect starter and starter solenoid wires. Tag wires to facilitate 
connection at proper terminals during starter installation.

Remove two remaining starter motor mounting bolts. Remove starter.

 Installation 

Position starter on engine. Install three bolts. Tighten to 150-200 Nm
 (110-148 lb-ft).

Connect solenoid wire to starter S-terminal. Tighten nut to 1.8 Nm
 (16 lb-ft).

Connect remaining starter wires to starter B-terminal and tighten nut 
to 18 Nm (13 lb-in).

Connect battery ground cable and close battery box. Check operation of 
starter.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Starter Motor 

 Disassembly 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter.

Scribe a mark on starter motor frame, drive end housing and lever 
housing for assembly.

Disconnect starter motor lead on frame from starter solenoid 
M-terminal. Reinstall nut on solenoid terminal.

Remove the two through-bolts.

Remove the four brush plate screws.

Remove the commutator end frame and O-ring.

 NOTE: Use care not to lose the small dowel pin installed between frame, field 
and brush holder assembly, and gear reduction and drive assembly. Dowel pin is 
required for reassembly and must be saved. If dowel pin is lost, replace with 
2-mm (0.079-inch) diameter x 10-mm (0.394-inch) long pin.

Remove the frame, field and brush holder assembly, dowel pin and frame 
seal.

 NOTE: Armature assembly might come off with frame, field and brush holder 
assembly or might be retained by gear reduction and drive assembly.

Remove armature assembly with ball bearings. Do not remove ball 
bearings from armature assembly unless replacement is required.

Remove the solenoid retaining screws.

Remove the solenoid assembly. Pivot inside end of solenoid assembly out 
of engagement with shift lever in gear reduction and drive assembly and 
withdraw solenoid assembly.

 Starter Motor, 28-MT, Disassembled View 

[FIGURE: J5182B.gif]

 Assembly 

Support gear reduction and drive assembly with pinion gear end down and 
install solenoid assembly. Pivot plunger of solenoid assembly into engagement 
with shift lever in gear reduction and drive assembly.

Position starter solenoid mounting flange and install solenoid mounting 
screws. Tighten screws to 2.8 Nm (25 lb-in).

Install the frame seal.

Install armature assembly with ball bearings into gear reduction and 
drive assembly. Make sure gear teeth are aligned, then seat ball bearing on 
armature shaft fully into drive housing recess.

Place dowel pin in hole in armature support bracket of gear reduction 
and drive assembly.

Position frame, field and brush holder assembly over armature assembly. 
Align hole for dowel pin and marks made prior to disassembly and seat in gear 
reduction and drive group.

Twist brush springs away from brushes. Slide brushes in to contact 
commutator on armature and release brush springs to contact ends of brushes.

 NOTE: O-ring can easily be damaged during installation of the commutator end 
frame. To prevent such damage, install O-ring as described.

Install O-ring on frame, field and brush holder assembly so that it is 
against the shoulder on the frame and field assembly that will abut the 
commutator end frame when installed. This is the normal installed position for 
the O-ring.

Carefully roll the O-ring out of its normal installed position up onto 
the major OD of the field frame. Allow O-ring to remain in this position until 
commutator end frame is partially installed.

Align marks on commutator end frame and frame and field assembly made 
prior to disassembly. Start commutator end frame onto frame and field 
assembly, leaving a gap just slightly larger than the thickness of O-ring.

Install brush plate screws. Use a scribe or similar tool to align 
tapped holes in brush holder assembly with screw holes in commutator end 
frame. Tighten screws to 2.8 Nm (25 lb-in).

Install through-bolts and tighten by hand but do not close gap between 
commutator end frame and frame and field assembly where O-ring goes.

Roll O-ring back down into its installed position between commutator 
end frame and frame and field assembly.

Align timing ribs on edge of commutator end frame with timing spots on 
frame and field assembly to assure proper brush alignment. Marks are located 
in two places on motor but will only match one way. Tighten through-bolts to 
8.5 Nm (75 lb-in).

Remove nut from M-terminal on solenoid. Install starter motor lead 
terminal and reinstall nut. Tighten nut to 11 Nm (100 lb-in).

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Starter Drive Replacement

 Disassembly 

Disassemble starter motor.

Remove the drive housing bolts.

Remove the armature support bracket. Washers might stick to armature 
support bracket or to output shaft and clutch assembly as armature support 
bracket is removed. In either case, note the position and number of each of 
these washers.

Remove washers. The same washers will be installed in the same position 
and number at assembly.

Remove drive housing plug and plate. Pry out drive housing plug using a 
large screwdriver.

Remove shift lever nut, washer and screw.

Remove shift lever and output shaft and clutch assembly from drive 
housing together, then separate. Do not remove bushing plug or bushing from 
drive housing unless replacement is required.

Position driveshaft and clutch assembly on workbench with internal gear 
end down.

Using open tube slightly larger than shaft drive pinion stop toward 
clutch drive assembly until it clears stop rings.

[FIGURE: J6435A.gif]

Using care not to scratch driveshaft, pry stop rings out of shaft 
groove and slide off end of shaft.

Inspect edges of shaft groove for burrs that might have been formed 
through repeated cranking cycles. Such burrs make removal of pinion stop and 
clutch drive assembly difficult. If burrs are found, use a suitable file to 
carefully remove burrs only — not base metal. Thoroughly clean 
away metal filings.

Slide pinion stop off driveshaft. Discard pinion stop and stop rings. 
New parts must be used at assembly.

Remove clutch drive assembly from driveshaft.

Remove driveshaft support from driveshaft.

Do not remove bearing from driveshaft unless replacement is required.

[FIGURE: J6436A.gif]

 Assembly 

Install driveshaft support on driveshaft, seating bearing in support.

Install drive assembly on driveshaft.

Slide pinion stop onto driveshaft, end with recess for stop rings 
facing up.

Install stop rings in groove in driveshaft.

Pick up and support assembly under pinion stop. A metal block, with a 
U-shaped cutout that will slide over shaft between pinion gear and stop, can 
be clamped in a vise to provide support.

[FIGURE: J6437A.gif]

Make sure stop rings (in driveshaft groove) are fully seated in pinion 
stop recess and stake upper edge of pinion stop over stop ring at four places, 
equally spaced. Do not allow staked metal to contact driveshaft.

Lubricate the drive housing bushing, shift lever, and driveshaft.

Connect arms on shift lever with shift collar on output shaft and 
clutch assembly.

 NOTE: Make sure driveshaft support is fully seated in drive housing and that 
driveshaft bearing remains fully seated in driveshaft support.

Install assembled shift lever and output shaft and clutch assembly into 
drive housing, aligning holes in driveshaft support with those in drive housing.

Install shift lever screw, washer and nut. Tighten nut to 4.5 Nm
 (40 lb-in).

Install plate, if used, and drive housing plug in drive housing.

Install washers in same number and position as noted at disassembly.

Install armature support bracket to drive housing, aligning mark made 
prior to disassembly with mark on drive housing.

Install drive housing bolts and tighten to 8.5 Nm (75 
lb-in).

Assemble starter motor.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Brush Replacement

 Disassembly 

Disassemble starter motor.

Remove the insulated brush screws. Move brush holder assembly away from 
frame and field assembly slightly. Reach across with screwdriver and remove 
screws.

Remove the frame and field assembly.

Remove the grounded brush screws.

Remove the brushes. Grasp brush end of each brush spring with 
needlenose pliers. Twist brush spring end away from brush and withdraw brush.

Remove the brush springs. Grasp brush end of each brush spring with 
needlenose pliers. Twist brush spring end away from brush socket on brush 
holder assembly and remove spring.

 Frame, Field and Brush Holder Assembly

holder assembly, just enough to hold inside end of spring from turning.

 NOTE: Brush leads might be damaged by excessive handling. Do not overflex 
leads near clip welds or clips might break off.

Grasp free end of spring with needlenose pliers and twist clockwise 
over top of brush socket. Push spring fully onto post and release free end to 
engage notch in brush socket.

Refer to the illustration for proper installed position of all brushes. 
Make sure insulated brushes go into brush sockets of brush holder assembly 
that are mounted on insulation.

To install each brush, grasp free end of brush spring with needlenose 
pliers. Twist clockwise to clear brush socket and insert brush partly into 
brush socket.

Remove the commutator end frame and O-ring.

 NOTE: Use care not to lose the small dowel pin installed between frame, field 
and brush holder assembly, and gear reduction and drive assembly. Dowel pin is 
required for reassembly and must be saved. If dowel pin is lost, replace with 
2-mm (0.079-inch) diameter x 10-mm (0.394-inch) long pin procured or 
manufactured locally.

 NOTE: Armature assembly might come off with frame, field and brush holder 
assembly or might be retained by gear reduction and drive assembly.

Remove the frame, field and brush holder assembly, dowel pin and frame 
seal.

Remove armature assembly with ball bearings. Do not remove ball 
bearings from armature assembly unless replacement is required.

 Assembly 

Install the frame seal.

Install armature assembly with ball bearings into gear reduction and 
drive assembly. Make sure gear teeth are aligned, then seat ball bearing on 
armature shaft fully into drive housing recess.

Place dowel pin in hole in armature support bracket of gear reduction 
and drive assembly.

Position frame, field and brush holder assembly over armature assembly. 
Align hole for dowel pin and marks made prior to disassembly and seat in gear 
reduction and drive group.

Twist brush springs away from brushes. Slide brushes in to contact 
commutator on armature and release brush springs to contact ends of brushes.

 NOTE: O-ring can easily be damaged during installation of the commutator end 
frame. To prevent such damage, install O-ring as described.

Install O-ring on frame, field and brush holder assembly so that it is 
against the shoulder on the frame and field assembly that will abut the 
commutator end frame when installed. This is the normal installed position for 
the O-ring.

Carefully roll the O-ring out of its normal installed position up onto 
the major OD of the field frame. Allow O-ring to remain in this position until 
commutator end frame is partially installed.

Align marks on commutator end frame and frame and field assembly made 
prior to disassembly. Start commutator end frame onto frame and field 
assembly, leaving a gap just slightly larger than the thickness of O-ring.

Install brush plate screws. Use a scribe or similar tool to align 
tapped holes in brush holder assembly with screw holes in commutator end 
frame. Tighten screws to 2.8 Nm (25 lb-in).

Install through-bolts and tighten by hand but do not close gap between 
commutator end frame and frame and field assembly where O-ring goes.

Roll O-ring back down into its installed position between commutator 
end frame and frame and field assembly.

Align timing ribs on edge of commutator end frame with timing spots on 
frame and field assembly to assure proper brush alignment. Marks are located 
in two places on motor but will only match one way. Tighten through-bolts to 
8.5 Nm (75 lb-in).

Remove nut from M-terminal on solenoid, install starter motor lead 
terminal and reinstall nut. Tighten nut to 11 Nm (100 lb-in).

Section 03A-12: Air Intake System, FD-1060 Diesel Engine

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Induction System 

Air is pulled into the engine through an air cleaner element. Clean air 
is very important to the life of the engine. Ingested dust and dirt can damage 
the engine very quickly. 

On turbocharged and aftercooled engines, the intake airflow is from the 
air cleaner to the turbocharger and then routed to the charge air cooler 
located in front of the radiator. Air leaves the charge air cooler and is 
routed to the intake manifold where it is forced into the cylinders and used 
for combustion. The charge air cooler reduces the temperature of the intake 
air, which lowers combustion chamber temperatures, and in turn reduces NOx 
emissions. Also, cooling the intake air makes it more dense allowing more fuel 
to be injected into the engine to increase the power-to-weight ratio. 

 Typical Intake Air System, Turbocharged Engine

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Cleaner Element

A dry-type air cleaner element is standard equipment on all Ford 
vehicles equipped with diesel engines. Air is filtered through a pleated, 
chemically treated paper air cleaner element to remove contaminants before 
entering the turbocharger system.

Air Restriction Gauge

Air cleaners are equipped with an air restriction gauge (mounted in the 
instrument panel) or an air restriction indicator (mounted at the air cleaner 
housing) that indicates when the air cleaner element needs servicing. When the 
air restriction indicator or gauge reads 6.2 kPa (25 inches of water) vacuum, 
the air cleaner element needs servicing.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Cleaner Element

 Removal 

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element, air cleaner housing or turbocharger inlet 
tube is removed, use a clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering 
the engine. 

Remove fasteners retaining the air cleaner housing cover.

Remove the air cleaner housing cover.

Remove wing nut retaining the air cleaner element and remove the air 
cleaner element.

 Installation 

Before installing a new air cleaner element in the air cleaner housing, 
check the following items:

Gasket surfaces should be clean and undamaged.

Outlet tube should be clean and undamaged.

Air cleaner element should be dry and free of holes, ruptures, damaged 
gaskets or dents in end covers and liners.

Air cleaner element retaining nut or bolt should have the gasket washer 
attached and in good condition.

After the air cleaner housing, air cleaner element, dust cup and other 
parts are found to be in good condition, assemble the parts as follows:

Install the air cleaner element and tighten the wing nut. Make sure the 
rubber face of the washer seals against the air cleaner element.

Install the air cleaner housing cover to housing.

Install fasteners retaining the air cleaner housing cover. Tighten the 
air cleaner housing cover bolts to 11 Nm (96 lb-in) maximum.

 NOTE: Make sure a seal is made between the dust cup and the air cleaner 
housing. A leak would reduce element life.

Reset the air restriction indicator.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Inlet Restriction Check

The best method for determining dry-type air cleaner maintenance 
periods is through periodic air restriction checks at the air restriction 
indicator or the air restriction gauge (if so equipped).

It is recommended that the air restriction indicator or the air 
restriction gauge be used to determine service intervals. A visual inspection 
of the air cleaner element will not ascertain the need for service. 
Overservicing is not recommended.

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Cleaner Element

 CAUTION: Never attempt to clean a dirty or restricted air cleaner element. Use a 
new replacement only. 

Check the old element. It could help in the detection of foreign 
material on the sealing surface that is causing leakage. A streak of dust on 
the clean air side of the air cleaner element seal is a tell-tale sign. If it 
exists, make sure the cause is removed before installing a new air cleaner 
element.

Inspect the new air cleaner element for damage. Always look for 
possible shipping or handling damage. Pay particular attention to the inside 
of the open end (the sealing area). Check for cuts. Do not use a damaged air 
cleaner element.

Engine Air Cleaner Housing

compressed air. Wipe the air cleaner housing and cover dry. Inspect the air 
cleaner housing and cover for distortion or damage at the gasket mating 
surfaces. Replace the air cleaner housing cover or body if damaged beyond 
service.
