DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Identification

For exact engine identification and adjustment information, two decal 
labels are located on the valve cover above cylinder No. 1. The ENGINE 
INFORMATION decal contains pertinent information about the engine and 
adjustments. The IDENTIFICATION decal contains information concerning the 
basic engine component group, engine displacement, design level, build date 
and engine calibration code. Always refer to these labels when replacement 
parts are required or when checking engine calibrations. Some engine parts may 
vary with engine application and vehicle type. The identification codes will 
ensure that the proper parts are obtained. The codes contain all pertinent 
information relating to dates, optional equipment and revisions. The Ford 
Master Parts Catalog contains a complete listing of the codes and their 
application. In addition, there is an engine serial number located on a pad at 
the lower right side of the block.

[FIGURE: A18184A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 6353
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cylinder Head 

The cylinder head is a one-piece, crossflow design with two valves per 
cylinder. The head has valve seat and valve guide inserts that can be repaired 
using the appropriate parts.

The cylinder head has a cast intake manifold, fuel filter head, 
thermostat housing and an internal water bypass. The injectors are mounted in 
the head for direct injection into the cylinders. Oil is distributed by 
manifold.

The cylinder head gasket is a laminated design with print-o-seal on 
both sides around the water holes. A fire ring in the gasket seals the 
cylinder bores. The gasket also provides orifices to control coolant and 
circulation past and around the cylinder liners.

================================================================================
PAGE 6354
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Manifolds

The intake manifold is integral with the cylinder head. The exhaust 
manifold mounts to the right side of the cylinder head and is designed to 
maintain exhaust velocity to provide maximum input to the turbocharger. 
Exhaust exits via the exhaust pipe, through the muffler and tail pipe.

================================================================================
PAGE 6355
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Exhaust Brake

 CAUTION: Exceeding maximum exhaust pressure will result in engine damage. 

The following guidelines must be followed when installing an exhaust 
brake on Ford FD-1460 diesel engines or the warranty may be voided.

Exhaust brake assembly must be mounted a minimum of 1.7 meters (5.5 
feet) downstream from the turbocharger.

Maximum allowable exhaust back pressure is 241 kPa (35 psi), standard 
exhaust valve springs, and 448 kPa (65 psi), orange-striped heavy-duty exhaust 
valve spring, both at 2860 rpm.

================================================================================
PAGE 6356
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cylinder Block 

The cylinder block has provisions for the oil cooler housing, 
thermostat seats, coolant bypass line, water pump housing, oil pump housing, 
water pump inlet and replaceable cylinder liners.

The six-cylinder crankshaft is a balanced, forged steel, full-fillet 
hardened unit with seven main bearing journals. The lower bearing shells are 
the same except for the No. 4 journal which uses a flanged upper bearing 
shell. The flanges on the bearing shell control the end thrust of the 
crankshaft. Oversize main bearings and thrust bearings are available for 
service.

All crankshaft seals are the Teflon® lay-down 
lip-(scroll) type. The Teflon® lay-down lip-type seal does 
not contain a spring on the back of the sealing lip. The sealing lip is a 
thin, stiff piece of Teflon®.

Teflon® seals must be dry before installation. Do not 
lubricate the seal lip or the shaft. After the first few turns of the shaft, a 
thin film of Teflon® is transferred from the seal lip to the 
shaft. If the shaft is not clean and dry, this transfer will not occur and the 
seal will leak.

The pistons have a cast aluminum body, high swirl combustion bowl and 
three ring grooves. The top two ring grooves have a nickel-coated 
scuff-resistant insert with a Keystone profile. The piston pin end of the 
connecting rod is angle cut to provide additional bearing surface. The rod end 
is fitted with a bronze bushing. Steel backed tri-metal bearings are used in 
production for the additional loading resulting from turbocharging and 
aftercooling.

Oversize service rod bearings are available for use with reground 
crankshafts.

A free-floating, hollow piston pin is used to attach the piston to the 
connecting rod. Lubrication of the pin and journal is accomplished by residual 
spray from dual piston cooling nozzles.

The camshaft is gear-driven from the crankshaft. Replaceable bushings 
are used on all camshaft journals. The remainder of the journals operate in 
cast iron bores in the cylinder block. The camshaft has lobes to operate the 
intake and exhaust valves and a special lobe to drive the lift pump. The 
camshaft lobes contact "mushroom" shaped valve tappets that operate the push 
rods. The operating arm of the piston type lift pump rides directly on the 
special lobe on the camshaft.

================================================================================

 Lubricating Oil Pump 

The lubricating oil flow begins as the gerotor pump draws oil from the 
pan through the rigid, internal suction tube. The pump then delivers the oil 
through an internal drilling in the cylinder block to the top of the oil 
cooler via the inner channels of the cover.

 Pressure Regulating Valve 

From the cooler, the oil is directed to the combination full 
flow/bypass oil filter and also to the pressure regulator.

The regulator valve remains closed until the oil pressure is 
approximately 345 kPa (50 psi). At high pressure, the plunger moves toward the 
plug and relieves the system by allowing some oil to return to the oil pan.

The tapered shoulder on the plunger creates a variable opening to 
regulate pressure.

================================================================================
PAGE 6358
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Oil Cooler

When the oil from the oil pump reaches the top of the oil cooler, it 
flows by the thermostat before entering the oil cooler.

If the oil is cold, the thermostat will open, allowing oil to bypass 
the cooler and flow to the filter. As the temperature of the oil increases, 
the thermostat will close and force the oil to flow through the cooler 
element, thereby regulating the oil temperature to the block.

Coolant passing around the plates of the element cools the oil.

================================================================================
PAGE 6359
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Oil Filter

A combination full flow/bypass oil filter is used. The upper section of 
the filter contains the full flow filter element while the lower section 
contains the bypass element.

Oil that flows through the full flow portion of the oil filter returns 
to the block. Oil that flows through the bypass returns to the oil pan.

================================================================================
PAGE 6360
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Oil Filter Bypass Valve

If the full flow section of the combination filter becomes plugged to 
the point that a 137 kPa (20 psi) pressure difference exists across the 
filter, the bypass valve opens in the oil filter head and routes unfiltered 
oil to the main oil rifle. This is done to prevent oil starvation to the 
engine with a plugged filter.

PAGE 6361
================================================================================

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lubrication for the Turbocharger

At the filter head (on engines equipped with a turbocharger), the oil 
flow is divided. A portion flows to the turbocharger; the rest flows down a 
passage in the cylinder block that connects to a cross drilling over the No. 3 
main bearing.

The cooled and filtered oil flows through the cross drilling over the 
No. 3 main bearing to the main oil rifle. The main oil rifle is drilled 
through the length of the cylinder block and carries oil through individual 
drillings to the overhead and the fuel pump.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lubrication for the Power Components

A transfer drilling from the main oil rifle intersects with a drilling 
between the main bearing bore and the camshaft bushing bore. These drillings 
supply oil to the cam bushing and main bearing.

The groove in the upper main bearing shell supplies oil to the piston 
cooling nozzles located in the main bearing saddle. The spray from the nozzle 
provides cooling for the pistons, and splash lubricates the piston pin. From 
the main bearings, the oil enters the crankshaft and lubricates the connecting 
rod bearings through internal cross drillings.

Drillings in the cylinder block and gear housing connect to the 
external groove on the No. 1 camshaft bushing to supply oil to the injection 
pump. An overflow hole located above the injection pump shaft allows oil to 
return to the oil pan.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lubrication for the Overhead

Oil for the overhead components is supplied by a vertical drilling 
through the cylinder head and block that intersects the external groove on the 
No. 7 camshaft bushing. The main oil rifle supplies oil to the camshaft bushing.

Oil flows from the vertical drilling to an angle drilling in the 
cylinder head. From the angle drilling, the oil flows through the transfer 
tube. The rocker lever supports are installed over the transfer tube.

From a hole in the transfer tube the oil is transferred to the rocker 
lever support capscrews by the relieved area in the base of the support.

Oil flows around the capscrews up to the rocker lever shaft. Oil flows 
into the inside diameter of the shaft and along its length. The ends of the 
shaft are sealed by cup plugs.

Drillings in the shaft allow the oil to flow from the inside diameter 
to the bores of the rocker levers. The rocker lever has a drilling that 
transfers oil from the bore to a trough on the top of the lever. Oil flows 
along the trough to lubricate the push rod socket and the valve stem.

The front gear train assembly is lubricated from oil splash and 
carryover. The oil pump idler gear is force-lubricated. From the gear train 
assembly, the oil drains back to the oil pan for recirculation.

 Lubrication for the Overhead

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cooling System

Coolant is drawn from the radiator by the integrally mounted water 
pump. The output from the water pump empties into the bottom of the oil cooler 
cavity in the cylinder block.

From the cooler cavity, the coolant flows into the upper water 
manifold. A portion of the coolant flows through the coolant filter and 
returns to the lower manifold. The remainder flows through six cast openings 
up to the cylinder head.

 Cooling System 

[FIGURE: A18181B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Coolant Inlet (Part of 6010)

2

—

Water Pump Impeller (Part of 8501)

3

—

Coolant Flow to Cooler

4

Coolant Flow Past Oil Cooler

6

Coolant to Cylinder Head

Coolant Flow from Upper Coolant Manifold

8

Coolant to Liner Cavity

9

—

Coolant Flow Orifice (Part of 6051)

10

6051

Cylinder Head Gasket

A portion of the coolant flowing into the cylinder head is directed to 
the liner cavity and, by means of a diffuser plate cast into the cavity, is 
circulated around the top portion of the liners.

The remainder of the coolant flows across the valve bridges around the 
injector bores and down into the liner cavities through two orificed holes per 
cylinder. The orificed holes control the coolant flow around the liners.

From the liner cavities the coolant flows through cast openings into 
the lower manifold and on to the thermostat cavity.

When engine is below operating temperature, the thermostats are closed. 
Coolant is bypassed to the water pump inlet. As the coolant temperature 
increases, both thermostats begin to open, allowing some of the coolant to 
flow to the radiator. At normal operating temperature, both thermostats are 
fully open and the bypass circuit is closed.

The engine thermostats must operate properly in order for the engine to 
operate in the most efficient heat range. Overheating or overcooling will 
shorten engine life.

 CAUTION: Never operate the engine without a thermostat. If operated without a 
thermostat, the path of least resistance for the coolant is through the bypass 
to the pump inlet. This will cause the engine to overheat. 

The thermostats control the coolant temperature. When the coolant 
temperature is below operating temperature, the thermostats are closed, and 
coolant is bypassed to the water pump inlet. As the coolant temperature 
increases to the intermediate range, both thermostats will start to open, and 
coolant flow to the bypass will start to be restricted. At engine operating 
temperature the thermostat will be open and the bypass will be closed.

Two identical thermostats are used. An incorrect, damaged, or 
malfunctioning thermostat can cause the engine to run too hot or too cold.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air System

The engine was designed as a turbocharged engine, but a naturally 
aspirated engine is available for industrial applications.

Air is pulled into the engine from an air filter. Clean air is very 
important to the life of the engine. Ingested dust and dirt can very quickly 
damage the cylinders.

Make sure an excellent quality air cleaner is used and that it is 
periodically replaced according to the manufacturer's recommendations.

Intake air for the naturally-aspirated engine flows from the air 
cleaner to the intake manifold. From the intake manifold, the air is pulled 
into the cylinders and used for combustion. After combustion it is forced out 
of the cylinders and through the exhaust manifold.

 Air System 

[FIGURE: A18183B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Intake Air Inlet to Turbocharger

2

—

Turbocharger Air to Charge Air Cooler

3

6K775

Charge Air Cooler

4

—

Intake Manifold (Integral Part of 6049)

5

6507

Intake Valve

6

6505

Exhaust Valve

7

9430

Exhaust Manifold (Pulse Type)

8

—

Dual Entry to Turbocharger

9

—

Turbocharger Exhaust Outlet (Part of 6K682)

On the turbocharged engines the intake air is drawn through the air 
cleaner into the compressor side of the turbocharger and then through the 
crossover tube and into the intake manifold.

From the intake manifold the air is forced into the cylinders and used 
for combustion. Energy from the exhaust gases is utilized by flowing the 
exhaust through the exhaust side of the turbocharger to drive the turbine wheel.

The turbine wheel and shaft drives the compressor wheel, which forces 
more air into the cylinders for combustion. The additional air provided by the 
turbocharger allows more fuel to be injected to increase the power output from 
the engine.

The engine uses a chassis-mounted charge air cooler instead of an 
engine-mounted aftercooler to provide cooler charge air to the engine to 
improve engine performance and reduce emissions. This system also uses large 
diameter piping to transfer the air from the engine turbocharger to the charge 
air cooler, then returns the air from the charge air cooler to the engine 
intake manifold.

The engine uses a wastegated turbocharger to limit the maximum boost 
pressure that the turbo can develop. Wastegate operation is controlled by an 
actuator that senses compressor pressure and balances it against a preset 
spring load.

The wastegate valve is located in the turbine inlet passage. When open, 
it diverts a portion of the exhaust gas around the turbine wheel, thereby 
controlling the shaft speed and boost.

 CAUTION: The wastegate bracket is an integral part of the turbocharger. The 
turbocharger is a performance part and must not be tampered with after it is 
adjusted at the factory. Tampering with the wastegate components can reduce 
durability by increasing cylinder pressure and thermal loading due to 
incorrect inlet and exhaust manifold pressure with a potential for poor fuel 
economy and failure to meet regulatory emission laws. 

The turbine and compressor wheels and shaft are supported by two 
rotating bearings in the bearing housing. Passages within the bearing housing 
direct filtered, pressurized engine oil to the shaft bearings and thrust 
bearing.

The oil is used to lubricate and cool the rotating components to 
provide for smooth operation. The oil then drains from the bearing housing to 
the engine sump through the oil drain line. A restricted or damaged oil drain 
line can cause the turbocharger bearing housing to be pressurized, causing oil 
to leak past the seals.

 NOTE: An adequate supply of good, filtered oil is very important to the life 
of the turbocharger. Make sure that an excellent quality oil is used and that 
it and the oil filter are changed according to the maintenance recommendations.

Engine

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable(s).

Remove hood and front bumper.

Drain engine oil and coolant.

Release air system pressure, if so equipped.

Remove air cleaner assembly, turbocharger air supply tube and 
turbocharger-to-charge air cooler tube.

Position drain pan and disconnect power steering pump supply hose at 
pump.

Disconnect power steering pump pressure hose at pump.

Disconnect brake air compressor air supply hose at compressor (if so 
equipped).

Disconnect air conditioner compressor electrical connectors (if so 
equipped).

Remove the air conditioner compressor mounting bolts and position air 
conditioner compressor to the side (if so equipped).

Remove the air conditioner condenser-to-charge air cooler retaining 
bolt and move condenser forward out of the way (if so equipped).

Remove fan shroud retaining bolts and hang shroud over fan.

Disconnect the radiator upper and lower hoses.

Disconnect coolant purge and supply hoses at coolant recovery reservoir.

Disconnect low coolant sensor at reservoir.

Remove the two reservoir-to-bracket retaining bolts and remove reservoir.

Disconnect the overflow hose at the radiator.

Remove the radiator retaining bolts and remove the radiator and charge 
air cooler as an assembly.

Remove shroud and remove fan-to-hub retaining bolts. Remove fan.

Disconnect brake compressor pressure hose or hydraulic brake lines (if 
so equipped).

Mark brake compressor governor hoses (if so equipped) prior to 
removing. Disconnect hoses.

Remove hose retainers at engine block.

Position hoses away from engine.

Disconnect oil cooler line at cooler and position out of way.

Disconnect exhaust pipe at turbocharger.

Remove air hose from air charge cooler to intake manifold.

Disconnect heater hoses from tubes at top of thermostat housing.

Disconnect throttle cable, hand throttle cable and transmission 
kickdown cable (automatic transmission only) and position aside.

Cut tie wraps and disconnect generator electrical harness.

Disconnect wiring to coolant temperature senders on thermostat housing.

Disconnect wiring from starter motor.

Disconnect speed sensor at flywheel housing.

Remove cable clamp retaining nut at flywheel housing.

Remove fuel lines-to-flywheel housing retaining bolts.

Disconnect two fuel lines at rear of fuel block and cap all openings.

Remove ground wire retaining bolt at flywheel housing.

Disconnect electrical connector at fuel shutoff solenoid.

Loosen clamps and remove oil fill hose.

Disconnect lower radiator hose at engine.

Remove lower hose strap retaining bolt and remove hose.

Remove exhaust pipe clamp retaining nut. Remove exhaust pipe.

Disconnect clutch slave cylinder at cross-shaft.

Remove clutch slave cylinder retaining bolts and remove cylinder.

Remove transmission. Refer to appropriate transmission section in Group 
07.

 NOTE: Lift engine only by front and rear lifting eyes attached to cylinder 
head.

Install Engine Mounting Brackets D92T-6000-C or equivalent on engine.

Remove the rear engine mount retaining bolts.

Remove the front mount-to-crossmember retaining bolts.

Position lifting equipment and remove engine assembly from the vehicle.

Mount engine on engine stand and move to work area.

 Installation 

 NOTE: For fastener torque values, refer to Torque Specifications at the end 
of this section.

Install Engine Mounting Brackets D92T-6000-C or equivalent on engine.

Lift and position engine in truck.

Attach front mount-to-crossmember retaining bolts.

Attach rear engine mounting retaining bolts.

If removed, install clutch. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Position clutch slave cylinder and attach retaining bolts. Connect 
hydraulic fitting. Refer to Section 08-02 for linkage assembly and hydraulic 
system bleeding.

Install transmission. Refer to the appropriate transmission section in 
Group 07.

Install exhaust pipe and clamp retaining nut.

Connect lower radiator hose and hose strap retaining bolt.

Install oil fill hose and clamps.

Connect fuel shutoff solenoid connector.

Attach ground wire retaining bolt to flywheel housing.

Remove protective caps from two fuel lines and attach to rear of fuel 
block.

Attach fuel lines-to-flywheel housing retaining bolts.

Attach cable clamp retaining nut at flywheel housing.

Connect speed sensor at flywheel housing.

Connect wiring for starter motor.

Connect wiring to coolant temperature senders on thermostat housing.

Connect generator electrical harness.

Connect throttle cable, hand throttle cable and transmission kickdown 
cable.

Connect heater hoses at top of thermostat housing.

Connect exhaust pipe at turbocharger.

Connect air hose from intake manifold to charge air cooler.

Connect oil cooler line to oil cooler.

Connect brake compressor governor hoses (if so equipped) and attach 
hose retainers to engine block.

Connect brake compressor hose or hydraulic brake lines (if so equipped).

Attach fan to hub and install shroud.

Install radiator and charge air cooler.

Attach overflow hose to radiator.

Assemble coolant reservoir.

Connect low coolant sensor at coolant reservoir.

Connect radiator upper and lower hoses.

Connect the air conditioner compressor and mounting bolts (if so 
equipped).

Connect the air conditioner compressor electrical connectors (if so 
equipped).

Connect the brake air compressor air supply hose to compressor (if so 
equipped).

Connect the power steering pump pressure hose to the pump.

Connect the turbocharger-to-charge air cooler, turbocharger air supply 
tube, and air cleaner assembly.

Add engine oil and coolant.

Install hood and front bumper (tilt hood), or entire front clip 
(alligator hood).

Connect battery ground cable(s).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Valve Spring, Valve Spring Retainer and Valve Stem Seal

Broken valve springs or damaged valve stem seals and retainers may be 
replaced without removing the cylinder head, provided damage to the valve or 
valve seal has not occurred.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Valve Spring Compressor

T83T-6513-A

 Removal 

Remove the valve cover and rocker arm assembly.

Remove the fuel injectors.

Install an air line using the Rotunda Compression Test Adapter 
D92T-6600-B or equivalent in the injector nozzle hole and turn on the air 
supply.

 CAUTION: Take care not to drive the valve into the piston. Doing so could damage 
the valve and/or piston. Make sure the piston is not at TDC when loosening the 
retainers from the locks. 

 NOTE: It may be necessary to break the retainer loose from the valve locks. 
This can be done by tapping the edge of the retainer with a plastic hammer or 
by placing a socket (of approximately the same outside diameter) on the 
retainer and tapping the socket with a plastic hammer. Do not strike the tip 
of the valve stem.

Use Valve Spring Compressor T83T-6513-A to compress the valve spring.

[FIGURE: A21985A.gif]

Use a pencil magnet to remove the valve collets. Discard the valve 
collets.

Slowly release the pressure on the valve spring.

Remove the valve spring retainer and the valve spring.

Remove the valve spring seat/valve seal assembly.

 NOTE: If air pressure has forced the piston to the bottom of the cylinder, 
any removal of air pressure will allow the valve(s) to fall into the cylinder. 
A rubber band, tape or string wrapped around the end of the valve stem will 
prevent this condition and will still allow enough travel to check the valve 
for binding.

Remove the valve stem seal.

[FIGURE: A90331A.gif]

[FIGURE: A23419A.gif]

 Installation 

Inspect the cylinder head and valve assembly. Inspect the valve stem 
for damage. Rotate the valve and check valve stem tip for eccentric 
(out-of-round) movement. Check for binding by moving the valve up and down 
through its normal travel in the valve guide checking for binds. If valve has 
been damaged, it will be necessary to remove cylinder head for repairs. 
Inspect the retainer locks for excessive wear, and replace in pairs, as 
necessary. When installing a new valve, always use new retainer locks.

If the valve is OK, hold it in the closed position and apply air 
pressure within the cylinder. This will hold the valve in the closed position.

Lubricate the valve stem with recommended quality engine oil.

Install the valve spring seat/valve seal assembly over the valve stem. 
To prevent oil carryover, the seals are color coded and must be installed as 
follows:

Exhaust valve: orange (with 64 grooves per inch)

Intake valve: black (with 40 grooves per inch)

[FIGURE: A18316A.gif]

Install the valve springs.

Install the valve spring retainers.

[FIGURE: A18317A.gif]

Use Valve Spring Compressor T83T-6513-A to compress the valve springs.

[FIGURE: A21985A.gif]

 NOTE: Use new valve spring retainer collets when rebuilding the cylinder head.

Install the new valve spring retainer collets.

 WARNING: WEAR EYE PROTECTION. IF THE COLLETS ARE NOT CORRECTLY INSTALLED, THEY 
CAN FLY OUT WHEN THE STEMS ARE HIT WITH A HAMMER. 

Use a plastic hammer to gently hit the top of the valve stems to make 
sure the valve collets are correctly seated in the spring retainer.

[FIGURE: A18319A.gif]

Remove the compressor tool. Turn off the air and remove the air line 
adapter.

Install the rocker arm assembly, push rods and valve cover.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Water Pump

 Removal

Drain the engine coolant.

Remove the accessory drive belt(s).

Loosen the generator link bracket at the generator and remove the link 
bracket retaining bolt at the water pump. Position bracket out of the way.

Remove the remaining water pump retaining bolts.

Remove the water pump from the cylinder block.

Clean the gasket sealing surfaces of the cylinder block and water pump.

 Installation 

Position the water pump with a new gasket onto the cylinder block and 
install two water pump retaining bolts.

Position the link bracket to the water pump and install the remaining 
water pump retaining bolt.

[FIGURE: A21473A.gif]

(15-19 lb-ft) and the link bracket-to-generator bolt to 43 Nm 
(32 lb-ft).

Install the accessory drive belt(s). Check torque of belt tensioner 
mounting bolts. Correct torque value is 43 Nm (32 lb-ft).

Fill and bleed the cooling system.

Connect the battery ground cable(s).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Oil Seal, Crankshaft, Front 

 Removal 

Remove the drive belt.

Remove the vibration damper and pulley. Use Engine Barring Tool 
D92T-6000-A or equivalent to hold the crankshaft while removing the capscrews. 
Remove the crankshaft oil seal dust shield, if used.

[FIGURE: A18249A.gif]

Remove the front cover.

[FIGURE: A18250A.gif]

Clean the gasket sealing surface.

Remove the oil seal from the front cover. Drive the oil seal from the 
back side of the cover toward the front side of the cover, while supporting 
the front cover.

[FIGURE: A17375A.gif]

Clean the front cover seal bore and the crankshaft surface of all oil 
and seal residue.

Inspect the crankshaft for excessive wear. If the crankshaft has 
excessive wear, a service wear sleeve is available.

 Installation 

Apply a bead of Loctite® 227 or equivalent to the 
outside diameter of the seal.

Position the seal on the service tool, Cummins Engine Company Part No. 
3824499, with the lubricating oil seal dust lip facing outward. Leave the 
plastic pilot installation tool in the lubricating oil seal.

[FIGURE: A23639A.gif]

Properly support the front cover lubricating oil seal flange to prevent 
damage to the lubricating oil seal and from the cover.

 CAUTION: Always use a seal pilot when installing a seal. 

Press the lubricating oil seal into the front cover from the back side 
of the cover toward the front side of the cover.

[FIGURE: A23640A.gif]

Press the lubricating oil seal until the service tool bottoms against 
the front cover.

Install the gasket and front cover on the engine using the plastic 
pilot installation tool to guide the seal on the crankshaft.

Install the front cover mounting capscrews and tighten to 24 Nm
 (18 lb-ft). Remove the plastic pilot installation tool.

[FIGURE: A23641A.gif]

 NOTE: Lubrication is not required for installation.

Install the crankshaft oil seal dust shield if used. Push the dust 
shield onto the crankshaft with the part number facing out away from the 
engine. The dust shield must contact the oil seal.

[FIGURE: A23642A.gif]

Install the vibration damper and pulley. Use Engine Barring Tool 
D92T-6000-A or equivalent to hold the crankshaft while tightening the 
capscrews. Tighten the vibration damper screws to 200 Nm (148 
lb-ft) and the pulley-to-vibration damper screws to 77 Nm (57 
lb-ft).

Install the drive belt. Check torque of belt tensioner mounting bolts. 
Correct torque value is 43 Nm (32 lb-ft).

 Wear Sleeve, Front Crankshaft Replacement 

 Removal 

Remove the fan drive belt, vibration damper, gear cover and seal. Refer 
to Oil Seal, Crankshaft, Front in the Removal and Installation portion of this 
section.

 CAUTION: Do not nick or gouge the crankshaft with the chisel. If the crankshaft 
is damaged, it must be replaced. 

Use a hammer and dull chisel only as wide as the wear sleeve. Make one 
or two soft blows across the wear sleeve. This will expand the wear sleeve, 
allowing the sleeve to be removed.

[FIGURE: A23643A.gif]

Clean and inspect the crankshaft at the oil seal area for dirt, nicks, 
chisel marks, scratches, rust or corrosion, or other damage that would prevent 
a proper wear sleeve installation.

 Installation 

Use Cummins Engine Company Part No. 3823908, Crankshaft Front Wear 
Sleeve Installation Tool, to install the wear sleeve to the correct position 
on the crankshaft.

 Crankshaft Front Wear Sleeve Installation Tool 

[FIGURE: A23644A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Spacer (Part of 3823908)

2

—

Hair Pin Cotter (Part of 3823908)

3

—

Driver (Part of 3823908)

4

—

Capscrew, M14 x 1.5 x 60 mm (Part of 3823908)

Apply a thin coat of 15W40 engine oil to the driver inside diameter and 
capscrew threads.

[FIGURE: A23645A.gif]

Position the chamfered end of the wear sleeve onto the end of the 
crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A23646A.gif]

Position the counterbore end of the driver onto the wear sleeve.

[FIGURE: A23647A.gif]

Install two capscrews (without spacers or hairpin cotters) through the 
driver and into the crankshaft capscrew holes. Align the wear sleeve and 
driver perpendicular with the crankshaft. Tighten the capscrews finger-tight.

[FIGURE: A23648A.gif]

 NOTE: To prevent damage to the wear sleeve, do not exceed one-half revolution 
of each capscrew.

Alternately tighten the capscrews until the sleeve is installed to a 
depth of approximately 16 mm (0.625 inch). Tighten to 20 Nm 
(15 lb-ft).

Remove the capscrews and install a spacer on each capscrew. Install the 
two capscrews again.

[FIGURE: A23649A.gif]

Continue to tighten the capscrews alternately until the bottom of the 
driver contacts the end of the crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A23650A.gif]

Remove the driver. Use hairpin cotters to secure the capscrews and 
spacers to the tool during storage.

[FIGURE: A23651A.gif]

 NOTE: The wear sleeve and oil seal mating surface must be clean and dry to 
ensure proper oil sealing.

Clean the wear sleeve and crankshaft of any lubricate.

Install the oil seal, crankshaft front cover, vibration damper and fan 
drive belt.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Cover, Front 

 Removal 

Remove the tachometer drive cable.

Remove the tachometer drive.

[FIGURE: A18189A.gif]

Remove the drive belt.

Remove the vibration damper and pulley. Use Engine Barring Tool 
D92T-6000-A or equivalent to hold the crankshaft while removing the capscrews.

Remove the crankshaft oil seal dust shield, if used.

[FIGURE: A18249A.gif]

Remove the front cover.

[FIGURE: A18250A.gif]

Clean the front cover and gear housing gasket surface.

Inspect the front cover for cracks or damage.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: The crankshaft must be clean, dry and oil free before installing the 
front cover. Failure to properly clean the sealing surface will result in an 
oil leak. 

 CAUTION: Always use a seal pilot when you install a seal. 

 CAUTION: The seal lip and the sealing surface on the crankshaft must be free 
from all oil residue to prevent seal leaks. 

Thoroughly clean and dry the front seal area of the crankshaft.

Install the seal tool pilot from the service seal replacement kit onto 
the nose of the crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A18264A.gif]

Use two M8 x 1.25 x 70 mm guide pins to aid in alignment of the gasket. 
Apply a coat of Perfect Seal Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A to both sides of the 
gasket.

Install the gasket and front cover over the pilot.

 NOTE: The seal will align the front cover at the seal bore.

Install the capscrews.

[FIGURE: A18265A.gif]

Tighten the front cover capscrews to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft). 
Remove the seal tool pilot from the nose of the crankshaft.

 NOTE: No lubrication is required for installation.

Push the crankshaft oil seal dust shield onto the crankshaft with the 
part number facing out away from the engine. The dust shield should contact or 
be within 4 mm (0.15 inch) of the oil seal.

[FIGURE: A18266A.gif]

Install the vibration damper and pulley. Use Engine Barring Tool 
D92T-6000-A or equivalent to hold the crankshaft. Tighten the vibration damper 
capscrews to 200 Nm (148 lb-ft) and the pulley-to-vibration 
damper capscrews to 77 Nm (57 lb-ft).

Install the drive belt. Check torque of belt tensioner mounting bolts. 
Correct torque value is 43 Nm (32 lb-ft).

Install the tachometer drive and cable.

Operate the engine 5 to 10 minutes to check for leaks and proper 
operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft Drive Gear and Thrust Plate, In Vehicle

 Removal 

Remove the following components:

valve cover

rocker arm assemblies

push rods

crankshaft vibration damper

front cover

fuel lift pump. Refer to Section 03A-04A .

 NOTE: It is necessary to partially remove the camshaft to replace the 
camshaft gear; therefore, the tappets must be raised and secured with the 
dowel rods.

Insert Lifter Holders, part of Lifter Holder Set D94T-6500-A or 
equivalent such as wooden dowels, securely into each tappet. Use a soft-face 
hammer if necessary.

[FIGURE: A17395A.gif]

Pull each valve tappet up until it makes contact with the cylinder 
block. Put a rubber band around two dowels to hold the tappets off the 
camshaft. 

[FIGURE: A18268A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft to align the timing marks before trying to remove 
the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A17397B.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the thrust plate.

 NOTE: Rotate the camshaft as it is being removed. Use extreme care to make 
sure the camshaft bushings are not damaged during the camshaft removal process.

Remove the camshaft from the cylinder block just enough to expose the 
first two camshaft lobes.

[FIGURE: A23421A.gif]

Install retainer to secure the camshaft in position. Secure the 
retainer between the second camshaft lobe and the second camshaft journal 
using an 8 mm x 1.25 capscrew in one of the holes used to secure the camshaft 
thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A23422A.gif]

Position the gear remover yoke over the first camshaft journal and 
assemble the rods through the access holes in the camshaft gear web. Assemble 
the remainder of the tool as shown. Gear installer yoke is not used for 
camshaft gear removal. Tighten the nuts and rods finger-tight.

[FIGURE: A23423A.gif]

Tighten the pressing screw by hand while positioning the gear remover 
mandrel between the screw press and the end of the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A23424A.gif]

 CAUTION: Hold the tool securely while tightening the pressing screw to prevent 
the tool and camshaft gear from falling during removal. 

Using the torque arm inserted in the screw press, tighten the pressing 
screw in a clockwise direction while keeping the tool from rotating.

[FIGURE: A23425A.gif]

Remove the tool and camshaft gear assembly from the vehicle. 
Disassemble the tool.

 Installation 

Assemble the Camshaft Gear Installer Part No. 3323589 to the camshaft 
gear. Place the rods through the holes in the camshaft gear and screw the rods 
into the gear installer yoke. Secure the screw press to the rods with the 
nuts. The nuts and rods need only be finger-tight. Turn the forcing screw 
counterclockwise as far as it will go.

Be certain the chamfer in the camshaft gear will be positioned toward 
the cylinder block during camshaft gear installation.

[FIGURE: A23426A.gif]

Lubricate the inside diameter of the camshaft gear and the end of the 
camshaft. Position the tool and camshaft gear assembly over the camshaft and 
slide the gear installer yoke over the front camshaft journal.

[FIGURE: A23427A.gif]

Engage the camshaft gear keyway with the camshaft locating pin and, by 
hand, turn the forcing screw clockwise until the camshaft gear, camshaft and 
tool are all held firmly together and properly aligned with each other.

[FIGURE: A23428A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an impact wrench with this tool, otherwise damage may result 
to the camshaft gear, camshaft or the tool. 

Using the torque arm inserted in the screw press, tighten the forcing 
screw in the clockwise direction while keeping the tool from rotating.

[FIGURE: A23425A.gif]

While turning the forcing screw, the effort required should increase 
steadily until the camshaft gear is against the camshaft shoulder.

When the camshaft gear is pressed firmly against the camshaft shoulder, 
camshaft gear installation is complete.

[FIGURE: A23429A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not try to force the camshaft into the camshaft bore as damage to 
the camshaft bushing can result. 

Install the camshaft. While pushing in slightly, rotate the camshaft 
and carefully work the camshaft through the camshaft bushings. As each 
camshaft journal passes through a bushing, the camshaft will drop slightly and 
the camshaft lobes will catch on the bushings. Rotating the camshaft will free 
the lobe from the bushing and allow the camshaft to be installed.

[FIGURE: A17418A.gif]

Before the camshaft gear engages the crankshaft gear, check the 
camshaft for ease of rotation. When installed properly, the camshaft should 
rotate freely.

Align the timing marks on the camshaft with the timing mark on the 
crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A18275A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the camshaft assembly does not drop on your fingers when 
installing the thrust plate. 

Install the camshaft thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A18276A.gif]

Install the camshaft thrust plate capscrews and tighten to 24 Nm
 (18 lb-ft).

 NOTE: If the camshaft end clearance is greater than the stated limit, the 
thrust plate must be replaced.

Measure camshaft end clearance with a dial indicator. End clearance is 
controlled by the thickness of the thrust plate and the groove in the 
camshaft. Camshaft end clearance limits are 0.12-0.46 mm (0.0047-0.0181 inch).

 NOTE: The gears must be replaced if the backlash is greater than the above 
limit.

 NOTE: Excessive gear backlash can be caused by worn camshaft bushings.

Put a dial indicator on the camshaft gear and check the gear backlash 
between the camshaft gear and the crankshaft gear. Camshaft gear backlash 
limits are 0.08-0.33 mm (0.003-0.013 inch).

Remove the wooden dowel rods from the valve tappets.

Install all parts that were removed:

fuel lift pump

front cover

crankshaft vibration damper

push rods

rocker arm assemblies

valve cover

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft Drive Gear and Thrust Plate, Out of Vehicle

 Removal 

Remove the camshaft.

 CAUTION: Place a wooden block under the camshaft to prevent damage as the 
camshaft drops free from the cam gear. 

Place the camshaft and gear assembly in a hydraulic press. Press the 
gear off the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A18277A.gif]

Push the camshaft from the gear.

Remove the camshaft dowel pin.

[FIGURE: A18278A.gif]

 NOTE: If the fretting, burrs or raised material cannot be removed, replace 
the gear.

Visually inspect the camshaft gear for cracks and chipped or broken 
teeth. Inspect the bore of the gear for fretting or burrs. Remove fretting, 
burrs and raised material with Scotch-Brite® 7448 or 
equivalent.

 NOTE: If the keyway is damaged or the burrs cannot be removed, the gear must 
be replaced.

Inspect the gear keyway for burrs. Remove burrs with Scotch-Brite®
 7448 or equivalent.

 Installation 

Use a leather hammer to install the camshaft gear dowel pin.

[FIGURE: A18279A.gif]

Install the key.

Lubricate the camshaft gear journals with Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

 CAUTION: The gear will be permanently distorted if overheated. The oven 
temperature must never exceed 177°C (350°F). 

For steel camshaft gear (bolted), heat the gear in an oven for a 
minimum of 45 minutes, but not longer than six hours.

 CAUTION: The gear will be permanently distorted if overheated. The oven 
temperature must never exceed 149°C (300°F). 

For austempered camshaft gear (nonbolted), heat the gear in an oven for 
45 minutes.

 WARNING: USE INSULATED GLOVES, PART NO. 3823730 OR EQUIVALENT, WHEN HANDLING 
HEATED PARTS. HOT PARTS CAN CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY. 

 CAUTION: To prevent engine damage, the timing marks and gear part number must be 
facing away from the camshaft when the gear is installed. 

 CAUTION: Keep the camshaft in a vertical position with the gear up until the 
gear has cooled. Do not use water to reduce the cooling time. Using water will 
crack the gear. 

 NOTE: The gear must be installed within 30 seconds after it is removed from 
the oven.

Remove the gear from the oven. Align the keyway in the gear with the 
dowel pin in the camshaft and install the gear on the camshaft. Make sure the 
gear is seated against the camshaft shoulder.

[FIGURE: A18280A.gif]

Using a 0.025-mm (0.001-inch) feeler gauge, check to see if the feeler 
gauge can be inserted between the gear and the shoulder on the camshaft. If 
the feeler gauge can be inserted, the gear is not properly seated.

For bolted camshafts, install camshaft bolt and washer. Tighten the 
capscrew to 27 Nm (20 lb-ft), then rotate the capscrew an 
additional 180 degrees.

Install the camshaft.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Crankshaft Gear

 Removal 

Remove crankshaft from engine.

Using Bearing Pulling Attachment D84L-1123-A, Push-Puller Set 
D80L-927-A and Shaft Protector D80L-625-5 or equivalents, remove gear from 
crankshaft. 

[FIGURE: A17880C.gif]

Remove all burrs and make sure the crankshaft sprocket surface on the 
end of the crankshaft is smooth. 

 Installation 

If previously removed, install the alignment pin until it bottoms in 
the bore. 

 CAUTION: The gear will be permanently distorted if overheated. The oven 
temperature must never exceed 177°C (350°F). 

Heat the crankshaft gear in Rotunda Gear/Bearing Heater 164-R3900 or 
equivalent for 45 minutes at 149°C (300°F). 

Apply a thin coat of lubricant on the nose of the crankshaft. 

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE GLOVES TO PREVENT PERSONAL INJURY. 

 NOTE: Do not stop once you have begun to install the gear onto the 
crankshaft. Do not turn the gear while you are installing it. The gear will 
get stuck on the crankshaft once you stop or if you turn the gear while 
installing it. If this occurs, remove the gear and start again. 

Install the hot gear up to the crankshaft shoulder with the timing mark 
facing out. 

Install the crankshaft.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Geartrain Timing, Initial

 Removal 

The timing pin assembly is precisely located on the gear housing to 
correspond to top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1. Failure to locate the 
timing pin assembly to TDC for cylinder No. 1 prior to removal will result in 
incorrect fuel injection timing.

 NOTE: If the timing pin has been damaged and cannot be used to locate TDC, 
refer to Relocating Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head 
Installed in the Removal and Installation portion of this section for procedure to locate top 
dead center with the cylinder head installed on the engine. If the cylinder 
head is removed, refer to Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head Removed .

Locate top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1 by barring engine 
slowly while pressing on the engine timing pin.

[FIGURE: A17171A.gif]

Remove the timing pin assembly and seal.

[FIGURE: A17435A.gif]

 Installation 

Install a new O-ring into the groove of the timing pin assembly. 
Lubricate the O-ring with 15W-40 engine oil.

Apply a coat of Threadlock® 262 E2FZ-19554-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 to the threads of the Torx®
 screws and install the timing pin assembly.

Push the pin into the hole in the cam gear to align the housing.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the pin and gear, make sure the timing pin is 
disengaged before rotating the crankshaft. 

Hold the timing pin in while tightening the Torx® 
screws to 8 Nm (71 lb-in).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft and Valve Tappets

 Removal with Oil Pan Installed 

 NOTE: On tilt hood vehicles, it is necessary to remove the radiator, charge 
air cooler and air conditioning condenser to facilitate camshaft removal. 
Also, once these items are removed, it is necessary to remove the front engine 
support-to-frame bolts and lift the front of the engine about six inches so 
the camshaft will clear the lower radiator support.

Remove the following components:

valve cover

rocker arm assemblies

push rods

crankshaft vibration damper

front cover

fuel lift pump. Refer to Section 03A-04A .

The valve tappets can be removed with the oil pan installed by using a 
tappet removal tool kit consisting of:

valve tappet tray (1)

dowel rods (12)

rubber bands (12)

nylon string (1)

[FIGURE: A18267A.gif]

Lift the tappets so the camshaft can be removed using the kit shown.

 NOTE: It is necessary to remove the camshaft to replace the valve tappets; 
therefore, the tappets will be raised and secured with the dowel rods.

 NOTE: Number each tappet with the cylinder number position as it is removed. 
The tappets must be installed in the same positions as removed.

Insert Lifter Holder Set D94T-6500-A or equivalent such as wooden 
dowels, securely into each tappet. Use a soft-face hammer if necessary.

[FIGURE: A17395A.gif]

Pull each valve tappet up until it makes contact with the cylinder 
block. Put a rubber band around two dowels to hold the tappets off the 
camshaft. 

[FIGURE: A18268A.gif]

Remove the nut and washer from the fuel injection pump drive gear.

[FIGURE: A18269A.gif]

Install the puller on the drive gear. Tighten the capscrews until the 
gear is loose on the fuel injection pump driveshaft.

Remove the fuel injection pump drive gear.

 NOTE: If the camshaft or gear is being replaced due to geartrain noise, check 
the gear backlash.

 NOTE: Excessive gear backlash can be caused by worn camshaft bushings.

Position an indicator on a tooth of the camshaft gear.

[FIGURE: A18270A.gif]

Note the camshaft gear backlash and end clearance. Mark the camshaft 
gear and crankshaft gear for further analysis if backlash or end clearance 
exceeds limits. Camshaft end clearance (A) limits are 0.12-0.46 mm 
(0.0047-0.0181 inch). Camshaft gear backlash (B) limits are 0.152-0.38 mm 
(0.006-0.015 inch).

[FIGURE: A18271A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft to align the timing marks before trying to remove 
the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A17397B.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the thrust plate.

 NOTE: Rotate the camshaft as it is being removed. Use extreme care to make 
sure the camshaft bushings are not damaged during the camshaft removal process.

Remove the camshaft thrust plate and camshaft from the cylinder block.

To aid in tappet removal and to prevent tappets from dropping down into 
oil pan, fabricate a trough and insert the trough to the full length of the 
camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17400A.gif]

Make sure the trough is positioned so it will catch the tappet when the 
holder is removed.

Only remove one tappet at a time. Remove the rubber band from the two 
companion tappets, securing the tappet not to be removed with the rubber band.

[FIGURE: A17402A.gif]

Remove the rubber bands from the wooden dowels that are used to hold 
the tappets up during camshaft removal/installation.

Remove the tappets from the wooden dowels.

Pull the wooden dowel from the tappet bore allowing the tappet to fall 
into the trough.

[FIGURE: A17401A.gif]

When the tappet is dropped into the trough, most of the time it will 
fall over. However, if it doesn't, gently shake the trough just enough to 
allow the tappet to fall over before removing.

Carefully pull the tray and tappet from the camshaft bore and remove 
the tappet. Repeat the process until all tappets are removed.

 NOTE: Special care must be taken not to knock or shake the tappet over the 
end of the trough when removing the No. 6 cylinder tappets.

Carefully pull the trough and tappet from the camshaft bore and remove 
the tappet. Repeat the process until all tappets are removed.

Inspect the tappets and camshaft. Refer to Camshaft and refer to Valve 
Tappets in the Cleaning and Inspection portion of this section.

 Removal with Oil Pan Removed 

 NOTE: Only four tappets are accessible at one time. The crankshaft must be 
rotated three times to access all of the tappets.

Rotate the crankshaft to access the tappets.

[FIGURE: A18272A.gif]

Only remove the rubber bands from the wooden dowels holding the 
accessible tappets.

Remove the accessible tappets/dowels.

 Installation with Oil Pan Installed 

Insert the plastic tray or trough the full length of the camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17400A.gif]

Insert the installation tool through the tappet bore and into the 
trough. Feed the installation tool through the camshaft bore by carefully 
pulling the trough out the front. The barrier at the rear of the trough will 
pull the tool out most of the time.

[FIGURE: A17410A.gif]

Lubricate the tappets with Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

 NOTE: To aid in removing the installation tool after the tappet is installed, 
move the tool in and out of the tappet bore several times before installing 
the tappets.

Insert the installation tool into the tappet.

Slide the trough into the camshaft bore.

Pull the installation tool and tappet through the camshaft bore and up 
into the tappet bore.

[FIGURE: A17411A.gif]

If difficulty is experienced in getting the tappet to make the bend 
from the trough up to the tappet bore, pull the trough out enough to allow the 
tappet to drop down and align itself, then pull the tappet up into the bore.

After the tappet has been pulled up into position, slide the trough 
back into the camshaft bore and rotate it one half turn. This will position 
the round side of the trough up, which will hold the tappet in place.

[FIGURE: A17413A.gif]

Remove the installation tool from the tappet.

Insert a lifter holder or wooden dowel rod into the top of the tappet. 
Wrap rubber bands around the wooden dowels to secure the tappets. Repeat this 
process until all tappets have been installed.

Remove the trough from the camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17414B.gif]

 Installation with Oil Pan Removed 

Lubricate the tappets with Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

 NOTE: Only four tappets are accessible at a time which will require rotation 
of the engine to install the remaining tappets.

Insert the wooden dowel rods used for holding the tappets up during 
camshaft removal into the tappets.

Insert the dowel rods with the tappets attached through the tappet bores.

[FIGURE: A18273A.gif]

Wrap rubber bands around the wooden dowels to secure the tappets. 
Repeat this process until all tappets have been installed.

[FIGURE: A18274A.gif]

Install the oil pan.

 NOTE: The crankshaft should be positioned so the No. 1 cylinder is at 
approximately TDC, so the camshaft does not hit the crankshaft counterweight 
during installation.

Before installing the camshaft, apply a coat of Engine Assembly 
Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A 
to the front camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17416A.gif]

Lubricate the camshaft journals and lobes, and the thrust plate with 
Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A.

[FIGURE: A17417A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not try to force the camshaft into the camshaft bore as damage to 
the camshaft bushing can result. 

Install the camshaft. While pushing in slightly, rotate the camshaft 
and carefully work the camshaft through the camshaft bushings. As each 
camshaft journal passes through a bushing, the camshaft will drop slightly and 
the camshaft lobes will catch on the bushings. Rotating the camshaft will free 
the lobe from the bushing and allow the camshaft to be installed.

[FIGURE: A17418A.gif]

Before the camshaft gear engages the crankshaft gear, check the 
camshaft for ease of rotation. When installed properly, the camshaft should 
rotate freely.

Align the timing marks on the camshaft with the timing mark on the 
crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A18275A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the camshaft assembly does not drop on your fingers when 
installing the thrust plate. 

Install the camshaft thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A18276A.gif]

Install the camshaft thrust plate capscrews and tighten to 24 Nm
 (18 lb-ft).

 NOTE: If the camshaft end clearance is greater than the stated limit, the 
thrust plate must be replaced.

Measure camshaft end clearance with a dial indicator.

End clearance is controlled by the thickness of the thrust plate and 
the groove in the camshaft. Camshaft end clearance limits are 0.12-0.46 mm 
(0.0047-0.0181 inch).

 NOTE: The gears must be replaced if the backlash is greater than the above 
limit.

 NOTE: Excessive gear backlash can be caused by worn camshaft bushings.

Put a dial indicator on the camshaft gear and check the gear backlash 
between the camshaft gear and the crankshaft gear. Camshaft gear backlash 
limits are 0.152-0.38 mm (0.006-0.015 inch).

Remove the wooden dowel rods from the valve tappets.

Install all parts that were removed:

fuel lift pump

fuel injection pump drive gear

front cover

vibration damper

push rods

rocker assemblies

valve cover

Fill the engine with oil.

Fill and bleed the engine cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Operate the engine at idle until the coolant temperature reaches 82°
C (180°F) and check for leaks and proper 
operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft Rear Cover

 Removal 

 NOTE: It is necessary to remove the rear camshaft cover when the camshaft 
bearings are being removed and replaced.

If the camshaft has not been removed from the block, pry the cover from 
the rear countershaft bore with a wide-lipped screwdriver.

[FIGURE: A108141A.gif]

If camshaft removal is necessary or if the camshaft has been removed, 
insert a long rod through the camshaft bore and knock the cover out. Be 
careful not to damage the cam bearing surfaces.

 Installation 

Clean all of the old sealer from the cover. If the sealing edge is 
nicked or damaged, replace the cover.

Liberally coat the sealing edge of the rear cam cover with Perfect Seal 
Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

Tap the rear cam cover into place with a soft mallet until it is fully 
seated.

[FIGURE: A107771A.gif]

 Removal

T65L-6250-A or equivalent.

 NOTE: Bearings 2 through 7 align with only one oil hole. Bearing 1 must align 
with two oil holes.

installing the camshaft. If the clearance is not within 0.076-0.127 mm

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Piston and Piston Rings

 Removal 

Remove engine from vehicle and place on engine stand.

Remove the cylinder head.

Remove the oil pan and suction tube.

Roll the engine to a vertical position. Rotate the engine enough so the 
pistons are below the carbon deposits which are found above the ring travel 
area.

 CAUTION: Use care not to damage the liner when removing carbon. 

Use a scraper or blunt edged instrument to loosen the carbon deposits. 

[FIGURE: A24605A.gif]

Remove any remaining carbon with a cleaning pad.

 WARNING: TO PREVENT SERIOUS EYE DAMAGE, WEAR EYE PROTECTION DURING THIS OPERATION. 

 CAUTION: Do not use the steel wire wheel in the piston travel area. Operate the 
wheel in a circular motion to remove the deposits. 

An alternative method to remove the carbon ridge is to use a 
high-quality steel wire wheel installed in a drill or die grinder.

[FIGURE: A24606A.gif]

Mark each rod cap according to cylinder.

Mark each piston according to the cylinder.

Remove the nuts from the connecting rod capscrews. Tap on the rod bolts 
to loosen and remove the rod cap.

Push the connecting rod and piston assembly out of the bore.

Remove piston rings from piston.

 Installation 

Position the oil ring expander in the oil control ring groove.

[FIGURE: A17504A.gif]

Install the oil control ring with the end gap opposite the ends on the 
expander.

 NOTE: The top surface of the upper two rings is identified with the word TOP 
or the supplier mark. 

Install the intermediate and top ring with the word TOP or supplier 
mark up.

[FIGURE: A24607A.gif]

Install bearing shells into both the connecting rod and the cap. 
Lubricate the connecting rod and cap bearings with clean engine oil.

Lubricate the rings and piston skirts with clean engine oil.

Position the rings.

[FIGURE: A17317A.gif]

Turn the crankshaft until connecting rod journal for the piston to be 
installed is at bottom dead center. 

Using clean engine oil, lubricate the cylinder walls and crankshaft 
journal with clean engine oil.

Compress the rings using a strap-type ring compressor.

Position the piston and rod assembly into the cylinder bore with the 
word FRONT on the piston toward the front of the engine. Push the piston into 
the bore until the top of the piston is approximately 50 mm (2 inches) below 
the top of the bore.

Pull the connecting rod onto the crankshaft journal.

[FIGURE: A18245A.gif]

Lubricate the connecting rod bolts with clean engine oil.

 CAUTION: The number stamped on the rod and cap at the parting line must match 
and be installed on the camshaft side of the engine. 

Install the connecting rod cap and start the connecting rod nuts. 

Lubricate under the connecting rod nuts with clean engine oil.

[FIGURE: A24608A.gif]

Tighten the connecting rod cap to the connecting rod evenly. Tighten 
the connecting rod nuts in three steps to the following torques.

Step 1 — 40 Nm (30 lb-ft)

Step 2 — 80 Nm (59 lb-ft)

Step 3 — 120 Nm (88 lb-ft)

Move the connecting rod side to side to verify side clearance.

[FIGURE: A24609A.gif]

Measure the side clearance between the connecting rod and the 
crankshaft. Clearance should be 0.1-0.3 mm (0.004-0.012 inch).

[FIGURE: A24610A.gif]

Install suction tube and oil pan.

Install the cylinder head.

Install engine in vehicle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Cylinder Liner

 Removal 

Drain the cooling system.

Remove the cylinder head.

Drain the engine oil. After the oil is drained, reinstall the drain 
plug and a new gasket. Tighten to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft).

Remove the oil pan and oil suction tube.

[FIGURE: A23471A.gif]

Remove the pistons and the connecting rods.

[FIGURE: A18219A.gif]

 NOTE: Before removing the cylinder liners, visually inspect the condition to 
determine reuse.

Visually inspect the inside diameters of the liner for cracks, scuffing 
or scoring.

 NOTE: If a fingernail catches in the scratch, the liner must be replaced.

Inspect the inside diameters for vertical scratches deep enough to be 
felt with a fingernail.

Visually inspect the inside diameter for liner bore polishing. A 
moderate polish produces a bright mirror finish in the worn area with traces 
of the original hone marks or an indication of an etch pattern. A heavy polish 
produces a bright mirror finish in the worn area with no traces of hone marks 
or an etch pattern.

Do not reuse liners exhibiting heavy polish or any indications of 
particle embedment from a failure. Severely worn liners will have a ridge near 
the top of the liner bore.

[FIGURE: A18232A.gif]

If the wear pattern indicates the liner bore is not straight or not 
round, use a dial bore gauge to measure the liner inside diameter in four 
places 90 degrees apart at the top and bottom of the piston travel area.

Cylinder Liner Dimensions

mm

Inch

Maximum Out of Round

0.04

0.0016

Maximum Taper

0.04

0.0016

Maximum Inside Diameter

114.117

4.4928

 NOTE: If a liner bore is not acceptable for reuse, it must be replaced. 
Damaged liners cannot be honed or deglazed. This would destroy the cross-hatch 
pattern needed for oil control.

 NOTE: Do not remove or disturb the liner seals for liners which pass the 
inspection criteria.

Liner protrusion is the distance the liner protrudes above the block 
face. Before removing the liners, check the protrusion in the unclamped state. 
Cylinder liner protrusion limits are 0.025-0.122 mm (0.001-0.0048 inch).

[FIGURE: A18233A.gif]

If the liner was installed correctly and the liner protrusion is out of 
limits, it will be necessary to machine the counterbore and add shims to 
restore to the original specifications.

Use clean shop rags to cover the crankshaft to prevent debris from 
falling into the main journal area or into the connecting rod journal oil 
drilling.

 CAUTION: The liner puller must be installed and used as described to avoid 
damage to the cylinder block. The puller must not contact the block casting at 
points A, B, C and D. 

 NOTE: The liner puller must be centered on the top of the cylinder block.

Insert the liner puller into the top of the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A18234A.gif]

Turn the puller jackscrew clockwise to loosen the liner from the 
cylinder block. Use both hands to remove the liner.

[FIGURE: A18235A.gif]

 CAUTION: The liner puller must be installed and used as described to avoid 
damage to the cylinder block. The puller plate must be parallel to the main 
bearing saddles and must not overlap the liner outside diameter. 

 NOTE: The liner puller must be centered on the top of the cylinder block.

Insert the liner puller into the top of the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A18236A.gif]

Turn the puller jackscrew clockwise to loosen the liner from the 
cylinder block. Use both hands to remove the liner.

Use Dykem® or equivalent to mark the cylinder number 
on each liner.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Clean all deposits and debris from sealing surfaces A, B and C. Use 
Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent and cleaning solvent to 
polish the surfaces. Due to the critical machined tolerances, care should be 
taken not to remove any additional material. 

 NOTE: If surface C has cracks or signs of extreme wear, the counterbore will 
require machining and the installation of shims for the correct liner 
protrusion.

Cylinder liner shims are available as follows:

 CYLINDER LINER SHIM THICKNESS

[FIGURE: A18237A.gif]

Lubricate surfaces A and B with clean 15W40 engine oil.

 NOTE: Part No. 3823567, cutter plate, and Part No. 3823570, cutter bit, must 
be used with the counterbore machining tool.

Machine the counterbore to the proper depth.

[FIGURE: A18238A.gif]

Clean the combustion deck with a gasket scraper or Scotch-Brite®
 7448 cleaning pad or equivalent and diesel fuel or solvent.

Thoroughly flush the block with mineral spirits or cleaning solvent.

Remove the shop rags and clean the crankshaft with a cleaning solvent.

Blow dry the cylinder bores and crankshaft and wipe them clean with a 
lint-free cloth.

 NOTE: The cylinder liner must be installed within 15 minutes after applying 
oil to the cylinder liner O-ring seal.

Use clean 15W40 engine oil to coat the cylinder liner O-ring seals.

Install new O-ring seals on the cylinder liners.

Make sure the cylinder liner O-ring is not twisted or damaged during 
installation.

[FIGURE: A18239A.gif]

 NOTE: When reusing liners, install them in the same cylinder from which they 
were removed and rotate them 45 degrees (1/8 turn) from their original 
position. When correctly installed, any cylinder liner pitting will be 
positioned so the pitted surface is rotated away from the original location 
where pitting occurred.

Install the cylinder liner into the cylinder block bore.

 NOTE: If the cylinder liner does not rest on the cylinder block counterbore 
seat, remove the cylinder liner. Inspect the counterbore seat and cylinder 
liner for nicks, burrs or dirt. Install the cylinder liner again.

Use a cylinder liner driver and a leather mallet to drive the cylinder 
liner into the bore.

[FIGURE: A18240A.gif]

Use two cylinder head capscrews and position the two cylinder liner 
clamps as illustrated.

Tighten the capscrews to 68 Nm (50 lb-ft).

Remove the clamps and repeat this procedure until all cylinder liners 
have been clamped and released.

[FIGURE: A18241A.gif]

Cylinder liner protrusion is the distance the cylinder liner protrudes 
above the block face. Measure the cylinder liner protrusion at four points, 90 
degrees apart. Cylinder liner protrusion limits are 0.025-0.122 mm 
(0.001-0.0048 inch).

[FIGURE: A18242A.gif]

If the cylinder liner protrusion varies more than 0.025 mm (0.001 inch) 
for 180 degrees, install and tighten the cylinder liner clamps again. Inspect 
the cylinder liner protrusion again.

[FIGURE: A17874A.gif]

 NOTE: If the out-of-limit condition is minimal, tolerance stack-up may allow 
the cylinder liner protrusion limits to be obtained by installing other new 
cylinder liners in the out-of-limit bore.

If the cylinder liner protrusion still varies more than 0.025 mm (0.001 
inch), perform the following:

Remove the cylinder liner.

[FIGURE: A18244A.gif]

Inspect the cylinder liner sealing edge for burrs, dirt or damage.

Replace the cylinder liner if it is damaged.

Install the cylinder liner again.

Inspect the cylinder liner protrusion.

If the cylinder liner protrusion still does not meet the 
specifications, machine the cylinder block liner counterbore and add 
counterbore shims to adjust the cylinder liner protrusion to the proper 
specifications.

[FIGURE: A18238A.gif]

Use a feeler gauge to inspect the cylinder liner-to-block clearance at 
the four block casting points. Cylinder liner-to-block clearance limit is 
0.229 mm (0.009 inch).

[FIGURE: A18231A.gif]

If the cylinder liner-to-block clearance is less than 0.229 mm (0.009 
inch), perform the following:

Remove the cylinder liner.

Inspect the cylinder liner and cylinder block for dirt or damage.

Replace the cylinder liner if it is damaged.

Install the cylinder liner again.

Measure the cylinder liner bore for out-of-roundness at points C, D, E, 
F and G. Measure each point in the direction AA and BB. The cylinder liner 
bore must not be more than 0.04 mm (0.0016 inch) out of round.

If the cylinder liner bore is more than 0.04 mm (0.0016 inch) out of 
round, remove the cylinder liner so the cylinder block liner bore can be 
measured.

[FIGURE: A18229A.gif]

Install the pistons and connecting rods.

[FIGURE: A18245A.gif]

Install the oil pan and suction tube.

Install the cylinder head.

Fill the engine cooling system.

Fill the engine with oil.

Prelube (prime) the engine prior to start-up by disconnecting the fuel 
shutoff solenoid and cranking the engine until the oil pressure gauge reads 
pressure, or no more than 30 seconds. Allow the starter to cool for two 
minutes between crank times.

Bleed the engine cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Bleed the fuel supply lines and injector high pressure fuel lines. 
Refer to Section 03A-04A .

Operate the engine to normal operating temperature and check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Connecting Rod Bearings

 Removal 

Drain the engine oil. After the oil is drained, reinstall the drain 
plug with a new gasket. Tighten to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft).

Remove the oil pan and oil suction tube.

[FIGURE: A23471A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft to position two of the connecting rods at bottom 
dead center (BDC).

[FIGURE: A17336A.gif]

Loosen, but do not remove, the connecting rod capscrew nuts.

Hit the connecting rod capscrew nuts with a plastic hammer to loosen 
the rod caps.

Remove the capscrew nuts and rod cap.

Remove the lower bearing shell from the rod cap and mark it with the 
letter L (lower) and the cylinder number from which it was removed.

[FIGURE: A17337A.gif]

Push the rod away from the crankshaft to allow the upper bearing shell 
to be removed.

Remove the upper bearing shell and mark it with the letter U (upper) 
and the cylinder number from which it was removed.

[FIGURE: A17339A.gif]

Clean and inspect the bearings and caps. Refer to Cleaning and 
Inspection in this section.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: The connecting rod and bearing shell mating surfaces must be clean and 
dry when the bearing shells are installed. Used bearings must be installed in 
their original locations. 

Use Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A to lubricate the inside diameter of the upper 
bearing shell.

Install the upper bearing shell in the connecting rod with the tang of 
the bearing in the slot of the rod.

[FIGURE: A21469A.gif]

Install the bearing shell in the connecting rod cap with the tang of 
the bearing in the slot of the cap. Use Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A to coat the inside 
diameter of the bearing shell.

Use clean 15W40 oil to lubricate the threads and underside of the 
connecting rod capscrew head.

 CAUTION: The connecting rod cap number must match the number on the connecting 
rod and must be installed with the numbers aligned to prevent damage to the 
connecting rods and the crankshaft. The locking tang of the connecting rod cap 
must be toward the camshaft side of the cylinder block. 

Install the rod cap and capscrews to the connecting rod.

[FIGURE: A19035A.gif]

Alternately tighten the connecting rod capscrew nuts in a three-step 
sequence.

Step 1 — 40 Nm (30 lb-ft)

Step 2 — 80 Nm (59 lb-ft)

Step 3 — 120 Nm (88 lb-ft)

Measure the side clearance between the connecting rod and crankshaft. 
Do not measure the clearance between the rod cap and crankshaft. Side 
clearance limits are 0.10-0.33 mm (.0039-.013 inch).

 CAUTION: The crankshaft must rotate freely. 

Check for freedom of rotation as the rod caps are installed. If the 
crankshaft does not rotate freely, check the installation of the rod bearings 
and bearing size.

Install the oil suction tube and oil pan.

Fill the engine with oil.

Operate the engine until the coolant temperature reaches 82°
C (180°F) and check for leaks and proper 
operation.
