CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Block Sleeves

 CAUTION: Do not use any abrasives in the ring travel area of the liner. The 
liner can be damaged. 

Use a soft wire brush or a fine fibrous abrasive pad such as Scotch-Brite®
 7448 or equivalent to clean the flange seating area.

 WARNING: WHEN USING A STEAM CLEANER, WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES 
OR A FACE SHIELD. HOT STEAM CAN CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY. 

Use solvent or steam clean the liners and dry with compressed air.

 NOTE: Use lint-free paper towels to wipe the oil from the inside of the liners.

Use clean 15W40 oil to lubricate the inside diameter of the liners. 
Allow the oil to soak in the liner for 5 to 10 minutes.

Continue to lubricate the inside of the liners and wipe clean until the 
paper towel shows no gray or black residue.

Visually inspect the liners for cracks on the inside and outside 
diameters.

Inspect for cracks under the flange.

Visually inspect the outside diameter and seat area for excessive 
corrosion or pitting. Pits must not be more than 1.6 mm (0.06 inch) deep.

Replace the liner if the pits are too deep or if the corrosion cannot 
be removed with fine emery cloth.

Visually inspect the inside diameter for liner bore polishing.

A moderate polish produces a bright mirror finish in the worn area with 
traces of the original hone marks or an indication of an etch pattern.

A heavy polish produces a bright mirror finish in the worn area with no 
traces of hone marks or an etch pattern.

Replace the liner if the following condition(s) exist:

A heavy polish is present over 20 percent of the piston ring travel area.

Both moderate and heavy polish over 30 percent of the piston ring 
travel area and one half (15 percent) is heavy polish.

Measure the liner inside diameter in four places 90 degrees apart at 
the top and bottom of the piston travel area. Cylinder liner ID limits are 
114.000-114.117 mm (4.4882-4.4928 inches).

Measure the outside diameter of the liner top press fit area. Cylinder 
liner OD limits (top press fit) are 132.938-132.958 mm (5.2338-5.2346 inches).

Measure the cylinder liner bore in the block. Cylinder line bore limits 
are 132.900-132.990 mm (5.2323-5.2358 inches).

[FIGURE: A18338A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Head

 NOTE: Omit the first seven steps if a replacement head is to be installed.

Clean the carbon from the injector nozzle seat with an injector bore 
brush.

Scrape the gasket material from all gasket surfaces.

 CAUTION: When using a steam cleaner, wear protective clothing and safety glasses 
or a face shield. Hot steam can cause serious personal injury. 

Steam clean the cylinder head and dry with compressed air. Blow out all 
capscrew holes.

Clean the buildup of deposits from the coolant passages. Excessive 
deposits can be cleaned in an acid tank but the cup plugs must be removed first.

Use Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent and solvent to 
clean the cylinder head combustion face.

Clean the exhaust manifold gasket surface.

Clean the valve cover gasket surface.

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE EYE COVERING. 

 NOTE: An inferior quality wire wheel will lose steel bristles during 
operation, causing additional contamination.

Clean carbon deposits from the valve pockets with a high quality steel 
wire wheel installed in a drill or a die grinder.

Wash the cylinder head in hot soapy water solution. After rinsing, use 
compressed air to dry the cylinder head.

Visually inspect the cylinder head and valves for obvious damage that 
would prohibit reuse. Check for cracks and damage to the deck surface that 
would result in loss of sealing.

Check for cracks on the combustion face. Cracks that extend from the 
injector bore away from the valve seats and are not over 10 mm (0.394 inch) 
long are acceptable.

[FIGURE: A18323A.gif]

Any cracks that extend from the injector bore toward the valve seats 
are unacceptable and the cylinder head must be replaced.

Cracks between the valve seats are not acceptable and the cylinder head 
must be replaced.

Use a straightedge and feeler gauge to check the cylinder head 
combustion surface for flatness.

 CYLINDER HEAD FLATNESS SPECIFICATIONS

Measurement

mm

Inch

End to End

0.20

0.0079

Side to Side

0.076

0.003

 NOTE: A maximum of 1.00 mm (0.040 inch) can be machined from the combustion 
surface of the cylinder head.

Use a small 51-mm (2-inch) straightedge and a 0.0254-mm (0.001-inch) 
feeler gauge to measure local flatness. Check between the cylinder bores and 
also between the coolant passages. If the 0.001-inch feeler gauge fits under 
the 2-inch straightedge, the cylinder head must be replaced or resurfaced.

[FIGURE: A18324A.gif]

If the cylinder head is machined, place the valve in the respective 
bore and check the valve depth dimension. If the depth is less than the 
minimum specification, the valve seat will require machining. Valve recess in 
cylinder head is 1.09-1.62 mm (0.043-0.064 inch) for the exhaust valve and 
0.69-1.09 mm (0.027-0.043 inch) for the intake valve.

Visually inspect the valves for indications of leakage or burning.

[FIGURE: A18325A.gif]

Exhaust Manifold 

 Cleaning

must be replaced.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Flywheel

 Transmission, Automatic 

Inspect the flywheel for cracks or other damage that would make it 
unfit for further service. Inspect the flywheel ring gear for worn, chipped or 
cracked teeth. If the teeth are damaged, replace the ring gear and flywheel 
assembly. 

With the flywheel installed on the crankshaft, check the gear face 
runout. 

 Transmission, Manual 

Inspect the flywheel for cracks, heat check or other damage that would 
make it unfit for further service. Machine the friction surface of the 
flywheel if it is scored or worn. If it is necessary to remove more than 1.0 
mm (0.040 inch) of stock from the original thickness, replace the flywheel. 

Inspect the ring gear for worn, chipped or cracked teeth. If the teeth 
are damaged, replace the ring gear. 

With the flywheel installed on the crankshaft, check the flywheel 
housing runout. Refer to Section 03-00 .

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Oil Pan 

 Cleaning 

Scrape any dirt or metal particles from the inside of the pan. Scrape 
all old gasket material from the gasket surface. Wash the pan in a solvent and 
dry it thoroughly. Make sure all foreign particles are removed.

 Inspection 

Check the pan for cracks, holes or damaged drain plug threads. Check 
the gasket surface for damage caused by overtightened bolts. Replace with a 
new oil pan if repairs cannot be made.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Oil Pump 

 Cleaning 

Wash all parts in a solvent and dry thoroughly with compressed air. Use 
a brush to clean the inside of the pump housing and the pressure relief valve 
chamber. Make sure all dirt and metal particles are removed. 

 Inspection 

 NOTE: Internal components are not serviced. If any component is out of 
specification, the pump assembly must be replaced. 

Check the inside of the pump housing and the inner and outer gears for 
damage or excessive wear. 

Check the mating surface of the pump cover for wear. Minor scuff marks 
are normal, but if the cover, gears or housing surfaces are excessively worn, 
scored or grooved, replace the pump. Inspect the rotor for nicks, burrs or 
score marks. Remove minor imperfections with an oil stone. 

Measure the inner to outer rotor tip clearance with feeler gauge 
inserted 13 mm (0.5 inch) minimum. Inner and outer rotor tip clearance must 
not exceed 0.1778 mm (0.007 inch).

[FIGURE: A23430A.gif]

With the rotor assembly installed in the housing, place Straight Edge 
D83L-4201-A or equivalent over the rotor assembly and the housing. 

Measure the vertical clearance (rotor end play) between the 
straightedge and both the inner rotor and the outer race. Maximum clearance 
must not exceed 0.127 mm (0.005 inch).

[FIGURE: A23431A.gif]

Measure clearance between outer rotor and housing in several areas 
around the circumference of the outer rotor. Clearance must not exceed 0.381 
mm (0.015 inch).

[FIGURE: A23432A.gif]

Measure oil pump drive gear backlash. Backlash must not exceed 0.33 mm 
(0.013 inch).

[FIGURE: A23433A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Rocker Arms

 Cleaning 

Clean all parts in a strong solution of laundry detergent and hot water.

 NOTE: The rocker arm shaft supports are made from powdered metal and will 
continue to show wetness after they have been cleaned and dried.

Use compressed air to dry the parts after rinsing in clean hot water.

 Inspection 

Inspect for cracks and excessive wear in the bore and the contact 
surface for the valve stem.

 NOTE: The rocker arms do not use a bushing in the bore for the rocker arm 
shaft. The rocker arm must be replaced if the bore is damaged or worn beyond 
the specification.

Measure the rocker arm bore. Rocker arm bore maximum diameter limit is 
22.301 mm (0.878 inch).

[FIGURE: A17509A.gif]

Visually inspect the rocker arm shafts for pitting, scoring or other 
damage.

Measure the rocker arm shaft diameter. Rocker arm shaft diameter must 
be within 22.199-22.231 mm (0.874-0.8752 inch).

[FIGURE: A18322A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Valve Tappets

 CAUTION: Any time a new camshaft is installed, new tappets must also be installed. 

Clean the valve tappets with solvent and dry with compressed air.

Inspect the socket, stem and face for excessive wear, cracks, concavity 
and other damage. Maximum allowable tappet face concavity for reuse is 0.025 
mm (0.001 inch).

[FIGURE: A17570C.gif]

Measure the valve tappet stem. Tappet stem diameter limits are 
15.925-15.98 mm (0.627-0.6291 inch).

Pit marks on the tappet face are acceptable.

The following criteria define the size of the pits allowed.

A single pit cannot be greater than 2 mm (0.078 inch).

Interconnection of pits is not allowed.

Total pits when added together must not exceed 6 mm (0.236 inch) 
diameter or a total of four percent of the tappet face.

No pitting is allowable on the edges of the wear face of the tappet.

[FIGURE: A17571A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Push Rods

Clean the push rods in hot soapy water.

Inspect the push rod ball and socket for signs of scoring. Check for 
cracks where the ball and the socket are pressed into the tube.

Check the push rods for roundness and straightness.

[FIGURE: A17511B.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Valves

 Cleaning 

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE EYE COVERING. 

Clean the valve heads with a soft wire wheel. Keep the valves in a 
labeled rack to prevent mixing prior to making measurements.

Polish the valve stem with a Scotch-Brite® pad or 
equivalent cleaning pad and diesel fuel or solvent.

 Inspection 

Inspect for abnormal wear on the heads and stems.

Visually inspect the valves for damage. Replace the valves if any of 
the following conditions are found:

valve stems worn below specifications

rust or pitting on the valve stem or sealing surface

worn collet grooves

[FIGURE: A18326A.gif]

worn stem tip

bent valve stems

damaged valve heads (burned, cracked or broken)

[FIGURE: A18327A.gif]

Measure the outside diameter of the valve stem. Valve stem OD limits 
are 9.46-9.50 mm (0.372-0.374 inch).

It may be possible to grind and reuse valves with the following 
conditions:

minor grooves on the valve sealing surface

fine pitting on the valve sealing surface

carbon or varnish buildup on the valve stem

[FIGURE: A18328A.gif]

Check the valve stem tip for flatness.

Visually inspect for bent valves.

Measure the rim thickness to determine if there is enough stock to 
grind the valve. The minimum limit is 1.50 mm (0.059 inch).

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Head Deck

 Cleaning 

 NOTE: Excessive deposits may be cleaned in an acid tank, but the camshaft 
bushings must first be removed to prevent damage.

Place clean lint-free rags over the pistons to prevent dirt from 
falling into the engine.

Plug or cover the coolant and oil passages in the cylinder block deck.

Use a gasket scraper to clean the cylinder block deck surface.

Use Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent and solvent to 
remove any residual gasket material from the cylinder block deck surface.

 WARNING: WHEN USING COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN CAPSCREW HOLES, ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY 
GLASSES OR A FACE SHIELD TO PROTECT THE EYES. PERSONAL INJURY CAN RESULT. 

 NOTE: Make sure the cylinder head capscrew holes are clean.

Use compressed air to clean debris from the capscrew holes.

Inspect the coolant passages. Buildup of deposits in the coolant 
passages can cause engine overheating. A large buildup of rust and lime will 
require removal of the cylinder block for cleaning in a hot tank.

Be sure the coolant passages are clean.

[FIGURE: A18331A.gif]

 Inspection 

 CAUTION: Do not proceed with the repair if the cylinder block head deck is 
damaged or not flat. The engine will have to be removed for resurfacing the 
block. 

 NOTE: The cylinder block head deck can be resurfaced in a machine shop and a 
thicker surface head gasket installed to keep the piston-to-head clearance the 
same.

Use a straightedge and feeler gauge to measure the overall flatness of 
the cylinder head deck. The overall flatness, side to side, must not exceed 
0.075 mm (0.003 inch). The overall flatness, end-to-end, must not exceed 0.200 
mm (0.008 inch).

Use a small 51-mm (2-inch) straightedge and a 0.0254-mm (0.001-inch) 
feeler gauge to measure local flatness. Check between the cylinder bores and 
also between the coolant passages. If the 0.001-inch feeler gauge fits under 
the 2-inch straightedge, the cylinder head must be replaced or resurfaced.

Visually inspect for any localized dips or imperfections. If present, 
the cylinder head deck must be reground.

The cylinder block head deck can be resurfaced two times. The first 
resurface should be 0.25 mm (0.010 inch). If additional resurfacing is 
required, an additional 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) can be removed.

[FIGURE: A18332A.gif]

Use the gasket where block deck has been resurfaced 0.50 mm (0.020

[FIGURE: A18333B.gif]

 NOTE: The liners must be checked in the "free state," without clamps.

Check the liner protrusion. Liner protrusion is the distance the liner 
protrudes above the block face. Cylinder liner protrusion limits are 
0.025-0.122 mm (0.0010-0.0048 inch). If the cylinder liner protrusion is below 
specifications, it will be necessary to machine the counterbores.

Visually inspect the cylinder liners for cracks, scuffing or scoring.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Valve Seat

 Inspection 

Inspect the valve seat inserts for cracks or burned spots. Refer to the 
following reuse guidelines for any cracks discovered. Service valve seats are 
available for seats with burned spots that will require more than 0.254 mm 
(0.010 inch) grinding to clean up.

 NOTE: The sealing surface of the valve must seat in the center of the valve 
seat insert.

Measure the width of the valve seat area of the valve seat inserts. 
Valve seat area width limits are 1.5-2.0 mm (0.059-0.079 inch).

If the valve seat area is worn wider than the maximum specified, 
replace the valve seat insert.

[FIGURE: A18334A.gif]

Install the valves in their respective bores and measure the recess in 
the cylinder head.

Make sure the seats are clean before measuring the recess. Valve recess 
in cylinder head limits is 1.09-1.62 mm (0.043-0.064 inch) for the exhaust 
valve and 0.69-1.09 mm (0.027-0.043 inch) for the intake valve. If the valve 
recess is out of limits, before replacing the valve seat, try replacing the 
old valve with a new valve. If the recess is within limits with the new valve, 
grind the old valve seat and use the new valve.

[FIGURE: A18335A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Head Cracks, Reuse Guidelines

These guidelines apply only to cracks extending from the injector bore 
to the intake valve seats. Replace cylinder heads that exhibit valve bridge 
cracks in any other location.

The reuse guidelines for a cylinder head with a crack extending from 
the injector bore to the intake seat are as follows:

If the crack does not extend into the valve seat, the head is reusable.

If the crack extends into or through the valve seat, the head must be 
repaired by installing a valve seat insert.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Valve Spring

 Inspection 

Inspect the valve springs for obvious damage (breaks, etc.).

Measure the valve spring. Valve spring free height is 65.66 mm (2.585 
inches).

[FIGURE: A18336A.gif]

Use a valve spring tester to measure the valve spring load at the 
opening height. Valve spring opening height is 37.90 mm (1.492 inch). Valve 
spring load for opening height is 960-1060 N (216-238 lbf) for new valve 
springs. Valve spring load for used valve springs is 940 N (213 lbf).

If the valve spring load for the opening height is less than the 
minimum specified, the valve spring must be replaced.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Water Thermostat

 NOTE: If the problem being investigated is insufficient heat, the thermostat 
should be checked for leakage. This can be done by holding the thermostat up 
to a lighted background. Light leakage around the thermostat valve (thermostat 
at room temperature) is unacceptable and the thermostat must be replaced. On 
some thermostats, a slight leakage of light at one or two locations on the 
perimeter of the valve may be detected. This should be considered normal.

Remove the thermostat and immerse it in boiling water. Replace the 
thermostat if it does not open more than 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) after one minute 
in water.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cooling System

 Rust or Dirt Contamination 

If the cooling system is contaminated by residual solids such as rust 
or dirt, the system must be cleaned by using Ford Premium Cooling System Flush 
F1AZ-19A503-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P7-A. Heavy rust 
or scale may require additional radiator cleaning service.

 Oil Contamination 

If the cooling system is contaminated by oil, perform the following 
steps:

Determine the source or cause of the contamination and eliminate it.

Drain the cooling system and fill with clean water containing two 
ounces per gallon of nonfoaming automatic dishwasher detergent.

Run the engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm.

Drain the cooling system. Allow engine to cool.

Refill with Ford Heavy Duty Diesel Engine Cooling System Fluid 
E6HZ-19549-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESE-M97B18-C and Heavy 
Duty Cooling System Additive FW-15 or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESN-M99B169-F.

================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Lubrication System 

 NOTE: Observe condition of coolant. If there is evidence of oil contamination 
in coolant, the cooling system must be cleaned.

If the engine oil has been contaminated by coolant, the engine 
lubrication system must be cleaned. 

Determine the level/severity of contamination and proceed with the 
appropriate cleaning procedure. 

 Contamination Slight to Moderate with No Sludging 

Defined as showing evidence of coolant in oil. Sludging is defined as 
evidence of gelled, slimy deposits attached to engine parts. 

 Cleaning 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Remove 
crankcase breather element.

 WARNING: READ AND FOLLOW ALL STATEMENTS ON CLEANING SOLVENT CONTAINER TO ENSURE 
SAFE OPERATION. 

Mix 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) of kerosene with 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) 
of recommended engine oil and refill crankcase. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. 

Repeat Steps 3, 4, 5, 6 and go to Step 8. 

Fill crankcase with recommended engine oil. 

Replace crankcase breather element. 

 Contamination Heavy with Sludging 

Defined as showing heavy concentration of coolant in oil with sludging. 
Sludging is defined as evidence of gelled, slimy deposits on parts under 
rocker cover and bottom end (oil pan area). 

 Cleaning 

Determine the source or cause of the contamination and eliminate it. 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

If sludge is heavy and built up, remove as much sludge deposit as 
possible from exposed engine parts, i.e., under rocker cover and lower end 
(oil pan removed) before proceeding further. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Remove 
crankcase breather element.

 WARNING: READ AND FOLLOW ALL STATEMENTS ON CLEANING SOLVENT CONTAINER TO ENSURE 
SAFE OPERATION. 

Mix 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) of commercially available cleaning solvent 
such as Butyl Cellosolve (Union Carbide) or Downol E-B (Dow Chemical) or 
Glycol Ether E-13 (Chem Central) or equivalent with 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) 
recommended engine oil and refill crankcase. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter.

 WARNING: READ AND FOLLOW ALL STATEMENTS ON CLEANING SOLVENT CONTAINER TO ENSURE 
SAFE OPERATION. 

Mix 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) of commercially available cleaning solvent 
such as Butyl Cellosolve (Union Carbide) or Downol E-B (Dow Chemical) or 
Glycol Ether E-13 (Chem Central) or equivalent with 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) 
recommended engine oil and refill crankcase. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Fill the 
crankcase with the recommended engine oil. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove oil pan and inspect main and rod bearings for signs of distress. 
Replace bearings if necessary and replace oil pan. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Fill the 
crankcase with the recommended engine oil. Install new crankcase breather 
element.

ADJUSTMENTS

Valve Adjustment, Cold

 CAUTION: Adjust the valves when the engine is cold — below 60°
C (140°F). 

 NOTE: Valve lash must be checked and adjusted at the first 32,000 km (20,000 
miles) and thereafter at 64,000 km (40,000-mile) intervals.

Use the timing pin to locate top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1, 
and then remove the valve covers.

[FIGURE: A18191A.gif]

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the timing pin, make sure to disengage the pin 
after locating top dead center (TDC). 

When the pin engages the hole in the camshaft gear, cylinder No. 1 is 
at TDC on the compression stroke.

[FIGURE: A18192B.gif]

 NOTE: The clearance is correct when slight resistance is felt as the feeler 
gauge is moved between the valve stem and rocker lever.

Adjust the valves with engine cold (below 60°C [
140°F]).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cooling System

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE THE RADIATOR CAP UNDER ANY CONDITIONS WHILE THE ENGINE IS 
OPERATING. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS CAN RESULT IN PERSONAL INJURY 
AND DAMAGE TO THE COOLING SYSTEM AND ENGINE.

TO AVOID HAVING SCALDING HOT COOLANT OR STEAM BLOW OUT OF THE RADIATOR, 
USE EXTREME CARE WHEN REMOVING THE CAP FROM A HOT RADIATOR. IF POSSIBLE, WAIT 
UNTIL THE ENGINE HAS COOLED, THEN WRAP A THICK CLOTH AROUND THE RADIATOR CAP 
AND TURN IT SLOWLY TO THE FIRST STOP. STEP BACK WHILE THE PRESSURE IS RELEASED 
FROM THE COOLING SYSTEM. WHEN YOU ARE SURE ALL THE PRESSURE HAS BEEN RELEASED, 
PRESS DOWN ON THE CAP (STILL USING A CLOTH), TURN AND REMOVE IT. 

Refer to Section 03-03 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Thermostat, Water 

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to service the thermostat. It should be replaced if it 
is not operating properly. 

The poppet-type thermostat used in production is a high-temperature 
thermostat for use with a mixture of water and permanent-type antifreeze. 
Install a low-temperature thermostat if a non-permanent antifreeze and water 
coolant solution is used (except on vehicles with automatic radiator 
shutters). 

When changing the thermostat to a higher or lower temperature range on 
vehicles equipped with automatic shutters, always change the shutterstat to a 
corresponding higher or lower range. 

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery ground cables.

Drain the engine coolant. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Remove the accessory drive belt. Refer to Section 03B-05 .

Disconnect the upper radiator hose from the water outlet connection.

Disconnect the air duct assembly at the turbocharger inlet.

Loosen bolts retaining generator to mounting brackets.

Remove bolts securing generator upper mounting bracket and reposition 
generator assembly.

Remove water outlet connection retaining bolts.

Remove the water outlet connection and tube from the cylinder head.

Remove the thermostats.

 CAUTION: Do not let any debris fall into the thermostat cavity when cleaning 
gasket surfaces. 

Remove the gasket and any residue from the water outlet connection and 
cylinder head sealing surfaces.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Check the thermostat before installing it. Refer to Section 03-03 . 

 CAUTION: Always install two thermostats. Failure to install two thermostats can 
cause overheating and serious damage to the engine. 

Install two thermostats. 

Position a new gasket over the thermostats.

Position the water outlet connection over the thermostats and gasket, 
making sure the gasket is aligned with the bolt holes.

Install the water outlet connection retaining bolts and hand-tighten.

 CAUTION: Do not allow any debris to fall into the water outlet connection when 
cleaning surfaces. 

Inspect the water outlet connection tube sealing surfaces. Clean any 
debris or old sealing material if necessary. Replace seal if necessary.

Install the water outlet connection tube onto the water outlet 
connection and install remaining bolts. Tighten all bolts to 21-27 Nm
 (15-20 lb-ft).

Position the generator upper mounting bracket to the water outlet 
connection and install the retaining bolts.

Tighten the bolts retaining the generator to both mounting brackets.

Install the accessory drive belt. Refer to Section 03B-05 .

Connect the upper radiator hose to the water outlet connection and 
tighten the clamp to 14-17 Nm (11-13 lb-ft).

Connect the air duct assembly to the turbocharger inlet.

Fill and bleed cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Connect the battery ground cables.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator Hoses 

Replace the cooling system hoses whenever they become cracked or 
deteriorated, or have a tendency to collapse. 

 Removal 

Partially drain the cooling system to replace cooling system upper 
hose(s). Drain the cooling system to replace the radiator outlet hose. 

Loosen the clamps on each end of the hose(s) to be removed. Slide the 
hose(s) off the connections. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: If the connections have a single bead around the edges, make sure the 
clamps are located beyond the beads. If the connections have a double bead, 
make sure the clamp is located between the beads after assembly.

Position the clamps on each end of the new hose. Slide the hose onto 
the connections, then tighten the clamps.

Fill the cooling system with coolant and bleed the system. Refer to 
 Section 03-03 . 

Operate the engine for several minutes, then check the hose(s) and 
connections for leaks.

Water Pump

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator

 Removal 

Install hose on drain nipple and drain radiator coolant into a suitable 
container. 

Disconnect the spring-loaded hood support cables. 

 WARNING: USE EXTREME CARE AND OBSERVE ALL SAFETY AND SERVICE PRECAUTIONS RELATED 
TO THE USE OF REFRIGERANTS. REFER TO SECTION 12-00. 

Recover refrigerant from the air conditioning system in accordance with 
safety and EPA regulations (if necessary). Refer to Section 12-00 .

Remove transmission oil cooler (if so equipped) and set aside. Do not 
disconnect or drain oil cooler. 

Disconnect lower radiator hose. 

Remove the turbocharger-to-charge air cooler inlet pipe. 

Disconnect the radiator-to-radiator coolant recovery reservoir vent 
hose. 

Disconnect the radiator upper hose. 

Remove the charge air cooler-to-intake manifold tube. 

Disconnect the air conditioning compressor-to-condenser core hose (if 
necessary). 

Disconnect the air conditioning condenser core-to-orifice tube hose (if 
necessary). 

Remove seven plastic ties. 

Remove the hose and electrical support bracket. 

Remove the two large (1/2-inch) lower mount retaining nuts and washers. 

Remove the two radiator support-to-dash brace rod nuts, and position 
radiator support-to-dash brace out of the way. 

Attach lifting eyes and chain to two threaded studs in top of radiator 
assembly, and attach lifting equipment. 

Remove the air conditioning condenser core retaining bolts (if so 
equipped). 

Using lifting equipment and, with the aid of an assistant, remove 
radiator assembly from the vehicle. 

Remove the screws and washers and remove shroud. 

Lower radiator to floor and remove lifting equipment and eye bolts. 

Disassemble the module by removing the four bolts (manual) or two 
bolts/two nuts (automatic), spring packs, steel plates and Teflon®
 pads that hold the charge air cooler (CAC) to the radiator 
support frame.

Remove the charge air cooler.

Remove the nuts holding the gusset to vertical support at each corner.

Remove the drain cock and de-aeration fitting as required.

Remove the steel support members by lightly tapping in a horizontal 
direction on the two vertical support members.

Service heat exchangers as required. Refer to Section 03-03 .

 Installation 

 NOTE: During the assembly process, use Ford Threadlock® 262 
E2FZ-19554-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 on all 
fasteners.

Install four corner rubber shock mounts on radiator.

Install radiator core to the lower frame.

Install upper radiator frame.

 NOTE: Do not tighten strut nuts.

Install vertical strut rods and two Nyloc nuts.

Install two radiator side frames by lightly tapping in a horizontal 
direction on the two vertical support members. Loosely install the fifteen 
nuts for the side frames and upper and lower frames. Using a 6.4-mm 
(0.25-inch) drift and the eight assembly aid holes, align side frames until 
nuts are aligned with marks left in frame member paint. Tighten the fifteen 
nuts to 34 Nm (25 lb-ft). This will compress and secure the 
four corner shock mounts.

If removed, install the drain cock and deaeration fitting.

Tighten the vertical strut support nuts.

Install the charge air cooler.

 NOTE: Use Ford Threadlock® 262 E2FZ-19554-B or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 on all fasteners.

Assemble the module by installing the four bolts (manual) or two 
bolts/two nuts (automatic), spring packs, steel plates and Teflon®
 pads that hold the charge air cooler to the radiator 
support frame. Tighten 3/8-inch shoulder bolts to 34 Nm (25 
lb-ft). Tighten 3/8-inch nuts to 34 Nm (25 lb-ft).

Position shroud and install retaining screws and washers.

Use suitable lifting equipment and with the aid of an assistant, lift 
radiator into position and install two (1/2-inch) lower mount retaining bolts 
and washers. After cleaning threads, apply Threadlock® 262 
E2FZ-19554-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6. Tighten 
to 75-102 Nm (55-75 lb-ft). 

Position condenser on radiator and install retaining bolts.

Remove lifting equipment and lifting eyes. 

Install the charge air cooler-to-intake manifold tube. 

Install the turbocharger-to-charge air cooler inlet pipe. 

Connect radiator support-to-dash brace to radiator.

Connect the air conditioning condenser core-to-orifice tube (if 
necessary).

Connect the air conditioning compressor-to-condenser core hose (if 
necessary). 

Install the hose and electrical support bracket.

Connect the upper and lower radiator hoses. 

Connect vent hose to coolant recovery reservoir. 

Install the transmission oil cooler. 

Install the seven plastic ties for overflow hose and other hoses. 

With the aid of an assistant, connect the spring-loaded hood support 
cables. 

Fill and purge coolant system. Refer to Section 03-03 . 

Evacuate and recharge air conditioning system. Refer to Section 12-00 . 

Check system for proper operation.

Radiator Coolant Recovery Reservoir 

 WARNING: DO NOT STAND IN LINE WITH OR NEAR RADIATOR COOLING FAN WHEN REVVING

Section 03B-05: Drive Belts, Accessory, FD-1460 Diesel Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Drive Belts, Accessory 

L-Series vehicles are equipped with two types of accessory drive belts. 
The drive belt type is selected for each engine based on performance 
requirements. To ensure maximum life, replacement belts must be of the same 
type as originally installed. These belts must be properly adjusted at all 
times. Loose belt(s) will result in slippage, which can cause a noise 
complaint or improper accessory operation (generator will not charge, etc.). 
Overly tight belts will place severe loads on accessory bearings. 

The poly-V (serpentine) drive belt tension is maintained by an 
automatic belt tensioner. Regular inspection is required to check belt 
condition to ensure that excessive belt stretch does not occur. The vee drive 
belt is not automatically tensioned and requires periodic inspection for 
proper belt tension.

[FIGURE: Q1690E.gif]

Fan and Clutch, Engine Operated

Section 03B-05: Drive Belts, Accessory, FD-1460 Diesel Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Drive Belts, Accessory

 Inspection and Verification 

 Drive Belt Cracking/Chunking/Wear 

Under severe operating conditions (high temperatures, low humidity), 
drive belt rib cracking can occur at less than 96,000 km (60,000 miles). Drive 
belt rib cracking perpendicular to the belt ribs is not a reason for concern 
and has no detrimental effect on belt performance. Cracks parallel to ribs are 
not acceptable.

Drive belt "chunking" is the condition in which the rubber material 
actually chunks out between the cracks. The drive belt should be replaced if 
chunks are missing on two adjacent ribs, or a chunked-out section is 13 mm 
(0.5 inch) or longer.

[FIGURE: Q4077C.gif]

 Drive Belt Noise 

Drive belt chirp is a regularly occurring chirping noise that occurs 
due to pulley misalignment or excessive pulley runout. It can be a result of a 
damaged pulley or an improperly replaced pulley that was not properly aligned.

To correct, determine the area the noise comes from. Then check each of 
the pulleys in that area with a straightedge to the crankshaft pulley and look 
for the accessory pulleys to be out of position in the fore/aft direction or 
at an angle to the straightedge.

Belt squeal is an intermittent noise that occurs when the drive belt 
slips on a pulley during certain conditions, such as engine start-up, rapid 
engine acceleration or A/C clutch engagement.

Drive belt squeal can occur under the following conditions:

A/C discharge pressure goes above 2895 kPa (420 psi). This can occur if:

the A/C system is overcharged

the A/C condenser core airflow is blocked

the engine fan blade is not engaging fully at idle

A/C OFF equalized pressure (the common discharge and suction pressure 
that occurs after several minutes) exceeds 965 kPa (140 psi), which is a rare 
occurrence at high ambient temperatures with a hot engine. Turn A/C off for a 
few seconds and then back on after fan blade begins to cool A/C condenser core.

Any of the accessories are damaged, or have a worn or damaged bearing 
or internal torsional resistance above normal for any reason. All of the 
accessories should be able to be rotated by hand in the unloaded condition. If 
any are not, the accessory should be inspected.

Fluid gets on the drive belt. These would include power steering fluid, 
engine coolant, engine oil or air conditioning system lubricant.

If fluid does get on the drive belt during service, the best policy is 
to clean the drive belt with soap and water and thoroughly rinse with clean 
water. The drive belt does not have to be replaced if no apparent damage has 
occurred.

Drive belt is too long. A drive belt that is too long will allow the 
drive belt tensioner arm to go all the way to drive belt tensioner arm travel 
stop under certain load conditions, which will untension the drive belt. If 
the drive belt tensioner is resting on the stop, replace the drive belt.

If the drive belt tensioner is worn or damaged. The drive belt 
tensioner arm should rotate freely without binding.

 Symptom Chart — Accessory Drive Belt Diagnosis 

 ACCESSORY DRIVE BELT DIAGNOSIS 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Excessive Noise/Belt Squeal

Seized accessory.

CHECK all accessories for free rotation and REPLACE accessory if 
necessary. REPLACE drive belt.

Loose drive belt.

CHECK condition and tension of all drive belts. REPLACE drive belts or 
ADJUST tension of manually tensioned drive belt as necessary.

CHECK that automatic drive belt tensioner is within the indicator 
marks. CHECK for correct drive belt length if drive belt tensioner is out of 
operating range.

Rattle

Loose pulley or accessory.

CHECK for looseness and TIGHTEN.

Noisy Tensioner Pulley Bearing

Worn bearing.

REPLACE pulley per automatic belt tensioner pulley replacement procedure.

Belt Chirp

Misaligned power steering pump pulley.

ALIGN power steering pulley. REFER to Drive Belt Tensioner, 
Automatic , in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Severe Belt Flutter

Loose drive belt.

CHECK belt tension and ADJUST (manually tensioned belts only) if 
necessary. CHECK condition of drive belt and REPLACE if necessary.

Binding tensioner arm.

REMOVE drive belt from drive belt tensioner and VERIFY that tensioner 
arm is not frozen in position or that arm does not bind when manually moved 
throughout its operating range.

Frayed Drive Belt

Drive belt not seated correctly (poly-V belt).

REPLACE drive belt and VERIFY correct belt seating.

Severely misaligned pulley.

USE a straightedge to CHECK for severe angular misalignment between 
adjacent pulleys. CORRECT as necessary.

Drive belt too tight.

REPLACE drive belt.

Drive belt worn out.

REPLACE drive belt.

Severely Glazed Drive Belt

Seized accessory.

CHECK all accessories for free rotation and REPLACE if necessary. 
REPLACE drive belt.

Loose drive belt.

REPLACE drive belt.

Improper Accessory Operation (Power Steering or Air Conditioning 
Doesn't Work, Engine Overheats or Battery Doesn't Charge)

Loose drive belt.

CHECK drive belt for looseness or glazing and REPLACE or ADJUST tension 
of manually tensioned belts if necessary.

Drive Belt Jumps off Pulley

Greatly misaligned pulleys.

CHECK for misalignment between adjacent pulleys.

Drive belt not seated correctly (poly-V belt).

REPLACE drive belt and VERIFY correct seating.

Pulley wobble.

VERIFY that no pulley wobbles during engine operation. Conditions 
causing wobble are: bent pulley, bent accessory shaft, rear face of pulley not 
seated flat against mating surface.

Excessive crankshaft end play.

REBUILD engine.

Excessive Wear on Drive Belt Tensioner

Extended off-road operation.

REPLACE drive belt tensioner per automatic belt tensioner pulley 
replacement procedure.

Sticking or seizing pulley bearing on tensioner.

REPLACE drive belt tensioner per replacement procedure.

Wrong belt installed (too short).

VERIFY and REPLACE belt and tensioner per procedure.

 Component Tests 

 Drive Belt Tension 

Check drive belt tension. Refer to Drive Belt Tension 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section. If tension is not within specification, 
check drive belt tensioner. Service components as required.

 Drive Belt Tensioner, Automatic 

The drive belt tensioner will maintain correct belt tension if the 
correct length drive belt is on the engine. The drive belt tensioner can be 
checked as follows:

With the engine running, observe drive belt tensioner movement. The 
drive belt tensioner should move (respond) when the A/C compressor cycles or 
when the engine is accelerated rapidly. If the drive belt tensioner movement 
is constant and excessive, a pulley or shaft is probably bent or a pulley is 
out of round. In rare cases, excessive belt rideout (uneven depth of grooves 
in belt) can cause excessive drive belt tensioner movement. This condition can 
be checked by replacing the suspect drive belt with a known good original 
equipment drive belt and repeating the observation.

With the engine off, check for proper drive belt routing. Refer to the 
illustrations under Removal and Installation . Service as required.

Visually inspect the condition of the drive belt. Replace the drive 
belt as required.

Rotate the drive belt tensioner and check for a binding or frozen 
condition. Replace components as required.

 Drive Belt Misalignment 

 CAUTION: Incorrect drive belt installation will cause excessive drive belt wear 
and can cause the drive belt to come off the drive pulleys. 

 NOTE: Original equipment drive belts are made of a special cord construction 
and are subjected to special testing before approval for use.

 NOTE: Replacement drive belts, other than O.E.M., can track 
differently/improperly. If a replacement drive belt tracks improperly, the 
drive belt must be replaced with an O.E.M. drive belt to avoid performance 
failure or loss of drive belt during cold operation.

With the engine running, check drive belt tracking (the position of the 
drive belt on the drive belt tensioner). If the edge of the drive belt rides 
beyond the edge of the drive bent tensioner, this can cause noise and 
premature wear.

If a drive belt tracking condition exists, visually check the drive 
belt tensioner for damage, especially the mounting pad surface. If the drive 
belt tensioner is not installed correctly with the locating pins in the 
locating holes, the mounting surface pad will be out of position. This will 
result in drive belt tension and chirp and squeal noises.

If the above procedures do not correct the drive belt noise, try 
replacing the drive belt with a known good original equipment drive belt. 
However, the drive belt noise may return again (with mileage) if one of the 
above conditions still exists uncorrected.

With engine running, visually observe the grooves in the pulleys (not 
the pulley flanges) for excessive wobble. Replace components as required.

Check all accessories, mounting brackets and drive belt tensioner for 
any interference that would prevent the component from mounting properly. 
Correct any interference condition and recheck belt tracking.

Tighten all accessories mounting brackets and drive belt tensioner 
retaining hardware to specification. Recheck drive belt tracking.

Check drive belt tension. Refer to Drive Belt Tension 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Belt Replacement 

Conditions requiring drive belt replacement are rib chunk out, 
excessive wear, severe glazing and frayed cords. Replace any drive belt 
exhibiting any of these conditions. Minor cracks in the ribbed side of 
V-grooved portion of the drive belt are considered acceptable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Belt Tensioner, Automatic

 Removal

With tension released, remove drive belt from tensioner pulley.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Starter Motor

 Removal 

Open battery box and disconnect battery ground cable. 

Remove starter motor upper mounting bolt. 

Disconnect starter motor and starter solenoid wires. Tag wires to 
facilitate connection at proper terminals during starter motor installation. 

Remove two remaining starter motor mounting bolts. Remove starter motor. 

 Installation 

Position starter motor on engine. Install three bolts. Tighten to 
150-200 Nm (110-148 lb-ft). 

Connect starter solenoid wire to starter terminal. 

Connect remaining starter motor wires to starter terminals. 

Connect battery ground cable and close battery box. Check starter motor 
operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Glow Plug, Air Intake Heater

 Removal 

 CAUTION: The glow plug heater can be damaged by excessive torque at the 
electrical connector terminal. Do not exceed 4 Nm (36 lb-in) 
torque when removing or installing the connector retaining nut. 

Pull back the protective boot and remove the electrical connector 
retaining nut.

 CAUTION: The glow plug contains a fine mesh filter and a small fuel metering 
orifice. Use care to prevent entry of contaminants. 

Disconnect and cap fuel line.

Loosen jam nut and remove glow plug.

 Installation 

Thread glow plug into intake cover until it bottoms. Back plug out two 
turns and align with pointer on cover.

Connect fuel line. Tighten nut to 10 Nm (89 lb-in).

Tighten glow plug jam nut to 25 Nm (18 lb-ft).

Install wiring connector. Tighten retaining nut to 4 Nm
 (35 lb-in). Overtightening retaining nut can destroy heater element.

 Intake Air Heater System — Engine-Mounted Components

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Starter Motor 

 Disassembly 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter motor.

Scribe an alignment mark on starter frame, lever housing and drive end 
housing for assembly reference.

Remove motor terminal retaining screw at solenoid.

Remove retaining screws and drive end housing. Tap housing with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from lever housing, if necessary.

Tap snap ring retainer toward drive pinion using a hammer and socket.

Remove snap ring from armature shaft and discard.

Remove snap ring retainer.

Remove lever housing retaining screws.

 NOTE: Use care when removing assembly to prevent damage to armature shaft lip 
seal located at front of lever housing.

Remove lever housing, drive pinion and solenoid as an assembly. Tap 
housing with plastic-tipped hammer to remove assembly from frame, if necessary.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Remove brush end plate retaining screws. Tap edge of end plate with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Remove screws attaching brush terminals to brush holder.

Pry brush springs upward using screwdriver and remove brushes.

Remove armature.

Remove screws attaching field terminals to brush holder.

Remove retaining screws and brush holder.

Remove drive assembly from lever housing.

Remove lever housing plug.

Remove pinion depth adjusting screw from end of solenoid plunger shaft.

Remove retaining screws and solenoid.

Remove solenoid plunger and protective boot.

Remove snap ring and shift lever pin.

Remove shift lever from housing. Note direction of installation before 
removing.

Remove screws attaching pole shoes to frame using a pole shoe 
screwdriver and arbor press.

Remove field coils and pole shoes from frame.

Clean and inspect parts. Refer to Section 03-06 .

 Assembly 

Follow disassembly procedure in reverse order.

Inspect O-ring seals on shift lever pin drive end housing, frame and 
lever housing. Replace seals if cut or otherwise damaged.

Lightly coat armature shaft seal and thrust washers with a 
multi-purpose lubricant.

Check pinion depth adjustment. Refer to Starter Drive Pinion Depth 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Starter Drive

 Removal 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter motor.

Scribe alignment marks on drive end housing, lever housing and frame 
for assembly reference.

Remove motor terminal retaining screw at solenoid.

Remove retaining screws and drive end housing. Tap housing with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from lever housing, if necessary.

Tap snap ring retainer toward drive assembly using hammer and socket.

Remove snap ring from armature shaft and discard.

Remove snap ring retainer.

Remove lever housing retaining screws.

Remove lever housing, drive pinion and solenoid as an assembly. Tap 
housing with plastic-tipped hammer to remove assembly from frame, if necessary.

Use care when removing assembly to prevent damage to armature shaft lip 
seal located at front of lever housing. Also, note thrust washer installed on 
armature shaft.

Disengage drive assembly from shift lever and remove.

Inspect O-ring seals on drive end housing and lever housing. Replace 
seal if cut or otherwise damaged.

Inspect armature shaft lip seal in lever housing. Replace seal if worn, 
cut or otherwise damaged.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Shift lever is under solenoid spring pressure. Pry lever away from 
housing to provide clearance needed to install drive assembly.

Coat armature shaft seal with a light application of multi-purpose 
lubricant.

Make sure thrust washer is in position on armature shaft before 
installing lever housing.

Check drive pinion depth adjustment. Refer to Starter Drive Pinon Depth 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Solenoid

 Removal 

Remove retaining screws and brush end plate. If necessary, tap edge of 
end plate with plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame. Note thrust 
washer installed on armature shaft.

Remove screw attaching motor terminal to solenoid.

Pull solenoid away from lever housing and maneuver as necessary to 
clear motor terminal. Carefully pulling forward on motor terminal can provide 
additional clearance.

Inspect end plate O-ring seal on frame and solenoid O-ring seal on 
lever housing. Replace seals if cut or otherwise damaged.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Make sure thrust washer is installed on armature shaft before 
installing brush end plate.

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Brush

 Removal 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter.

Remove brush end plate retaining screws. Tap edge of end plate with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame. Note thrust washer 
installed on end of armature shaft.

Remove screws attaching brush terminals to brush holder.

Pry brush springs upward using screwdriver and remove brushes.

Inspect O-ring seal on starter frame. Replace seal if cut or otherwise 
damaged.

Inspect armature commutator.

If commutator is contaminated, remove brush holder and clean using 00 
grade sandpaper. If commutator is excessively worn or scored, it should be 
replaced.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Make sure thrust washer is installed on end of armature shaft before 
installing brush end plate.

================================================================================
PAGE 6491
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03B-06: Starting System, FD-1460 Diesel Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Armature

 Removal 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter motor.

Scribe an alignment mark on starter frame, lever housing and drive end 
housing for assembly reference.

Remove motor terminal retaining screw at solenoid.

Remove retaining screws and drive end housing. Tap housing with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from lever housing, if necessary.

Tap snap ring retainer toward drive pinion using hammer and socket.

Remove snap ring from armature shaft and discard.

Remove snap ring retainer.

Remove lever housing retaining screws.

 NOTE: Use care when removing assembly to prevent damage to armature shaft 
seal located at front of lever housing.

Remove lever housing, drive pinion and solenoid as an assembly. Tap 
housing with plastic-tipped hammer to remove assembly from frame, if necessary.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Remove brush end plate retaining screws. Tap edge of end plate with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Pry brush springs upward using screwdriver and pull brushes out of 
holder until spring can be released against side of brush, holding it away 
from armature.

Remove armature.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Inspect O-ring seal on drive end housing and frame. Replace if cut or 
otherwise damaged.

Inspect armature shaft lip seal in lever housing. Replace if worn, cut 
or otherwise damaged.

Coat armature shaft seal with a light application of multi-purpose 
lubricant.

Make sure thrust washers are installed on armature shaft before 
installing brush end plate and lever housing.

Check drive pinion depth adjustment. Refer to Starter Drive Pinion 
Depth Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

ADJUSTMENTS

Starter Drive Pinion Depth Adjustment

Remove M-terminal retaining screw. To prevent contact between 
M-terminal and solenoid, carefully bend M-terminal away from solenoid using 
needle nose pliers.

Place an insulating material between M-terminal and solenoid.

Connect battery to S-terminal and to a clean metal ground on solenoid 
case.

[FIGURE: J35651A.gif]

 CAUTION: Keep fingers and tools away from opening in drive end housing while 
making electrical connections. The strong shifting action of the solenoid 
could cause personal injury or damage as the drive pinion moves into cranking 
position. 

Momentarily flash a jumper lead from ground to terminal M. The drive 
will now shift into cranking position and remain so until battery is 
disconnected. 

Press on overrunning clutch just enough to take up any drive assembly 
free travel.

Measure distance between pinion and snap ring retainer.

If clearance is not within specifications, adjust by removing access 
plug and turning solenoid plunger shaft nut. If shaft turns, remove solenoid 
so the shaft can be held.

DESCRIPTION

Air Induction System 

Air is cleaned and supplied to the engine in the air induction system. 
Clean air is very important to the life of the engine. Ingested dust and dirt 
can damage an engine very quickly. 

On turbocharged and aftercooled engines, the intake airflow is from the 
air cleaner to the turbocharger. It is then routed to the charge air cooler 
located in front of the radiator. Air leaves the charge air cooler and is 
routed to the intake manifold where it is forced into the cylinders and used 
for combustion. The charge air cooler reduces the temperature of the intake 
air, which lowers combustion chamber temperatures, which in turn reduces NOx 
emissions. Also, cooling the intake air makes it more dense, allowing more 
fuel to be injected into the engine to increase the power-to-weight ratio. 

 Typical Intake Air System, Turbocharged Engine

DESCRIPTION

Air Cleaner Element

A dry-type air cleaner element is standard equipment. Air is filtered 
through a pleated, chemically-treated paper air cleaner element to remove 
contaminants before entering the turbocharger system.

DESCRIPTION

Air Restriction Gauge

Air cleaners are equipped with an air restriction gauge (mounted in the 
instrument panel) or an air restriction indicator (mounted at the air cleaner 
housing) that indicates when the air cleaner element needs servicing. When the 
air restriction indicator or the air restriction gauge reads 6.2 kPa (25 
inches of water) vacuum, the air cleaner element needs servicing.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Cleaner Element

 Removal 

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element, air cleaner housing or turbocharger inlet 
tube is removed, use a clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering 
the engine. 

Loosen latches.

Remove fasteners retaining the air cleaner housing cover.

Remove the air cleaner housing cover.

Remove the air cleaner element from the air cleaner housing.

 Installation 

Before installing a new air cleaner element in the air cleaner housing, 
make sure the following conditions exist:

gasket surfaces clean and undamaged

outlet tube clean and undamaged

air cleaner element dry and free of holes, ruptures, damaged gaskets or 
dents in end covers and liners

drain valve clean and free of debris

Install the air cleaner element into the housing.

Install air cleaner housing cover to air cleaner housing.

Install fasteners retaining air cleaner housing cover. Tighten to 11 Nm
 (96 lb-in).

 NOTE: Make sure the drain valve is installed properly. A leak would reduce 
air cleaner element life.

Reset air restriction indicator.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Inlet Restriction Check

The best method for determining dry-type air cleaner maintenance 
periods is by checking the air restriction indicator or gauge.

It is recommended that the air restriction indicator or gauge be used 
to determine service intervals. A visual inspection of the air cleaner element 
will not ascertain the need for service. Overservicing is not recommended.

================================================================================
PAGE 6505
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03B-12: Air Intake System, FD-1460 Diesel Engine

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Cleaner Element

 CAUTION: Never attempt to clean a dirty or restricted air cleaner element. Use a 
new replacement only. 

Check the old air cleaner element. It could help to detect foreign 
material on the sealing surface that is causing leakage. A streak of dust on 
the clean air side of the air cleaner element seal is a tell-tale sign. If 
dust exists, make sure the cause is removed before installing a new air 
cleaner element.

Inspect the new air cleaner element for damage. Always look for 
possible shipping or handling damage. Pay particular attention to the inside 
of the open end (the sealing area). Check for cuts, etc. Do not use a damaged 
air cleaner element.

Engine Air Cleaner Housing

Clean the air cleaner body and the cover with a mild detergent or 
compressed air. Wipe the air cleaner housing and cover dry. Inspect the air 
cleaner housing and cover for distortion or damage at the gasket mating 
surfaces. Replace air cleaner housing or cover if damaged beyond service.

 Cummins 

This section provides in-chassis service information for the various 
cubic inch displacement (CID) Cummins diesel engines. All Cummins diesels are 
four-stroke cycle, in-line six-cylinder, overhead valve (OHV) engines with 
various compression ratios.

The Cummins NTC N-14 engines feature air-to-air charge cooling and 
variable injection timing. These engines may be optionally equipped with 
Cummins CELECT electronics, which include speed control, engine protection 
system, and engine diagnostics capability. Some Cummins N-14 engines may be 
equipped with the optional Cummins Model C Brake engine brake.

Removal and installation information for Ford Diesel trucks equipped 
with all Cummins turbo diesel engines is also included in this section. For 
service procedures, refer to the Cummins Engine Service Manual.

Diagnosis and testing procedures for Ford installed components are 
covered in this section.

Refer to the applicable Cummins Engine Service Manual for diagnosis and 
testing, adjustments, disassembly and assembly, cleaning and inspection, 
overhaul specifications, and wear limits for Cummins engine components.

at Pin 01 of AH is off.

Refer to Cummins Troubleshooting and Repair Manual.

312

Current detected at No. 5 Injector return Pin 02 of AH when voltage supply
at Pin 11 of AH is off.

Refer to Cummins Troubleshooting and Repair Manual.

313

Current detected at No. 3 Injector return Pin 12 of AH when voltage supply
at Pin 03 of AH

 Diagnostic Tools Required for Troubleshooting

easy to use tool that can effectively furnish the information necessary to 
diagnose the electronic subsystem.

Compulink — Is the primary service tool of the CELECT

Echek plus some added abilities.

Cumpuchek — Is a service bay engine analysis tool for

tests that Echek and Compulink provide as well as a complete set of mechanical 
tests.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Engine Assembly, Cummins

 Removal 

Remove the hood. Refer to Section 01-02 . Remove passenger seat and interior engine cover. Remove transmission and 
engine noise shields. 

Disconnect battery ground cable. Drain the engine crankcase, oil 
filters and cooling system. Refer to Section 03C-03 .

Disconnect the radiator upper and lower hoses at the engine. Disconnect 
the radiator shutter air line at the radiator. Remove the cooling fan. Refer 
to Section 03C-05 . Disconnect heater hoses at thermostat housing.

Remove the radiator brace retaining nuts, washers and insulators at the 
radiator brackets. Remove the radiator support-to-frame mounting nuts, 
washers, insulator and springs. Use a hoist to lift the radiator, radiator 
support and shutter assembly off the vehicle. Refer to Section 03C-03 .

Loosen the accessory mounting bolts, and disengage the drive belts. 

Disconnect the air reservoir supply line at the air compressor. Remove 
air piping.

Remove the alternator wiring harness from the frame clips, and position 
it on the engine.

Tape turbocharger inlet to protect against debris entry.

Remove block heater wires. 

Remove A/C compressor, if so equipped. Refer to Section 12-03A .

Remove clutch linkage.

Remove clutch bellcrank.

Remove throttle linkage.

Remove starter cables and identify them for proper connection.

Disconnect fuel inlet and drain at rear of block.

Bleed air tanks.

Remove transmission shift tower.

Remove hand throttle cable.

Remove air compressor governor line.

Disconnect tachometer sensor.

Disconnect water temperature indicator switch.

Remove water temperature sending unit electrical wire.

Disconnect speedometer sensor at transmission.

Remove exhaust pipes. 

Disconnect U-joint at transmission. 

Remove fuel shutoff electric wire.

Close fuel tank shutoff valves between tanks (rectangular tanks only).

Remove fuel cross-over tube.

Remove channel supporting bottom of tanks. (Use hydraulic jacks to lift 
tanks to remove weight from channel.) Remove two pins holding channel.

Position transmission jack under transmission and connect safety chain 
to support transmission.

Install lifting hooks on front of engine. Attach one to outside 
capscrew of water pump and the other to left side of front cover. To maintain 
engine tilt, use Rotunda Load Positioning Sling 014-00037 or equivalent.

Remove front engine supports.

Remove rear engine supports.

Lift engine 75-100 mm (3-4 inches) and move forward.

Lower transmission below engine mounts.

Move engine forward enough to uncover the lifting hook between number 2 
and 3 heads.

Raise transmission to normal level.

Remove wire clamp from fuel filter bracket and oil pressure sender 
electrical wire.

Place a block of wood between the flywheel housing and crossmember. 
Lower engine onto block of wood.

Move lifting hook to lifting eye between number 2 and 3 heads, and 
remove slack in hoist cables.

Remove safety chain on transmission.

Raise engine and move forward.

Use pry bar to help clear the rear valve cover at the radiator support 
bracket.

 NOTE: An alternate method can be used if the transmission is removed first.

Lift engine and transmission out of chassis and set on suitable stand 
or dolly.

Mark position of engine and transmission and separate using suitable 
hoists or jacks.

Remove clutch, generator and starter. Refer to Section 08-01 for clutch 
removal and Section 14-02B for generator removal.

 Installation 

Install generator. Refer to Section 14-02B .

Install starter.

Install clutch with pilot for alignment. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Position transmission to engine.

Line up throw-out bearing.

Push engine and transmission together and install bolts.

Tighten bolts to specification.

Rethread threads in flywheel housing with a tap.

Put anti-seize on bolts for engine mounts.

Lift engine.

Position engine in vehicle. Use pry bar to clear rear valve cover.

Position transmission jack under transmission and secure with chain.

Move engine rearward.

Attach Rotunda Load Positioning Sling 014-00037 or equivalent and lower 
engine onto block of wood between flywheel housing and crossmember.

Change lifting point to front of engine. Attach one lifting hook to 
outside capscrew of water pump and the other lifting hook to left side of 
front cover.

Move engine rearward.

Connect wire, and clamp on fuel filter bracket and oil pressure sender.

Move engine into final position.

Install top halves of rear engine mounts.

Start front engine mount bolts.

Lower engine down onto mounts. Tighten cotter pin front mount bolts and 
nuts.

Install caps of rear mounts.

Remove transmission jack and safety chain.

Install oil filter.

Connect speedometer sensor at transmission.

Install exhaust pipe.

Install fuel tank support channel.

Connect fuel crossover tube. Open both valves and check for leaks.

Attach clutch linkage at transmission.

Attach fuel shutoff solenoid wire.

Connect Luber-Finer filter line to engine.

Connect tachometer sensor.

Connect throttle linkage.

Connect air compressor unloader valve line.

Connect water temperature sending unit.

Connect water temperature indicator switch.

Install clutch bellcrank and linkage.

Connect two heater hoses.

Install A/C compressor if applicable. Refer to Section 12-03A .

Install fan and tighten bolts.

Install power steering pump.

Connect air piping.

Connect air compressor discharge line.

Connect fuel drain line.

Connect fuel inlet.

Connect backup lamp wires.

Attach battery cable bracket on transmission.

Connect shift tower.

Connect driveshaft.

Install radiator. Refer to Section 03C-03 .

Connect block heater, if so equipped.

Connect hoses to radiator.

Connect shutter air line and clamps.

Connect generator wire.

Attach radiator support from dash panel to top of radiator.

Install hood. Refer to Section 01-02 .

Connect wire harness and two clamps to hood.

Attach generator wire harness bracket on left frame rail.

Connect driving light harness.

Attach bumper.

Secure driving light harness.

Install transmission and engine shields.

 NOTE: When the battery has been disconnected and reconnected, some abnormal 
drive symptoms may occur while the electronic control module (ECM) relearns 
its adaptive strategy. The vehicle may need to be driven 16 km (10 miles) or 
more to relearn the strategy.

Connect battery cables.

Fill engine oil reservoir with oil. Check level.

Fill cooling system. Refer to Section 03C-03 .

Start engine and check for leaks.

Install splash guard on right side.

Install in-cab engine cover.

Install passenger seat.

Close hood.

Test drive vehicle and check for power and operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Engine Assembly, CAT

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery ground cable. Remove the engine noise panels.

Drain the cooling system. Refer to Section 03C-03 .

Release the air pressure in the air supply tank.

Disconnect the hood check cable and springs. Support the hood and 
fenders in a vertical position. Remove the radiator support rod.

Remove the radiator, radiator shroud and the fan from the vehicle. 
Refer to Section 03C-05 .

Discharge air conditioner and remove condenser, if so equipped. Refer 
to Section 12-00 and Section 12-03A .

Remove the air cleaner and air cleaner hoses.

Remove the generator and identify each wire for installation.

Disconnect the power steering hoses, if so equipped.

Disconnect the heater hoses and position them out of the way.

Disconnect the tachometer sensor.

Disconnect the throttle linkage from the injection pump.

Disconnect the fuel inlet and fuel return lines.

Disconnect the air lines from the air compressor.

Disconnect the wires from the engine shutoff solenoid, the oil sending 
unit and the temperature gauge sending unit.

Disconnect all cables from the starter motor. Identify for installation 
and position them out of the way.

Disconnect exhaust pipe from the exhaust manifold.

Remove the transmission. Refer to the appropriate manual or automatic 
transmission section in Group 07.

Disconnect the clutch release mechanism at the clutch release lever.

Connect Rotunda Load Positioning Sling 014-00037 or equivalent to the 
engine lifting eyes.

Remove attaching parts from the engine front support.

Make sure the lifting tool is tight enough to support weight of engine, 
then disconnect the engine rear mounts.

Position all lines, wires and accessories out of the way and lift the 
engine from vehicle.

 Installation 

Use Rotunda Load Positioning Sling 014-00037 or equivalent to lower the 
engine into position. Start the engine front mount attaching parts and 
position the engine rear mounts.

Install all engine mount bolts or nuts. Tighten to specification.

Install the transmission. Refer to the appropriate automatic or manual 
transmission section in Group 07.

Connect the clutch mechanism at the clutch release lever, and adjust 
the clutch as required. Refer to Section 08-00 for clutch adjustments.

Connect exhaust pipe to the exhaust manifold.

Connect all wires to the starter motor, installing each wire on its 
respective terminal.

Connect the wires to the engine shutoff solenoid, the oil sending unit 
and the temperature gauge sending unit.

Connect all air lines to the air compressor.

Connect all fuel lines.

Connect throttle linkage at injection pump and connect tachometer sensor.

Connect heater hoses and power steering lines.

Install generator and connect all wires to their respective terminals.

Install A/C condenser core, if so equipped. Refer to Section 12-03A 
for A/C condenser core installation.

Install the air cleaner.

Install the fan and the radiator with shroud. Refer to Section 03C-03 
for radiator and fan and clutch installation. Install the radiator support rod.

Install all drive belts and tighten to specifications.

Install the hood check cables and springs.

Fill cooling system. Refer to Section 03C-03 .

 NOTE: When the battery has been disconnected and reconnected, some abnormal 
drive symptoms may occur while the electronic control module (ECM) relearns 
its adaptive strategy. The vehicle may need to be driven 16 km (10 miles) or 
more to relearn the strategy.

Connect battery ground cable.

Check oil and coolant levels, and replenish as required.

Install engine noise panels.

Start the engine and check for any oil leaks.

Charge air conditioner system, if so equipped. Refer to Section 12-00 
in the Body, Chassis Manual for system charging procedure.

Before attempting to move the vehicle, verify the air supply tank is up 
to pressure.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cooling System

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE THE RADIATOR CAP UNDER ANY CONDITIONS WHILE THE ENGINE IS 
OPERATING. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS CAN RESULT IN PERSONAL INJURY 
AND DAMAGE TO THE COOLING SYSTEM AND ENGINE. 

TO AVOID HAVING SCALDING HOT COOLANT OR STEAM BLOW OUT OF THE RADIATOR, 
USE EXTREME CARE WHEN REMOVING THE CAP FROM A HOT RADIATOR. IF POSSIBLE, WAIT 
UNTIL THE ENGINE HAS COOLED, THEN WRAP A THICK CLOTH AROUND THE RADIATOR CAP 
AND TURN IT SLOWLY TO THE FIRST STOP. STEP BACK WHILE THE PRESSURE IS RELEASED 
FROM THE COOLING SYSTEM. WHEN YOU ARE SURE ALL THE PRESSURE HAS BEEN RELEASED, 
PRESS DOWN ON THE CAP (STILL USING A CLOTH), TURN AND REMOVE IT. 

All L-Series vehicles have liquid engine cooling systems. The cooling 
system consists of the engine cooling jackets, coolant pump, radiator and 
hoses. Heavy-duty diesel applications can include an engine oil cooler, 
coolant conditioner and surge tank.

The engine oil cooler consists of tubes or plates inside a housing 
attached to the engine.

Some engines have a coolant conditioner installed that contains 
chemicals to clean the coolant and neutralize any acids formed in the coolant. 
For information on a specific Cummins, CAT or DDC engine, refer to the 
appropriate service manual(s):

Cummins Diesel Engine Maintenance Manual

CAT 3176 Diesel Engine Manual

CAT 3406 or 3306 Engine Service Manual

Detroit Diesel Engine Service Manual

Most large diesel engines have a coolant recovery reservoir as part of 
the cooling system. It serves three functions:

provides a coolant reservoir

provides air space for coolant expansion

provides a calm point (a point without turbulence) in the cooling 
system where any air trapped in the coolant can escape

The last function is important because the water pump can whip air in 
the system along with coolant into foam, greatly reducing cooling efficiency. 
Air bubbles in the coolant can erode the water pump impeller and, in some 
cases, even parts of the cylinder block and head.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cooling Fan and Fan Clutch

These engines are equipped with an eight- or nine-blade moulded plastic 
fan with a moulded-in steel hub. The plastic fan reduces fan noise, weight and 
the amount of engine power required to accelerate it compared to a metal fan.

An air-actuated fan clutch is used on some of these engines. This 
allows the fan to be shut off when the engine is cold, allowing quicker 
warm-up. The cooling system is designed so that when ram air from the 
vehicle's movement is adequate for cooling at highway speeds, the fan can be 
shut off, taking that power draw from the engine, reducing fuel consumption.

The fan clutch is operated from the vehicle's air brake supply system 
and is controlled by a thermostatic valve located in the cylinder head or 
water outlet.

Refer to Section 03C-05 for further information on cooling fan and 
air-actuated fan clutch.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Thermostat, Water, Cummins Diesel Engines

The following procedure pertains only to Cummins diesel engines. For 
water thermostat removal and installation procedure for CAT or DDC engines, 
refer to the appropriate service manual(s):

CAT 3176 Diesel Engine Manual

CAT 3406 or 3306 Engine Service Manual

Detroit Diesel Engine Service Manual

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to service the thermostat. It should be replaced if it 
is not operating properly. 

The poppet-type thermostat used in production is a high-temperature 
thermostat for use with a mixture of water and permanent-type antifreeze. 

Check the thermostat before installing it. Refer to the thermostat test 
procedures in Section 03-03 . 

 Cummins Diesel Engines 

 Removal 

Drain the cooling system to below the thermostat level. 

Disconnect the oil cooler coolant hose, radiator supply tank vent line, 
and air compressor coolant line from the thermostat housing. 

Close the air control valve. Disconnect the air hoses from the 
shutterstat, if so equipped. 

Remove the thermostat housing retaining bolts. Move the thermostat 
housing forward and to one side, then remove the thermostat. Discard the 
gasket. 

 Installation 

Clean gasket and apply Perfect Sealing Compound B5A-19554-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A to the 
gasket surfaces at the coolant manifold and thermostat housing. 

 NOTE: If the thermostat is not properly installed, an air lock and incomplete 
coolant circulation can result.

Position the thermostat in the housing with the V notch at the top to 
vent as much air as possible. 

Install a new gasket on the thermostat housing. Position the housing to 
the water manifold. Install and tighten the retaining bolts. 

Connect the oil cooler coolant hose, radiator supply tank vent line, 
and air compressor water line to the thermostat housing. Connect the air hoses 
to the shutterstat. Open the air control valve.

Fill the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 . Operate the engine and check 
for coolant leaks.
