REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator Hoses 

Replace the cooling system hoses whenever they become cracked or 
deteriorated, or have a tendency to collapse. 

Refer to illustrations in this section for hose locations and routing.

 Removal 

Partially drain the cooling system to replace cooling system upper 
(inlet) hose(s). Drain the cooling system to replace the lower radiator 
(outlet) hose. 

Loosen the clamps on each end of the hose(s) to be removed. Slide the 
hose(s) off the connections. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: If the connections have a single bead around the edges, make sure the 
clamps are located beyond the beads. If the connections have a double bead, 
make sure the clamp is located between the beads after assembly.

Position the clamps on each end of the new hose. Slide the hose onto 
the connections, then tighten the clamps. 

Fill the cooling system with coolant and bleed the system. Refer to 
 Section 03-03 .

Operate the engine for several minutes, then check the hose(s) and 
connections for leaks.

Radiator, Except LL and LTL

lifting these radiators.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator Coolant Recovery Reservoir

 Removal 

 NOTE: Refer to illustrations in this section.

Partially drain cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Disconnect any electrical connections from sensors on surge tank.

Disconnect hoses from surge tank.

Remove fasteners securing reservoir bracket to radiator brace and 
remove reservoir.

If necessary, remove nuts and bracket from reservoir.

If necessary, remove sensors from reservoir.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order. Refer to illustrations for 
torque specifications, or refer to Specifications at the end of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fan Shroud, Single Piece

 Removal 

Drain cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Disconnect upper and lower radiator hoses from radiator.

Remove shroud-to-radiator screws and hang shroud on fan.

Loosen lower radiator mounts.

Remove radiator brace-to-radiator retaining nuts.

Tip radiator forward and support.

If necessary, remove fan-to-fan clutch bolts.

Lift out shroud and, if necessary, lift out fan along with it.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order. For torque specifications, 
refer to appropriate illustrations in this section and in Section 03C-05 , or 
in Specifications at the end of this section and Section 03C-05.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Radiator Coolant Level Check

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE THE RADIATOR CAP UNDER ANY CONDITIONS WHILE THE ENGINE IS 
OPERATING. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS CAN RESULT IN PERSONAL INJURY 
AND DAMAGE TO THE COOLING SYSTEM AND ENGINE.

TO AVOID HAVING SCALDING HOT COOLANT OR STEAM BLOW OUT OF THE RADIATOR, 
USE EXTREME CARE WHEN REMOVING THE CAP FROM A HOT RADIATOR. IF POSSIBLE, WAIT 
UNTIL THE ENGINE HAS COOLED, THEN WRAP A THICK CLOTH AROUND THE RADIATOR CAP 
AND TURN IT SLOWLY TO THE FIRST STOP. STEP BACK WHILE THE PRESSURE IS RELEASED 
FROM THE COOLING SYSTEM. WHEN YOU ARE SURE ALL THE PRESSURE HAS BEEN RELEASED, 
PRESS DOWN ON THE CAP (STILL USING A CLOTH), TURN AND REMOVE IT. 

 NOTE: On vehicles with butterfly hood, it is not necessary to open the tilt 
hood to check the coolant; open one side of the butterfly hood.

 CAUTION: Do not add coolant to an overheated system. This can crack the cylinder 
block or head. Allow system to cool gradually. 

Open hood (or butterfly hood) and remove radiator cap.

Make sure coolant is up to bottom of filler neck. Refill as necessary 
with premixed 50/50 concentration of Ford Heavy-Duty Diesel Engine Cooling 
System Fluid E6HZ-19549-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESE-M97B18-C and water.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fan Blade

 WARNING: ALWAYS INSPECT FAN BLADE BEFORE PERFORMING MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES WITH 
THE HOOD OPEN AND THE ENGINE RUNNING. A BROKEN FAN BLADE CAN CAUSE SERIOUS 
INJURY. 

Inspect fan assembly for cracks. Cracks are most likely where each 
blade meets the fan hub. Replace damaged fan.

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Charge Air Cooler, Aluminum

Listed in the following chart are the components of the air cooler 
system and the types of damage that occur. Some types of damage can be 
repaired while other types cannot. The corrective action is shown for each 
type of damage. In some cases, the cooler should be replaced not repaired.

 ALUMINUM CHARGE AIR COOLER

Condition

Action to Take

 · Tubes torn or cracked

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Tubes dented, kinked or bent, resulting in a round edge (radius less than
1 mm [1/32 inch])

 · Weld or epoxy. Refer to Welding Repairs or Epoxy Repairs in the Service
Procedures portion of this section.

 · Tubes dented, kinked or bent, resulting in a round edge (radius greater
than 1 mm [1/32 inch])

 · No repair required.

 · Holes in tubes less than 1 mm (1/32 inch) in all directions on tube surface

 · Weld or epoxy to fill. Refer to Welding Repairs or Epoxy Repairs in the
Service Procedures portion of this section.

 · External fins crushed or bent, but no more than 1-mm (1/32-inch) height
reduction per fin row and the sidemember-to-sidemember dimension is within
specification (687 mm [26-3/4 inch])

 · No repair required.

 · External fins pushed in with no tearing

 · Straighten fins. Refer to Straightening in the Service Procedures portion
of this section.

 · External fins pushed in with tearing less than 10 mm (3/8 inch) deep from
core face; also tearing is less than 20% of a given fin row and less than 5%
of the total fin rows

 · Remove loose fin material and straighten. Refer to Straightening in the
Service Procedures portion of this section.

 · External fins pushed in with tearing of more than 10 mm (3/8 inch) from
face core, or more than 20% of a given row, or more than 5% of the total fin row

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Sidemembers bent or dented

 · Straighten sidemember to original form. If tubes are dented or fins
crushed, refer to Straightening in the Service Procedures portion of this
section.

 · Sidemembers' surface cracked or broken through

 · Weld sidemember. Refer to Welding Repairs in the Service Procedures
portion of this section.

 · Headers bent or dented, resulting in three or fewer tube or tube-to-header
leaks, and cracks are less than 2 mm (1/16 inch)

 · Weld header. Refer to Welding Repairs in the Service Procedures portion of
this section.

 Note: If crack is less than 1 mm (1/32 inch), repair can be
made with epoxy.

 · Headers bent or dented, with more than three tube or tube-to-header leaks
or a crack width greater than 2 mm (1/16 inch)

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Headers cracked

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Tank walls dented but not cracked or broken through, and fit and function
of cooler is not affected

 · No repair required.

 · Tanks cracked, but crack is no more than 2 mm (1/16 inch) wide and 20 mm
(3/4 inch) long

 · Weld tanks. Refer to Welding Repairs in the Service Procedures portion of
this section.

 · Tanks cracked, and crack is more than 2 mm (1/16 inch) wide or 20 mm (3/4
inch) long

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Tanks punctured, but hole is no more than 5 mm (3/16 inch) in all
directions on tank surface

 · Weld tanks. Refer to Welding Repairs in the Service Procedures portion of
this section.

 · Tanks punctured, and hole is more than 5 mm (3/16 inch) in any direction
on tank surface

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Tank-to-header welds cracked or porous

 · Weld. Refer to Welding Repairs in the Service Procedures portion of this
section.

 Caution: Repair welds must not start or stop where a 
production weld ends. 

 · Threads stripped in tapped holes

 · Drill out stripped threads and tap to accept proper helicoil insert of
same diameter and thread pitch as original hole.

 · Bosses and mounting brackets cracked or broken off, but crack or fractured
surface does not go into tank wall

 · Weld. Refer to Welding Repairs in the Service Procedures portion of this
section.

 · Bosses or mounting brackets cracked or broken off, and crack goes into
tank wall

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 · Mounting pins or other hardware cracked, broken or otherwise damaged, and
repair will not affect fit, function or durability

 · Repair to original condition.

 · Mounting pins or other hardware cracked, broken or otherwise damaged, and
repairs will affect fit, function or durability

 · Replace cooler. Refer to Charge Air Cooler in the Removal and Installation
portion of this section.

 Straightening 

 Straightening Fins 

Use a pointed object no more than 0.5 mm (0.2 inch) in diameter at the 
tip that will allow access to the apex of the fin. Straighten fins, taking 
care not to damage louvers or distort louver angle.

 Straightening Sidemembers 

Using pliers, locking pliers or similar tool, straighten sidemember 
from sides only. Never pry against tubes or header. Care must be taken not to 
damage fins, tubes or headers when straightening sidemembers.

================================================================================
PAGE 6566
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-04: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Welding Repairs

 Surface Preparation 

All surfaces to be welded must be free of all paint, oil, grease, water 
and other foreign matter in the area so the weld repair will adhere to the 
bare aluminum and will not be contaminated.

 Welding Tanks 

Prepare surfaces as outlined. Heat crack to chase ends until they stop. 
MIG-weld to fill crack, and continue bead past ends of crack approximately 25 
mm (1 inch). Wire brush and grind excess weld material to blend with tank 
surface.

 Welding Sidemembers 

Prepare surface as outlined. Cut a V-shaped groove along the length of 
the crack to a depth equal to the member thickness. MIG-weld to fill the 
groove, and grind excess material away to provide a flat surface.

 Welding Mounting Brackets 

 CAUTION: Care must be taken not to melt fins of tube-to-header braze joint. If 
welding near core, shield the core with large steel plate. This protects it 
from sparks and weld splatter and will act as a heat sink. 

Tack brackets in place so bracket will retain its correct orientation. 
MIG-weld in place. Allow to air cool. Check alignment.

 Welding Tubes or Tube Header Joints 

TIG-weld using aluminum wire designated Alcan MIG Electrode Wire, 
1.20-mm (3/16-inch) diameter, 4043 aluminum alloy or equivalent.

================================================================================
PAGE 6567
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-04: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Epoxy Repairs

 Surface Preparation 

Remove all paint, oil, grease, water and other foreign matter in area 
of the epoxy repair so epoxy will adhere to the bare aluminum.

 Epoxying Tubes or Headers 

Use only high temperature epoxy. The recommended epoxy is a resin (CIBA 
GEIGY ARALDITE AV 138M) and a hardener (CIBA GEIGY HV 998) or equivalent. Mix 
and cure instructions on product label must be strictly adhered to.

================================================================================
PAGE 6568
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-04: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Cleaning After Weld or Epoxy Repairs

The cooler must be flushed after either a weld or an epoxy repair to 
remove all debris that may have dropped into the cooler during service.

The recommended procedure for cleaning is to power-flush the cooler 
with water at a rate of 127 mm (5 inches)/sec. for three minutes. To ensure 
that debris exits the cooler, orient the cooler so the tank containing the 
repair or closest to the repair point is at the bottom. The flushing water is 
to be introduced into the opposite tank at the top. When complete, invert the 
cooler and power-flush in opposite direction.

If power-flushing is not possible, flush cooler by hand. Lay cooler 
flat with inlet and outlet ports pointing up. Fill cooler to forty percent of 
its volume with water, seal off both ports, and agitate by hand so water 
flushes all internal surfaces at least ten times. Empty cooler and repeat 
flushing process until no debris is found in the flushing water.

After flushing (either by power or by hand), drain cooler of all water 
and allow to air dry. Leak test cooler to check all repairs prior to painting 
or installing cooler into vehicle.

================================================================================
PAGE 6569
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-04: Turbocharger and Charge Air Cooler, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Leak Testing Cooler After Repairs

 NOTE: To ensure proper performance, the repaired cooler must be leak tested 
and pressure checked prior to reinstalling it into the vehicle.

Connect an air pressure gauge in one port of the cooler and a stop/air 
supply in the other port. Apply a gauge pressure of 345 kPa (50 psi) to the 
cooler. Reduce pressure to a gauge pressure of 200 kPa (29 psi) and plug the 
cooler to hold pressure. Let the cooler stand a few minutes and note any loss 
of air pressure. Loss of air pressure should not exceed a gauge pressure of 
10.3 kPa (1.5 psi) per minute. If leakage exceeds this limit, check cooler and 
make any necessary repairs. Leak test cooler again and continue until cooler 
will hold pressure as stated. Replace cooler if permanent distortion is present.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Painting

Clean all repaired areas. Wash thoroughly with fresh water. Allow to 
dry and paint as required.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Drive Belts, Accessory

L-Series vehicles are equipped with two types of accessory drive belts. 
The belt type is selected for each engine based on performance requirements. 
To ensure maximum life, replacement belts must be of the same type as 
originally installed. These belts must be properly adjusted at all times. 
Loose belt(s) will result in slippage, which can cause a noise complaint or 
improper accessory operation (generator will not charge, etc.). Overly tight 
belts will place severe loads on accessory bearings and also reduce belt life 
significantly.

[FIGURE: Q1690E.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fan and Clutch, Engine Operated 

The fan and clutch assembly is used to cool the engine. The fan is 
driven by the engine through the use of drive belts.

================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-05: Drive Belts, Accessory, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fan Clutch Control System, Bendix

 Index Control with A/C 

Air flows from the air supply to the air solenoid valve. With the A/C 
refrigerant pressure and the engine coolant temperature within normal ranges, 
electric current flows through the coolant temperature switch and the A/C 
refrigerant high-pressure switch to the air solenoid valve.

The current opens the normally closed air solenoid valve so that air is 
supplied to the fan clutch, disengaging it. When the temperature switch or the 
A/C high-pressure switch opens, the electrical circuit is broken.

Without current, the air solenoid valve closes, cutting off the air 
supply to the fan clutch, venting the air in the fan clutch and engaging it.

In addition, after the A/C high-pressure switch resets, a timer within 
the temperature switch case is triggered, which keeps the air solenoid valve 
deactivated (i.e., fan on) for three more minutes.

 Index Control Without A/C 

Air flows from the air supply to the air solenoid valve. With the 
engine coolant temperature within normal range, electric current flows through 
the A/C jumper plug and the coolant temperature switch to the air solenoid 
valve. The current opens the normally closed air solenoid valve so that air is 
supplied to the fan clutch, disengaging it. When the temperature switch opens, 
the electrical circuit is broken. Without current, the air solenoid valve 
closes, cutting off the air supply to the fan clutch, venting the air in the 
fan clutch, and engaging it.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Drive Belts, Accessory

 Inspection and Verification 

 Drive Belt Cracking/Chunking/Wear 

Under severe operating conditions (high temperatures, low humidity), 
drive belt rib cracking can occur at less than 96,000 km (60,000 miles). Drive 
belt rib cracking perpendicular to the belt ribs is not a reason for concern 
and has no detrimental effect on belt performance. Cracks parallel to ribs are 
not acceptable.

Drive belt "chunking" is the condition in which the rubber material 
actually chunks out between the cracks. The drive belt should be replaced if 
chunks are missing on two adjacent ribs or a chunked-out section is 13 mm (0.5 
inch) or longer.

[FIGURE: Q4077C.gif]

 Drive Belt Noise 

Drive belt chirp is a regularly occurring chirping noise that occurs 
due to pulley misalignment or excessive pulley runout. It can be a result of a 
damaged pulley or an improperly replaced pulley that was not properly aligned.

To correct, determine the area the noise comes from. Then check each of 
the pulleys in that area with a straightedge to the crankshaft pulley and look 
for the accessory pulleys to be out of position in the fore/aft direction or 
at an angle to the straightedge.

Belt squeal is an intermittent noise that occurs when the drive belt 
slips on a pulley during certain conditions, such as engine start up, rapid 
engine acceleration or A/C clutch engagement.

Drive belt squeal can occur under the following conditions:

A/C discharge pressure goes above 2895 kPa (420 psi). This can occur if:

the A/C system is overcharged

the A/C condenser core airflow is blocked

the engine fan blade is not engaging fully at idle

A/C OFF equalized pressure (the common discharge and suction pressure 
that occurs after several minutes) exceeds 965 kPa (140 psi), which is a rare 
occurrence at high ambient temperatures with a hot engine. Turn A/C off for a 
few seconds and then back on after fan blade begins to cool A/C condenser core.

Any of the accessories are damaged, or have a worn or damaged bearing 
or internal torsional resistance above normal for any reason. All of the 
accessories should be able to be rotated by hand in the unloaded condition. If 
any are not, inspect the accessory.

Fluid gets on the drive belt. These would include power steering fluid, 
engine coolant, engine oil or air conditioning system lubricant.

If fluid does get on the drive belt during service, the best policy is 
to clean the drive belt with soap and water and thoroughly rinse with clean 
water. The drive belt does not have to be replaced if no apparent damage has 
occurred.

If drive belt is too long. A drive belt that is too long will not allow 
proper belt tension to be achieved. If the drive belt is too long, replace the 
drive belt.

 Symptom Chart — Accessory Drive Belt Diagnosis 

 ACCESSORY DRIVE BELT DIAGNOSIS 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Excessive Noise/Belt Squeal

Seized accessory.

CHECK all accessories for free rotation and REPLACE accessory if 
necessary. REPLACE drive belt.

Loose drive belt.

CHECK condition and tension of all drive belts. REPLACE drive belts or 
ADJUST tension of manually tensioned drive belts as necessary.

CHECK for correct drive belt length if drive belt is out of operating 
range.

Rattle

Loose pulley or accessory.

CHECK for looseness and TIGHTEN.

Severe Belt Flutter

Loose drive belt.

CHECK belt tension and ADJUST if necessary. CHECK condition of drive 
belt and REPLACE if necessary.

Frayed Drive Belt

Drive belt not seated correctly (poly-V belt).

REPLACE drive belt and VERIFY correct belt seating.

Severely misaligned pulley.

CHECK with a straightedge for severe angular misalignment between 
adjacent pulleys. CORRECT as necessary.

Severely Glazed Drive Belt

Seized accessory.

CHECK all accessories for free rotation and REPLACE if necessary.

Loose drive belt.

REPLACE drive belt.

Improper Accessory Operation (Power Steering or Air Conditioning 
Doesn't Work, Engine Overheats or Battery Doesn't Charge)

Loose drive belt.

CHECK drive belt for looseness or glazing and REPLACE or ADJUST tension 
of manually tensioned belts if necessary.

Drive Belt Jumps off Pulley

Greatly misaligned pulleys.

CHECK for misalignment between adjacent pulleys.

Drive belt not seated correctly (poly-V belt).

REPLACE drive belt and VERIFY correct seating.

Pulley wobble.

VERIFY that no pulley wobbles during engine operation. Conditions 
causing wobble are: bent pulley, bent accessory shaft, rear face of pulley not 
seated flat against mating surface.

Excessive crankshaft end play.

REBUILD engine.

 Component Tests 

 Drive Belt Tension 

Check drive belt tension. Refer to Drive Belt Tension 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section. If tension is not within specification, 
adjust tension. Service components as required.

 Drive Belt Misalignment 

 CAUTION: Incorrect drive belt installation will cause excessive drive belt wear 
and can cause the drive belt to come off the drive pulleys. 

 NOTE: Original equipment drive belts are made of a special cord construction 
and are subjected to special testing before they are approved for use.

 NOTE: Replacement drive belts, other than O.E.M., can track 
differently/improperly. If a replacement drive belt tracks improperly, the 
drive belt must be replaced with an O.E.M. drive belt to avoid performance 
failure or loss of drive belt during cold operation.

With the engine running, check drive belt tracking (the position of the 
drive belt on the accessory and idler pulleys). If the edge of the drive belt 
rides beyond the edge of the pulleys, this can cause noise and premature wear. 

If a drive belt tracking condition exists, visually check the accessory 
and idler pulleys for damage. If the drive belt tensioner accessory or idler 
pulleys are incorrect they will be out of position. This will result in drive 
belt tension and chirp and squeal noises.

If the above procedures do not correct the drive belt noise, try 
replacing the drive belt with a known good original equipment drive belt. 
However, the drive belt noise may return again (with mileage) if one of the 
above conditions remains uncorrected.

With engine running, visually observe the grooves in the pulleys (not 
the pulley flanges) for excessive wobble. Replace components as required.

Check all accessories, mounting brackets and accessory and idler 
pulleys for any interference that would prevent the component from mounting 
properly. Correct any interference condition and recheck belt tracking.

Tighten all accessory mounting brackets and accessory and idler pulley 
retaining hardware to specification. Refer to the torque specifications at the 
end of this manual. Recheck drive belt tracking.

Check drive belt tension. Refer to Drive Belt Tension 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Belt Replacement

Conditions requiring drive belt replacement are rib chunk out, 
excessive wear, severe glazing and frayed cords. Replace any drive belt 
exhibiting any of these conditions. Minor cracks in the ribbed side of 
V-grooved portion of the drive belt are considered acceptable.

 Removal 

Loosen the cooling fan clutch mounting bolts and back off the adjusting 
screw. 

Remove the drive belts from the accessory pulley and the fan hub. 

 Installation 

Position the new drive belts on the cooling fan hub and the accessory 
pulley.

Adjust the tension of the drive belts to specifications, and tighten 
the fan clutch mounting bolts.

Fan Pulley and Bearing Replacement, CAT 3306 

 Removal 

Remove nut and washer. 

Using a 1-3/4-inch diameter arbor, press bracket out of pulley assembly.

[FIGURE: Q2770B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Bracket (Part of 7121)

2

7121

Pulley Assy

3

9042

Step Washer

4

9032

Nut

A

—

Tighten to 135-169 Nm (100-125 Lb-Ft)

Place pulley assembly down on front face, allowing approximately 25.4 
mm (1 inch) of clearance to remove bearings. 

Offset bearing spacer until the wall of the spacer is centered on the 
bearing inner race. 

 NOTE: Once bearing is pressed out, it cannot be reused because the inner race 
will be damaged. 

From the back of the pulley, using a 1-3/4-inch arbor, slide the arbor 
through the rear bearing to the spacer. Press out front bearing.

Remove bearing spacer.

[FIGURE: Q27711A.gif]

Remove retaining ring. 

 NOTE: Once bearing is pressed out, it cannot be reused because the inner race 
will be damaged. 

Using 1-7/8-inch diameter arbor, press out the rear bearing.

 Installation 

Place pulley down on rear face. 

 NOTE: Use a 3-1/4-inch diameter arbor that will apply an even pressure on the 
outer and inner races of bearing, making sure that the rear bearing seats to 
the bottom of the bore. 

Press rear bearing into pulley.

 NOTE: Retaining ring will not fully expand if the bearing is not completely

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Starter Motor

 Removal 

Open battery box and disconnect battery ground cable.

Remove starter motor upper mounting bolt.

Disconnect starter motor and starter solenoid wires. Tag wires to 
facilitate connection at proper terminals during starter motor installation.

Remove two remaining starter motor mounting bolts. Remove starter motor.

 Installation 

Position starter motor on engine. Install three bolts. Tighten to 95-120 Nm
 (70-90 lb-ft).

Connect starter solenoid wire to starter terminal.

Connect remaining starter motor wires to starter terminals.

Connect battery ground cable and close battery box. Check starter motor 
operation.

================================================================================
PAGE 6595
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-06: Starting System, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Starter Drive

 Removal 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter motor.

Scribe an alignment mark on drive end housing, lever housing and frame 
for assembly reference.

Remove motor strap to solenoid retaining nut.

Remove screw attaching motor strap to field terminal and remove strap.

Remove retaining screws and drive end housing. It may be necessary to 
tap housing with plastic-tipped hammer to remove.

Remove lever housing retaining screws.

 NOTE: Use care when removing assembly to prevent damage to armature shaft lip 
seal located at front of lever housing. Also, note thrust washer installed on 
armature shaft.

Remove lever housing, drive pinion and solenoid as an assembly. Tap 
housing with plastic-tipped hammer to remove assembly from frame, if necessary.

Disengage drive assembly from shift lever and remove.

Inspect O-ring seals on drive end housing and lever housing. Replace if 
cut or otherwise damaged.

Inspect armature shaft lip seal in lever housing. Replace seal if worn, 
cut or otherwise damaged.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Shift lever is under spring pressure. Pry lever away from housing to 
provide clearance to install drive assembly.

Coat armature shaft seal with a light application of multipurpose 
lubricant.

Make sure thrust washer is in position on armature shaft before 
installing lever housing.

Check drive pinion depth adjustment. Refer to Starter Drive Depth 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

PAGE 6596
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-06: Starting System, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Solenoid

 Removal 

Remove motor strap to solenoid retaining nut.

Remove screw attaching motor strap to field terminal and remove strap.

Remove retaining screws and solenoid.

Inspect solenoid O-ring seal. Replace if cut or otherwise damaged.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten solenoid retaining screws to 15-21 Nm (11-15 
lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Brushes 

 Removal 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter.

Remove brush end plate retaining screws. Tap edge of end plate with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame. Note thrust washer 
installed on end of armature shaft.

Remove screws attaching brush terminals to brush holder.

Pry brush springs upward using screwdriver and remove brushes.

Inspect O-ring seal on starter frame. Replace seal if cut or otherwise 
damaged.

Inspect armature commutator. If commutator is contaminated, remove 
brush holder and clean using 00 grade sandpaper. If commutator is excessively 
worn or scored, replace.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order. 

Make sure thrust washer is installed on end of armature shaft before 
installing brush end plate.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Armature

 Removal 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter motor.

Scribe an alignment mark on starter frame, lever housing and drive end 
housing for assembly reference.

Remove motor strap to solenoid retaining nut.

Remove screw attaching motor strap to field terminal and remove strap.

Remove retaining screws and drive end housing. Tap housing with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from lever housing, if necessary.

Remove lever housing retaining screws.

 CAUTION: Use care when removing assembly to prevent damage to armature shaft lip 
seal located at front of lever housing. 

Remove lever housing, drive pinion and solenoid as an assembly. Tap 
housing with plastic-tipped hammer to remove assembly from starter frame, if 
necessary.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Remove brush end plate retaining screws. Tap edge of end plate with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Remove screws attaching brush terminals to brush holder.

Pry brush spring upward using screwdriver and remove brushes.

Remove armature.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Inspect O-ring seal on drive end housing and frame. Replace if cut or 
otherwise damaged.

Inspect armature shaft lip seal in lever housing. Replace if worn, cut 
or otherwise damaged.

Coat armature shaft seal with a light application of multipurpose 
lubricant.

Make sure thrust washers are installed on armature shaft before 
installing brush end plate and lever housing.

Check drive pinion depth adjustment. Refer to Starter Drive Pinion 
Depth Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

Tighten all retaining screws to specified torque. Refer to Specifications 
 in this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Starter Motor

 Disassembly 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter motor.

Scribe an alignment mark on starter frame, lever housing and drive end 
housing for assembly reference.

Remove motor strap to solenoid attaching nut.

Remove screw attaching motor strap to field terminal and remove strap.

Remove retaining screws and drive end housing. Tap housing with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from lever housing, if necessary.

Remove lever housing retaining screws.

 CAUTION: Use care when removing assembly to prevent damage to armature shaft lip 
seal located at front of lever housing. 

Remove lever housing, drive pinion and solenoid as an assembly. Tap 
housing with plastic-tipped hammer to remove assembly from starter frame, if 
necessary.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Remove brush end plate retaining screws. Tap edge of end plate with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame, if necessary.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Remove screws attaching brush terminals to brush holder.

Pry brush springs upward using screwdriver and remove brushes.

Remove armature.

Remove screws attaching field terminals to brush holder.

Remove brush holder.

Remove drive assembly from lever housing.

Remove lever housing plug.

Remove pinion depth adjusting screw from end of solenoid plunger shaft.

Remove retaining screws and solenoid.

Remove solenoid and protective boot.

Remove snap ring and shift lever.

Remove shift lever from housing. Note direction of installation before 
removing.

Remove screws attaching pole shoes to frame using a pole shoe 
screwdriver and arbor press.

Remove field coils and pole shoes from frame. Note field terminal 
insulator.

Clean and inspect parts. Refer to Section 03-06 .

 Assembly 

Follow disassembly procedure in reverse order.

Inspect O-ring seals on drive end housing, frame and lever housing. 
Replace seals if cut or otherwise damaged.

Lightly coat armature shaft seal and thrust washers with a multipurpose 
lubricant.

Check pinion depth adjustment. Refer to Starter Drive Pinion Depth 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

Tighten all screws to specified torque. Refer to Specifications in this 
section.

ADJUSTMENTS

Starter Drive Pinion Depth Adjustment

Remove motor strap to solenoid retaining nut.

Remove screw attaching motor strap to field terminal and remove strap.

Remove retaining nut and wiring terminal from solenoid ground terminal.

Connect battery positive terminal to solenoid S-terminal.

Connect battery negative terminal to solenoid G-terminal.

Momentarily flash a jumper lead from G-terminal to M-terminal. Drive 
will now shift into cranking position and remain so until battery is 
disconnected.

[FIGURE: J6428A.gif]

Press on overrunning clutch just enough to take up any drive assembly 
free travel.

Measure distance between pinion and end housing. Pinion clearance must 
not exceed 10 mm (0.39-0.42 inch).

Section 03C-12: Air Intake System, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Induction System 

Air is pulled into the engine through an air cleaner element. Clean air 
is very important to the life of the engine. Ingested dust and dirt can damage 
the engine very quickly. 

On turbocharged and aftercooled engines, the intake airflow is through 
the air cleaner to the turbocharger. After being pressurized in the 
turbocharger, it is then routed to the charge air cooler located in front of 
the radiator. Air leaves the charge air cooler and is routed to the intake 
manifold where it is forced into the cylinders and used for combustion. The 
charge air cooler reduces the temperature of the air, which lowers combustion 
chamber temperatures, which in turn reduces NOx emissions. Also, cooling the 
intake air makes it more dense, allowing more fuel to be injected into the 
engine to increase the power-to-weight ratio.

================================================================================
PAGE 6604
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-12: Air Intake System, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Cleaner Element

A dry-type air cleaner element is standard equipment. Air is filtered 
through a pleated, chemically-treated paper air cleaner element to remove 
contaminants before entering the engine induction system.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Restriction Gauge

Air intake systems are equipped with an air restriction gauge (mounted 
in the instrument panel) or an air restriction indicator (mounted at the air 
cleaner housing) that indicates when the air cleaner element needs servicing. 
When the air restriction indicator or gauge reads 6.2 kPa (25 inches of water) 
vacuum, the air cleaner element needs servicing.

Section 03C-12: Air Intake System, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Cleaner Element (Except LLS, LTLS, LLA, LTLA-9000)

 Compression Seal Element 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element, air cleaner housing or turbocharger inlet 
tube is removed, use a clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering 
the engine. 

Remove wing nut or fasteners retaining the air cleaner housing cover.

Remove the air cleaner housing cover.

Remove wing nut retaining the air cleaner element and remove the air 
cleaner element.

 Installation 

Before installing a new air cleaner element into the air cleaner 
housing, make sure the following conditions exist:

gasket surfaces clean and undamaged

outlet tube clean and undamaged

air cleaner element dry and free of holes, ruptures, damaged gaskets or 
dents in end covers and liners

air cleaner element retaining nut or bolt has gasket washer attached 
and in good condition

Install the air cleaner element and tighten the wing nut. Make sure the 
rubber face of the washer seals against the air cleaner element.

Install the air cleaner housing cover to housing.

Install wing nut or fasteners retaining the air cleaner housing cover.

Reset the air restriction indicator.

================================================================================
PAGE 6608
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-12: Air Intake System, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Cleaner Element (LLS, LTLS, LLA, LTLA-9000)

 Radial Seal Air Cleaner Element 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element, air cleaner housing or turbocharger inlet 
tube is removed, use a clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering 
the engine. 

Remove the fasteners that retain the air cleaner housing cover 
assembly, and remove the air cleaner housing cover.

Release the seal gently. The air cleaner element fits tightly over the 
outlet tube, creating the critical seal on the inside diameter of the air 
cleaner element end cap. Remove the air cleaner element gently to reduce the 
amount of dust dislodged. There will be some initial resistance, similar to 
breaking the seal on a jar. Gently move the end of the air cleaner element up 
and down and side to side or twist to break the seal.

[FIGURE: V8451A.gif]

Avoid dislodging dust from the air cleaner element. Gently pull the air 
cleaner element off the outlet tube and out of the air cleaner housing. Avoid 
knocking the air cleaner element against the air cleaner housing.

[FIGURE: V8452A.gif]

 CAUTION: To minimize air leaks, use care to avoid damage to the air cleaner 
housing outlet tube. 

With a clean shop cloth, carefully clean the outlet tube where it 
extends into the housing. Inspect for possible air leaks in housing, inlet or 
outlet pipes.

[FIGURE: V8453A.gif]

Clean the inside of the outlet tube carefully. Dirt accidentally 
transferred to the inside of the outlet tube will reach the engine and cause 
wear. Be careful not to damage the air cleaner element sealing area on the tube.

[FIGURE: V8454A.gif]

Check the old air cleaner element. It could help in the detection of 
foreign material on the sealing surface that is causing leakage. A streak of 
dust on the clean air side of the air cleaner element seal is the tell-tale 
sign. If dust exists, make sure the cause is removed before installing a new 
air cleaner element.

 Installation 

Inspect the new air cleaner element for damage. Always look for 
possible shipping or handling damage. Pay particular attention to the inside 
of the open end (the sealing area). Check for cuts, etc. Do not use a damaged 
air cleaner element.

Insert the new air cleaner element properly. The radial seal area is on 
the inside of the open end of the air cleaner element. This critical sealing 
area will stretch slightly, adjust itself and distribute the sealing pressure 
evenly as the air cleaner element is forced onto the outlet tube. Apply firm 
pressure to complete a tight seal. Apply pressure at the outer rim of the air 
cleaner element, not the flexible center. Cover pressure is not necessary to 
compress the air cleaner element seal.

[FIGURE: V8457A.gif]

Position the air cleaner housing cover to the housing and install the 
fasteners that retain the air cleaner housing cover. Air cleaner housing cover 
pressure is not necessary to compress the air cleaner element seal.

Reset the air restriction gauge or indicator.

[FIGURE: V8345D.gif]

Check connections and ducts for airtight fit. Make sure all clamps, 
flange connections and air cleaner mounting bolts are tight. Seal any leaks in 
the clean air ducting immediately that could permit dirt to enter the engine 
directly. All ducts, from air cleaner to engine, must be tight.

 Air Intake System, L, LT, LTS, LS, LN, LNT-9000 with Cummins N14, L10 
and M11 Engines

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Engine Air Cleaner Housing

 Removal 

Open the hood.

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element, air cleaner housing or turbocharger inlet 
tube is removed, use a clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering 
the engine. 

Loosen clamp at air cleaner outlet.

Disconnect air cleaner outlet hose from air cleaner outlet.

Remove two bracket-to-air cleaner retaining bolts.

Remove air cleaner housing from vehicle.

 Installation 

Position air cleaner assembly on bracket.

Install and tighten two retaining bolts.

Connect hose to air cleaner and tighten clamp.

Close hood.

================================================================================
PAGE 6610
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-12: Air Intake System, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Cleaner Outlet Tube

 Removal 

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element, air cleaner housing or turbocharger inlet 
tube is removed, use a clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering 
the engine. 

Loosen the clamp and disconnect air cleaner outlet tube from 
turbocharger.

Loosen the clamp and disconnect the air cleaner outlet tube from the 
air cleaner housing.

Remove the air cleaner outlet tube assembly.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Inlet Restriction Check

The best method for determining dry-type air cleaner maintenance 
periods is by checking the air restriction indicator or gauge.

It is recommended that the air restriction indicator or gauge be used 
to determine service intervals. A visual inspection of the air cleaner element 
will not ascertain the need for service. Overservicing is not recommended.

================================================================================
PAGE 6612
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-12: Air Intake System, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Cleaner Element

 CAUTION: Never attempt to clean a dirty or restricted air cleaner element. Use a 
new replacement only. 

Check the old air cleaner element. It could help to detect foreign 
material on the sealing surface that is causing leakage. A streak of dust on 
the clean air side of the air cleaner element seal is a tell-tale sign. If 
dust exists, make sure the cause is removed before installing a new air 
cleaner element.

Inspect the new air cleaner element for damage. Always look for 
possible shipping or handling damage. Pay particular attention to the inside 
of the open end (the sealing area). Check for cuts, etc. Do not use a damaged 
air cleaner element.

================================================================================
PAGE 6613
================================================================================
1997 L-Series

Section 03C-12: Air Intake System, Cummins, CAT and DDC Engines

1997 L-Series Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Engine Air Cleaner Housing

Clean the air cleaner housing and the cover with a mild detergent or 
compressed air. Wipe the air cleaner housing and cover dry. Inspect the air 
cleaner housing and cover for distortion or damage at the gasket mating 
surfaces. Replace the air cleaner housing cover or body if it is damaged 
beyond service.
